## ADR 0442 — A function handed to project code takes the role of each place that code invokes it
A function literal, or a same-file named function the file hands on (a whole argument, a non-intrinsic JSX attribute value, a `const` alias), takes for a write the join of the roles of all invocations ADR 0319's forward walk finds: through the callee's parameter (every use a call or a hand-on to another exact project callee); through `props.<name>` of an exactly resolved project component (an intrinsic `on…` attribute or a call in the child's handler is a delivery, a call in the child's body or a tracked computation is owned, a leaf-scope call is exempt, a prop forwarded to another component recurses within the walk's budget); and through a reviewed scheduler's callback slot (`setTimeout(fn)`, a fresh stack). A call is placed by what its own position proves, with no census of its function's other entries; in a function entered through a parameter it takes the role of the call that handed the value over, not of other callers. The join follows ADR 0378: an owned invocation (the body, a tracked computation) makes the write a violation regardless; otherwise every invocation must be placed (several non-reporting roles give `Unreported`), and the obligation stays for a census gap, an unplaced invocation, a destructured, `let`, stored or escaped use, a `merge`/`omit` view, a spread or repeated attribute on the element, a package component known only by declarations, a primitive's callback slot, or an unresolved child. A prop literal needs no closed program (a child's use of a prop ignores other callers); ADR 0450 makes the answers one memo per function. In a closed program the walk also follows an exported function declaration through other modules' references when each is a call the graph accounts for (`export *` is no hand-out; an alias, re-export specifier, value use, escaping namespace or open program refuses). So ADRs 0437 and 0438's censuses place a dispatch in `fireAndFlush(() => el.dispatchEvent(…))` called only from test callbacks (class `test-only helper`, leaving the veto) and in a handler-only `withTx(() => el.click())`, and flows through exported helpers (`makeNavigation`'s returned closures) are placed. Supporting steps: a `const` object pattern over an object the value is a member of binds the member by its plain-identifier key (`const { add } = renderPanel()`; a rest element or a quoted, computed or nested key refuses); in the test census only, a call past a possible suspension in an async helper is a satisfied entry, as in a registered async callback (the resumption has no owner or window, ADR 0333; the part before the first await runs on the caller's stack, which must still be a runner's). A write in a layer the walk runs in place (an immediately invoked function, a callback the standard library runs inline) takes the enclosing function's answer only if no layer's position follows a suspension: an `await` that may precede the write in its own or any enclosing function up to the answered one puts it in the ownerless continuation (ADR 0333), which no invocation places, so it stays unplaced (`write_flow_role`; fixture `prop-callback-roles/variants/after-await`). Under a synchronous dispatch (ADR 0356) host event deliveries are gated alike on both routes: the invocation found through `onClick={props.onPress}` and a call in `onClick={() => props.onPress()}` (placed by ADR 0327's census, which then refuses) both stay unplaced (`variants/sync-dispatch`). Premises: ADR 0319, 0327, 0333, 0378 and 0438's. Not built: reads for a forwarded or aliased owned call (SC1001 stays uncertifiable; a direct body call is ADR 0204), `merge`/`omit` views for an owned role, a registered test callback named by identifier, and unmodeled positions the walk refuses. Owners: `execution_role/event_literals.rs`, `invocation_flow.rs`, `write_roles.rs`; fixtures `prop-callback-roles`, `helper-literal-roles`, `test-runner-vitest/variants/helper-literal-*` and `helper-exported-*`; `solid-facts-backend/tests/invocation_flow_process.rs`.

## ADR 0444 — A workspace package a sibling depends on is an open program
ADR 0193's default made every `"private": true` package, and every manifest publishing nothing, a closed program. But an unseen workspace sibling may import it, so closed-program proofs (ADR 0203, 0213, 0214, 0442) falsely certified "no other caller" (kui's `kernel`, imported by every `feature-*`). An application is now closed only if no package of a workspace holding it depends on it. Workspaces read: `package.json` `workspaces` (array or `{ packages }`; npm, yarn, bun), `pnpm-workspace.yaml` `packages` (no key: pnpm's default, every subdirectory) and `lerna.json` `packages` (default `packages/*`), in the package's directory or any ancestor; patterns are `*`, `?`, `**` and `!` negation over directories holding a `package.json`. It is a member if a pattern lists it or it is the root; its dependents are the other members and the root manifest. A dependency is a name in `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies` or `optionalDependencies`, a `workspace:` or `npm:` spec naming it, or a `file:`, `link:`, `portal:` or `workspace:` path resolving to its directory. Open instead: a workspace not read exactly (brace, class or other pattern syntax, an anchored or multi-line YAML list, another `workspaces` shape, an invalid or unreadable sibling or ancestor manifest, over 20,000 directories listed), and `rush.json` or `nx.json` without workspace patterns (a project graph not package-based). An explicit boundary still wins. An open boundary only withdraws proofs: results move to uncertifiable, never to violations. Premises: a package imports a sibling only through a declared dependency, as managers require (not via a relative path out of its directory, a `tsconfig` `paths` alias or an undeclared hoisted install); Deno and Bazel workspaces are not read. The daemon keys its answer on one digest of every file and member listing read (`program_boundary_digest`), so a new dependent reopens the package at once. Owner: `solid-facts-backend/src/program_boundary.rs`; fixtures `program-boundary-workspace`, `program-boundary-pnpm`, `program-boundary-standalone`.

## ADR 0445 — A census with no entry proves no component
ADR 0331's census is vacuously complete for a function referenced only by its declaration and module surface, so it needs a reference that renders the function: a tag, a dialect renderer prop, a proven `lazy` default, an audited route option, or a compound member a tag reaches. A JSX-returning function with none is a component only as an exported capitalized binding, the host's by module surface (a file route's default export, a library component). Otherwise (dead, unexported, lowercase, or bound to a call's result, `const rows = items.map((x) => <li/>)`) its body is an undecided region, as for an escaped reference: non-style violations stay uncertifiable. An anonymous function literal called where written has that call as its only entry and is no component: it takes its caller's role, and module scope has no owner. Premise left: an exported capitalized function nothing renders, called plainly by unseen code, is judged a component. ADR 0203, 0213 and 0214 discharge toward silence for a function with no caller and never report; their closure is ADR 0444's. Owner: `compute_function_component_status` (`indexes/components.rs`); fixture `component-census-no-entry`.

<a id="adr-0446"></a>
## ADR 0446 — Precision is measured on a reproduction set, refreshed by one pre-release run
`fixtures/uncertifiable-repro` stands in for the corpus: a slice iterates on it in seconds anywhere, and each case is a test the slice must move. A case is one cause or shape, never one finding, of a `kind`: `uncertifiable` (a cause holding results, ADR 0328), `violation` (a triaged real defect) or `clean` (a certified shape a runtime probe or mutation confirmed, which no later change may make uncertifiable or a violation). A local case is one short file in its main rule's shared project; a whole-project cause gets a project: the dispatch veto (ADR 0356), one per site kind since one unexcluded site holds every handler proof, and the open program boundary (ADR 0444), which also defeats the test-only-helper exclusion (ADR 0438). The component census (ADR 0445) moved no corpus result and gets none. The one `node_modules` holds only published bytes (files `tsc` and the browser/development conditions read, each with its sha256 under the package's version and integrity, `packages.json`); every case type-checks against them and runs under the corpus configuration. `cases.json` is the one table: kind, cause, files, source (app, file:line, commit), weight (ADR 0448's for uncertifiable cases), expected results, status; snapshots pin findings. A cause is what `scripts/uncertifiable-causes.mjs` reads around a site with TypeScript's symbol resolution, from the premises and a second sweep with `--program-boundary closed`: a grouping label, never evidence. A case is faithful when its result matches its source's rule, analysis context and message family and reads as the same cause; `make repro-causes` checks the set side, `--report` the corpus side. No continuous intake: issues with minimal repros carry what users see; once before each release a pinned, versioned manifest of public Solid 2 repos is restored, swept, reproduced and discarded (CONTRIBUTING.md): a known cause updates its weight, a new one becomes a case unless not faithfully reproducible (then `notReproduced`, with why), and a false positive blocks the release. Budgets, with separate lines for violation and clean cases: `scripts/repro-budget.mjs` in `make verify`. Owners: `fixtures/uncertifiable-repro`, `scripts/{uncertifiable-causes,repro-reduce,repro-budget,corpus-sweep}.mjs`.

## ADR 0448 — Coverage counts sites whose mechanism a source read verified
A label is a grouping: the rc.17 corpus gave 95.7% of results a case's label, yet sampled sites read as their case's mechanism in 315 of 551 reads. So an uncertifiable case records `labelWeight` (results its label takes), `sites` (distinct app, file, line and rule; a file several projects analyze counts once) and `verification.samples`, a seeded draw of 5 sites (all if fewer), each read from source against the case's file (`same`, `different`, `unsure`, with the mechanism). `verifiedWeight` is `sites` if every sample reads `same`, else 0; `unsure` counts against. The classifier splits a mixed label until each case is one mechanism; a mechanism under 10 distinct sites gets no case and joins `notReproduced` with its reason. `--report` checks counts and samples against the sweep; `--draw` redraws. Only verified coverage is quoted: 2,350 of 5,183 sites (45.3%) at 187 cases; label coverage 4,834 of 6,734 results (71.8%); 1,494 sites sit under 611 labels of fewer than 10. A source read can miss a second blocker the label hides, so every verified case was also tested by experiment: in a corpus clone, remove the case's blocker at a recorded or drawn site and see whether the site moves (859 site runs). A stay sets the case's weight to 0 (74 cases, 1,427 sites refuted: writes unplaced before the await, other obligations on the line, a project-wide veto or census). 2,247 verified sites are experiment-confirmed; 103 (25 cases) had no faithful edit and rest on reading. Owners: `scripts/{uncertifiable-causes,repro-budget}.mjs`.

## ADR 0451 — A change that moves findings is gated on edit latency at a looser ratio
The ratio is gated whenever the base answered from its retained daemon: 1.25 for equal answers, 1.5 (`DIFFERING_RATIO_LIMIT`) for differing ones; a head answer outside its retained daemon still fails outright. A ratio, because ceilings are uncalibrated absolute times of one runner image (ADR 0423), while the paired median needs no calibration and is already measured. 1.5 because moved findings can add work (a new rule, more results); a real 2.0 to 2.7x regression still exceeds it. Ceilings stay reported. Owners: `benchmarks/lib/real-projects.mjs`, `scripts/real-projects.test.mjs`.

## ADR 0452 — A closure a tracked scope builds runs where it is called
A tracked scope (a memo or effect compute, a tracked JSX expression) gave every write and read in it its role, but building a closure runs nothing. `enclosed_by_stored_function` skipped named functions ("the call sites' business"; anonymous stored literals went to their invocations), and the lexical role returned before call sites were consulted (`write_roles.rs`, `direct`): `SC2001` reported `const openFn = () => setOpen(true); return openFn` (legal: rc.17 runs it from a click), and a read in a returned or stored closure was certified tracked though rc.17 warns `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` when the body calls it. Writes: the named closure's calls decide (`named_closure_in_tracked_scope`): in the scope's own pass, directly or via in-place layers (an IIFE, an inline standard-library callback), an alias or an outer closure, a violation; in a leaf scope or handler, legal; only returned or stored, uncertifiable. Names decide nothing (a capitalized closure is judged by its calls; one returning JSX is a possible component). Reads (`unrun_closure_within`, both tracked arms of `semantic_role_before_awaits`): a stored function, or a named closure not entered only by tracked calls, takes no role (uncertifiable); an IIFE, or a name whose every reference is a tracked call, keeps `Tracked`. A default (`(x = set(1)) => x`, `({ a = count() }) => a`) runs only when its function is called, so closure questions (`functions_around`: the stored-literal, JSX-attribute, region and named-closure guards) take the functions whose body or parameter list (by whole span) holds the site: a function inside a default (an IIFE, an inline callback) belongs to the closure, and a write there is unplaced whatever its lexical role (`write_flow_role` and the walk's entries had used the body-based function, placing it by a returning helper's calls). For summary rows (`interproc/graph.rs`, `callback_chain.rs`) a call in the owner's own list is no body call: it runs only when the caller omits the argument. The `containing_ast_function` lookups (about 150) still put nested list sites in the surrounding function: ADR 0454. The same query serves the component-child, provider-value, `merge` argument, named-callback, retained-literal and summary-owner questions. A named closure with a default is unplaced for writes and reads: its list is not inert, so the call graph withholds its call sites (ADR 0339), costing the violation for a body write of a closure with a non-literal default called in the scope. Also uncertifiable: an object method run by coercion (`valueOf`), a recursive closure (its calls are in progress). The corpus gains 17 uncertifiable results, no violation. Unchanged: `project_consumer` and `runs_outside_owner_call` read `attribute_function_within` alone. Fixtures `write-named-closure-in-tracked-scope`, `read-closure-in-tracked-scope`; rule page `no-write-in-pure-computation`.

The owner primitive, `AstFacts::innermost_function_owning` / `functions_owning`, is the innermost function whose body or parameter list (first parameter to body; name and type parameters are bound around it) holds the site. Over it, `owners.rs`: `owning_function`; `containing_body_function` (the owner if its body holds the site, else none); `owned_by_body` (`containing_ast_function(span) == function` for a call, member, JSX element or binding; true only in the body); `in_parameter_list`; `functions_around` is `functions_owning`. `containing_ast_function` stays the role pipelines' lexical lookup: a list site takes the role around its function, then is withheld (`parameter_default_owner`, now the owner of a site directly in a list, `unrun_closure_within`, the write guard); switching it globally made `prop-head-get`'s dormant default a violation instead of uncertifiable. A call in the owner's own list (`run(cb, x = cb())`) runs when a caller omits `x`: no body call, kept unplaced; no proof that every caller omits it is built. A parameter called in a list may run: `calls_parameter_in_parameter_list` keeps the summary row uncertifiable. The write guard covers every function's list, not only a named closure's: an anonymous callback's default is uncertifiable (`forEach((item, i = setV(1)) => …)`, index supplied), as is a true one (an IIFE omitting the argument, `createMemo((prev = setV(1)) => …)`). ## ADR 0455 — A write's owner is the one its callback's call gives it, through the layers that run in place
A callback's lexical hold no longer places a write (`write_region_adjustment`, `write_roles.rs`). The root, call-site, first-run and unaudited-root arms use `direct_callback_runs`, so a list site reaches the write guard (uncertifiable) in all their scopes (`createRoot`, `render`, `hydrate`, `untrack`, `dynamic` static, `flush`, `dispatchAsInteraction`, `createRenderEffect`'s first-run apply, an unaudited root; `createRoot` and `untrack` pinned). Owner `None` (`runWithOwner(null, …)`) is `Detached`, legal anywhere. Owner `Conditional` (maybe null, or a bound `createOwner()` result, which `run_with_owner_callback_owner` does not prove non-null) is `OwnerUnknown`, uncertifiable directly and through layers (there it was an unproven violation). A proven owner (`createOwner()`, a component's `getOwner()`) is a root whenever the callback runs: the write is `CreatedRoot`'s, a violation directly and through layers, even in a handler (rc.17 throws; not through a parameter-list layer, whose omission is unproven). A write in a layer under `untrack` takes the role at the `untrack` call (`CallSite`), like a direct one. An anonymous literal the callback returns, stores or hands to a call not run in place is unplaced (`unrun_layer_in_owner_keeping_callback`); handed to a project helper that calls it, a violation by the helper's summary (rc.17 throws). Costs, uncertifiable instead of violations: a closure with a default called in a root or `untrack` body with the argument omitted (rc.17 throws; the omission is unproven, as in a memo), and a write under a bound `createOwner()` owner, directly or in a layer. An action call stays a violation (its guard does not test `disposalDepth`). Cost: a named root helper called from a body is no longer reported. A function passed by name to `createRoot` asks the same at its call; an effect created in a cleanup is unplaced, since a flush there applies it in the disposal. ## ADR 0458 — A violation at a site no execution reaches is uncertifiable
Five Chrome-confirmed fuzzer false positives (on rc.17 each flagged site had 0 hits and no diagnostic; rendering the function or removing the dead guard raises it) had one cause, unpruned unreachable code: `false && setW(1)` in a called handle's callback (SC2001), `return; class K { static { onCleanup(…) } }` and `return; onCleanup(…)` in a timer (SC4001), `f1()` only in a `Child1` nothing renders or names (SC2001), and an async `Child1` returned from a discarded IIFE, or never rendered (SC4001). One query, generalizing ADR 0456's handle-call reachability, answers it (`SiteReach`, `execution_role/site_reach.rs`): `Unreached` proves the site never runs; `MayRun` proves nothing. Syntax gives dead regions (`AstFacts::unreachable_regions`, facts schema 77, `solid-facts` `ast/unreachable.rs`): statements after one in the same list that never completes normally (`return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue`, a block or `if` whose arms all do; a hoisted `function` declaration is not dead), and arms a literal test excludes (`if`, `?:`, `while`, `for`, the right of `&&`, `||`, `??`; literals: booleans, `null`, numbers, strings, `void`, function, object and array literals, and `!`/`&&`/`||` over them; no identifier, `undefined` included). Whether the site's function runs is a least fixed point; it never does if: written in dead code or a never-run function; a constructor, method or accessor of an unexported class with only unreached references (no static block, static initializer or `@` in scope); bound to an unexported name, no module calls `eval`, and every resolved call or render and every reference is unreached, in a type query or returned by a discarded IIFE; or an anonymous function a discarded IIFE returns. A module-scope function may run (modules and hosts are not followed; ADR 0445 keeps the module surface), as may any other unnamed value once created. The pipeline asks it of every reportable row's location after all producers and gates (`unreached_report_sites`, `Program::unreached_sites`, compared by the shadow build); the backend makes a violation at an exact unreached location uncertifiable for any rule, beside the undecided-component downgrade (`diagnostics.rs`), except style rules (SC80xx) and SC2008 (it claims a no-op wherever it runs). The handle census (ADR 0456) uses the same query, and a named function with only unreached calls that is also handed on as a value no longer counts as unreached. Not covered: a site after an always-throwing call (SC3001's dead tracked-effect body), a `try` that cannot complete, `undefined` or a constant binding as a test, an unreferenced module-scope function, a site reached only through an unreached call of a function also called elsewhere (the finding's location is reached), an evidence step in dead code. Fixture `dead-code-sites`.

A case's `oracle.json` may now list `mount`, its exported components: the entry imports them by name and renders each by its own top-level `render(() => <C />, host)` in the namespace's sorted order; the namespace loop after skips them, so other exports render as before and the hand-out stays. Without `mount` the entry is byte-identical. The generator lists every `export function` component (`scripts/fuzz/emit.mjs`); the checker materializes the same entry (`scripts/fuzz/checker.mjs` `mainSourceFor`).

<a id="adr-0502"></a>
## ADR 0502 — `schedule` withholds a render effect's first run as `defer` does
rc.17's `effect()` runs a render effect's first apply on the call only when neither `options.defer` nor `options.schedule` is set (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/dev.js:1865-1868`); with `schedule` it is enqueued and runs from the flush, not under the caller's owner. The checker read only `defer`. The dialect now answers `effect_apply_schedule_options` (`createRenderEffect`'s apply); a `schedule` set or unreadable makes the apply's owner conditional (`callback_owner_at_call`), never none, since which releases honour the key is not modelled per release, and a first-run read with it is not the caller's (`read_escapes_synchronous_extent`). This is a precondition for proving a first run (ADR 0503).

<a id="adr-0503"></a>
## ADR 0503 — A render effect's first run is on the call under a module-scope render
ADR 0460 left a write in a body's `createRenderEffect` apply uncertifiable. The first run is on the call (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/dev.js:1851-1869`, `runEffect` keeping the caller's `context`) unless `defer` or `schedule` is set, the first pass is born staged (`dist/dev-shared.js:4438-4462`) or lane-seated (`:4388-4396`), the compute errors or goes pending (`:4227-4240`), or a boundary above shows its fallback (`dist/dev.js:1957`); and nothing placed the mount. `first_run_proven_at_call` (`execution_role/write_roles.rs`) excludes each: no options argument; a function-literal compute, not async or a generator, that calls, reads, references, awaits, renders and throws nothing; the call on every completion of the body; and a synchronous mount (`Dialect::mount_runs_component_synchronously`: `render`, not `hydrate`, `@solidjs/web` `dist/web.dev.js:542-568`) at module top level whose first argument is an arrow whose whole body is the component's self-closing tag (`mounted_by_module_render`, `owners/async_context.rs`). Module scope is outside every flush, lane, transition and boundary, so a write in that first run throws `REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE` (an action, `ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE`). One such mount suffices. A `schedule` that may keep the first run off the call (ADR 0502) leaves a write directly in the apply unplaced (it was silent). Fuzzer cases carry such a mount (ADR 0501). Fixture `render-apply-first-run` (violations `FirstRunWrite`, `FirstRunWriteLayered`; uncertifiable `Unmounted`, `Scheduled`, `OptionsVariable`, `ComputeReads`, `ConditionalEffect`, `Hydrated`, `RenderedLater`). Review: the compute must be one primitive literal, returned or the whole body, with no parameter or one plain one (a dynamic `import()`, a literal thenable or a destructuring parameter keeps the first run off the call); the rendered binding must hold its function (`function_value_is_current`: a `let` reassigned before the render); and the `render` must run on every module evaluation (outside a class, in straight-line module flow, a completion site; solid-facts schema 85 gives the module its own frame for `try` blocks and exits, so a top-level `try { render(…) }` is straight-line).

## ADR 0504 — A render-effect apply's first read of a source pending since the body is SC5001
ADR 0467 kept an apply's read of an async source SC1001: rc.17's `read()` throws `PENDING_ASYNC_UNTRACKED_READ` for a pending source before it would warn (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/dev-shared.js:5320-5325`, `:5441-5446`), and nothing ordered the first run against the settling. A render effect's first run is on the call (ADR 0503, `dist/dev.js:1869`), and a halt does not stop it (only `schedule` checks one, `dist/dev-shared.js:2038-2042`). `pending_apply_first_read` (`execution_role/write_roles.rs`) proves the read is in that run: it sits in a function-literal `createRenderEffect` apply, directly or through in-place layers crossing no library callback, list, await or callback-handing helper, after no written apply call (an earlier throw ends the run); ADR 0503 places the call on the mount; the source is a same-body `const` declared on every completion before the call, `createMemo` of one async function literal, pending from creation until a microtask (`:4626`, `:3642-3660`), with no `loadingValue`; and nothing between source and call runs code (each call there creates a signal or memo or calls a `const`-bound local function that calls nothing). The row (`AsyncRead::apply_first_run_pending`; at a closure's call, `pending_origin`/`pending_apply`) is an SC5001 violation, and the strict read at the site or with that origin in that apply is withdrawn, since the run throws first. Not built (review): a `createEffect` apply, whose first run in `render`'s tail flush any pending render effect in the mount (a fragment, a helper's JSX or effect, a module-level effect) holds until the source settles. Fixture `strict-read-async-apply` gains `main.tsx`: `RenderApplyReadsAsync`, `RenderApplyReadsAsyncRendered` move SC1001 -> SC5001 (their rendered reads' SC5003 a violation, the mount resolved); `ApplyReadsAsync`, `ApplyReadsAsyncRendered`, `ApplyComputeReadsAsync`, `ApplyComputeWaitsOnOtherAsync`, the review's `SharedClosure`, `ReadAfterCall`, `BodyReadsFirst` and the unmounted `UnmountedApplyReadsAsync` keep SC1001 for apply reads.

## ADR 0505 — A user effect's first apply under a static first mount meets its source pending
ADR 0504 left a `createEffect` apply SC1001: its first run, queued at the call, runs in `render`'s tail `flush()` (`@solidjs/web@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/web.dev.js:542-568`), which a pending render effect in that flush or a transaction an earlier pass left holds (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/dev-shared.js:1690-1733`, `:2180`). `user_apply_runs_in_mount_flush` (`execution_role/write_roles.rs`) adds premises so nothing can create such a node:
- the component renders a static intrinsic tree: lowercase tags only, no attribute, spread, expression child, fragment or component;
- the body runs only the effect, the source, signals or memos of primitive literals and calls of inert local `const` functions; it reads no member, has no `throw`, class or tagged template, and destructures only local literals;
- the source's async compute is one primitive literal;
- the mounting `render` is the first code that can create a node. The memo `ModuleScopeRuns` lists project files whose module scope may run code (a call, member, reference, JSX, class, `await`, `throw`, method or hazard) and whether any file loads a module other than Solid's own (whose evaluation only installs hooks) or an analyzed project file. Only the entry may run code; before the call, only standard-library code and local `const` functions running only that, referencing no import but `render`.

solid-facts schema 86 records `throw_statements`. Fixture `effect-apply-first-run`: two positives, one variant per premise; `strict-read-async-apply`'s `ApplyReadsAsync` (the first render) moves SC1001 -> SC5001. Mounts by a child, router, loop or `hydrate`, and later renders, stay SC1001. Review (also ADR 0504): the read must be on every completion of the apply and each in-place layer up to it (`read_on_every_completion_of_apply`), and a closure-carried read on every completion of each function up to the call (`push_call_attributed_async_reads`); `if (v === 1) return;` or a loop that may not run, before the read in the apply or a closure it calls, was SC5001 though the first run skips the read. Fixture rows `RenderApplyGuarded` and the `guarded` variant. Fuzzer: legal contexts `{effect,render}-apply-guarded` and `-guarded-closure` (container `guard-return`); the legal judge counts an SC5001 violation the runtime never matches, at an unexecuted site or anywhere else, as a false positive; probes `pending-async/apply-guarded-first-run`, `apply-guarded-closure`.

## ADR 0506 — Reachability follows function literals a call runs or receives; a call-result binding's calls run nothing
The fuzzer's mount axis renders each misuse component as a parent's child, not exported, and found two defects:
- **False cleans (364 per mount, confirmed in Chrome).** A write in an IIFE or helper callback in such a component was dropped and the program certified: reachability (`reachability.rs`) reached functions only as roots, which only functions nested in exported declarations are. Now a function literal a call invokes (an IIFE's callee) or receives (a project helper's callback, `[1].forEach(fn)`) is reached when the call is, and (review) so is every function created in a reached function's body or parameter list; before, an arrow a private component only returned or stored (`(() => () => set(1))()`, `[() => set(1)]`) was certified. Reaching says nothing about when a function runs; the write and read roles decide.
- **A false positive, already on #141.** `const wrapped = wrap(() => set(1)); wrapped()` was a violation even when `wrap` never runs the arrow: `functions_by_symbol` names the function nested in a call initializer for the binding, and the call graph took each call of the binding as a call of it, though the binding holds the call's result. The mapping stays as identity evidence (server functions a `query` wraps, `lazy` loaders' tags). `SymbolFunction::Resolved` records `through_call`, and `CallSitesOf` drops such a symbol's call and render sites (census table `FileCallResultSymbols`). `lazy(loader)`'s result is not such a binding: its render runs the loader (ADR 0292).

Moved: `use-site-role`'s `UsesWrite`, violation -> uncertifiable (its write in `writeOf`'s memo was proved only by the unsound call path; the use-site arm places no write). `Tdz.tsx`'s module-scope `wrap` arrow, `unplaced-site-obligations`, `write-scope-roots-rc3/rc9` and `uncertifiable-repro/sc1001` gain uncertifiable rows for newly reached code. Fixtures `private-component-layers`, `call-result-binding`. Fuzzer: `--mounts root,child,show,for` on both grids; probes `write/private-child-iife`, `write/call-result-binding`, `write/private-returned-closure`, `write/private-array-element`. Unchanged: a write a helper runs only on a branch its arguments rule out (`maybe(cb, false)`), in `[].forEach`, or in a component JSX renders in a dead branch is claimed wherever it may run (the `SiteReach` convention, ADR 0457), as in exported components.

## ADR 0507 — A child an inert parent renders is mounted as its parent is
ADRs 0503-0505 prove a first run under a module-scope `render` of the component itself. `module_render_sites` (`owners/async_context.rs`) now also returns a mount through up to four parents (`MountSite::parents`). The child's tag must be:
- self-closing, with no attribute, spread or child;
- in the parent's own body, in the argument of its one (unconditional, straight-line) return or its expression body;
- reached from there through intrinsic elements only, each a child of the next (`static_child_tag`).

The compiler evaluates such a tag (`createComponent`) while the parent builds its tree, so the child's body runs inside the parent's, outside any computation. The parent must run nothing else (`inert_parent`): its body is one `return <tree>` (review: an earlier statement may coerce, iterate or read a throwing getter, ending the mount), with plain parameters, no call, member read, tagged template, class, `throw`, nested function or fragment, and no JSX but static intrinsic elements and the tag. A pending earlier pass of the mount stages later ones (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/dev-shared.js:1690-1708`), and a throw ends it. ADR 0505's other premises (`render_runs_first`, the static tree) apply to the root render. Not built: `<Show>`, `<For>` and other components, which run children in a computation or later. Residual, as in ADRs 0503-0505, which assume the body completes normally: an implicit throw in the component's body before the site (a coercion through a throwing `toString`), and a loop that never ends. Fixture `child-mount-first-run` (violations `PlainParent` SC2001, `Grand` SC5001 through two parents, variant `effect-child` SC5001 through ADR 0505; uncertifiable `CallingParent`, `ShowParent`, `PropParent`, `ConditionalParent`). Probe `write/child-mount-first-run`.

<a id="adr-0508"></a>
## ADR 0508 — `<Show when={true}>` and a one-row `<For>` render their child during the mount
ADR 0507's climb from a child's tag to the parent's returned tree may now pass two holders besides intrinsic elements:
- The dialect's `<Show when={true}>`: one attribute, `when`, the literal `true`, no spread, its one child the climbed node (`shown_child`). Its value memo computes when `Show` is created (`computed` runs a non-`lazy` node then, `@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/dev-shared.js:4913-4932`) and reads `props.children` when the condition holds (`solid-js@2.0.0-rc.17` `dist/solid.dev.js:1571-1600`), rendering the child inside that compute.
- The dialect's `<For each={[…]}>`: one attribute, `each`, a non-empty array literal of primitive literals, no spread, its one child a parameterless arrow whose expression body is the tag (`for_row`). `For` builds its `mapArray` on the first read of its result (`dist/solid.dev.js:1548-1562`), which the parent's insert makes on its first pass.

The child's body then runs during the parent's tree under an owner (the memo or the row), and a render effect created there runs its first apply on the call (`dist/dev.js:1851-1869`). `inert_parent` admits the holders and the row arrow. Not built: a non-literal `when` or `each`, `keyed`, `fallback`, a row taking the item, `<Switch>`/`<Match>`, `<Index>`. Fixture `child-mount-first-run`: `ShowParent` (uncertifiable under ADR 0507) and new `ForParent` are violations; new negatives `ShowBindingParent`, `ForEmptyParent`, `ForItemParent`. Probes `write/show-mount-first-run`, `pending-async/for-mount-first-run`. Review (Chrome-checked): whitespace text without a line break is a child the compiler keeps (`<For> {() => <C />} </For>` hands `For` an array, and the row never runs); and ADR 0503's first-run write, like ADR 0504's read, now needs no call written before it in the apply (`apply_runs_nothing_before`), since a pending read there throws first (fixture row `render-apply-first-run` `ReadThenWrite`; probes `write/for-inline-whitespace`, `write/apply-write-after-pending-read`).

## ADR 0509 — A value a caller hands over is followed, or its use stays open
The fuzzer's source axes (PR #149) hand the misuse component its signal, store, action or async memo through a prop, a context, a hook's return or a module export. Causes and fixes:
- **Setters and stores found by type alone were silent.** On rc.17 a setter not proven `createSignal`'s took the role that reports nothing (an optimistic setter meets no guard); it is now unplaced unless proven `createOptimistic`'s. The three store rules read only proven stores; a typed store is now an obligation. The demand plan types names destructured from a non-primitive call (`const [, set] = useCount()`).
- **Accessor transport carried reads only.** A hook's returned object or tuple slot and a context value now also resolve to `Callable::Setter`/`Callable::Action` (in `write_call_targets`, out of every read consumer's table); a post-pass writes or acts with the source's row, replacing a typed one, and gives a transported async read its async row.
- **A call of a prop's value was dropped.** Pass 10 records per prop the exact sources visible sites pass (`PassedSources`) and whether a getter calls an async source; `props.name(…)` on the exact parameter, directly in the component or a primitive's callback, reads, writes or acts with each (one witness suffices); deeper, or with any other value passed, it is an obligation (`closed-parameter-member-dispatch`).
- **One fail-closed net for the rest (`handed-member-dispatch`).** A call whose callee has no row and is, through members, aliases, destructuring or local literals, a caller-supplied value (props or a view, `useContext`, a project function's result, an alias of an imported source) is an obligation where it would report a write, action or untracked read, or may run in a leaf owner; for a callee typed as a Solid accessor (declared in an installed Solid package, ADR 0509's `descriptor_type_role`), only for a read. It also covers store writes past such a root, `refresh` of an unresolved target, reads after an `await` through helpers, argument closures and IIFEs, and an unproven helper call of a prop read. Pushed last, it yields to any other cause at its site. Correction: transport drops it only where the target's summary is complete (ADR 0686), and a hook's result used unbound or iterated is such a value too (ADR 0689).
- **A strict read of an async source that may meet it pending is unproven** (rc.17 throws first): an obligation, fixing the module/context async wrong-rule class.
 Cost: two real-app clean repro cases (`clean-context-provider`, `clean-store-draft`) are uncertifiable. Not built: context proofs in an open program, props through views, the producer's empty origin module for published `.d.ts` files (typed rules elsewhere still need a stub's `declare module`).

## ADR 0510 — A module-scope or parent-handed async memo meets the first run pending; nothing in a layer runs before the read
ADR 0509 left an apply's read of an unseen async source an obligation. Three sources now meet ADR 0504/0505's first run pending (`pending_apply_first_read`, `execution_role/pending_sources.rs`), each `createMemo` of one async function literal with no options, pending until a microtask:
- **A module-scope memo** with a literal compute, in a project module whose scope only creates (`module_scope_only_creates`: each call a `const`'s whole initializer, `createMemo` of a literal compute, `createSignal` of at most one literal, `createContext`; nothing else runs), read under a mount whose `render` passes `render_runs_first` (no TLA, every module seen) from an entry no project module imports (the `ModuleScopeRuns` census now also lists creation-only modules and imported files; the entry is then a root of evaluation, so every module it loads has evaluated, ECMAScript `InnerModuleEvaluation`), the component with plain parameters and nothing in its body before the effect (`body_runs_nothing_between` from the body's start). Unread, such a memo joins no transaction (`joined` false, `:4520`), and a parking seam skips a loading source (`:2194-2204`), so `render_runs_first` admits such modules for ADR 0505 too.
- **A parent's memo** in a mount site's last parent, as an exact prop (`<C data={data} />`, `props.data()` on the one plain, never-written parameter) or through one provider of a module-scope `createContext` (`<Ctx value={{ k: data }}>`, `useContext(Ctx).k()`; the provider sets its value on a root before `children` builds the memos the parent's insert reads). ADR 0507's climb admits such parents: `const` creations before the one return, tag attributes naming them (`handed_attribute`), the provider as a holder (`provided_child`).
- **A static tree** (ADR 0505) may hold string attributes, primitive-literal children (`insert` of a non-function places it with no effect) and reads of the body's own signal or synchronous memo of a literal (`settled_expression_child`); an async memo's read still holds the flush.

Correction (Chrome-confirmed false positives of ADRs 0503-0505): only the apply's own earlier calls were checked, so `(() => { JSON.parse("{"); a1(); })()` was SC5001 (a write there SC2001). `runs_nothing_before_in_layers` now walks each layer up from the site: no call in its body before the position or among the layer call's arguments before the function, a project helper calling the argument first (`parameter_called_first`, ADR 0495), and a wrapper's body too (`push_call_attributed_async_reads`). Wrong rule: a read through a local function whose call got no local-access row (`wrapUse()` after an `action` creation) kept SC1001; it gets ADR 0509's opening row. Review (Chrome-confirmed false positives): `const v = props.cfg.x;` (an `any`, undefined) before the effect, or `(v as any).a.b;` before the read, throw first but were claimed; `throws_nothing_before` now also refuses, in each layer and in the body before the effect, a member read, computed member, spread or iteration, operator, `delete`, destructuring (except a creation's tuple or ADR 0505's local literal), tagged template, class, `throw` or loop, and a layer with a pattern parameter. A second root reaching the source's module (a project file none imports, `warm.ts`: `import "./source"`) refuses: a page loading it first settles the memo in the checkpoint between the two scripts (the census now records import edges); premise: no script outside the project's files imports the source. The body's name for an imported source is the read's own resolved callee, not an import matched by name. Fixture `pending-source-first-run`.

## ADR 0511 — Handed and hook-created async memos meet the first run pending through layers and closed aliases
Shapes ADR 0510 left uncertifiable SC5001 although rc.17 throws `PENDING_ASYNC_UNTRACKED_READ`:

A body-defined wrapper the apply calls once (`const wrapUse = () => { props.a1(); }`) is read at `wrapUse()`, as for an own source (`discover_props_call`, `pending_apply_first_read_from`); a second call keeps it.
- **A memo a hook of another module creates** (`const { a1 } = useVals()`, `const vals = useVals(); vals.a1()`; the transport already carried the read to the memo's declaration). `hook_source_pending` (`pending_sources.rs`) proves it where the hook is inert (`inert_hook`: a sync, non-generator, parameterless project function running only inert creations, throwing nothing, its one straight-line `return` a literal of data properties naming its bindings), creates the memo with a literal compute on every completion, and the body calls it once before the effect (`hook_call_in_body`: no argument, the exact unwritten hook, every completion, a `const` name or object pattern). `BodyAdmits::hook` lets ADR 0505/0510's body premises admit that call and an object pattern of its result (`hook_result_destructuring`). The read must go through that call's own result (`read_through_hook_call`); another instance's read (`shared.a1()` of a module-scope `useVals()`, settled before mount) was SC5001 where rc.17 warns SC1001 (`hook-shared-instance`).
- **Closed aliases of handed values** (`const d = props.k`, `const d = ctx.k`, `const { d } = { d: props.k }`) hit SC9012 before the proof. Two exact steps: the resolver's escape census (`census_rows`, `accessor_provenance/resolver_index.rs`) no longer counts as an escape a Get of a named member held whole by a one-name `const`, a data property or an array element (`gets`): it copies the value (a named write of the member keeps its veto); and an object pattern of an inline object literal follows a slot whose own value is transported (`resolver_values.rs`; a local source keeps ADR 0463's alias facts). For props, `handed_member_alias` (`pending_sources.rs`) follows both forms to `props.k`, and `discover_call` treats the alias as the prop's call (ADR 0509's `discover_props_call`). The pending proof takes the alias declared in the body before the effect, `only_called_members` admits it, and `BodyAdmits::handed` lets the body read named members of the handed object (a data property of the object the proven mount passes). A passed function is followed through the alias; a write in it stays claimed at the passed arrow.
- **`<Loading>` holders (researched, then built).** rc.17's `Loading` returns `createLoadingBoundary(() => props.children, …)`, which builds the children in `computed(fn, { name: "children" })` at creation. Chrome: a child's render effect meets the parent's memo pending, as does a user effect under a static tree; a render-effect write throws; a user effect whose tree reads the memo waits for the reveal and warns `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED`. - **Aliases of an imported source** (`const d = a1`, `const { d } = { d: a1 }`, `a1` a named runtime import) hit SC9012, since ADR 0463's exact alias is a `const` of the file. Tuples of an imported source stay open with the handed ones.
- **Tuples: not built** (`const [, d] = [0, props.k] as const`, or of a context member or imported source). ADR 0282's census follows a slot only where no code may change the array iterator and the value is proven no code constructor (`string_code_reference`). The fuzzer's harness entry calls `make(type)`, an unresolved call of a non-literal argument, which alone sets ADR 0282's veto in every grid program.

<a id="adr-0512"></a>
## ADR 0512 — The fuzzer's fast path is Chrome, driven by a Rust executor
The differential fuzzer's fast path runs in headless Chromium, not Happy DOM: one Vite server with the Solid plugin serving cases from memory, one reused page per worker, a fresh document per program, on Chrome's virtual time. Projects, `tsrs -b` batches, checker runs and pages (over CDP, with Playwright's switches) run in a Rust executor (`scripts/fuzz/exec`, its own workspace); verdicts stay in JS. Trust is measured: a stratified runtime differential against `feedback run` gives records identical to the host's (both keep 41 frames; the oracle runs `--source-instrumentation off`, whose `withOperation` wrapper frames moved 8 of 4,340 sampled records), and hosts are compared record for record after each host change. Loops: `make fuzz-focus CODES=…`; `make fuzz-smoke` (ADR 0916); full grids before a PR. `--fast-host happy-dom` remains. Owners: `scripts/fuzz/chrome-host.mjs`, `exec/`, `focus.mjs`, `smoke.mjs`.

<a id="adr-0513"></a>
## ADR 0513 — The fuzzer measures recall on axes the base grids do not draw
`--recall` grids (`mx-recall`, `lg-recall`) cross each new binding, callee form, layer, callback form, mount and file source with every cell's base grid, adding recall-only contexts and a `LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD` template; mutation mode pairs each misuse shape with its legal twin, checker only. They are opt-in, so base grids, seeds and baselines stay byte-identical, and out of `fuzz-focus` by default. Owners: `scripts/fuzz/misuse.mjs`, `mounts.mjs`, `matrix.mjs` (`recallAxes`), `mutation.mjs`.

<a id="adr-0514"></a>
## ADR 0514 — The fuzzer's browser is the pinned Playwright's; a Linux VM where process starts are gated
Without `--browser`, the oracle and the Chrome host run the headless shell the pinned Playwright names (`browsers.json` revision, the platform's cache and layout; `scripts/playwright-browser.mjs`) and stop when it is absent, never taking the cache's newest build (invariant 7: a cache held Chrome 156 where Playwright 1.60.0 pins 148). `scripts/fuzz/vm.sh` runs the fuzzer in a Colima VM on a Mac whose security agents gate every process start: equal outcomes, 3.7x faster than the best macOS setting.

## ADR 0515 — Exact copies, named callbacks and assigned callees the fuzzer's recall grid found silent
Each is the same value or call by construction, so every rule follows it (fail-closed facts, no name matching). In `solid-facts`: a `const` initialized by a conditional whose arms are both one `const` (`c ? r : r`) or by an inline identity arrow on it (`((x) => x)(r)`) aliases that variable (ADR 0463's fact); a slot of `const { k } = N` over a `const N = S` holding a namespace import is `S.k` (ADR 0459's fact); `(slot = f)()`, a plain assignment to a binding as callee, invokes `f` (ADR 0468's peel; not in an `async` function, whose after-await owner placement reads the operands and went silent on the peel). In the IR, a primitive's callback position names a function through an exact `const` copy only when every reference to the copy follows its declarator in the declarator's function (a copy reached from a nested function may run first and throw), and through a named function expression's binding whose own name is unreferenced (reads and `by_name_position` alike); a read in a function nested in a named callback climbs the in-place layers to its call, as in an inline callback.

## ADR 0518 — A top-level `await` leaves pending-read findings unproven
SC5003 (`async-outside-loading-boundary`) claimed every rendered read of an async source outside a `Loading` boundary, assuming the source pending at the read's first run. A top-level `await` suspends module evaluation (microtasks run, timers too if it waits on one), so a node created before it (a module-scope memo, or a module-scope hook instance a root already read) can settle by the mount, and a settled read needs no boundary (rc.17 warns nothing). The fuzzer's `module-hook-shared` source found 50 such legal programs reported (`const shared = useVals(); createRoot(…shared.a1()…); await …; export function C1() { createRenderEffect(() => { shared.a1(); … }) }`), false positives confirmed in Chrome. Fix: `ModuleCensus::may_settle_before_mount` (a project module with a top-level `await`, or a load the census cannot see) sets `AsyncRead::settle_unproven`, and projection then makes SC5003 uncertifiable; its `ssrSource: "client"` wording stays, since that throws on the server whatever the client's timing. Premise: no dependency module awaits at its top level (the census does not scan installed packages; SC5001's apply proofs refuse any unseen load). Trade: any top-level `await` in a project makes every SC5003 uncertifiable, even for a memo the reading body creates; which nodes the checkpoint settles is not modeled. Fixture variants `pending-source-first-run/{module-render-read,module-render-await}` (violation, uncertifiable); `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json` records the rediscovery. Review (Chrome-confirmed false positive): SC5001 on a component-body or root read had the same gap (`settled-body`: rc.17 warns `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED`, the checker proved SC5001), so the flag makes SC5001 uncertifiable too, except an apply's first-run row (ADR 0510's own proof). Those proofs (`render_runs_first`, `module_scope_only_creates`, `module_scope_may_run`) now also count `for await` and `await using`. Precision cost: an unread module memo stays pending through an `await` (`module-body-await` throws in Chrome) yet is uncertifiable. The generator's `settled` variant also takes `body` and `root`. Variants `module-body-settled`, `module-body-await`, `module-for-await` (uncertifiable).

## ADR 0520 — An action body is placed by its callers, and a yielded promise detaches the next step
The fuzzer's `action` recall context (NO_OWNER_CLEANUP, 588 certified false cleans of 624): with `const a1 = action(function* () { onCleanup(() => {}); })` called as `a1()` from a button handler, the checker certified `onCleanup` clean, since the generator, a callback with no owner edge, took the component body's providing region by position. rc.17 steps the generator on the stack of the action's caller (`@solidjs/signals` `dist/dev.js:1573-1607`), so the body's owner is the caller's (none in a handler), as also for `createEffect`, `useContext`, `Loading(props)` and an `onSettled` cleanup there (probed in Node, dev build). Fix: the stepped generator's owner node takes the symbol of the `const` holding the action (`action_binding_name`); a call or callback argument naming that binding (through `const` copies, not a written binding) targets the generator (`named_action_generator`); no providing region answers for a stepped generator, so its operations are judged on the graph: every caller unowned is a violation, a caller's owner is inherited (a leaf caller's leaf, where `onCleanup` is SC3001's claim; a children-capable caller throws `ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE` first and the body's context is owned), and a generator no binding holds, or whose binding reaches a component prop, a slot or an assignment (`action_binding_escapes`), is seeded open-world unowned: an obligation. Steps: a yielded native promise (`Promise.resolve()`, `new Promise(…)`, `Promise.all` and siblings, resolved by the standard library's declaration, which the demand plan now asks for a `yield` operand) is assimilated, and the next step runs from its continuation with no owner (`:1618-1636`), as does every step of an async generator; a plain value steps again synchronously (`:1637`). solid-facts records every `yield` with its operand and dominated block region (schema 88, `AstFacts::yields`); `action_step_resumption` makes an operation in the region proven unowned (`after_yield`, a new `OwnerRequirement` flag with its own evidence line), and uncertain where a possible-thenable `yield` may precede it; a call after one carries the new `ResumesUnowned` edge. Legal twins stay silent: an action called only from a root or body (the action-call rule reports), never called, from a tracked body, or after `yield 1`; writes in an action body are unchanged (execution roles untouched). Residual: an action handed to a component prop is an obligation, not the violation the ADR 0319 census gives a plain helper (the census refuses generators); a stored prop called from a timer is certified clean for a helper and an action alike (pre-existing).

## ADR 0544 — Role work and reachability stay polynomial in nested layers
A read's role asks of each named closure around it (`unrun_closure_within`, ADR 0452) whether all its calls are tracked, and placing each call asks the same of the closures around it: one call per layer costs 2^depth placements per read (debug, 189 s at depth 20). `closure_unplaced` (`execution_role/body_roles.rs`) keeps the outermost query's placement, reused only where recomputing answers the same: its computation met no cut on a closure in progress before it began, no closure it entered is in progress now, and the context is equal (the read-recording frame `base::reads::current_frame`; an open role-log decision; `flow_cache_state`: whether a flow or write-flow answer computes and how often their per-answer caches were cleared; the callbacks `inherits_callback_role` places). Not kept under a probe or a proof's deferred check; a reuse replays its role-log record. Placements grow as depth·(depth+3); `BuildTimings::closure_placements` counts them, and the complexity ladder gates them under 2·depth²·placements(1) to depth 20. Reachability from a root into a call-graph cycle no longer walks every simple path (factorial when dense): `path_counts` counts on the condensation (`condensation_counts`, Tarjan), equal to the path count when acyclic and nonzero exactly where a path reaches the call. `ReactiveWrite::multiplicity` is read only as zero or not (projection ignores it), so no decision moves; on a cyclic graph it is no longer the simple-path count.

## ADR 0545 — Warm checks: parsed files outlive a chain, the producer's build inputs are witnessed, the role log is each answer's
Imports moving defeats in-place replacement (`reuse_program`), and the fresh chain reparsed every file (bundled libraries, installed declarations: most of a ~25 ms warm check) and redigested every text (~1.9 ms). `file_regions::ParseCache` gives a new chain each file with equal parse options and text byte-equal to what the host reads now; the chain adopts the file's region, alive while any chain reads it; only a committed head's files stay cached. A parse depends only on options and text, a bound file is frozen (`unsafe_boundary` invariant 8), and tsrs's watch mode and project system share files likewise. A cached file's text digest stays in its entry (its address is unique while held). The randomized incremental oracle runs without the cache.

The daemon's resolution witness modelled only bare and `#` imports; relative and `paths` resolutions relied on tracked sources and directory stamps, so a `package.json` rewritten in place in an imported directory kept the old resolution, unlike one-shot (`warm_resolution_process` fails on the old build). The producer now records every question its builds ask below the overlay (build-scope lookups and read paths; a new chain replaces them, an in-place update adds its own) and answers them on `Modules` with `buildInputs`. The witness observes each at least as finely as tsrs reads it: kind following links, a stat's kind and file size (all tsrs reads of it), the canonical path, a listing with each entry's followed kind, a read's bytes; a tracked source's bytes stay the overlay's. Absent probes under an unchanged directory `lstat` stamp stay absent. `graph_kept` also reports an in-place update that asked nothing new; a kept update fetches no inputs. Observation trails the build by a few milliseconds, like every witness entry.

A warm slot keeps one directory, `slots/<n>/program/`: per-program slot names (e34cb6e75) gave each program a socket and so a daemon (`warm-identity.mjs` sent no ids, hiding it). Each check names its program in `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ROLE_LOG_PROGRAM`; path lines carry it as `g`, which `roles.mjs` prefers to the path. The client sends role log and program with the check; the daemon points the process-wide log at them for that answer only (`role_log::configure`), with a fresh diagnostic session and no cached answer, and waits out a cancelled idle check, recording none. Appends are whole buffers under an exclusive advisory lock; path ids never repeat in a process. Owners: apps/solid-typefacts/src/{file_regions,overlay,project,inputs}.rs, rust/crates/solid-facts-backend/src/{daemon,daemon_resolution}.rs, rust/crates/solid-reactive-ir/src/role_log.rs, rust/crates/typefacts (`BuildInputs`), scripts/fuzz/{exec/src/main.rs,roles.mjs,warm-identity.mjs}.

k mutually calling local functions took 2.1-3.7 s at k = 8, 38-52 s at k = 9, over five minutes at k = 10 (release, f31337fa8); now 30-34 ms at k = 8-9, 50-54 ms at k = 12, 42 MB. - Write-walk caller fold (`execution_role/write_components.rs`, `region_fold`). Path-dependent in general (a function whose callers are all on the path folds to nothing: a Hamiltonian-path question), but in a region of plain-call edges into plainly folding loops a rejecting entry ends every fold above it and a revisit reaches no function or entry the first visit did not, so the paths' first rejection is a depth-first search's with one visited set; without one, `Unknown` is absorbing, so each fold stops at its first `Unknown`, and where none can be `Unknown` the region folds to the role its first entries lead to. Each call site is placed once (root walk state plus its own function), recording every `visiting` query (`visit_contains`, `visit_insert`); the walk follows paths if a placement asked about another region function, an answered entry is written in one, an edge's loop is not plain or the fallback would place its `Unknown`, or after 2^20 steps.

## ADR 0560 — Path-dependent walks end at a bound; the helper climb and site reach answer exactly
ADR 0546 left walks exponential where its folds do not apply (ed30c5738): `untrack(() => fj(n - 1))` edges among k local functions (38.7 s at k = 8), alias closures `const gj = () => fj(n - 1); gj();`, site reach with 64 or more functions (over 40 s at k = 8), and a helper climb whose one rejecting call is its helper's last.

Where a reached call rejects (ADR 0546's ball), a helper's climb rejects exactly when a path within its remaining calls, over helpers not in progress, reaches a call whose own answer (`handed_tail`) rejects; a shortest such path repeats no helper, so breadth-first search decides it (`rejection_within`). - Site reach (`site_reach.rs`). A derivation holds in progress only functions the answer may read: the one written around it and those holding a call, render or reference of its name or its class's name. Where those are under 64 and all the program's own (`reads_few`), no derivation reaches the depth limit, so the least fixed point answers at any program size. Elsewhere the fixed point answers only functions it proves run (the limit only adds `true` to a monotone system); the rest derive depth first.

A write walk with its own `visiting` set counts region and path steps (`bounded_walk`; a nested walk with a fresh set counts its own, so an answer is a function of where the walk starts); past the bound it answers `Unknown`, which no flow fallback replaces; a climb answers `Unknown`, which no hand-off tail replaces; a site-reach query stopping at the bound or depth limit answers every later question undecided (`Reach::Undecided`, `function_runs` true): a violation there is uncertifiable with its own message (`UnreachedSite::undecided`), a cleanup-handle call unplaced, an owner operation kept. untrack k = 8 38.7 → 3.3 s, each write U.
Counters `BuildTimings::bounded_walk_peak` and `bounded_walks_exhausted` (also in `SOLID_CHECKER_TIMINGS` output). The complexity ladder builds these shapes at k = 2..12 within the cubic envelope, no walk at its bound; `write_walk_strategies_process` lowers the bound to 2^10 (test hook `bound_walks`) and requires each walk to end within 2·bound, work under 8·k²·bound, no write to come out clean, and an undecided query to leave its sites undecided.

The linker computes it over the whole output, so a changed binary changes it; an image without exactly one build id of 16 to 64 bytes (8-byte `--build-id=fast`, big-endian or 32-bit, a malformed note) keeps the digest. Premise, as on macOS: nothing rewrites a linked checker's code and keeps its build id.

<a id="adr-0592"></a>
## ADR 0592 — The fuzz executor hands a slot the program its daemon can update
A warm slot's daemon (ADR 0543) updates its program in place when the next has the same file names and tsconfig.json, else reopens it (new producer, full reparse): 52.9 ms of daemon and producer CPU against 26.1. In grid order a third of programs differ from the previous (78% `App.tsx` alone, the rest add `helpers.ts`, `lib.ts` or `solid-api.ts`), and with as many slots as step-1 workers each worker got back the slot it had freed. Now a worker takes the oldest of the first 64 queued requests whose shape (`project_shape`: names and tsconfig) a free slot last held, else the oldest; a slot prefers a request of its shape; no request is passed over more than four times the workers. Only preparation order moves, never an answer.

A warm fuzz check started about 100 daemon threads (11 checks traced: 1,138 clones), 77 in `base::memo::each_shard`, which gave the 16 graph shards to min(cores, 16) fresh threads at every flush and graph sync however small, each re-reading the cgroup quota (`available_parallelism`, uncached in `analysis_parallelism`). Now `each_shard` stays on the caller's thread below `SHARD_THREADS_MIN_WORK` (4,096) edges or nodes, as `parallel_slice_results` and `parallel_balanced_results` do below 256 and 64 items, and the core count is read once per process. The inline arm is the existing sequential (wasm32-wasip1) one; results keep shard order and each item touches its own shard. A random 6,000-node graph keeps the worker arm tested against a fresh store.

At a check per core (24 slots on 12 vCPUs warm), each check still spread its reactive IR, producer per-file passes and tsrs pool over every core: thread starts, futex wake-ups and `sched_yield` from 24 pools of 12. The executor now sets `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_WORKERS`, `SOLID_TYPEFACTS_PER_FILE_WORKERS` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` to 1 (`CHECK_WORKERS`) unless its caller set them; the checker's own `tsrs` type checks keep their threads. Answers do not depend on worker counts (`context_census_workers_process`; full JSON of 600 programs equal).

## ADR 0597 — A grid prepares two chunks ahead
`matrix.mjs` and `legal.mjs` prepared chunk k + 1 (150 programs) only after chunk k's preparation answered, so each chunk's end drained the executor's queue until the slowest check answered (VM about 70% busy, caches warm), and ADR 0592's slots took whatever came last. `preparedAhead` (pipeline.mjs) keeps chunks k + 1 and k + 2 preparing while chunk k finishes; stages and row order are unchanged.

Evidence: scripts/fuzz/README.md ("Demoting saturated recall values"). Nightly audits are lean; Sunday and manual `recall: full` runs are full; a report is compared only with an earlier audit of its mode. Trade: a defect only a demoted value shows is found weekly, not nightly; `rediscovery.json` `fullIds` pins such programs.

A `createEffect` apply, a `createRenderEffect` apply after its first run, a `createReaction` callback and an effect bundle's `error` member run from the queue's drain, and rc.17's `flush()` drains on its caller's stack without setting an owner (`dist/dev-shared.js:2646-2721`), so a flush under an owner runs them owned. On the fast runtime, after a `createEffect`, a `flush()` in a component body, memo compute or root body let a `createEffect` in the apply raise nothing (an SC4001 false positive) and made a write there throw `REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE` (a certified false clean); in a handler or `runWithOwner(null, …)` the throws stay. The dialect names those callbacks (`callback_runs_drained_by_flush`); a census (`indexes/flush_census.rs`) lists every reference to the flush primitive. A call does not veto where its position proves no owner (the dispatch census's classes, ADRs 0356, 0435, 0437, 0438, and a compiler-reported inline element handler: the owner graph's unowned edge; handler classes only without the dispatch veto) or where the effect-phase walk proves it runs only on a `createEffect` apply of the same `solid-js` copy (the running queue drains nothing). Any other call, or non-call reference (`run(flush)`), vetoes program-wide (`FlushVetoAnswer` memo, `FlushVeto` section, kept as ADR 0450 keeps the dispatch veto; a debug tripwire refuses reads while the census computes). Under the veto the drained callback's unowned edge is `DrainedByFlush` (possibly owned, never proven, and leaving any region written around the call; a plain conditional edge would let a `createRoot` around the effect answer for the apply, a false clean); SC6002 is uncertifiable; a write in such a callback, a layer it runs in place, a render effect's later run, an apply's returned cleanup (a rerun runs it from the drain), a bundle member or with an apply role is unplaced (SC2001 uncertifiable). Not built: narrowing to effects created before an owned flush can run (cross-component order is not modelled). Not vetoed: a flush in dependency code, packages analyzed as source included (premise; `@solidjs/router`'s `preload` calls one), via a computed member or an escaped namespace object. Fuzzer: `FLUSH_DRAIN_CONTEXTS`. Fixtures `flush-veto-*`; eight older snapshots moved to uncertifiable, none to clean. Review added: `onSettled` called without an owner takes the same queue, so under the veto its callback is possibly owned (`QueuedLeafDrained`) and its writes unplaced (probed: a `missing-owner` false positive, a write false clean); a `flush()` in a parameter default runs at its function's call, not at module evaluation (in the dispatch census too). An `onSettled` under an owner is a true leaf, but the write role cannot tell call sites apart, so under the veto it is unplaced too, a recall cost (`leaf-owner`, `setter-in-root-*`, `write-scope-roots-*`, `eslint-plugin-corpus` move to uncertifiable).

## ADR 0615 — A defect fails where it is created
Owner's question: find an issue when it is created. Of the ledger's 72 rows and this stack, 7,264 flagged rows all fail on main (only `flush-*` shapes new), found hours to three months after the cause (ADR 0585: `named_callback_execution_role`, 2026-07-31, found 11-03). Causes: (1) cells are hand tables per code, so a context reached a code only by a slice's choice: 2,334 of 4,100 code × context pairs had none (`memo-async`, from 10-27, reached SC2001 on 11-04: 16,528 false positives). (2) Second codes (tallied since ADR 0498), `not-fired` rows (judged no finding, no second code computed) and another rule's violation at a site (never judged) were measured but failed nothing. (3) No generated program ran per pull request: CI and `make verify` ran the fuzzer's unit tests only, `make fuzz-smoke` ran by hand, and `existsSync` skipped 60 of 64 ledger rows, which named a grid with no manifest; ADR 0586's regression (5820be453) lived five hours to a hand run. (4) A fix reached one of parallel paths (ADR 0614). (5) A premise written down, not exercised: the flush premise, ADR 0483 to ADR 0613.
Built: **the census** (`mx-census`, `matrix.mjs censusCells`), a default grid of every pair no cell lists, in plain shapes, judged as any grid, so a new context or code meets everything in the run it lands, with no table entry (excluded, with reasons: a thrown code a promise swallows, pairs halting before the driver); alone it caught none of the store misses, which are in listed pairs. **The covering samples** (`cover.mjs`, owner decision): a greedy cover of every pair of axis values over the whole enumeration of misuse, legal and pair grids (`side` is an axis), computed from the shapes, so a new value enters the next sample. Tiers: per pull request, the census and all pairs at a fixed seed (`fuzz-pr.yml`, `make fuzz-smoke`), so a failure belongs to it; nightly or before a merge, pairs within each code, nightly on a seed of the day (`make fuzz-premerge`); weekly or before a release, the full grids. **The ledger's programs are required** in every sample. **A capped oracle** (`--runtime-diff-cap`): 25 a grid, the census's stratified by code and outcome (a census took 878 s, 870 in the oracle). **The judge reads all it saw**: a claiming violation on a `not-fired` site that ran, another rule's violation at a site, a second code on a `not-fired` program. **`store-link`** read variants for SC1001 and SC1002.
A greedy cover cut the owner's random-order sample of mx rows from about 8,800 to 7,350 programs with no loss. With the ledger's 1,508 programs the pull-request sample is 13,099. Not yet run on a runner: 16,300 programs at 6.4-11.4 a second (cold, cached) is 24-42 minutes before the build. The one category the top tier ever misses, 24 programs of `pos-flush-fn` × `dynamic`, is a four-way interaction; `context × mount × layer` caught it on half the seeds.
Not built: test selection from role arms (only `execution_role` and owner arms are tagged, so ADR 0614's member path would select nothing); a premise ledger (no fact marks prose as a premise: review's job); `context × mount × layer` in the cover (29% more programs for a category caught on half the seeds).

A hint that the runtime does not warn excused its finding on its own word; `window.mjs` now measures it: a control run reads one signal per counter, and rc.17 warns there exactly when a strict-read window is open (24 `pos-flush-fn` × `dynamic` rows: none; mounted plainly: all). No evidence excuses nothing. The pair grids join the audit. The sample found three older false positives, `delete store.key` past an await; the per-code tier, a pending read through a helper in a handler's `onSettled` proven SC5001 (332 of 1,284 programs on main), which now takes the owner fixed point's `onSettled` gate.

<a id="adr-0616"></a>
## ADR 0616 — The runtime oracle runs its cases in `feedback batch` processes
Each oracle worker is one `feedback batch` process (packages/cli README), not a `feedback run` per case. A fresh run spent about 1.1 of a case's 3.2 s on case-independent work: Node and tooling imports (0.3 s), two Chromium binary hashes (0.13 s), Chromium's launch (0.23 s), parsing TypeScript lib declarations (0.25 s), process exit (0.3 s); the page's own pauses (1 s) are semantic and stay. A batch shares loaded tooling, one Chromium process (a context per case), the browser's pin (hashed at open and close, file stamp checked after every run, ADR 0600's trust) and the execution cache's harness and tooling identities; each run keeps its own snapshot, native analysis, Vite server, context and input pins, and starts from a fresh run's environment and working directory (Vite sets NODE_ENV). A process retires after a failed run, an application Vite config (application code in the process), a changed working directory, a lost browser or a context left open; one refusing its close takes its cases with it. Declaration files are parsed once per process, keyed by path, options and bytes. 741 fixture cases (c8, cache off): identical rows, 324 s against 840 s; 20 lg programs serially: 39.7 s against 64.9 s, and 10.6 s against 27.0 s on execution-cache hits, with the same cache keys in both modes. `--session per-case` keeps the old shape.

<a id="adr-0617"></a>
## ADR 0617 — The oracle samples are split over the run's runners by size
`audit.mjs pick` gives each grid's oracle sample one job, then adds parts one at a time to the grid with the largest part while the run has fewer than 20 jobs (the account's concurrent runners) and that part exceeds 200 programs (every N-th id, as before), replacing the by-name map (mx-recall 4, lg-recall 2). A program took 1.0 to 2.3 s of a job's differential, the same code 1.6x apart between runners, so a part costs its size, not its grid. That run never exceeded 20 concurrent jobs and started shards in no index order (shard 0 was 29th), so ordering large parts first would not keep them out of the queue; the budget does. Its samples give 20 jobs of at most 439 programs (census 6, both recall grids 3), about 17 minutes on the slowest runner before ADR 0616; the floor leaves a lean night's runners unused rather than add jobs whose setup and warm-state artifact cost more than they save. A changed part count makes that job's warm state cold once.

## ADR 0618 — Main's CI builds, and does not retest, a tree a pull request passed on
A pull request's passing CI run uploads `ci-tested-tree-<tree>`, the tree of the merge ref it tested. A push to main looks it up by its commit's tree and accepts it only from a fully successful `ci.yml` `pull_request` run in this repository. Then `rust-engine` and `wasm-package` only build (clippy, `cargo test --no-run`, the debug checker, the WASM package), writing main's caches; `wasm-parity` and `scripts-and-cli` are skipped; `rust-package` is unchanged. A missing, expired or unaccepted record runs everything, as does a merge after main moved (a different tree). CI cancels a pull request's superseded run, never main's. Owner: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

The flip's rule asks for a clear uncertifiable with a named blocker, but only rows the flip added had one: 9,216 of the corpus's 18,502 carried a function's name or nothing in `analysisContext`, the reason only in wording (SC1001 4,792, SC2001 3,220, SC9012 558, SC2008 237). `project_finding` now derives the blocker from the row's own holes, in the order the proof meets them; each backend escalation (`instance-field-run-unplaced`, `component-identity-unproven`, the four site-reach answers, `binding-before-initialization`, `compiler-refused-file`) names its own, and a final pass names a row from its rule. `proof-step-unnamed` is the last resort, not a blocker: `check.mjs` fails on it or any unnamed row, `scripts/flip/blockers.mjs` likewise over a sweep. The old context stays as detail, `blocker:context`. No finding moves.

## ADR 0683 — A method a project subclass may replace is not the standard one
TypeFacts resolves `held.forEach` to `Array.forEach` when `held: number[]`, and every in-place, fresh-stack and carrier proof trusts that, so `class Late extends Array` overriding `forEach` with a microtask left a violation Chrome contradicts (`d05 d06 g24`). A class extending `Array`, `Map`, `Set`, `WeakMap`, `WeakSet` or `Promise` (global, `globalThis.` member, or `const` alias) raises a recorded hazard per declared member, or for every member if a key is computed. While raised, `resolved_callee_call` answers nothing for that container's method, in the lookup and the memo context, so those proofs fail closed (uncertifiable). Per member, not container: the corpus's `ogl` vectors extend `Array`, and a container-wide veto moved 3 true SC8014 violations and 279 rows on methods no subclass replaces. An array-literal receiver is exempt, locally proven no subclass instance. Limits: a mixin-made class or a patched prototype raises nothing; these are premises, like `Object.prototype` writes. Cost: +68 uncertifiable in `app-game`, all but one SC9012, where classes overriding `Map` and `Set` members leave plain maps unproven; a receiver bound to `new Map()` could be proved like an array literal.

So `saved = C`, `me={C}`, `<C>{C({ run: setN })}</C>` and `<Dynamic component={C} run={setN} />` inside `<C>` handed the component on and stayed certified; Chrome throws (H-D5). Now only the name and the element's own opening and closing tag are exempt; any other reference escapes, and the reads are uncertifiable. The census's JSX row rests on this.

Those three no longer count. They matter because `Object.prototype`'s members are the only names `tsc` accepts beyond a closed literal's own slots.
