## ADR 0966 — Every flush site is accounted for, per code (batch 11, slice 5)
A flush no producer rowed was a clean nobody accounted for: SC2006 returns from its arm with no row when the program steps no action callback, SC2008 when the program defers none or the walks answer "placed off", SC3001's leaf walk when the flush is not in a leaf callback, and every one of those exits read the same whether a fact ruled the code out or the walk gave up (`unplaced_blocker` answers "placed off" for a function no call edge reaches, a body that may be a component and an owner set around the call as well as for a proof). `flush_accounting.rs` (its own typed endings and its own universe, like ADR 0838's and ADR 0886's passes; run once after the site accounting, over the final rows) lists the flush census's references (`render` and `hydrate` are listed for its veto and answer none of the three questions: each code asks its own producer's question of the primitive, SC2006 the dialect's `throws_inside_action_step`, SC2008 its `warns_inside_effect_phase`, SC3001 the leaf walk's own operation kind, `cleanup::files_as_flush_operation`, one mapping with `forbidden_operation_kind`) and asks, per code it applies to, whether the site ends in a row of that code's rule (a violation, an uncertifiable row, a leaf operation), an SC9012, the compiler's discard, or a typed reason (`FlushSafe`); else the code's own uncertifiable row, never a violation: SC2006 `flush-in-action-unaccounted`, SC2008 `flush-in-effect-unaccounted`, SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` (blockers.rs).

The reasons are the producers' own silent exits written down, each a fact of the program or of the site's census class and nothing else: the three program censuses (`NoSteppedAction`: no primitive the project names runs a callback as an action's steps; `NoDeferringPrimitive`: none defers one to a later flush; `NoLeafScope`: none runs one under a leaf owner), the census class of the caller that puts the flush on an empty stack (`FreshStack`, `AwaitContinuation`, `ModuleInitialization`, and `TestRunner`, assigned only to a flush written directly in a callback a reviewed runner schedules: `direct_callback_contains`), and `NeverRuns` (`SiteReach`). Owner ruling 5a (2026-11-12): a give-up is not a reason. None of the walk-derived exits is named (`unplaced_blocker`, the effect-phase origin, the climb that stopped), and neither are the census classes that may stand inside a step (`DetachedOwner` keeps the action depth, `TestHelper` may be called from a step inside a test, an `EventHandler`'s delivery may be dispatched from a step) nor `EffectApply`: those sites stay uncertifiable. Owner-approved (2026-11-12): the pass and its ids (`flush_accounting.account.<end>`) join the list of passes with their own typed endings (`site_accounting.rs` test), and the pass joins the proof lint's `PRODUCERS`; it names no primitive and ends no walk in a silent slot, so it needs no baseline entry.

*Measured* (34 projects, release, slice 0's candidate log and the pass): the census lists 1,799 references, 1,481 end in nothing today (1,452 in test files). Rows on: standard U 121,998 to 122,413 (+415: SC3001 310, SC2008 103, SC2006 2), development build +695 (SC3001 316, SC2006 276, SC2008 103: the packages analyzed as source name `action`, so `NoSteppedAction` no longer holds), 0 removed, V unchanged. Ablation (`SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE=all` or a reason's id): each reason is witnessed by a fixture (`flush-universe`, `-no-action`, `-bare`, `-test-runner`). Not done: the `SiteSilence` per-code endings of slice 4 will fold this pass in; `FlushServerBuildSelectsNone` (a server build) is not named.

*Review of #213 (2026-11-12), B1 and B2, fixed here.* A census class says where the function around the flush runs; it ends the three codes only when it is a statement about the flush's own stack. (B2) The flush is written in the body of its function, not in a parameter list: a default value runs wherever its function is called (`late = (x = flush()) => x` in a timer's callback, `late()` in an effect's apply: FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK in Chrome), which the class of the code around the nested function does not say; so no class reason for a site in a parameter list (`owners::in_parameter_list`), `ModuleInitialization` excepted. (B1) For `FreshStack` and `TestRunner`, no function around the flush is a named function expression whose name is used (`setTimeout(function tick() { flush(); … tick(true) })`: the name is bound inside, so the code using it enters `tick` again on the stack of its own host, an action's step or an effect's apply: FLUSH_IN_ACTION in Chrome); `AwaitContinuation` needs only the first. A site that fails either has no reason, so its uncertifiable row. Both were certified on main (no accounting) and signed here as `FlushSafe::FreshStack`; the fuzz cells `fc-*` (`scripts/fuzz/fc-shapes.mjs`) found four false cleans on the PR head (the old build fails `make fuzz-focus`), none on the fix; `scripts/fuzz/patterns/flushclass` and the fixtures `flush-universe-class` and `flush-universe-test-runner` hold the shapes.

*Re-review of #213 (same day), N1 to N3, fixed here.* The same cause in three more shapes: code written in the scheduler's callback that does not run when the callback runs. `callback_runs_it` (one function for `FreshStack` and `TestRunner`) asks, of what is written inside the call that hands the callback over: no parameter list holds the flush, no function is a generator (N2: `[1].map(function* () { flush() })` only creates the generator object, `.next()` runs the body on whatever stack calls it) or a named function expression its own code uses (B1), and no class field initializer (N1: an instance's construction runs it), JSX element or compiler tracked region (N3: a prop written in JSX is a getter that runs where the component reads it) holds it, the last three by `runs_with_its_function`, the predicate `continuation_function` already asks of the code after an await. A function or region written around the call is not asked: the callback still runs from the scheduler. Chrome confirmed three false cleans in an effect's apply on the fix of B1 and B2, and the cells `fc-field-*`, `fc-gencarrier-*`, `fc-jsxprop-*` five (an action's step for the prop, a leaf callback for the generator); none on this fix.

*Second re-review of #213 (same day), N4 and N5, fixed here.* Two more places where the class says less than the proof needs. (N4) `ModuleInitialization` was given unasked: the census gives a flush written directly in the suite body a reviewed runner runs inside its registration (`node:test`'s `describe`, jest-circus, mocha, playwright; ADR 0438) the class of the registration's position, and the class, parameter-list, JSX and field questions had been asked of the registration call, not of the flush. `Late = class { x = flush(); }`, a default value, `<Child v={flush()} />` or a named suite body its own code uses ended all three codes while an instance's construction, a call, a read of `props.v` or a second call of the name ran them elsewhere (Node 24 with the real `node:test` and rc.21 ran the first in an effect's apply and raised FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK; Chrome cannot load `node:test`, so the generator cannot express the shape and the fixture `flush-universe-inline-suite` holds it). `suite_body_runs_it` asks, of everything written inside the outermost registration of the chain, the questions `callback_runs_it` asks (`runs_when_the_call_runs`, one predicate for the three classes); a flush directly in the body, in a nested body or in a named body nothing uses keeps the class. (N5) `callback_runs_it` dropped the resolved call of `fresh_stack_callback_call`, whose documentation says a consumer that relies on the stack must refuse `catch` and `finally`: they run their handler through the receiver's `then` (ECMAScript 27.2.5.1), and a Promise subclass whose `then` runs it at once calls it on the stack of the caller, an effect's apply, an action's step or a leaf callback. A call that `dispatches_through_receiver_then` gives no reason; a plain `Promise`'s `catch` is refused with it (precision lost, three rows a site, none in the corpus). Chrome on the previous head: three false cleans, one per host (`patterns/flushclass/recvthen-*`; cells `fc-recvthen-*`, 42 contexts with their twins); none on this fix. Corpus delta 0 (standard 122,211, development build 142,933): no site is ended by `ModuleInitialization` or `FreshStack` there (all 945 are `TestRunner`). Open, measured only (owner ruling pending, review finding F1): fake timers (`vi.useFakeTimers`, `jest.useFakeTimers`) run a timer's callback on the caller's stack (`vi.runAllTimers()` in an apply), the host premise of every `FreshStack` use and not of this fix.

<a id="adr-0967"></a>
## ADR 0967 — A flush in a function a package nothing here reads may run gets no census reason (batch 11, B3 of the review of #213)
The Fable review of #213 (B3) found a flush the accounting certified on a program census while a package ran it under a step: an installed package whose source the build does not read (a standard build reads none; a development build reads the packages whose manifest names a Solid package) can call `action`, `createEffect` or `createTrackedEffect` itself on a function the project hands it (`runStep(() => { flush(); })`, `action(function* () { cb(); })()` in the package), and nothing in the build's own table shows it. The three program censuses (`NoSteppedAction`, `NoDeferringPrimitive`, `NoLeafScope`) read that table only; Chrome (rc.21) reports FLUSH_IN_ACTION at the flush, while the program names no action, effect or leaf primitive (`probes/p21-dependency-step`, certified on the PR head and on main). Owner ruling, option b, fail closed, no premise (a premise like ADR 0613's dependency-flush premise would say what the package does, which nothing here can know): **a flush in a function a package nothing here reads may run gets no census reason**, so it keeps its uncertifiable row of each code (`flush-in-*-unaccounted`), never silence and never a violation. The class reasons (`FreshStack`, `AwaitContinuation`, `ModuleInitialization`, `TestRunner`, `NeverRuns`) are unchanged: each is a statement about the flush's own stack.

`package_hand_off.rs` answers, per function that owns the flush (the function written around it, each enclosing function too), whether a package nothing here reads may run it. A package runs a function it is handed and a function that function calls, so the question follows the routes a function reaches a package, each by the facts of the program (references and containment by the binder's declarations, never a spelling): the function written as an argument of a call, a `new` or a tagged template's substitution, or inside one (a member of an object literal, a method, an element of an array literal, a branch of a conditional, a spread); a reference to its binding (a declaration, a `const` arrow, a named function expression) written as such an argument, through every `const` copy, assignment and holder, in the file or, through an import, in another; a JSX prop, a spread attribute, a child expression or a `use:` directive of a component the program does not read; a project function's parameter that goes on to any of these (`function wrap(f) { pkg(f) }`, followed with the call graph's exact mapping); a function a project function returns, whose calls evaluate to it (`pkg(make())`, an immediately invoked function); a reflective call that forwards its arguments to its target (`pkg.run.call(null, cb)`, `.apply`, `.bind`, `Reflect.apply`, `Reflect.construct`: the target is known only when it is a project function); and a caller: a function whose exact call edge reaches the function (`pkg(() => helper())`), asked the same way. A function or a JSX element written inside the argument is its own business (`crosses`).

What receives the value decides (owner-approved list, declaration-resolved, no spelling): (1) a **dialect primitive**: the call resolves through `primitive_at_call` to a declaration in a Solid package whose symbol root is in the dialect catalog (ADR 0826); a JSX tag the dialect names is the same; (2) a **reviewed fresh-stack scheduler**, standard-library declarations only: `queueMicrotask`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `requestIdleCallback` and their `WindowOrWorkerGlobalScope`, `AnimationFrameProvider` and `Window` member forms, `Promise.then`/`catch`/`finally`, `Scheduler.postTask`, `MediaSession.setActionHandler`, the `IntersectionObserver`, `ResizeObserver`, `MutationObserver`, `PerformanceObserver` and `ReportingObserver` constructors; (3) a **reviewed test runner's registration**, by the callee's identity (`reviewed_test_runner_registration`: `test_runner_callback` without the suite-body timing it also answers, which is `Unproven` for `bun:test` and where a registration has declarations in two runners): the callee's root identifier resolves only to declarations in an installed declaration file of `vitest`, `@vitest/runner`, `bun-types/test.d.ts`, `@types/node/test.d.ts`, `@playwright/test`, `playwright/types/test.d.ts`, `@jest/globals`, `@types/jest` or `@types/mocha`, is one of `test it describe suite beforeEach afterEach beforeAll afterAll before after`, possibly through `only skip todo concurrent sequential parallel serial fails fail fixme slow describe each for skipIf runIf`; nothing else of those packages is exempt (`expect`, `vi.*` and `waitFor` are not); (4) the **standard library**: the resolved declaration is a default-library declaration (`Array.prototype.*`, the `Promise` executor, `JSON`, `Map`); (5) a **project function**: a function with a body the call graph resolves exactly (`project_callee_at_parameter`), whose parameter is followed, and a DOM element (an intrinsic JSX tag: its handlers run on the browser's own stack); a project declaration no function body defines (a function-typed parameter or field: it may hold a package's function) is not one; (6) a **package the build reads as source**: the declaration's file is among the analyzed files (`in_dependency_source`), as in the development build with the Solid plugin. A declaration in a package the build does not read (a `.d.ts` under `node_modules`) and a callee nothing resolves get no census reason.

Not followed, named in `docs/open-work.md`: a value kept in a collection or a property and read elsewhere (`handlers.add(cb)`, `handlers.forEach(pkg.run)`), a method of a class whose instance is handed, an assignment into an object a package exports, a project component's props (the component's body is analyzed, the props object is not followed), a class constructor of the project that stores a callback, and an export a framework enters from outside. *Measured* (34 projects, release): standard U 122,211 to **122,236 (+25**: SC2006 24, SC3001 1; 0 removed, V unchanged), development build 142,933 to **142,943 (+10)**; corpus time unchanged. The arguments, references, members, JSX, parameters and callers cost **+12 standard, +0 development build** (the packages that name a Solid package are read as source, so their receivers are known): a callback handed to `expect(() => { …; flush() }).not.toThrow()` (compass-ui, 2), to a function-typed parameter (`body(store, settled)`, 1), to `Sortable.create` (app-game `createFlip.ts`, 4), to a UI package's `<Button onClick>` (1), to `createEventListener` and `access` (folder-tabs, kui, probus-hk). The route of a returned function costs **+13 standard, +10 development build**, all test doubles in kui (`fakeStream()`-style factories that return an object literal whose methods call `flush()`, handed to `expect(…)` or to a project function that passes it on) and two helpers in solid-groove: the object is the value of the call, and handing any member of it hands the object. They are precision lost, not defects the corpus reports (a test double's `connect()` is called by the test), and the one route the owner's list did not name; dropping it gives back 13 and 10 rows. A first build that took `test_runner_callback`'s answer for the runner's identity gave +169 on the first routes: 147 of them were flushes written in the `describe` bodies of compass-ui's `store.test.ts`, because `describe` has two declarations there (vitest's and `@types/jest`'s) whose suite-body timings differ, which `SuiteBodyRun::Unproven` answers with nothing; the registration is a reviewed runner's by its declaration all the same (`reviewed_test_runner_registration`, the callee's identity without the timing; the fixture's `Bun.test.tsx` pins it with `bun:test`, whose suite bodies are `Unproven` by design). Chrome (rc.21, real oracle): the twelve patterns `patterns/pkghand/*` (a package `fz-step` that names no Solid package) are false cleans on the previous head's build and fine on this one, and the cells `ph-*` (`scripts/fuzz/ph-shapes.mjs`: thirteen routes by three hosts, 78 contexts with their twins) give 39 false cleans on the previous head's build (13 per code) and 0 on this one (39 recall gaps; the 39 twins uncertifiable, never silent). Fixtures: `flush-universe-package-hand-off` (72 rows: 24 handed sites by every route, the package named through a namespace and an alias, a returned function and a reflective call, and the silent twins: the standard library, a project function, a DOM element, a shadowing local, a reviewed runner's registration); `impostor-withheld-no-run` (+2: its program-wide veto withholds every `forEach`, so their callee is a callee nothing resolves) and `rc21-anchor-listener-forms` (+2: a `.call` on a variable that holds the DOM method forwards to a target nothing resolves).

*F1 of the review of #213 (owner ruling 2026-11-12), added here.* `FreshStack` says the host runs the callback from an empty stack. A fake clock replaces the host's timers (`setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, and with jest's modern timers `queueMicrotask`) with ones the test advances, so the callback runs on the stack of whoever advances the clock, which may be an action's step or an effect's apply. Confirmed in vitest 4.1.7 on solid-js 2.0.0-rc.21 (development build, jsdom): a real `setTimeout` callback's `flush()` runs on an empty stack and raises nothing; the same callback run by `vi.advanceTimersByTime(10)` inside an `action(function* () { … })` step throws `[FLUSH_IN_ACTION]`. **A program that installs fake timers gets no `FreshStack` reason**: every flush a scheduler's callback holds keeps its uncertifiable row of each code (`flush-in-action-unaccounted`, `flush-in-effect-unaccounted`, `leaf-operation-unaccounted`), never a violation. Only `FreshStack` is withheld; `TestRunner` (the runner calls the callback), `AwaitContinuation` (the promise job queue no fake clock replaces) and `ModuleInitialization` stand. The ruling named the file; the census is the program's, because the clock is global to the run: a test reaches it through a helper another file declares (`useClock()`), and the flush is written in the code under test, not the test file. It is read once per build and only when a scheduler's callback would end a flush (`flush_accounting.rs`, `FakeTimers`). The installer is recognized by the compiler's resolution, never the spelling alone: a member's or a destructured key's property that resolves to a declaration named `useFakeTimers` in an installed declaration file of `vitest`, `@types/jest`, `@jest/environment`, `@jest/globals` or `bun-types/test.d.ts` (path components, as ADR 0438's runner list is; `vi.useFakeTimers()`, `jest.useFakeTimers()`, `bun:test`'s `jest`, a call through any typed handle, `vi["useFakeTimers"]()`, `const { useFakeTimers: install } = vi`); or the same name written as a member of, or destructured from, an object such a library declares (the entity of a property that is not called is not in the table, and the one a shorthand key names is the local binding: `const install = vi.useFakeTimers`, `vi.useFakeTimers.call(vi)`, `(vi as any).useFakeTimers()`, `const { useFakeTimers } = vi`), the object resolved through its import aliases to a reviewed library's declaration. The unit test `a_fake_timer_installer_is_a_reviewed_library_declaration` pins the declaration list; the fixtures `flush-universe-fake-timers` (vitest through a helper file: nine rows; its `real` twin, `vi.useRealTimers()` and `vi.advanceTimersByTime`, none; the `jest`, `bun` and `destructured` variants: three each) pin the rule, and nine probes of spellings (alias, `.call`, string key, renamed import, pattern key, namespace import, `vitest`, a cast, a typed handle) agree. *Measured* (34 projects, release, against #216's head before this change): standard 122,236 to 122,236, development build 142,943 to 142,943, **0 rows move**: the corpus's 945 sites that end on a class reason (every one on `TestRunner`, 152 of them in five test files that call `vi.useFakeTimers`) end on no `FreshStack` at all, and the programs that install fake timers (compass-ui, dashiboard-ui, kui) hold none either. The fuzz grid cannot express it (the oracle's page runs in Chrome, where vitest and jest do not load): an `outside` entry in `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json` says so. Named misses, each a decision not built (`docs/open-work.md`): another library's installer (sinon's `useFakeTimers`, `@sinonjs/fake-timers`' `install`, jasmine's `clock().install()`, `node:test`'s `mock.timers.enable()`), a configuration that enables fake timers without a call (jest's `fakeTimers: { enableGlobally: true }`), a value read through a handle no reviewed library declares (`const clock = vi; const install = clock.useFakeTimers`), a destructured parameter, and a receiver the compiler types `any` that is not written as the reviewed object (`const loose = vi as any; loose.useFakeTimers()`).

*The flip (the Fable review of #216, owner ruling 2026-11-12), added here.* A review of #216 (head a0c17af80, BLOCKED) probed fourteen programs that stay silent where a package runs the flush as an action's step; each is a false clean on `main` too, five of them routes the PR did not list. The cause was one default: `position` answered "not handed" for every context it did not recognize (an iterable, a receiver, a `yield`, a class field, `this.x =`), and a value that is called asked nothing of the function that owns the call. The ruling: **a value counts as handed unless a fact of the program proves where it goes**, so the flush keeps its uncertifiable row of each code. `package_hand_off.rs` reads each reference of a function, and of each holder it is copied into, at its position:

- *a call* (`f()`, `new C()`, a tag, a JSX tag, `f.call(…)`, `holder.run()` of a member the project declares) runs it on the stack of the function the call is written in, so the owner is asked (the review's N-B: `[1].forEach(cb)`, `untrack(cb)`, `call(cb)` with `call(f) { f() }` inside a step a package runs);
- *an argument* is judged by its receiver's declaration: a dialect primitive and the standard library's inline callbacks run it where the call is written (the owner is asked); a reviewed fresh-stack scheduler, a DOM listener's registration and a reviewed runner's registration run it elsewhere and keep nothing; an exact project callee goes on in its parameter (a component's props are parameter 0, a `use:` directive's accessor is parameter 1, a reflective call's forwarded arguments are shifted by the thisArg, `Reflect.apply(f, …)` runs `f` inline: the review's E1); a package the build reads as source is known; the rest is handed: a collection's insertion, a standard call the argument-behavior table does not list (`Promise.resolve`, `Object.assign`, `Array.of`: they may return or copy the value), a package nothing reads, a spread, a callee nothing resolves;
- *a JSX prop, spread, child or directive* by what the element is: an intrinsic element is the DOM's, `Dynamic` is the component its `component` prop names (a string is an intrinsic tag, a project function is that component, anything else is handed: E2), a project component's props are its first parameter (E3), a package read as source is known, any other is handed;
- *the initializer of a binding, the value of an assignment, a `return`* goes on in every read of the holder (the file's and its importers'); an assignment into an import, `this` or a call's result is handed; a function that returns the value is itself asked, since a package that runs it may call what it returns (N-A: `pkg(() => cb)`);
- *a member* `holder.slot` is the member's own value, `holder.run()` runs a member whose property symbol the project declares where it is called, any other method of a holder (`list.forEach(pkg.run)`) may pass its members on and is handed, and a write through the holder takes nothing out;
- *an operand nothing takes* (the whole operand of `typeof`, `===` or an expression statement) is not handed; **anything else is**.

A function is also handed when written in a class (an instance, a subclass or `this` may hand it on from where nothing here follows: r2a), when exported from a program whose boundary is open (code this build cannot see may enter it; a binding it exports is read by such code), and when its module's namespace escapes with no name the analysis can read (`runNs(NS)`: the namespace census of ADR 0347, N-C). A closed boundary is the owner's declared premise (ADR 0193), so an export nothing in a closed program enters keeps the reasons (it never runs).

*Measured* (34 projects, release, against #216's head): standard U 122,236 to **122,294 (+58**, all SC2006 `flush-in-action-unaccounted`), development build 142,943 to **142,943 (+0)**. The open-boundary export rule is **1** of the 58 (kui `feature-alerts/src/fixtures.tsx`; switched off, the other 57 stand). The 57 are one kui test file, `feature-messages/src/messages.test.tsx`: the helper `mount(component)` puts `component` in the holder `dispose` (`const dispose = render(component, container)`: a call's result may hold its argument), the closure it returns calls `dispose()`, `screen()` spreads that object into `{ ...mounted, fake, session }`, and a test does `const { fake, dispose } = screen(); expect(fake.urls)` with vitest's `expect` (a package nothing reads, not exempt by the owner's list). The holder-following is field-insensitive, so every callback handed to `mount(…)` is judged handed; no package step runs there at run time, so these are precision lost (named in `docs/open-work.md`; the cut is a field-sensitive destructuring of a returned object literal). `make coverage`: 36 existing fixture snapshots add 362 uncertifiable rows (SC3001 161, SC2006 126, SC2008 75; none removed): the flushes written in exported functions of fixtures that carry no `.solid-checker/runtime.json`, so an open boundary; each README says so.

*Evidence.* The review's fourteen probes were silent on #216's build and keep their three rows now (`rv-r1a`, `r1b`, `r1c`, `r2a`, `r3`, `r4`, `n1`, `n2`, `n3a`, `n3b`, `n3c`, `n4` with the real `@solidjs/web` `Dynamic`, `n5`, `n6`); the owner-approved twins (the standard library's, a project function's, a DOM element's, a shadowing local, a reviewed runner's) stay silent; the 49 earlier probes are unchanged but `x-collection` (a named miss of #216, now handed). Chrome (rc.21, the real oracle): the thirteen new `ph-*` routes by three hosts (`set`, `forof`, `recv`, `resolve`, `class`, `assign`, `props`, `getter`, `reflect`, `inline`, `param`, `untrack`, `dynamic`) are **39 false cleans on #216's build (13 per code), 0 on the flip's** (their 39 legal twins: 39 clean, now uncertifiable); `patterns/pkghand/namespace-step`: a false clean on #216's build, fine on the flip's. Three rediscovery entries (13 ids per code) and two `outside` entries (the namespace route: the cells cannot place a second module's export; an open-boundary export: Chrome cannot enter an export from outside). Fixtures: `flush-universe-package-hand-off-flip` (45 rows over fifteen handed sites, eight silent twins; `variants/open`: three rows against the closed parent's silent `Unreferenced`). Named misses, each a decision not built: a field-insensitive holder (above); a class's functions are handed whole (a flush in a method keeps its row whether or not its instance reaches a package); an export of a closed program that only a framework enters; a standard call the table does not list hands its function arguments; a destructured parameter is read through its pattern's names.
*Causes A–E of the review of #217 (batch 11).* Containment is not a hand-off proof: a context places a value only along a path that carries it (parentheses, TypeScript wrappers, conditional arms, logical operands, a comma's last operand, array elements, object property values and spreads). A dialect primitive's arguments are carried too: `action(step)` returns a function that runs the step. A receiver inside an initializer (`const rs = [cb].map(f)`), an iterable, a template part or an operand of `yield` or `await` is handed unless another fact proves its destination (A). A non-arrow project function that names `arguments` hands every argument (B). A callback given literally or by an exact reference returns its value to the receiving call's position (`p.then(() => cb).then(runStep)` and `p.then(give).then(runStep)`, C). A separate return-flow walk follows named bindings and copies; an unwritten let and a function declaration use their exact current function, a member requires closed-object selection and an exact function target, and a missing target retains the obligation. An intrinsic element's compiler-recorded `ref` operation runs on the creating stack, including `Dynamic` with a string tag; a package may supply that stack (D). The closing JSX name is the same component reference as its opening name and asks the same render owner (E): `<Card>body</Card>` and `<Card />` have the same answer. E restores proof only when the render owner is proved; a package-run owner still withholds it.

The fixture `flush-universe-package-hand-off-causes` holds 26 handed sites and an unresolved closed-member twin (81 uncertifiable rows), transparent-path and unused-ref twins, and both JSX spellings under an ordinary and a handed render owner. The ph recall cells and eighteen pattern programs retain the runtime counterexamples for A–D. E is an over-refusal: the legal judge accepts uncertifiable results, so the old build cannot fail a grid on that distinction; the fixture and `repro-causes` hold it instead. Unresolved destinations continue to withhold proof, never report a violation.

*Final validation (2026-11-13).* Release `a2529de9413e` (including C by reference): 14,418 misuse and 32,660 legal recall programs, no false clean or false positive; 1,642 Chrome comparisons, no behaviour or attribution difference, none inconclusive. Main `1d0c25ec2` failed the original 46 counterexamples; pre-extension `b635745c2939` failed all twelve added named spellings (four per code), generated by `thenconst`, `thenlet`, `thenfn`, `thenmember`. All retain their three U rows on the final build. Every moved grid row was reviewed; the twelve new legal twins become U too, with no other C-extension moves. Final corpus, 34 projects: development 137,368 to 137,368 U, standard 116,845 to 116,845; no row added or removed, zero errors. E was isolated before the C reference extension: with/without the closing-name condition, all 47,054 then-existing recall programs have identical outcomes and finding details; its own development and standard corpus deltas are also zero. E's closed-boundary controls remain silent, its package-run pair retains six rows. The anonymous closed-member discarded-result twin remains U because its selected symbol has no resolved function-body target; const, unwritten-let and declaration twins are clean. Inventory expansion and the fixture's total +27 rows per census key are owner-approved.

*The review of #222 (B1, D, E; 2026-11-13).* An assignment expression's own value is the value it writes (plain `=`, or a logical assignment): after the target is followed, the expression is asked as any value is, so `const first = (last = cb)`, `first = last = cb` and `[(last = cb)].map(f)` keep their rows (B1: the first two were silent since cause A; the receiver was silent on main too). An intrinsic element (or `Dynamic` with a string tag) inserts its children where it is created, calling a function child as an accessor, and applies a spread's `ref` and `children` there too: its children, its spreads (whose keys are not read) and every attribute the compiler does not record as an event handler are handed where a package may create the element (D; Chrome: FLUSH_IN_ACTION for a spread `ref`, a function child, a `children` attribute and an array child, all silent on main). An element written as a child or a prop of another element, with no function between, is created where that element evaluates it: `<Pkg><Own>x</Own></Pkg>` asks the element's own position, so an unread component's children are handed (E; the closing-name change had silenced the children form, and the bare form was silent on main). Fixture: +9 handed sites (27 rows; an `onClick` spread among them, a precision cost), five silent twins (an `onClick` attribute rests on the compiler's event-handler fact). Routes `chainconst`, `chainassign`, `chainrecv` (three hosts), `spreadref`, `spreadvar`, `childfn`, `framechild`, `framebare` (step host); the PR head fails `make fuzz-focus` on all of them.

*The re-review of #222 (N1).* Code written in an element's prop, spread or child expression, with no function between, runs where that element evaluates it: the compiler makes it a getter of a component's props, so under a component nothing here reads it runs when the package reads the prop (`<Pkg>{[1].map(() => <Own />)}</Pkg>`, `<Pkg>{helper()}</Pkg>`, `<Pkg render={make()} />`, an IIFE, a `ref` in a `map` callback, `void`/`typeof` of an element, a flush written in the expression). `runs_where_written` and a call site ask `evaluated_by_element`: the innermost such element's creation, and for a component its receiver (an unread package hands it; a project component follows its first parameter). The `map` form kept its rows on main and lost them with cause A; the rest were silent on main too (Chrome: FLUSH_IN_ACTION for all eight). Fixture +8 handed sites (24 rows), a project-component twin silent; routes `framemap`, `framecall`, `framerender`, `frameiife`, `framemapref`, `framevoid`, `frametypeof` (step host); a flush written in the expression itself is held by the fixture and a pattern (a route's site is a function's statements).

*The review of #222's check 3 (R1, R2).* An accessor runs where it is read, not where its value goes. A project component's props object holds getters for its prop and child expressions, and an object literal may hold a getter; following either by value missed a read whose value goes nowhere (`runStep(() => { void props.children; })` in a wrapper, `runStep(() => { void p.g; })` with `p` an object with a getter). Both are now also followed as an object of accessors (`Walk::accessors`): every reference of the object asks where it runs, except a props reference written directly in the component's body, which runs where its element is created (already asked); an accessor no literal fact holds is handed. Chrome: FLUSH_IN_ACTION for all eight programs, with the step outside the owned scope (the reviewer's `runStep` in a component body throws ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE first); silent on main and on #222. Fixture `flush-universe-package-hand-off-accessors` (six handed sites, three silent twins); routes `propsread`, `propsrender`, `getterparam` on three hosts. The review of #226: the accessor mode is set on the asking walk (`as_accessors`), whose visited sets it shares, so a getter that names its own object or a self-rendering component ends (B1: each had overflowed the stack); in the component's body a props read is still asked `evaluated_by_element`, and a read in a class body is handed (B2); a literal with an accessor whose own functions name `this` is handed (B3). Routes `selfgetter`, `treerec`, `propsjsx`, `propsclass`, `getterthis`.

*The re-check of #226 (N1, N2).* N1: a method call on an object of accessors binds `this` to it, and the method may read an accessor through `this`, which is no reference of the object: a method written outside the literal (`{ m }`, `m: fn`, an import), one assigned to it later (`o.m = m`), or a prop of a component (`props.pick()`) read a getter in a step the package runs, silent on every build (Chrome: FLUSH_IN_ACTION). In the accessor mode a member that is called (a call, a tagged template; not `new`) now hands the object unless the member resolves, through the program's own exactness (`callback_target`: a member the program may replace, a conditional, a spread or an unresolved callee is not exact), to exactly one function that never names `this` (a file that does not parse names it). N2: one callback returning the flushing function or the object (`[0].map(pick)`) was silent: it is a regression of the one-walk fix (the review had taken it for older, with a binary that was Mac 5's mislabelled copy of the fixed build), whose return-flow sets (`returned_positions`, `returned_bindings`) were kept without the mode, so the function's flow cut the object's; they are keyed by mode and owner as `positions` is. Fixture: +5 handed sites (`outerShorthand`, `outerProperty`, `assignedMethod`, `propsMethodChild`, `pickHelper`), two silent twins (an inline method that never names `this`, the picked object read in a timer). Routes `getterouter`, `getterassign`, `propsmethod`, `getterpick` on three hosts.

*The re-check 2 of #226 (`super`).* `super.x` reads the prototype's member with the object as `this`, so a getter of the prototype that reads `this.g` runs the literal's getter: an accessor of the literal that holds `super` in a closure a package runs (`get h() { runStep(() => { void super.x; }); … }`, read in a timer, no member call) was silent on every build, though a called method that holds it (P570) and an uncalled sibling that holds it beside a called method that never names it (P593) were U, by an incidental cover: `member_value_candidates` refuses to resolve any member of a literal whose function text mentions `this` or `super` (ADR 0320), which the method-call rule then handed. The literal's own check (`receiver_in_literal`) and the callee's (`function_names_receiver`) now count every `this` and every `super` (`solid_facts::ast::receiver_expression_spans`, syntax only; `this_expression_spans` is unchanged for its other consumer), so the hand-off no longer rests on the text rule. Chrome: FLUSH_IN_ACTION for the accessor and the method. Fixture: three sites (`superAccessor`, `superMethod`, `superSibling`: P570 and P593 are pinned), routes `gettersuper` and `methodsuper` on three hosts. Cost: a literal with a getter that holds `super` anywhere is handed, as one that holds `this` is (the re-check's twin P592, silent before, keeps a row).

*The check of #227 (G1, G2 and the receivers' neighbours; the review of #229, B1).* `this` and `super` name an object no reference of it shows, and the walk that asks whether a package may run a member follows references. A getter that flushes on a prototype literal (`const base = { get g() { flush(); … } }`), read by `super.g` or `this.g` in an accessor of the derived object (`{ __proto__: base, get h() { runStep(() => { void super.g; }); … } }`, read in a timer), was silent on every build (G1; so were the prototype written after the literal, two levels up, a setter, a prototype named by a conditional or a call, across files, a method on the prototype). So were its neighbours with no prototype, older than #226: a method of the literal called through `this.m()` in a closure a package runs (silent since #222), the method handed through `this` (`runStep(this.m)`), an arrow member read back by `const { m } = this`, a function written outside and placed in the literal (`{ m: helper }`), a prototype's members spread into it, and a method written outside that names `this` and is called on the literal (`{ m, g }` with `g` naming `this`, `o.g = g` after, or reaching the literal through a parameter, a call's result, an alias a destructuring makes or an array's element). Chrome: FLUSH_IN_ACTION at each flush (`patterns/pkghand/proto-*-step`, `method-this-arrow-step`, `foreign-*-step`; 33 of 33 `ph-*` programs of the eleven routes certified with no finding on main). Three rules, each only handing more (`package_hand_off.rs`): a value placed directly in an object literal that writes a receiver (a property's value, a spread's argument, a `__proto__:` value: the contexts `carries` places, `placed_in_receiver_literal`) is handed, whatever the receiver reads; a write of `prototype`, or of `__proto__` into anything but a `const` that holds one literal writing no receiver (that one is a `__proto__:` key written late, and the value goes on in the reads of the object), or a write through a computed key where a file of the project spells `__proto__` (ADR 0643's net for a handed key), is handed (`installs_prototype`); a call of a member the project declares hands its holder unless the callee resolves to exactly one function that never names a receiver (`method_call_may_read_receiver`, until now asked only of a holder of accessors), so a method written outside the literal, a parameter, a call's result, an alias and an array's element are handed. A first variant handed an unresolved callee only when the project stored a function that names a receiver under that key (a name net): it moved nothing and certified four shapes Chrome reports (the review of #229, B1: P01-P04), because a key absent from the set is no proof that a callee names no receiver, a function reaching a member in ways no key follows; it is removed. The other ways a prototype is installed were handed already: `Object.create`, `Object.setPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.setPrototypeOf`, `Object.assign` and `defineProperty` are arguments of a standard call the argument table does not list; a class's functions are handed whole; a spread's getters run where the spread is written. G2 is ADR 0300's (below). Fixtures: `flush-universe-package-hand-off-receivers` (21 handed sites, five silent twins), `dependency-source-integrity-r2-super-write`, `-outside-write` and `-super-twins`; routes `protogetter`, `protogetterthis`, `protoassign`, `protomethod`, `ownmethod`, `ownvalue`, `foreignthis`, `foreignparam`, `foreigncall`, `foreignalias` and `foreignarray` on three hosts; unit rows beside the `this[key]` row. Measured against main c09560009: eight existing fixtures move, 16 rows, all additions (`handler-placement-closed`: an arrow placed beside a getter that writes `this.onClick`; seven more: a callback prop or an alias called through a member nothing resolves: `props.render()`, `props.content()`, `h.onClick()`, `o.f()` after a write), the 34-project corpus 191,268 to 191,277 uncertifiable rows (+9, in three projects: six SC6002, three SC3001; 212 violations on both builds), the six default grids' 5,897 programs for the three flush codes move none, and the 33 misuse cells of the eleven routes go from false clean to recall-gap, their 33 legal twins from clean to uncertifiable (the named cost). The members that reach a receiver other than by being placed in the literal, and a prototype installed through a computed key no file spells, were left to the next paragraph (the review of #229, B2 and S2).


*The review of #229 (B2, S2).* A member reaches a receiver by no placement in the literal that writes it, and the object that holds it is no reference the read follows: assigned after the literal and read by its getter or setter through `this` (`o.m = function () { flush(); }`, `o.sub = { m() { flush(); } }`, written by a project function `put(o)`), the receiver on the prototype and the flushing member on a derived literal that writes none (`{ __proto__: base, m() { flush(); } }`), on an `Object.create` result, on a class's instance, or reached through a computed key no file spells (`o[k] = base`, `k = "__pro" + "to__"`: ADR 0643's premise). Chrome (rc.21) reports FLUSH_IN_ACTION at each; main certified all of them with no finding (the review's eight, P10, P26/Q01, Q04, Q05, Q08, Q09, Q10, Q11, and the forms probing found beside them: the receiver kept in a local, a destructuring of it in the step, `this[key]`: `patterns/pkghand/late-*-step`, `proto-class-step`, `proto-create-step`, `proto-key-step`, `proto-receiver-step`: 12 of 12). Rule 4 (`package_hand_off.rs`, hands more only): a function stored under a key (a property of an object literal, the target of an assignment) is handed when a use of a receiver, in code a package may run, reads that key. The uses are collected from every file of the program, dependency source included (`ReceiverReads`): `this.k`, `super.k`, `this["k"]`, `const { k } = this`, a unique symbol key (`this[_m$]` where the file binds `_m$` once to a call of the global `Symbol`: read and stored under that symbol alone), a computed key the program does not name (any key), and the receiver used as a value (any key). `this.constructor` and `this.__proto__` name other objects of the receiver and read any key. The receiver is followed: an alias (`const self = this`) and the parameter of a function the build reads that receives it, when the parameter is a plain name (`f(this)`, to depth six), are followed to their uses; a parameter that is a pattern or a rest is no name for the receiver (the review of #232, B3): a pattern reads the keys it names, every key for a rest and an array pattern (which runs the iterator), where the function runs, and the receiver goes on as a value; `return this`, `{ ...this }`, `Object.assign(x, this)`, an iteration, a callee nothing resolves exactly and any other use hand it where nothing here follows and read any key. A use reads no key and gives the object no other name when it is `super(…)`, a private member (`this.#k`), an operand nothing takes, the first argument of a weak collection's `get`, `has`, `delete` or `set`, of `WeakSet`'s `has`, `delete` or `add`, of `Map`'s and `Set`'s `get`, `has` or `delete` (the compiler resolves the standard declaration, or, in a script of a package whose calls resolve to none, the file's own `const` bound to `new WeakMap(…)` or `new WeakSet(…)` whose constructor the compiler resolves to the library's global), the argument of `Object.isFrozen`, `isSealed`, `isExtensible`, `keys` and `getOwnPropertyNames` (names and booleans), and the argument of `Object.defineProperty`, `defineProperties`, `freeze`, `seal`, `preventExtensions` and `setPrototypeOf` whose value is dropped: they return the object they are given, and a descriptor's functions are arguments of a standard call the table does not list, so they are handed whole, not as a store under a key. `Object.assign(this, …)` is none of these (the review of #232, B4): it writes every key of its sources through `[[Set]]`, which runs a setter of the receiver, own or inherited, so it is a write of any key where the call is written, and a call whose value is kept hands the receiver on as well. Whether a use of the receiver runs on a package's stack is the innermost function that owns it (`function_in`), not the functions around it. The store is skipped when the holder provably cannot be a receiver (`holder_confined`): a plain object literal (no `this` or `super` in it, no `__proto__` or computed key) bound by a `const`, every use of which keeps it so (a member call whose callee names no receiver; a write under a key the program names that is not `__proto__`; a weak collection's key; a call of a function the build reads whose parameter, a plain name or a pattern, is confined in turn; and the uses that give out a name for an object of the holder's own, which are asked in turn as the holder is, the review of #232, B1: a member read of a key under which some literal of the program holds an object (`hh.sub` where a literal writes `{ sub: { … } }`, or a key the program does not name), a pattern's local for such a key, a rest or an array pattern (a copy that holds the same functions under the same keys), a computed or nested pattern; a member read of any other key, and a pattern's local for it, give a value that is no object a literal built inside the holder); a value passed to, returned to or stored where code nothing here follows can reach it (a package, a callee nothing resolves exactly, `return o`, `[o]`, `x.p = o`, an export, `Object.defineProperty(o, …)`, `Object.setPrototypeOf(o, …)`) may be given a prototype, have a member called with it as `this` or be made the receiver of a function, and what is not proved is handed. Two premises stand beside the uses (the review of #232, B1 and S3): an exported name is reached by the importers of a namespace that escapes with no name the analysis reads (the namespace census: `runNs(NS)`, `NS[key]`) in a closed program as it is by every importer of an open one, and no object is confined in a program that can name `Object.prototype` (the re-check of #232 widened the question: `package_hand_off/object_prototype.rs`, below), because every plain object inherits it and a read of any key may run an accessor with the object as its receiver. S2: `proto_key_spelled` reads every file of the program as the reads do, dependency source included (`dep-keys` exporting `"__proto__"`; a file that spells it with an escape is read as spelling it). A key is the property key the runtime gives it, not its text (the review of #232, B2): a name's unicode escapes are decoded (`\u006d` is `m`, `__\u0070roto__` is `__proto__`), a number written as a key is its whole-number key (`0x1` and `1.0` are `1`, `1_0` is `10`; a fraction, a bigint, a legacy octal or a number past 2^53 names nothing the program fixes), and a computed literal's key is the facts' own. A name an object pattern assignment rewrites (`({ s } = …)`) is no unique symbol (B5: the facts record the shorthand target as a write target, facts schema 94). Cost, measured against main a60c90e01: a first cut that took every use of the receiver as a value for a read of any key, with no prefilter, moved 768 corpus rows in seven projects (route components stored under `component` in analysed library classes' reach); the strict prefilter and the followed escapes leave +7 in two (app-game +5, solid-groove +2: `fn.call(this, …)` with an unknown callee, `for (cb of this)` in a class that extends `Set`, a helper that aliases `Object.defineProperty`, one computed-key write), 212 violations unchanged. Two existing fixtures move, nine rows, all additions: `flush-universe-package-hand-off-receivers`'s `twinProto` and `twinWritten` (their base is the prototype of another object, and the program reads `g` through a receiver) and `-accessors`'s `twinPick` (its getter is stored under `g`, and its object reaches an array's element through a callback's return): the name net's known cost, a read of the same key on another object, kept as the expectation, each beside the same twin under a key of its own, which stays silent. Fixtures `-receiver-reads` (11 handed sites, three silent twins), `-receiver-escapes` (six sites), `-receiver-reads-twins`, `-receiver-key` (P10) and `-receiver-key-source` (S2); routes `lateassign`, `latesetter`, `latenested`, `lateput`, `protoreceiver`, `protocreate`, `protoclass`, `protokey`, `lateself`, `latedestr` and `latecomputed` on three hosts. Measured against main a60c90e01: coverage moves two existing fixtures by nine rows, all additions (the five same-key twins of `-receivers`: `twinProto` and `twinWritten` keep rows, `twinNull`, `twinUnrelatedReader` and `twinOwn` stay silent because their holder is proved plain; `-accessors`' `twinPick`), and records five new snapshots (57 rows); the ownership gate 96 cases; the 34-project corpus 191,277 to 191,284 uncertifiable rows (+7, in two projects: four SC3001, three SC6002; 212 violations on both builds); the six default grids' 5,897 programs for the three flush codes move none, program by program; `make fuzz-focus` over every `ph-*` cell (536 contexts) passes: main fails the 33 misuse cells of the eleven routes (33 false clean) and the fix passes them (33 recall-gap), their 33 legal twins go from clean to uncertifiable (the named cost), the 470 pairs of the earlier routes move none; the pattern lane's 12 new programs are false clean on main and fine on the fix, its other 1,382 move none.


*A store through a parameter (the neighbours of the review of #229, B2).* `function put(t) { t.m = function () { flush(); }; } const o = {}; put(o); runStep(() => { o.m(); });`, with no receiver in it, was certified with no row on every build, and Chrome (rc.21) reports FLUSH_IN_ACTION (typed and `any` holders, an outer function that passes the argument on, a copy of the holder's name made after the call, an arrow bound to a `const` with a rest parameter, `class B { add() { return this; } m: any }` with `o.add().m()`): `assignment_hands` followed the reads of the parameter `t` inside `put` and never the caller's argument `o`, so the later read `o.m()` by the caller's own name was invisible. `parameter_holder_hands` (`package_hand_off.rs`, hands more only): a store into a member of a parameter is followed to each caller's argument, like a store into it, when every use of the function is a direct call the build resolves (`exact_callers`: a use that is no call, an export a program may enter, a function no binding names, a parameter that is a pattern or a rest: the callers are not known, and the store is handed). The argument is followed under the name written at the call, through the reads of that one binding (the parameter of an outer function, a copy of the name made after the call, an import); a fresh object literal reaches nothing but the parameter, any other expression is handed. Not followed, and not claimed (the review of #232, B6 and S2, one root on main: alias tracking of stored functions, `docs/open-work.md`): another name for the same object made before the call (`const a = o; put(a); o.m()`, a loop variable, a destructured local, a function's return), a copy of the parameter inside `put` (`const s = t; s.m = …`), a default parameter that receives the store (`put()` with `t = shared`), a spread argument, a function that is a method of an object literal, and a direct call from another file. Fixture `flush-universe-package-hand-off-holder-param` (six sites, two silent twins), routes `putparam`, `putparamany` and `putchain` on three hosts, four pattern programs (`pkghand/put-*-step`), three rediscovery entries. Measured against the B2 head: coverage records the new fixture and moves no existing one; the ownership gate 96 cases; the 34-project corpus moves 0 rows (191,284 both, 212 violations); the six default grids' 5,897 programs and the 536 earlier `ph-*` contexts move none, program by program; `make fuzz-focus` over the 18 cells of the three routes: 9 false clean on the B2 head and on main, 9 recall-gap here, their 9 legal twins go from clean to uncertifiable (the named cost); the pattern lane's three put programs are false clean on both and fine here.
*The review of #232 (B1 to B5, S3: the soundness of this ADR's own rules).* The Fable review of #232 (head 9a0a1a894) found 47 shapes Chrome (rc.21) reports FLUSH_IN_ACTION at that the head certified with no finding, all of them certified on main as well and none a regression. Twenty-one are in the rules this ADR added (B1 to B5 and S3), and are closed here; the other twenty-six (B6 and the alias with no `put`) are not this ADR's rules but main's (`package_hand_off.rs`, hands more only, each with its programs): (B1, seven) the strict prefilter called a holder confined while a name it gives out was never asked: a rest copy of it given a prototype, the nested literal of a holder bound by a pattern, read through a member or a chain, given to a function the build reads; and an exported holder of a closed program was never asked the namespace census (`import * as NS`, `NS[key]`); (B2, five) the key of a store and of a read was compared as text (`\u006d` and `m`, `0x1` and `1.0` and `"1"`); (B3, six) a parameter that is a pattern or a rest was followed as the receiver itself, so the key a pattern reads, a getter it runs and an iterator an array pattern runs were recorded nowhere; (B4, one) `Object.assign(this, …)` was on the list of uses that read nothing; (B5, one) a symbol an object pattern assignment rewrites counted as unique (a facts defect: the shorthand target of `({ s } = …)` was no write target; facts schema 94); (S3, one) a plain holder inherits from `Object.prototype`, where an accessor runs with any object as its receiver. The fix keeps the owner's condition (escapes prove nothing) and adds the premises its proof had skipped: what a use gives out is asked as the holder is (`nested_keys`, `pattern_confined`), the census is asked of an exported name, a program that can name `Object.prototype` has no confined holder (`object_prototype_written`, widened by the re-check), keys are spelled as the runtime spells them (`spelled_key`, `member_spelled_key`), a pattern parameter is a read of every key where its function runs (`ReadKind::Pattern`) and `Object.assign(this, …)` is a write of any key (`ReadKind::MemberWrite`). A symbol-keyed write is no prototype install (a unique symbol is none of the strings `installs_prototype` asks). The ratchets: the `default-on-missing` arm the review found hidden behind a rewritten match (`Array | Object => true` in `use_confined`, which the B1 shapes went through) is replaced by `pattern_confined`, which asks the locals; the one `default-on-missing` hit the S3 rule had (a use of `Object.prototype` nothing here follows answered "touched", stated in `scripts/proof-lint.allowlist.json`) is gone with the rewrite the re-check asked for (below), which has no fail-open exit; the `ast.functions` to `declared` rename of the ir-read-lint was a real false match (`ast.functions` is a `Vec`, the lint reads names) and stays. Not closed here, and not claimed (B6, the 22 the review counts, and the alias with no `put` at all, three: one root on main): the walk of a store follows the written name only, so an alias of the holder made before the call, a copy of the parameter inside `put`, a default or a spread argument, a function that is a method of an object literal and a direct call from another file are not followed; they are a named item of `docs/open-work.md`, with the other residuals this review found (the routes to `Object.prototype` of the re-check, below, and the weak-collection rule's package-script branch, which no fixture exercises). Fixtures `-receiver-confinement` (15 sites, two files, eight silent twins), `-receiver-patterns` (six sites, three twins), `-object-prototype` (three sites) and the twins fixture's `twinPattern`; routes `restcopy`, `nestedpattern`, `nestedread`, `nestedchain`, `nestedarg`, `restnested`, `nestedspread`, `keyescape`, `keyreadescape`, `keymethodescape`, `keyhex`, `keyfloat`, `parampattern`, `paramgetter`, `paramarray`, `paramrest`, `paramrestpass`, `assignthis`, `symbolrewrite` and `objproto` on three hosts (120 contexts: 60 misuse programs and their 60 legal twins; 674 `ph-*` contexts in all), 23 pattern programs (`pkghand/rest-copy-step` and its neighbours: the review's twenty, two more false cleans found probing the fix, and one the reviewed head already handed), three rediscovery entries, unit tests of the key spelling and of the shorthand write target. Measured against main 45c56c08d (#231 merged), release builds: coverage records three new snapshots (24 flush sites, 72 rows; 23 SC2002, one SC2003 and three SC9012 beside them) and moves no existing one (1,230 fixture projects compared); the ownership gate 96 cases; the 34-project corpus 203,852 to 203,859 uncertifiable rows (+7: app-game +5, solid-groove +2, the B2 head's own, so these fixes add none; 212 violations on both); `make fuzz-focus` over the 120 cells of the twenty routes: the reviewed head fails all 60 misuse cells (60 false clean, each certified with no finding at all, their 60 twins clean) and the fix passes (60 recall-gap, their 60 twins uncertifiable: the named cost), and every `ph-*` cell (674 contexts: 337 recall-gap, 337 uncertifiable twins; the Chrome oracle agrees on each) leaves the 554 earlier pairs as they were, program by program; the six default grids' 5,897 programs move none against the reviewed head, program by program (nothing needs a look); the pattern lane's 23 new programs are fine on the fix, and 22 are false clean on the reviewed head (the twenty-third, `param-pattern-nested-step`, it already handed). Of the review's 209 probe programs exactly 22 change (silent to uncertifiable: A3, C1 to C5, C11, C12, E17, K1 to K4, K8, M4, R1, R15e, R2, R2b, R2c, R5, S1); C11 (`d.sub = hh.sub`, no flush at run time) is the one that is legal, a nested literal stored under another holder's key, which is an escape. A pattern parameter that names only keys no object is held under keeps its holder confined (`twinLeaf`), which the reviewed head asked as a use of the pattern's names: the one place the probes show a program going from uncertifiable to silent, and sound (a value a pattern binds from a key no object is held under is no object a literal built inside the holder).
*The re-check of #232 (S3: the ways to `Object.prototype`).* The re-check of a59025c35 (`pr232-review/recheck.md`) found B1 to B5 fixed, the 22 flips exact, X4 sound in Chrome and no false positive, and 19 Chrome-confirmed false cleans on the one rule that was new in the review round, the `Object.prototype` one, all certified on main and on the reviewed head as well: it exempted a built-in whose call returns the prototype (`Object.prototype.valueOf()`), followed only a `const` alias of `Object` and a `globalThis` written in the member (`names_global_object`, with two fail-open exits: an expression it could not read was "not Object", and an alias chain past depth three was dropped), and did not follow `getPrototypeOf`, `.constructor.prototype`, `.__proto__` or `super.prototype`. Probing the first fix found 16 more, and Research B's probe of the second 16 (each Chrome-confirmed, each a program of the pattern lane): other names for the window (`top`, `parent`, `frames`, `window.document.defaultView`, a `document` reached by an alias, a pattern or a call); a key built at run time (`({})["const" + "ructor"].prototype`, the same in a `const`, `Reflect.get({}, "const" + "ructor")`, a key that is a parameter, a computed key of a pattern, a `for of` variable, `Reflect.get` kept as a value); a package the project only imports that writes `Object.prototype` (statically, with `import()`, through `globalThis`, through another package, in a function the project calls, handed out by a package export or by a package function, or handed the prototype by the project to define the getter itself); and code a string builds that defines the getter (a string timer, a `<script>` element's text or Blob `src`, an `onerror` or `onclick` attribute, an `innerHTML` handler, `import()` of a `data:` URL). Decided (the owner, 2026-11-14: fail closed; a named premise does not clear a false clean), closed in #232, hands more only, as a rule of its own (`package_hand_off/object_prototype.rs`, with its unit table; facts schema 95) whose polarity is "touched unless the use provably gives nothing out": (1) every reference in a value position to `Object`, `Reflect`, `globalThis`, `window`, `self`, `global`, `top`, `parent` or `frames` that no binding of the file declares (`global_value_references`, which leaves out a type annotation and a shadowing name) is touched unless it is an operand nothing takes or the object of a member whose key the program spells and by which the global gives no prototype out (`Object.keys`, `window.addEventListener`); an initializer, an argument, a return, an assignment, a pattern, a heritage, a sequence, a logical operand and a key the program does not spell are names for the global, so no alias is followed and no depth is cut; (2) the same names read as the key of a member of anything (`x.Object`, `x.Reflect`, `x.Function`, `x.eval`) are asked as the references are, because the last step from a window to the global is that read, whichever way the window was reached (no list of the ways to a window, no special case for `defaultView`); (3) `Object.prototype` is touched unless it is an operand nothing takes or the object of a read of `hasOwnProperty`, `isPrototypeOf`, `propertyIsEnumerable`, `toLocaleString` or `toString` (`valueOf` returns its receiver and is no longer one); (4) a call of `Object.getPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.getPrototypeOf`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` or `getOwnPropertyDescriptors` is touched unless its value is an operand nothing takes; (5) a read of `constructor` (the global `Object` where the receiver is a plain object) and of `__proto__` is touched under the same rule, a write or a `delete` of either is no read, and so is a pattern that binds `__proto__` or `constructor` (a declaration pattern, a parameter, the keys of an assignment pattern: `assignment_pattern_keys`) and a call given the string `"__proto__"` or `"constructor"`; (6) a read under a computed key (`x[k]`, `({ [k]: p } = x)`, `Reflect.get(x, k)`) is touched unless the facts prove its key is none of `constructor`, `__proto__`, `prototype`, `Object`, `Reflect`, `Function` and `eval` (`computed_keys`: a number or a symbol, a numeric operator, `++`, a constant or a concatenation or template of constants, the text a `typeof` gives, a `const`, and a `let` or `var` whose initializer and every write are such; a parameter, a call, a member, an iteration variable, an import and a name a destructuring writes prove nothing, a file with a `with` statement follows no name, and a key known only from its type is no proof); a write, a `delete` and an operand nothing takes read nothing out, and `Reflect.get` kept as a value is touched; (7) `__defineGetter__`, `__defineSetter__`, `__lookupGetter__` and `__lookupSetter__`; (8) a file that builds code as a string (`code_sinks`: `eval`, `Function`, a `.constructor(..)` call, a timer given anything but a proven function, a `<script>` element made at run time, an event attribute set as text or written `onclick` in JSX, markup written as a string that is not proven inert, a load by a computed specifier or a `data:` or `blob:` URL, a `javascript:` URL, a global looked up by a computed name) is touched, and its receivers are unreadable (`ReadKind::Unreadable`): the generated code may give `Object.prototype` an accessor that reads any key through `this`, and the file shows no read, so a touched program never confines a holder and reads any key; (9) an installed package is asked of the backend's own walk of its closure (`package_reach/prototype.rs`, beside the action walk, which stops at the first hazard and the first Solid load): every file reached is asked the rule above and its scan's hazards (a load by a computed name, code generation, a file Oxc does not parse) end the closure undecided, as do a file or a load nothing answers; a package that names `Object.prototype`, builds code or is undecided is touched with unreadable receivers (`PackageReachIndex::unseen_code`: unavailable source is no evidence, so the old premise that a package the build does not read as source is left out is gone), and a package read to its end that holds a `this` or a `super` (`reads_receiver`) reads any key as soon as a file of the program can name the prototype, because the program may hand it the prototype and its getter reads through `this`; Solid's own packages are the dialect's and are not asked. `super.prototype` needs no rule of its own: a class that extends `Object` names it (1). The first round's fact for strings spelled `__proto__` is gone: (6) asks every read under a key nothing proves, whether or not the program spells the word. The cost is the named one: a program with such a read in any file it reads, a dependency's included, withholds the strict prefilter, and a store into a plain holder is asked of the name net (an uncertifiable row, never a silence); the fixtures' synthetic `steplib` no longer reads `ns[k]()` under a `for in` key (`runNs` is `Object.values(ns).forEach`), which would have made every hand-off twin touched by the package's own text. Named in `docs/open-work.md`, not closed: the top-level `this` of a script that is no module. Cost, measured against main dfa6c5dec (rc.21 frozen corpus, 34 projects, release builds, jobs 3): the standard build 190,085 to 190,100 uncertifiable (+15, the B2 head's own: `leaf-operation-unaccounted` 8 and `effect-creation-unaccounted` 7, in app-game, kui and solid-groove), the development build 210,097 to 210,865 (+768: 771 added, 3 relabelled from `package-finding-at-entry`; viviana-ui-web +395, probus-hk +167, ai-memory-ui +159, spotify-desk-thing +35 (-3), kui +8, app-game +5, solid-groove +2), violations 218 and 212 on both sides, summed time unchanged (216.2 s). Every added development row is a row of the head's standard build, and the 756 of the four large projects are rows of the standard build on main: that build reads no dependency source, so those sites were never proved there, and the head withholds the development build's proof of them where a package may run code nothing reads. All of it comes from one thing, the unreadable any-key receiver read, which has two independent triggers, both present in all four projects: a package the backend's walk cannot clear (a closure that names `Object.prototype`, builds code as a string or is not read to its end: 5, 25, 21 and 14 packages) and code a file of the program builds as a string (dependency source in all four, a project file in three). The head with either trigger removed gives every row, and with both removed its findings are main's, row for row (debug builds, one project at a time). The keys rule and the spelled routes touch files (24, 53, 7 and 1 project files) and add no row of their own: a touched program with no unreadable read has no receiver to ask. Narrowing one trigger buys nothing while the other stays.
