## ADR 0968 — A site ends for a Chrome code only by an ending that answers that code (batch 11, slice 4)
Any row or finding at a site's span used to end the site: `Endings` kept, per `(path, start, end)`, only the best class of any row, defect or violation, whatever its rule or table, and a named silence ended every table's site at its span. A read that only the async-read table's row stood at, or a write that only another rule's finding stood at, was accounted for, although neither row answers the Chrome code the site can raise (STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED, REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE).

**Each site now carries the codes it may raise (`SiteCode`: `StrictRead`, `ReactiveWrite`, `OptimisticWrite`, `ActionCall`, `StoreWrite`, `OnFlush`, each with its `RuntimeCode` and home rule), and each (site, code) ends only by an ending that answers it.** `credits(policy, code, by)` is one `match` over the ending's kind with no wildcard: a row of the site's own table answers the table's codes, a census obligation answers a code that has a place, a finding answers the code when the dialect's policy (`Dialect::code_policy`, ADR 0955) says the rule claims it (a rule that declines it answers it only as an obligation), the compiler's discard answers every code; no policy for a code answers nothing (fail closed). A named silence ends the codes its `SiteSilence::codes()` lists (an exhaustive `match` per variant): the read silences STRICT_READ, `SetterOptimistic*Unguarded` REACTIVE_WRITE only (an optimistic write before the first answer still fires), `UnreachedWriteCannotRun` REACTIVE_WRITE and the action call (module-scope optimistic writes can still fire), the shared-reactivity silences STORE_WRITE, `static_api.on-flush.role-allows` ON_FLUSH; the four removal silences (`ApplyNeverRuns`, `ClosedProgramExportDischarge`, `ArgumentPrimitiveDischarge`, `ArgumentMemberPrimitiveDischarge`) answer what the removed row's ending answered (`RemovedBy`). A (site, code) with no ending and no silence gets the **code's own** home rule's uncertifiable row (`unaccounted_row(file, site, code)`): SC1001 `strict-read-unaccounted`, SC2001 `write-unaccounted`, and, new, SC2009 `optimistic-write-unaccounted` for the OPTIMISTIC code. Never a violation.

A write site carries OPTIMISTIC_WRITE_BEFORE_LOAD beside REACTIVE_WRITE when the setter's source is optimistic and may be async, or when no fact names the primitive that made it (`optimistic_async_setter`, one definition shared with SC2009's producers, `local_access.rs`): an unresolved primitive is fail closed, and a sync source (`createOptimistic(0)`), which the existing proof of synchronous names, has no such code. `StaticDefectFamily::rule_name()` maps a defect family to its rule exhaustively, and the rules crate pins that it equals `static_defect_wording`'s (a test fails when the two drift); the IR still matches no rule by a name prefix.

**The proof log and the gate.** One `site` line per (site, code) (`code`, `by`: `table:<t>`, `census`, `rule:<name>[:u]`, `discarded`, `credited`: whether the strongest ending at the span answers the code), and the `silent` lines of the named silences carry `codes`. `scripts/lib/proof-log.mjs` folds C1, C2(b) and C3 per (site, code): only a named end (`rule: "end"`) ends a code, and only the codes its `codes` list (a line with no `codes`, a line of another pass at the span (`PendingSafe`, `FlushSafe`, a `row:*` stage, SC4001) and a site line with no `code` end none, fail closed: the writer omits an empty list, and the checker then files the code's row; the review of #218's F1, **owner-approved** 2026-11-12), and the classifier's decisions are about the table's first code (`SITE_CODE`), so SC2009's line at a setter call has no decision to be explained by; `scripts/lib/proof-credit.mjs` reads `site.code`. This is a judge change, **owner-approved** (2026-11-12) with no C2 exemption for a site whose only ending answers another code: that is the case the slice exists to expose. The 22 sites the gate now reports (the 17 the corpus fixtures show, 12 reads, 4 writes and 1 setter whose primitive no fact resolves, and 5 in the slice's own two fixtures) are listed in `fixtures/proof-log/candidates.json`, owner "batch 11 slice 4: masked site, the code's U row stands; the proof is its producer's own"; `gaps.json` stays `{}`.

*Measured* (34 projects, release, against #216's head, which is main): standard U 122,236 to **122,240 (+4**, all SC1001 `strict-read-unaccounted`, app-game: `createTreeView.ts:172`, `solid-three/core/store.ts:383`, `:384`, `:391`), development build 142,943 to **142,948 (+5**, the same four and jar-hell-web `theme.ts:34`); **0 `optimistic-write-unaccounted` rows** on the corpus (the brief's estimate was under 50); nothing removed, V unchanged. `make coverage`: nine existing fixtures move by **22 uncertifiable rows, none removed** (SC1001 14: `caught-handed-read`, `handed-carrier-tracked`, `handed-net`, `handed-net-guards`, `async-carried-leaf-owner`, `async-unsuspendable-call-attributed`; SC2001 7: `rc21-optimistic-before-load`, `rc21-optimistic-handed-prop`; SC2009 1: `local-alias-literal-slots`), each a site that only another table's row or another rule's finding stood at. Fixtures: `ending-by-code-other-rule` (a read ended only by the async-read table's row: SC1001's row beside SC5003 and SC5008; a write ended only by SC2009's violation: SC2001's row beside it) and its `-crediting` twin (the own rule's finding stands: no row beside it), `optimistic-write-site-code` (async, aliased, sync, and an object-slot alias whose primitive no fact resolves). Chrome (rc.21): the read raises CAUGHT_REACTIVE_READ only and the write OPTIMISTIC_WRITE_BEFORE_LOAD ahead of any owned-scope guard (`caught-handed-read`, `rc21-optimistic-before-load`), so the new rows are U where Chrome fires one other code, the cost of not having a proof that the second code cannot fire; no defect is found (nothing was a false clean), so there is no rediscovery entry. Named in `docs/open-work.md`: an OPTIMISTIC row on a setter whose primitive is unresolved is a fail-closed trade until slice 8 names SC2009's silences (`NoOptimisticAsyncSource`, `OptimisticSourceSynchronous`).

## ADR 0969 — Every owner call ends, per code, in a row, an SC9012, the compiler's discard or a named silence (batch 11, slice 6)

**The defect.** SC3001 (CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE) and SC6002 (PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK) had no site universe: a call of `onCleanup`, or of a creation (`createMemo`, `createEffect`, `createRoot`, `render`, ...), that no walk rowed was silent by omission, and nothing said whether it was silent because no leaf owner or effect apply can reach it or because a walk gave up (`unplaced_blocker`'s `None` answers both "placed, nothing reaches" and an anonymous function, a component by convention, a function with no call sites, a parameter list). No confirmed defect: a ratchet, so no rediscovery entry.

**The universe.** `owner_call_sites` lists every call whose resolved primitive is one of these, outside dependency source, whatever its callee is spelled, with the codes `owner_call_codes` gives it (one definition, asked again by the silences): `onCleanup` raises CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, a creation a leaf owner refuses (`cleanup::creates_forbidden_primitive`) PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, and on a client build a creation the dialect says throws on an apply (`throws_creating_in_effect_callback`, the argument test is `static_api::first_argument_is_function`, shared with both SC6002 arms) PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK (`SiteCode::{CleanupForbidden, PrimitiveForbidden, EffectCreation}`, ADR 0968's per-code endings). A leaf operation ends the code its kind answers (`leaf_operation_row`: a cleanup, a creation, a call the walk could not place; the observer guard, a flush, a callback no walk followed answer none of these), an SC9012 ends every code, and a finding of the claiming rule ends its code. **SC4001 does not decline** (ruling of the coordinator, owner delegated: `codes.mjs` unchanged): an SC4001 obligation at an `onCleanup` ends nothing for SC3001's code. A site no ending and no silence holds gets the code's own row, **never a violation**: SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` (the blocker flush accounting shares) and SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted`. A removed leaf operation (an effect whose apply never runs) names what it answered.

**The silences (seven, each a typed `SiteSilence` with a premise registered in `boundary.mjs`; coordinator-approved, owner delegated).** Every silence that rests on the owner graph or on a census is gated by **B3** (policy A, owner-ruled): no package the build does not read may run the function that holds the site (`UnreadPackageHandOff`, ADR 0967). A package a build reads as source is known; a component only an unread package renders (the router's) is not trusted to be rendered under an owner: that waits for a proof from the package's source (proof batch). In `owners/leaf_universe.rs` (the owner stage, where the graph is in scope): **`OwnerCallNeverRuns`** (ADR 0458's query proves no execution runs the site, premise `SiteReach`, every code); **`OwnerCallModuleScope`** (no function owns the site and no instance field's initializer holds it: module evaluation runs it once on a stack of its own, premise `ModuleScope`, every code); **`LeafNoOpenerInProgram`** (the project names no primitive that opens a leaf scope, `project_opens_leaf_scope`, which includes a package read as source, premise `ProgramCensus`, SC3001's two codes); **`LeafOwnerAbsent`** (the owning function's context has an edge, no leaf bit and is not the bare open-world seed of an export, `open_world_unowned_only`, premise `OwnerContextNoLeaf`, SC3001's two codes); **`OwnerCurrent`** (the context gives an owner on every entry, owned, a leaf owner or both: no unowned bit, so `inEffectCallback && context === null` is never met, premise `OwnerContextCurrent`, SC6002); **`EffectCreationRunsOffApply`** (the role engine places the site off every apply: rendering, a deferred callback, a directive apply, module code, discarded code, an event handler where no synchronous dispatch is present, premise `RoleDoesNotReport`, the exit the second SC6002 arm took silently) and **`EffectCreationOwnerSetAround`** (an exact primitive whose callback creates an owner wraps the site, premise `OwnerSetAround`; `owner_created_around_call` answers only `SlotOwner::Creates`, since `owner_set_around`'s "sets or may set" also holds for `runWithOwner` with an owner that is a value or null, and only where every layer the climb crosses runs in the primitive's synchronous run: not a generator, a parameter list, or after a suspension of an async layer). The graph's two silences and the role silence answer only where the site is plain (written directly in a function that is no generator, not in a parameter list and not after a suspension of its async function), with no layer around it entered by a route the graph has no edge for (`layer_entry_open_by_reference`, ADR 0868's test without its component-render premise: a function that returns JSX is entered by renders alone only where every reference of its binding is a JSX tag; its "caller holds no context" question extracted as `caller_holds_no_context`), and for a function no package the build does not read may run (B3). The two effect-creation silences were `static_api`'s, asking the role or the wrapper and nothing else, until the review of #220 found them ending sites Chrome throws at (below).

**The proof gate and the decline (judge change, coordinator-approved, owner delegated).** A site no proof ends gets the code's home row, which under policy A is the ruled ending for a function a package the build does not read may run, a layer entered by reference and the like, so `make proof-gate` reported 2,705 sites that end in nothing. The checker now writes, for each group of codes (SC3001's pair, SC6002's) of an owner-call site that no silence of the owner stage ends, a typed `declined` line naming why (`Decline`: `UnreadPackageMayRun`, `InstanceFieldInitializer`, `ParameterList`, `GeneratorBody`, `AfterSuspension`, `NoOwnerNode`, `NoEdgeIntoFunction`, `OpenWorldExport`, `LeafBitPresent`, `UnownedEntry`, `EntryByReference`: a closed enum, no catch-all, the id function denies a wildcard arm). A decline is no proof and ends nothing: it goes to the proof log only and no ending or silence reads it (`an_owner_call_decline_ends_nothing` holds that a declined-only site keeps its uncertifiable row and that no silence lists its code). The gate (`scripts/lib/proof-log.mjs`, `ownerCallDeclined`) accepts an owner-call (site, code) that ends in nothing if and only if the code's home row stands at the span (the final report's `leaf-operation-unaccounted` or `effect-creation-unaccounted`, uncertifiable) AND a `declined` line at the span lists the code; either alone, a decline for another code, one with no code list, and any other table's site stay hits. Five unit tests, three of which fail on the old gate.

**Found while building the fixtures.** Where the callee's declarations sit under no installed package directory (a project's own ambient `declare module "solid-js"`, or declarations that disagree on the package) the effect-phase walk, which asks `callee_package_root`, files nothing, and nothing else accounted for the creation: `createMemo(() => 1)` written directly in a `createEffect` apply was **certified** although the runtime throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK there. The creation is now a site with no silence, so it gets `effect-creation-unaccounted` (fixture `owner-call-effect-creation-unresolved-package`; the same program with the declarations in an installed package is the walk's violation). The generator writes every program against the pinned real install, so the shape is an `outside` entry in `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`.

**Chrome (rc.21) and the fuzzer.** The fixtures' programs ran in real Chrome (the runtime oracle): `owner-call-effect-creation`'s legal components (`RootInMemo`, `Body`, `Handler`, `Timer`, `Fielded`, `SharedBody`, `SharedTimer`, the module-scope memo, `dead`, `stored`) are quiet (the checker's row at `Handler`'s inline arrow is the cost named below); `InApply` and `RootInApply` fire PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, each covered by SC6002's violation; `owner-call-leaf-universe` fires only at the leaf walk's two violations (`Opener`, `Both` through `useBoth`); the no-opener program, its `with-opener` twin and the `sync-dispatch` twin (the click's target cannot reach the handler, so Chrome is quiet and the U is the cost) are quiet; the unresolved-package program fires against the real packages (the walk gives its violation there), so its ambient form, certified before, was a false clean. `make fuzz-focus` on the three codes needs no look (0 false clean, 0 false positive): on the build with the review's fixes the misuse grids are unchanged against the build before (mx-base 1,320 programs: agree 1,128, recall-gap 192; mx-combo 1,320: agree 1,099, recall-gap 221; mx-census 8,262), and the legal grids are all uncertifiable (lg-base 1,680, lg-combo 1,680; before slice 6, 1,680 and 1,025 of 1,680 were clean): the cost of policy A, since the generator's programs export their components from an open program, where every function is handed. The review's cells (`er-shapes.mjs`, below) are in the recall grids.

**Measured** (34 projects, release, against the head with #218 and the flip, standard build; the figures after the review's fixes, the first ones in brackets): the raw universe, with endings and no silence, is 5,988 (site, code) lines of which 5,802 rows (unique sites 5,352: SC3001 creation 2,677, SC3001 cleanup 272, SC6002 2,403); with the silences **+4,372 uncertifiable rows (SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` 2,465, SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted` 1,907) [+2,876: 2,337 and 539]**, none a violation; development build +4,381 (SC3001 2,475, SC6002 1,906) and nine SC6002 `package-finding-at-entry` rows superseded at the same sites [+2,878, six]. The review's fixes add 1,496 rows to the first measurement (SC6002 1,368: B3 gating the role silence 1,248, a layer entered by a reference 51, a function no edge reaches 34 (an inline handler is one), after an `await` 29, an unowned entry 6; SC3001 128, a layer entered by a reference: the components F1 found), 0 removed, 0 violations moved. What the silences end (unique records, owner stage): `owner-context-no-leaf` 697 [827], `effect-creation-runs-off-apply` 666 [recorded wherever the role placed the site: 1,857], `owner-context-current` 22 [239], `no-opener-in-program` 19, `module-scope` 13, `effect-creation-owner-set-around` 4 [13], `never-runs` 1. What stays uncertifiable, by decline (unique (site, code), standard): SC6002 `unread-package-may-run` 1,714, `entry-by-reference` 99, `no-edge-into-function` 44, `after-suspension` 34, `unowned-entry` 16; SC3001 creation `unread-package-may-run` 1,845, `entry-by-reference` 162, `no-edge-into-function` 151, `after-suspension` 34, `open-world-export` 25; SC3001 cleanup `unread-package-may-run` 176, `entry-by-reference` 49, `open-world-export` 14, `no-edge-into-function` 8, `after-suspension` 1 (B3 is most of it: a component an exported route hands to the router). `make coverage`: **1,197 projects (the three review fixtures are new): 279 existing projects gain 1,380 rows and lose 5 (1,375 SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted` and one SC3001 are new; the five removed are the old offsets of four SC6002/SC9012 rows and one `effect-creation-unaccounted` that moved only because `owner-call-effect-creation`'s comments grew, counted again among the added); no row changes kind, no violation moves** (against main, in all: 452 existing projects move, 4,311 rows added and 7 removed, and 8 are new); the first measurement had 423 projects and 2,906 rows (the seven removed, which stay, are slice 5's SC3001 flush rows in `resolve-inline-entries` and `slot-run-effect-phase`, which yield to any row of their rule that overlaps the flush call, and the new row at the `resolve` or `until` inside it now does: both stay uncertifiable beside it, named in `docs/open-work.md`). Fixtures: `owner-call-leaf-universe`, `owner-call-no-leaf-opener` (variants `with-opener`, `package-opener` in the development build and `package-unread` in the standard one), `owner-call-effect-creation` (variant `sync-dispatch`), `owner-call-effect-creation-unresolved-package`, and the review's `owner-call-component-by-reference`, `owner-call-saved-callback` and `owner-call-root-generator`.

**The review of #220 (BLOCKED, and the fixes).** The Fable review of the head 280f766c1 (`slice6-review/review.md`, probed read-only) found three of the seven silences ending sites rc.21 throws at: certified on the head, and on main with no silence at all (so no output got worse, but #220 would have signed them with a named proof). Each is a hole in its silence's premise, not in the rule. **F1, `OwnerCurrent` and `LeafOwnerAbsent`:** `named_layer_entry_open` (the emission's test of what enters a function, ADR 0868) stops at `function_proven_component` (a function that returns JSX that no call enters, one that a reference also enters included: `Escaped`) before it looks at the references, and the graph gives such a function an owned context: the component-render premise the ruling excludes. `function view() { createMemo(…); return <p/> } … pick = view; createEffect(() => 0, () => { pick!(); })` runs `view` on the apply's stack with `context === null`. Fix: `layer_entry_open_by_reference`, for the universe's silences only: a component is entered by renders alone only where every reference of its binding is a JSX tag (the opening and the closing name are one reference); the emission keeps its own test and its premise (a change to SC4001's proofs is a slice of its own, with grid diffs). **F2, `EffectCreationRunsOffApply`:** it asked the lexical role only, which places a handler or a timer callback off every apply from where the function is registered and follows no other reference (`saved = h` then `saved!()` in an apply; an array's element; a generator body `untrack` hands back and an apply steps), and it carried none of the conditions the graph's silences have. Fix: the silence moved to the owner stage and rests on the role AND the same three facts (a plain site, `layer_entry_open_by_reference`, B3). **F3, `EffectCreationOwnerSetAround`:** `owner_created_around_call` never asked whether the callback runs in the primitive's synchronous run (`createRoot(function* () { createMemo(…) })`, stepped from an apply: the body runs after the root's owner is gone). Fix: every layer the climb crosses must be plain (no generator, no parameter list, no site after a suspension), the owner stage's `generator-body` decline being the same question. Each fix is Chrome-confirmed (oracle cases `owner-call-component-by-reference`, `owner-call-saved-callback`, `owner-call-root-generator`: `unproven-clean` on the head of #220, `covered-uncertifiable` on the fix), has a fixture (a positive, the negative and the twin; the README tables) and is a fuzz cell: `er-shapes.mjs`, 14 contexts of the recall grids, of which the head of #220 certifies 12 programs (`view`, `saved`, `timer` and `root` on an apply, three each) and the fix none (rediscovery.json lists the three entries; the `array` and `generator` routes and the leaf cells are covered by the SC9012 at the call that reaches the function, on both builds). The cost is the corpus rows above: B3 now gates the role silence as it gates the graph's (policy A), and an inline event handler (`onClick={() => …}`, a function value no binding names that is not a whole argument of a call) is no closed layer for the entry test, so a creation in one keeps its row (at most the 34 sites above; Chrome is quiet there). The proof batch's refinement: a literal the compiler binds as the element's event handler is entered only by the event.

**The re-review of #220 (BLOCKED once more: B1).** The F2 fix left one hole in the role silence: the test that a site is plain asked `function.generator` of the innermost function only (`leaf_universe.rs`), so a creation in an arrow, an IIFE or an `untrack` callback written inside a generator was a plain site, the role engine placed it where the iterator is made (rendering), and `EffectCreationRunsOffApply` ended it, though an apply that steps the iterator with a `for…of` or a spread runs the layer with no owner (`probes2/r6q-forof-certified`, `r6r-spread-untrack-certified`; Chrome rc.21 PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK). Fix: `generator_layer_around` asks every function layer around the site, innermost first, and stops at the layer whose callback runs under an owner its primitive creates (`creates_owner_for`, the emission's own notion of an owner layer): the owner is current there whoever steps what is around it, so a creation in a root's callback inside a generator stays silent (`effect-creation-owner-set-around`) and its `createRoot` keeps its row. The same predicate guards the graph's two silences (`OwnerCurrent`, `LeafOwnerAbsent`) and the effect pair, since all four follow `plain`. Measured on the re-review's 21 generator probes, the head of #220 against the fix (release, closed boundary): `r6q` and `r6r` certified → one SC6002 row each; ten others gained the SC6002 row their silence had hidden (the file already had other rows); nine controls unchanged; no row lost. The fixture `owner-call-generator-layer` pins the three false cleans, the owner-layer stop and the cost (`Idle`: a generator made and never stepped keeps its row, Chrome quiet). Chrome-confirmed through the oracle case (the entry hands every export to the real `@solidjs/web`, so B3 covers the sites on every build and the case cannot show an unproven clean: the closed run of the fixture can) and the fuzz cells `er-genlayer-apply` and `er-genuntrack-apply` (the generator and its iterator at module scope, for the same reason: no function is around the call that makes the iterator, so B3 asks nothing of it): the head of #220 certifies the three `genuntrack` programs, Chrome confirming (false clean), and the fix none (recall-gap, an uncertifiable row stands; the legal twins become uncertifiable, the named cost); the `genlayer` cells are covered on both builds by the ADR 0710 row at the creation. Corpus (34 projects, release): 0 rows added or removed against the head in the standard build and in the development build (one SC9012 `standard-member-impostor` row of `expenses-app` `src/lib/clerk.tsx:49` differs from an earlier run of the head: the head itself gives it when rerun alone, 948 rows on both builds).

**The check of B1 (BLOCKED once more: N1, N2).** `slice6-review/b1-check.md`: the lexical form of B1 held, and two stops of the entry walk (`layer_entry_open`, the emission's test of what enters a layer, which the universe shares) let a layer through. **N1:** B1's test asked the functions written *around* the site, so a function written outside a generator and called from its body (a helper, an arrow beside it, a plain function `yield*` delegates to) had no generator layer, and the caller walk, which follows a closed layer's calls out to their callers and asks each caller's layers the same question, took the generator's body for a placed run: `function helper() { createMemo(…) } function* gen() { helper(); yield 1 }`, `const it = gen()` in the component body, `for (const _ of it)` in an apply (`probes3/a4b`, `a4c`, `a4e`; Chrome rc.21 PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK). **N2:** its stop at an owner-creating layer (and at a control-flow child) returned before it read the function's references: `createRoot(function f() { if (!saved) { saved = f; return; } createMemo(…) })`, then `saved()` in an apply, runs the callback on its own stack under no owner (`b5`); `owner_created_around_call` and `generator_layer_around` had the same stop. Fix, for the universe only (`Premises::Universe`; the emission keeps the premises of ADR 0868, a change to SC4001's proofs being a slice of its own with grid diffs): a layer that is a generator is an open entry, whether it is written around the site or is the caller at the end of a call (a root's generator callback is no owned run either, so the test precedes the owner-creating stop); the stop at an owner-creating layer or a control-flow child holds only where nothing references the function (`referenced_only_by_entry`: a callback with no binding cannot be referenced, a named function expression is asked for the references of its own name, the position that enters it being no reference); the same test guards the lexical climb and the climb of `EffectCreationOwnerSetAround`. Measured: the 115 probes of the three reviews, the head against the fix (release, closed boundary): exactly `a4b`, `a4c`, `a4e` and `b5` move (certified → one SC6002 uncertifiable row each), every other probe is unchanged, no row lost. Fixture `owner-call-layer-stops` (the head certifies all six components; the fix files four rows and leaves the two controls silent: a root's named callback nothing references, a helper called from a plain function). Chrome (oracle case `owner-call-layer-stops`, the shapes at module scope because the oracle's entry hands every export to the real `render`, a hand-off B3 answers with a row below an exported component): the self-saving root is `unproven-clean` on the head and covered on the fix; the three N1 shapes are covered on both builds (a helper at module scope has no rendering role: the graph gives it `unowned-entry` and the ADR 0710 row stands), so the closed run of the fixture and the probes are N1's evidence. Fuzz: `er-rootself-apply` (the root at module scope): the head certifies the three programs, Chrome confirming, the fix none; `er-genhelper-apply`: recall-gap on both builds, so rediscovery.json lists an `outside` entry for N1 saying why. Corpus (34 projects, release): 0 rows added or removed against the B1 head, standard (126,670) and development (147,321) builds.

## ADR 0970 — The owner emission takes a function a reference enters for a layer like any other (batch 11, the follow-up of the review of #220)
`named_layer_entry_open` (ADR 0868), the emission's test of whether a layer around an owner-requiring operation (`onCleanup`, an effect, a context read, a render effect) may be entered by a route the owner graph holds no edge for, ended its walk at three places it took for proofs. It now adopts the premises the owner-call universe (ADR 0969) gave the same walk, each Chrome-confirmed (rc.21, the real oracle) as a certified program that throws. **(1) The component-render premise:** a function the census proves a component (it returns JSX, no call enters it; a function a reference also enters, an *escaped* component, included) was entered by renders alone, and the owner graph's owned context for it was read as every entry: `function view() { onCleanup(…); return <p/>; } … pick = view; setTimeout(() => pick!())` ran the cleanup with no owner (NO_OWNER_CLEANUP; NO_OWNER_EFFECT for an effect created there, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT for a context read), and main certified it. A component is now entered by renders alone only where every reference of its binding, in its file and the others, is a JSX tag (the opening and the closing name are one reference) and a tag or a call renders it (`entered_by_tags_only`); any other reference (`pick = view`, a prop, an array element, a `lazy` loader's module, a router's `component={…}`) is an entry the graph holds no edge for, so the function is a layer like any other and the operation keeps an uncertifiable SC4001 row (`owner-callers-unenumerated`). **(2) The stop at an owner-creating layer** (and at a control-flow child) returned before the function's references: `createRoot(function f() { if (!saved) { saved = f; return; } onCleanup(…) })`, then `saved()` from a timer, a handler or an effect's apply, runs the callback on its own stack under no owner (N2 of the check of B1 on #220); it holds only where nothing references the function (`referenced_only_by_entry`: a callback with no binding cannot be referenced, a named function expression is asked for the references of its own name). **(3) A generator's body** runs where an iterator is stepped, so a layer that is one, or a function its body calls (the caller walk follows a closed layer's calls out), is an open entry (B1, N1); the emission already answered a helper called from a generator's body on main with its generator-step obligation, so this one only makes the two walks agree. The emission and the universe now share one walk (`Premises` is gone: both ask the same question). **Measured** (34 projects, release, the branch stacked on #220 against #220's head, so only this change): standard build **+3,768** SC4001 uncertifiable `owner-callers-unenumerated` rows, development build +3,784 (the same 3,768 and 16 `package-finding-at-entry`), **0 removed, 0 violations added or removed**; almost all are components a router or a reference hands on (app-game 633, viviana-ui-web 326, donegeon-client 289, kui 3,000 over ten copies), and a component no reference enters in an open program (an unmounted export). Snapshots: 415 fixture projects move (+2,584 `owner-callers-unenumerated` and +29 `package-finding-at-entry` rows, one row renames its blocker from `execution-context-unaccounted`, no row lost, no violation moved); eight fixtures turn from certified to uncertifiable (`handed-root-patch-{definer-key-other,fresh,shadowed,unhanded}`, `path-alias-consumer`, `prefer-component-syntax-v2`, `rc21-created-anchor`, `tracer-corrected`), each an exported component no tag renders in the fixture's open program. **Chrome and the fuzzer:** oracle cases `owner-emission-component-by-reference` (main `unproven-clean` at five sites, the fix `covered-uncertifiable`) and `owner-emission-layer-stops` (the self-saving root: main `unproven-clean`, the fix covered; the helper called from a generator was covered on main already); cells `em-view-*`, `em-self-*` and `em-gen-*` (`scripts/fuzz/em-shapes.mjs`, three routes on a handler, a timer and an effect's apply, each with a never-run twin): main certifies 20 programs of `em-view` and `em-self` (rediscovery.json lists the ids by code, Chrome confirming), the fix none; `em-gen` is recall-gap on both builds; the legal twins of `view` and `self` become uncertifiable (the named cost). **Gate expectations that moved** (assertion-class edits, flagged for the review; no gate code changed except the cap): 34 ownership-case claims (checker-only, uncertifiable, in 32 cases, one classified a distinct claim over its TS2430), three tsc-oracle cases isolated with a `Root` component that renders theirs by tag (no `distinctFindings` added), the reproduction case `clean-lazy-route` held on the proof below (HELD_CAP 58 to 59: the reviewed raise the cap asks for; the case's `lazy` module is named only by `mod.Admin`). **The proof that ends most of this cost** is first in the proof batch: prove that a package (a router, `lazy`, `Dynamic`) renders a component under an owner, from its dependency source.

**The review of #221 (BLOCKED, and the fixes).** The Fable review of the head 69b38ff55 (`pr221-review/review.md`, probed read-only, no Chrome) found three shapes the walk still certifies where rc.21 warns (NO_OWNER_CLEANUP, NO_OWNER_EFFECT), all certified on #220's head and on main too: each is a stop that read symbol references where the census holds an entry no reference names. **B1, a function handed to a wrapper call:** the census takes `const Wrapped = hoc(() => { onCleanup(..); return <p/> })` for a component (`hoc_bound`: a JSX-returning function that is an argument in a binding's call initializer) whatever the wrapper does with it, and the walk's binding-less branch took any argument for a placed run; `hoc` calling it from a timer (or keeping it for a handler) runs it with no owner (`p5b`-`p5f`, `q7`). Fix: such a function (`function_may_be_component`, not an in-place call) is an open entry unless the call is a primitive's position (the whole argument of a primitive the dialect gives an owner for: `primitive_position`, the walk's own test moved out of its closure) or a standard-library call that runs it inline (`HandOff::Inline`); what a wrapper does with it is the proof batch's, like a router's. **B2, a module namespace:** `entered_by_tags_only` read symbol references only, and a namespace read by name or enumerated with no name (`Object.values(ns)`, an alias, a spread, `ns[key]`, a dynamic `import()`'s module, a re-export) names no symbol: the census (ADR 0347) holds it (`b2-min`, `b2-dyn`, `b2-handler`, `p3`, `p3l`). Fix: `entered_by_tags_only` is false for a function its module exports while the module's namespace is read by name or escapes with no name (`handed_out_without_reference`: `hands_out_by_name`, `escapes_unnamed`). The census is a closed program's, which the re-review of #221 below found out: in an open program it holds nothing. **B3, direct `eval`:** `program_has_eval()` was asked after the stop that closes a component entered by tags alone and the owner-creating stop, though a program that calls direct `eval` reaches any binding by name (`p16`, `p16b`); it is asked right after the generator test now, before both stops. **Measured** (34 projects, release, the fix against the head of #221; the share of each fix from one build with each switched off in turn, the all-off build equal to the head row for row): standard **+382** rows (378 SC4001 `owner-callers-unenumerated`, 2 SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` and 2 SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted`, the universe's silences sharing the walk), development +382 (the same), **0 removed, 0 violations**; B2 378 (kui 337, app-game 32, solid-groove 6, every-deck-of-cards 3: the components a `lazy` or `import()` loader hands the module of, whose namespace escapes), B1 4 (app-game's `createRootMapPool` callbacks), B3 0 (no direct `eval` in the corpus). **Snapshots:** five fixtures move, rows only added (+8 SC4001, +2 SC3001, no row lost, no violation): the new `owner-emission-eval`, `owner-emission-layer-stops` (B1's wrapped arrow, B2's `lib.tsx`), `package-access-helper` (`exported-mut.ts` walks the module's namespace with `Object.values`: B2), `rc17-callback-exports-mixed` (an effect in `dynamicComponent(() => ..)`: B1) and `wrapped-components` (`withTheme(({ name }) => <h1>{name}</h1>)`: B1). **Chrome and the fuzzer:** oracle cases `owner-emission-layer-stops` (the wrapped arrow), `owner-emission-namespace` and `owner-emission-eval` are `unproven-clean` on the head of #221 and `covered-uncertifiable` on the fix; cells `em-hoc-*`, `em-ns-*` and `em-eval-*` (three routes more, 36 contexts in all): the head certifies 30 programs (10 each, Chrome confirming), the fix none, and the legal twins of the three routes, clean on the head, become uncertifiable (the named cost; `rediscovery.json` lists the ids by code, nine entries). **Gate expectations that moved** (assertion-class edits, flagged): the five `wasm-parity` cases that run `Row.tsx` or the oracle's app each pin the one uncertifiable SC4001 row #221 gives them (an exported component no tag renders), and three `solid-facts-backend` process tests that took the owner rows for another rule's or for none (`arrow_bound_functions_get_the_same_owner_analysis_in_both_passes`, `joins_real_oxc_compiler_and_tsgo_facts`, `rust_cli_emits_snapshot_text_and_certification_exit_codes`) now read them as uncertifiable rows; the two test filters that dropped every SC4001 row use `owner_entry_row`.

**The re-review of #221 (BLOCKED again: R1, R2, R3).** The Fable re-review of b80d5ad57 (`pr221-review/rereview.md`, probed read-only) held B1 and B3 and found three false cleans left in B2's test; Chrome confirms each (oracle cases `owner-emission-specifier`, `owner-emission-open-namespace`, `owner-emission-open-importer`: `unproven-clean` on b80d5ad57, `covered-uncertifiable` on the fix). **R1, an export written as a specifier:** `module_exports` (`execution_role/write_roles.rs`), which B2 asked for the unnamed escape, took an export statement that contains the function, or Type Facts' export flag, for an export, and `function Comp() { .. } export { Comp }`, `export { Comp as Other }` and an arrow `const Comp` exported so have neither: they counted as unexported while the module's namespace was enumerated (`rr-alias2`, `rr-alias3`, `rr-alias5`). It asks `binding_exported` (an exported declaration, `export { name }`, `export default name`; the exact declaration the specifier's local resolves to) too. The test feeds the read, write and creation walks (`entered_by_unseen_code`, `site_reach`, `static_api`, `owners`, `value_use`, the upstream-compat callers test), so the same hole was a false clean there: in an open program `function helper() { return count(); } export { helper }` was certified legal where `export function helper` was an SC1001 obligation (probe `sp-read-spec`; fixture `exported-specifier-open-read`). **R2, B2 is off in an open program:** the namespace census is a closed program's (an open program's exports already have an unknown caller), and the component stop (`entered_by_tags_only`) asked the census only, so `b2-min` with the enumerating timer in the program was certified under an open boundary. **R3, the review's o1:** an exported component a local tag renders, in an open program, was certified, though an importer the program does not hold calls it with no owner (`rr-o1b`); the same export with no tag was an obligation, as a plain exported helper is. ## ADR 0971 — A JSX creation is an owner-call site (batch 11, B2 of the re-review of #220)

**The defect.** The owner-call universe (ADR 0969) listed calls. JSX has no call node, yet it creates a computation or a root as a call does (ADR 0883: an intrinsic's dynamic child, attribute or spread is a render effect, a fragment's dynamic child a memo, a component element runs `createComponent` under a root of its own), so a creation written as JSX was no site, and nothing ended it or filed it. The re-review of #220 (`probes2/r5c-r5f`) found a program that certifies on #220's head and on main and that Chrome rc.21 throws at: `pick = view; createEffect(() => 0, () => { pick!(); })` with `view` returning `<Inner />`, no creating call written anywhere. The tag runs on the apply's stack with no owner set and throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK (and the same tag under a leaf owner's callback is a forbidden creation, PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE). Fuzz: five `er-view-apply-jsx-*` programs (insert, attribute, spread, fragment, component) are false cleans on #220's head and none on this change; `rediscovery.json` lists them.

**The change.** `owners::universe_jsx_sites` lists the JSX creation sites: `jsx_sites`' (ADR 0883) minus the one kind that proves no creation (a static child that may hold a function, `MaybeRenderEffect`), once each by span, with what a component element around the site makes of it (the review of #225, F2; the amendment below): the first build left out every JSX written inside a component element's span (`in_getter`), which let two shapes certify. `proof_universe.rs` adds each to the `owner-call` table (`source` and `via` `jsx`, the element's name as an alternate span) with `jsx_site_codes`: PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE always, and PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK on a client build; the list and the owner stage's silences read that one definition. `owners/leaf_universe.rs::silences` takes its candidates from the calls and from the JSX sites alike (one pass over the file slots, `ir-read-lint` unchanged), so every silence, every decline and B3's gate (ADR 0967) answer a JSX site as they answer a creating call: no new silence, no new rule, no new blocker. A site nothing ends gets SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` and SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted`, never a violation. A site the effect-phase walk already rows (`viewDirect`: the tag in a function the apply calls directly) keeps that row.

**Gate change (judge, coordinator-approved 2026-11-13, narrow).** `scripts/lib/proof-log.mjs` `ownerCallDeclined` accepted a decline only beside the standing home row. A JSX site on the server arm of `isServer ? <ServerOnly /> : null` has its SC6002 home row removed by the projection's ExecutionPaths pass on a browser build (a client claim on code a client build never runs; fixture `rc21-arm-only-helper`), so the gate reported the site as ending in nothing. It now also accepts the code when that row was dropped by an ExecutionPaths `drop` at the site (the home row's own code, `uncertifiable` kind and blocker) that carries its typed `ClientRuntimeReach` premise, with the decline still required. An untyped drop, a drop of any other pass, a drop that is not the home row's own and a `reclass` line end nothing. Three unit tests (`scripts/proof-gate.test.mjs`): the typed drop ends the site (it fails on the old gate); an untyped drop ends nothing; a drop of another pass, or not the home row's, ends nothing (the last two pin that the change is no wider).

**Measured** (34 projects, release, this change against #221's head): standard **+27,904** rows (13,952 SC3001 and 13,952 SC6002, all uncertifiable), 1 removed; development +27,695, 76 removed; violations 218 and 212, unchanged, and no project's status moved. The 76 development rows removed are 69 `package-finding-at-entry:SC6002` and 6 `package-finding-at-entry:SC3001` rows (ADR 0949's hand-off of a package finding to the project site that enters the package) and one SC3001 flush row: each code stands at the same span (65 of them) or at the JSX element's covering span (11) as the site's own row. On #220's head the figures were +27,902 and +27,693 (1 and 76 removed). 83% of the declines the proof log records at JSX sites are `unread-package-may-run` (B3, policy A): a component or helper an unread package may run, and every export of an open program. Snapshots: 550 fixture projects move and 1 is new (`owner-call-jsx-sites`): +2,804 SC3001 and +2,815 SC6002 uncertifiable rows and no violation moved; 6 SC3001 rows are removed (a `flush()` in a prop arrow of a JSX element yields to the element's own row: `flush_accounting`'s `row_at` accepts a row that covers the flush, the looseness ADR 0969's open-work lists); five fixtures go from certified to uncertifiable (`rc21-dispatch-project-method`, `rc21-sync-exec-project`, `rc21-sync-project-focus`, `rc21-sync-shadowed-focus`, `row-handler-no-dispatch`: an exported component's JSX in an open program). Three wasm-parity cases (`w2-uncertifiable`, `w4-project-intact`, `w6-changed-fresh`) gain the two rows of their JSX creation and `proofObligations` +2; 76 ownership claims are added (38 SC3001, 38 SC6002; six are `distinct-claim` over TS2430, TS2322 and TS2786, each with its justification) and the tsc oracle's case 21 gains two `distinctFindings`. Chrome rc.21, `fixtures/runtime-oracle/owner-call-jsx-sites` (each reference written at module scope: the oracle's entry hands every export to `render`, so B3 keeps a row at every site written inside an exported component): PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at the component tag (`App.tsx:14:10`) is `unproven-clean` on #220's head and `covered-uncertifiable` on this change (the site's SC6002 row), and PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE at line 28 is covered by an SC3001 row.

**Pins (assertion-class edits, each only this change's new uncertifiable rows; listed for the review).** Sixteen backend process tests count rows the new sites add. `rule_quality_process::eslint_plugin_solid_two_corpus_matches_native_rule_semantics`: SC3001 +21, pinned per file for the seven files. `sessions_process::joins_real_oxc_compiler_and_tsgo_facts`: the tracer's findings +2. `sessions_process::rust_cli_emits_snapshot_text_and_certification_exit_codes`: the violation is asserted, not the first row; the corrected program certifies as a closed program, and as an open one it is uncertifiable, with the four SC3001 and SC6002 rows beside ADR 0970's owner obligations. **Amendment (the review of #225: F1, F2; Fable, BLOCKED on F1; F2 a false clean on the base and the head).**

*F1 (a regression).* `flush_accounting::row_at` ended a flush's code on any row that covered it, and B2 adds an owner-call row at every JSX element an unread package may run, so a `flush()` in a multi-line prop arrow of such an element lost its own SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` row: the element's row covers the flush by span but is reported at the element's start, where the judge places a multi-line finding, so no row stood at the flush, and rc.21 throws FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK there (an unread package's component running `props.render()` in a `createTrackedEffect` callback). `row_at` takes only a row that starts where the flush starts: a covering row of another site, or an inner row at a later position, is another site's. The six SC3001 flush rows the first build removed (`phase-handed-by-name` x5, `rc9-heldout-execution-shapes`) and the seven of ADR 0969 (`resolve-inline-entries`, `slot-run-effect-phase`: the row at a `resolve` or `until` inside the call) return, and so do seven more of the same looseness: a `flush(() => { … })` whose callback holds another row (`flush-write-path`: SC3001 and SC2008, `leaf-generator-step`, `pending-read-unresolved`, `stored-throw-class-member-wrapper`: SC2006, SC3001 and SC2008) had its own accounting ended by the inner row (20 rows in all). It does not close `Errored`'s `fallback`, the dialect's one function prop position (not a control-flow child): there the test costs one SC6002 uncertifiable row per site, named or anonymous, never a violation and never a silence. The first wording of this bullet, and the re-check's note N1, read the test as keeping a row for `arguments.callee` and then as changing no outcome; the follow-ups of that re-check measured both positions (fixture `owner-call-inplace-escapes`: `ErroredReadsArguments` keeps its row, `ForReadsArguments` ends in a silence, `ErroredQuiet`, the same fallback that never reads `arguments`, is no site).

The in-place function positions are the dialect's: the new `Dialect::control_flow_prop_function_run(primitive, prop)` (rc.21, `solid.dev.js`: `Errored`'s `fallback`, called as `f(err, reset)` at any arity; `children` as `control_flow_child_run` says: `For` and `Repeat` always, `Show` and `Match` under `Switch` with a parameter) and the function child written as the element's only child at run time (a comment is none: the corpus's kui `Show`s have them), with `runs_as_child` (a generator's body runs where its iterator is stepped: B5, the review's note, handled with it: a generator handed to `For` type-checks only with a cast, so it has no cell). A function in any other prop, and `Show`'s function child with no parameter (`NonZeroParams` rejects it against the real typings; a parameter with a default or only `this` counts for none: `Function.length`), is a site like any other: fourteen rows (seven sites) in the fixtures, none on the corpus.

<a id="adr-0972"></a>
## ADR 0972 — A package that cannot reach Solid cannot call an action
SC2002 placed only actions the program creates. An installed package the build does not read as source (a standard build reads none; a development build reads the packages whose manifest names a Solid package, ADR 0297) can call Solid's `action` itself: `runStep(cb)` is `action(function* () { cb(); })()` in a package whose manifest names no Solid package. Chrome (rc.21) throws `ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE` at `runStep(() => {})` in a component body, a memo's compute and a `createRoot` body, and main certified all three (`patterns/pkgaction/reach-*`). Owner ruling (option B, fail closed): **each project call into such a package's code is an SC2002 site, silent only where the package's source proves it cannot reach a Solid action.**

**Premise.** A package the build does not read runs only its own code and what it loads. If none of that, followed as written, names a Solid package, and nothing in it loads code by a computed name, generates code or reads a global the host's libraries do not declare, it cannot reach `action`. A function the program hands it is the hand-off's (ADRs 0949, 0967). Solid's own runtime (the dialect's `primitive_defining_packages`) calls no `action` of its own (checked on the pinned rc.21 `@solidjs/signals`, `solid-js` and `@solidjs/web` dist: `action(` appears only in documentation comments); its catalog answers for its exports. Code no installed package holds (a `declare module` shim in a project declaration file) cannot reach this build's Solid instance unless the program hands it the function, so it is no site: the import's attested file stands for a shim's package. A global a declaration file declares is not this: it says nothing of who provides it (ADR 0974).

**Fact.** `solid-facts/src/module_reach.rs` scans one runtime file with Oxc (never text): its loads (static `import`, `export … from`, `require("…")` of the unbound `require`, literal `import()`, `import x = require()`) and its hazards: a computed load (`import(x)`, `require(x)`, `require` as a value, `module.require`, `import.meta.glob`), code generation (`eval`, the `Function` constructor, a call, `new`, store or hand-off of a `.constructor` member), a read of an unbound name the pinned TypeScript's `lib.es*`/`lib.dom*` files do not declare (`module_reach/known_globals.txt`, generated from the tsrs revision the producer pins; a static member of the global object counts as that name, a computed one or an escaping use of it is a hazard), and a file Oxc does not parse. `typeof x` reads nothing; a plain assignment writes; CommonJS's `exports`, `__filename`, `__dirname` and `module.exports`/`id`/`hot`/`loaded` hold no code.

**Walk.** `solid-facts-backend/src/package_reach.rs` decides each installed package (under `node_modules`) the project's facts name a declaration in (a call's resolved declaration outside the standard library, a referenced symbol's declarations, an attested import's file, by its link's `node_modules` spelling for a workspace package), keyed by the package directory under the last `node_modules`; a workspace package linked into `node_modules` has its declarations at the link's real path, in no `node_modules`, so the backend finds each link from the attested imports (the real directory of the link's package root, which the compiler's own resolved path lies in: `PackageReachIndex::linked`) and a declaration there is spelled by the link, where the package's verdict stands (`linked_spelling`; the review of the first head found `kernel.run(cb)` on an object a linked package made, with no site: fixture `action-in-owned-scope-linked-package`); a linked package whose source the program analyzes is project code, read and not assumed; `@types/<name>` stands for the `<name>` Node finds from it (`@types/node` for the host's builtins, which are no package code). Entries are a superset of any resolver's choice (every `exports` target under every condition, patterns expanded, `main` where it names something, `module`, a `browser` map's files, else `index.js`), so no host's conditions are assumed. Loads are followed as a bundler follows them (relative paths with extensions and `index`, `#imports`, Node's lookup and self-reference to the package's entries, a Node builtin to nothing). **Clear** when the closure has no Solid load and no hazard; **reaches-solid** at the first Solid load (a package of the dialect's ecosystem scope, `@solidjs/*`, counts); **undecided** at the first hazard, a load nothing installed answers (`missing-source`), a `.node` or `.wasm` file (`native-module`), a file type a bundler plugin compiles, an unread manifest or more than 20,000 files. Scans are kept per process by path, length and modification time. The verdicts travel in the package boundary (`PackageBoundary::package_reach`, fingerprinted). The WASM `checkSync` entry reads no filesystem, so it has none and every such call is `no-filesystem`: uncertifiable there and decided natively, the one WASM difference; the owned entry reads the mounted tree as native does.

**Site and row.** `solid-reactive-ir/src/package_action_calls.rs`: a call, `new`, tagged template, non-intrinsic JSX tag (a member of an import, or a name that only aliases one: `const View = Pkg.Comp`) or an import binding handed on as a value (`const run = runStep`, `[1].map(Pkg.fn)`, `{ runStep }`, a namespace passed whole; one the compiler types non-callable, or whose declaration is type-level, is no function) enters code of such a package when the code its callee runs is the package's: the callee's **origin**, never where its signature type is declared. The origin is the import its root names, followed through the member chain, the call or `new` that made the value and the project binding of one initializer (`const handle = makeHandle()`, six hops: `origin_of`), through a project module's re-export to the package function the compiler's resolution ends on (a barrel), to a project declaration file with runtime JavaScript the program does not analyze (`vendor/step.d.ts` beside `vendor/step.js`, `allowJs` off: `unanalyzed-project-js`, never decided: the review of #231 found Chrome throwing there), and to the callee's own declaration only where the chain ends in something it does not follow (a parameter, a property, the result of a project function). The host answers only where it is proven: a bare global the standard library declares (`new Float32Array(4)` under babylonjs's augmentation was about 270 wrong rows: the constructor is the host's, whatever a package adds to its type) and a member whose every declaration is the standard library's; a member a package adds to the global's type and installs (`window.fzRun`, `Uint8Array.fzFrom`) is not, and falls to its declaration. The result of a host or runtime call (`untrack`, `useContext`, `createMemo`, `Object.freeze`, `Object.assign`) is not followed (it may hand back what it was given or a value a package made), so the callee's declaration decides as before, except a host constructor's fresh object; an array literal has the origin of its elements, a call of a project function the origin of what it returns, a member of a namespace import of the project's own module the origin its own symbol resolves to (a barrel's re-export), and a call's result handed on as an argument is a site at the receiving call. A relative import the compiler resolved to no analyzed source (a declaration file, an ambient `declare module "*.vendor.js"`) names a runtime file the bundler loads; when it exists and the program does not analyze it, the import is undecided. The origin is installed code: a file under `node_modules` or in a linked workspace package that the build does not read (not the standard library, not a package read as source nor a JavaScript file the program analyzes, not the dialect's runtime, not a call of what a dialect primitive returns, not a reviewed test runner's registration, not an import the compiler could not resolve, which TypeScript reports and the boundary's SC9005 stands for). A value handed on is a site when it is a reference to such an import or to a project binding that holds what one makes and the compiler types callable, or a member of any import object (`[…].forEach(kernel.run)`) the compiler types callable (a property signature's kind says nothing: a function and a number share it); the row stands at the call that receives it, where a throw has its project frame. With a verdict that is not clear it is an `action` site of the proof universe (ADR 0936). It is placed by SC2002's own classifier (`semantic_write_execution_role`, `handed_write_execution`, `RootBodyGuard::Rejects`; reachability as ADR 0715): a role that allows an action ends it silently (`package_action_calls…role-allows`), a call that cannot run likewise (`cannot-run`), anything else is an uncertifiable SC2002 row `package-may-call-action:<why>`, never a violation. A render always runs the component's body under an owner, and a function handed on as a value runs where nothing here follows, so both have no legal role; the value of an intrinsic element's event attribute and a direct argument of a standard-library fresh-stack scheduler (`setTimeout(runStep, 0, cb)`) are the host's and silent. An import the attestation does not cover is `unattested` (undecided). In a package read as source the row is located in package code and stands at the project's entry (ADR 0949).

**Inline actions.** The probes for this ADR found a second hole: `action(step)(…)`, the call of what an `action(…)` call returns, had no site and no row (Chrome throws in a body; `patterns/pkgaction/inline-*`), in the project and in a package read as source (where the named form was already re-reported at the project's call). It is now an action invocation placed as a bound action's call (`local_access.rs`, `push_inline_action_invocation`; `Dialect::returns_action` names the primitive) and a universe site.

*Not followed* (named in `docs/open-work.md`): a getter a package declares (`void clock.now`: a declaration file does not tell a getter from a data property; ADR 0974 reads the closure for it); a member read where the compiler gives no callability (a value handed anywhere but as a call's argument); an implicit call (an iterator, `toString`) of a package's object; an origin the walk cannot finish where the callee's own declaration is the standard library's (a value a host or runtime call returns that is not in ADR 0974's table of calls that carry an argument; an object literal's member, a method, a field, a conditional, a returned parameter and a cap are followed by ADR 0974), an asset import typed `string` handed on in a JSX attribute (a value row: the compiler's callability is not asked there); a member declared in a linked workspace package no attested import of the project names (a workspace package reached only through another's declarations has no link to map; the entry call that made the object stands, and its package's closure includes the other); an action value an `action(…)` call returns that the program stores anywhere but a binding (an object's member, a hook's return without transport). **Counterexamples to the `Clear` proof, found by the review of #231** (Chrome throws, no row): the global object reached by one member and then back to itself (`window.self.__act`, `globalThis.globalThis`, `document.defaultView`), a global-only `@types` package whose global a Solid-reaching package provides, and a package component loaded lazily (`lazy(() => import("pkg"))`) are closed by ADR 0974, as is the getter above; a sloppy `this` and a builtin prototype a package extends stay named there.

*Measured* (rc.21 corpus, 34 projects, release, `--internal`; origin/main `302d92b43` against this change `441cf0001`; every program of both builds, one producer): standard uncertifiable 171,545 to **183,847 (+12,302**, all SC2002 `package-may-call-action`), development build 191,307 to **203,882 (+12,575**: 11,812 `package-may-call-action` and 763 `package-finding-at-entry:SC2002`, the second the rows in the code of a package the build reads as source that ADR 0949 stands again at the project's entry); violations 218 and 212 unchanged, 0 rows removed. By blocker (standard / development): `unknown-global` 4,714 / 4,577, `code-generation` 3,628 / 3,628, `reaches-solid` 1,821 / 1,384, `global-object-escape` 1,625 / 1,621, `dynamic-load` 490 / 578, `missing-source` 7 / 7, `unanalyzed-project-js` 17 / 17; by entry (standard): call 9,936, value 1,508, render 659, tag 199; 166 packages in 23 apps (standard). Time: the sums of the 34 runs are 145.3 s to 171.5 s (standard) and 247.0 s to 245.5 s (development build) on a shared machine; the closure walk reads each file once per process. The first head measured +10,801 standard; the review of #231 (origin of the callee's value, barrels, project JavaScript, members handed on) moved it to +11,976 (value entries 311 to 1,272; the babylonjs host-constructor rows, about 270, are the host's and gone), and the re-check (the host proof, a host or runtime call's result, namespace barrels, array elements, project function returns, wildcard shims) to +12,302. The walker's first corpus run (superset entries) held 13,506 standard rows: the refinements above (entries from the imported subpaths, `.ts` sources for `.js` specifiers, scripts only for a `./*` pattern, a store slot's root, `.constructor` and dead export hints, type references, asset queries, host-global `@types`) moved rows between blockers and removed 539; what remains is the ruling's own price (a Solid package's closure, a global the pinned libs do not declare, a computed or escaping use of the global object, real code generation). Accepted trade (owner ruling 2026-11-13, option B): every call into such a package in an owned scope is uncertifiable until a declared host reads the package as source or a premise names its behavior.

## ADR 0973 — Every read and call that may run a project function, written after an async function's own suspension, ends, or is uncertifiable (batch 11, slice 9B)
**The defect (a net's hole).** SC1002 (UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT) is raised for a reactive read a continuation runs after one of its async function's own suspensions. Its producers (`static_rules/after_await.rs`) walk from the tracked async computations they find (ADRs 0195, 0318, 0963, 0964, 0961) and file a row where they prove or cannot decide; a read or a call written after an `await` in any other async function (an event handler, a helper no computation calls, a test callback) had no row and no record of why, so the claim was answered only for the sites a walk chose to visit. ADR 0961 (parameter initializers), ADR 0963 (members a continuation runs without a call) and ADR 0964 (functions the program stored) are nets on chosen shapes, not a universe: they list no site and name no ending.

**The change.** `after_await_accounting.rs` (its own typed endings and its own universe, like `flush_accounting.rs`, ADR 0966, and ADRs 0838 and 0886; no `SiteSilence`, no premise kind, no entry in the proof-lint PRODUCERS list and no new lint-baseline entry: owner rulings 3 and 4) is run once per build after the flush accounting, over the final rows. Its universe is the one `site_accounting::account` already lists (the function now returns it): every read of `proof_universe`'s `read` table, and every call that may run a project function, written directly in an `async` function after one of that function's own suspensions (`may_follow_suspension`: an `await`, an implicit suspension, a loop that repeats one), outside dependency source. By how the callee is named (the `via` of the candidate line): `call` and `member` (the walk's own resolver, `execution_role::project_callee_at_parameter`, ADRs 0278, 0279, 0299, 0314, finds a project function and the call runs it **exactly**: an identifier whose name still holds it, a module namespace's member, a method of a `const` object literal nothing writes a member of, of an instance of the exact class that declares it); `inexact` and `inexact-member` (it finds one and an override or a replacement may run instead: a `let` the program reassigns, `this.helper()`, a receiver typed as a class, a spread in the first argument); `invocation` (a function value no exact declaration resolves: a parameter, a stored callback, a call's result, a member slot no function body defines, ADR 0964's shape, taken first, so a `let` the program reassigns is one whatever its initializer is); `iife` (a function literal called where it is written, `(() => …)()`, `(async () => …)()`); `apply` (a standard call that runs a function value its receiver or arguments name: `f.call(…)`, `f.apply(…)`, `Reflect.apply(f, …)`, `Reflect.construct`; `bind` runs nothing where it is called); `project` and `unresolved` (any other call the resolver names no project function for and that is no outside code, below: a project declaration it withholds, ADR 0299's receiver census over a method, a computed or an optional member, an arrow property of a module-scope `const` object literal; or no declaration at all). Not sites: a `.then` continuation or a callback a later microtask runs, a read in a nested function (that function's own site), a tagged template's tag, a call of a primitive; and the four named below. A function a reviewed test runner schedules is a function like any other (owner ruling 9b, slice 9B decision 1): its sites are sites. The members were added at the coordinator's ruling (2026-11-13: a call that is a silent miss is what "unproven is uncertifiable" targets).

**One arm skips a call, and it is narrow.** The first build left every call the resolver names no project function for through a `continue`; the review of #233 found what left through it (B2: a method, a computed and an optional member and an arrow property of a module-scope literal; B3: `f.call`, `f.apply`, `Reflect.apply` and an immediately invoked function literal, each Chrome-confirmed). It now skips a call only when the callee is shown to be outside the project or Solid's own: a construct (a constructor runs where no call shows, ADR 0963's member route); an accessor, a setter, an action or a typed candidate (a read of the universe, or a rule of its own); a callee whose resolved declaration is the standard library's or an installed package's (it runs project code only through what it is handed or a protocol the project's objects implement: a callback, a getter, a listener, a thenable); and, where the call demanded no resolved-call fact (an argumentless call), a callee whose own symbol the compiler declares only in a package or a default library file (`expect(x).toBeNull()`: the matcher an installed package declares). The first version of that last test did not exist and every such call was `unresolved`: 1,723 rows in the standard build, 1,137 of them test matchers. The symbol is a fact every call's callee already demands, so no demand was added (extra resolved declarations move other analyses, ADR 0192). The four skipped families are holes of their own, each Chrome-confirmed and **named in `docs/open-work.md`, not closed here** (the review's S1 to S3): a no-call run written in the async function itself where no computation is recognized (a getter, a coercion, an iterator, a Proxy, a constructor, a tagged template), a project callback the standard library or a package runs synchronously (`forEach`, `sort`, `Array.from`, `Promise` executors), and a `.then` continuation of a non-async compute.

A site ends in a row of SC1002 that stands at exactly its span or one of its alternates (the exact span: a row that covers the site from another position is another site's, the lesson of ADR 0971's F1), an SC9012 there, the compiler's discard, or a typed reason (`AfterAwaitSafe`, ids `after_await_accounting.account.<end>`, `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE`, a `silent` line of SC1002 in the proof log). A row of another rule at the span ends nothing (SC1001's row for the same read claims another code). A site no ending holds gets an uncertifiable row of SC1002, blocker `read-after-await-unaccounted`: a static defect of the rule's own kind with the new obligation `AfterAwaitObligation::Unaccounted` (SC1002 is emitted through the static-defect channel, so the dialect words the reason, `solid-v2-rules`; a static violation there panics), never a violation, never a silence.

**One reason: the site never runs** (`SiteReach`): none on the corpus. **There is no callee reason.** The first build had one, owner-ruled: a call of a project function whose whole transitive closure reads no reactive source ended its site, in a program whose member-route net runs. The review of #233 found it unsound, with Chrome-confirmed programs the build was silent on and a proof line (`AfterAwaitSafe::CalleeReadsNothing`) that was false: the closure is a list of reads and calls, and a read reaches a continuation through values no call shows, a store read through an alias binding, a stored generator object stepped by a spread, a `for…of` or a destructuring, a Proxy trap or a getter installed through a handler or a descriptor declared apart (the inline spellings have a row of their own at the read, the net's), a props alias (the oracle case `after-await-closure`). Making it exact asks for facts the checker does not have (which values are plain data: an alias of a store or props value, a generator object and a value handed to a Proxy or `defineProperty` by reference would have to count as "reads possibly", and the argument types at the call as well), so the call keeps its row. It cost the 575 calls it ended (610 in the development build). **There is no census reason** either. Owner ruling 2 asked for one (no tracked async computation in the program, `holds_suspending`, the census of ADR 0963, and no package nothing here reads may run the function), the first build had it, it ended none of the corpus' sites, and Chrome showed it silently ends a read that runs as a computation: `async function work` handed by identifier to a project wrapper (`function track(compute) { return createMemo(compute); }`, `track(work)`) is a start the producers' index does not find (ADR 0873's `handed_compute` follows a function literal and an arrow through the wrapper, not a function declaration), and so are `createMemo.call(undefined, work)`, `Reflect.apply(createMemo, undefined, [work])` and `[createMemo][0](work)`; rc.21 reports UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT at each read (the oracle cases `after-await-universe-census-*`), main has only SC1001's `function-run-unplaced` row there, a row of another rule. Every site in a program the census calls computation-free keeps its row (the fixture `after-await-universe-census`); a reason there needs a proof that no computation runs the function (no value use of it, callers only module-level code or such functions), not the absence of a recognized start.

**Package entry rows.** A package finding the attribution seam (`package_drop::hand_off`, ADR 0949) hands to the project call that enters the package function holds the site with its own row (`package-finding-at-entry:SC1002`). The accounting's row at that call is a placeholder, no "finding of the rule already at the site": the entry row stands beside it, and nothing is dropped (a first version dropped the placeholder where the entry row stood, and proof-lint's `finding-filter` and proof-gate's `package-drop-unattributed` named it).

**Measured** (34 projects, release builds, current main 45c56c08d against this head, plain runs). Standard build: **183,847 to 190,085 uncertifiable rows (+6,238)**, no row removed, **violations 218 to 218** (none added, none removed), every added row `SC1002 uncertifiable read-after-await-unaccounted`. Development build: 203,882 to 210,097 (+6,215), none removed, violations 212 to 212. Project statuses unchanged. By kind of site (standard): a call of a project function 5,076 (575 of them the callee reason would have ended), a call of a function value 423, an inexact member 404, an exact member 117, a read 91, a project declaration the resolver withholds 72, no declaration 41, a name the program rewrote 11, a function literal called in place 3, `f.call` and kin 0; 4,157 in test files (3,717 in the callbacks of a reviewed runner: `it`, `test`), 2,081 elsewhere. Timing (sum of the per-project times, main then this head, back to back): standard 176,229 ms to 174,148, development 276,051 to 276,503: no measurable overhead. The session bench (`verify-performance`, best first-IR time per source, interleaved with main's build under the same load): main 169,226, 169,666 and 171,056 ns, this head 170,527, 172,538 and 171,657, and the enforcing run passes (171,813 against the limit of 175,000; main's own bench is about 170,000 now, it was about 162,000 at 302d92b43). The first measurement of this review's fixes filed 1,723 `unresolved` rows (the arm without the symbol test above), 7,867 in all (+7,867 against main).

**A known issue of main, not of this change.** With `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_PROOF_LOG` on, main itself drops one development-build row, `SC9012 standard-member-impostor` at expenses-app `src/lib/clerk.tsx:49` (`@solidjs/router` `query.js:517`): 1,538 findings without the log and 1,537 with it, on main (177402dfb) and on this change alike; the documented invariant that the findings are byte-identical with and without the proof log does not hold for that row. Every number above comes from runs without the proof log; the candidate counts come from the log's own account. The coordinator queued it as its own item.

**Fixtures and tests.** `after-await-universe` (the sites that keep the row: a handler, a helper, calls of project functions whatever their callee does, through a namespace import, a `let` the program reassigns, exact and inexact members, `for await`; the review's B1 shapes in a recognized computation, B2 and B3 in a function started through a wrapper; and what stays without a row, a standard-library call, a setter and a construct), `after-await-universe-none` (the never-runs reason, and four pure calls that keep theirs: no callee reason) and `after-await-universe-census` (a program with no recognized computation keeps every row: its functions, an export, a pure call that reaches a getter, and the wrapper hazard); the mutation test of the reason and the pins of what the arm skips (`after_await_accounting_process`); unit tests of the ids; the oracle cases `after-await-universe` (a getter, a coercion, an iterator, a Proxy trap and a class getter a callee reaches: each read keeps a row, and the call too), `after-await-members` (a project method called after the await of a tracked async computation), `after-await-closure` (B1: a store alias, a stored generator, a trap and a getter installed by reference, a props alias), `after-await-calls` (B2 and B3 in functions started through a wrapper), `after-await-universe-census-{call,reflect,element,wrapper}` (a tracked async computation started through `Function.prototype.call`, `Reflect.apply`, an array element, and a function declaration handed to a wrapper: Chrome raises the code at each read, main has no SC1002 row there, each keeps its row now) and `after-await-universe-census-callee` (the same hidden start, the read in a getter a pure callee reaches: the call's row covers it).

**Fuzz.** The shape family `cs-*` (`scripts/fuzz/cs-shapes.mjs`): the read after the `await` of an async function the program starts as a tracked async computation, on `createMemo` and `createEffect`. Four hidden starts (a wrapper's parameter, `.call`, `Reflect.apply`, an array element), crossed with two routes (the read written in the started function, or in a getter it reaches through a project function); the review's routes over one hidden start (B2: `-ns-method`, `-ns-arrow`, `-ns-computed`, `-ns-optional`; B3: `-dotcall`, `-apply`, `-reflect`, `-iife`, `-iife-fn`, `-iife-async`) and over a recognized one (B1: `-gen`, `-proxy-ref`, `-defprop-ref`); each with its two twins (`-never` starts nothing, `-before` reads ahead of the await): 42 misuse programs in `mx-recall` and 84 twins in `lg-recall`. The store-alias and props-alias shapes of B1 are not cells: their site is a store or props read through an alias, which the checker lists as no read at all (S4 of the review, open-work), so the generator has no marked site to place; the oracle case holds them. Four entries in `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json` list the ids (`mx-untracked-read-after-await-cs-<form>-<host>[-<route>]-x-direct-none`): the hidden starts, the getter route, B1, B2 and B3. On main 45c56c08d all 42 misuse programs are false clean (SC1001's row is the only finding at the read; the Chrome host and the real oracle agree: 126 comparisons, 0 differences); the build under review (e241aa9bd) is false clean on the 26 programs of the review's routes (B1: 6, B2: 8, B3: 12) and recall-gap on the 16 earlier ones; this build (release, sha256 4d3da3bddf38…) is recall-gap on all 42, and the 84 twins are uncertifiable or clean on every build, 0 false positive. `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json` holds six entries: the hidden starts, the getter route, B1, B2, B3, and the shapes that are no cell.

**Open** (each in `docs/open-work.md`). The review's S1 to S4, found Chrome-confirmed and decided out of this change: the no-call run written directly in the async function where no computation is recognized, a project callback the standard library or a package runs synchronously, a `.then` continuation of a non-async compute, and a store read through an alias that the read universe lists as no read (a false clean of main, in a recognized computation too). The rows the walk or another SC1002 row already answers are filed twice (the review's S5: `new GoogleAuthProvider()` at the `new` and at the callee, `release!()` at two spans); accepted noise. About 6.2k rows are the named cost, ended later by proofs and not by trusting a name: the test runner's own source (the proof batch's 1b), the standard library's value-only calls (`new Set`, `Math.min`, `toUpperCase`: reviewed tables exist, ADRs 0211 and 0320, and would end them given the argument types), a sound callee reason (value facts: which values are plain data), and the router and package render entries. A census reason would need the closure proof above; the producers' hand-off does not follow a function declaration handed by identifier through a wrapper's parameter (a recall follow-up).
