## ADR 0974 — The Clear proof follows the global object, the globals a declaration names, lazy components and getters; the origin walk follows a value to where it was made and says where it stops (the reviews of #231: B4, B5, S2, S6, and the second re-check)
The review of #231 ran Chrome (rc.21) against the `Clear` silence of ADR 0972 and found programs it certified that throw `ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE`: the global object reached by one member and back (`window.self.__fzAct`), a global a package provides that a global-only `@types` package declares, a package component loaded by `lazy(() => import("pkg"))`, and a getter a package declares (`void clock.now`); the project-declared and augmented forms of the second were found closing it. Coordinator ruling (2026-11-13): close these four and keep a sloppy `this` and a builtin prototype a package extends named, since neither is exact without a fact of the whole program (no package writes the shared object); the walk reads the whole closure, so a proof that discharges one hazard still sees the next (S6); a getter is no site only where the whole closure is read, defines no accessor by any form and takes no value from outside.

**The global object.** `solid-facts/src/module_reach.rs` (`global_use`) follows the global object through every member that gives it back: the names it goes by (`globalThis`, `window`, `self`, `top`, `parent`, `frames`, `global`), read as a static or string-literal member of one of them, and `document.defaultView` (so `window.self.x`, `window.window.x`, `globalThis.globalThis.x` and `window.document.defaultView.x` are `window.x`). A member read off the end of the chain that no pinned library declares is an unknown-global hazard, the global object itself used as a value at any step (an alias, an argument, a computed key) is the escape hazard, a plain assignment reads nothing, and any other use of `document` holds no global object.

**Globals a declaration names.** A call of a global some declaration file declares says nothing of who provides it: the host, a script or a package that writes it (`fz-pub` sets `window.__fzAct`; Chrome threw at `__fzAct(cb)` and at `window.__fzAct(cb)` in a body). Three origins that were silent are now undecided, `package-may-call-action:unknown-global`: a package of global declarations only (`declares_only_globals`: the entry holds no import, export or module declaration, as `@types/webxr` and `@types/google.maps`; `@types/node` stays the host's by its manifest, named), a global only a project declaration file declares (`declare function`, `declare var`), and a member of a global the standard library declares that only a declaration adds (`interface Window { __act(cb: () => void): void }`, `globalThis.__act`: the compiler's symbol of the property name decides, else the call's resolved declaration). `Origin::Host` is a standard-library global; `PackageReachIndex::for_declaration` answers the pseudo-path `ambient:<file>` as unknown-global, and a member of a global the library declares is the host's where the library alone declares the member (`window.setTimeout`); a member or an overload a package adds to the global's type (`Uint8Array.from` with a package's overload) is that package's, and a member only a project declaration file adds is ambient (the re-check of ADR 0972 made `Host` a proof, and `Runtime` the dialect's and `node:`'s).

**Lazy components.** The component `lazy(loader)` makes is the code of the module its loader imports. `lazy_origin` reads the loader's function literal for its dynamic imports (`() => import("pkg")`, `() => import("pkg").then((m) => ({ default: m.View }))`): a runtime module is no package's, a relative module is the project's own unless JavaScript the program does not analyze stands behind it (an ambient wildcard shim: `import("./view.vendor.js")` is `unanalyzed-project-js`, found as the static import of such a file is, `imports_of_unread_js` reading dynamic imports too), a package's is that package's (the first of several whose closure is not clear), and a specifier that is not a literal, or is rooted (`/x.js`, a path only the bundler resolves), is `computed-load:` (undecided, `dynamic-load`). `Origin::Lazy` marks the value: rendering or calling it enters the package, a member of it (`Lazy.preload`) is the dialect's wrapper.

**The whole closure (S6).** `Walk` reads every file of the closure: a hazard, an unreadable file or a load of Solid ends that branch only (a Solid package is the dialect's runtime and is not walked), problems accumulate (distinct, at most 256) and the first in walk order is the verdict as before, so no row changed blocker. What a later file holds is known whatever an earlier one did.

**Getters.** `ModuleScan::accessors` lists every way a file defines an accessor: class and object-literal `get`/`set`, `accessor` fields, `Object.defineProperty` and `Reflect.defineProperty` with a literal name and a descriptor that names a `get` or `set` (a data descriptor defines none), `defineProperties` and `Object.create(proto, descriptors)` over a literal map, `__defineGetter__` and `__defineSetter__`; a name the syntax does not fix (a computed key, a descriptor that is a variable, `defineProperty` read as a value, a `Proxy`) matches every name. `PackageReachIndex::accessors` holds, per closure, the names, whether one matches every name, and `closed`: the whole closure was read and holds no problem but a load of Solid's runtime (any other leaves code or a value nobody read). A member of an object a package made, evaluated for its value (`void clock.now`, `typeof clock.now`, an assignment: not a callee, a tag, the object of a longer chain, or a type or import position) or read by an object pattern (`const { now } = made`: each key it names, nested patterns too, a computed key or a rest element any; an array pattern reads the iterator and is not followed; the site is the pattern, where the runtime reports the getter's call, not the value it reads) is an `Entry::Read` site unless the closure is closed, defines no accessor under a name of the chain and none under an unfixed name; a Clear closure needs none (it names no Solid package). It is placed as a call is (`semantic_write_execution_role` at the read, `cannot-run` where nothing may run it), the row stands at the read, and a global a project declares has none (its provider is no closure).

**The origin walk (the second re-check of #231: 18 programs Chrome throws on and #231 certified, B1–B4, S1–S3).** What a call runs comes from where its value was made (`origin_of`); the walk is exact where it follows and says so where it stops. *B1:* a host global is silent only when the signature the compiler resolved for the call is the standard library's, so a package's overload of a global (`setTimeout(cb, "fz")`, `new Float32Array("fz", cb)`, which the package replaces where it loads) is the package's, and a property only a package declares is the package's whatever type it has (`fzHook: VoidFunction`; the old early return on a standard-library signature is gone). The rule "every declaration of a global is the library's" was measured and not taken: `@types/node` declares `setTimeout`, `URL` and the rest again, so every such call in a project with Node types would be a row (`feature-topics`: `URL.createObjectURL` at once). *B2:* a standard-library function that hands back, wraps or merges what it is given carries a package's argument (`CARRIES_ARGUMENT`, by the qualified name of the declaration the call resolves to: `Object.assign`, `freeze`, `seal`, `preventExtensions`, `setPrototypeOf`, `Array.from`, `Array.of`, `new Proxy`); a `Proxy` is not a fresh host object. *B3:* a project module's namespace is `Origin::Namespace` and is followed through an alias, a destructuring slot, a nested `export * as` and the module's exports (`export_origin`: its own `const`s, `export { a as b } from`, `import` then `export {}`, `export *`, with a cycle guard and a memo per name) to the package's import. *B4:* `imports_of_unread_js` reads `export … from` and dynamic imports too, and `join_relative` drops a `?query` or `#fragment` (the bundler serves the file whatever it says). *S1:* every cap ends in a row, never in silence: a question may take 48 hops and 4,096 steps, an array, a function's returns, a call's arguments and a module's `export *` are read to 256, and what is not finished is `package-may-call-action:origin-limit` (`ReachBlocker::OriginLimit`, pseudo-path `origin-limit:`), not followed by reads (a limit names no closure). A conditional, logical or comma operand, a returned parameter (the argument the call passed), a method or a field of a project object literal or class instance, and a nested array are followed. *S2:* the row stands at the call. *S3:* each program is in the pattern lane (`pkgaction/*`) and the new fixture `action-in-owned-scope-walk` pins each shape with a silent twin. The dear question (where did the value come from) is asked after the cheap ones (is it handed on as a callable, is it evaluated for its value). Measured and said first: the walk now finds package functions that flow through project functions (`erase(raw.GET)` handed to `wrap`: +5 rows in `feature-alerts`), and the rows whose declaration path was the signature's now name the origin's (a blocker word may move: `drizzle-orm` `missing-source` to `unknown-global` in `sensor-sim`, same sites). `ir-read-lint` gets one allowlist line (`project_file`, the pass's one read of another file's facts by path; the lookup records the read).

**Global writes (the coordinator's condition on B1).** The signature rule of B1 rests on a named premise: *types are sound for declarations, and runtime writes come from the scan.* A resolved standard-library signature proves the type of a global, not that no installed package replaced it where it loads. `module_reach.rs` records the globals each runtime file writes (`GlobalWrites`): a member of the global object assigned (also through `window.self` and `document.defaultView`, as a destructuring target or as a loop head), `Object.defineProperty`, `defineProperties`, `Reflect.set` and `Reflect.defineProperty` of it, `Object.assign` of a source, an unbound `x = …`. The key is a name where the file's own constants decide it: a literal, a `const`, `let` or `var` that nothing reassigns or declares again (bundled code declares its constants with `var`), a conditional or logical of those, a loop variable over an array literal or over `Object.keys` of an object literal, a `for…in` over one, and a source that is an object literal (a spread or `Object.freeze` of one included) or a binding of one that nothing in the file changes (every use reads it, iterates it, spreads it, or hands it to `Object.keys`, `entries`, `values`, `freeze` or, as a source, `assign`; a `push`, an assignment, a call of a member or any other use leaves it unknown). `Symbol(…)` and `Symbol.for(…)` of the unbound global write no name. Only a key nothing in the file decides (a call, a parameter, an import, a table another module holds, a destructured binding, `Object.setPrototypeOf(globalThis, p)` and a write of `globalThis.__proto__`, which make the members of `p` globals) writes any global. The backend unions the writes over each closure and the index keeps the writer roots by name (`global_writers`) and the writers of any (`global_writers_any`), in the boundary's fingerprint (tag `package-reach-v3`). A call of a global the library declares (a bare one by `global_origin`, a member of the global object by `host_member_origin`) is a site, whatever signature it resolves to, when some installed package the program loads writes it by that name (`global-write:<name>:<root>`, `Provider::Written`) or may write it under a key nothing decides (`global-write-any:<name>:<root>`, `Provider::WrittenAny`: "may write … under a key the scan does not decide"), and that package's closure may reach a Solid action (the writer's verdict); a clear writer is none. Fixtures `action-in-owned-scope-global-writes` (a literal name, a `const` key, a loop over a literal array, `Object.defineProperty`, `Object.assign` of a literal; a clear writer, a symbol-keyed writer and an untouched global stay silent) and `action-in-owned-scope-global-writes-any` (a key nothing decides: every call of a global is a row), pattern programs `pkgaction/global-write-{btoa,window,define,assign,key,any,symbol,clear}` (Chrome).

*Writers under a key nothing decides are followed (coordinator ruling, 2026-11-13; said first).* The first build recorded them and did not follow them: "any global may be its" made a row of every `Math.max`, `JSON.parse` and `new Map` of a twelve-file project (`kui` `feature-alerts`, 318 rows). The ruling: leaving them out is the quiet side, not the conservative one, so they are followed, made exact by resolving every key the file's constants decide. That resolution turns all of storybook (`var KEY = "__STORYBOOK_ADDONS_PREVIEW"`, `Symbol.for` keys), vitest's symbol keys and jest-dom's into names. What stays unknown, honestly: vitest 4.1.11 and 5.0.0 (`setup-common.js`: `for (const key in config.defines) globalThis[key] = …`, where `config.defines` is the project's own vite or vitest config; `stubGlobal(name, value)` and `unstubAllGlobals`, whose name is the caller's argument; `globals.js`: `globalApis` imported from another chunk and a `forEach` callback), `@vitest/mocker`'s `register.js`, `playwright-core`'s `coreBundle.js`, `@firebase/database`, `fetch-blob`'s `streams.cjs` (`web-worker` is clear: silent). *Measured:* the writers are the largest part of this change's cost (the whole of it is in *The cost, accepted* below): every row they add is `package-may-call-action`, uncertifiable, and the violations of the corpus did not move (218 standard, 212 development). The queued follow-up reads vitest 4.1.11 and 5.0.0's writes under pinned digests (the key set of `config.defines` is exact where the project's config `define` is a literal object).

*Module-reach scoping of writers: built, measured, not landed (coordinator ruling, 2026-11-13).* A writer affects only the files whose process loads it. The backend built that scope: the project's import graph from the attested resolution of every import, re-export, literal dynamic import and `require`, a writer's scope being the files that share an ancestor with a file that loads it, closed programs only; a file that loads code the facts do not read (a module named by an expression, `import.meta.glob`, a `require` used as a value, an import the compiler did not resolve that is no stylesheet, asset or `node:` module, a resolved file the program does not analyze) leaves no fact, so every site counts. On 33 of the 34 standard-corpus projects (debug build; `app-game` not run) the graph was whole in 18, and vitest's scope was 93% to 99% of the files in nine of the 11 `kui` projects (a test imports the code it tests), 77% in `api` (10 of 13), 62% in `kernel` (109 of 176) and 22% in `jar-hell-web` (12 of 54); rows were not counted per file. In the other 15 a load the facts do not read (`virtual:file-routes` in `sensor-sim`, unresolved imports, `import.meta` in `vitest.config.ts`) left no fact. It also rests on a premise no fact holds: entries that share one realm (an HTML page's second script tag, vitest's `setupFiles`) are unrelated in the import graph, and a lazy `import.meta.glob` is recorded by no fact. The patch stays in scratch (`mac9/drafts/b-state`, 2026-11-13) and is named in `docs/open-work.md`.

**The call side of a global and the writers' functions (the third batch of reviews of #231: Research B, twenty-seven programs Chrome throws on and the first follow-up left silent).** Coordinator ruling (2026-11-14): close every one in this change, by general rules and by adding hand-offs only; a named premise does not clear a false clean.

*Writes.* Every assignment operator on a route to the global object writes the member (`globalThis.btoa &&= f`, `window.x ||= f`, `self["y"] ??= f`; a compound operator also reads the member, so a name no library declares stays a hazard). A function of the writer family (`Object.assign`, `defineProperty`, `defineProperties`, `setPrototypeOf`, `Reflect.set`, `Reflect.defineProperty`, `Reflect.setPrototypeOf`, `Object.prototype.__defineGetter__` and `__defineSetter__`) is followed exactly to its calls where the file uses it without naming the global object: `Reflect.apply(Object.assign, null, [globalThis, …])`; `.call`, `.apply` and `.bind` of it; a name it is bound to (`const assign = Object.assign`, `const { defineProperty } = Object`, `Object.assign || fallback`, a name assigned later). Each call is judged like a direct call: a target that is a fresh object (an object or array literal, `new`, a function or class expression, a primitive, `exports`, `module.exports`, a `const` bound to one of those, `Object.create(…)`) writes no global; any other target may be the global object, so the package writes any global (and, for the writers that define accessors, may define one under any name); and a writer that escapes (exported, passed on, stored where the walk does not follow it, read as a value, a name that is assigned again) may be called with the global object anywhere: the same. The scan records the accessors a package defines on the global object, apart from its writes (`GlobalWrites::accessor_names`, `accessors_any_name`): `defineProperty` or `Reflect.defineProperty` with a descriptor that names a `get` or a `set` or that the syntax does not read, `defineProperties` descriptor by descriptor, `__defineGetter__` and `__defineSetter__` called on a route to the global object, a change of its prototype (`setPrototypeOf`, a write of `__proto__`: the members of the new prototype become globals) and any writer used where its target is not seen. The index keeps those roots by name and under any name (`global_accessor_writers`, `global_accessor_writers_any`), and the boundary fingerprints them (tag `package-reach-v4`).

*Writers and the global object, as ruled (coordinator, 2026-11-14, on the measurements below; the owner accepted the cost).* A writer reached through a name, `.bind`, `.call`, `.apply` or `Reflect.apply` is judged exactly as a direct call is: a write where its target names the global object (`assign(window, …)`, `assign(cond ? window : other, …)`, `Reflect.apply(Object.assign, null, [globalThis, …])`), none where the target is read and names something else (a name, a parameter, a member, a call's result: `define(to, key, { get })` of a bundler's runtime helper), and any global, an accessor under any name included, only where nothing reads the target (a spread, an array that is not a literal, an escaping alias, `bind` with no target). That is sound only because **every use of the global object other than a spelled member read is itself recorded, and an escape makes the package a writer under any name**: the scan records as `GlobalObjectEscape` each name of it (`window`, `self`, `globalThis`, `top`, `parent`, `frames`, `global`; `window.self`; `globalThis.window`; `document.defaultView`) used as an argument, an assignment, a return, an element or a branch of a conditional, `defaultView` read off *any* object (`el.ownerDocument.defaultView`), `this` at the top of a file with no module syntax (a script or CommonJS, where it can be the global object; `this &&`-style uses that go nowhere are not routes) and `window.valueOf()` (which hands the object back), and as `CodeGeneration` every way to build code that can write it (`eval`, `Function(…)`, a string timer, `.constructor("…")`, and the same through a member of the global object: `window.eval(…)`, `globalThis.Function(…)`, `self.setTimeout("code")`). Each of those makes the package a writer of any global and of an accessor under any name (`GlobalWrites::undecided`). A call of one of the writers that is judged to the end (the global object the first argument of `Object.defineProperty`, `Reflect.set`, `Object.assign`… as a statement, so that the object it returns goes nowhere) writes exactly what it names and is no escape; the same call whose result is kept (`const w = Object.defineProperty(window, "k", d)`) is. A member read of the global object by a key the file's constants decide to one name (`const KEY = "x"; window[KEY]`) is a member of that name, as a write by that key is; a key that is not decided is an escape. `this.x` read at the top of a script looks the global `x` up as `window.x` does (a premise that a bundler wraps the file is no evidence). Two routes no syntax can record stay named premises (`docs/open-work.md`): a typed DOM member that hands the window back (`event.view`) and a sloppy `this` in a plain function (the build serves strict modules). *Measured* (release build of the working tree, standard and development corpora, sites compared by rule, path, span and kind): the four variants (the writer functions as first ruled; judged like a direct call; with escapes and code generation as any-name writers; with `this`, members and `defaultView` of any object) flag **the same sites** on both corpora (0 added, 0 removed), only the reason a row names moves; reading `this.x` as a lookup adds 54 standard-corpus rows (`app-game` 30, `ai-memory-ui` 24); on `uncertifiable-repro/sc4001` the checker's rows are 153 on the previous head, 174 as first ruled, 154 judged like a direct call alone (quieter than the soundness allows) and 174 with the escape rule.

**The cost, accepted (coordinator ruling and the owner, 2026-11-14).** Release build, the frozen rc.21 corpus (34 projects), origin/main dbb5e7612 to this head, one hold: standard 190,144 to 227,645 uncertifiable rows (+37,501), development 211,387 to 249,371 (+37,984); violations 218 and 212, unchanged; every row added or removed is `package-may-call-action` (333 removed: vitest 318, `@tanstack/hotkeys` 9, `vite-plus` 6). Where: `app-game` +18,193, `solid-groove` +3,282, `probus-hk` +1,848, `kui` 24 +1,578, `inferay` +1,465, nine more `kui` projects +500 to +900 each. Behind which package (the first problem of the closure of the writer): `zod` 14,863 (an `unknown-global`: `this.x` read at the top of a script is a lookup), `axe-core` 3,387 (`dynamic-load`), `@firebase/analytics` 2,923, `@testing-library/dom` 2,658, `@inlang/paraglide-js` 1,784, `storybook-solidjs-vite` 1,464 (loads `solid-js`), `@babel/types` 1,444, `@tanstack/query-core` 792, `@codemirror/commands` 608. Added by class: 19,940 calls of a global some package may write under any name, 12,128 reads that run an accessor, 2,952 members of a package's object, 1,157 other any-name rows, 866 calls of a global a package writes by name. The rows are the price of the soundness rules above: an escape or generated code makes the package a writer under any name, so every call of a host global is a site wherever such a package is loaded and may reach a Solid action. More precise readings of package source are how rows are won back, one reading at a time and pinned to the bytes read (ADR 0975 does it for vitest): the first candidate is the alias `const g = globalThis; g[Symbol.for(key)] ??= init()` of published `@solid-primitives/utils`, an alias escape and so an any-name writer, which following a never-reassigned alias exactly would clear.

*Calls.* The origin walk knows the global object as an origin of its own (`Origin::GlobalObject`): the names it goes by (`window`, `self`, `globalThis`, `top`, `parent`, `frames`, `global`), a member that gives it back (`window.self`, `window.window`, `document.defaultView`), a name it is bound to, an operand of a conditional or logical expression, an element of an array and what a project function returns. A member of it by a key the program spells (a static name, a string-literal key, a `const` or a chain of names that only holds a string) is the global of that name, so a package that writes it is the code the call runs, by every route: `window["btoa"]`, `const k = "btoa"; window[k]`, `window.self.btoa`, `const enc = window.btoa`, `const { btoa: enc } = window` (every level of a pattern is read off the global object by its key), `[btoa][0]`. A key the program does not spell, a computed pattern key and a rest element read any global: the call runs the code of any package that may reach a Solid action and writes a global (`global-read-any:<writer root>`, `Provider::Unspelled`). So does the global object handed to a call (`reader(window)`, `Object.entries(globalThis)`): the package side calls that an escape and is undecided there; here what the callee reads off it is not followed, and the row stands at the call that receives it, where a throw inside the callee has its project frame.

*Reads.* A global a package defines an accessor for runs the accessor where the global is read, which a data write does not (reading a data property runs nothing; calling it runs the function, which is the call's site): a member of the global object read for its value (`void window.devicePixelRatio`, `typeof self.x`, `globalThis["x"]`), a bare name (`void devicePixelRatio`, `typeof devicePixelRatio`) and a key of a pattern that destructures the global object (`const { devicePixelRatio: ratio } = window`) are an `Entry::Read` site wherever such a package's closure may reach a Solid action; a key not spelled reads any accessor. Reading *any write* instead would make every read of `window`, `document` or `console` a site wherever a package writes under a key nothing decides (`vitest`: `for (const key in config.defines) globalThis[key] = …`). `undefined`, `NaN` and `Infinity` cannot be redefined and are not reads of an accessor.

*Lazy.* The component `lazy(() => import("./view"))` makes is the export of that module that `lazy` reads (the facts name it: `default`; any export where the loader reads the result itself, `.then((m) => ({ default: m.View }))`), followed through the module's own declarations and every re-export, whatever form: `export { default } from "pkg"`, `export { View as default } from "pkg"`, `export * from "pkg"`, `export { View } from "pkg"`, `import View from "pkg"; export default View`. The row stands at the element, never in the module.

*Patterns.* The row of a getter an object pattern reads stands at the pattern whatever the pattern's form (the lane maps V8's frame on a binding to the pattern's start): renamed, with a default, assigned to names that exist (`({ now: n } = clock)`), nested, and written as a parameter (`(({ now = 0 }) => now)(clock)`: a parameter pattern of a function of the same file, with the call that passes the value). The first follow-up let the hand-off row of an imported value (`clock` may be a function) stand in the pattern's place; the pattern's row is now its own and the hand-off keeps its row: two rows for an imported value destructured, which Chrome's frame needs.

*A frame mapping for the judge (`scripts/fuzz/call-starts.mjs`; it moves no finding).* A finding covers a Chrome frame by its exact start. V8 puts the frame of a global's accessor read at the start of the *statement* whose whole operand the bare read is (`void devicePixelRatio;`, `if (devicePixelRatio)`, `return devicePixelRatio`, `typeof devicePixelRatio;`), and the row stands at the read, so the judge reported the row misplaced although it names the one read that can be the frame: the identifier is the whole operand of that statement (through parentheses, casts and unary operators), so a frame at the statement's start can be that read only. The mapping gives that statement's start to the read. Ten forms were probed in Chrome (rc.21, `mac9/probes-bare`): in five the frame is at the statement (`void x;`, `void typeof x;`, `return x as unknown as null;`, `if (x) {…}`, and `void x;` after a statement that reads a member), and in five it is at the read itself with no mapping needed (`use(x)`, `use(x)` after another call, `void [x]`, `const r = x`, `use(0) + x`). The judge, its assertions and its limits are unchanged; `call-starts.test.mjs` pins the form.

*Where the programs are.* Pattern lane (`scripts/fuzz/patterns/pkgaction/`, 28 new programs): Research B's twenty-seven under names that say the shape (`global-write-and-assign`, `global-write-reflect-apply`, `global-call-*`, `global-value-*`, `getter-*-pattern*`, `lazy-reexport*`) and `global-call-handed`; the grid (`scripts/fuzz/pa-shapes.mjs`): twenty-eight `pa-*` kinds on five hosts (140 contexts: the writes `gwriteand`, `gwritereflect`, `gwritealias`, `gwritebind`; the routes `gcall{key,const,destr,alias,array,self,handed}`; the redefined accessors `gacc{member,bare,typeof,pattern}`; the patterns `getter{rename,default}`); fixtures `action-in-owned-scope-global-routes`, `-writer-functions`, `-writer-functions-fresh` (the silent twin: only fresh targets), and the extended `-lazy`, `-getters` and `-global-writes`. The registry (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`) lists the grid ids; the lazy re-exports need a module of the project and are pinned by the lane and the fixture.

**The cost of the walk.** ADR 0972's walk read each file once per closure and rebuilt what it had read for every package: the package reach phase of the standard corpus was the largest part of this change's cost. A closure's walk now shares what one analysis reads: a per-computation `Memo` interns files, problems and entries and keeps each file's `Visit` (the ordered steps a visit took: notes, pushes, entries), replayed in the same order wherever the file is reached again, so every verdict, problem list and entry order is what the walk without the memo gave; the manifests, resolutions, canonical paths, package roots and directory listings are one `Snapshot` behind mutexes, installed on each thread by a `Reading` guard (a path is canonicalized once, never by a shortcut: the filesystem may fold case); and `prepare()` scans the files one step out on up to six threads, one per 128 KiB of file or more, a file over 1 MiB under a 24 MiB budget, results kept in level order. Proof: every closure of the standard corpus was walked by the head's walk and by this one and compared whole (verdict, problems, loads, accessors, writes, in order): 1,216 compared, 0 differences (a temporary comparison, not committed); the corpus's rows are identical to the build without it. #232's walk (whether a package's closure names `Object.prototype`, builds code or is not read to its end: `PackageReachIndex::unseen_code` and `reads_receiver`) is a step of the same visit: each file's visit holds the rule's answer on its facts and the places where the closure is undecided, in order, and the closure's `why` is the first of them in walk order, so it is not a second walk and no file is read for it twice; proof, the same kind: the old walk and this one asked of every runtime of the standard and development corpora, `why` and `reads_receiver` compared whole (standard corpus 749 runtimes, development build 758, each asked of both walks: 0 differ, none answered by one walk only; a temporary comparison, not committed). Time (release, the frozen rc.21 corpus of 34 projects, `--jobs 3`, one hold, the sum of the projects' times): standard 141.0 s to 158.5 s (+12.4%), development 212.7 s to 231.2 s (+8.7%); the package reach phase is 13.3 s over 1,257 packages. #232's walk first ran its rule on every file of every closure and the standard corpus took 178 s (+28%): it is now asked only for a package the program loads, ahead on the scan threads, and not past the first place the closure is found to run unseen code (the package reach phase 37.4 s to 13.3 s, the same rows).

*Not followed* (`docs/open-work.md`): a sloppy `this` in a plain function and a builtin prototype a package extends, the global object reached through a DOM object's typed member (`event.view`; `defaultView` of any object is recorded), a call of an `any` or untyped member of a global, `declare global` written in a project source file, a member a declaration adds to a host global handed on as a value (no symbol is recorded for a property that is not called), `@types/node` clear by its manifest (S5), a package's object handed to a project function that reads its parameter's member, a builtin prototype a package extends without declaring it (`Float32Array.prototype.reverse = …`: no fact of the whole program says who writes it; pattern `patch-f32-undeclared`), a key table another module holds (`globalApis.forEach((api) => globalThis[api] = …)` over an import) or a namespace import as the source of `Object.assign(globalThis, ns)` (both are any global), a global written through a member of a host object (`console.log = …`) or by a script's top-level `var` (an alias of the global object and `install(window)` are escapes: the package writes under any name), the global object kept in a field or an array the walk does not follow, the later call of a name an assignment destructuring of the global object assigns (`({ btoa: enc } = window); enc(…)`: the read is a site, the call is not followed), `Object` or `Reflect` bound to a name (`const O = Object; O.assign(…)`) or reached through a member (`globalThis.Object.assign`), a parameter pattern of a function of another file than its call, a standard-library function that carries an argument but is not in `CARRIES_ARGUMENT` (`Object.entries`, `Promise.resolve`) and a container's stored value (`new Map([[k, run]]).get(k)`), an implicit getter (an iterator, `toString`, a spread or `for…in` of an object a package made, `Object.keys`, `Object.assign` or `JSON.stringify` handed one), and a lazy loader that is no function literal or gets its module another way (`pkg.load()`).

## ADR 0975 — A reviewed reading of vitest 4.1's `expect` and `vi`, pinned to the bytes read (the cost proof of ADR 0974)
vitest's own API was the largest class of ADR 0972's price: 1,923 of the standard corpus's rows (1,545 calls, 378 values), 1,602 of them `expect(…)` chains. No closure proof can clear it: the closure of `vitest` holds `eval` and the `Function` constructor (the bundled fake timers, `vite/module-runner`), a computed `import()` in vite's module runner, `__vitest_worker__`, `__vitest_mocker__`, `__vitest_required__`, `process`, `Buffer` and `window` escapes, and no Solid package (the label `globalThis.__vitest_worker__` was only the first problem the old walk met; ADR 0974's walk lists them all). The only route is a reading of the source for one API at a time, as ADR 0438 reads the registrations of the test runners. Coordinator ruling (2026-11-13) on four conditions: (1) the premise is pinned per member and per digest, applies only where the installed bytes are the files read, and 5.0.x and anything unmatched stay uncertifiable; (2) `expect` is judged by what is called on its result: a matcher that calls the value or a getter on it stays a site; (3) `vi.fn`, `vi.spyOn` and `vi.stubGlobal` clear only where the source shows the argument is stored and not called at registration, and a later call through the mock is a site of its own; (4) its own commit, this entry, and a "Said first" line. The middle reading of (2): a listed matcher clears only when its traversal provably runs no foreign getter, that is when `actual` is (a) primitive-typed by the compiler (not `any`, `unknown`, a union with an object, or a type parameter), (b) a spy `vi.fn` or `vi.spyOn` made, for the spy matchers only, or (c) a plain project data literal; everything else stays a site.

**Mechanism.** `solid-facts-backend/src/reviewed_packages.rs` names each premise by an id (`vitest-4.1`), the package it starts from and every file it rests on with the SHA-256 of its bytes: ten files, `vitest`'s `dist/index.d.ts`, `dist/chunks/test.DNmyFkvJ.js` and `dist/chunks/utils.BX5Fg8C4.js`, `@vitest/expect`'s `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.js`, `@vitest/spy`'s `dist/index.js`, `chai`'s `index.js`, `@vitest/runner`'s `dist/chunk-artifact.js` (three digests, one per release read) and `dist/index.js`, and `@vitest/utils`'s `dist/helpers.js`. The backend looks each package up from the `vitest` directory as Node does and hashes the file; a package that is not found, a file that is missing and a digest that differs each leave the premise off, for the package and for every package it rests on. The verdict travels in the package boundary (`PackageReachIndex::reviewed`, fingerprinted) and the analysis (`reviewed_api.rs`) applies it only to a declaration in a file of a package it holds for. Everything is identified by the declaration the compiler resolves, never by the spelling at the call: the root of `expect(…)` is `globalExpect` declared in `vitest/dist/index.d.ts`, a matcher is the declared name in `@vitest/expect/dist/index.d.ts`, `vi` and its `fn` and `stubGlobal` are declared in `vitest/dist/index.d.ts`, and every declaration of the symbol must be there (a project that augments one keeps its site). The demand plan asks the compiler's primitive value domain at the arguments of calls into an installed package's function (stable for every inhabitant of a type).

**The reading** (vitest 4.1.11; `@vitest/expect` 4.1.11 `index.js` 1,952 lines, `chai` 6.2.2, `@vitest/spy` 4.1.11; 4.1.6 and 4.1.7 ship the same bytes in nine of the ten files and a runner chunk whose `getCurrentTest` is the same three lines). `expect(value)` is `createExpect`'s arrow (`test.DNmyFkvJ.js:4089`): `getState` and `setState` of a `WeakMap` that `@vitest/expect` keeps on `globalThis` under keys it defines with its own getters when they are absent (a program that defines them first is outside the premise), `chai.expect(value, message)` (stores the value in a flag, returns chai's proxy whose `get` trap throws for an unknown name), `getCurrentTest()` (`function getCurrentTest() { return _test; }`) and `assert.withTest(test)`; it calls nothing of `value`, and the message, a second argument, is concatenated into a failure message, so only the one-argument form is read. Each matcher is `def(name, fn)`: `wrapAssertion` (the non-soft path is `fn.apply(this, args)`) inside chai's `addMethod` wrapper, and its `this.assert(…)` (chai: `test`, and on failure `getMessage`, `objDisplay`, `getActual`, `getOperator`, `new AssertionError`). `toBe` is `Object.is` and, on a mismatch only, `equals` twice (a strict and a loose one, with the registered equality testers, `iterableEquality`, `typeEquality`, `sparseArrayEquality`, `arrayBufferEquality`); `toEqual` and `toStrictEqual` are `equals`; `toBeTruthy`, `toBeFalsy`, `toBeNull`, `toBeUndefined`, `toBeDefined`, `toBeNaN` and `toBeTypeOf` are `Boolean`, `===`, `typeof` and `Number.isNaN`; `toBeGreaterThan`, `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`, `toBeLessThan` and `toBeLessThanOrEqual` throw unless both are a number or a bigint (`assertTypes`: a `typeof` test) and then compare primitives; `toMatch` throws unless `actual` is a string and then calls `String.prototype.includes` or `match`; `toHaveBeenCalled`, `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` and `toHaveBeenCalledOnce` read `getSpy` (`isMockFunction`, or a `TypeError`), `spy.getMockName()` and `spy.mock.calls.length`, and format the recorded calls only under `.not`, so a `.not` chain is not read. `equals` is `eq`: `asymmetricMatch` reads a member of an operand only when it is an object (`typeof obj === "object" && "asymmetricMatch" in obj`), then it calls the **registered equality testers** (functions the program handed to `expect.addEqualityTesters`: handed to a package, so the hand-off's, ADRs 0949 and 0967), then `Object.prototype.toString.call`, `Object.is`, and for objects `for…in`, own symbols and a recursive `eq` of the own data. `vi.fn(impl)` is `isMockFunction(impl)` (a `typeof` and an `in` test), `createMockInstance` (reads `impl.length`, stores `impl` as the mock's implementation) and never calls `impl`, which a later call of the mock does; `vi.stubGlobal(name, value)` is `Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, name)` and `Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, { value, … })`: `value` is stored and never read. `vi.spyOn(object, key)` reads `object[key]` and redefines the property on the object it is given, which may be an accessor, so it is not cleared. The values these paths take from outside are the registries above, vitest's own worker state (`testPath`'s getter) and the functions the program registered; nothing reads or calls a value the program holds except `value` and the arguments, judged by (a) to (c).

**What clears** (`expect(a).m(b…)` written exactly so, no `.not`, `.resolves`, `.rejects` or `.soft`, and one argument to `expect`): `toBe`, `toEqual`, `toStrictEqual`, `toBeTruthy`, `toBeFalsy`, `toBeNull`, `toBeUndefined`, `toBeDefined`, `toBeNaN`, `toBeTypeOf`, `toBeGreaterThan`, `toBeGreaterThanOrEqual`, `toBeLessThan`, `toBeLessThanOrEqual` and `toMatch` when `a` and every `b` is a primitive (a literal; or the compiler's primitive value domain has no object bit and is not unknown: the producer closes a type parameter over its constraint, so a value typed `T extends string` is one and an unconstrained `T` is unknown, and the printed type may not be read for a decision, ADR 0367, so the fact cannot say it was a type parameter), or for `toEqual` and `toStrictEqual` a flat object literal of primitives written there; `toHaveBeenCalled`, `toHaveBeenCalledTimes` and `toHaveBeenCalledOnce` when `a` is a spy a `vi.fn` or `vi.spyOn` call made (a `const` of that one initializer, or the call written there) and every `b` is a primitive; the registrations `vi.fn()`, `vi.fn(function written there)` and `vi.stubGlobal(name, value)`. Both calls of the chain (`expect(a)` and the matcher's) and a value of a package handed to a matcher (a constant typed as a primitive, a spy) are then no site; the registration `vi.stubGlobal` clears the call, not the value: a function of a package handed to it keeps its site, since the global now holds it and the program may call it anywhere (fixture `StoredPackageFunction`). **What keeps its site:** every other matcher (`toHaveLength` reads `.length`, `toContain` calls methods on `actual`, `toHaveBeenCalledWith` and `toHaveBeenNthCalledWith` traverse the recorded arguments, `toThrow`, `toMatchObject`, `toHaveProperty`, the snapshot matchers, `@testing-library/jest-dom`'s, which `expect.extend` registers from another package), every `.not`, `.resolves`, `.rejects` and `.soft` chain, `expect.extend`, `expect.poll`, `expect.soft`, an object, an array, a class instance, an `any`, an `unknown`, an unconstrained type parameter's value, a union with an object, a value a package made, a call through a mock (`mock(…)`, a site of its own), a mock handed on as a value to anything but a cleared matcher or registration, `vi.fn(identifier)`, `vi.spyOn`, every other member of `vi`, every other release (5.0.x lays the package out differently and was not read) and every file that does not match.

*Named premise, typed values are sound* (coordinator, 2026-11-13): a value whose compiler type is a primitive is a primitive at run time. A `T extends string` value carries the same premise as a plain `string`; both can be lied to only through an `any` or a cast, and an expression typed `any` is excluded (its domain is unknown). No producer fact and no parameter exclusion was added for a constrained type parameter.

*Named misses* (a premise reading, not a proof of the whole package): a program that defines the registry keys on `globalThis` before `@vitest/expect` does, an `expect.extend` or a plugin that overrides a listed matcher (the function handed is the hand-off's), and a builtin prototype a package extends (a flat literal's `for…in` reads inherited enumerable keys).

*Said first:* this is a classification change, approved by the coordinator on the conditions above: calls that were uncertifiable `package-may-call-action` rows are silent where the reviewed reading shows what they call. The Fable review checks the reading. No judge, assertion, limit or allowlist changed for it (the proof lint passes on its code unchanged); the snapshots and counters that move do so in the same series, read in the PR.

## ADR 0976 — A call into code outside the project, a promise handler, a member read of a value no fact proves plain and the code a continuation runs with no call, written after an async function's own suspension, ends or is uncertifiable (the follow-up to #233's reviews: S1-S4, R1-R6)
**The defects.** ADR 0973's accounting skipped every call whose callee is outside the project or Solid's own, on the argument that a library "runs project code only through what it is handed or a protocol the project's objects implement". The reviews of #233 and their re-checks found each way that holds, all Chrome-confirmed false cleans of UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT, silent on main: **S2/R4** a callback the standard library runs on this stack (`[1].forEach(() => source())`, `Array.from([1], reader)`, `new Promise((done) => done(source()))`, a `Map` subclass's `get`, an iterator literal under its library type); **R1** a setter given an updater that reads a signal (`setCount((p) => p + source())`); **R2** a synchronous dispatch to a listener registered earlier (`el.dispatchEvent`, `click()`, `abort()`); **R3** `it.next(1)` on a stored generator; **N1** a constructor that calls its argument; **R5** `runWithOwner(null, () => read())` (the owner of a continuation is none); **S1** code the async function runs with no call written there where no computation is recognized (a getter, a `toString` a template coerces, an iterator a `for…of` runs, a constructor, a tag function, a Proxy trap); **R6** a stored generator object spread, iterated or destructured; **S3** the continuation of a promise chain in a function that is no `async` function (`function work() { return pause().then(() => source()); }` handed to `createMemo` through a wrapper); **S4** a store or props value read through an alias (`const local = store.n; await …; local.x`: a module-scope alias, a destructuring, an element of a store array, a function's return, a cell of a literal, a props alias). Research B's 66 afterawait programs added: a standard call reaches other built-ins (`Promise.all("ab")` calls `Promise.resolve`, `new Set("ab")` calls `add`, `JSON.stringify({ a: 1 })` reads `toJSON` from `Object.prototype`, `Object.assign` sets through an inherited setter), a setter whose signal has a function-valued `equals`, a string timer or `eval`, and a package call handed a function inside an object, array or `bind`.

**The change: the skipping arm is gone, and one typed fact ends a library call.** Every call written after the function's own suspension is a site; one that no ending holds is an uncertifiable `read-after-await-unaccounted` row (never a violation, never a silence). `AfterAwaitSafe` has four reasons: `NeverRuns` (ADR 0973), `LibraryRunsNothing`, `OwnerCaptured` and `PlainReceiver`. `library_call.rs` is the fact `LibraryRunsNothing` asks, and it is the only thing that ends a call into the standard library or a setter: **the program leaves every built-in alone** (no standard global or member of a standard prototype is written, no reflective definer is spelled, no mutating reflective call, no `eval` or `Function`, no array intrinsic obtained as a value: the census hazards, none present anywhere), **the callee resolves exactly** (`resolved_callee_call`: a vetoed call, a subclass, an impostor or a symbol found only by its declarations never ends here, which is also R4's first step: the symbol fallback undid `subclass_veto`, `impostor_veto` and `patch_vetoed`), it is not `eval`, the `Function` constructor or a call that delivers to listeners on this stack (`delivers_synchronously`), its receiver is the library's own (none, a primitive proven from its own expression, an unshadowed ECMAScript global), and **every argument is inert**: a nullish literal, a primitive proven from its own expression, an exact data literal (and only where no file of the program can name `Object.prototype`: #232's "touched" fact, `UnreadPackageHandOff::object_prototype_touched`, an unread package included), or a function at a slot the audited table says runs later. A string at a deferred slot is code the host evaluates and is never inert. A setter is inert on the same arguments when the `createSignal` call it was destructured from has no `equals` option or `equals: false` (`Dialect::signal_creation_options`). An action is never inert. **The owner ruled FULL (2026-11-14) over narrower scopes: a call into a package, and a call found only by its symbol, is a site that nothing ends** (the package-source proof, the proof batch's 1b, would win those rows back).

**R5** is a `Dialect` question (`callback_keeps_after_await_flag`: `runWithOwner`'s callback at 1; `untrack` and `createRoot` clear the flag, probed on rc.21): a call whose callback keeps the flag is a site unless the owner it passes is an unreassigned `const` of `getOwner()` (`Dialect::returns_current_owner`) written in the same function ahead of its first suspension (`OwnerCaptured`).

**S1 and R6.** The member-route net (ADR 0963) opened only for a recognized async computation; its gate is now any suspension in the program (`program_suspends`), and for the read-after-await net only (`unplaced_member_or_generator_blocker`, `Routes::MembersAndGenerators`) a generator's body is a member route too: it runs when its object is stepped, by a call on a member or by an iteration no call shows. The first build widened `runs_implicitly` for every rule, which rewrote 15 SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` rows of `rc9-flush-in-action` to `function-run-unplaced` ones and added two; the other rules' member nets keep their rows, and `a_generator_body_is_a_member_route_of_the_read_after_await_net_only` pins it.

**S3.** A promise handler (`then` at 0 and 1, `catch` and `finally` at 0: a function literal, or a function named by reference) is code written after a suspension of the function that holds the chain, `async` or not. The callee is `Promise.prototype.*` or `PromiseLike` by its resolved declaration, or a member named by a literal key on a receiver the program does not prove non-thenable (the text-named case only adds sites). The universe's gate "the file holds an async function" is now "an async function or a promise handler". There is no census reason (ADR 0973): a function no computation starts is still a site.

**S4, the full rule (owner ruling 2026-11-15).** A member read, a member call's callee, a destructuring, an iteration or a spread written after an async function's own suspension is a site unless its object is proven plain: a primitive proven from its own expression, a fresh built-in value (`value_origin`), or an unshadowed ECMAScript global in a program that leaves every built-in alone (`PlainReceiver`). A type proves nothing (`{ x: number }` is what the store proxy has). The census-only variant (a forward census of the store and props roots through aliases, destructurings, cells and returns: +196 rows) leaves an object of unknown origin silent, which is not fail-closed (it is silent on the three stored-generator shapes of `after-await-net`), and was removed; the full rule priced +9,980. A destructuring is reported from its pattern (the position a stack frame of the iteration has), and a `new` from the `new` token.

**Measured** (34 projects, release builds, plain runs; origin/main `9d875bff0` against this change `rel-r7`, one producer, every row read). Standard build: uncertifiable **227,645 to 256,755 (+29,110)**; development build **249,371 to 277,878 (+28,507)**; **violations 218 to 218 and 212 to 212**, none added, none removed, nothing proved moved. The added rows are all SC1002 uncertifiable `read-after-await-unaccounted` (29,101 standard) and `unresolved-invocation` (15); 21,536 of the 29,116 added rows stand in test files (74%); six rows left (standard and development), each the same site filed twice by ADR 0973 (`new X()` at the `new` and at the callee: the S5 noise) now answered once. The pieces, priced on the hooks build one at a time (base 207,654 standard / 228,374 development, same binary): S3 +803 / +725, S4 census +196 / +196, **S4 full +9,980 / +9,980**, S1+R6 +13 / +16 (measured before the merge of #235); the library-call rule with packages is the rest (+17,509 standard on the first full build, by kind of site: 14,437 package calls, 1,451 package-symbol calls, 865 constructs, 537 library calls, 178 symbol-only calls, 41 setters). `library-runs-nothing` ends 18 standard / 2 development calls on this corpus (the built-in guard takes the proof from about 230 of the 249 the logging build counted, Research B's item 2). Corpus time, `--jobs 3`, alone, release: standard 155.1 s against 154.9 s on main, development 232.3 s against 231.2 s.

**Chrome.** The real oracle on the follow-up's cases (`after-await-library`, `-primitives`, `-net`, `-then-handler`, `-store-alias`, the review's `cases3`/`cases2`): 0 unproven-clean (Chrome is quiet on ten programs of the two review sets: `untrack`, `createRoot`, an action and a thenable, which the checker may leave uncertifiable; the programs that do not type-check are not run). Research B's 66 afterawait programs through the corrected runner (`patterns-m11.mjs`): 98 of 100 fine, 0 false clean; `aa-match-exec-hid` and `-rec` are no-run (Chrome's own stack overflow) and named. Fuzz: the old build fails `make fuzz-focus CODES=UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT` on the 13 library routes and the 10 `net-*` routes of `cs-shapes.mjs`, this one passes (S3 and S4 are not cells: a handler's read is after a suspension wherever the chain is written, and S4's site is a store read through an alias, which the cells' model does not have; the oracle cases hold them).

**Fixtures and tests.** `after-await-library` and `-library-patched` (the calls that end in no row, and the same calls in a program that writes `String.prototype.concat`), `after-await-universe` (R5 variants, the library sites that keep a row), `after-await-net`, `after-await-then-handler` and `after-await-store-alias` (the exact row sets: `after_await_accounting_process`); the mutation test of `library-runs-nothing`; unit tests of the dialect questions. Assertions moved, each only new uncertifiable rows, read: `rule_quality_process` `reactive-read-after-await` 23 to 28 (four library calls in `await-control-flow-invalid.tsx`: `console.log(await …)` and three `Math.random()`, plus `after-await-invalid.tsx:18` `result.value`, a member of a project literal the full rule does not prove plain) and the file entries 11 to 15 and 2 to 3; `diagnostics_process` `solid2-precision` 10 to 14 (the filter callbacks and `Promise.resolve(result).then(…)` twice), `resolve-scope` `4 + 16 + 15 + 6` plus 1 (`setUser(current)` after `await resolve(…)`), and `rc9-flush-in-action` `beside` 34 to 36 (`yield* inner()` and a parameter named `flush` called in a generator an action runs).

**Open** (`docs/open-work.md`): a project object literal is not proven plain (a sound proof needs each step of a chain: `cell.v.x` reads a store value stored in the literal), the largest cut of the S4 cost; the package-source proof and the test runner's own source (1b) for the package rows; a standard call with no argument has no resolved-call fact, so `text.trim()` keeps its row; `aa-match-exec` programs cannot run in Chrome; a computed `then` is an SC9012 at the call, not a handler row.

## ADR 0978 — Every entry of `Loading` is asked (SC5006, SC5007), and a hand-called or call-form boundary covers its children (the ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY false positive and the JSX `fallback` false clean closed)
**The defects.** `Loading` is a component function, so the tag is not the only way a program enters it. SC5006 (`on` holds a read the boundary re-arms) was asked of the JSX tag only, and SC5007 (an accessor handed as `on`) of the tag and the direct call: `Loading(props)` through an alias, a namespace, a wrapper, `createComponent(Loading, props)`, `Loading.call(null, props)`, `[Loading][0](props)`, `dynamicComponent(() => Loading)`, `<Dynamic component={Loading}>`, a tag a parameter holds, and `createLoadingBoundary(children, fallback, { on })` were each a false clean, Chrome-confirmed (Research B's L01-L14, a01-a12, o12; the primitive by a probe). The cover walk (`loading_cover_at`) counted only a JSX `Loading` as cover, which made two more: a read in the `children` getter of a hand-called boundary (or in `createLoadingBoundary`'s first argument) was read as outside, a false positive (violation of SC5003 where Chrome is quiet; the pattern lane judges a placeless code per file, so it never showed), and a read in the JSX `fallback` attribute was read as covered, a false clean (Chrome warns: `Loading(props)` is `createLoadingBoundary(() => props.children, () => props.fallback, ..)`, `solid-js/dist/solid.dev.js`).

**The change.** The boundary's props (`children`, `fallback`, `on`) and primitive (`createLoadingBoundary`, with the positions of its held content, fallback and options) are a `Dialect` question, `Dialect::async_boundary_shape` (rc.21 answers it from `Loading(props)`), so no analysis file spells them. `loading_entries.rs` holds the vocabulary: `entry_call` (a call exactly `Loading(props)`, the callee resolved as the tag is, or exactly `createComponent(Loading, props)`: the dialect's component renderer by its exact import binding, its first argument resolving to the boundary), `props_on` (a props literal closed against spreads and computed keys states `on`'s absence and kind; anything else is open), `loading_value_references` (every other naming of the boundary), `unresolved_tag` (a component that resolves to nothing the analysis reads: a parameter, a props member, a call's result) and `layer_cover`. SC5006 is an obligation at each entry that may pass `on` (no children proof: coarse and exact, never a violation); SC5007 reads the same props as the tag's attributes, a violation only where the call is exact and the value proven a function, uncertifiable where the boundary is a value or the tag unresolved (the target may not be the boundary). A closed literal with only accessors (`get children()`) no longer gets an SC5007 row for being a getter-bearing literal (a spread or a computed key keeps it). `layer_cover` asks the walk what a function no call edge places is: the `children` getter of an exact call's props, or `createLoadingBoundary`'s first argument, is covered; a `fallback` getter, or its second argument, goes on outward from the call; every other member (a function-valued `children`, a method, `on`), array element, class element, tag function, or closure handed to a call the analysis does not resolve is uncertifiable, never uncovered. A read in a `Loading` element's `fallback` attribute goes on outward from the element; `on` and the other attributes stay covered.

**Measured** (rc.21 corpus, 34 projects, release, `--internal`; origin/main `eb0e2dd16` against this change, one producer, every moved row read). Standard: uncertifiable 190,100 to **190,144 (+44**: 23 SC5006 at `inferay`'s `<IconX {...props} />`, 4 SC5007 on unresolved tags with a spread, 12 SC5003 and 6 SC9012 at reads left through a `fallback`, one SC9012 removed); development 210,865 to **211,387 (+522**: those, and 472 `package-finding-at-entry` rows of a package source's unresolved tag with a spread, 362 of them in `error-menu-web`'s Kobalte); **violations 218 to 218 and 212 to 212**, none added or removed. The rows are uncertifiable only: nothing proved moved.

**Fixtures, Chrome and fuzz.** `loading-entries` (every entry, with the shadowed local `Loading`, a project component, `on: 1`, a closed literal with no `on`, a spread and a computed key) and `loading-entry-cover` (a violation at the sibling read and none at the covered getter's, per component; the fallback reads). The Chrome programs (cover, L, o, a, fb, lb): no false clean, no false positive on the fix (the lane's per-file judge on main: 3 false cleans in `acc`, 11 in `lo`, 1 in `props`, 1 in `clbon`; read per site, main also holds a violation at the covered read of cv02-cv04, cv06-cv09, L01, L03, L05, L09-L11, L13, ra-loading-hand, o07, a01-a03, a05, a10-a12, fb5, fb7-fb9 and lb1, all gone on the fix). Fuzz: `lf-shapes.mjs` crosses the way the boundary is entered with what is asked (`lf-*` hold, `lf-acc-*`, `lf-cover-*` legal, `lf-fb-*`); `make fuzz-focus CODES=LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD,LOADING_ON_ACCESSOR,ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY FUZZ_GRIDS=mx-recall,lg-recall` exits 1 on main (31 false cleans, 9 false positives) and 0 here; four entries in `rediscovery.json`. The same run showed a generator defect, fixed in its own commit: the `arrow` on-variant wrote an undeclared name under a sourced prop (tsc TS2304 and SC5007 on the arrow overlapped, 12 `tsc-overlap` rows, red on main); it writes the sourced name now (0 rows).

**Open** (`docs/open-work.md`): no children proof for a call-form entry (U where the children read no async source); a getter or method named `on` is not followed; the getter's own run is placed by no call edge, so `call-attributed-read` stands at its async reads; the pattern lane's judge still judges a placeless code per file (to the owner).

## ADR 0979 — Violations are judged by site, not by file: the pattern lane, the matrix, the legal grid and the oracle (owner-approved judge change)
A false positive of main (an ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY violation at a read a hand-called `Loading` covers, Chrome quiet there) sat in 8 of 28 pattern-lane programs and the lane passed them: each held a true violation of the same code, and the judges asked "did Chrome report a code of this rule anywhere in the file?". The pattern lane (`judgePattern`, every code), the matrix and legal grids' off-site rows (`offSiteVerdicts`, the placeless codes) and the legal grid's at-site check (`judgeLegal`, every code) all took the code anywhere as the answer; the oracle took CAUGHT_REACTIVE_READ by file (ADR 0946). Mac 11's PR (ADR 0978) fixes that checker false positive; this one fixes the judges that hid it. The owner approved changing these judges for this purpose only.

**What moved.** One function, `scripts/fuzz/site-judge.mjs` `accountViolations`, now answers for a violation, and each judge calls it (or its counting half, `placelessExcess`):
- A code Chrome places: the violation is accounted for when a frame of a diagnostic of one of its rule's codes is on its lines (its span, in its file; a compiled call's start counts as the frame). A diagnostic of the code elsewhere accounts for nothing. A diagnostic of the code with no frame at all may be the violation's: `unplaced`, unjudged, never a false positive (as the matrix already reads it).
- A code Chrome cannot place (`unplaceableCodes`): recall keeps the file judge; for precision it counts. The distinct violation sites of the rules that claim the code (a site the ledger shows never ran, or one a code of its rule already placed, is not counted) against the diagnostics the run raised of it, not merged by stack. More sites than diagnostics leaves each of those sites a false-positive candidate (`excess`, with the code and the two counts; read by a person, never a verdict that fails a gate by itself).
- The pattern lane (`patterns.mjs`): `judgePattern` takes `counts` (the diagnostics per code, recorded by the page) and judges each violation by its code's stacks; `positions: false` (the witness rows, no frames) keeps the file test. A violation of a rule whose code Chrome reported and no finding covers stays that code's `misplaced`. The record also holds `entry-record.tsx`, below.
- The matrix and legal grids (`classify.mjs` `offSiteVerdicts`): only its placeless clause changed (a code reported anywhere substantiated every violation of its rules): `siteFindings` (the violations the caller judged at the row's own sites) count as sites too, and an excess site that ran falls through to the existing verdicts (`false-positive`, or `unexecuted` when it never ran), noted `excess`. Frames, repeats, stacked claims, twins and halts are as they were.
- The legal grid's at-site check (`legal.mjs` `judgeLegal`, `contradicted`): a violation at the site is accounted for by a diagnostic at that site, not by a code of its rule reported anywhere. **Assertion moved:** `legal.test.mjs` "is no false positive when the runtime reports one of the rule's codes elsewhere" (`not.toBe("false-positive")`) now expects `false-positive`, renamed "is a false-positive candidate when the runtime reports one of the rule's codes only elsewhere", with two new tests (a code at the site or on a frame of its stack, and a placeless code against one diagnostic). `claimedRuns` (the run-claiming rule's violation anywhere) keeps its file test: it asks whether the site ran, not whether a diagnostic covers it.
- The oracle (`runtime-oracle.mjs`): a violation of a code it judges by file (`fileJudgedCodes`, CAUGHT_REACTIVE_READ only: ADR 0946 stands) is covered by the file's diagnostics only as far as they go: more violation sites than diagnostics the case raised (raw, before the site merge) leaves the surplus uncovered (`static-only`). Which codes the oracle judges by file did not change.
- Recall keeps its judge everywhere: `coversCodeAt`, `placelessCodes` (the recall judges and the Rust policy table) and the frozen judge rows are untouched.

**Which codes Chrome cannot place, and how often the runtime raises each** (pinned `@solidjs/signals` 2.0.0-rc.21, `scripts/runtime-oracle-install`). Read from the dist, never from names; a count is exact only per that unit, so a program with several true sites in one unit is a candidate to read, not a verdict:
| code | raised from | multiplicity | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY | the scheduler's flush, `notifyEffectStatus` | once per mount ("N async siblings at mount used to produce N copies") | `dev.js` 2655-2700; gate `dev-shared.js` 2261-2273, reset 2285 |
| LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD | a boundary's re-arm walk, run by the flush | once per re-arm (`return` after the first source) | `dev.js` 10967, 10981-11028 |
| CAUGHT_REACTIVE_READ | the settle of a computation's flight | once per computation (`caughtReadReported`) | `dev-shared.js` 1275-1296 |
| SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED | the queued one-shot's `fire`, after the callback returned | once per fire | `dev.js` 3890-3914 |
`LOADING_ON_ACCESSOR` (once per boundary, `dev.js` 11103-11125, called from the boundary's first synchronous run, 11175) is in `placelessCodes` for the recall judges, but its Chrome stack holds the `<Loading>` element's frame: a pattern with `<Loading on={() => route()}>` records App.tsx 7:5, a mount frame, with the lane's recorder. So the precision judge places its violations by that frame (`unplaceableCodes` leaves it out); the recall table is a separate decision and is not changed here. No judge can tell the units apart (the host records neither the mount nor the owner of a diagnostic), so every excess is a candidate. In the audit's manifests every fired row of the other three (ASYNC 19, CAUGHT 103, SETTLED 376) is `placed: unplaced`; LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD fired in none of them, so its row rests on the bytes alone.

**The lane's entry.** `patterns.mjs` mounted App through `await import("./App")` while the checker models a static `main.tsx`; the await gap let a module-level async source settle before render. `const [v, setV] = createOptimistic(async () => 1);` at module level with `setV(2)` in App: Chrome quiet (codes `[]`) under the dynamic entry, OPTIMISTIC_WRITE_BEFORE_LOAD thrown at App.tsx 6:3 under the static one, so a correct violation read as a false positive and a false clean could hide the same way. The entry now imports `entry-record.tsx` (the OBSERVE subscription, evaluated first) and then App statically (`ENTRY`, `RECORD`, tested). The matrix hosts already mount from the entry's own task (`chrome-host/runner.tsx`).

**Measured** (VM, checker built from main eb0e2dd16; the old judge is origin/main's scripts, same binaries, same Chrome host). Pattern lane, 1,518 programs, all families: 1,499 fine, 18 false clean, 0 false positive before and after; 0 new false-positive candidate; one verdict moved, `types/c08-clientonly` (Chrome STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED under the dynamic entry, no code under the static one: the `clientOnly` component is still pending when the static entry renders; still `fine`). The 11 fuzz grids' Chrome-judged samples of the dfa6c5dec audit (the 76,309 programs of its oracle manifests, regenerated by id; the host is Chrome, `--fast-host chrome`, so its records are Chrome's): 0 outcomes moved, 0 new false-positive candidate, in all 11 grids (old judge and new judge rows compared by id, `outcome` and `offSite`). A first pass flagged 44 mx-census programs: a measurement artifact of mine (the budget read the diagnostic's `loc` as its file, and `loc` carries a path); removed where it arose, and the re-run moves nothing. The runtime oracle (776 cases, `fixtures/runtime-oracle`, real Chrome, 4 minutes per tree): the same tally on both judges (114 covered-violation, 239 covered-uncertifiable, 416 quiet, 3 known-open, 1 static-only, 1 stale-open, 1 type-error, 1 behaviour-clean; it exits 1 on both for the stale-open and the type-error), the same verdict on every case; one case, `c4-seen-origin`, lists one Chrome diagnostic fewer in the second run (a Chrome difference, the verdict is `covered-uncertifiable` in both). `make fuzz-smoke` (the 11 grids' smoke sample, seed 666919979, then the lane): the same tallies and the same "moved from the manifest" counts under both judges (lg-base 7 worse and lg-combo 3 worse are the checker's drift from the manifest on main, not this change). `make verify` in the VM: the fuzz tests lane passes (93 files, 1,717 tests); the rust lane stops at `program_boundary::tests::a_kept_decision_follows_the_disk_as_an_uncached_one_does`, the Linux file-stamp test that also fails at dfa6c5dec, so the steps after `builds-and-suites` did not run.

**The other judges that read a violation** (each asked whether it can pass or excuse a violation row): `replay.mjs` `unmatched` and `run.mjs`'s `classify()` can, so both moved to the shared function in this PR (`replay`: a violation no diagnostic reaches at its site is `violation-without-diagnostic` though Chrome reported its code elsewhere, test added; `classify()`: a code Chrome cannot place agrees with as many violations as the run raised diagnostics of it, test added). Legal `claimedRuns` cannot: it only adds an early `false-positive`/`unexecuted` for a run-claiming rule's violation when no code of the rule is reported anywhere; when it is empty, every violation is still judged at its site by `judgeLegal`'s at-site check or `offSiteVerdicts`, so it excuses nothing and keeps its file test. Recall is untouched everywhere. The hidden false positive itself is Mac 11's fix (ADR 0978) and its rediscovery. The count over-flags a program with several true sites of one once-per-mount code (the table above): such candidates are read.

## ADR 0980 — A stored function is followed only into a sole-named holder, and a store through a parameter only when every caller is known (the review of #232's B6 and S2 and the probes a01 to a18, 33 shapes; the pattern lane reproduces 22)
A function stored into an object (`X.m = function () { flush(); }`) was followed in every read of the name `X`, and a name is not the object. Chrome (rc.21) reports FLUSH_IN_ACTION, and main certified with no row: `const a = o; a.m = f; runStep(() => { o.m(); })` (S2: `o` is never read), `put(a)` with `a` another name of `o` (B6(a)), `const s = t; s.m = f` inside `put` and a parameter reassigned to another (B6(b)), a default value that receives the store and a spread before the index (B6(c), where a missing argument answered "not handed"), a method of an object literal (B6(d)), and, under a closed program boundary, a direct call from another file (B6(e): `exact_callers` took its list from `foreign_reference_hand_offs`, which skips a call the call graph holds, returns an empty list on a missing name or symbol and skips a file it lacks). The coordinator's probes added a01 (a getter returns the object), a08 (`a["m"] = f`), a12 (an instance of a project class), a14 to a18 (`(0, o)`, `cond ? o : null`, `o ?? null`, `const { o: a } = { o }`, `new Proxy(o, {})`). Ruling of the coordinator: the coarse fail-closed rule now, one change, and the caller rule applies to every user of `exact_callers`.

**The rule** (`package_hand_off/holders.rs`, `callers.rs`; hands more only, no violation path changes). (1) A store into a member is followed only through the name it is written through, directly (`a.m = f`, `a["m"] = f`; `box.o.m = f` stores into the object `box.o` names, which is no name) and only when that name is **sole-named**: a `const`, or a `let`/`var` nothing reassigns, declared in no export, bound to a fresh object (an object literal whose keys are all spelled and none `__proto__`, an array literal, or `new` of a class this file declares with no superclass, no constructor and no `this`), with every reference of the name the object of a member access (a write through any key; a read of a key the program spells, not `valueOf`, which returns the object), an operand nothing takes (`typeof o`, `o === x`) or a type query. Any use that copies the object (an initializer or assignment's value, an argument, an element or property's value, a return, an iterable, a spread, a destructuring source, an export, a getter's return, a `Proxy`, a comma, conditional or nullish expression) makes the store handed, and so does a holder whose own initializer is another name or a call's result. (2) A store through a parameter is followed only when the parameter is a plain identifier no assignment reassigns whose uses are all of that kind, every caller is known (3), and each caller writes the argument at the index (no spread at or before it; a default value or an omitted argument carries a holder no caller names) as the name of a binding that is sole-named except for that call (the argument of an outer function's parameter goes on by the same rule; a fresh object literal is reached through the parameter only). (4) `exact_callers` returns a list only when every reference of the function's binding, in every file of the program, is a direct call or an import whose uses are direct calls; a method or class member, a function no binding names (an IIFE's argument, an element of an array), a reassigned binding, a use that is no call (a copy, an argument, a tag), a re-export or any export specifier of another module, an export a program may enter, a namespace that hands the function out by name, and a missing symbol, reference list or file give `None`, and a store with no list is handed. `foreign_reference_hand_offs` is unchanged: fifteen other rules read it, and the strict census is its own.

**Fixtures.** `flush-holder-alias` (14 positives silent on main, 17 ratchets, 5 negatives), `flush-holder-put` (9 positives silent on main, 6 on main too, 4 negatives), `flush-holder-put-crossfile` (closed boundary: N1 named import, N3 `export { } from`, N4 `export *`, N5 default export, N6 `await import()`, N8 a third module, all silent on main; two twins whose step never reads the member stay silent) and `flush-holder-put-crossfile-open` (open: unchanged). One brief deviation: the negative `const o = {}; o.m = f; o.m()` is not silent on main either (the member is replaced, so its callee resolves to no one function and a callee nothing resolves may read a member through `this`: `member_call_hands`), so the negatives read the member without calling it.

**Named costs (coordinator: option A; option B, treating a standard-library factory's result as fresh, is out: an appended element is reachable by any package through the DOM, so it is not sole-named however fresh it was).** Two existing sites move from silent to three uncertifiable rows each (SC2006, SC2008, SC3001): `flush-universe-package-hand-off-flip` `DomProperty` (`const el = document.createElement("button"); el.onclick = () => { flush(); }`) and `flush-universe-package-hand-off-receiver-reads-twins` `twinPattern` (`Object.create(null)`; that fixture goes `certified` → `uncertifiable`). A holder that is copied anywhere or exported keeps the row although the copy is never run. Coverage: 4 new fixtures, 2 moved (6 rows added, none removed); `scripts/guard/rises.json` names the rises.

**Measured** (the VM, release builds, main f690aaf3f against this change). The pattern lane in real Chrome over the 32 programs of `pkghand/alias-*` and `put-*` (27 new, 5 older): main 22 false clean (14 alias and 8 put programs: `alias-store`, `-let`, `-forof`, `-getter`, `-computed`, `-class`, `-sequence`, `-cond`, `-nullish`, `-destr-literal`, `-proxy`, `-member`, `-destr-name`, `-chain`; `put-alias`, `-outer-copy`, `-class`, `-inner`, `-reassign`, `-default`, `-spread`, `-method`), this change 0 (32 fine). The four cross-file programs and `put-id-step` are uncertifiable on main already with the lane's entry. The rc.21 frozen corpus (34 projects, the standard command and `--runtime-target browser --runtime-build development --rendering csr`): standard 229,938 rows before and after, 0 added, 0 removed; development 251,502 before and after, 0 added, 0 removed (Linux release builds over the mounted corpus; the VM's totals are its own, not the rows of the older ADRs). The 96 contexts of the 16 new `ph-*` routes (`make fuzz-focus` on FLUSH_IN_ACTION, FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK and FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK, mx-recall and lg-recall, Chrome compared 15 of 16 programs per unit, the sixteenth is typed away): nothing needs a look on this change, and the same cell by cell on main. That is the grid's entry, not the fix: its `main.tsx` loops over `App`'s exports, so the module's namespace escapes and main already reports the flush uncertifiable in every cell; with the lane's entry (App imported by name) the same program is certified (swapped on one materialized program). The grids cannot show this defect on main, so `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json` holds three entries with `outside`, the pattern-lane programs and the fixtures; `ph-shapes.test.mjs` counts the routes (163 → 179, 914 → 1010 contexts, the route list, one `it` printing them: approved by the coordinator).

**Not done.** A program of two project files has no `ph-*` route (the generator prints one file per program): `putimport`, `putreexport`, `putstar` are fixtures and lane programs only.
