## ADR 0981 — A package whose code imports Solid is a Solid package for selection, and a value an unselected package returns is read as possibly reactive (the false clean of STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED behind `dep-router`)
Main was a Chrome-confirmed false clean of STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED when an installed package imports `solid-js` without declaring it (a phantom dependency). ADR 0297's default selected a package only where its manifest's `dependencies` or `peerDependencies` name a Solid package, so `dep-router` (no peer, `dist/routing.js` imports `createMemo` and `createSignal` from `solid-js`, `useLocation()` returns a getter over a memo) was never source, and `createSignal(location.search)` in a component body, which Chrome warns for, had no row. The premise "a package whose manifest names no Solid package has no Solid behaviour" is false for a phantom import, for a wrapper of one, and for a package that returns what the program hands it. Three changes, owner-delegated rulings of the coordinator (2026-11-14).

**1. The oracle expresses a case's selection (harness).** `oracle.json` gains `dependencySources` (each name also in `packages`), passed to `feedback run` and, per job, to `feedback batch` as `--dependency-source`; `development-feedback.mjs` accepts and forwards the flag to the native child, and the execution cache keys on it. The checker side is the `check` command's flags and nothing else: `.solid-checker/runtime.json`'s `dependencySources` of a fixture and `oracle.json`'s of a case are the same selection. The cases `g2-holder-{none,super,super-read}` (the check of #227, G2) are committed under `fixtures/runtime-oracle/` with the `dep-router` stub: the oracle does not select `dep-router` without the pin, and the three end `covered-violation` (none, super-read) and quiet (super), as Chrome does. `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json` cites them.

**2. Selection reads the closure for a Solid import (`dependency_sources.rs`, `SolidImports`).** A package that declares no Solid package is read: its entry (`select_entry`, the declared host's conditions), the relative closure inside the package, the bare runtime imports of every file (`runtime_bare_imports`: a type-only import or one never referenced runs nothing). An import is a Solid import when the directory it resolves to (`runtime_package_root`) is the dialect's runtime or a package of an ecosystem scope by its manifest `name`, or declares one (the old test): decided by the resolved module, never by the spelling of the specifier (`"my-solid": "npm:solid-js"` is one; a directory named `solid-js` whose manifest is another package is not). A package the closure loads that is none of these is read the same way, so a wrapper that re-exports a phantom package is found; the whole scan shares `MAX_CLOSURE_FILES` files and walks no file twice. A package it finds importing one is selected as a declared one is (and then walked and refused as a selected package is: a closure file the compiler refuses is `closure-unavailable`). A package whose closure was read and imports none keeps the `no-demand` refusal; one the scan cannot follow (an entry, a relative import resolving to no source file, an unparsable file, a manifest it cannot read, the limit) is **undecided**: it stays off source, with its own refusal (`closure-unavailable`, `closure-limit`, `runtime-entry-unavailable`, ... and "undecided" in the detail), apart from `no-demand`. A later subpath of a refused package that loads Solid selects the package and the subpaths refused before it. A standard build selects nothing (unchanged).

**3. A value an unselected package returned is read as possibly reactive (`package_action_calls/value_reads.rs`).** A value that is the result of a call or `new` into a package the build does not read (a member of one, an operand of a conditional, logical or comma expression that is one, a project binding of one plain name that holds one, through project files), read where nothing tracks it, is an uncertifiable SC1001 (`package-value-read:untracked`, or `:unplaced` where nothing places the read), never a violation. A read is a member get (the first of a chain), a call of the value, a pattern that destructures it, an iteration over it (`for…of`, an array or argument spread, an array pattern) or an object spread; its role is a reactive read's (`read_execution_role`): rows stand at untracked and unplaced roles, not at a tracked expression or a role Solid does not warn in. The package is the callee's (`origin_of`): the dialect's runtime, a package read as source, the host's globals are not it. Why not narrower: the coordinator priced three options on the rc.21 corpus (release, standard and development builds identical: +4,968 uncertifiable, 810 at a proven-untracked role and 4,158 unplaced, no violation moved; restricting to packages whose reach is not Clear saves 74) and chose the literal rule, since a readable package with no Solid import can return what the program hands it (`const g = wrap(() => count()); g()`, read untracked, raises STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED in Chrome rc.21, `phantom-solid-wrap`) and neither "only where the scan is undecided" nor "only proven-untracked" would catch it. The rows win back by proving, from the package's readable source, that a returned value cannot come from a function or object the program hands it and defines no accessor (`docs/open-work.md`). Awaited values (`await value` reads `then`) are not a read here, and a pattern in a parameter reads what its caller passes (the callee's concern).

**4. The unread-package site pass no longer exempts a package because the build reads it (`package_action_calls.rs`, `installed_path`).** The first build of change 2 made 29 programs of the pattern lane (`patterns/pkgaction/*`: a stored handle, a getter, a lazy name, a namespace member, `fnret-*`, `std-*`, `untrack-made`) false clean of ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE where main passed them: their packages import `action` from `solid-js` without declaring it, selection now read them, and ADR 0972's site pass (a project call into code the build does not read is an SC2002 site, silent only where the closure cannot reach Solid) skipped every selected package, trusting ADR 0949 to report what its analysis finds at the project's call. That trust is wrong for the project-side forms no analysis follows to the package's source, and it was wrong for a DECLARED package too: the same three programs with `peerDependencies` added are Chrome-confirmed false clean on main (stored-handle, fnret-value, getter-class). Owner ruling: close it here. A file of an installed package is code the pass asks about whether or not the build reads the package; what stays out is the program's own code (a project file, an analyzed JavaScript file) and a standard-library declaration. Rule 3 skips a package read as source (its values are proven by its analysis, not assumed). Corpus (release, standard and development identical): SC2002 `package-may-call-action` +472 and `package-finding-at-entry` +29 over the first head (+5,961 over main with rule 3), 0 removed, violations 212. Nine of the rows are ai-memory-ui's `navigate(...)` into `@tanstack/router-core`, a package nested in a selected package's directory whose manifest names no Solid package: **main treated every file under a selected package's root as read as source, by path prefix (`ProjectFacts::dependency_source_root`)**, so a package merely nested there was silent. The other users of that prefix test are listed in `docs/open-work.md`.

**A judge position correction (coordinator-approved, `scripts/fuzz/call-starts.mjs`).** The phantom axis found 20 programs the grid called false clean (`new-phantom` 8, `jsx-phantom` 6, `hop-phantom` 6: a package that imports no Solid name, handed an accessor it calls) while the checker already answered each with an SC9012 withholding at the handed value (`package-callee` at `r1` of `new Site1(r1)`, `value-to-unresolved-callee` at the prop value of `<Site1 r1={r1} />` and at the three places of `createComponent(Site1, { r1 })`), as it does for `site1(r1)`, which the judge accepts as a withholding on a code about a handed value. Chrome (rc.21) puts the frame of that read on the first token of the statement (the `new` keyword, a dependency element's `<`, `createComponent`), and the runtime oracle's own line judge calls all four `covered-uncertifiable`. The judge's call-start model put a `new`'s frame in its callee, gave an element no handed values, and excluded `createComponent` as Solid's: so the withholding sat where no frame mapped to it. The correction is the position model alone: a `new`'s handed range starts at its keyword; a dependency's element hands the expressions of its attributes and spreads to a frame on its `<`; `createComponent(X, props)` with X a non-Solid, non-project import hands its arguments (a Solid or project component and an intrinsic element hand nothing). No threshold, table or assertion moved; `call-starts.test.mjs` pins the three forms and their negatives. A second correction of the same kind (R20 for writes and actions, coordinator-approved after checking the product's own output): in the three sample programs of the handed write, store and action shapes (a plain package handed a setter, a store, an action it calls) the checker prints exactly one SC9012 `value-to-unresolved-callee` at the handed argument, no row of the claiming rule (SC2001, SC2002, SC2003), the project `uncertifiable`: withheld, not certified. `handedCodes` gains REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE and ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE; STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER keeps R22 for a member call's argument (`list.push(x)`) and a project function's argument other than the first, but a withholding covers any argument of a dependency's unread function (the flag `dependency` on the handed starts; the old line, that a judge does not assume what an unread body writes, is kept for a member and relaxed only for a store handed whole, where the checker's own U is at it). ## ADR 0982 — The proof gate's C4: a site ended by a finding the report no longer holds (batch 11, slice 11(a); gate only, no finding moves)
Site accounting (`site_accounting::account`) decides each (site, code) ending before the passes that can remove the finding that ended it: IR projection (`RuntimeConfiguration`, `ExecutionPaths`, `SupersededByViolation`, `EqualFinding`, `OwnedByEnabledRule`) and the backend's (`PackageStyleNotProject`, `DependencySource`, `SupersededByViolation`, `RuleDisabled`, `AbsentProp`, `HostSuppression`). The proof gate trusted the ending: `if (site.end !== "none" || …) continue`. A site whose `end` is a row (`by: "rule:<R>"`) was never checked against the final report, so a later pass that dropped that finding, with nothing else at the span answering the code, left the site silently clean: a hidden false clean (Research A, C4). This change closes the gate, not a checker behaviour.

**The check** (`scripts/lib/proof-log.mjs`, `endedByDroppedFinding`). A site with `end !== "none"` and `by: rule:<R>[:u]` needs a crediting verdict at its own span or an `alt` span (exact keys, never ranges): a verdict whose rule the dialect's code policy says claims the site's code, or an obligation of a rule that declines it (`codeRules`, `declinesCode` of `scripts/fuzz/codes.mjs`, never a rule's spelling). With none, the last `drop` of that finding (its `rule`, at those spans, in log order) must be an accepted pass: ExecutionPaths, AbsentProp, RuleDisabled and HostSuppression with their typed premise; DependencySource only with its C2(c) `attributed` line; OwnedByEnabledRule only with a `PendingThrowsFirst` premise the final list confirms (an SC5001 violation at the premise's span, like `SetterGuardThrowsFirst`). SupersededByViolation, EqualFinding and any other pass are accepted only while another crediting verdict remains, which is the case that did not reach here, and a missing drop line is a hit as well: `C4 ended-by-dropped-finding` (detail: code, rule, pass, spans). C4 is in `neverAccepted`: never a gap.

**Log changes (no behaviour change).** Drop and reclass lines carry the finding's `rule` (`StageEntry`). `ProofStage::end_with` writes one more typed fact beside the pass's own, and `suppress_findings_owned_by_enabled_rules` writes `PendingThrowsFirst` for a strict read an SC5001 *violation* owns (the run throws before it warns; an open SC5001 names no such fact, so a read it alone owns stays a hit). A store write's chain finding stands at a span inside the site's (a wrapper's paren): its site line now names that span as an `alt`, so the verdict is read by exact span (the first run had four hits, in `store-delete` and `store-delete-anchor`, that were this artifact: the finding stood, one byte in).

**Measured** (VM, debug build for the fixtures, release for the corpus). `make proof-gate` over the 1,255 fixture projects: 0 C4 hits (821 sites ended by a rule; drops by pass: DependencySource 3,267, OwnedByEnabledRule 75 of which 47 carry `PendingThrowsFirst`, ExecutionPaths 54, HostSuppression 15, RuleDisabled 14, EqualFinding 12, PackageStyleNotProject 4, AbsentProp 1, SupersededByViolation 1; every drop line carries its rule). The same fold over the 34 rc.21 corpus projects (development build, proof log on): 0 C4 hits. Unit tests: `scripts/proof-gate.test.mjs` C4 block (i) to (v), the DependencySource and OwnedByEnabledRule cases and the never-accepted case; one Rust test of the drop line. No defect known: no C4 hit stands at the head, so there is no program to judge in Chrome.

**Not covered.** The gate cannot see a pass that drops a finding without a stage (a drop outside `ProofStage`); that is C2(a)'s. A site whose ending is a row of a table (`table:…`) or a census obligation is not C4's: its row stands in the final program or the SC9012 does.

## ADR 0983 — vitest's global writes: a pinned reading cannot replace its `any_name` (a measurement record; nothing is built)
ADR 0974 (#235) records the globals each runtime file of a package writes (`GlobalWrites`). A closure with a write under a key the scan cannot decide sets `any_name`, and every standard-library global call in a program that loads that package becomes `package-may-call-action:global-write-any:<name>:<root>` (`Provider::WrittenAny`). vitest is an any-writer. Research A's brief 01, half A, proposed replacing vitest's `any_name` with an exact name set under a pinned-digest reading (ADR 0975's pattern): the 19 `globalApis`, the keys of the config's `define`, the literal names of `vi.stubGlobal`, and the mocker's accessor. The measurement came first, and it says not to build it.

**Upper bound.** Release builds of main (715814e88) and of a logging build that drops every root named `vitest` from `global_writers_any` (nothing else changed), over the 34 rc.21 corpus projects: standard command 259,078 rows, 259,049 without vitest's any-writes (29 removed); development build (`--runtime-target browser --runtime-build development --rendering csr`) 280,054, 280,025 (29 removed). The 29 rows are all SC2002 `package-may-call-action` rows in ONE project, kui (`frontend/packages/api`: `client.test.ts` 14, `client.ts` 8, `csrf.ts` 2, `errors.ts` 2, `bootstrap.ts` 1, `section.ts` 1, `types.test.ts` 1). Nothing is added and no violation moves. The other 16 projects that load vitest gain nothing, because each also loads another any-writing package (vite, rolldown, jiti, jsdom, std-env, tinybench, `@jridgewell/*`): a global call there stays a site under one of those roots.

**Why the brief's sites are not the any-writers.** The scan was given the span of each any-write and the files of each closure that set `any_name` (a measurement-only change, not committed). The writes the brief names (`setup-common` line 32 `globalThis[key] = config.defines[key]`, `globals` line 27, `vi.stubGlobal`, the mocker's register) are not what sets `any_name` in a program that imports `vitest`: the entry the program demands does not reach `setup-common` or `globals`, and `stubGlobal`'s `Object.defineProperty(globalThis, name, …)` is in `test.DNmyFkvJ.js` among other sites. What sets it is `globalThis` handed on by value (the `escaped` rule: an argument, a return, a branch of a conditional), in many files of vitest's closure: for 4.1.11 (solid-groove, ai-memory-ui, dashiboard-ui, every-deck-of-cards), `@vitest/expect/dist/index.js` (10 sites), `@vitest/snapshot`, `@vitest/utils/dist/timers.js`, the chunks `_commonjsHelpers.D26ty3Ew.js`, `index.Chj8NDwU.js` and `test.DNmyFkvJ.js` (about 70 sites in the 14 to 16 files of the smaller closures), and the third-party files the closure reaches: `vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js` and `build.js`, three `rolldown` chunks, `std-env`, `source-map-js`, `@jridgewell/sourcemap-codec`, `jiti`. The larger closures add jsdom (with `cssstyle`, `nwsapi`, `@asamuzakjp/dom-selector`, `bidi-js`, `whatwg-url`, `@exodus/bytes`), `undici`, `decimal.js`, `es-module-lexer`, `tinybench`, `@vitest/mocker`, `happy-dom` or `tsx`. Census per vitest root (distinct files, any-sites, standard command): 4.1.11 7 to 14 files (38 to 70 sites) in the small installs and 40 to 45 files (121 to 122 sites) with jsdom; 5.0.0 5 files (38 sites) in kui's workspace packages, 33 (hoxxes-briefing), 48 (sensor-sim), 44 files and 1,408 sites in kui's own root; 5.0.1 (skyjtx-website) 39 files, 127 sites.

**Why it is not built.** The ruling's condition (i), every file of the closure that set `any_name` is a pinned file, would need a pinned reading of each of those files, which means of vite's node chunks, rolldown, jiti, jsdom and undici, none of which is a vitest reading; condition (ii), each any-site covered, would need every one of them read. The payoff is 29 rows in one project (0.01%), and kui's own closure (the one that pays) is the largest. A reading of the brief's four write sites alone would silence a name the other sites may write, which is what the ruling forbids ("never silence a name it does write"). Half B (Vite CSS modules) is not built either, by the coordinator's ruling: app-game's config uses unaudited plugins (including top-level-await), so its payoff is 0. `GlobalWrites.any_sites` and the closure's list of any-writing files were built to measure this and are not kept: no consumer reads them.

**What would make it worth doing.** A rise in the number of projects whose only any-writer is vitest's own chunks (the narrow 5.0.0 workspace-package closures have `@jridgewell/sourcemap-codec`, `tinybench` and vitest's own 3 files: 38 sites, 5 files; a reading of those 5 files would clear their global calls only if the root also loads nothing else), or a reading of vite's `node.js` chunk pinned for its own sake (it is in the closure of every Vite project's tooling).

## ADR 0984 — A `let` timer handle is an inert argument in a browser when every reference of it is a proven write or a clear (the follow-up of ADR 0976's held case `clean-copied-timer`)
ADR 0976 made a promise handler's code a site and held one reproduction case, `clean-copied-timer` (ai-memory-ui `page-reader.tsx`): `clearTimeout(copiedTimer)` in a `.then` handler, `copiedTimer` a `let` written only by `setTimeout(…)`. `clearTimeout` coerces its argument, and the argument was a `let` no fact proves primitive (`proven_primitive` follows a `const` only), so it kept an uncertifiable SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` row; the hold was a reviewed raise of `HELD_CAP` from 60 to 61 (owner-approved as this follow-up).

**The proof** (`after_await_accounting/timer_handle.rs`, one more clause of `argument_is_inert`; hands less only, so rows leave, none arrive). The argument is an identifier whose binding is a `let` of one identifier in this file, with no initializer (or `undefined`, or a timer call), unexported, no parameter, and the program names `--runtime-target browser` (a handle is a number there; in Node it is a `Timeout` object, and an unselected target proves nothing). Every reference of the binding is one of two: the target of a plain `=` (never `+=`, `++`, `??=`, a destructuring or a loop target: each must be an `AssignmentFact` with `reads_target` false and no logical operator) whose value is the unshadowed `undefined` or a call, written with an identifier callee (`window.setTimeout` names a member a project may replace), that the compiler resolves to the standard library's `setTimeout` or `setInterval`; or the sole argument of a call resolved the same way to `clearTimeout` or `clearInterval`. Anything else gives no proof: the handle copied (`const r = { t }`, a `const` copy), handed to a function (even before the clear), returned, spread, written by a call nothing resolves, written through a closure or destructuring that is not a plain assignment. The proof asks the existing fact that the program patches no built-in (`builtins_untouched`, asked by the caller before any argument): a program that writes a standard member keeps the row. No type is asked.

**Fixtures.** `after-await-timer-handle` (browser, development, csr): `Cleared` and `ClearedInterval` end in no row; `UnknownWrite`, `Copied`, `Handed`, `Compound`, `Member` and `ConstCopy` keep theirs; twins `after-await-timer-handle-patched` (writes `String.prototype.concat`) and `after-await-timer-handle-node` (`--runtime-target node`) keep the row of the same shape. Process test `a_let_timer_handle_is_inert_in_a_browser_when_every_reference_is_a_proven_write_or_a_clear` pins each site. The reproduction case `clean-copied-timer` loses its `held` block and stays in `uncertifiable-repro/sc4001-clean`, which now declares the browser runtime the proof needs (`.solid-checker/runtime.json`: the corpus configuration the case was taken under; its other six cases stay certified, and a project of its own would exceed the reproduction set's budget of 11; `sc2001` cannot host it, its program patches a built-in); the case is certified again. `HELD_CAP` is 60 again, and the open-work item that was its `restoredBy` is removed. The one-way count guard records the fall (`scripts/guard/counts.json` `drops`: `uncertifiable-repro/sc4001-clean`, `SC1002 read-after-await-unaccounted`, 1 to 0, proof `timer_handle.rs::is_timer_handle`).

**Measured** (VM, release builds, main 715814e88 against this change, the 34 rc.21 corpus projects). Standard command 259,078 rows before and after; development build (`--runtime-target browser --runtime-build development --rendering csr`) 280,054 before and after; 0 rows added or removed, violations unchanged. The corpus moves nothing because ai-memory-ui's own copy buttons are not sites there (`navigator.clipboard.writeText(…).then(…)` hands the handler to a host call, and no SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` row stands in `page-reader.tsx`): the held case was a reproduction of the shape, not of a corpus row. Coverage records 3 new projects and moves one (`uncertifiable-repro/sc4001-clean`, uncertifiable to certified, one row fewer, with its runtime declared); every other of the 1,259 projects is unchanged.

## ADR 0985 — The resolve/until universe: every SC2004 and SC2005 call ends in a row, a typed silence or `resolve-scope-unaccounted` (batch 11, slice 7)
`resolve` and `until` open with the observer guard (`if (getObserver()) throw`), and the rule's silent exit was "tracked-scope proof `None` and `resolve_scope_unplaced` false": the false came from untyped returns, the widest being `judged_by_primitive → false` (any primitive that states an execution for the callback). Slice 7 makes each call a site (`table: "resolve"`, `proof_universe::primitive_call_sites`; codes `RESOLVE_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE` and `UNTIL_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE`, one per site) and each ending typed.

**Sites.** Every call whose resolved primitive the dialect gives an observer guard (new `Dialect::observer_guard_code`; `Solid2`: `resolve`, `until`), whatever the callee is spelled; and every value reference to one (`[resolve]`, `pick(until)`, `Reflect.apply`), by the value-use census's own enumeration (`static_rules::primitive_value_candidates`, now shared), which the census's `SC9012 primitive-value` row ends. A callee, an import specifier, a type and the initializer of a binding the primitive is copied into (the alias is followed: each of its references is a site) are no references. A creation under a leaf owner stays an owner-call site too (slice 6); the codes are separate.

**Answers** (`static_api::resolve_scope_answer`, `ScopeAnswer { Tracked, Unplaced, Silent(SiteSilence, premises) }`, no arm but `Tracked` makes a violation): a tracked scope is the violation as before. Past an `await` on every path: `static_api.resolve_scope.past-suspension`, premise the `await` (`PremiseKind::AfterAwait`; `past_suspension_witness` names it, and a proof no span names stays an obligation). An action's step: `step-resumed` (premise the `yield`, `action_step_resumption_witness`), `step-callers-untracked` (every invocation enumerated and none under an observer; `ClosedProgramCallers` at each caller, at the step itself when only handlers reference the action), else an obligation. The primitive whose callback holds the call is matched on the dialect's `slot_run` with no wildcard: `Deferred` is `slot-runs-elsewhere`, `InPlace` with `Clears` is `slot-clears-observer`, a synchronous callback of a `Swallows` slot (`isPending`) is `slot-swallows-throw` (answered before the walk reaches the primitive's own call, which is what made it quiet before), each with the primitive call as premise; an async callback of `isPending` keeps ADR 0959's obligation; `Computation`, `Unknown` and in place with `Keeps`/`Unstated` and `Escapes` are obligations, never silence. No role answer is reached for a callback of a primitive (the slot answers); the nine roles that clear the observer are `role-untracked-rendering`, `-untracked-callback`, `-untracked-unwindowed`, `-effect-apply`, `-event-callback`, `-directive-apply`, `-module-initialization`, `-deferred-callback`, `-discarded-rendering` (premise `RoleDoesNotReport` at the call), as before except that each is typed. Every other role, a deferred role inside tracked JSX and a callee-callback timing the walk does not prove are obligations as before. Four new premise kinds (`SlotRunsElsewhere`, `SlotClearsObserver`, `SlotSwallowsThrow`, `StepResumedByYield`), each with its `boundary.mjs` entry and fixture; a silence dropped by `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE` leaves the call `resolve-scope-unaccounted` (SC2004/SC2005, uncertifiable).

**One change from the brief, stated.** `judged` no longer asks `callback_execution_at_call(..).is_some()` before it asks the slot: the slot answers for every primitive callback that runs directly in the call, so an unstated slot is an obligation. The ids are `static_api.resolve_scope.<end>` (underscore): the two lints that read `site_silences!` match `<stem>.<function>.<end>` with `[a-z0-9_]+` in the function part, so a hyphen there (`static_api.on-flush.role-allows`, `OnFlushRoleAllows`) is not listed by either; that gap is not closed here (the coordinator queued the regex fix and the rename). Ledger edits, approved: `proof-lint.allowlist.json` shrinks (`static_api.rs` default-on-missing 2 to 1, primitive-name-match 8 to 4, prose-hand-off 1 to 0), and `guard/counts.json` rises by the new fixture's rows (SC3001 +66, SC6002 +66, SC4001 +18, SC2004 and SC2005 `async-slot-unmodelled` +1 each; the corpus total is unchanged).

**Measured** (VM, release builds of main 23ad6b7f4 and this change). Corpus, rc.21 34 projects: standard 259,078 findings on both sides, development 280,054 on both, 0 added and 0 removed by key. `make coverage`: the 1,256 fixtures except the new `resolve-until-slots` (the SC2004 and SC2005 twins of three violations, an obligation, nine silent cells and a shadowed local; with every silence ablated each silent cell is `resolve-scope-unaccounted`, never a violation, and `site_accounting_process` pins each silence's count) move nothing. `make proof-gate`: ok, no `resolve` site ends in nothing. Pattern lane in Chrome, the 40 shapes `patterns/resolve/r01-r20` and `u01-u20` (alias, namespace destructure, namespace, `.call`, `Reflect.apply`, array element, `isPending`, `forEach`, helper, map value, `untrack`, `runWithOwner`, `createRoot`, generator, async prefix, object member, class method, `latest`, parameter, returned) and ten probes `x01-x10` of the typed silences (cleanup in a memo, effect apply, microtask, an action called from a memo and from a handler, `onSettled`, a synchronous `click()` in a memo, past an await, a step resumed by a yield, an async `isPending`): main and this change both 50 of 50 fine, 0 false clean. `make fuzz-focus CODES=RESOLVE_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE,UNTIL_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE`: 4,278 programs, nothing needs a look, outcomes equal on both builds. No false clean was found on main (the alias `const r = resolve; createMemo(() => r(p))` is a violation there already: the generator's `alias` binding writes it), so no rediscovery entry.

## ADR 0988 — Every in-place climb ends in a typed stop, and the bound is a seventeenth layer (batch 11, slice 10a)
`climb_in_place_layers` crossed up to sixteen function layers and answered with flags: `exhausted`, `in_list`, `suspended`. Each exit of its loop (no function, a generator, `within`, a fresh stack, a stored function, a withheld call, a JSX-placed layer, the bound) was a `break` that left the same answer, so a consumer that matched on the flags decided those exits by not mentioning them, and a new exit would have been a silent `None`.

**The type.** `InPlaceClimb { at, stop: InPlaceStop, in_list: Option<Span>, suspended: Option<Suspension { every, after }>, among_others, withheld, unmodelled }` and `InPlaceStop { NoFunction, Generator, Within, FreshStack, Elsewhere, Withheld, JsxPlaced, Bound }` (a separate type from ADR 0959's `ClimbStop`, which is the slot climb's; it has no `owes_obligation()` yet: every deciding consumer matches the stop itself, and one is added when a reader needs the grouping). The builders (`climb_layers`, the generator-step run site, the slot climb's in-place segments) always answer with a stop, also for a climb that crossed no layer. The consumers that decide on the climb match `climb.stop` with no wildcard (`#[deny(clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm)]` on the functions, and `every_match_on_a_climbs_stop_names_every_stop` over the sources): `resolve_tracked_scope_within`, `resolve_scope_answer` (twice), `action_step_body_unplaced`, `action_step_body_through`, `unplaced_step`, `unplaced_member_step`, `runs_unplaced_once`, `stored_throw`'s `site`, and the after-await member climb in `static_rules`. The others read the bound only (`climb.bound()`), which is `stop == Bound`. A mutation check: deleting `InPlaceStop::Withheld` from one of the matches fails to compile (E0004, `Withheld` not covered). Each arm that answers `None` or `false` names the net that answers it: the bound's `None` in `action_step_body_through` is `action_step_body_unplaced`'s (it asks again from where the climb stopped), and `runs_unplaced_once`'s bound is the obligation `search-depth-limit`. The `Routes::Members` arm of `runs_unplaced_once` for a generator returns `None` by `(routes == Every && ..)`; its answer is the leaf walk's `GeneratorStepped` operation at the generator's call (slice 6), which a generator stepped in a leaf callback carries as an uncertifiable row (probed, `patterns/depth/g1-leaf-generator`: `onCleanup` in a generator stepped by a `for..of` in a `createTrackedEffect` callback has `generator-stepped` at the generator's call and the body's own `leaf-operation-unaccounted` row, and Chrome reports CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, which both cover).

**The behaviour fix.** `exhausted = step == 15` was set at the sixteenth crossing whether or not anything sat above it, so sixteen layers that ended at a memo's callback, a component, or module scope read as the bound. Now the step after the last one crossed asks the same question of the next layer and says `Bound` only where a seventeenth layer would be crossed. The retrace `climb_crosses_library_callback` and the stepped-generator run site (eight steps, the same off-by-one) follow the same rule. Chrome rc.21 fires `RESOLVE_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE` in a memo, `FLUSH_IN_ACTION` in an action step and `STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED` in a flow child at depth 15, 16 and 17 (the pattern lane, `patterns/depth/`: 3 + 3 + 3 programs, plus `until`).

**Moves** (VM, release builds of slice 7's head and this change). Corpus, rc.21 34 projects, standard and development: 0 findings added or removed. Fixtures: new violations, each Chrome-confirmed: `in-place-depth` `Memo16` (SC2004) and `act16` (SC2006), and `write-climb-depth` `FlowReadSixteen` (SC1001; its twin `FlowReadSeventeen` keeps the obligation). New obligations: only the new fixture's rows. Four obligations leave `value-walk-chain`, each a site exactly sixteen closure layers below the memo's compute (`f284()` in `const f285 = () => f284();`, `f300()` being the chain's last layer): SC1001 `function-run-unplaced` (the caught file's and the settled twin's), SC5001 `source-pending-unproven` and SC5003 `async-read-unaccounted` (the caught file's). The climb now ends at the memo's callback, a function that is no layer, so the site is placed in a tracked, suspendable computation read under `<Loading>`: the strict read is tracked, a pending read there is suspendable, the read is under a boundary. These are the facts that already left the sixteen sites above and the hundreds below it with no row. Chrome (`patterns/depth/w-caught-past-budget`, `w-settled-past-budget`): the caught program reports CAUGHT_REACTIVE_READ only, which SC5008 still covers as an obligation; the settled twin reports nothing. Each fall has its `drops` row in `scripts/guard/counts.json` (proof `climb_layers`; open fixtures `write-climb-depth`, `pending-read-accounted`, `async-boundary-call-attributed`).

**Not done.** The other sixteen-step loops that are not an `InPlaceClimb` (the disposal and write-legality climbs in `write_roles.rs`, the helper-callback retrace in `cleanup.rs`, `static_api`'s two walks) keep their own bounds. `FreshStack` and `Withheld` need a callee the compiler resolved, which the unit tests' synthetic project does not carry; the fixtures on real typings reach them.

## ADR 0987 — SC5006 and SC5007 decide every candidate of one site universe, each exit a named silence; an optimistic setter takes the async decision wherever it is recorded (batch 11, slice 8a; a ratchet for the loading rules, a fix for one false clean of SC2009)
Slice 8a of the total-decision series. **1. The `loading-on` universe (`proof_universe.rs`, `loading_hold::candidates`).** Every place the dialect's async boundary is entered with a way to pass `on` is a site, found by identity and never spelling: a tag, a namespace member, an exact call (`Loading(props)`, `createComponent(Loading, props)`, `.call`), the primitive behind it (`createLoadingBoundary`), a value reference (`dynamicComponent(() => Loading)`, `<Dynamic component={Loading}>`), an unresolved tag. A boundary with no `on` and no spread is a filter and no site. The codes are LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD (SC5006) and LOADING_ON_ACCESSOR (SC5007), both placeless (an SC9012 never credits them: it has no position to name). `loading_hold.rs` is one loop over the candidates (`hold_decision`, `accessor_decision`): each site ends in the rule's own finding, or in a named silence with its premise, or in the uncertifiable row of its rule (blockers `loading-on-outside-hold-unaccounted`, `loading-on-accessor-unaccounted`). **2. The silences.** `LoadingOnNamesNothing` (`OptionLiteral`: the value of `on` has no identifier and no call, so no dependency changes and the boundary never re-arms), `LoadingHoldsNoAsyncSource` (`BoundaryHoldsNoAsync`: the children, only where `unproven_hold` answers `None`, so every child is seen and none reads an async source) and `LoadingOnNotFunction` (`OnValueNotCallable`: the compiler's callability of the value is non-callable, so the boundary's `typeof on === "function"` is false). The primitive's SC5007 is not asked today (its options are not read for a function), so a `createLoadingBoundary` candidate carries only the hold code; that is an open item, not a silence. `loading_hold` is a proof-lint producer. **3. The fixture and the ablation.** `total-decision-silences` holds one negative per silence (`on={1}`, `on={count()}` over children with no async read, a `createOptimistic(0)` setter in a handler) and the namespace and shadowed variants; with `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE=all` each boundary site becomes an uncertifiable row of each rule (the process test `a_loading_boundary_exit_is_a_named_silence_and_unnamed_it_is_an_uncertifiable_row`). **A moved assertion (coordinator-approved)**: `a_removed_row_ends_the_codes_it_answered` asserted that a census-removed row answers every `SiteCode`; it now pins both directions: a placeless code is never answered by SC9012, and every positioned code still is.

**4. SC2009: an optimistic setter takes the async decision wherever it is recorded (`source_discovery/discover_file.rs`, `optimistic_setter_is_async`).** The audit of the SC2009 producers found a false clean on main. A setter is async (it throws OPTIMISTIC_WRITE_BEFORE_LOAD before the first answer) when it comes from `createOptimistic` or `createOptimisticStore`, its first argument is not a data value and no loading value is declared; the declaration path pushed it into `async_sources` on that rule, and absence from `async_sources` was read as a synchronous source. The assignment path (`[o, setO] = createOptimistic(async () => 1)`) and the callback-result path (`returned_sources.rs`, the `setter` arm) recorded the setter and its primitive and never asked, so `setO(2)` raised nothing where Chrome throws (runtime-oracle case `optimistic-setter-forms`, rc.21: unproven-clean on main at the assignment form). All three recordings now ask the one function. The assignment form is an uncertifiable SC2009 (`optimistic-reach-unresolved`, no creating-stack proof exists for an assignment), never a violation; the callback-result (`createRoot(() => createOptimistic(async …))`) and factory forms were already obligations on main (SC9012 `value-held-in-binding`, `handed-member-dispatch`), so the change there is structural (no recording skips the decision) and moves no row. `source_may_be_async` itself is sound: three-state, Sync only by a data literal, a non-callable type or a closed function, anything else Open and so async, a spread argument Open, and a zero-argument `createOptimistic()` synchronous by its text. Fixtures: `rc21-optimistic-setter-forms` (four async forms, four synchronous twins) and the runtime-oracle case; generator: the recall variant `assigned` (`optimistic-async-assigned`). **Proof-gate candidates (coordinator-approved)**: the fixture's `Declared` and `Assigned` setter calls (App.tsx:9:3 and :17:3) are two C2 `reporting-decision-no-row` candidates in `fixtures/proof-log/candidates.json`, the shape and reason of main's four for `rc21-optimistic-before-load` (the code's SC2009 row and SC2001 `write-unaccounted` stand beside each other: no false clean).

**Measured** against main 9878ba9d7 (release builds, 34 projects, rc.21): the standard build 259,078 rows old and new, 0 added, 0 removed; the development build (browser, development, csr) 280,054 and 280,054, 0 and 0; no violation moved; no project failed. `make fuzz-focus` over LOADING_ON_ACCESSOR and OPTIMISTIC_WRITE_BEFORE_LOAD on mx-recall and lg-recall: the old build 36 false cleans (all the `assigned` variant), this head none and no false positive; `rediscovery.json` lists them. The uncertifiable-count ledger rises by the two new fixtures' rows (12 and 57, other families' rows at tags and the stub's SC9014), recorded with `count.mjs --update`; no count falls and no existing snapshot moves.

## ADR 0986 — The promise handler scan skips a file where no call can be a promise handler call (a per-source cost of ADR 0976; no finding moves)
`make verify-performance` failed on this Mac on main: "best first Reactive IR analysis" at 177,000 to 179,000 ns/source against the 175,000 limit (limit unchanged). Measured on release builds of three commits, interleaved, alone under one hold (the widget corpus, 1,000 sources, no `await`): `9d875bff0` (before #237), `23ad6b7f4` (main), and this change.

**What cost.** ADR 0976 S3 added `after_await_accounting::handlers::handler_functions`, which asks `is_handler_call` of every call of every file (the compiler's resolved declaration of the callee, several lookups, then the member's text) before the accounting knows whether the program has any async function. In process, timed around the call (1,000 sources, release, 5 runs each): 0.89 to 1.04 ms before (about 1,000 ns/source), 0.021 to 0.026 ms after (about 22 ns/source). No other code of 0976 runs per source on a program with no `await`: the rest of `sites` is the loop the accounting already ran (about 0.2 ms).

**The change.** A call is a promise handler call only if its callee resolves to a standard `Promise.then`, `.catch`, `.finally` or `PromiseLike.then`, or, with no standard resolution, is a member spelled `then`, `catch` or `finally`. So a file is skipped unless (a) some entity of the path carries a valid resolved call of one of those standard declarations (a flag `EntityLocations` computes once per path, from the rows `is_handler_call` itself reads), or (b) some member of the file is spelled so. Both are necessary conditions of `is_handler_call` answering true, so the answer is the same by construction; a debug build asks again without the gate and asserts the same handler set, so every fixture, process test and coverage run checks it. Nothing was gated on text alone: a call resolved to `Promise.then` through a computed key or a destructured `then` still passes (a).

**No answer moved.** `make coverage`: 1,255 fixture projects, 32,729 findings, no snapshot moved. The corpus (rc21 frozen, 7 apps, 7 projects, release builds of `23ad6b7f4` and this change, `corpus-sweep.mjs --jobs 8`): 36,088 findings each (132 violations, 35,956 uncertifiable), identical rows and hazards project by project (the whole `findings` and `hazards` arrays compared, 51 MB, not only keys).

**Time, as measured (drift included; the limit is untouched).** The gate's statistic (reactiveIrTotal per source, one cold process each), 30 interleaved runs per build, in ns/source:

| build | min | p25 | median | p75 | mean | sd |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `9d875bff0` | 166,139 | 170,765 | 174,701 | 178,774 | 177,238 | 10,469 |
| `23ad6b7f4` (main) | 167,532 | 171,638 | 173,910 | 176,409 | 176,371 | 8,425 |
| this change | 167,781 | 172,387 | 173,599 | 180,621 | 176,969 | 7,696 |

The three builds are not distinguishable at this load: paired medians differ by 106 (main − old), 981 (fix − old) and −309 (fix − main) ns/source against a spread of 8,000 to 10,000. The gate itself (best of 9 per round, mean of the rounds): set 1, 5 rounds: `9d875bff0` 175,014, `eb7055052` 176,950, main 177,059; set 2, 5 rounds, later: `9d875bff0` 178,654, main 180,908, this change 180,926; set 3, 8 rounds, later still: `9d875bff0` 176,916, main 180,864, this change 179,946. `9d875bff0` itself read 172,963 when it was built, 175,014 and 176,916 now, 174,701 as a median of 30: the same commit moved by 2,000 to 4,000 ns/source (1% to 2%) between measurements, which is more than the step this change removes (about 1,000 ns/source) and as much as the margin below the limit. The in-process timing of the removed scan is therefore the proof of what was cut; the gate itself cannot resolve it on this Mac.

**The gate's own noise, and what it taught (same ADR; limit untouched, `report` mode as it was).** `verify-performance` took the best of 9 cold processes with no knowledge of the machine. Changes in `benchmarks/verify-performance.mjs` and `benchmarks/lib/performance-invariants.mjs`: (1) cold samples are drawn one at a time until one reads at or under the ceiling or 40 are spent (`FIRST_IR_MAX_SAMPLES`): the decision is still the minimum, which is at most the ceiling exactly when some sample is, so the early stop cannot change it; a regression raises the floor under every sample and still fails after all 40 (tested); a bootstrap over 117 gate-harness samples of `9d875bff0` gave a hit within 9 samples 38% of the time and within 40 88%; (2) before the first sample the gate waits up to 30 s for the 1-minute load to fall to a quarter of the cores (3.5 on this 14-core Mac), then measures anyway: it never skips and never passes for lack of data; (3) every result, pass or fail, prints the spread (n, min, p25, median, p75, max), the load at the first and last sample, the bound, and the corpus path length; a failure says whether every sample was over and whether the machine was quiet. Cost: a quiet machine reads one or two samples (about 10 s less than 9), a busy one waits 30 s, a failing one takes 40 samples (about +35 s). No other statistic was kept: over 25 loaded samples the median and p25 pass the good commit 0% (they read the load, not the code), the minimum 74%.

**Measured: the corpus path length is an input (open item).** Probe, 15 interleaved rounds, one binary, 1-minute load 4.5 to 5.9: the gate's own launch path against direct runs. Parent process (bun or node) made no difference (paired median +905 ns/source). The corpus in `$TMPDIR` (93-character directory) read +10,992 ns/source over a corpus in a short scratch directory (51 characters); in a second probe, a corpus in a `.noindex` temp directory read +9,286 (Spotlight is not the cause), the temp corpus +7,542, and a scratch corpus under a padded 93-character path +8,040: the path length is the cause, about 190 ns/source per character. A per-source cost that grows with the path is a checker inefficiency (real projects have long paths), likely repeated path-string work per entity; it is not fixed here (docs/open-work.md, perf leads). The gate does not shorten or pad its corpus path to pass: it prints the path and its length. This also means the in-process timing of the handler scan above (60-character path) understates its cost at the gate's path.

**Not done.** The per-call cost of `is_handler_call` stays for a file that does name a promise handler: its `function_called_at` per argument was about 0.35 ms of the 0.75 ms an argument-first order left, and costs the same lookups as the call it replaces. A cheaper exact order for those files needs a per-file index of calls by resolved standard declaration, which `EntityLocations` does not keep.

## ADR 0989 — The static API's calls end (SC7001, SC7002, SC2007), `sync` is read as the runtime reads it, and a render effect's async compute is a site of SC5003 (batch 11, slice 8b)
Slice 8b gives the `static_api` rules with only unnamed negative branches a site universe (`proof_universe::primitive_call_sites`, found from `primitive_at_call` and the dialect's own questions, never a spelling: a namespace member and an alias are sites, a shadowed local is none) and names each silent branch. The probes (below) found three false positives and one false clean on main, which close here.

**Sites and silences** (ids `static_api.<function>.<end>`; each with its premise span, a `boundary.mjs` entry and `fixtures/reactive-ir/static-api-silences` / `rc9-static-dynamic-async`; `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE=all` turns each silent call into the family's `<family>-unaccounted` row, pinned by `site_accounting_process`).
- `effect-fn` (MISSING_EFFECT_FN; every call of a primitive with `effect_function_slot`): `slot-callable` (the apply is provably callable: a function, a bundle whose `effect` is one, a callable-only type domain; premise `ArgumentShape`) and `tsc-rejected` (the resolved call is `Recovery` and no directive may silence it; premise `TscReportsAtSite`; where one may, the SC9012 stands). **The no-fact path is an obligation:** a call with no resolved-call fact (or `Unresolved`) used to fall into the invalid branches and end `No`, a silent clean; it is `Uncertain` (`effect-argument-shape-uncertain`) now, for `missing_effect_function` only (`owner_registration` is unchanged). No program of the corpus or the lane reaches it (the demand plan asks a resolved call for every call), so it has no cell. SC7001's unaccounted row is a static defect, as the rule is.
- `sync-option` (SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC; `supports_sync_option && options_argument`): `not-asserted` (premise `OptionsLiteral`), `tsc-reports` (a duplicate `sync` key, TS1117 in every configuration: strict and not, ES5 and ES2022, TypeScript 5.9.3 on the rc.21 typings; premise `TscReportsAtSite` at the later key) and `computation-not-async` (`StaticSource::Sync`, or a value that is no function; never `Open`; premise `StaticSourceState`).
- `dynamic-static` (DYNAMIC_STATIC_PROMISE; `Dialect::static_dynamic_form`, new: `Static` or `MayBeStatic`): `source-synchronous` (a closed return type with no thenable, a sync or async generator: the static form throws on a thenable only; premise `StaticSourceState` at the source function). `Open` stays an obligation. A `dynamic()` call with no argument has no static form, so it is no site.

**The `sync` option is read as the runtime reads it.** The rule took `sync: true` from ANY literal `true` property, and the runtime reads the LAST `sync` (a spread after the literal, or a later duplicate key). Chrome rc.21, `createMemo(async () => 1, OPTS)` under `<Loading>` (pattern lane `syncopt/`): `{ sync: true, sync: false }`, `{ sync: true, ...{ sync: false } }` and `{ sync: true, ...over }` (`over: { sync?: boolean }`, `sync: false`) are quiet, and main reported a violation for each; `{ sync: false, sync: true }` (under a directive) and `{ sync: true }` fire and are violations. Only the `{ sync: true, ...over }` form is not TypeScript's (TS2783 fires on a literal spread under strict only, and not for an optional type). The fix (`sync_option_state`): a violation only where the exact literal's last `sync` is `true` (`call_option_literal`: no spread, no computed key); any other options the syntax cannot read keep the existing obligation; a duplicate key with no directive is TypeScript's (`TscSilence::Reports` at a later key), under a directive both compilers read the last one decides, and one compiler's possible suppression is an obligation. Main: 14 lane programs false positive (5 primitives x spread and duplicate, `d1`, `d3`, `d4`); this head 0. `fuzz-focus` (`--grids lg-recall`, SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC), the new recall legal cells `opt-spread` and `opt-spread-effect` (body, root, memo, every binding and layer; `variantOnlyLegal`, since the plain `sync: true` variants report in those contexts): 660 programs, main 180 false positives, this head none (540 uncertifiable, 120 unexecuted).

**`createTrackedEffect` takes no `sync`.** Chrome rc.21: `createTrackedEffect(async () => ..., { sync: true })` raises nothing. `@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.21` `dist/dev.js:2878-2892`: `trackedEffect` builds its node as `computed(() => { ... const cleanup = staleValues(fn); if (cleanup !== undefined && typeof cleanup !== "function") throw ...; node._cleanup = cleanup; }, { ...options, lazy: true })`, so the node's compute returns `undefined`; SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC is raised in `handleAsync` on the node's compute result (`dist/dev-shared.js:3769-3812`, the `CONFIG_SYNC` check at `:3797`), which is never a thenable there. `sync` is forwarded and inert, as for the store family. `CreateTrackedEffect` leaves `supports_sync_option` (a main false positive, `syncopt/s-tracked-*`, `t1`).

**A render effect's async compute is a site of SC5003** (a false clean on main). `createRenderEffect(async () => 1, () => {})` outside any `<Loading>` raises ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY in Chrome (`syncopt/r0`, `r1`, `r5`) and no row stood at it: the pending accounting's sites (ADR 0838) were reads of pending sources, and a compute is no read. The runtime's report is `notifyEffectStatus` (`dist/dev.js:2672-2700`), made `else if (this._type === EFFECT_RENDER)`: a render effect whose status is pending with no boundary above (`_hitUnhandledAsync`, set by the root's `notify`). A user effect's compute (`createEffect`, `EFFECT_USER`) and a tracked effect's are not (`r2`: Chrome quiet), and the other compute slots (a memo, a projection, a signal) reach the code only through a read of them, which the read sites cover (`r3`). New dialect question `render_effect_compute` (`createRenderEffect`); `static_api::render_effect_computes_not_proven_sync` lists the calls whose compute is not proven synchronous (`computation_answer`, the one SC7002 asks); the pending accounting's site (5), SC5003 alone, is ended by the cover walk's `UnderLoading`, a discarded region or a reviewed fresh stack, else it is an uncertifiable `async-read-unaccounted` row. Always an obligation, never a violation: that the call runs inside the mount's enforcement window with no boundary above is not proven (a module-level or handler-created render effect may be outside it), so no new violation needs Chrome. The corpus holds no such call.

**Measured** (VM, release builds of main 23ad6b7f4 and this head; `static_api` and the pending accounting are the same on 1c4474512 for these shapes). Corpus, rc.21, 34 projects, standard 259,078 findings and development 280,054 on both sides, 0 added and 0 removed. `make coverage`: seven existing fixtures gain one obligation each, all the render-effect compute site (`createRenderEffect(other, ..)` over an async memo accessor in the four `effect-apply-first-run` variants, a variable in `rc13-flush-in-effect-callback`, `render-apply-first-run`, and an async function in `eslint-plugin-corpus`), named in `rises.json`; the new fixture `static-api-silences` (and `rc9-static-dynamic-async` for SC2007) pins every silence. `make proof-gate`: ok. Pattern lane in Chrome, `syncopt/` (32 programs): main 18 fail (15 false positive, 3 false clean: `r0`, `r1`, `r5`), this head 0. `proof-lint`: `static_api.rs` `primitive-name-match` 4 to 3 (approved shrink). Known and equal on both builds: `fuzz-focus`'s two `stacked-claim` programs of `mx-sync-node-received-async-apply-void-call-*` (open defect R-stacked) and one inconclusive oracle run.

**Not done.** A `createRenderEffect` created in an event handler is a `missing-owner` (SC4001) obligation on main that Chrome does not report (no NO_OWNER diagnostic): untouched, equal on both builds. The `dynamic-static` family's other arms were already obligations. The duplicate-key and tracked-effect shapes are lane programs only (no generator shape; `rediscovery.json` says why).

## ADR 0990 — The closed-program twin, three more fuzz cells, and a named callback of a slot that takes what it throws (batch 11, slices 5 to 7)
**The twin.** A generated program has no manifest of its own, so the checker reads the install's `{ "private": true }`: every grid ran closed. `focus.mjs --boundary open|closed|both` gives each checker project that boundary's manifest (`SOLID_CHECKER_FUZZ_BOUNDARY`, checker.mjs `boundaryOverride`); `both` runs the grids twice with the Chrome records taken from the runtime cache (the runtime does not read the manifest) and `boundary-twin.mjs` reads the two runs side by side: `closed-silent`, `open-silent` and `open-false-positive` are blockers, a violation the open world hands off is a named cost. Measured (release 3bd824913, ph er em ob la sf rs cs pa fc, mx-recall and lg-recall, 6,296 programs a run): closed and open gave the same outcome for every program. The cause is the harness entry (`import * as mod`, a loop over the exports): every export of App is entered by code the checker cannot see, so no closed-only proof is reached in a grid (ADR 0980 says the same of its own cells). `--entry named` gives the checker project an entry that names the exports the loop enters (`namedEntry`: `default` and the capitalised function exports, mount names first, the rest in namespace order, the oracle's driver byte for byte; an export it cannot classify keeps the namespace entry); Chrome's entry and records are unchanged. Validated: 40 grid programs (two cells of each family and side) through the real oracle with each entry (the oracle's new opt-in `main` field), 40 of 40 Chrome records equal. (closed,named) against (open,named): 0 blockers, 0 lost violations; the named entry changes 15 legal verdicts and no violation (`ob-field-helper-*-never` twins: clean closed, SC4001 uncertifiable open, a named cost of the open world). The cross-file closed axis (brief 05's variant 2) is not built: ADR 0980's fixture `flush-holder-put-crossfile` and the `pkghand/` pattern lane hold it, and a grid's entry cannot show it.

**The cells** (recall contexts, measured on rc.21 in the Chrome host and the real oracle, 0 behaviour differences). A: `pl-<layer>-named` and `pl-<layer>-named-async` (the callback declared in the host's callback, handed by name), 84 contexts of the ten codes; Chrome measured every named layer as its literal twin in all 840 (code, host, layer) pairs (462 cells added to `PL_MEASURED`, none changed). B: `fr-<form>-<host>[-never]` (`untrack(flush)`, an alias, `[flush][0]()`, a helper's parameter; `flush`, `resolve`, `until`; action, tracked, effect-apply, memo), 30 contexts. C: ob family C on the leaf hosts (`ob-<form>-tracked-exp`, `-settled-exp`), 36 contexts for the three leaf codes. B and C: 198 programs a grid, 0 not-fired, 0 false clean, 0 false positive; every checker violation is Chrome-confirmed (4 alias cells, 120 leaf-C). One leaf-C row reads `unproven-clean` in the oracle and `agree` in the grids (the violation stands at an application frame of Chrome's stack); recorded in open-work.md. The API-fire plan grew from 1,885 to 2,377 programs and is now three test files (125 to 136 s each against the 300 s limit that stays).

## ADR 0991 — The write walk's region fold asks the withheld-layer veto the path walk asks (brief 07: the proof log dropped a row the plain build never had)
**What was measured.** On main 3bd824913 (release, the rc.21 frozen corpus, 34 projects) the plain build and the build with `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_PROOF_LOG` (or the role log) answered differently: the standard build's log run has 10 more rows, the development build's 7 more and 1 fewer (expenses-app's SC9012 `standard-member-impostor` at `clerk.tsx` 1316..1323). The 10 and the 7 are SC2002 `package-may-call-action` rows: expenses-app `src/lib/clerk.tsx` (5, in `sync`'s `setState` call), app-game `apps/abr-viewer/src/features/brush-preview/thumbnail-cache.ts` (2), skyjtx-website `NavigationMenu.tsx` (3, standard build only). Each is a call into an unread package that the plain build left silent and the logged build made an uncertifiable row: an unproven clean claim.

**Cause.** `every_path()` (`write_components.rs`) is true under the role log, which the proof log switches on, so the write walk's region fold (ADR 0546) is skipped and the paths are followed. The path walk asks, of each caller, `semantic_write_execution_role_within`, whose first check is ADR 0874's veto (a caller in a callback of a withheld standard call has no role: nothing places code an impostor may run, or never run). The fold's `place_sites` called `write_role_walk` and `write_role_fallback` directly and never asked it. In `clerk.tsx` a program-wide veto (`hashKey`'s unspelled-key write into a handed object, in `@solidjs/router`) withholds `Promise.prototype.then`, so `sync`, called in a `then` callback and in a listener nested in it, has two callers nothing places: the paths answer `Unknown`, the fold answered a deferred callback and the writes and calls in `sync` were silent. ADR 0546 promised the two answers are the same; the fold's was the less conservative one, in the plain product build.

**Fix (`execution_role/write_roles.rs`, `write_components.rs`).** One helper, `withheld_caller_role`: the veto with its `role_arm!`, asked by `semantic_write_execution_role_within` (the path walk, `caller_loop`'s reference fold) and by `place_sites` (the region fold, before the walk and the fallback, in the order `caller_loop` uses). A withheld caller is an `Entry::Value(Unknown)` with a `Placed` entry, so only `Unknown` is added and no violation can follow. **The audit of the other folds `every_path()` turns off**: `site_reach.rs` and `indexes/initialization.rs` read `every_path_asked()`, the test toggle only (the log does not move them); the helper-walk memo (`local_access.rs`) is a cache. The corpus diff below is the check that nothing else differs.

**Measured** (main 3bd824913 base, release, 34 projects, plain and `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_PROOF_LOG=/dev/null`): before, standard 264,422 plain / 264,432 log, development 285,667 / 285,673; after, plain = log exactly (264,432 and 285,673, 0 added, 0 removed in both), and the fixed plain equals the pre-fix log (the 10 and the 7 rows appear, expenses-app's SC9012 is back): **+10 rows standard, +7 rows development, 0 violations moved**. **Chrome**: no runtime check applies to the 17 rows: none of the three programs calls an `action`, and the unread packages the rows name call none, so Solid reports nothing there; they are obligations on calls whose role the plain build had placed as deferred under a veto that says nothing places them (an unproven clean, not a defect Chrome shows).

**Fixtures and tests.** `write-fold-withheld-caller` (the veto, `onSettled` → `load().then(…)` → `bus.addListener(() => { sync(); }); sync();`, an arrow alias of the call, a callee in another file, which is exported so uncertifiable in both builds) and `write-fold-withheld-caller-no-veto` (the same without the veto: silent in both). `write_walk_strategies_process::a_caller_in_a_withheld_layer_is_unknown_in_the_fold_and_on_every_path` builds the program following every path, folded and with the role log and asserts the three equal and every write `Unknown` (and the no-veto program none `Unknown`); `proof_log_process::the_proof_log_changes_no_answer` holds both fixtures. Each fails on the pre-fix code (the fold differs from every path; the proof log moved an answer) and passes on the fix. **Not generated**: no fuzz grid writes the proof-log toggle, and the shape (a program-wide veto, a `then` callback, a listener nested in it, in an `onSettled`) is not in a generator, so `rediscovery.json` names the fixtures and the corpus diff.

## ADR 0992 — The Solid 2 dialect answers what Solid's own components do with a value that enters them (`Dialect::component_entry`): `lazy`'s loaded export, `Portal`'s children, `Dynamic`'s `component` (batch 11, the Solid half of the proof batch's first item)
**The premise (ADRs 0970, 0971).** The owner emission read a component a reference enters (a `lazy` loader's module, `<Dynamic component={X}>`) as entered by a route no owner edge shows, and a creation written in a component element's children as a getter that runs where an unknown reader calls it, so each kept an uncertifiable SC4001, SC3001 and SC6002 row. Solid's own components are dialect vocabulary, never dependency source, so what they do with such a value is a `Dialect` question read from the pinned source (invariant 7), not a package proof. The package half (a router, a literal `import("pkg")` loader, the `-pk-lazy` placement) stays the proof batch's first item.

**The question.** `Dialect::component_entry(export, slot) -> Option<ComponentEntry>`, answered by `Solid2` on the rc.21 triple only (every other installation, and every slot no source was read for, answers `None`, which leaves the layer open). The engine asks it only of a component whose every declaration is in one of the dialect's packages under one export name (`SemanticLookup::component_entry_of_tag`), never by spelling. Read on rc.21 (`solid-js` `dist/solid.dev.js`, `@solidjs/web` `dist/web.dev.js`): `lazy`'s `wrap(props)` is `createMemo(() => createComponent(Comp, props), { sync: true })` with `Comp` the loaded `mod.default` or `mod[options.export]` (`:1409-1446`), `createComponent` running the body in a transparent root: `RenderedUnderOwner`. `Portal` is `runWithOwner(createOwner(), …)` and reads `props.children` in `createMemo(() => [startMarker, props.children])` (`web.dev.js:2388-2399`): `ReadTrackedUnderOwner` for `children`; `mount` is read again under `untrack(mount)` in the render effect's apply (`:2402`), so it answers `None`. `Dynamic` is `createComponent(dynamic(() => props.component), omit(props, "component"))` and `dynamicCore`'s component calls a function in `createMemo(() => … untrack(() => component(props)))` (`:2451`, `solid.dev.js:1544`): `RenderedUnderOwner` for `component`. `dynamic(source)` answers `None` (its `static` form calls the component with no computation around it, `staticDynamic`, `:1570`), `lazyModule` renders nothing, and `Loading` answers `None` here: `async_boundary_shape` is its one answer (ADR 0978), not a second one.

**What asks it.** (1) `getter_relation` (ADR 0971): a creation written directly in the slot the dialect answers `ReadTrackedUnderOwner` for (a `Portal`'s children, not a namespaced attribute, a spread or another prop) is `InPlace`, as in a dialect control-flow element, so it is no getter site. (2) The namespace census (ADR 0347) already named a function a `lazy(() => import("…"))` loader reads; it now says which are handed out only by such a loader the dialect says renders under an owner (`NamespaceHandOuts::named_only_by_lazy_render`): the facts' `Lazy` consumer (the loader is the whole first argument, a concise arrow whose body is the import; options with no spread, computed key or non-literal `export`), `lazy` Solid's by its import binding, the specifier resolving to one project module, the export a function declaration or a `const` whose binding no write, redeclaration or `eval` reaches, and no other read of it (a static member read, a named dynamic-import read that is no such `lazy`). `entered_by_tags_only` (ADR 0970) takes such a render, and a reference that is the exact value of a prop the dialect answers `RenderedUnderOwner` for (`<Dynamic component={X}>`, through the ADR 0138 value-flow index), for an entry as a tag is; every other test of `entered_by_unseen_code` stays (an open program, a namespace that escapes with no name). (3) The package hand-off (ADR 0976's `unread-package-may-run`) no longer takes the value of such a prop for one handed to a package nothing here reads: the dialect's component runs it in a memo of its own. It is placed, never handed, and only for the dialect-answered slot of an exactly resolved tag. Closing a layer turns an uncertifiable row into silence, never into a violation.

**Fail closed, and what stays open.** A loader through a variable or a `.then` (the shape the corpus writes), `S.lazy` and `lazy as load` (the facts name a `lazy` read only for the identifier `lazy`), a local function named `lazy`, a `let` export rebound later (the module's export is live and `lazy` reads it once the promise settles), an export another read names, an open program, `<Web.Dynamic>` (a dotted tag the value-flow index does not resolve), a `Dynamic` value reached through a memo's accessor (the owner emission closes it, the package hand-off keeps its row), a project component named `Portal` or `Dynamic`, and `Portal`'s `mount` keep their rows (docs/open-work.md). `clean-lazy-route` stays held: its loader is `import("./clean-lazy-route").then((mod) => ({ default: mod.Admin }))` and its B3 and SC1002 rows are other proofs'; `HELD_CAP` 60 to **59** (not 58), `clean-portal-show`'s `held` block removed (coordinator, 2026-11-15).

**Measured** (rc21 frozen corpus, 34 projects, release, `make corpus-delta`-style `--all`, origin/main `09f905f78` against this change, a per-row old/new diff on top): development build V 212 to 212, U 283,812 to **281,596 (-2,216**: SC3001 -934, SC6002 -865, SC4001 `owner-callers-unenumerated` -416, `package-finding-at-entry` -1); standard build (no runtime flags) V 218 to 218, U 262,415 to **260,209 (-2,206**: -925, -865, -416). 18 projects move (kui 10 at -48 each, Portal children; app-game -1,534, lazy pages; probus-hk, every-deck-of-cards, ai-memory-ui, inferay, expenses-app, solid-groove, hoxxes-briefing), **0 rows added, 0 violations moved**. The SC4001 total is over the brief's 378: the corpus and the base moved since the brief's base `eb0e2dd16`. Fixtures: `portal-children-owner`, `lazy-entry-owner`, `dynamic-component-owner` (positive, negative and the shadowed, aliased, namespace, member and rebound variants), three existing projects move by removed rows only (`uncertifiable-repro/other-rules`, `stored-throw-value-mount`: `Handled` and `Reported`'s SC3001, `context-package-lazy`: `Local`).

**Chrome (rc.21, `fixtures/runtime-oracle`).** `lazy-entry-owner`, `portal-children-owner`, `portal-mount-owner`, `dynamic-component-owner`: the silent sites report nothing, and each twin a false clean would hide in fires and is covered: a lazy component also called from a timer is a checker violation confirmed in Chrome (NO_OWNER_CLEANUP), also read through a namespace and called, covered; a `Dynamic` component also stored and called from an effect's apply, covered; `Portal`'s `mount` (PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK), covered.
