## ADR 0994 — `verify-performance` under its limit: three quadratic scans removed, a file's own path answered by address, and mimalloc as the process allocator (no answer moves)
`make verify-performance` read 178,771 to 183,609 ns/source on main (limit 175,000, unchanged; 93-character corpus path). Attribution first (ten first-parent merges `23ad6b7f4`..`1108e2186`, release builds, 30 interleaved rounds of 5 runs each, one `SC_HEAVY_FIRST` hold per round; reactiveIrTotal per source, median): 176,848 to 181,465, of which one step is outside the spread, `3bd824913` (ADR 0981, +4,354 paired, all in `reactiveIr.finalOrdering`, 38.5k to 42.7k); every other merge moved less than the +-2-3k paired spread. Main `5ef5d7914` re-measured as the baseline: median 180,342 to 181,862 over three sets.

**Three scans, each the same answer by construction** (a debug build asks the old way and asserts the same, so every fixture, process test and coverage run checks it). (1) `local_access::optimistic_async_setter` asked, for every setter call, whether ANY setter row of the program shares the declaration of an optimistic async creation, by scanning every row and comparing locations (one setter per file on the benchmark corpus: calls x setters path compares). Only a symbol of `async_sources` can be that creation, so it asks those: -5.2k ns/source, all in `finalOrdering`. (2) `FileTable::id_of` hashed and compared the whole path for each question; a file's own path (`file.path.as_str()`, a location made from it) now answers by the address and length of the allocation the table holds (a held `Arc`, so the address names those bytes while the table lives; any other `&str` takes the string's route): -3.5k, and it removes most of the path-length cost ADR 0986 measured. (3) `tracked_async_computation_context` compared the path of every file to the async function's for each of the 1,000 module-level async facts (1M compares); it reads the slots of the function's path (`FileTable::slots_of_path`, the whole-program read is still noted): -1k. Three-fix total -7.5k (median 173.4k).

**The read ratchet** (`scripts/ir-read-lint.allowlist.json`, `local_access.rs` hashmap-iteration 4 to 6, the coordinator's yes): the two new sites are the `any` of `optimistic_async_setter`, one over the async-source set (production) and one over every setter row (the debug assertion). Both are order-independent membership tests that read no other file's facts; the old scan's `.iter()` sat on its own line, which the lexical lint never counted, so the count rises though the scan shrank.

**mimalloc.** malloc, free and table growth were about a sixth of the CPU of a first build in the profile (24 sampled cold runs). `mimalloc-safe =0.1.67` (napi-rs; MIT; locks `libmimalloc-sys2 0.1.63`, MIT, which vendors C mimalloc 2.5.2, MIT, and `cmake 0.1.58` as a build dependency; `libc` and `cc` were already locked) is the global allocator of `solid-checker-rust` and of both bench binaries, so the gate measures what ships; it is a target dependency under `cfg(not(target_family = "wasm"))` and so are the statics (the wasm32-wasip1 tree holds none). Non-MSVC targets need the `cmake` binary at build time (GitHub-hosted ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-15 and windows-2025 images carry it; the windows-msvc branch of its build script uses `cc` only). Paired, 50 runs, reactiveIrTotal median: main 180,342 (min 176,248), three fixes 171,369, fixes + mimalloc 155,020 (min 150,632): -25.4k (14%); wallTotal -35.9k (11%).

**The daemon's reclaim.** `idle_memory::reclaim_idle_pages` (after each materialized answer) called libSystem's `malloc_zone_pressure_relief` / glibc's `malloc_trim`, which mimalloc bypasses. The replacement in `unsafe_boundary` (a safe wrapper, `// SAFETY:`) calls `mi_collect(false)`, mimalloc's ordinary pass. The forced pass (`mi_collect(true)`) was measured and rejected: 1,000-file project, one edit and one request each, daemon RSS after 40 requests 2,416 MB with it, 677 MB with no reclaim, 621 MB with `mi_collect(false)`; after 120 requests 4,054 MB with it (the daemon's 15%-of-RAM limit would end it and the next check run cold). Final, 120 edited requests, release checker, daemon RSS: main 849 MB (process tree 1,164 MB), this change 667 MB (967 MB); neither falls after 4 s idle. In-process (session bench, 60 edited iterations): 484 MB against 574 MB. Peak RSS of one cold run: 301 MB against 316 MB.

**No answer moved.** `make coverage` (debug build: the three `debug_assert`s ask the old scans): 1,277 fixture projects, 34,058 findings, no snapshot moved. Corpus (rc21 frozen, 34 projects, release builds of `5ef5d7914` and of this head, `corpus-sweep.mjs --jobs 8` over five app groups because one whole-corpus report overflows a JavaScript string; `findings`, `hazards`, `premises`, status and exit code compared as whole arrays, project by project): identical in all three configurations, 34 of 34 projects each, 102 results: development 281,814 findings (212 violations, 281,602 uncertifiable), production 281,814 (the same), and no runtime flags 260,437 (218 violations, 260,219 uncertifiable). The allocator changes no answer by construction; the corpus run is the check.

**The gate.** `make verify-performance` enforced, this head, release, 1-minute load 3.4 (quiet bound 3.5): `performance certification passed (wall-time gate: enforce): ... best first IR 159961 ns/source (1 cold sample ...; stopped at the first sample under the ceiling)`, limit 175,000 untouched: 15,039 ns/source (8.6%) under it on that one sample (the interleaved median of reactiveIrTotal is 155,020, min 150,632). The limit, the judge and the statistic are as they were.

**Not done** (docs/open-work.md, the path-length lead): the path-length cost fell from about 160 to 115 ns per character per source (93-character against 60-character directory, 20 interleaved runs: main 179,981 against 174,650, this 154,835 against 151,008). The serial tail of a first build still holds `package_action_calls::sites` (8.1 ms on 1,000 sources: an origin walk per call), `value_reads::rows` (4.8 ms, ADR 0981: 8,000 origin walks) and the runtime-configuration scan (7.6 ms); none is a scan that grows with the project, and a per-site gate for the first two needs a proof that no origin can end in a package, which `origin_of`'s limit and ambient arms make no cheap premise. The new allocator is measured on macOS aarch64 only; the other three CI targets build it for the first time in CI.

## ADR 0993 — Every project source file of a case is judged like App.tsx (the grid judge: matrix, legal, the oracle's record and the pattern lane; owner-approved judge change)
**The miss.** The judges that read a checker row and a Chrome frame mapped them only through App.tsx: `classify.mjs offSiteVerdicts` (the matrix and legal off-site violations) read `appLines`, App.tsx's text and counters; `matrix.mjs judgeSite` read `attributed` frames and `checker.findings` of App.tsx and, for a code Chrome cannot place (`unplaceableCodes`), looked for the claiming row in App.tsx only; `legal.mjs` read `checker.findings` as the program's. A violation or a frame in a second PROJECT module (`site1.tsx`, `helpers.ts`) was unplaced and unjudged. ADR 0992's project-site cells (`lazy-call-proj` on SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED) showed it: SC4001 at `site1.tsx:4:13` and Chrome's SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED, scored `false-clean` (6 programs). **A judge miss, not a checker defect**: the checker reports the violation and Chrome confirms it. The runtime oracle (`runtime-oracle.mjs`) and the pattern lane (`patterns.mjs`) were already file-aware (their findings and positions carry `file`): the tests pin them, no behaviour changes there.

**The change** (`scripts/fuzz`). `site-judge.mjs` is the one place: `positionFile`, `framesIn`, `linesIn` (a frame is one file's, never another's), `programFindings`/`findingsIn` (App.tsx's rows and every module's, each with its `file`), `labelOf`/`lineOfLabel`/`fileOfLabel` (a module's judge row is `rule@site1.tsx:4`, App.tsx's keep `rule@4`), and `splitChecker` (the real-Chrome oracle's record lists every file's rows in `findings`; the fast path keeps App.tsx's there and the others in `moduleFindings`: the judges split the first into the second, so a module's row is never read as App.tsx's by its line, which the Chrome path did by accident). `offSiteVerdicts` judges each finding in its own file: that file's frames, text and `placedAnywhere` (a report with a frame in no project file at all is unplaced; one placed in another file is that file's); a module carries no counter, so a violation there nothing accounts for is a false-positive candidate of unknown run (`why: "module"`, as `site-judge.mjs accountViolations` counts an unknown run as ran). `judgeSite` honors `site.file`, and a code Chrome cannot place is claimed by a violation of the rule in any project file; `judgeParts` and `legal.mjs judgeLegal`/`withOffSite` judge every file's violations, a row at the site only in the site's file; `repeat-twin.mjs` builds no twin for a module claim. **`unattributed` is a report** (`offSiteVerdicts`): the oracle's record keeps a diagnostic Chrome could not attribute to a file in `unattributed`, not in `diagnostics`, so the budget of a placeless code saw 0 raised against one violation and judged the module's violation `false-positive(disturbed)` (on main the Chrome path read it as `agree`, by the accident above); a code now counts as many times as the larger of the two lists says. **Wired**: the project-site cells (`PROJECT_SITE_CODES` on `-proj` entries `lazy`, `dynamic-el`, `lazy-call`) are crossed by the recall grids (`matrix.mjs packageShapes`), 31 mx and 48 lg programs. The ADR 0992 entry of `rediscovery.json` and the open-work item are closed by this one.

**Tests.** `project-modules.test.mjs` (30): a V in `site1.tsx` with a frame there is an agreement, with no diagnostic a false-positive candidate, a frame there with no row a false clean, a package frame places nothing, a frame in App.tsx at the same line number accounts for nothing in the module, the matrix, legal and offSiteVerdicts judges, the oracle's record shape. 14 fail on the old judge and pass on this one; the pattern-lane and `accountViolations` cases (already file-aware) pass on both. The whole `scripts/fuzz` suite: the same 27 environment failures (`stripTypeScriptTypes` absent in the VM's Node) before and after, +30 passing.

**Measured, no browser rerun.** (1) *The 79 project-site programs in Chrome* (the grids' own run, the oracle confirming the 31 mx programs), the judge of main 8e05f2a1c against this one on the same records: exactly 6 verdicts move, `false-clean` to `agree` (`mx-settled-cleanup-unowned-{handler,timer,then,micro,async,owner-null}-x-direct-none-pk-lazy-call-proj`, each SC4001 at `site1.tsx:4:13` with the SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED page error in the oracle's record); the other 25 mx programs and all 48 lg (uncertifiable on both) are identical. (2) *Stored outputs*: the programs whose generated case holds a project module (585,976 of 2,193,773, all 11 grids), judged by the old and this judge from the audit's own Chrome records (`cachefs/audit`, read-only, the checker rerun, no browser): 579,038 identical, 0 moved, 6,938 (1.2%: mx-recall 4,924, lg-recall 2,014) have no stored record (programs newer than the audit) and are not judged. The stored dfa6c5dec oracle records (76,490) explain it: 3,793 hold a module file in a finding or diagnostic, 8,451 module findings, every one uncertifiable, 1 diagnostic of 44,960 in a module (covered-uncertifiable): no generated program had a module violation. (3) *The `unattributed` change*: the audit's fast-host records hold no `unattributed` at all (0 of the 2M files), so the grids cannot move by it; the 4,679 dfa6c5dec oracle records with one (REACTIVITY_HALTED 2,827, SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED 2,514, ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY 130, CAUGHT_REACTIVE_READ 126, ...) were judged by `judge`/`judgeLegalProgram` from the oracle row (3,425 regenerated by id; 1,254 ids are no longer generated and are not judged): 3,386 identical, **0 outcome moved**, 39 detail-only changes, all toward accounting: 35 off-site `unjudged(disturbed-no-hit-ledger)` rows now `substantiated` (the code Chrome could not attribute is counted), 4 `agree` rows list fewer findings (a helper's row at the same line number is no longer read as App.tsx's).

**The oracle's `stack: []`** (docs/open-work.md, `runtime-oracle.mjs` builds a thrown diagnostic with no application frames): this function would let it be fixed later without touching a judge, because `framesIn`/`positionFile` already attribute each frame to its file: the oracle would only have to put the throw's frames (with their files) into the diagnostic's `stack`, and `accountViolations` and the matrix judge would read them like any placed code's. Not done here: it needs the observation's frames, which the feedback report does not carry.

## ADR 0995 — Precision ratchets that hold a change to its base: sites, removed violations, frozen judge, candidates, held cases, lints, no base is a failure
A proved result could silently become an unproven one, and a ledger could be regenerated to launder it. The review of the guards (2026-11-15, items 1-14) found each ratchet compared with itself, or with a total that hides the move. This tightens them; no limit, allowlist entry, judge verdict, held case or classification changed, and each new check passes on main itself (base = head).

**What fails now, and how an intended change is recorded** (each tool's `--help` prints its own row):

| Moved | Fails when | Record it in | Row |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Uncertifiable rows per site (`count.mjs`) | a (fixture, key, path) lost rows while the fixture's total held, rose, or fell by less than its paths lost | `scripts/guard/counts.json` `drops` | `{ fixture, key, path, from, to, adr, kind: "moved", movedTo }` (a row that stayed in the fixture at another path: no proof), or `{ …, path, proof, fixtures }` (a clean at that path, proved at that path and in total) |
| A proved violation (`regress.mjs`) | a violation of a code left a path (turned uncertifiable at its span, or gone; a deleted fixture's too); by span where the file's bytes are unchanged since the base, by count where they changed | `scripts/guard/regress.json` | `{ fixture, path, code, removed, adr, why }` via `node scripts/guard/regress.mjs --append "ADR NNNN" --why "…"` |
| `scripts/fuzz/judge-frozen.json` (`base.mjs`) | a row removed or changed, or a judge table changed, with no new `changes` row | its `changes` list, same commit | `{ id, was, now, adr, why, program }` (a table: `{ table, added, adr, why, program }`); `freeze-judge.mjs` writes only to a path (`--out`) and refuses one that holds rows or changes |
| `fixtures/proof-log/candidates.json` (`base.mjs`) | a key the base lacks has no `adr` or no `owner` | the entry | `{ owner, adr, why, at }`, or fix the site and delete the entry |
| Held cases and `HELD_CAP` (`base.mjs`) | a case held now and not at the base whose `held.adr` section of this file does not name it, or already named it at the base; or the cap rose by more than the new held cases | this file and `cases.json` | name the case id in the ADR written for it; `held.adr` is that ADR; raise `HELD_CAP` by the count |
| `proof-lint.allowlist.json` | `--update` with a rise (refused without `--allow-rise`; with it the entry's `why` is reset to pending-review); in check mode, a hit text the base lacks under a stated `why` that did not change | the entry's `why` | read the hit, then restate the `why` (or leave pending-review) |
| `ir-read-lint.allowlist.json` | `--update` with a rise or a replaced site (refused without `--allow-rise`; with it the entry's pending-review list names it); in check mode, a site whose text the base lacks where the file and kind lost another | the entry's `pending-review` list | `node scripts/ir-read-lint.mjs --update --allow-rise`, then read it in the diff |

**No base is a failure** (`scripts/guard/base-revision.mjs`): `COUNT_BASE=<rev>` names the base explicitly (a ref git cannot resolve fails too); otherwise it is the merge base of HEAD with origin/main (while the flip runs, with origin/claude/flip-census), and none fails with the two ways to name one. A base without the file under comparison fails.

**CI.** A new `guards` job (full history, `fetch-depth: 0`; Bun and Node, no Cargo) runs `count`, `rises`, `regress`, `base`, `proof-lint` and `ir-read-lint`, which CI never ran (only `make verify` did). `proof-gate` and `repro-causes` run in `rust-engine` after `make coverage`, on the debug checker that job already built. `record-tested-tree` waits for `guards`.

**verify-delta.** The `fixtures/` row and the `fixtures/uncertifiable-repro/` row select `proof-gate` (it runs the checker over every fixture project). The witnesses read no fixture (`scripts/flip/witnesses.json` carries its programs), so they are not added. `scripts/uncertifiable-causes.mjs` and `scripts/fuzz/judge-frozen.json` select `guard-count`, which now also runs `regress.mjs` and `base.mjs`.

**verify-performance.** The first-IR corpus path is fixed at 93 characters whatever TMPDIR is (`corpusRootPrefix`: the mkdtemp name is padded with `-`; a temporary directory too long to pad throws). The checker's per-source cost grows with the path (ADR 0986, 0994) and the corpus path was `$TMPDIR`-dependent (93 on this Mac, 51 under Linux's /tmp); 93 keeps every number comparable with those ADRs.

**boundary-inventory.** `dialectQuestions` throws when the Dialect impl's `fn` count differs from the parsed questions or there is not exactly one impl; an arm whose role expression has any part that is not a role literal (or `Some(..)`) is `computed` and needs a pair. On main: 147 questions and 249 arms, identical before and after.

**Limits, stated.** Sites are paths: spans are byte offsets that move with any edit of a fixture, so a (fixture, key, path) is the finest site that holds for rows; spans are used only where a file is unchanged (`regress.mjs`). A fixture edit that moves proved violations in one file is compared by count there. A candidate re-keyed by a fixture edit is a new key and needs an ADR. `ir-read-lint` has no `why` to reset, so its record is the pending-review line. `fixtures/proof-log/gaps.json`, the witnesses and the obligation audit are not held against the base or run in CI here (docs/open-work.md).

## ADR 0997 — A deferred slot ends a `resolve`/`until` call only where the dialect states that no observer is active there
ADR 0985 ended a `resolve` or `until` call written in a callback its primitive runs elsewhere (`SlotRun::Deferred`) in the silence `static_api.resolve_scope.slot-runs-elsewhere`, on the premise that no observer is active there. `Deferred` is the attribution answer (whose reads the callback subscribes) and says nothing of the observer. Three slots it covers run under one: `resolve(fn)` and `until(fn)` hand `fn` to `watch(fn, …)` (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.21` `dist/dev.js:3588`, `:3741`), and `from(subscribe)` runs `subscribe` where its iterator is started, inside the computation that consumes it. Found by review of the batch (2026-11-15) and confirmed in Chrome rc.21: `resolve(() => { resolve(…) })`, `resolve(() => { until(…) })` and `until(() => { resolve(…) })` from a click handler, and `createMemo(() => from(set => { resolve(…) }))`, each throw the guard's error with no SC2004 or SC2005 row. The exit is older than ADR 0985 (`judged_by_primitive → false`); ADR 0985 named it a proof.

**Change.** `Dialect::deferred_slot_observer(primitive, argument) -> Option<bool>` states the observer of a deferred slot apart; the default states nothing. `Solid2`: `Some(true)` for `resolve` and `until` argument 0; `Some(false)` for an effect's apply, `onCleanup`, `onSettled`, `createReaction`, `onFlush`, `onHydrationEnd` and an action's step (what the silence already held; a `flush()` under a computation stays `callback_runs_drained_by_flush`'s); `None` for `from`, `lazy`, `lazyModule` and `clientOnly` (the loader runs where the component first renders, or where `preload()` or the returned read is called). `static_api::slot_answer` matches it: `Some(false)` is the silence, `None` the obligation the rule already has, and `Some(true)` a new `ScopeAnswer::OwnComputation`: an uncertifiable SC2004 or SC2005 that says an observer is active and the guard throws, blocker `computation-error-unobserved`. It is no violation: the throw rejects the promise the holder returned, Chrome reports it only when that rejection is unhandled, and no fact proves that here (`docs/open-work.md`). Where a slot that is silent and one that is a computation both hold the call directly, neither is proven (an obligation).

**Checked.** Fixture `resolve-until-own-computation`: seven obligations in a `resolve` or `until` callback (the import, an alias, the namespace member), two in `from`'s subscribe function, silences for an effect's apply, a memo's cleanup and an `untrack` written inside a `resolve` callback, and a shadowed local. Chrome rc.21 (`fixtures/runtime-oracle/resolve-own-computation`, `resolve-in-from-subscribe`): every obligation cell throws and is `covered-uncertifiable`; the silent cells raise neither code. Pattern lane `resolve/{r,u}21`–`24`: main has 6 false cleans of 8, this change 0 (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`; the grids have no context that is legal for the plain call and misuse for a nested one, so the lane holds the shape). The two `candidates.json` entries ADR 0987 added gain their `adr`.

## ADR 0998 — A value an unread package returned is read as possibly reactive on every route to its read inside project code
ADR 0981's rule 3 followed a read BACK to the call that made its value: through a call, a member, an operand, a plain binding of one name. A value that reached its read by another route had no row, and Chrome rc.21 warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED there all the same (review of the batch, 2026-11-15; `dep-router`'s `useLocation()`, not read as source): through an array literal and a pattern (`const [l] = [useLocation()]`), a binding assigned after it is declared, a slot of an object literal (`o.location.search`), a parameter of a project function (`show(useLocation())`), a copy a standard function makes (`Object.assign({}, { location })`), and an export read in another module (an imported binding was never followed). Five of eight probed routes were silent.

**Change.** The value-use census walks every such value FORWARD (`value_use::Census::package_value_start`, called by `package_action_calls/value_reads.rs` `flowed_rows`): the result of each call into a package the build does not read is walked as a value past an escape (ADR 0860), which follows a binding and its references, a pattern and its slots, an assignment, a literal's slot and the Gets of it, a return, a project function's parameter, a standard method's result and its callbacks, an export and its importers. Each call or Get through the value in project code is a site, asked the question rule 3 asks (a row where the role reports an untracked read or places nothing): an uncertifiable SC1001 `package-value-read:flowed`, unless rule 3's own row stands on the same span. A position inside the project the walk cannot follow is a row with that position's name (`value-in-class-field`, `value-through-generator`, `value-thrown`, `value-forwarded`, `value-use-unclassified`, the last also for a walk past its step budget). The package mode differs from ADR 0860's walk in four stated ways: a call through the value is a read, not a write of a root; a write through it is no site (the claim is the read's); a pattern's slots are walked on (a tuple's element may be such a value); a name in a type holds no value. Never a violation: nothing proves the value reactive.

**Not claimed (recorded in `docs/open-work.md`).** A value handed to code that is no function of the project: a package or an unresolved callee, a constructor, a component (a project component's `props.x` is the props rule's read), a Solid primitive, an `await`. The walk ends there with no row; a package's own result is a start of its own.

**Cost (owner's yes, 2026-11-15, over the 1,000-row guard).** rc.21 frozen corpus, 34 projects, release, ADR 0997's head against this change: development 212 V / 281,602 U to 212 V / 288,067 U (+6,465 rows, 6,408 of them on a span that held no SC1001 row: `flowed` 6,326, the open positions 82), standard 218 V / 260,219 U to 218 V / 267,475 U (+7,256 rows, 7,197 on a new span); 0 removed, no violation moved. (Corrected by ADR 0999's change: the first text gave the new-span counts as the row totals.) The routes inside the module that made the call are +2,426 of the development rows (app-game 1,610: three.js values); the rest are exports read in another module (inferay 1,792: design tokens; an API client). Win the rows back by reading the package as source, or by a fact that a value cannot hold an accessor (a primitive type: the producer's `primitive_value_domain`, not demanded for these spans today).

**Checked.** Fixture `dependency-value-flow` (the five routes, ADR 0981's direct read, two tracked twins, a project function of the same name). Chrome rc.21, `fixtures/runtime-oracle/package-value-flow`: the six untracked reads warn and are `covered-uncertifiable`, the twins are quiet. Pattern lane `pkgvalue/v01`–`v08` (a package that imports no Solid name and returns a getter over what the program hands it): main `3ae84a221` has 6 false cleans of 8 (the array pattern, the assigned binding, the object slot, the parameter, the copy, the other module), this change 0 (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`).

## ADR 0999 — A global a package writes is found whatever way its name or the route to the global object is spelled, and a call of it after an `await` is no library call
Three false cleans of the package-global work (ADRs 0974, 0976), each read by the review of the batch (2026-11-15) and confirmed in Chrome rc.21.

**1. An escaped identifier (project side, `package_action_calls.rs`).** A global's name was compared as source text, and `is_identifier_name` refused a backslash: `\u0062toa("x")` in a component body, where an installed package replaces `btoa` with a function that calls an action, had no SC2002 row (Chrome: ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE). `cooked_identifier` reads the name a spelling means (`\uXXXX`, `\u{…}`); a bare global, a static member of the global object, the global object's own names and `document` are compared by it. `is_identifier_name` accepts a Unicode letter.

**2. `x["defaultView"]` (package side, `module_reach.rs`).** ADR 0974 reads `defaultView` off any object as a route to the global object; the pass matched the static member only, so a package that writes `el.ownerDocument["defaultView"].btoa = …` was no writer of `btoa` and the project's call was silent. The pass reads a string-literal key, and a key the file's constants decide to be that one name, as the static member. A member of `document` read by a key the syntax does not fix (`document[k]`, `document[c ? "defaultView" : "body"]`) may be its `defaultView`: it is an escape of the global object, as `window[k]` handed on is (the package is then a writer under any name).

**3. A package-replaced global after an `await` (`after_await_accounting/library_call.rs`).** `library-runs-nothing` ended a call of a standard-library declaration after a suspension on the declaration alone. What runs is whatever holds the global: a package that replaces `structuredClone` and calls, from it, an accessor the program handed it earlier reads after the await (Chrome: UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT, the project frame is the call). `package_writes_global`: the reason does not hold when an installed package the program loads writes the global the call goes through (the callee's name, or a name of its member chain), or writes globals under a name nothing decides. Every writer counts, one whose closure names no Solid package too: it calls no action, but it may call a function of the project.

**Not fixed here (read only, no program run; `docs/open-work.md`).** A package closure with unread code (a computed `import(x)`, a file the parser refuses, the file limit) is no writer under any name; the after-await member-read list has no compound assignment or `await` operand (`in` and `for…in` were run: Chrome rc.21 is quiet); ADR 0975's flat literal is cleared without the `Object.prototype` question, and its pins leave `vitest/dist/index.js` and the manifests unpinned.

**Checked.** Fixtures `action-in-owned-scope-global-spellings` (the plain call, four escaped spellings and the computed-view writer are rows; an unwritten global and a shadowed local are silent) and `after-await-package-global` (the replaced global is a row; `JSON.stringify` and `Math.max` keep the reason). Unit tests `default_view_by_a_computed_key_is_the_global_object`, `only_an_identifier_names_a_global`. Chrome rc.21, `fixtures/runtime-oracle/package-global-escaped-name`, `package-global-defaultview`, `after-await-package-global`: each diagnostic `covered-uncertifiable`. Pattern lane `pkgglobal/g01`–`g05`: ADR 0998's head has 4 false cleans of 5 (the escaped name, the escaped member, the computed view, the replaced global after an await), this change 0 (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`). Corpus, rc.21 frozen, 34 projects, release, ADR 0998's head against this change: development +2 rows, standard +13, all SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` (a standard call after an await in a project that loads a package writing that global, or writing globals under a name nothing decides); 0 removed, no violation moved.

## ADR 1001 — The pull request's smoke runs as two jobs of one sample: `smoke` (every grid but the census) and `smoke-census`
The all-pairs cover is 67,086 programs (mx-census 38,448, mx-recall 19,060, lg-recall 5,534, mx-pairs 2,347, lg-pairs 1,072, the six base grids 625), and the job's Smoke step took 49.6 min on CI run 43688105588 (PR #252) behind a setup of 8.0 min; on two later runs the setup took 15 to 16 min (cache restore 7.4 to 7.7, build 6.5) and the 60-minute limit cancelled the step at 52 min. The cover cannot be cut without losing coverage (ADR 0996's measurement: 16,928 programs are required, and a per-code cap or the census's with-`code` rule loses 7,600 to 13,700 pairs); the owner ruled the job split, with the same cover. **Mechanics.** `focus.mjs --smoke-leg rest|census` runs the leg's grids (`SMOKE_LEGS` in `focus-grids.mjs`: `rest` every grid but `mx-census`, `census` that one) and `--cover-grids` (set by the leg, any list on its own) names the grids the cover is computed over: every grid, so both legs draw the one sample, the programs of a leg being the cover's, restricted to its grids; the same seed, required ids and families. `writeSample` prints `sha256 <16 hex>` of the sample's ids grid by grid: both legs print the same line, and a run without a leg prints it too. A run without `--smoke-leg` is the single job it was (`make fuzz-smoke`). **Workflow.** `fuzz-pr.yml`'s `smoke` job is a matrix of two legs named `smoke` and `smoke-census`; each has its own installs, cache restore, build and runtime cache (`fuzz-pr-runtime-<leg>-<sha>`, restoring its own, then any, so the first run reads the combined cache of the single job); `fail-fast: false`; the push to main records each leg's cache under its own key, so two jobs never write one key; the nightly and the manual per-code tier take the same legs (`rest` the per-code cover of its ten grids as before, `census` the whole census beside it). No rule of `focus.mjs` judges across both legs: attention, the moved-from-manifest check, the ledger's standing and the executor stop are per unit, and "the run judged no program" holds per leg. The checks required of a pull request do not change. **The size hook.** ADR 0996 made `scripts/fuzz/smoke/mx-census.json` 6 MB (the census's whole grid), over `.githooks/pre-commit`'s 5 MB limit, so merging main into a branch was refused there; the hook has an allowlist entry for exactly that file (the limit and every other file unchanged, and `--no-verify` unused). The hook is local (`make hooks` turns it on); nothing in CI or any script enforces the 5 MB limit, and no other tracked file is over it. **Cache size.** The repo's Actions caches stood at 10.9 GB of the 10 GB limit when this was decided, 5.1 GB of it the seven `fuzz-pr-runtime-<sha>` caches (about 800 MB each, one per push to main): two whole copies a push would have evicted the cargo and real-projects caches. So a push saves only what a leg used: a step sets `strictatime` on the runner's disk and touches a marker before the Smoke step, and after it deletes the files not accessed since (the entries the leg read or wrote; a leg that used fewer than 20,000 saves the cache whole, with a warning; a failed remount does the same). Rehearsed on an ext4 loop disk: the 783 MB combined cache (183,091 files) held 99,360 files, 423 MB, after the census leg, and that census run was warm on it again. A leg restores the combined cache until its own exists. **Measured predictions** (the per-grid rates of the run above): `smoke` 25.1 min, `smoke-census` 24.1 min of Smoke step, so 33 to 41 min a job with a setup of 8 to 16. The pull request that lands it reports the first run's setup and step minutes of both legs.

*ADR 1156 splits the `rest` leg again, into `smoke` and `smoke-2` (the cover divided by program id); `smoke-census` is as described here.*

<a id="adr-1000"></a>
## ADR 1000 — After an `await`, a write that reads its target first is a read of it; the vitest reading pins the file an import loads
ADR 0976 (S4) lists every member read after an async computation's suspension whose object is not proven plain. Its list (`after_await_accounting/member_reads.rs` `chains`) left every write target out. A compound assignment (`local.x += 1`), an update (`local.x++`) and a logical assignment (`local.x ||= 5`) Get the member before they Set it, and on a store alias Chrome rc.21 reports that Get as UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT; the checker had the store write's row (SC2003) and no SC1002. Read by the review of the batch (2026-11-15), then confirmed in Chrome (3 of 3 `unproven-clean`).

**Change 1: the read.** A write target whose assignment reads it first (`AssignmentFact::reads_target`: every compound and logical operator, and an update) stays in the list of reads. A plain `=`, a `delete` and an iteration target read nothing and stay out. The row is the one ADR 0976 gives a listed read: an uncertifiable SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted`, or nothing where a reason proves the object plain. An object literal the function made is no receiver ADR 0976 proves plain, so the same write on one gets the row its plain read already has (Chrome is quiet there).

**Not changed, checked.** `"k" in local` and `for (const k in local)` after an `await` are quiet in Chrome rc.21, and so is `await local`: none is listed.

**Change 2: the pins of ADR 0975.** The reading of vitest 4.1 pinned the files it read and found each by its path below the package. It did not pin what decides which file an import loads: `vitest/dist/index.js` (the entry, which names the chunk's `expect` and `vi`), `vitest/index.cjs` (the `require` entry, which only throws), and the manifest of each package the reading rests on (`vitest`, `@vitest/expect`, `@vitest/spy`, `@vitest/runner`, `@vitest/utils`, `chai`). A patch of the entry or of an `exports` map kept every digest, so the premise held over code nobody read. Each is now a pinned file: the two entries have one digest over 4.1.6, 4.1.7 and 4.1.11; each manifest has one digest per release, read in each (`type`, `main`, `module`, `exports`, `imports` and `browser` are the same in the three; the releases differ in the version and dependency fields). The digest kept for the process was keyed on a file's length and modification time; a package manager extracts every file with one fixed time, so a rewrite of the same length kept the old digest in a long-running process. The key adds the inode and its change time (`reviewed_packages::file_stamp`; the same for the answer `package_reach/prototype.rs` keeps), and where the platform gives no change time nothing is kept.

**The flat literal of ADR 0975, checked and kept.** vitest's deep equality reads members the literal inherits (`"asymmetricMatch" in b`, then `b.asymmetricMatch`), and a failing assertion on a primitive reads `Symbol.toStringTag` the same way: run in Node on the pinned bytes, an accessor on `Object.prototype` runs in both (a passing assertion on a primitive runs none). An accessor a file of the project defines there is not silent: the action it calls is a row at the accessor itself (`function-run-unplaced`). One a package defines is the named miss of ADR 0974 (a builtin prototype a package extends), for a literal as for a primitive. Asking `object_prototype_touched` here was built and measured: the fact holds on a real install (vitest 4.1.11 with the packages of the corpus project `probus-hk`: every literal kept its site), so the question would end the clearing wherever the premise holds.

**Checked.** Fixture `after-await-read-first-writes` (the three writes are rows, a plain assignment is none). Chrome rc.21, `fixtures/runtime-oracle/after-await-read-first-writes`: three UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT, each `covered-uncertifiable`. Pattern lane `net/aw-compound-store-alias`, `aw-update-store-alias`, `aw-logical-store-alias` and the legal twin `aw-compound-local-object`: 3 of 4 false clean on ADR 0999's head, 4 fine on this one (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`). The pins: `reviewed_packages` tests (the published bytes of `fixtures/reactive-ir/reviewed-vitest-4-1` hold the premise; a patched entry or manifest holds nothing; a rewrite of the same length and modification time is hashed again); the fixture's findings are unchanged. Corpus, rc.21 frozen, 34 projects, release, ADR 0999's head against this change: development 288,069 to 288,080 uncertifiable rows (+11), standard 267,488 to 267,499 (+11), violations 212 and 218 unchanged. The 11 are the same sites on both builds, each read: an SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` at a read-first write after an `await` on an object nothing proves plain (`this.pendingLoads -= 1`, `this.contextsClosed++`, `scratch.abr ??= …`, `acc.sessions += row.sessions`; `solid-groove` 5, `app-game` 5, `ai-memory-ui` 1). <a id="adr-1002"></a>
## ADR 1002 — Code of a package nobody read may write any global; a package value handed as a JSX attribute is followed to the reader the tag names
Two false cleans left open by the review of the batch (2026-11-15) and priced before they were built (the owner asked for the prices first).

**1. Unread code is a writer of any global.** ADR 0974 records the globals the files of a package's closure write, and a call of a standard-library global in an owned scope is a site where some loaded package may have replaced it. A closure with code the walk did not read (a load by a computed name, a load no installed file answers, a file the parser refuses, a native module, a manifest the walk does not read, files past the closure limit) was a writer only of what its read files wrote. A global written by the unread part had no writer: `btoa("x")` in a component body was silent beside a package whose entry is `await import(name)` and whose loaded file replaces `btoa` with a function that calls an action (Chrome rc.21 throws ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE). The walk now keeps whether it noted such a problem (`Walk::unread`, apart from the capped problem list), and such a closure writes any global and defines an accessor for any (`GlobalWrites::any_name`, `accessors_any_name`). `unknown-global`, `code-generation` and `global-object-escape` are not unread code and keep their own rules.

**2. A named JSX attribute is followed to its reader.** ADR 0998 walks a package's value forward and ended, with no row, at every hand-off out of the function that holds it, a component's prop included. Where the tag names the reader the walk can go on, with the machinery the value-use census already has (`Census::jsx_value`): a project component's reads of that prop (`props.view.search`, a pattern's slot), and each `useContext` of a context provider. Chrome rc.21 warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at the read in the child exactly as at a read beside the call. The row is ADR 0998's (`package-value-read:flowed`, or the position blocker where the child forwards its props: `value-forwarded`). A tag nobody resolved (a package's component, `<Dynamic>`, a `lazy` binding), a spread and a child are not followed and stay in `docs/open-work.md`.

**Checked.** Fixtures `action-in-owned-scope-unread-code` (three calls are rows, a local of the same name is silent) and `dependency-value-flow` (`ViaProp`, `ViaPropPattern`, `ViaContext` are rows; `ViaPropTracked` is none; `ViaCopy`'s `Object.assign` is now a site of part 1, since `dep-router`'s closure cannot be read). Chrome rc.21, `fixtures/runtime-oracle/package-value-flow`: three more STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED (the prop, the pattern, the context consumer), `unproven-clean` on ADR 1000's head and `covered-uncertifiable` here. Pattern lane: `pkgglobal/g06-computed-import`, `pkgvalue/v09-prop`, `v10-prop-pattern`, `v11-context` are 4 false cleans of 18 on ADR 1000's head and 18 fine here, with the legal twin `v12-prop-tracked` fine on both (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`). The runtime oracle pre-bundles a case's packages, which moves the file a computed name loads, so part 1 has no oracle case: the pattern lane is its Chrome run.

**The cost.** Corpus, rc.21 frozen, 34 projects, release, ADR 1000's head against this change. Part 1 alone: 0 rows on both builds (every program that loads a package with unread code already loads a writer of any global). Part 2: development 288,080 to 288,360 uncertifiable rows (+280 rows at 275 new sites), standard 267,499 to 267,817 (+318 rows at 313 new sites), violations 212 and 218 unchanged, all SC1001 `package-value-read` (`flowed` 224 and 270, `value-forwarded` 51 and 36, `value-use-unclassified` 0 and 7). Each row was read: a child's read or call of a prop that holds a package value (`props.audio.seekTicks(…)`, `props.onClose()`), a context consumer's read (`kui.api` after `useKui()`, `useContext(ClerkContext).clerk`), or a hand-off the child forwards (`class={cn(…)}` to a component that spreads its props). `kui` 144, `app-game` 44, `donegeon-client` 37 (standard only), `solid-groove` 33. Many hold a string in practice; the fact that would prove it (a primitive static type) is the one ADR 0998 names as the way to win its own rows back.

## ADR 1003 — A promise handler written another way than a literal or a name is followed to the functions it may be
ADR 0976 (S3) made a promise handler code written after a suspension, and listed as handlers a function literal and an identifier that exactly names a project function. A handler given as a member of a project object (`then(handlers.ok)`), a conditional (`then(c ? a : b)`), a parameter (`then(handler)` in a helper), a bound function (`then(f.bind(null))`) or a spread array (`then(...fns)`) was no handler, so the reads in the function it runs were not after a suspension and had no row. Chrome rc.21 raises UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT at each (suspected by the review of the batch, 2026-11-15; 4 of 4 `unproven-clean` in the probe).

**Change** (`after_await_accounting/handlers.rs`, `Resolver`). Each argument of a promise handler call is followed, to a depth of eight hops, to the functions it may be: both operands of a conditional or a logical expression, the tail of a sequence, the target of `f.bind(…)`, a `const` to its initializer, a function declaration of the file the binder resolves the name to where nothing assigns it (an operand of a conditional has no type fact), the value an object literal a `const` holds writes under the member's key, the elements of an array literal that is spread, and for a parameter the argument of each call the program names. Every function found is a handler. Where the walk cannot name every function, **the handler argument itself is a site that nothing ends** (`via: handler`, the uncertifiable SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted`): a parameter (a caller the program does not name may hand any function), a member (nothing proves the object kept the function it was written with), a call's result, an import of a package. Two forms are no function and no site: a nullish or primitive literal (`then(undefined, onError)`), and a parameter of the executor of a standard `new Promise(…)` (the library's own `resolve` and `reject`).

**Checked.** Fixture `after-await-handler-forms` (rows at the read in each function a member, a conditional, a parameter, a bound function and a spread may be, and at the argument for a member, a parameter and a call's result; none for the executor's `resolve` and a nullish literal). Chrome rc.21, `fixtures/runtime-oracle/after-await-handler-forms`: five UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT, `unproven-clean` on ADR 1002's head and `covered-uncertifiable` here; `after-await-then-handler` is unchanged. Pattern lane `net/th-bound`, `th-conditional`, `th-parameter`, `th-spread`: 4 false cleans of 6 on ADR 1002's head, 6 fine here (`th-member` is covered on both by the row of the arrow's own read; the legal twin `th-executor-resolve` is fine on both; `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`). Corpus, rc.21 frozen, 34 projects, release, ADR 1002's head against this change: development 288,360 to 288,380 uncertifiable rows (+20), standard 267,817 to 267,837 (+20), violations 212 and 218 unchanged; the same 20 sites on both builds, each read: a hand-off of a prop or a parameter as a handler (`.catch(props.onError)` seven times in `app-game`, `lock.then(work, work)`), and the reads and calls in a function now known to be a handler (`probus-hk` `autoSync.ts`).

## ADR 1004 — A site after an await written directly in a callback a reviewed test runner schedules is on no flight (`runner-scheduled`)
SC1002's universe (ADR 0973) lists every read, and every call that may run a project function, written after an async function's own suspension, and ends each one in a row, an SC9012, the discard or a typed reason. The role silences were left out on purpose (owner ruling, decision 5: "each needs a premise and a Chrome twin of its own"), so a test file's sites kept `read-after-await-unaccounted`: 34,781 rows of that blocker on the development corpus (main 5a627070c), 25,052 of them in test files.

*The proof.* Solid 2.0.0-rc.21 raises UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT only for a read with an async computation's tail-flight frame on its V8 async stack (`@solidjs/signals` `dist/dev-shared.js`, `attributedFlight`: `Error.captureStackTrace` at a limit of 50 frames, the first frame whose function name is a tail frame's; no frame, no diagnostic). ADR 0438 read the runners' published bytes: a registered test or hook, and a suite body of a runner that defers it, is called from the runner's own loop with no Solid API on the stack, and "a registered `async` callback is wholly in the premise", its prefix and every resumption. The async stack of a continuation of such a callback is the callback and the runner's awaiting frames: no flight is on it, whatever the callback reads or calls synchronously from there. So a site written directly in the callback ends: `AfterAwaitSafe::RunnerScheduled` (`after_await_accounting.rs`, id `after_await_accounting.account.runner-scheduled`).

*The facts asked* (a missing one is no reason, and the site keeps its row):
- the registration call resolves, through its root identifier's alias chain, to declarations that all lie in a reviewed runner's installed declaration files and are named for a registration function (`SemanticLookup::test_runner_callback`, ADR 0438: never a spelling, so a project `it`, a shadowed one and a wrapper are not the runner; an import alias and a re-export are);
- the runner **schedules** the callback (`TestRunnerCallback::Scheduled`): a test, a hook, a suite body of vitest. A suite body a runner runs inside the registration call (jest-circus, mocha, `node:test`, playwright: `InlineSuiteBody`) runs on the stack of that call, which may be a computation's, and is not covered;
- the runner is one whose published JavaScript was read (`SemanticLookup::test_runner_schedules_by_read_bytes`): `bun:test` is native, ADR 0438 cites no bytes for how it calls a test, and this reason does not take it (narrower than `FlushSafe::TestRunner`, which is unchanged);
- the function around the site is the literal written directly as the registration's argument, and the flush accounting's questions for the same class hold of the site and of each of its alternate spans (`flush_accounting::runs_when_the_call_runs`, the reviews of #213): the site is in the literal's body (no parameter default), no class field, JSX expression or compiler tracked region written inside the registration holds it, the literal is no generator, and its own name (a named function expression) is used nowhere, since code that names it can hand it to a computation.

*Not covered, each keeping its row:* a helper the tests call (ADR 0438's test-only helper census is the next step, not built), a callback handed by name or through a wrapper, a function written inside the callback (a promise handler, a nested async arrow: its own function, and an async computation written there is the walk's violation as before), and the accessor read, setter or call another producer already rows (`function-run-unplaced`, an SC9012: the reason ends only a site no row stands at).

*Evidence.* (1) Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/after-await-runner-callback`: async callbacks a loop of the project's own records and later awaits one by one (as vitest's `runTest` awaits `fn()`) read after their awaits, directly and through a called function, and Chrome is silent at each; the same shape awaited by an async memo's compute raises the code at the read (`covered-violation`, the only diagnostic of the case). (2) The real runner on V8, `scripts/probes/rc21-runner-callback-after-await` (vitest 5.0.5, Node 26.13.0, `@solidjs/signals` 2.0.0-rc.21's dev build, diagnostics collected from the console; `diagnostics.recorded.json`): a read, a call of a function that reads and `expect(count())` after an await in `beforeEach`, in a `describe` body, in `it(…)` and in `it.each(…)(…)` are silent; the control (the same body awaited by an async memo written in a test) and a named test callback handed by its own name to `createMemo` each raise UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT, the second on the computation's run only. The corpus has no runtime, and the fuzz harness runs its programs in Chrome with no runner, so no grid cell can hold the shape (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`, an `outside` entry).

*Measured* (rc.21 frozen corpus, 34 projects, release, main 5a627070c against this change): standard build 269,143 to 246,843 uncertifiable rows (**-22,300**), development build 289,573 to 267,623 (**-21,950**, 7.6% of its rows; the blocker's own rows 34,781 to 12,831). Every moved row is a removed SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` row: 0 added, violations 218 and 212 unchanged, no project's status moved, no row of another rule or blocker moved. Development build by project: kui 8,858, solid-groove 8,253, dashiboard-ui 2,703, jandibat-web 809, ai-memory-ui 489, skyjtx-website 278, jar-hell-web 227, every-deck-of-cards 193, hoxxes-briefing 82, expenses-app 58; 221 files, each a file that registers with a reviewed runner (`*.test.*`, `*.spec.ts`; outside those names: `solid-groove/src/persistence/projectRepositoryContract.ts`, a vitest contract suite, 388; `expenses-app/tests/browser/ui.e2e.ts` 58 and `solid-groove/tests/e2e/emulator/warmDevServer.setup.ts` 8, playwright). The rows of `bun:test` callbacks stay (compass-ui 1,556, expenses-app 116, inferay 95 on the development build: what taking the native runner on ADR 0438's word would add). Fixture snapshots: 8 rows removed in four existing fixtures (`test-runner-vitest/variants/async-dispatch` 2, `async-role` 3, `helper-test-only` 2 of 3, `test-runner-vitest4` 1: `dispatchEvent`, `count()`, `settle()`, `choose()` after an await directly in an `it` callback), each a `drops` row of `scripts/guard/counts.json`; no violation moved (`scripts/guard/regress.mjs`: 0). *Re-measured on the merge with main 78ddeb849 (ADRs 1000, 1002 and 1003):* standard 269,497 to 247,197 (-22,300), development 289,889 to 267,939 (-21,950): the same rows, 0 added, violations 218 and 212 unchanged, no status moved. ADR 1003's `handler` site (a promise handler handed as an argument, which a later job runs) is not taken by the reason, as a handler written as a function literal is not.

*Residual, inherited from ADR 0438 and named there:* a runner configured to wrap tests in a Solid root or component, a patched runner, a `node:test` test registered after its build phase (it may run inside the call), and project code that drives a runner's own loop from inside a computation. Fixtures: `after-await-runner-callback` (the ended sites, the hook, vitest's suite body, a modifier, a curried registration, an alias and a re-export; kept: a wrapper, a binding, a shadowed `it`, a named callback that hands itself on, nested functions, a helper), `test-runner-node/variants/after-await` (a scheduled test ends, the inline suite body keeps its row), `test-runner-bun/variants/after-await` (kept).

## ADR 1013 — A timer's callback behind a `const` is the function the `const` names: the slots of a primitive are not withdrawn for it
ADR 0803 withdraws a primitive's array-pattern slots when the global object may reach code the build does not see, and a timer calls a function callback with the window as `this` (review D3), so `setTimeout(f, 0)` is cleared only where `f` is a function the census can name and that function is an arrow or never mentions `this` (`mutation_sites.rs` `received_by_seen_code`, `Slot::TimerCallback`, `callback_seen`). `callback_seen` named a literal, a name that holds one, a conditional's arms, a call's result and a parameter by its entering call, but not a `const` initialized with another name: `const cb1 = cb2; setTimeout(cb1, 0)` (`cb2` an arrow) was "any function", the slots of every primitive of the program were withdrawn, and a store write or a setter call there fell from a violation to `tuple-iteration-written`. The fuzz grids hold the shape (`…-timer-…-cb-alias`): 924 programs of STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER's `timer` context moved from agree to recall-gap between the audits of aa4702650 and 6e33e0b08, at the merge that brought ADR 0803's step 2 (281ae31d3). Nothing in such a program hands the global object on: the alias is the arrow.

*The change.* A `const` identifier binding initialized with a value that is neither a function literal nor a call holds exactly that value, so `callback_seen` asks the question of the initializer too (one level of its depth budget), and takes only a yes from it: an initializer the walk cannot answer leaves the name to the lookup that answered before. A `let`, a pattern and a binding with no initializer are not followed. No other slot rule changes; the test each caller hands `callback_seen` (an arrow, or no mention of a receiver) is asked of the function found.

*Measured.* Grid differential, checker alone, main 87b324e2f against this change: of the 2,195,028 programs the grids generate, the 37,694 whose text holds a `const x = y;` alias and a platform callback caller ran under both builds: 36,119 identical, 1,575 moved, and no move is anything but uncertifiable to violation, uncertifiable to clean, or one uncertifiable row for another at the same line (0 violation lost, 0 violation or uncertifiable row at a line that had none). Uncertifiable to violation: 462 programs, all misuse, all STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER `timer` `-cb-alias` (mx-pairs 330, mx-recall 132): the lost ones. The legal grids (lg-pairs 495 and lg-recall 198 moved programs of REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE and STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER) only lose uncertifiable rows. The fuzz harness on every moved program with each compared in real Chrome (`focus.mjs --runtime-diff all`, ids per grid): mx-pairs 630 agree, mx-recall 252 agree, lg-pairs 431 uncertifiable and 64 clean, lg-recall 192 clean and 6 uncertifiable; 1,575 compared with the oracle, 0 behaviour, 0 attribution, 0 inconclusive, nothing needs a look. *Left open:* the other half of the lost ids, the 462 `-cb-bundle` programs (`setTimeout(cb1.cb, 0)`, the callback a member of a `const` object), stays uncertifiable: naming a member needs the exact-member facts and is its own change. Corpus (rc.21 frozen, 34 projects, release, against main 87b324e2f): standard 247,197 and development 267,939 uncertifiable rows on both sides, 0 rows moved, violations 218 and 212 unchanged (no project holds the shape). Chrome rc.21, oracle case `iteration-timer-callback-alias`: REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at a setter call in a component body and STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER at a store write run from a timer handed the alias both fire, each `covered-violation` (they were uncertifiable before). Fixtures (`iteration-written-slots/variants`): `handed-timer-callback-alias` is proved SC2001; `handed-timer-callback-alias-this` (the aliased function reads its `this`) and `handed-timer-callback-alias-let` (the alias names a `let` two writes may fill) stay uncertifiable. Found by the bisect of the violations lost between the two audits (`scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`).
<a id="adr-1008"></a>
## ADR 1008 — A plain throw that leaves an `async` function is a rejection: it reports only where the promise is dropped, awaited or returned to a call that drops it
*A false positive on main (78ddeb849 and 87b324e2f), found while Chrome-checking another change.* `<p ref={() => { (async () => { await Promise.resolve(); useContext(Ctx); })().catch(() => {}); }}>` was an SC4001 violation. Chrome rc.21 reports nothing: `useContext` with no owner is a plain `throw` (ADR 0893), and inside an `async` function a throw, before the first `await` or after it, rejects the promise the call returned; `.catch` takes it. ADR 0893's walk (`stored_throw.rs`) left an `async` function as if its throw propagated on the caller's stack; only `Thrower::UnderObserver` asked about a suspension, and that question is another one (whether an observer is still active). Every rule the walk serves had it: SC4001 and SC4002 (`useContext`), SC2004 and SC2005 (`resolve`, `until`), the static `dynamic` source, SC3001's `flush` in a tracked effect.

*Decision.* Where the walk leaves an `async` function through a call, the throw is a rejection of that call's promise (`Walk::rejection`), and what it does is read off the call:
- **rethrown**: the call is awaited (`await f()`): the rejection is thrown again where the `await` is written, and the walk goes on from the call as before (a `try` around it, the function around it, which is `async` in turn);
- **returned**: the call is a `return`'s argument or an arrow's expression body: the function around it returns the promise, so its own calls are read the same way (`Walk::returned`); a compute of a primitive that takes a promise (an async memo) stores the rejection as it stores a throw, which is the walk's existing answer for a tracked compute;
- **unhandled**: nothing holds the promise or a chain on it (`promise_chain_unheld`, the reading ADR 0893 already has for `then`: an expression statement or `void`, each later link a `then` with no rejection arm or a `finally`): the host reports the rejection, and the walk goes on from the call as before (a violation still needs the walk above to report, so this is never wider than it was);
- **kept**: anything else (assigned, passed on, given a handler, an element of what a standard call returns such as `map`'s array): `computation-error-unobserved`.
The same reading holds for the function's direct call and its literal called in place, a `const` alias's call, a holder's call of the parameter or prop that is the function, a standard carrier that runs it inline (`forEach` drops what the callback returns, `map` returns it), a primitive that runs an `async` callback inline and returns its value (`untrack`), and each layer the in-place climb crossed (`Walk::layers_rejection`: an `async` layer, a layer that returns such a promise, an `async` project helper that calls its callback; an `async` callback a project helper calls is not read and keeps the row). A handler, a `ref` and a scheduler's callback are unchanged: the host drops what they return.

*The review of 199456520 (three false positives left, one false clean made), fixed in the same change.* (F1) `await f().catch(…)` and `await f().then(ok, err)` read as rethrown, because the test was the text before the call: it is the `await` fact whose operand is the call itself, through parentheses (`awaited`); anything else is read by the chain. (F2) A leaf operation anchored at the helper call it is reached through (SC2004, SC2005 and SC3001's `flush` in a tracked effect, "reached through `run()`") started the walk at that call as a throw: `const run = async () => { resolve(…) }; createTrackedEffect(() => { run().catch(() => {}) })` stayed a violation. The leaf walk already knows whether it entered an `async` function on the way (`entered_async`); the operation now carries it (`LeafOwnerOperation::through_async`, in no report), and such an operation is followed only where the promise is the anchored call's own (`rejection_unobserved`: the callee is one `async` project function or its literal, every place the operation is written lies in it, no other `async` function is around any of them); an `async` function deeper in the chain is an obligation. (F3) A named `async` function handed to a primitive that runs it inline (`untrack(run).catch(…)`, and through a `const` alias) was read as a throw, because only a literal callback was asked whether it is `async`: the walk passes what it knows of the function whose entries it reads. (F4) A promise returned to a handler or a `ref` (`onClick={() => boom()}`) had become an obligation though Chrome reports it: the host drops what they return, so a returned promise there is unhandled and the walk goes on as for a throw. The message's tail names the promise ("taken by a `try`, an error boundary or a promise that holds it").

*The re-check of 0c0733bb5 (one false clean made by F2, one false positive of main in the same reading), fixed in the same change.* (1) F2 read the leaf walk's `entered_async`, which is sticky for a whole walk: a synchronous helper that also calls an `async` function (`const run = () => { flush(); void load(); }`) had every operation it reached marked as a rejection, the anchored callee was not `async`, and SC3001 or SC2004 at `run()` became an obligation though the throw is on the tracked effect's stack and Chrome reports it. The walk now knows the path to each operation: `async_depth` counts the `async` functions it is inside of, an operation written with none on the way is listed (`sync_sites`), and an anchored row is a rejection only where no reach of its sites was synchronous. A body read inside an `async` function and the same body read with none on the way are two entries of the walk (`Visited`), so the order of the calls decides nothing. It is not a lexical test: a synchronous function an `async` helper calls is reached inside that helper, and `const inner = () => { resolve(…) }; const run = async () => { inner() }; … run().catch(…)` stays an obligation. (2) `promise_chain_unheld` (ADR 0893) took `.then(...arms)` for a `then` with no rejection arm, since a spread is one argument: a violation on main where Chrome is silent. A `then` with a spread argument holds the promise.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/stored-throw-async-rejection` and the two probes it was built from: the fixture's 45 components with the probes it was built from, every violation the fix keeps fires its code at its site (NO_OWNER_CONTEXT; RESOLVE_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE for the helper a tracked effect calls and drops) (discarded, `void`, named and called, before the first `await`, `then` with no rejection arm, awaited in a discarded `async` function, `forEach`, `untrack` discarded, a module function one entry of which drops the promise) and every row it makes uncertifiable is silent (caught, `then` with a rejection arm, held, returned and caught, awaited in a caught function, a synchronous inner function, `untrack` caught or held, `Promise.all(xs.map(…)).catch`, the same in an effect's and a memo's compute, an `await` of a `catch` or a two-armed `then`, `untrack` of a named function or its alias, a helper's or a literal's `resolve`, `until` and `flush` whose promise a tracked effect catches, an `async` helper one call deeper). On main 26 of the fixture's rows were violations Chrome does not report. The pattern lane holds the shapes one a program (`scripts/fuzz/patterns/asyncthrow`, 45 programs): main 87b324e2f fails 25 of them as false positives, this change passes 45 of 45. The recall grid has the re-check's pair as a context of FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK, `tracked-sibling-async` (411 lean programs): on 0c0733bb5 all 411 are recall gaps, here 90 agree and 321 are the recall gaps main has too (the 411 answer as main's do).

*Measured* (release, main 87b324e2f against this change). Grids: every program of the six plain-throw codes (114,583 misuse, 76,251 legal) and the stratified samples of the other codes (32,331 recall-gap and 18,243 legal programs), 237,272 programs, each under both builds: **0 programs moved**. The first form of the fix, which kept a returned promise, moved six (`aw-inplace-await`, `aw-inplace-return`: an `async` function a helper returns into a memo's compute, read by an effect): four of them are violations Chrome confirms, so a returned promise is followed instead. Corpus (rc.21 frozen, 34 projects): standard build 218 violations and 246,346 uncertifiable rows, development build 212 and 267,239, **0 rows moved** in either. So the defect was reachable only by shapes neither the grids nor the corpus hold: the fuzzer gives no cell to a promise that swallows a throw (`PROMISE_SWALLOWS`, the note at `ASYNC_FAMILY_PLACEMENT`: its silence is no measure of a legal program), which is why it never drew one.

*Not covered* (docs/open-work.md): a kept promise whose rejection ends unhandled all the same (`const p = run(); await p;`, `Promise.all` with no handler) is an obligation, never a violation. Fixtures: `stored-throw-async-rejection` (14 violations; the obligations are `computation-error-unobserved` rows of SC4001, SC2004, SC2005 and SC3001), oracle case of the same name. Owners: `stored_throw.rs` (`Rejection`, `Walk::call_end`, `layers_rejection`).

<a id="adr-1006"></a>
## ADR 1006 — A function the render runs in place reports where its element does: the functions an intrinsic `ref` applies, and a control-flow tag's function child
ADR 0893 (commit b0b6d3d66, in #173) made a plain throw (`useContext` with no owner or no provider, a static `dynamic` source, `resolve`, `until`, `flush` in a tracked effect) a violation only where one run's throw reaches a report, and its walk knew one function the render runs in place: the literal written as an intrinsic `ref`. Every other one fell to `computation-error-unobserved`, though the owner pass already places them exactly: the 11-05 full audit had 2,480 programs of the recall grid's `ref-array`, `ref-cond`, `ref-factory` and `ref-row` contexts as proved NO_OWNER_CONTEXT violations, and on main all 2,964 programs of those four contexts are recall gaps (Chrome reports the code, the user sees nothing).

*Decision.* `host_runs` (`stored_throw.rs`) gains `render_runs`: the function held at the position the walk reached is one the render runs in place, so its throw ends where its element's does (the walk's own answer for that position: a boundary above it, a compute around it, the component's mounts).
- **An intrinsic `ref`'s applied functions**, by the owner pass's exact fact (`ref_application_of`, split out of `ref_applied_element`, ADRs 0345 and 0469): a value the attribute's expression yields, an array literal's element, a conditional's branch, an operand of `||` or `??`, a sequence's tail, a bare identifier of a function never rebound, or the literal that the exact, same-file, never rebound, non-async, non-generator callee of a yielded call returns (`ref={directive()}`). rc.21 applies each synchronously while the element is created. A component's `ref` is a prop and is not one.
- **A control-flow tag's function child** (`control_flow_parent`, ADRs 0883 and 0937: the tag's exact dialect primitive, the element's only child): `For` and `Repeat` at any arity, `Show` and `Match` in `Switch` with a parameter. The tag runs it under an owner of its own inside its compute, which **stores** what the child throws: only a render that reads the tag's result reports it. So the tag must be written in place in the JSX its function returns (`written_in_returned_jsx`): the element is the `return`'s argument or the arrow's expression body, or a direct child element of one that is, through intrinsic elements and the tags that render their children in place (ADR 0937's list: `For`, `Index`, `Repeat`, `Show`, `Switch`, `Match`, `Loading`, `Errored`, a context provider). A tag held in a binding, written in a child expression or an attribute, in a fragment, or a child of a project component keeps its row (the review of the first form: `const rows = <For …>…</For>` never inserted was a violation and Chrome is silent; the same for `Show`).
Nothing else is read as run: a factory reached through a member or an import, a rebound name, a project component's function child and a `Show` child with no parameter (which `tsc` rejects against the published typings) keep their rows. An `async` function among them is read by ADR 1008.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/stored-throw-render-run`: each of the 8 violations fires its code at the site (NO_OWNER_CONTEXT for the array element, the branch, the factory result, a `ref` in a `For`, `Repeat` and `Show` child, and an `async` row; CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND for a default-less read in a row's body), and the obligations are silent: the same shapes under an `Errored` with a handling fallback, a caught `async` function in an array element and in a row, a rebound name, a project component's child. A member factory (`ref={maker.make()}`) fires and stays an obligation (docs/open-work.md).

*Measured* (release, main 581bd7b18 against this change; #265 after it changes no checker code). Grids, each program under both builds: every program of the six plain-throw codes (114,583 misuse, 76,251 legal) and the stratified samples of the other codes (32,331 recall-gap, 18,243 legal), 237,272 programs. **2,579 programs moved, every one an uncertifiable `computation-error-unobserved` row at Chrome's site that became a violation, in a misuse program; no legal program moved, no violation left, nothing clean changed.** NO_OWNER_CONTEXT 2,541 (`ref-array`, `ref-cond`, `ref-factory`, `ref-row` 612 each, `flw-flow-for-async` 92, `barm-climb-await` 1: 2,448 of the four contexts' 2,964 recall gaps; the 516 left are the `portal` and `dynamic` mounts, ADR 0893's value mounts), DYNAMIC_STATIC_PROMISE 19 and CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND 13 (the census's `flow-*` rows and `barm-climb-*`), and 6 CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND programs that gain an SC4001 violation where the cell's own code did not fire: Chrome fires NO_OWNER_CONTEXT at each (the six run as oracle cases, `covered-violation`). Of the 2,480 programs of the four contexts that were proved violations in the 11-05 full audit, 2,288 are again. Chrome's record for the 2,573 others is the audit's own (run 43739577046: `recall-gap` is a code Chrome reported at the site). Corpus (rc.21 frozen, 34 projects): standard build 218 violations and 246,346 uncertifiable rows, development build 212 and 267,239, **0 rows moved** in either.

A row is read as main reads it: it may run (`each` may be empty, `count` zero), as a tracked child expression in a row already is on main; whether a row that provably never runs should report is left open (docs/open-work.md). Fixtures: `stored-throw-render-run` (8 violations, the obligations and the silent twins above, the tags not written in returned JSX), oracle case of the same name; pattern lane `scripts/fuzz/patterns/renderrun` (6 programs: the reviewed form fails 2 as false positives, this passes 6). Owners: `stored_throw.rs` (`render_runs`), `owners/owner_context.rs` (`ref_application_of`).
