## ADR 1012 — A proved fuzz verdict, or a proved corpus violation, cannot be lost without naming it: the smoke's ledger, the audit's baseline, the known items and the corpus guard
**The hole.** A fuzz program that was `agree` (a misuse program whose violation matched Chrome) and is `recall-gap` after a change, or `clean` (a legal program) and is `uncertifiable`, failed nowhere. `focus.mjs` reads recall-gap and uncertifiable as outcomes like the others and `movedVerdicts` ranks them no worse than attention; the audit printed what moved (1,791,685 ids against the last report, none a failure) and compared with the latest earlier report, green or not; its needs-a-look list had held 872 recorded items for days (7 of the 9 nightly audits were red), so a new line could not stand out; #234 lost 24 proved violations nobody saw. The corpus was measured by whoever wrote the ADR. No judge, limit or gate changed here; the ledgers and lists below are new files.
**1. The smoke's ledger** (`scripts/fuzz/proved/<grid>.json`: the sorted ids whose outcome is `agree` on a misuse grid and `clean` on a legal one in the smoke cover on main; 12,636 ids in the eleven grids, 0.9 MB: mx-census 7,041, mx-recall 3,016, mx-pairs 1,609, lg-recall 702, lg-pairs 82, mx-src 90, mx-base 36, mx-combo 36, lg-src 19, lg-base 3, lg-combo 2). `proved.mjs record --from <smoke dir>` adds ids and never removes one. Every ledger program is in the pull request's cover (`cover.mjs sample` adds them after the greedy pass, so the cover does not depend on the ledger: a ledger drawn from a cover adds nothing), and the per-unit loop of `focus.mjs` (both legs) fails on a ledger program that is another outcome, or has no row (the grid no longer generates it), unless a row of `scripts/fuzz/proved/changes.json` names its id: `{ grid, ids, adr, why }`. A move into proof is printed (`newly proved`) and allowed. `scripts/guard/proved.mjs` (CI `guards`, `verify-delta`) holds the files against the base: `changes.json` only grows (a row of the base gone or edited fails; a new row needs an ADR in docs/decisions.md, a why, and ids the ledger holds), and a ledger never loses an id; a ledger file names its own grid and lists its ids sorted and distinct (the reader and the guard both refuse another). Proof, in the VM with the release build: the cover runs clean ("nothing needs a look"); 24 census ids the ledger holds as proved, made recall-gap, fail the smoke (exit 1, 24 lost, 0 named); naming 23 still fails (1 unnamed); naming all 24 passes. The two census `stacked-claim` ids the audit listed (`mx-sync-node-received-async-apply-void-call-{row,untrack}-memo-direct-none`, the same pair as their `-effect-` twins) were added to `scripts/fuzz/open-defects-rows.json` (as R-stacked rows) and its exact ratchet in `open-defects.json` moved with them: on main 581bd7b18, `stackedClaim` 151 to 153, `PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK|sync-computation-received-async` 44 to 46, `causes.R-stacked` 151 to 153. That moves the cover's hash `21c707fd29e16c3b` to `887f3333dc708f91`, 67,086 programs both.
**2. The audit.** `audit.mjs report --proved <dir>` holds a run to the PROVED LEDGER of the last audit on main that lost nothing unnamed (artifact `audit-proved-<mode>`: `id<TAB>code` lines per grid, gzipped; the full audit at 78ddeb849 proved 1,194,842 of its 3,257,929 programs, about 12 MB). A ledger program that is not proved now is a loss, grouped by (grid, code, to) and named by group rows of the same `changes.json`: `{ grid, code, from, to, count, adr, why }`; a row names its losses once (the digest of every row an accepted audit used is kept beside the ledger), and the new ledger is written only when every loss was named, so a red audit never hands its losses on (a main run uploads it; branch runs read main's). The first ledger is written by a manual run on main with `proved-bootstrap`; until then the audit says "no proved ledger". A bootstrap spends every row of `changes.json` that exists (their digests start `consumed`), and the workflow refuses it when an `audit-proved-<mode>` artifact of the mode ever existed: it asks the artifact API by NAME over the repository (`total_count`, expired ones included), not a window of runs. A ledger the workflow found and the run cannot read fails the run (`--proved-expected`): the download is not `continue-on-error`, and "could not read" never reads as "no ledger". An oracle program that comes back inconclusive runs once more inside its oracle job, its results ride the oracle artifact (`oracle/<grid>/rerun/*`), and only the residue counts.
**3. The known items** (`scripts/fuzz/audit-known.json`: a NEW id-exact allowlist, 110 KB, applied by `applyKnown`). An entry stores the exact ids it holds by recall mode (`ids: { lean, full }`, sorted, distinct) and a regex naming its grid, kind and ids. A reported id the entry stores leaves the needs-a-look list; one it does not store is attention (a new item, or a swap for a fixed one, which a count would have hidden); a stored id no longer reported is attention too (a fix is news); a `cap` entry accepts any subset of its ids and nothing else. `scripts/guard/proved.mjs` holds the file against the base: removing ids is the only change without an ADR, and a new entry, an added id, or a changed `idRegex` or `cap` needs a new ADR the base's entry did not name. Applied to the real reports, the full audit at 78ddeb849 goes from 872 items to 3 and the lean one at 356c97405 from 461 to 2; with the two stacked rows the full one holds 1: `oracle differs mx-flush-in-action-flw-action-slot-x-destructured-none-m-portal` (`happy-only FLUSH_IN_ACTION@9`), left in attention. The entries (ids, lean and full): `unplaced` `pk-lazy` (163 and 326; a throw in a lazily loaded package gives Chrome no App frame; brief 09, the package half), `unplaced` package-call shapes in deferred store-write contexts (144 and 288; the cause is not measured, its own item and open-work line), `halted-claim` `flw-flow-for-async` (58 and 98: the 58 are the same programs the audit at 63725c6bf held; the other 40 are in the full recall grid only, which generates more mounts of the same family than the lean one), and the oracle's page timeouts (census 66, the same 66 ids in the lean and the full audit, deterministic; mx-recall 28 and 91, caps: any subset of those ids, to come down with the rerun's residue).
**4. The corpus** (`scripts/guard/corpus.mjs`, `make corpus-guard`): a release sweep of the frozen corpus in both runtime builds against `scripts/guard/corpus/<fingerprint>.json.gz`. A violation of the baseline (project, file, rule id, byte span) that is not a violation now fails (`became-uncertifiable` or `gone`), and so does a (project, file, rule) that held no uncertifiable row and holds one, unless a NEW row of `scripts/guard/corpus-changes.json` (held append-only against the base by the same guard) names it: `{ project, rule, kind, build, count, adr, why }`. The baseline names where it was built (platform, architecture and a hash of every app's installed packages: findings differ with the install, ADR 0974) and the checker's git trees (`rust/`, `apps/solid-typefacts`) at main's tip plus the blobs of the corpus manifest and the sweep script; the check REFUSES (exit 2, not a pass) a baseline built elsewhere or older than the merge base's checker, and `record` writes one only from a tree whose checker is the merge base's, with a release checker and Type Facts producer not older than their sources (the build id is the constant `dev`, so the binary's age is what there is to compare). Measured on the VM (linux-arm64, 16 cores, 8 jobs): the baseline has 212 violations and 22,250 (project, file, rule) places a build, 4.36 MB as JSON and 273 KB gzipped; recording took 603 s for both builds, and the check of the same tree 398 s with 0 moves in both builds (the sweep is deterministic). That is too slow and too machine-bound for `make verify` (a baseline per machine), so it is a required step of verify-handoff for an engine change. This PR commits the VM's baseline (`linux-arm64-bf64ce6e4f90`); another machine, the Mac that runs `make verify` included, records its own once from a main checkout.
**The cover moves with main's required ids.** The hash the ADR names (`887f3333dc708f91`, 67,086 programs) is of the main it was drawn on: the greedy cover changes with any change of the required ids (a ledger row, a rediscovery id), and main 19235225b, one required id on, gives a greedy cover of 67,087 programs. The ledger's programs are added after the greedy pass, so a proved program stays in the cover whatever the greedy does, and the ones the new greedy dropped are added back: 67,514 programs (+427, about 20 s of CI) and the hash `1c2f161991d270e5` on that main. The growth is bounded by the ledger (12,636 ids) and is the price of "a proved program is always run"; when the ledger holds a large share of what the greedy would not pick (the cover over about 70,000), the ledger is reselected. That is an owner decision, not a tool: `scripts/guard/proved.mjs` refuses a ledger that loses an id, so dropping ids needs the guard changed with an ADR.
**Limits, stated.** The smoke holds the proved programs of the cover; the audit holds every program of the audit's grids. A row of the smoke's `changes.json` names an id for good, so an id proved again and lost again later passes under the old row (an audit group row is spent once). The corpus guard sees sites as (project, file, rule): an uncertifiable row that appears where some already stood is printed, not failed. Nothing here proves a program was never proved.
**Tests.** `proved.test.mjs`, `audit-proved.test.mjs`, `guard-proved.test.mjs` and `guard-corpus.test.mjs` each fail on the laundering they name: #234's 24 ids lost (smoke, audit; 23 named is not enough; a consumed audit row names nothing; an edited or removed `changes.json` row; a regenerated ledger that drops an id), a corpus violation that turns uncertifiable or vanishes, a baseline built on another machine or from an older checker.

## ADR 1007 — A `const` over a namespace import of the dialect's module confirms the primitive a leaf operation names
ADR 0711 (commit 7c710f319, in #173) made SC3001 attribute a leaf operation to a primitive only where the binder confirms the callee: a named import whose imported name is the primitive's, or a non-computed member of a namespace import of a module the dialect owns. Everything else became `leaf-operation-identity-unproven`, the destructured form among it: `import * as S from "solid-js"; const { createEffect: make } = S; createTrackedEffect(() => { make(…) })`. The 11-05 full audit had 2,705 such programs as proved violations (PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK); on main they are recall gaps.

*Decision.* `primitive_identity_proven_at` (`cleanup.rs`) also confirms the primitive through a `const` the file never rebinds:
- the callee is the slot of a `const` object pattern whose key is a plain identifier that names the primitive, the pattern holding no default (the slot would be the default's value where the export is `undefined`), no nested pattern and no computed key (a rest element and an `export` are fine), and whose initializer is the namespace;
- the namespace is the import's own binding or a `const` identifier that holds it, read through at most four holders (`dialect_namespace_value`: `const N = S; const { createEffect: make } = N`).
- neither `const` is a declarator written directly in a `switch` case clause: a jump to a later clause enters the scope without running it. (Defensive: on the fixture's case no primitive is attributed to such a slot at all, with or without this condition.)
The member form is unchanged: a plain member of the import's own binding (`S.createEffect(…)`). A member of a held namespace (`N.createEffect(…)`) is not read as the primitive, by this check or by the producer.
A module namespace object is frozen and a `const` is never rebound, so the slot holds that export for the life of the module. A `let`, a default, a nested or computed pattern and a `let` holder prove nothing and keep their rows. A member of the namespace must be written with a plain key (it was: a computed member's text never named a primitive).

*Not covered:* a re-export hop (`import * as R from "./api"` where `./api` re-exports the module: it needs the other file, which this check does not read), a `const` alias of a named import or of a member (`const make = S.createEffect`), and a member call on a held namespace (`N.createEffect(…)`: this check takes only the import's own binding as a member's object, and no primitive is attributed to that call, SC9012 `leaf-callback-opaque`).

*Measured* (release, main 581bd7b18's code against this change). Grids, each program under both builds: every misuse and legal program of the six leaf-operation codes (101,701 and 104,371), a twelfth of the programs of the other codes with a namespace, destructured or re-export binding (32,065 and 16,769) and the stratified samples (32,331 and 18,243): 296,695 programs. **4,654 moved, every one a misuse program Chrome reports (`recall-gap`): 4,530 `leaf-operation-identity-unproven` rows became SC3001 violations** (PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE 2,820, CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE 880, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK 830) and 124 kept an obligation under the next blocker (`leaf-owner-unproven`, `computation-error-unobserved`). No legal program moved, no violation left, nothing clean changed. Corpus (rc.21 frozen, 34 projects): standard build 218 violations and 246,346 uncertifiable rows, development build 212 and 267,239, **0 rows moved** in either.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/leaf-identity-const-namespace`: the five violations fire their code at the site (PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE for the destructured slot, the shorthand and the slot over a held namespace, CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE for the slot beside a rest, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK for the exported slot); the `let`, default, nested and computed slots and the held namespace's member fire too and stay obligations; a project object's member of the same name and the slot called in a component's body are silent with no violation. For the grid programs Chrome's record is the audit's (run 43739577046). Fixtures: `leaf-identity-const-namespace`. Owners: `cleanup.rs` (`primitive_identity_proven_at`, `dialect_namespace_value`).

## ADR 1014 — A timer's callback written as a member of a `const` object literal is the function written there
The other half of the store writes lost at ADR 0803's step 2 (ADR 1013 took the `const` alias): `const cb1 = { cb: () => { … } }; setTimeout(cb1.cb, 0)`, the 462 `-cb-bundle` programs of STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER's `timer` context. `callback_seen` refused every member on purpose (`function_value_at`, review R19a: "a member is no such name: its method may be overridden or written"), so the callback was any function, the window was taken to reach unseen code, and the slots of every primitive were withdrawn.

*The change.* `mutation_sites.rs` `literal_member_function`, asked only where `function_value_at` names nothing: for a non-computed member `holder.name`, the holder is a `const` whose whole initializer is an object literal with no spread; the literal has exactly one property of that name written directly in it, with a plain key, a data property or a method whose value is a function literal (an accessor's function is not the member's value, a shorthand names another binding); and ADR 0279's facts hold as the callee resolver asks them (`execution_role::member_runs_declared_method`, now `pub(crate)`): every reference of the holder reads a member of it, no export exposes it, and no assignment anywhere writes a member of that name nor a built-in prototype. The function found is then asked the caller's own test (an arrow, or no mention of a receiver). No binding holds a property's function, so `function_value_is_current` is not asked: the member's facts are its currency. Only a yes is taken; every other member stays any function.

*Measured* (against ADR 1013's head 5f59b4763). Grid differential, checker alone: of the 2,195,028 programs the grids generate, the 34,595 that are a `-cb-bundle` program or hand a platform callback caller a member (`setTimeout(x.y, …)`) ran under both builds: 33,020 identical, 1,575 moved, 0 violation lost, 0 violation or uncertifiable row at a line that had none. Uncertifiable to violation: 462 programs, all misuse, all STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER `timer` `-cb-bundle` (mx-pairs 330, mx-recall 132): the lost ones. The legal grids (lg-pairs 495, lg-recall 198 moved programs) only lose uncertifiable rows. The fuzz harness on every moved program, each compared in real Chrome (`focus.mjs --runtime-diff all`, ids per grid): mx-pairs 630 agree, mx-recall 252 agree, lg-pairs 463 uncertifiable and 32 clean, lg-recall 102 uncertifiable and 96 clean; 1,575 compared with the oracle, 0 behaviour, 0 attribution, 0 inconclusive, nothing needs a look. Corpus (rc.21 frozen, 34 projects, release): standard 247,197 and development 267,939 uncertifiable rows on both sides, 0 rows moved, violations 218 and 212 unchanged. Fixtures (`iteration-written-slots/variants`): `handed-timer-callback-member` is proved SC2001; `-member-written`, `-member-escaped`, `-member-getter`, `-member-method-this` and `-member-spread` stay uncertifiable. Chrome rc.21, oracle case `iteration-timer-callback-member`: REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at a setter call in a component body and STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER at a store write run from a timer handed the member both fire, each `covered-violation`, 0 typing errors. *An existing fixture regains its proof:* `dispatch-and-copies` holds `setTimeout(box.run, 0)` (`SlotInTimer`), so ADR 0803's step 2 had withdrawn the slots of the whole program and its README's own claim (ADR 0516: `DispatchInMemo`, `no-write-in-pure-computation`, twice) stood in the snapshot as two `tuple-iteration-written` rows. Both are violations again (`setV.call(null, 1)`, `setV.bind(null)(2)` in a memo; the same oracle case, one component each since the first write halts its memo: Chrome reports REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at both). Of the fixture's 17 `tuple-iteration-written` and 8 `pending-read-unresolved` rows, 2 are those violations, 3 keep an uncertifiable SC9012 under the blocker of their own cause (`function-prototype-callee-unresolved` 1, `value-held-in-binding` 2, and `value-use-unclassified` gains its second row: named in `scripts/guard/rises.json`) and the rest were rows of the withdrawal alone (`drops` rows in `scripts/guard/counts.json`); no violation of the fixture moved otherwise.

*Amended after the review of the first build (42104c910: BLOCK, three false positives).* The review probed three programs where the timer calls a `function` that reads its `this` and the first build still proved the write. Two are holes of ADR 0279's own predicate, which call resolution uses too; the third is this ADR's.
1. *A computed write with an unnamed key* (`const key = ["cb"][0] as "cb"; bundle[key] = function () { … }`): the index of assigned member names (`contributions.rs` `assignment_writes`) records a name only for a literal or a constant key, and `bundle[key]` is a member read of the holder to `only_member_reads`. `holder_written_by_unnamed_key` refuses a holder some reference of which is the object of a written computed member whose key no literal and no string constant names. Asked at the holder, not in the program-wide index: the holder is proven not to escape, so such a write goes through one of its own references, or through `this` (below).
2. *The holder reaches code through `this`* (`init() { Object.assign(this, { cb() { … } }) }`, `Object.defineProperty(this, "cb", …)`): no reference of the binding shows it. `literal_hands_its_receiver_on` refuses a literal in which a `this` or `super` is anything but the object of a non-computed member (`this.m`, `this.m(…)`; `this.m = f` is an assignment the index names). The receivers are read from the file's syntax (`solid_facts::ast::receiver_expression_spans`), only when the literal's text holds either word; a file whose receivers cannot be read refuses. Not memoized (a memo by path would outlive an edit in the daemon); the sweep times are below.
3. *A duplicate key written as a string* (`{ cb: f, "cb": g }`, which `tsc` rejects, TS1117): `literal_member_function` compared the key's source text; it compares it unquoted, so the literal holds two properties of the name and is refused.
Both 1 and 2 sit in `member_runs_declared_method_in`'s object-literal branch, so call resolution (ADR 0279) asks them too. *On main* the holes were probed through call resolution in Chrome (the literal's method writes a signal in a body or a memo, or calls `onCleanup` in `onSettled`; a harmless function really runs; component-local and module-level holders): main has no violation in any of them, controls included (uncertifiable at the operation and at the call), so no false positive of main is named. *Re-measured.* The hardening alone, first build against this one, on the 370,474 grid programs (of 2,195,028) whose own source holds `this` or a computed store: 0 moved, so it moves no grid row, of this ADR or of main: the holes live in the fixtures and probes only. Main against this build on the member selection: unchanged from the first build (1,575 moved, 462 uncertifiable to violation, 0 violation lost, 0 new row at a line that had none), and the harness with each of the 1,575 compared in real Chrome again: mx-pairs 630 agree, mx-recall 252 agree, lg-pairs 463 uncertifiable and 32 clean, lg-recall 102 uncertifiable and 96 clean, nothing needs a look. Corpus, standard and development: 0 rows moved; the sweeps are no slower (sum of the 34 projects' wall times, same machine and load: development 583 s on main's build, 555 s on this one; standard 407 s and 402 s), so the receiver read is not memoized. Fixtures: `handed-timer-callback-member-computed-write`, `-member-this-assign`, `-member-this-define` and `-member-quoted-duplicate` are SC2001 violations on the first build and uncertifiable on this one; Chrome rc.21, oracle case `iteration-timer-member-replaced`: REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at the write is `covered-violation` on the first build and `covered-uncertifiable` on this one.

## ADR 1016 — A component mounted through `const D = dynamic(() => C)` throws where `<D />` renders
ADR 0893's walk (finished at 666724c4a, "value mounts", in #173) reads a component's value use as a mount only as `Dynamic`'s `component` prop; any other value use counts as handled, so a plain throw in a component mounted through `dynamic` ends `computation-error-unobserved`. The 11-05 audit had Chrome agreeing on these programs as violations (the `-m-dynamic` mount of the recall grid: `const D1 = dynamic(() => C1); <D1 />`). It is a recall gap, not a defect: FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK is no coded diagnostic in rc.21 (`flush()` in a tracked queue callback is a plain `throw new Error("Cannot call flush() from inside onSettled or createTrackedEffect…")`, `@solidjs/signals` `dist/dev-shared.js`), so ADR 0893 applies to it as written.

*Decision.* `stored_throw.rs` `dynamic_mount_tags`: a reference that is the whole expression body of a parameterless, non-`async`, non-generator arrow, that arrow the only argument of a call of the dialect's `dynamic` (`primitive_at_call` is `Dynamic`, so no options object and no other form) called by its bare name, the call the initializer of a `const` (not in a `switch` case, not exported) every reference of which is a plain JSX tag name: the component mounts at each opening tag. It is asked where the walk meets such a reference (`dynamic_mount_end`: reported unless a boundary above every tag takes it, `handled_above`; open for a throw only under an observer, `resolve` and `until`, as for a proven component), and in `mounts_handled` when every use of the component is such a source (`dynamic_only_mounts`: its value current, not exported, no reference in another analyzed file), before the component-status question. A tag counts only where reach analysis says it may run (`SiteReach`, ADR 0458, with ADR 1015's literal-dead flow children), as a component's own tag does: `<Show when={false}><D /></Show>`, `false && <D />`, a tag after `if (false) return` and `<For each={[]}>` mount nothing (the bundle review's finding on b0bfc89fd: each was a violation there, Chrome silent), and with no tag left the throw is unobserved. Any other value use keeps ADR 0893's reading.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/stored-throw-dynamic-mount`: FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK at the tracked effect's `flush()` is `covered-uncertifiable` on main 5b950fce6 and `covered-violation` on this change; the same mount under an `Errored` with a handling fallback is silent; a project `dynamic` and a shadowed one never render `C` and are silent. Fixture `stored-throw-dynamic-mount`.

*Not covered* (docs/open-work.md): the namespace form `web.dynamic(() => C)`, which the dialect resolves to `Dynamic` and the bare-name check refuses; a member form, a `let`, a use of the binding outside a tag, a block body, an exported `const`. And a throw the owner pass also holds: `useContext` with no provider in the body of a component used only as a `dynamic` source (`MountsBodyRead`) is reported by this walk but stays `component-identity-unproven`, since such a function is no proven component to SC4002's owner pass; Chrome reports CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND. That side is a later ADR.

*Measured:* after the review (the owner's order), on the programs of the `-m-dynamic` mounts first, the full grid and the corpus on the final commit.

## ADR 1011 — A closure handed to a project callee is read as part of the function around the call, and the callee's body is walked for its own boundary (SC5003: the 24 programs ADR 0978 made uncertifiable, and a false positive it made)
**Two defects of one line.** ADR 0978's cover walk reads a layer no call edge places (`loading_entries.rs` `layer_cover`): a closure that is a call's whole argument is "part of the function around it" when the call is a primitive, a standard-library call or a project function (`function_called_at`), and otherwise runs where the analysis does not see, so a boundary may hold it (Unresolved: SC5003 uncertifiable, blocker `mount-unresolved`). (1) `function_called_at` names only an identifier callee (its comment: a member callee "names its own value through other facts", ADR 0346), so `H.run(() => slow())` with `import * as H from "./helpers"` and `run(cb) { cb(); return 1; }` read as a call to unresolved code: a proved violation Chrome confirms (ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY: no `Loading` anywhere) became an obligation. Found by the audit of main 78ddeb849 (an id-level comparison with the audit of dfa6c5dec: 24 mx-recall programs `agree` then, `recall-gap` now; ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY × show / jsx / flush-iife / named-flush-call × 6, all layer `module-ns`), bisected to #234 (dbb5e7612) over the 29 merges and read with the proof log: the only difference at the site is the SC5003 finding, violation to uncertifiable. #234's corpus delta (violations 218 and 212 unchanged) and `fuzz-focus` could not see it: no corpus project has the shape, and `recall-gap` is not a problem outcome. (2) The independent review of this change's first cut found the other way round, and on main: the `continue` read the closure as part of the CALLER and never looked into the callee, so a callee that wraps its calls of the parameter in a boundary of its own (`export function exprArrow(cb) { createLoadingBoundary(() => cb(), () => 0); return 1 }`, and the block-bodied `inBoundary`) left `exprArrow(() => { slow(); })`, with no `Loading` in the caller, a VIOLATION. Chrome rc.21 reports nothing there: the callee's boundary catches the pending read. A false positive of main since #234 for the identifier callee (pattern lane `membercallee/id-in-boundary`, `id-in-boundary-block`: `false-positive` on 78ddeb849, Chrome codes `[]`).

**The change.** `layer_cover` returns `LayerCover::Callee` for a closure that is an argument of a project function the analysis resolves exactly: an identifier callee whose function its binding still is (`function_called_at`, trusted only where `function_value_is_current_in` holds: a `let` something writes, and `const f = wrap((cb) => ..)`, whose value is what `wrap` returns, are not it, and keep the answer main gave: part of the function around the call) or a member `execution_role::project_callee_at_parameter` resolves exactly (its `exact` flag); a spread before the argument and an unresolved or inexact callee stay Unresolved. The walk (`async_context.rs` `callee_held`) then reads the callee's body for every use of the parameter (`loading_entries.rs` `parameter_uses`): a call of it, whose cover is walked from the call up to the callee's top (`loading_cover_from` gains a `stop`: reached with no boundary is Uncovered; each use has its own chain of places), or the parameter passed whole into another call (`passed_cover`: the boundary primitive's held argument covers, a project function is walked in turn down at most sixteen hand-offs, anything else says nothing). The uses are combined (`Held`): a use that runs the closure with no boundary around it decides, so the violation stays (a callee that holds one call in a boundary and runs another bare, `both`; `arguments[0]()`. `branch(cb, false)` and a returned `() => cb()` are uncertifiable on main already, `call-attributed-read`, and stay so); a boundary on every use is Covered; on some while the others are not known is Unresolved (uncertifiable); on none, or a body the walk cannot read (the parameter is stored, aliased, written, `new`ed, never called, or the body reads `arguments`; the callee is `async` or a generator), says nothing: an identifier callee keeps main's answer (part of the caller's function), a member callee, which main left Unresolved, stays Unresolved (the review of the third cut: `H.argLen(cb)`, a boundary beside `arguments.length`, was a new violation Chrome does not report). A read of `arguments.length` alone runs nothing and does not stop the walk: the identifier `argLen(cb)`, a violation of main where Chrome (`membercallee/arglen-id`) is quiet, is uncertifiable now, the one other V to U of the change. A chain longer than the sixteen hand-offs is not read and says nothing (an identifier callee keeps main's answer, a member callee stays Unresolved). A callee's own stop is keyed by file and span. Each callee parameter is walked once per build and memoized (`CalleeCovers`; an answer that rests on a walk still in progress, a recursive visitor handing the parameter to itself, is not kept: `Walk`'s stack and taint): the first cut walked a recursive visitor once per path, about 2^17 times for two calls, and did not finish for three (`loading_callee_cost_process`, counted by `BuildTimings::callee_walks`). The comment, the rule page and the fixture README say so.

**What it moves, measured.** Fixture `loading-member-callee` (snapshot): the control `Named` (an identifier) and `NamedReexport` stay violations, `Namespace` (`H.run(cb)`) goes from SC5003 `mount-unresolved` to a violation, `Forward` and `PassOn` (a chain of two project functions, the last calling the closure) are violations; `NsInBoundary`, `NsInBoundaryBlock`, `IdInBoundary`, `IdInBoundaryBlock` and `ForwardBoundary` (the callee, or the callee it forwards to, wraps the call in `createLoadingBoundary`) are uncertifiable and carry no violation, as are `Later` (`queueMicrotask(cb)`: not a call), `Maybe` (a call on a flag), `Stored`, `Replaced`, `Shadowed` and `Handed`. A re-exported namespace's member, a default import's method and a literal's method were `call-attributed-read` before and are after (no call edge places the closure in the callee: `docs/open-work.md`). Chrome (rc.21, uncached): the pattern lane `membercallee/` (22 programs, all `fine`): `ns-run`, `ns-forward`, `ns-maybe`, `ns-pass-on`, `reexport-ns`, `default-member` and `literal-method` report the code; `id-in-boundary`, `id-in-boundary-block`, `ns-in-boundary`, `ns-in-boundary-block`, `ns-forward-boundary`, `ns-keep`, `ns-later` and `ns-run-covered` (the same call inside a `Loading`) are quiet and carry no violation. The 24 ids agree again with the fix and the fast path equals Chrome on all 24. Corpus (rc.21, 34 projects, release, old 78ddeb849 against this change, standard and development): 269,715 and 290,101 findings on both sides, 0 added, 0 removed. The codes the cover walk serves (ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY, PENDING_ASYNC_UNTRACKED_READ, PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, LOADING_ON_ACCESSOR, LOADING_ON_OUTSIDE_HOLD) on all eleven grids, checker only, old binary against new, per program (133,000 programs): ten grids move nothing; mx-recall moves 29: the 24 above and five `mx-loading-on-outside-hold-…-module-ns` programs that gain the same SC5003 violation (Chrome reports it there too: the judge records it `corroborated`; their outcome stays `recall-gap`). No violation is lost anywhere. The cut before the passed-on follow (a parameter passed on read as unknown) lost 58 violations of the `forward-2` and `forward-13` layers that Chrome reports; following the parameter into the project function it goes to keeps them.

**Not done.** `make fuzz-focus` cannot fail on the 24: `recall-gap` is not a problem outcome and no smoke manifest holds a recall grid, so the old build passes it; the entry in `rediscovery.json` lists the 24 ids and says so, and the fixture's `Namespace` snapshot is the gate. The identifier false positive has an `outside` entry: no generator writes a boundary inside the helper that receives the closure; the pattern lane is its gate. The wider question the audit raised (the V to U moves between the last green audit, aa4702650, and 6e33e0b08: mx-base 240, mx-combo 283, mx-pairs 2,437, mx-recall 6,622) is not read here.

## ADR 1009 — A function a closed `const` bundle hands to a primitive runs where that primitive runs its callback
ADR 0667 (commit 3ffbc91b5, in #173) opened every possibly async read written in a function that is an object member: "an object method, class member or array slot has no binding to follow". `const bundle = { run: () => { user(); } }; onSettled(bundle.run);` became two uncertifiable rows (SC5001 `invocation-context-unproven`, SC5003 `call-attributed-read`), though the hand-off is plain and Chrome reports PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE. The 11-05 full audit had the recall grid's `bundle` callback form of that code as proved violations: 84 programs in mx-recall and 12 in mx-pairs are recall gaps since. The same shape handed by a `const` name (`const run = () => …; onSettled(run)`) is a violation on main.

*Decision.* A function has a place when it is handed from a closed bundle (`local_access.rs` `handed_from_closed_bundle`):
- it is the value of a plain data property (no method, no accessor, no computed key, no shorthand) of an object literal that is the initializer of a `const` identifier binding, directly (not inside a nested object or array), and the property is the key's final value: no spread after it in the literal, no later computed or otherwise nameless key, no later property of the same key (`property_is_final_value` in `flow_helpers.rs`, the check `origin_member_ignores_receiver` already made);
- the binding is not exported (both `binding_exported`, for `export { x as y }` and `export default x`, and `flow_binding_exported`, for an exported declaration and a script's global top-level binding, say no), and every reference to it is the object of a non-computed member read of that one key, never a write target: the object is never passed, spread, returned, aliased, called through or written;
- each such member read is the whole argument of a primitive's call.
Then the primitive's callback position is the only thing that runs it, as for a function a `const` names. Two places ask the fact, both in ADR 0667's arm: `placed_elsewhere` for the bundle function itself, and `unplaced_run_but` (`execution_role/site_reach.rs`: `unplaced_run` with the object-member layer left out where the caller proves its place) for a read in a closure, an IIFE or a helper's callback written inside it. Every other layer `unplaced_run` knows (a class element, an array slot, a tag function, a function that escapes unfollowed) is asked as before, and so is every other rule: only the async-read walk reads the new fact.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/pending-read-closed-bundle`: the five violations fire PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE at the read (`onSettled`, `createTrackedEffect`, a closure and an IIFE inside the bundle function, a bundle with a second property); the obligations keep their row whether Chrome fires (the object passed on, a computed key, a `let`, a method, the member aliased, a nested bundle, the member also called) or not (the property rewritten before the hand-off); the same bundle handed to a memo's compute has no violation.

*Measured so far* (release, main 0799a4629 against this change; the programs the change's shape selects, the full differential and the corpus run on the final commit). Every program of the six pending and async codes whose callback form is `bundle`, misuse and legal (2,034 and 147): 493 moved. 166 recall-gap programs of PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE gain the SC5001 violation at Chrome's site (mx-recall 84 of 84, mx-pairs 82); 19 programs that already agreed gain it at a second row; no violation left. 282 PENDING_ASYNC_UNTRACKED_READ programs keep an obligation under another blocker (`callee-callback-timing` for `invocation-context-unproven`: 318 rows out, 302 in). 7 legal programs, uncertifiable before and after, gain one SC5003 `call-attributed-read` row each; no legal program gains a violation.

*Not covered:* a bundle that escapes or is written (above), a class member, an array slot; and the 32 mx-combo programs that lost a pending-read violation at the same time, which hold no bundle: there the async value reaches a child through a component prop (`<C1 a1={a1()} />`, blockers `async-prop-getter`, `handed-member-read`, `async-options-opaque`), another proof. A write of a key anywhere in a file still opens every member of that name, so a closed bundle beside an unrelated `other.run = …` keeps its row. Fixtures: `pending-read-closed-bundle`. Owners: `local_access.rs` (`handed_from_closed_bundle`, `placed_elsewhere`), `execution_role/site_reach.rs` (`unplaced_run_but`).

*Review fixes (medium review of 4dd928e93: approve with fixes).* F1: the property's final value was never checked, so `{ run: () => { user(); }, ...extra }` and `{ run: () => { user(); }, [k]: () => {} }` took the replaced function for the one `onSettled` runs (Chrome is silent). Fixed by `property_is_final_value`. The reviewer's two snippets are NOT a violation on 4dd928e93 either: `handed_from_closed_bundle` answered true for both (instrumented), and a later stage of the walk keeps a literal with a spread or a computed key open, so no verdict differs between the builds on them; the check is made independent of that stage, and the shape is held by the fixture (`SpreadAfter`, `ComputedAfter`, both Chrome-silent) and by two legal fuzz cells (`dead-bundle-spread`, `dead-bundle-computed`: 2,400 programs of all codes, identical on main, 4dd928e93 and this change). F2: fixture variants, each Chrome-run. Obligations with Chrome silent: `onSettled` shadowed by a local and by a parameter, `keep(bundle.key)`. Violations Chrome reports: `bundle.key!`, `bundle.key as any`, `S.onSettled(bundle.key)`. Obligations where Chrome reports (known misses, kept closed): `onSettled(() => bundle.key())`, a quoted key, `const { run } = bundle`, a spread or computed key BEFORE the property, a module-level bundle (exported by declaration, by `export { x as y }` or as the default, and the unexported one). `export { bundle as x }` and `export default bundle` are exported for both questions.

## ADR 1015 — The children a literal prop keeps from ever running are unreached: `For each={[]}`, `Repeat count={0}`, `Show when={false}`, `Match when={false}`
**The defect.** Code in a row or a branch that can never run was reported as a violation while Chrome stayed silent: `<Repeat count={0}>{() => <p>{(() => { useContext(Bare); return 1; })()}</p>}</Repeat>` and `<For each={[]}>…` were SC4002 violations (`<Repeat count={1}>` is the same read where the row runs, and stays one). `SiteReach` (ADR 0458) knew only the syntax's dead regions (`if (false)`, after a `return`, `false &&`, a component nothing renders); a flow component's children were `MayRun` whatever the prop said. The 7,200 programs of the six `dead-flow-*` cells of `lg-recall` (all codes) hold it: on main 5b950fce6, 3,528 were a checker violation at a site that never ran (504 `false-positive` with a pending read, 3,024 `unexecuted`).
**The decision (owner's option c, 2026-11-16).** Only the LITERAL cases. The Solid 2 dialect answers `flow_children_exclusion(export, prop)` (`semantics.rs` `FlowChildrenExclusion`, read on the rc.21 triple only, `None` for every other dialect and release): `For`+`each` with `[]` (the row function's body is dead; `For` reads `props.children` once when it maps, so a child that is a call is evaluated), `Repeat`+`count` with `0` (returns before its mapper: no child is read), `Show`+`when` and `Match`+`when` with `false` (children are read only when truthy). The runtime facts are read from rc.21's `solid.dev.js` and `@solidjs/signals`. The IR side (`components.rs` `flow_dead_children`) accepts an element only when the tag resolves EXACTLY to the Solid declaration (`component_entry_of_tag`, ADR 0992: not the spelling, so `import { Repeat as Rep }` and `<S.For>` count and a project `Repeat` does not), it carries no spread, the prop is written once with no namespace, and its value text, under parentheses and a TypeScript assertion, is exactly `[]`, `0` or `false`. `site_reach.rs` `statically_dead` adds those spans to the syntax's dead regions at its three call sites (`site_within`, `runs_uncached`, `SyntaxReach::of`), so the site is `Unreached` and a violation there is the uncertifiable `unreached-dead-code`, never a violation and never a wrong silence. A `fallback` is not dead (it runs exactly when the children do not).
**Anything else keeps "may run"**: a name (`const zero = 0`, a named empty array, `!true`), a derived count, a spread. That is a remaining false positive (Chrome is silent where the value is 0 at run time), recorded in `docs/open-work.md` and pinned in `fixtures/reactive-ir/dead-literal-rows` (`RepeatNamedZero`, `ForNamedEmpty`, `ShowNegated`, `RepeatZeroWithSpread`), not excluded by guessing.
**Evidence.** Fixture `dead-literal-rows` (10 dead sites, 7 live, 4 non-literal, a shadowing project `Repeat`/`Show`): against main exactly the 10 dead sites move violation to uncertifiable; Chrome (`runtime-oracle/dead-literal-rows`, quiet; main's checker: 10 `static-only`) and its live pair (`dead-literal-rows-live`: 7 of 7 `covered-violation` at the live controls). `make coverage` on 1,293 projects: no snapshot moved. Fuzz: `dead-flow-<form>` contexts (`DEAD_FLOW_CONTEXTS`, misuse.mjs; the `flow-<form>` element printed with the literal that keeps its children from running), legal for every code. Old build, new generator: 7,200 programs, {unexecuted 3,024, uncertifiable 3,096, clean 576, false-positive 504}, `make fuzz-focus` exit 1; this build {uncertifiable 3,636, clean 3,564}, nothing needs a look. Moves by program: 3,528 violation to uncertifiable (all of them), 2,988 uncertifiable to clean (an obligation in a site no run reaches is dropped, as the syntax's dead regions already do for these codes: the `dead-if`, `dead-and-false`, `dead-after-return`, `dead-comp-never` cells show the same mix), none other. Not yet measured: the live flow cells (`flow-<form>`, `show-later`, `for-item`, `for-signal`) and the full grid differential, which run once on the final commit (owner's ruling 2026-11-16). Corpus (the rc.21 frozen set, 34 projects, std and dev; measured on the commit before review, to be rerun on the final one): 0 violations moved (212 in both builds), 8 uncertifiable rows gone, all in `app-game` `packages/svg-editor/index.tsx` under two `<Show when={false}>` blocks (SC2002 4, SC3001 2, SC6002 2: obligations at the handlers and reads written there).
**Limits.** The exclusion reads text, not values: a literal the program cannot see through a name stays live (above). `Match` is excluded by its own `when` only (a `Switch` whose first match is true makes a later `Match` dead too; that is not read). No other verdict changes.

<a id="adr-1018"></a>
## ADR 1018 — A checker violation at a site no run reaches needs a look; a provably dead site gives U, never V (the 2026-11-10 ruling is retired)
**The hole.** The legal judge filed a violation at a site Chrome never runs as `unexecuted` (legal.mjs; ADR 0458) and nothing failed on it: `unexecuted` is not in `PROBLEMS`, so the audit, the smoke and every focus run passed over it. The full audit at 78ddeb849 (run 43739577046) held 6,205 such rows, all in lg-recall, all a checker VIOLATION in a legal program, in four groups, each re-run on main 993e83f74 and Chrome-confirmed (the site never runs, nothing is reported, the runtime differential identical): a gate a default parameter throws before (5,852: the gate-throw contexts), a callback handed to a standard-library iteration of an empty literal collection (195: `tbl-*-zero`), a closure an effect's compute returns that nothing calls (120: `apply-void-value-row`, `-untrack`), a read in a class constructor, getter, setter or field helper nothing constructs or accesses (38: `ob-*-async-never`).
**The ruling it retires.** Owner, 2026-11-17: a provably dead site gives U, never V. That retires the ruling of 2026-11-10 ("a violation means wrong if it runs", kept at a zero-run carrier: boundary.mjs `EXPECTED_UNEXECUTED`), as ADR 1015 already did for the children of a literal-dead flow element. A fix proves "may not run" and answers U at that site, never clean. ADR 0563's silent read side stays. The four groups are fixed by ADR 1010 (gate-throw), ADR 1019 (`tbl-*-zero`), ADR 1020 (`apply-void-value`) and ADR 1021 (`ob-*-async-never`).
**The change.** `codes.mjs` `rowProblem` answers `unexecuted-violation` for a legal grid's `unexecuted` row unless `scripts/fuzz/unexecuted-known.json` holds it: an entry names a grid, an id pattern, a kind (`explained`: the judge is right and the row is no checker defect, a lane that never drives the site; `pending-fix`: a false positive whose ADR is named) and a reason, in the style of `audit-known.json`. Anything the ledger does not hold fails the audit, the smoke and the smoke-census jobs (focus.mjs and audit.mjs read `rowProblem`; smoke.mjs's move comparison too). The seed is the four groups as `pending-fix ADR 1010/1019/1020/1021`; each fix removes its entry, so the same rows fail if the fix regresses. A misuse grid's `unexecuted` (the page halted before the site, matrix.mjs) is another outcome and is untouched. boundary.mjs lists a violation at a zero-run carrier as a false positive pending ADR 1019, no longer as kept.
**Pending (2026-11-17, after #270).** The four seed groups' fixes have landed (ADRs 1010, 1019, 1020, 1021) and their entries left; the #270 smoke then found two groups no fix covers, held as `pending-fix`: ADR 1033 (`tbl-nodelist*-foreach-zero`, an empty DOM `NodeList`; landed for a `NodeList` of an element made there, `nodelistof` of the document's selector stays a violation, its rows held as `explained`) and ADR 1034 (`dead-bundle-spread`/`-computed` × SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC; landed, its entry left). **Pending (2026-11-20, #294):** the six `lg-strict-read-untracked-dny-legal-{click,keydown,pointer}-store-effect-{called,named-called}-direct-none` programs (ADR 1127's twin variant generated them; main c212ad5f5 gives the same findings) are held as `pending-fix` ADR 1132. (Removed with ADR 1132.) **Pending (2026-11-20, ADR 1132's twin):** the four `lg-strict-read-untracked-dny-legal-mount-disabled-store-{effect-called,effect-named-called,effect-carried,render-effect-carried}-direct-none` programs (a button disabled by its JSX from mount; SC4001 `missing-owner` violation where no event reaches the handler) are held as `pending-fix` ADR 1134 (Mac 22: uncertifiable, not silent).

<a id="adr-1019"></a>
## ADR 1019 — A callback handed to a standard-library iteration of a literal nothing can fill is unreached
**The defect.** `const tf1 = () => { a1(); }; ([] as number[]).forEach(tf1);` in a component body was an SC2002 violation (likewise SC2001 for a write, SC3002 for `onFlush`) while Chrome never runs `tf1`: the `InlineCallback` row says *when* a carrier runs its callback (before it returns), not *whether* (ADR 0563 drew the same line for a pending read's proof). Full CI audit run 43739577046, `lg-recall`: all 195 programs of the 39 `tbl-*-zero` contexts (table-shapes.mjs, the receiver on which the callback never runs) × REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, ON_FLUSH_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE were `unexecuted`; re-confirmed on main 993e83f74.
**The decision (owner's ruling 2026-11-17: a site that provably never runs is uncertifiable, never a violation, never clean).** `carrier_runs.rs` `carrier_provably_never_runs`, the dual of ADR 0563's `carrier_provably_runs`, on the compiler-selected standard-library declaration (never the spelling): an `Array`/`ReadonlyArray` iteration method and `sort` on an empty array literal; `reduce`/`reduceRight` on `[]`, or on a one-element literal with no spread or hole and exactly one argument (ECMA-262: the element is the accumulator and no call is made); `Array.from` and the typed-array `from`s with `[]` as the source; `Set.forEach`/`Map.forEach` on `new Set()`/`new Map()` written there with no argument, the constructor `SetConstructor.construct`/`MapConstructor.construct`; `String.replace`/`replaceAll` with a quoted receiver and a quoted non-empty pattern, no escape, the receiver does not contain. No argument may be a spread, parentheses and TypeScript assertions are peeled. `handed_to_idle_carrier` asks it of an argument at the row's inline position (`is_inline_standard_callback`, so a primitive, a project `forEach` or a local `Array` is no carrier); `site_reach.rs` reads such a reference as one that reaches nothing (`references_unreached`) and such a literal as never entered (`runs_uncached`), so a violation in the callback is the uncertifiable `function-unentered` (ADR 0458), and a second reference that calls the function keeps it live. The read side of ADR 0563 is unchanged.
**Not excluded** (known remaining false positives, `docs/open-work.md`): a name holding `[]`, a wrapper's parameter, a DOM `NodeList` (the two `tbl-nodelist*-zero` contexts, 10 programs), `globalThis.Array.from` (an intrinsic as a value withdraws the tuple slots: SC9012).
**Evidence.** Fixture `dead-site-empty-collection`: against main exactly the 10 sites of the never-run section move violation to uncertifiable (SC2001 ×8, SC2002, SC3002); the 7 may-run cases (`NonEmpty`, `NamedEmpty`, `ReduceWithInitial`, `SetWithElement`, `ReplaceMatch`, `AlsoCalled`, `ChildNodes`) stay violations and `Wrapped` stays uncertifiable; `dead-site-empty-collection-shadowed` (a project `Map`, a local `Array`) identical. Chrome: `runtime-oracle/dead-site-empty-collection` quiet (main: 10 `static-only`), `-live` 5 of 5 `covered-violation`. Fuzz slice (`lg-recall`, the 39 zero contexts, the three codes and STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED, 273 programs): main {unexecuted 195, uncertifiable 78}, this build {uncertifiable 263, unexecuted 10}; by program 185 unexecuted to uncertifiable, 78 uncertifiable to uncertifiable, 10 unchanged (the NodeList contexts), nothing else. Main's Chrome sample: 117 programs (39 per code), every one with no diagnostic and the same hits as the fast host (the site never ran). `make fuzz-focus` passes on both builds: an `unexecuted` row is not gated until ADR 1018's oracle guard.
**Obligations at a site that never runs close (coordinator's ruling 2026-11-17).** The ruling forbids a would-be violation at a dead site coming out clean while the site stays reported; a sound proof that the site never runs closing an obligation is allowed, by the never-runs silences `if (false)` and ADR 1015 already use (`OwnerCallNeverRuns`, `FlushSafe::NeverRuns`). So `lg-recall` `handed-flush-empty` × RESOLVE/UNTIL_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE (822 programs; the `flush` in `([] as number[]).map(k)`): 410 uncertifiable to clean, 412 unchanged; coverage: 6 rows gone (`resolve-inline-entries` `Empty`, 4; `unplaced-site-obligations` `ReduceCallback`, 2; drops rows in `scripts/guard/counts.json`) and 6 SC4001 relabels (`function-run-unplaced` to `owner-callers-unenumerated`). `use-write-foreach-empty`: no move.

<a id="adr-1029"></a>
## ADR 1029 — A Chrome result is taken once: content keys, one cache per machine, the checker always fresh
**The hole.** Owner, 2026-11-17: Solid's answer on a fixed program does not change, yet Chrome reran it. (a) The record keys held `treeStat` (every file's size and mtime) of the installs (`installedKey`), of `packages/cli/node_modules` (`ORACLE_SOURCES`), of the browser build (`browserKey`, `chromeHostKey`): a fresh clone or reinstall keyed apart. (b) The Chrome key held the fast path, the type check, `checker.mjs` and `cache.mjs` (`RECORD_SOURCES`), none of which runs in a browser. (c) The caches lived per checkout or per `$TMPDIR` (`rust/target/runtime-oracle-cache`, `$TMPDIR/solid-checker-fuzz-cache.noindex`). (d) The CLI's browser-execution cache keyed the checker's development models (`feedbackFacts`) even with `--source-instrumentation off` (the runtime oracle), where the browser half never reads them, and keyed and stored absolute paths, so no other checkout, and no other fuzz run (each stages under its own out dir), could hit it. (e) The fuzz Chrome entry cache (`runChrome` with `cache`) answered a hit with the stored record WHOLE, its checker half the storing run's.
**The change.** A Chrome record is keyed by the case's bytes, the installs by content (`installedContent`: npm's `node_modules/.package-lock.json`, else every package's name and version), the browser by its executable's bytes (`binaryHash`), the recorder and driver sources only (`CHROME_RECORD_SOURCES`: chrome.mjs, hits.mjs, pipeline.mjs, the Chrome host and what it serves; the oracle and `packages/cli` through `ORACLE_SOURCES`), the clock and page options, and a record format version (`RECORD_FORMAT`) instead of cache.mjs's bytes. One cache per machine: `~/.cache/solid-checker/fuzz.noindex` (`SOLID_CHECKER_FUZZ_CACHE`) for the fuzz caches and the execution cache below them, `~/.cache/solid-checker/runtime-oracle.noindex` (`SOLID_CHECKER_RUNTIME_ORACLE_CACHE`) for runtime-oracle.mjs. The CLI's execution cache, with the source instrumentation off, keys no checker model: the half's only model-derived parts (`candidateScopes`, the conflicting leaf models) are recomputed after the read from the raw scopes it keeps, with this run's models (`withCurrentModels`); frame attribution is source maps and the reviewed native reader, neither the checker's. Its key is project-relative and its body stores the project and tooling roots as placeholders, put back at the reading checkout's paths, where its runtime-input pins are re-hashed (a changed file is still a miss). `runChrome` always runs the oracle (whose execution cache skips Chrome for a seen case), so the checker half is every run's own; the entry cache keeps the runtime half only, names a seen case `cached`, and lists a fresh runtime that differs from the stored one (`spotMismatches`), which replaces it.
**Who used the stored checker half (e).** Only `replay.mjs` and `equivalence.mjs` with `--confirm-with-chrome` pass a `cache` to `runChrome`, and their Chrome verdicts (a replay's `fixed`, an equivalence's status) read `record.checker`. `matrix.mjs`, `legal.mjs`, `run.mjs`, the audit's oracle, `focus.mjs` and the smoke never did: they pass only the CLI's execution cache, which reruns the checker on every call. So no gate or grid measurement could take a stale checker half; a replay or equivalence run with a warm Chrome cache could, and none of the W runs of this week was one (the repository does not record other machines' tool runs).
**Not covered.** An installed dist file edited in place, with npm's record unchanged, is not seen (reinstall instead). A program whose case files are byte-equal but whose staging differs by path keys the same by design: the path is not the program.

<a id="adr-1030"></a>
## ADR 1030 — The pattern lane fails a build that loses a proved violation
**The hole.** The lane (`scripts/fuzz/patterns.mjs`) judged a program `fine` when a finding covered every code Chrome reported, a violation or an uncertifiable row alike, so a build that turned a proved violation into an uncertifiable row passed it: ADR 1011's second cut (17afe6c88) lost the violations of `membercallee/both-*`, `via-arguments-id`, `wrap-let` and `via-wrap` (V on main, Chrome warning) and passed the lane 22 of 22; only the fixture snapshot caught it.
**The change.** A `fine` program says how it passes (`proof`: `violation` when a violation covers every claimed code, `uncertifiable` when an uncertifiable row covers one, `silent` when Chrome claimed nothing). `scripts/fuzz/patterns-proved.json` holds the programs proved by a violation, recorded from a run on main (`--record-proved` adds, a run never removes). A program it holds that a run no longer proves by a violation, or no longer runs, fails the lane (`LOST PROOF`, exit 1), unless a row of its `changes` (`{ ids, adr, why }`) names it: the case expects the move, and the ADR says why. An `--only` run judges only what it ran.
**Measured.** The seed: a full lane run on main c2779cb39's checker (1,861 programs: 1,841 fine, 19 false clean, all held by open-defects.json) records 273 programs proved by a violation; the run exits 0. ADR 1011's second cut (17afe6c88) on `membercallee/` (32 programs) now exits 1: `LOST PROOF` for `both-id`, `both-ns`, `chain17`, `via-arguments-id`, `via-wrap` and `wrap-let` (each `fine/uncertifiable`, a violation on main); main's checker on the same 32 exits 0 (10 proved, 0 lost).

<a id="adr-1010"></a>
## ADR 1010 — A callback handed past a parameter default that may run code is not proven to run
*A false positive on main (993e83f74).* `const gt0 = (g, _gate = stopGate()) => { g(); }; try { gt0(() => { setW1(7); }); } catch {}` in a component body was an SC2001 violation: the default runs before the body whenever its argument is missing or `undefined`, `stopGate()` throws there, and `g` is never called (Chrome rc.21: no diagnostic, the site never executed; the fuzz judge classes it `unexecuted`, which its needs-a-look list does not hold). ADR 0931 refused the parameter-completion proof for such a helper, but SC2001's claim does not rest on that proof: it stood because reach analysis took the literal to run whenever its caller does. The full audit 43739577046 held 5,852 such rows in `lg-recall`'s `gate-throw` context (W3's scan of every `unexecuted` violation).

*Decision.* `site_reach.rs` `handed_past_live_default`: a function literal written as an argument of a call of an exact project function (`project_callee_at_parameter`, no primitive) whose parameter list has a default that may run code at that call (`callback_standing.rs` `defaults_run_no_code_at`) makes the reach query undecided (ADR 0560's bound): a violation there is `site-reach-undecided`, an obligation stays, nothing becomes clean (owner's ruling 2026-11-17: a provably dead site gives U). A default is inert when it is a function or primitive literal, `{}`, `[]` or `undefined`; a destructured parameter with defaults of its own is not; a default whose argument at the call is a function or primitive literal does not run. Anything else (no argument, a spread at or before it, a name or call that may be `undefined`) may run it.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/helper-throwing-default`: REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at the literal default (`InertDefault`) and at a literal argument (`DefaultSupplied`) is `covered-violation` on both builds; the throwing default (an arrow and a `function` declaration) and an argument that may be `undefined` are silent in Chrome, `static-only` violations on main and uncertifiable here. Fixture `helper-throwing-default`.

*Measured:* release, main 993e83f74 against this change, on the 69,313 grid programs of the `gate-*` contexts and every 20th program that hands a callback to a helper: 3,018 moved, every one a violation that became `site-reach-undecided`, every one a `gate-throw` program (3,014 legal `lg-recall`: SC2001 2,192 + 53 x2, SC2002 423, SC3002 346; 4 `mx-census` misuse programs, SC7001 2 and SC7002 2, whose site is the same dead callback); no `gate-default` program and no other program moved, nothing became a violation or clean. The full grid and the corpus run on the final commit of the batch.

## ADR 1021 — The members of a class or object literal nothing constructs or accesses are unreached
**The defect.** `class K1 { constructor() { r1(); } }; void K1;` after an `await` in an async memo was an SC1002 (UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT) violation while Chrome never constructs `K1`. ADR 0458's `class_unreached` already made a class's members unreached when every reference to it is unreached, but `void K1` is a reference that runs. Full CI audit run 43739577046, `lg-recall`: the 38 programs of `ob-{ctor-new,ctor-super,ctor-implicit,field-helper,getter,setter}-{memo,effect}-async-never` (ob-shapes.mjs) were `unexecuted`; re-confirmed on main 993e83f74.
**The decision (owner's ruling 2026-11-17, as ADR 1019).** `site_reach.rs`: (1) `references_unreached` also accepts a reference that is a value nothing takes (`inert_reference`: `AstFacts::inert_operands`, the operand of `void` or `typeof`, an expression statement, a side of `===`/`!==`, through parentheses and assertions) and a reference that is, as it stands, the `extends` clause of a class itself unreached (defining a subclass reads its superclass and its own `prototype`, no accessor, and runs none of its code); (2) a site or function written in a non-static field's initializer of an unreached class is never entered (`in_field_of_unreached_class`: the initializer runs only when an instance is made); (3) a function that is a property value (getter, setter, method, function-valued property) written directly in an object literal that is the whole initializer of an identifier binding, not exported, no `eval`, every reference unreached, is never entered (`literal_member_unreached`). The existing guards stand: a static block, a static initializer or a decorator keeps a class live. Anything that hands the value on (an argument, `Reflect.construct`, a property, a spread) keeps it live.
**Evidence.** Fixture `dead-site-unused-class`: against main exactly the 4 never-run violations (`CtorNever`, `CtorSuperNever`, `FieldHelperNever`, `GetterNever`) move to uncertifiable; `MethodNever` was uncertifiable on main; the 6 triggered cases stay violations; one obligation at the never-run field's `fh()` closes. Chrome: `runtime-oracle/dead-site-unused-class` quiet (main: 4 `static-only`), `-live` 6 of 6 `covered-violation`. Fuzz, `lg-recall`, every `ob-*-never` context × the six `ob` codes (1,644 programs): main {uncertifiable 1,606, unexecuted 38}, this build {uncertifiable 910, clean 734}: 38 unexecuted to uncertifiable (all of them), 734 uncertifiable to clean (the obligations at the never-run sites close by the never-runs silences, as for `if (false)` and ADR 1015: CLEANUP/PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK across the `ob-*-{settled,tracked}-never` constructs, iterators, coercions and `local`), none other. Chrome: 29 of the 38 sampled (`--runtime-diff 10`), each with no diagnostic and the site never run. The triggered twins (`mx-recall`, every non-`never` `ob-*` context, 1,644 programs): identical. `make fuzz-focus` exits 0 on both builds (`unexecuted` is gated by ADR 1018).
**Coverage.** No violation moved. 22 uncertifiable rows close at never-run sites, in seven fixtures, each a `void x`-only binding or a never-constructed class: `generator-step-owner` `localShadow` (2), `leaf-scope-by-value-callback` `BundleUnrun` (1), `owner-namespace-reachable` `unused` (2), `owner-region-no-edge` e13 `StoredNeverCalled` (2: the trade its README recorded is gone), `parameter-list-owner` `*Default` (8, SC4001's row stays at each), `rc13-flush-in-effect-callback` (5), `solid2-precision` `NestedSettledCleanup` (2; `diagnostics_process` counts updated); 3 SC4001 relabels (`function-run-unplaced` to `owner-callers-unenumerated`); drops and relabel rows in `scripts/guard/counts.json`. Five fixtures whose claim is another mechanism's row at a kept-but-unused value (`after-await-runner-callback` `later`, `flush-universe-inline-suite` `Field`/`withDefault`, `flush-universe-test-runner` `Late`, the two `flush-universe-package-hand-off` `plainHolder`s, `write-cleanup-handle-call` `K`) now write `void [x]` (an array element is no inert use), so their rows stand unchanged.

<a id="adr-1024"></a>
## ADR 1024 — A write whose object the program made reaches no standard root: the fresh written object, by its binding or through a standard factory (SC9012 `standard-member-impostor`)
ADR 0939's open-write census counts a member write whose object is not made where it is written as one that may put a member on a standard root, and `handed_root_patch` withholds every standard call of its key while a root is handed on. The census knew one made object (`fresh_object`: a literal, or a `const` or never-written `let` bound to one). On the rc.21 corpus (dev build) every one of the 41,518 `handed-root-patch` rows fires `OpenMemberWrite(*)`, and `@solidjs/router` next.41 alone puts six such writes into every program that installs it, each on an object its own code made: in 15 tsconfigs they are the only ones (the brief, `sc-scratch.noindex/mac22/brief-sc9012.md`). The handed side of the formula is no lever: `StandardRootHanded` fires in every row, and the iterator arm holds all but 83 of them without it.

*Decision.* `base/contributions/fresh_written.rs` (`fresh_written_object`) answers, at each write of the census (`impostor_sites`' `write`, and an `Object.assign` target), how its object is proven made:
- **Made** (by syntax alone, the census drops the write as before): a literal, `null` or `undefined`; a `const` bound to one; a `let` whose initial value and every plain or logical assigned value is one, each assuming the binding's previous value made (an induction over the order of its writes; a pattern, `for … of` head, update or compound write keeps it open; no direct `eval` in the file); `a || b`, `a ?? b`, `a && b`, `c ? a : b` of such values; and a static member path `o.p` written in the very function that declares `o`, `o` a `const` bound to a closed object literal (no spread, getter, setter, computed or duplicate key) whose own data property `p` holds a made value, every other reference to `o` a static member access that is never called and never writes or deletes `p`, or `return o` of that same function, and no `finally` in it (the straight code of the activation is all that holds `o` until it returns it).
- **Factory**: also through a standard function of `FRESH_FACTORIES`: `Object.create(null)`, `JSON.parse(text)` with no reviver, the target `Object.assign` hands back (its target made), and the first parameter of an inline callback passed with a seed to `R.reduce(callback, seed)` over an array a literal, `Object.keys`/`values`/`entries` or such an array's `sort` made: the seed and every return of the callback made, assuming the parameter made; never written, no default (an `undefined` return would hand on the default), an arrow or a function whose body never names `arguments`. `Object`, `JSON` are the globals no declaration of the file shadows. Such a write is recorded as `Hazard::FreshFactoryWrite(key)`, not `OpenMemberWrite(key)`.

**The premise of the factory form (the first-patch induction).** Take the first moment any factory-form write puts a member on a standard root. Before it, no factory-form write did, so a factory of the list could have been replaced only by a site the rest of the census sees: a spelled patch, an override, a definer, an impostor, or an open write outside the form. Where the program holds none that may reach any factory of the list, every factory call before that moment ran the standard code, so the object that write writes is the made one, and no such first moment exists. The program side asks exactly that: `SemanticLookup::hazard_present(OpenMemberWrite(key))` is also true where some file has `FreshFactoryWrite(key)` and `fresh_factories_intact` fails, i.e. `patch_vetoed` holds for some factory when asked of the census as the files fold it, in which no factory-form write is an open write (`open_member_write_through_factory`). Any doubt keeps every factory-form site an open write; the rows' `fired`, the hazards table's sites (`hazard_sites`) and the row detail (`handed_root_detail`) then list them as open writes again. The writers (`StandardImpostorWrite`) a factory-form write adds are kept: the form claims no more than this formula needs. "A non-callable value puts no function" is not a proof here (a number written over `Number.isFinite` makes the call throw).

*Evidence.* Unit test `a_write_is_open_unless_its_object_is_proven_made` (each form beside the shape that keeps it open: a holder handed to a call, a path rebound in place or written in a closure or through a computed member, a `let` assigned a parameter, a reviver, `Object.assign` of a parameter, `Object.create` of a parameter, a shadowed `Object`, a `reduce` over a parameter, an accumulator with a default or returning something else) and `a_direct_eval_keeps_the_binding_forms_open`. Fixtures `fresh-written-object` (the router's six shapes, `Number` handed on: `Number.isFinite` certified, was `standard-member-impostor`), `-factory-patched` (`JSON.parse` replaced: the factory sites open again), `-shadowed` (a local `Object`), `-escaped` (the member path's holder handed to a call): each keeps the row. Fuzz: five adversarial seam forms (`seam-shapes.mjs`: `pathescaped`, `pathrebound`, `letrebound`, `reviver`, `reduceforeign`), each writing through an object that looks made but is the helper's parameter, in the `bseam-isfinite`/`then`/`settimeout` pairs (misuse: the member replaced, Chrome warns; `-other`: legal).

*Measured* (release; main c2779cb39 against this change; rc.21 frozen corpus, all 34 projects). Development build: 212 violations in both, uncertifiable 267,231 to 257,244 (-9,987), nothing for a look (no violation added, lost or turned). `standard-member-impostor` 41,659 to 34,195 (-7,464), in the 14 tsconfigs whose only open writes were the router's (kui's 9, expenses-app, helge-dev, jar-hell-web, sensor-sim, spookysoftware-www); the rows the lifted veto had shadowed follow as their own rules' (SC9012 `handed-member-dispatch` -742, `parameter-use-unmodeled` -547, SC2002 `package-may-call-action` -127, …), and 254 rows appear at sites the withheld call held (SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` +177 and `unresolved-invocation` +36, SC1001 `package-value-read` +13, others ≤5): uncertifiable either way, now each under the rule whose walk reaches the site. The production-build run gave the same bytes, as main's own did on these projects. Boundary scan (checker alone): the five new forms, 180 programs, and every `bseam` form, 396 programs: no misuse cell silent, no legal cell reported. Not run: Chrome on the new forms (their misuse is JavaScript's own: each writes the root), left to the bundle's full measurement.

<a id="adr-1020"></a>
## ADR 1020 — A closure an effect's or a memo's compute returns is not proven to run
*A false positive on main (c2779cb39).* `createEffect(() => () => { createMemo(async () => 1, { sync: true }); }, (v) => { void v; })` was an SC7002 violation: the compute returns the closure, the runtime hands it to the apply as `v`, and nothing calls it (Chrome rc.21: no diagnostic, the site never executes; the judge classes it `unexecuted`). Reach analysis took a function literal to run whenever the function around it does. The full audit 43739577046 held 120 such rows in `lg-recall`'s `apply-void-value-row` and `-untrack` contexts (W3's scan of every `unexecuted` violation; W3 confirmed two in Chrome on 993e83f74).

*Decision.* `site_reach.rs` `returned_by_primitive_callback`: a function literal returned (an arrow's expression body or a `return`'s argument) by a callback at a position whose return the runtime hands on as a value and never calls, not called where it is written, makes the reach query undecided (ADR 0560's bound): a violation there is `site-reach-undecided`, an obligation stays, nothing becomes clean (owner's ruling 2026-11-17). The position is a new dialect question, `Dialect::callback_return_is_value(primitive, argument)`; Solid 2 answers it for argument 0 of `createEffect`, `createRenderEffect` and `createMemo` (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.21` `dist/types/signals.d.ts`: the compute's value goes to the apply, or is the memo's value). A cleanup an apply returns is called by the runtime and is not this: a first form that asked only for a primitive's callback took back 3 Chrome-confirmed violations in a cleanup an apply returns (`effect-cleanup-dispose`, `render-cleanup-rerun`), so the question is per argument.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/returned-closure-unrun`: SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC at a sync memo written directly is `covered-violation` on both builds; the closure an effect's compute returns (plain and under `untrack`) and a memo's value nothing calls are silent in Chrome, `static-only` violations on main and uncertifiable here. Fixture `returned-closure-unrun`.

*Narrowed after #271's smoke census (run 44013489276: 6 proved violations of the `apply-void-call` family lost, MISSING_EFFECT_FN and STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER, Chrome-agreed).* There the apply calls the value (`void v()`), so the closure runs. `returned_value_never_called`: the closure is withheld only where its value is provably never called: the apply (the next argument, a function literal) has no first parameter or uses it only as the operand of `void`, uncalled (`void v`); or a memo's result is discarded, or a `const` every reference of which is called with no argument and that call only read by `void` or `typeof`. Anything else (`v()`, `void v()`, `m()()`, a value handed on) may run, as on main. Probe of 1,732 programs (every `apply-void-call` program of every code and grid, 1,132, and 600 seeded `apply-void-value`): main c2779cb39 against the narrowed rule moves only 30 legal `apply-void-value` programs, violation to `site-reach-undecided`; against ADR 1020's first form, 292 misuse programs retain restored violations (STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER 288, MISSING_EFFECT_FN 4); four apparent SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC restorations were rejected by Chrome (PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK throws first). The 292 include all six census regressions. Fixture positives `AppliedVoidCall` and `AppliedVoidCallUntrack` (SC7001, Chrome `covered-violation`).

*Third cut (replaces a second narrowing that asked the ownerless effect-phase walk for a concrete origin).* That guard read the closure's text and the walk's found origin, so it was fail-open: a memo's value read by an effect's compute and called in the apply, `untrack(m)()` in an apply, a helper or a nested function the returned closure calls each kept a proved SC7002 where Chrome rc.21 reports only PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK (5 probes; the walk finds no origin there, so "no origin" decided nothing). Now the site's reach answers it: per function, a fourth query (`SiteReach::withholding_returned_values`, run only where the plain query met a returned value) withholds every value a compute returns, as the first cut did. A site the plain query runs and that one does not (or leaves undecided) is `UnreachedSite::returned_value_run`: it runs only through a call of such a value, which may be on an apply's stack, where creating a computation throws first. Only SC7002 reads it (`creation-throws-first`); every other claim reads the site as reached, so the 292 restored violations stay. A sync memo created in a returned value called in the component body (SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC in Chrome) stays uncertifiable, as under the first cut. Fixture `ReturnedAndCalled`, `MemoValueCalledInApply`, `HelperCalledInApply`, `MemoValueCalledInBody`; Chrome rc.21 matches each.

*Fourth cut (Fable's review of 14434c30f).* A site in a callback of a computation created inside the returned value (`createMemo(() => { createEffect(() => 1, undefined) })` in a closure the apply calls) was a proved violation of any rule but SC7002: Chrome rc.21 throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at the creation and the callback never runs (SC7001 `static-only` in Chrome; SC2008 at a `flush()` in a created effect's apply likewise). `UnreachedSite::returned_value_creation`: with `returned_value_run`, a function on the lexical path from the site up to the returned value is a callback of any dialect primitive (`untrack` included, whether the release says its creation throws or not: fail closed). Every rule reads it (`creation-throws-first`), SC2008 included. Fixture `CreatedInReturnedMemo`, `CreatedInReturnedEffect`. Probe of the same 1,968 programs: no change against the third cut (288 restored, 0 legal violations). Found, not this ADR's: a sync memo created directly in an apply (`createEffect(() => 0, () => { createMemo(async () => 1, { sync: true }) })`) is a proved SC7002 on main where Chrome reports only PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, and the oracle scores that site `covered-violation` without comparing codes (docs/open-work.md).

*Not covered* (docs/open-work.md): a value a compute returned that program code does call is now followed only in those forms; any other use keeps ADR 0458's "may run".

*Measured* (release, main c2779cb39 against this change; per-fix probe, owner's rule 2026-11-17): W3's 120 programs: all move violation to `site-reach-undecided`; a 2,000-program probe (600 programs of the `apply-void-value` contexts and a fixed-seed sample of the rest, legal included): 0 moved. One fixture moves with it: `fp-owner-nested-async-read` line 23 (`ReturnedAsyncClosure`, the async closure `createMemo(() => async () => …)` returns, never called) was an SC1002 violation on main, `static-only` in Chrome rc.21 (nothing reported there) and listed by the fixture's own README as a negative; it is `site-reach-undecided` here, named in `scripts/guard/regress.json`. The full grid and the corpus run once on the batch.
