## ADR 1022 — A construct-only local class places its members at their `new` or receiver call
A class element's code has no call edge, so every net called it unplaced (ADRs 0516, 0538, 0673, 0715): `class K { m() { r(); } } new K().m();` in a component body was `function-run-unplaced` while Chrome reports it, the largest recall family of G1 after the impostor receivers (`pos-class-*`). A class is *construct-only* (`execution_role/construct_only.rs`) when it is bound to a name (its own, or a `const`) that is not exported; it has no `extends`, decorator or computed key; its text names no `this`, `super` or `arguments`; the file runs no built code; and every reference to the name is the callee of one `new`. That `new` must be written after the class, in the body of the same function, outside JSX and in no class, and that function must be neither async nor a generator. Its constructor and the instance field initializers run at that `new`; a plain method that is the only element under its key runs at a call made directly on that `new` (`new K().m()`, through a cast too). The run is a statement of the function the class is written in, on its stack, under its owner and tracking context, so code written directly in the member takes the role that function's own code has: the class-member nets (`unplaced_run`, `runs_implicitly`, `inside_class_member`, `inside_instance_field`, `in_field_initializer`) stand down for it; `inside_non_component_function` takes the placed member as the enclosing body's code; and the timing walk (`callee_callback_timing`), the stored-literal walk (`runs_in_unproven_stored_literal`) and the write walk (`write_role_walk`) move from the member to its run as they move from an IIFE to its call.
Only code written directly in the member is placed. A closure, IIFE or helper's callback written inside one, and a field initializer holding any function, keep their obligation: the caller walks would climb from the inner function to the member and place it, while the summaries do not follow a call held in a class (`body_site_runs_during_call`), so the site would lose its row with no claim made anywhere (a first version that climbed went U→clean on 1,214 misuse programs, `closure` and `wrapper` layers). Nothing placed means nothing changes: a method no receiver call runs, a class never constructed (the owner's ruling of 2026-11-17, ADR 1021), two constructions, `this`, a run in a handler, in JSX or in another function, a computed member call and a shadowing parameter stay `function-run-unplaced`.
*Measured* (main 993e83f74 against this build, release, the 50,552 `pos-class-*` programs of mx-recall and lg-recall, checker alone): misuse U→V 7,371 (REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE 3,434, ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE 1,247, ON_FLUSH_IN_OWNED_SCOPE 1,132, STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED 1,119, STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER 439), nothing else moved: no V→U, no U→clean, and none of the 2,984 legal programs moved (they stay U: the legal cells are `onCleanup` in a member, which the owner walk does not place). Chrome rc.21 (`focus.mjs --runtime-diff all`): 200 moved programs, 40 per code, each compared with Chrome: 194 agree, 0 behaviour or attribution differences; the 6 others are STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER programs whose new violation is the strict read beside the store write (corroborated) while the store write's own row stays uncertifiable. Fixtures: `read-in-place-layers-summary`'s `ClassCtorWrapper` and `ClassMethodHookResult` (construct-only, rc.17 warns) go from uncertifiable to violations; `handed-call-results`' field `f = props.f` of a construct-only class keeps its row under the read's own blocker (`read-backing-unproven`). Oracle case `construct-only-class`: STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED, REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE (twice) and ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at the four placed members each `covered-violation`, the unplaced ones `covered-uncertifiable`, 0 typing errors. Fixture `construct-only-class`. Not done: the 11,348 `pos-class-*` programs whose site is in a layer inside the member (above), and the owner walk (`onCleanup`).

## ADR 1027 — The hazard table names where ADR 0803's slot withdrawal fires
`tuple-iteration-written` (SC9012, formula `array-slots-withdrawn`) named its two hazards, `VisibleIterationWrite` and `TupleSlotIterationMayBeMutated`, with no sites: on the rc.21 corpus it held 15,956 development rows in 30 of 34 projects, and no report said which file fired it. Each disjunct is now listed at the place its census decides it (`blocked_by.rs` `tuple_iteration_sites`), with a `cause`: a write or call `visible_iteration_write` finds (`visible-write`); a direct `eval` (`eval`); a place `intrinsic_census` finds an intrinsic or code from a string obtained (`intrinsic-obtained`); a call or a window-valued value `handed_to_unseen_code` finds handed to unseen code (`intrinsic-handed`, `window-handed`). Diagnostics only: the verdict is still the lookup's whole-program answer. The census functions became lazy site iterators whose first item is their old answer, asked in the same order with the same pushes (`intrinsic_obtained_sites` with `all` false takes one); the table asks the rest of each file with a throwaway call list, so no census entry changes. A site is a place that alone fires the hazard; a fired id with an empty list would be a census the table does not read (the process test asserts none on its fixture). Fixtures `tuple-hazard-sites` (one file per census) and its shadowed twin (local `Function`, `Array`, `window`; an iterator key on the file's own literal: no hazard). No defect, so no rediscovery entry. *Measured* in the commit message.

## ADR 1025 — A route definition's `component` an audited `@solidjs/router` renders is entered by a render under an owner
ADR 0970 made every reference of a component other than a JSX tag an entry the owner graph holds no edge for, naming "a router's `component={Home}`" among them, so an owner operation in a route component kept an uncertifiable SC4001 `owner-callers-unenumerated` row. ADR 0335 already reads, for the component census only, the route definitions of `createRouter({ routes })` that an audited release renders. This is the package half of the proof batch's first item (docs/open-work.md) for that router, read from its bytes as ADR 0992 read Solid's own components.

*The reading* (`@solidjs/router@2.0.0-next.41`, digest `cec58599…cefcef`; the premises of ADR 0335, unchanged). `createRoutes` copies a definition's `component` into the route record (`dist/routing.js:369-375`) and nothing calls it; `createRouteContext` renders it as `createComponent(component, routeProps)` in the route's `outlet` (`:862-906`), which `Routes` calls in a keyed `Show`'s child under `RouteContextObj` (`dist/routers/components.jsx:157-163`), the route contexts made in `runWithOwner(createOwner(), () => createRoot(…))` (`:63-95`), under `Root` and `RouterContextObj` where the project writes `<Router>` (`dist/routers/factory.jsx:283-289`). The router's other reads of the value are `component?.preload?.()` (under the route's root, no render) and the `SERVER_ROUTE` brand (`serverRouteOf`, rendered through `server.render`).

*Decision.* `owners/owner_emission.rs`: in `entered_by_tags_only`, a reference, in the function's file or another, that is such a route value (`SemanticLookup::solid_router_component_value`, the `@solidjs/router` half of ADR 0335's values alone: TanStack's are not read here) enters the function by a render, as a tag does; and an inline arrow written as one (`routed_inline`) is entered by that render alone. Only a bare function binding every reference of which is a tag or a route value qualifies, so a `.preload` or brand write (`(Home as any).preload = …`, `Object.assign(Home, …)`) is a reference no render accounts for and keeps the entry open; a call's result (`serverRouteComponent(…)`, `lazy(…)`, `protect(Home)`) is no function of the program's and is not read. Every stop the walk had stands before it (a generator, direct `eval`, an export in an open program or one a namespace hands out: ADR 0970's B2 and R1-R3). The claim is "rendered under an owner" and nothing more: it closes open owner entries; no violation is reported at a route's mount (a route renders only when the URL matches; ADR 1026 takes that question).

*Evidence.* Fixture `route-entries` (published router bytes, as `route-config`): `Layout`, the nested `Nested` and an inline arrow lose their row; `Shared` (also handed to `setTimeout`) and `Preloaded` (its `preload` written) keep it, and so does `Home`, exported to the route table's module (an export in an open program). Variants `route-entries-shadowed` (a local `createRouter`) and `route-entries-namespace` (a namespace import, which ADR 0335 refuses) keep it. `route-config` and its `next26` and `use-action-kept` variants: their route components' SC4001 rows go (15 rows, U to gone; no violation moved). Chrome (rc.21, the oracle's installed router): case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/route-entry-owner`, the route table in its own module, a parent and an inline child route matched by `*`: both render (each body read fires STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED, the render witness) and their `onCleanup` fires no NO_OWNER_CLEANUP. The oracle's entry enumerates `App.tsx` as a namespace, so the checker keeps its rows there (fail closed).

*Measured* (release; main c2779cb39 against this change; the 12 route-table apps of the rc.21 frozen corpus, 23 tsconfigs, development build; the owner's measurement ruling): 182 violations in both, uncertifiable 221,359 to 221,303: 56 SC4001 `owner-callers-unenumerated` rows gone (donegeon-client 53, jar-hell-web 3), nothing else moved, nothing for a look. Most corpus route components are exported page modules, which stay open while the program is.

## ADR 1023 — A member call on a closed object literal dispatches to its method, whatever its type says
Part of G1 (`function-run-unplaced`). `const t = { then(f) { f(); } }; (t as unknown as Promise<void>).then(() => { setW(1); })` was SC2001 uncertifiable (`function-run-unplaced`, plus the call's SC9012 `standard-member-impostor`), though the same call without the assertion is a proved violation and Chrome reports REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE. The impostor census (ADR 0840, ADR 0874) withholds the standard `Promise.prototype.then` the type names, and `layer_run` asked the standard resolution before anything else, so the callback was `Withheld`: no run at all. The object-member index (ADR 0299) already resolves that member to the literal's own function: the receiver is a `const` identifier under TypeScript wrappers, bound to the literal; every use of it is a member it calls; the literal is closed, has no accessor and no method that spells `this`, `arguments` or `super`; no assignment writes the member's name.
*The change.* `execution_role::closed_literal_dispatch` (`callback_standing.rs`): the index resolves the call's member, the member is not computed, and ADR 1014's and ADR 1009's literal checks hold as well: the property is the key's final value (`property_is_final_value`: no later spread, unnamed key or same key), no member of the holder is assigned (`holder_member_assigned`) or written by an unnamed key (`holder_written_by_unnamed_key`), and no function of the literal hands its receiver on (`literal_hands_its_receiver_on`). Such a call is no standard call to `layer_run` (the helper arm reads the literal's method: `helper_argument_run`, so a method that calls its argument on every completion runs it in place, one that hands it to `queueMicrotask` or a timer runs it elsewhere), nor to `handed_to_withheld_call`, and the pipeline's list of withheld calls leaves it out (no census row, no withheld start or callee). Every other reader of `standard_call_withheld` (after-await, owners, the interprocedural graph, upstream compatibility) still withholds the standard resolution: only placement through the literal's method is new.
*Refused, uncertifiable as before* (fixture variants, each its own project): `Object.assign(t, { then: … })` or any other escape of the literal, a getter, a spread or an unnamed key after the method, `t.then = …` or any member written after the literal, a `this` handed on, a `let`, a literal read through a module namespace, an alias (`const q = t as unknown as Promise<void>`), a `t` shadowed inside a nested block, a module-level receiver.
*Measured* (release; main c2779cb39 against this build). A sample of 1,844 of the 48,100 grid programs of the `cast-*` contexts, stratified by grid, code and context (mx-recall 43,848, lg-recall 3,732, mx-census 520; legal included): 420 moved, 0 violation lost, 0 legal violation, at the site 70 uncertifiable to violation. The harness with Chrome on the 420 (`focus.mjs --runtime-diff all`, ids per grid, both builds): nothing needs a look on either, 404 compared, 0 behaviour, 0 attribution, 0 inconclusive; mx-recall recall-gap 201 to 131 and agree 0 to 70 (REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, `cast-then` and `cast-any-then`); mx-census recall-gap 18 to 14, agree 9 to 13 (ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE and ON_FLUSH_IN_OWNED_SCOPE); lg-recall `cast-late-foreach` clean 3 to 27, the rest uncertifiable. Fixture `closed-literal-dispatch`: six violations (a method, a method under `as any`, an arrow member, a read through `forEach`, a method forwarding to a helper, a method that also keeps its argument), two clean twins that hand the callback to a microtask; Chrome rc.21, oracle case `closed-literal-dispatch`: the six diagnostics are `covered-uncertifiable` on main and `covered-violation` on this build, the twins quiet.
*Not covered* (stay uncertifiable): an alias, a slot path (`t.p.then`), a returned literal (`mk().then`), a single caller's argument (`run(t as any, f)`), the families `cast-held-then`, `cast-nested`, `cast-return`, `cast-param`, `cast-any-param`; they need the ADR 0299 census to follow the literal through those forms. STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED's `cast-then` grid programs keep their row under another blocker.

<a id="adr-1026"></a>
## ADR 1026 — A route component throws where its route renders: a conditional render, reported at the mount
**The ruling.** Owner, 2026-11-17: a route component counts as a conditional render, as `<Show when={x()}><C /></Show>` does, so a violation is reported at its mount; preload-only reach, a `SERVER_ROUTE`/server render, and a non-literal or mutated route table stay uncertifiable. ADR 1025 claimed only the owner; ADR 0893's stored-throw walk read a route table's value as "nothing here reads the mount" (handled: `computation-error-unobserved`), and a route component with no binding (an inline arrow) had no mount it found, so an empty mount list reported, whatever stood above the `<Router>`.

*Decision.* `stored_throw.rs` `route_mount_tags`/`definition_mounts`: where the walk meets a reference that is a route definition's `component` an audited `@solidjs/router` renders (ADR 1025's `solid_router_component_value`, ADR 0335's premises), the component mounts where its route renders (`createRouteContext`'s outlet, ADR 1025's reading):
- a definition written as an element of the `routes` array literal of `createRouter({ routes: [...] })` renders at each `<Router>` tag of the instance (a `const` every reference of which, in any analyzed file, is a JSX tag name, an import or an export of it, or its declaration);
- one written in a parent definition's `children` array literal renders where the parent's component reads `props.children` (the route props' `children` getter calls `outlet()`), each read written in a JSX element's child, the parent an inline arrow or a function of the file nothing rebinds whose first parameter is a plain name only read through static members; a parent with no `component` renders the child where its own route renders.

The throw is reported unless a boundary above every such site takes it (`route_mount_end`, `route_tags_handled`, `handled_above`, as ADR 1016 asks of a `dynamic` tag); a throw only under an observer stays open; only the sites reach analysis says may run count (ADRs 0458, 1015, 1018). The same reading answers `mounts_handled` for such a value (in place of "handled"), and for a binding-less component that is a route value: its route's sites, or, where the reading refuses, handled (never a report from an empty mount list). Kept uncertifiable: a table held in a binding or built by `defineRoute(s)` (ADR 0335 reads them; this reading does not), a parent that hands its props on (`<Frame {...props} />`) or reads `children` anywhere but a JSX child, an instance no tag renders. Preload-only reach and the server brand are outside by construction: a route definition's `preload` is no `component` value, and `serverRouteComponent(…)` and `lazy(…)` are calls, no function of the program's (`serverRouteComponent` wraps its source and never brands it, `dist/serverRouteComponent.js:60-90`).

*Evidence.* Fixture `route-mount-throw` (published router bytes): violations `First`, the inline `/second`, the nested `Child` and inline `/child-inline`; uncertifiable `Guarded` and the inline `/guarded-inline` (an `<Errored>` with a handling fallback above the only tag), `CaughtChild` (its parent wraps `props.children` in one), `HandedChild` (its parent spreads its props), `Held` (a table held in a binding), `Unmounted`. Chrome (rc.21, the oracle's installed router next.41; each case renders by name, because the default entry's namespace read of `App.tsx` withholds ADR 0335's premise, and its pass over every element clicks the route's link: the navigation): `runtime-oracle/route-mount-throw` (the initial route) and `route-mount-navigate` (`/second`, after the navigation) `covered-violation`; `route-mount-nested` (`/parent/child-inline`, after the navigation) `covered-violation`; `route-mount-guarded` quiet, uncertifiable. An uncaught throw halts the reactive system (REACTIVITY_HALTED), so each throwing route has a case of its own. Main (c2779cb39) on the same four: `route-mount-throw` covered-uncertifiable, `-guarded` **static-only** (the binding-less default above: a false positive, Chrome silent; rediscovery.json, `outside`: the grids hold no router), `-navigate` and `-nested` covered-violation.

*Measured* (release; main 1b03e7db9 against this branch, ADR 1025 under it; the 12 route-table apps of the rc.21 frozen corpus, 23 tsconfigs, development build, the owner's measurement ruling): 182 violations in both, uncertifiable 221,348 to 221,292: ADR 1025's 56 SC4001 rows, nothing of this ADR's (no plain throw in a corpus route component), nothing for a look.

<a id="adr-1031"></a>
## ADR 1031 — A project component's getter is placed at its reads when every read runs under the render's owner
A component element's children, or a prop's value, are a getter that runs where the component reads the prop (ADR 0971, the review of #225, F2), so every creation written there kept SC3001's and SC6002's rows (`getter-runs-where-read`): about 47% of those sites in the corpus (Mac 23's brief, P2). `owners::getter_read_sites` (`owners/jsx_sites.rs`) answers where such a getter runs when that is exact: the element has no spread, and its tag resolves to one function whose binding holds it now, in no package (not dependency source, not bundled, no package root), neither async nor a generator, taking at most one parameter, a plain identifier with no default. Every reference to that parameter must be a non-computed member read that is not written to, or the whole argument 0 of an exact `omit` whose other arguments are string literals, bound to a `const` used only as the spread of intrinsic elements (the spreads read every prop not omitted). The props object then never escapes. Every read of the prop must run on the component's own stack under its render's owner: directly in the body, outside every class, or in JSX written there whose every element is intrinsic or renders what it is handed in place (`renders_in_place`: a dialect control-flow element, a context provider), or directly in the function that is argument 0 of an exact `children` call written that way. There must be at least one read. The owner-call pass (`owners/leaf_universe.rs`) then asks each read, as code written there, the questions it asks any site (`Question::answer`, factored out of the loop unchanged: module scope, an unread package, the census, a plain site, the role engine, the owner graph), and a group of codes ends only where every read that may run ends it, on the premises of all of them (each in the file it is about). A read ADR 0458 proves unreached runs nothing; a getter no read runs keeps its rows (ADR 1021's ruling). The counterexample stays a row: a read in an effect's apply (`createEffect(open, o => { if (o) render(() => p.children) })`, Chrome rc.21 PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK), as does any read in a nested function (a handler, a timer, a leaf owner's callback), a props object handed on, destructured or spread anywhere but an intrinsic element, and a package's component.
*Measured.* Fixture `owner-call-getter-placed`: `InJsx`, `InBody`, `ViaHelper`, `SlotInJsx`, `ThroughShow` and `Spreads` lose their two rows; `OnApply`, `InLeaf`, `InHandler`, `Escapes`, `Destructured`, `SpreadOmits`, `SpreadEscapes` and `Ignores` keep them. Chrome rc.21, oracle case `owner-call-getter-placed`: 0 typing errors; nothing at the placed getters; PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK (`ByApply`) and PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE (`ByLeaf`) covered by uncertifiable rows. Coverage: seven existing fixtures lose 34 rows, all SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted` and SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted` at getters of project components read in intrinsic JSX or a `Loading` (`stored-throw-wrapper-boundary` 14, `loading-cover-children` 8, `async-creation-pass` 4, `owner-call-jsx-getter`'s `InBody` and `portal-children-owner`'s project `Portal`, both former named costs, `dead-literal-rows` and `flush-universe-package-hand-off-causes` 2 each); nothing is added and no violation moves. Corpus (rc.21 frozen, the eight projects of the probe, main c2779cb39 against this build, development): 134 uncertifiable rows (67 sites, SC3001 and SC6002 each) leave, in expenses-app (126: getters of `@/lib/clerk`'s `SignInButton`, `SignedOut`-style wrappers and `ui/button`'s `omit` spread) and pekochan-blog (8); 0 violations moved, nothing else moved; the six other projects 0 (ai-memory-ui's getters: 812 decline `getter-runs-where-read` on main, 452 now, the other 360 now decline `unread-package-may-run`). Most corpus getters stay rows: their reads are placed, but the component is reached from one a package renders (a route), so the read declines `unread-package-may-run` (P3's question, ADR 0970), or the props object is handed to a project function (`crumbItems(props)`) or destructured.


<a id="adr-1034"></a>
## ADR 1034 — A site only a replaceable object member runs is not proven to run
The unexecuted guard (ADR 1018) found SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC violations on main at sites Chrome never runs: `lg-sync-node-received-async-dead-bundle-spread-effect-direct-closure` and `-dead-bundle-computed-effect-namespace-module-helper`, ADR 1009's `dead-bundle-*` contexts, where `{ run: () => { … createEffect(async () => 1, apply, { sync: true }) … }, ...extra }` (or `[k]: …` after it) is handed on as `bundle.run` and the spread or computed key replaces the member. ADR 1009's `property_is_final_value` already refuses the bundle placement there, but SC7002 is a static claim (the call's own options and computation) that holds wherever the call runs, and ADR 0458's site reach answered such a member "may run once created".

*The change.* `site_reach.rs` asks a third question beside ADR 0576's lazy one, `SiteReach::proving_final_members`: in it a function written directly as a member value (a data property's value, a method, an accessor) that a later spread, a later key with no static name or a later property of the same key in the same literal may replace (`member_value_may_be_replaced`, on `flow_helpers.rs` `property_is_final_value`) is never entered, and everything only it reaches (a closure it calls, a helper's callback written in it, by the same least fixed point) is not entered either. Where the plain query says the function runs and this one says it never does, the site is `member_may_be_replaced` and a violation there becomes uncertifiable, blocker `member-value-overridden` (`diagnostics.rs`, beside `lazy-compute-unread`). It is "not proven", never "unreached": a spread whose value holds no such key (`SpreadWithoutKey`, Chrome reports) keeps an uncertifiable row, a recall gap named in docs/open-work.md. A spread or computed key before the member, a plain member and a later key of a nested literal leave the member final: unchanged violations.

*Evidence.* Fixture `sync-option-overridden-member` (five replaceable shapes: spread, computed key, a method with a closure, a namespace call in a module helper's callback, a spread without the key, and the `onSettled` fuzz shape; four final-member violations). Chrome rc.21, oracle case `fixtures/runtime-oracle/sync-option-overridden-member`: SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC at the four violations (`covered-violation`) and at `SpreadWithoutKey` (`covered-uncertifiable`), silent at the replaced ones. *Measured* in the commit message.

## ADR 1032 — Edit latency: three hot spots of the retained daemon's answer after an edit, findings byte-identical
**The cost.** On app-game (1,611 files, the W VM, release) after #270's handed-root speedup, a code edit to the retained daemon took 6.9 s and a cold analysis 13.8 s. A profile of the daemon during the edit named three hot spots in turn.
**The changes.** (1) The disposal-handle climb (`execution_role/cleanup_handle.rs`: `cleanup_handle`, `named_disposal_registration`) scanned every identifier of the file, with a binary search each, for the references of one declaration at every climb step (20% of the edit's self time in `reference_declaration`); it reads `AstFacts::reference_identifiers_to`, the index that yields exactly what that scan yielded. (2) `package_action_calls` (SC2002's sites, 45% of the edit) decided each call, tag and read site's role on one thread; the decisions (`site_decision`: unreached, role allows, reports) are computed on the analysis workers and applied in the files' and the sites' order, so the rows and the site ends are written as before. (3) That exposed lock contention in the span index's remembered flags (`AstSpanIndex::flag`, one `RwLock` for every per-declaration answer, `binding_written_by` among them: atomic acquire was 52% of self time); the flags are sharded over 64 locks by key.
**Measured.** app-game, release, W VM, main 1b03e7db9 against this change: the daemon's code edit 6.9 s to 3.0 s, a cold analysis 13.8 s to 7.9 s; the 81,024 findings byte-identical to main's after each step. Coverage (1,318 fixture projects) moves nothing.
**Next.** The write-role walk under `package_action_calls` (`place_sites`, `region_fold`) is still about half of the edit's CPU, now spread over the workers; the hottest flags still contend on their shard (`binding_written_by` through `function_value_is_current_in`, about 5%).

## ADR 1040 — ADR 0803's visible scan reads every target only where a hand-off is rejected; fresh arrays and made objects are separate
`tuple-iteration-written` (SC9012) fired on `VisibleIterationWrite` wherever any IntrinsicHandedAtCall census entry of the window or an array intrinsic existed, seen or not: `iteration_intrinsic_handed` counted every entry, so an unknown-key write on a target not proven separate (the router's `params[key]`, `handedBack[d]`, `result[key]`; `out[i]` of `new Array(n)`) withdrew every tuple slot even where every hand-off reached seen code.

*Decision* (`accessor_provenance/mutation_sites.rs`). (b) `iteration_intrinsic_handed` counts only an entry `received_by_seen_code` rejects (a call the file no longer holds counts). The check is asked under `refusing_scan_deferral`: `handed_on` then records a reflective mutator's intrinsic target (`Object.assign(p, s)`, `Reflect.set(p, k, f)`, `reflective_target`), which it otherwise leaves to this scan, as a hand-off to the mutator, which is no seen code. So the cut reads the strictly weaker census (the one that holds with `handed` true at every write the check defers) and never its own answer: the check reads the hazards, resolution and the files, not this scan. A seen receiver hands the value on to nothing, and writes through it under a key that may reach iteration (or a handler key on the window) are rejections already. (a) `fresh_global_array`: an array literal, `new Array(n)`, `Array(n)`, `Array.from(…)` (standard declaration, global `Array` unshadowed, and `Array`, the called function and for `from` the constructor intact per `standard_member_intact`), through `const` or never-written `let` (no direct `eval`) aliases, is separate. (c) ADR 1024's `fresh_written_object` is separate too: `Made` always, `Factory` while `fresh_factories_intact` holds, asked of the full hazard census (never weaker than ADR 1024's raw one).

*Evidence.* Variants of `iteration-written-slots`: `handed-seen-open-write` (b), `fresh-array-define`, `fresh-array-from-define` (a), `fresh-object-let-next`, `fresh-object-create-next` (c) go from uncertifiable to proved SC2001; `fresh-array-define-shadowed`, `-define-replaced`, `fresh-object-create-proto-next` and the hand-back `handed-seen-relay-back` (seen code hands the window to a callback parameter that patches the iterator) stay uncertifiable. The first build asked the check without the refusal, and `handed-assign-open`, `-assign-source` and `-reflect-set` (a helper's `Object.assign`/`Reflect.set` on its `Array.prototype` parameter) became violations; with it they hold. Chrome (rc.21): `iteration-fresh-targets` covered-violation, `iteration-relay-back` quiet, `iteration-seen-window-reads` (the shapes of the 4 SC1001 sites kui regained) covered-violation at each STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED.

*Measured* (release, sc VM, frozen rc.21 corpus, 34 projects; fed4aa902 against this change; development and production alike): `tuple-iteration-written` rows 15,977 to 13,998 (helge-dev 17, jar-hell-web 84, six kui projects 1,850, sensor-sim 23, spookysoftware-www 5 to 0; in each the router's 11 visible-write sites were the only cause). (a) and (b) alone gave all of it; (c) moved no row and takes 93 more visible-write sites off the hazard table (1,606, 1,495, 1,402). Violations 212 to 230 (U to V: SC8015 14 at four sites, a style rule no runtime reports: kui's BarChart.tsx:214 and LineChart.tsx:240 in six kui projects (feature-alerts, -clusters, -connect, -ksql, -schemas, -topics; still uncertifiable in feature-consumers, feature-messages and shell, already a violation in kernel), and sensor-sim's LoginForm.tsx:38 and UserAddForm.tsx:30; SC1001 4, Chrome above), none lost; 11 (project, rule) places newly uncertifiable, each a relabel of the file's tuple row (corpus-changes.json). A what-if run (`--assume OpenMemberWrite(*) ReflectiveDefinition(*)`) takes viviana-ui-web from 726 rows to 0 and ai-memory-ui to 2,189 (its test file writes `matchMedia`); neither moves with open writes alone. A precision gain, no defect: no rediscovery entry.

## ADR 1042 — A call under a label, in a finalizer, in a `do` body, or in a loop whose first test is true runs at least once
**The gap** (brief A, R1, 2026-11-17; audit run 43739577046). `every_unconditional_call` (ADR 0714) and the sibling walks (`synchronously_unconditional_calls`, `first_step_unconditional_calls`) admit a call only through the exactly-once whitelist of `evaluates_child_once`, whose last arm refuses every loop, label, `try` and `switch`. The six recall layers that wrap a site in one (`for`, `while`, `do`, `switch`, `try-finally`, `label`) each lost the same 178 misuse rows to `recall-gap` against their `none` siblings, at no legal cost.

*Decision.* `solid-facts` `unconditional_calls.rs`: the walks take a `Mode`. `unconditional_calls` (exactly once, the producer's whitelist, ADR 0161) keeps `ExactlyOnce`; the three walks above take `AtLeastOnce`, which also admits a label's body, a `try`'s finalizer, the block of a `try` with no `catch`, a `do` body, the body of a `while` or `for` whose first test the existing truthiness fold decides true (or a `for` with no test), a `for`'s initializer and first test, a `while`'s first test, and a `for … in`/`of` object (`evaluates_child_at_least_once`). Every reader of that mode asks whether the call runs, never how often: the owner graph's edges (`owner_discovery.rs`, ADR 0714), a leaf scope's reach (`cleanup.rs` `reached_on_every_call`), a rerun's read (`write_roles.rs` `effect_provably_reruns`) and an apply's guaranteed read (`read_context.rs`), read before the change. The premise is ADR 0714's, unchanged: an earlier call completes, and only a written `return`, `break`, `continue` or (for the synchronous walks) `throw` leaves; an earlier exit inside the admitted statement is refused by its block as before (a `break` that leaves only an inner loop is still counted: an over-count, slice 3).

*Evidence.* Unit tests `at_least_once_admits_labels_finalizers_do_bodies_and_entered_loops` (each form, and the exactly-once walk unchanged on all of them; every counterexample of the brief stays out: an early `break outer`, the handler arm, a finalizer that may return first, `do` with an early `break`, `do {} while (call())`, a counter `for`, a `for … of` body, `while (c)`, `while (true)` with an early `continue`, the update clause) and `every_unconditional_call_reads_at_least_once`. Fixture `unconditional-structural`: nine NO_OWNER_CLEANUP (SC4001) violations (label, finalizer, `try` with no `catch`, `do`, `while (true)`, `for (;;)`, a labelled loop, a finalizer beside a `catch`, a label in a finalizer), eight counterexamples uncertifiable; `LabelRead` stays uncertifiable (an SC1001 read through a function summary is placed by the Type Facts producer's exactly-once whitelist, untouched). Chrome (rc.21, `runtime-oracle/unconditional-structural`): the nine `covered-violation`, the counterexamples `covered-uncertifiable` (the handler arm never runs), no `static-only`.

*Measured* (release; main 1b03e7db9 against this change, the checker alone on 1,780 programs: the 890 recall-gap programs of the `label`, `try-finally`, `do`, `while` and `for` layers in brief A's join, and 890 `lg-recall` programs of the same layers and codes, picked by hash): misuse, 100 programs per admitted layer move from no violation at the site to a violation (400; Chrome reports each, the audit's `recall-gap`), 76 per layer stay uncertifiable (an SC1001 read through a summary, and paths the slice does not open), the `for` layer (a counter loop, slice 2) moves nothing, no violation lost; legal, no violation at the site in either build.

*Open* (docs/open-work.md): the counter `for` and a literal `switch` (slice 2), a `try` block a `catch` guards and the `EarlyExit` over-count (slice 3), the producer's whitelist (an SC1001 read through a summary), and the zero-run legal twins of the new forms in the generator (a layer must run once for `twins.mjs`).

## ADR 1041 — A write to a function object the program made reaches no standard root (SC9012 `handed-member-dispatch`, `standard-member-impostor`)
The SC9012 `handed-member-dispatch` slot. On the rc.21 corpus (dev, 0a03da1a2) 8,259 distinct rows, 2,780 of which lift only when ADR 0939's handed-root veto is assumed away (what-if build): an open member write anywhere in the program withholds every standard member of its key while a root is handed on, whatever the receiver. A per-project ranking of the open-write sites (the hazards table of an `--internal` run, not the row detail, which names only a program's first site) shows that sites decide per program: app-game holds 735, solid-groove 47, compass-ui 37. Ten tsconfigs are left with only `@solidjs/router` next.41's own keyed writes after ADR 1024, most of them onto a function object the router itself makes.

*Decision.* `fresh_written.rs` (ADR 1024's binding form, **Made**) also counts, by syntax alone:
- a function or arrow expression (`function_literal`; not a method or an accessor): each evaluation makes a new function object, so a write puts an own member on it and on no standard root;
- the name of a function declaration of the file that nothing rebinds (`declared_function`): no write names it (`binding_written`), no other declaration or binding of the file has the name (a second `function` or a `var` would replace it), and no direct `eval` in the file. Hoisting makes the binding hold that object wherever it is read; an importer cannot rebind it, so an exported declaration counts.
With a `const` or a `let` every value of which is such an expression, as ADR 1024 already folds. The shapes: `data/action.js:406-435` (`fn.toString`, `fn[symbol]` on `const fn = function …`), `data/query.js:368-395` (`query.get/set/delete/clear` on `function query`), `routers/factory.jsx:301` (`Object.assign(RouterComponent, …)`). Not covered: `liveQuery.js:67` (`ch.close`, `ch` read from a `Map`) and `preloadRoute.js:39` (a project function's returned literal). A store setter's draft was considered first: in rc.21 `@solidjs/signals` the setter calls `fn(proxy)` (`dist/dev.js:6845`), and the `set` and `defineProperty` traps write `ensurePB(target)` (`dev.js:6672-6720`, `5159-5191`): a clone or an `Object.create` of the backing, which `foldTarget` commits only after `privatizeCommitted` (`5414`, `5195`), with `__proto__` refused; prod is the same (`dist/prod/store/store.js:498, 526, 1825, 1719`). But the setter is exact only through `[s, set] = createStore(…)`, whose slots ADR 0349's iteration census withdraws in app-game (about 12 other sites), so it was not built.

*Evidence.* Unit test `a_write_to_a_function_object_the_program_made_reaches_no_root` (each form, beside a parameter, a `let` assigned a parameter, a rebound declaration, a second declaration, a `var` of the name, a direct `eval`). Fixtures `fresh-written-function` (the router's shapes and unknown-key writes, `Number` handed on: `Number.isFinite` certified, was `standard-member-impostor`), `-parameter`, `-reassigned`, `-shadowed` (each keeps the row). Chrome rc.21, oracle cases `fresh-written-function` (quiet on both builds; the checker's rows 15 to 10, the `Number.isFinite` row gone) and `fresh-written-function-parameter` (the helper handed `Number` replaces `isFinite` with a signal write: REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, `covered-uncertifiable` on both builds).
*Measured* (release; main 0a03da1a2 against this change; rc.21 frozen corpus, 34 projects). Development: uncertifiable 257,877 to 256,980 (-897: 998 rows out, 101 in), violations 212 on both, none moved: `standard-member-impostor` -503, `handed-member-dispatch` -205, `value-to-unresolved-callee` -99, `pending-read-unresolved` -55, …; the rows the lifted veto shadowed follow under their own rules (SC1001 `package-value-read` +61, SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` +20, SC9012 `value-in-carrier` +17). All in kui (shell -225, eight feature packages -65 to -133), jar-hell-web, sensor-sim, expenses-app, spookysoftware-www. Standard: 0 rows moved (242,626 and 218 on both). The what-if prediction (router keys assumed away) was -906 to -983.

## ADR 1046 — A counter loop whose literal bounds pass, and the case a literal `switch` enters, run at least once
Proof A slice 2, on ADR 1042's at-least-once mode. The recall layers `for` (`for (let i = 0; i < 1; i += 1)`) and `switch` (`switch (1 as number) { case 1: {…; break;} }`) lost 178 misuse rows each to `recall-gap`.

*Decision.* `unconditional_calls.rs`, `Mode::AtLeastOnce` only (the exactly-once walk and the producer's whitelist are unchanged), with a literal evaluator (`literal`: a number, a string or a boolean through parentheses and TypeScript's wrappers, a negated number included):
- a `for` body is entered when its initializer declares one binding (`let`, `const`, `var`) bound to a numeric literal and its test compares that name with a numeric literal by `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, `!=` or `!==`, true for those values (`counter_entered`): nothing runs between the initializer and the first test, and in the loop's scope the name is the initializer's binding;
- a `switch`'s discriminant is evaluated once; a case is entered when the discriminant and every case test up to it are literals of one primitive type, none earlier strictly equal to the discriminant, its own strictly equal (`literal_switch_enters`); a statement of that case's consequent runs when no earlier one leaves (a `break` included). A `default`, a case reached by fall-through, a test of another type and any non-literal test are not read.

*Evidence.* Unit test `at_least_once_admits_counter_loops_and_literal_switch_cases` (each form; out: zero-iteration bounds, `break`/`continue` before the call, a non-literal bound, a test on another name, two declarators, a non-literal discriminant or case, a missed case, an earlier equal case, fall-through, `default`, an early `break`, a case of another type; the exactly-once walk takes none). Fixture `unconditional-literal`: five NO_OWNER_CLEANUP (SC4001) violations (counter loops up, three times and down, a numeric and a string `switch`), nine counterexamples uncertifiable. Chrome (rc.21, `runtime-oracle/unconditional-literal`): five `covered-violation`, the counterexamples that run `covered-uncertifiable`, no `static-only`.

*Measured* (release; ADR 1042's build against this change, the checker alone): the 356 recall-gap programs of the `for` and `switch` layers in brief A's join, 100 per layer move from no violation at the site to a violation (200; the audit's `recall-gap`, Chrome reports each), 76 per layer stay uncertifiable as in ADR 1042, none lost; 1,073 `lg-recall` programs of the same layers and codes, no violation at the site in either build.

*Open:* a `try` block a `catch` guards and the `EarlyExit` over-count (slice 3); a counter compared with a `const` bound rather than a literal; fall-through and `default`.

## ADR 1038 — The body of a `for await` runs past its suspension
**The gap.** `createMemo(async () => { for await (const _x of [1]) { setW(1); } })`: the write runs after the loop awaited the iterator's first `next()`, with no owner, so it raises nothing (Chrome), yet the write roles read the body as unplaced (`function-run-unplaced`, uncertifiable), and an owner-requiring call there (`onCleanup`, `createEffect`) was a recall gap. The dominance facts (`dominating_awaits`) model an `await` expression only; a `for await` is an implicit suspension (`AstFacts::implicit_suspensions`) no proof placed.
**The decision.** `body_roles.rs` `dominating_await_before` (and so `follows_dominating_await`, the one proof every role that asks "past an await on every path" reads) also answers the `for await` whose body holds the site, in the same async non-generator function and with nothing between that runs later (`continuation_function`: no closure, JSX, tracked region or field initializer): `for_await_body_suspension` pairs the implicit suspension with the loop statement that starts where it does (a `yield*` or an `await using` starts where no loop does) and takes the rest of the loop after the iterable as its region. ECMAScript `ForIn/OfBodyEvaluation` with `iteratorKind` async awaits `next()` before every body run, so every run of the body follows a suspension. Not changed: code after the loop, a `catch` or `finally` around it (the iterable or `GetIterator` may throw synchronously and reach them unsuspended), the iterable itself, a loop whose `await` is on some path only (`async-loop`), and an async generator's body (its caller may resume it under an owner).
**Evidence.** Fixture `for-await-body`: `WriteInBody` uncertifiable to clean; `WriteInIterable` (the write in the iterable) stays a violation; `WriteInFinally` and `WriteAfterLoop` stay uncertifiable; `CleanupInBody` stays uncertifiable (an exported component's callers are not enumerated). Chrome (`runtime-oracle/for-await-body`): REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at the iterable's write only (covered), NO_OWNER_CLEANUP in the body (covered by the uncertifiable row), nothing at the body's write. Fuzz, the four `*-async-for-await` contexts × every code (lg-recall 23,904 legal programs, mx-recall 25,208): lg-recall 6,366 uncertifiable to clean (the write, action, flush and strict-read codes past the suspension), nothing else; mx-recall 6,993 recall-gap to agree (NO_OWNER_EFFECT, NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY, NO_OWNER_CLEANUP, SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT, 4 UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT), nothing else; no legal program has a new violation and nothing needs a look (Chrome compared 958 programs).

<a id="adr-1043"></a>
## ADR 1043 — A component under `<Portal>` renders in place: its plain throw ends where the Portal's does
**The gap.** `<Portal><C /></Portal>` with `useContext(Bare)` (no provider, no default) in `C`: Chrome reports CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, but the stored-throw walk (ADR 0893, 0937) read the throw as handled (`computation-error-unobserved`, uncertifiable): `element_prop_handled` counts a component element whose prop may be rendered inside a boundary of the component's own as handling it, and any primitive element it does not list (`Portal`) took that arm. R2's L3 scan: 1,178 misuse rows of the six stored-throw codes in the `-m-portal` mount.
**The decision.** Before the primitive arms, `element_prop_handled` asks the dialect's `component_entry` (ADR 0992, read on the rc.21 triple only): a prop the exact Solid component reads only in a computation of its own, under an owner it creates below the element (`ReadTrackedUnderOwner`: `Portal`'s `children`, `createMemo(() => [startMarker, props.children])` under `runWithOwner(createOwner(), ...)`, `web.dev.js:2389-2396`), is rendered in place: the throw is not handled at the element, and the walk goes on to the elements and boundaries above it (an `Errored` above the Portal takes it, uncertifiable as before). Not read so: an element with a spread (it may replace `children`), a site in a function written between the element and the child (it runs where the component calls it), any other prop (`mount` is read again in the render effect's apply), a project component named `Portal` (the tag resolves to the declaration).
**Evidence.** Fixture `stored-throw-portal`: SC4002 uncertifiable to violation at `InPortal`, `InNamespacePortal` (`<Web.Portal>`) and `InCalledChild` (`{make()}` in the children, evaluated by the memo); `UnderBoundary` (an `Errored` above), `InSpread`, `InMount` stay uncertifiable. A function child (`{() => <C />}`) is a type error against the published typings (`children: JSX.Element`), so it is tsc's, not a case. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/stored-throw-portal`): CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND at the three violations (`covered-violation`), at the spread and `mount` sites (`covered-uncertifiable`), nothing under the boundary. Probe (`--recall-full`, the six codes, the `-m-portal` mount, sampled from the audit's rows): 1,000 misuse programs, 348 recall-gap to agree (NO_OWNER_CONTEXT 88, RESOLVE 75, UNTIL 75, CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND 70, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK 40), nothing else; 1,000 legal portal programs, no move and no violation. The 4 `oracle differs` rows of the misuse sample stand on main too.

<a id="adr-1048"></a>
## ADR 1048 — A guarded first call that cannot be preceded by a throw, and a call after a jump that leaves only an inner loop, run at least once
Proof A slice 3, on ADRs 1042 and 1046 (`Mode::AtLeastOnce` only; the exactly-once walk and the producer's whitelist are unchanged).

*Decision.* `unconditional_calls.rs`:
- **A `try` a `catch` guards.** A throw in the block before the call is caught and the `try` completes without the call, so the block is admitted only for its first statement, an expression statement that is the call itself, and only when nothing evaluated before the call runs can throw (`guarded_first_call`): no optional call; the callee a bare name bound to a hoisted function declaration (bound at scope entry, no TDZ) or to an import from a package (bound before the module's code runs; a project module may be in a cycle), with no write to the binding anywhere; every argument a literal, a function or an arrow. The callee's own throw is the call having run. The handler stays out.
- **Inner jumps.** The early-exit scan (`EarlyExit`) no longer counts a `break` or `continue` that leaves only a loop, a `switch` or a label opened inside the earlier statement it visits; a labelled jump to a label outside it, an unlabelled `break` outside every inner loop and `switch`, and an unlabelled `continue` outside every inner loop still leave.

*Evidence.* Unit test `at_least_once_admits_a_guarded_first_call_and_inner_jumps` (admitted: a function declaration, a package import with an arrow argument, a `try` with a `finally`, calls after loops, a `switch` or a label left only from inside; refused: a call after another statement, a `let` callee, a relative import, a member argument, an optional call, a spread, a labelled `break` that leaves, a `continue` in a `switch`). ADR 1042's case `while (true) { if (c) break; } a();` moves from refused to admitted (the jump leaves only the loop; the call runs on every completion). Fixture `unconditional-try-catch`: five NO_OWNER_CLEANUP (SC4001) violations, five counterexamples uncertifiable. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/unconditional-try-catch`): five `covered-violation`, the counterexamples that run `covered-uncertifiable`, no `static-only`.

*Measured* (release; ADR 1046's build against this change, the checker alone): the 1,195 recall-gap programs of the seven layers in brief A's join: `try-catch` 88 move from no violation at the site to a violation, 37 stay uncertifiable; the other six layers are unchanged (the inner-jump refinement moves no grid program); no violation lost. 3,071 `lg-recall` programs of the `try-catch` layer (the 168 of brief A's legal join included): nothing moved; two (`lg-pending-async-untracked-read-memo-x-{destructured,hook-member}-try-catch`) have a violation at the site in both builds and on main 1b03e7db9, where the audit at 78ddeb849 judged them uncertifiable: pre-existing, filed for review.

*What stays* (493 of brief A's rows over the seven layers): 224 `action(function* …)` step bodies (PRIMITIVE_ and CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE: `effect-creation-unaccounted`, `owner-callers-unenumerated`), 210 STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED in `ref-factory-body`, `helper-handed-call` and `patch-key-bind` (`function-run-unplaced`, 72 with no row at the site), 35 class-field positions, 24 flushes in a tracked queue callback: walks of the reactive IR, not the producer's whitelist.

## ADR 1047 — After a `yield` of a plain value, an action's step goes on at once: the calls after it run as the calls before it (L4, `action-plain-yield-from-apply`)
Part of G1 (`function-run-unplaced`). `const a = action(function* () { yield 1; (() => { createEffect(…); })(); }); createEffect(() => 1, () => { a(); })`: Chrome rc.21 reports NO_OWNER_EFFECT at the inner effect, and the checker gave SC4001 uncertifiable, `function-run-unplaced`, though the same effect written directly after the `yield` (or in the IIFE without the `yield`) was a proved violation. The owner graph keeps a call edge's proof only when the call runs on every completion of its function (`owner_discovery`'s `runs_every_time`, `solid_facts::ast::every_unconditional_call`, ADR 0714), and that walk ends a generator's every-run calls at its first `yield`: a later step runs only if it is asked for. An action asks for it at once when the yielded value is no thenable.

*The runtime fact* (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.21`): the function `action` returns runs `step`, which calls `it.next(v)` and hands the result to `run`; `run` assimilates a thenable (`r.value.then(v => inTransaction(t, q, () => step(v)))`) and otherwise steps again synchronously, `inTransaction(t, q, () => step(r.value))` (`dist/dev.js:2348-2365`; the prod build is the same). `isThenable` is `value != null && typeof value === "object" && typeof value.then === "function"` (`dist/dev-shared.js:3727`, `dist/prod/core/async.js:272`): no primitive, whatever its prototype holds, and no function. `Dialect::action_step_resumes_after_plain_yield` answers it, `true` for `Primitive::Action` on the rc.21 triple only.

*The change.* `owners::action_resuming_yields`: the non-delegating `yield`s with a plain operand (`yield_operand_plain`: absent, a numeric or string literal, `true`, `false`, `null`, the global `undefined`) written directly in a non-async generator an action steps (`stepped_action_generator`), on that dialect answer. `solid_facts::ast::every_unconditional_call_resuming` is ADR 0714's walk with those `yield`s not counted as suspensions; `owner_discovery` asks it for its edges' every-run test, so a call after such a `yield` is judged by the walk's other rules (a branch, a loop, an earlier exit still make it conditional). Nothing else reads it. `yield_operand_plain` no longer takes a name that `f64` parses (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `inf`) for a number: a binding may shadow it (`const NaN = Promise.resolve()`); such a `yield` is now a possible thenable, as `yield p` is.

*Measured* (release; main 2e2b60bb6 against this change). All 7,996 grid programs of the `action-plain-yield-from-apply` context (misuse and legal): 876 moved, all misuse mx-recall U to V at the site (NO_OWNER_EFFECT 292, NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY 292, NO_OWNER_CLEANUP 146, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT 146), no legal program moved, nothing else moved. The harness with Chrome on the 876 (`focus.mjs --runtime-diff all`): recall-gap 876 on main, agree 876 on this build, 876 compared, 0 behaviour, 0 attribution, 0 inconclusive, nothing needs a look on either. A stratified probe of 2,000 programs over the 126,626 of every context naming an action, a yield, a generator or a step (one per grid, side, code and context): 0 moved. Fixture `action-plain-yield-layers`: `IifeAfterNumber`, `ClosureAfterString`, `AfterBareAndLiterals` proved (were `function-run-unplaced`); `ConditionalAfterYield` and `NotAnAction` (a generator stepped by hand) stay uncertifiable; `AfterBinding`, `AfterDelegate`, `AsyncGenerator` were already violations (a continuation has no owner, as the apply has none), and `ShadowedName` joins them. Chrome rc.21, oracle case `action-plain-yield-layers`: NO_OWNER_EFFECT at the four sites is `covered-uncertifiable` on main and `covered-violation` on this build; the hand-stepped generator's PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK stays `covered-uncertifiable`.

*Not covered.* The STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED programs of the context that keep SC1001 `function-run-unplaced` (112: a generator layer, not this edge). Found, not fixed: the resumed step's `inTransaction` flushes when no action is open (`dist/dev.js:2205`), so an action whose plain `yield` resumes inside an effect apply throws FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at the action's call; Chrome reports it in the oracle case, and no build of the checker does (`unproven-clean`).
<a id="adr-1037"></a>
## ADR 1037 — A setter or `refresh` in an inline apply's returned cleanup is legal on every run of it
The cleanup an effect apply returns runs only from the effect. On a rerun it runs from the queue's drain with no owner, and on a disposal under `disposalDepth`, where the release's write guard stands down. A `For` row's disposal runs it under the row's owner and the write is still exempt; so are `markRefresh` and the store setter's guard (`write_guard_in_disposal`, `StandsDown`; rc.17's bytes, read as such for rc.21). A setter or `refresh` written there therefore never meets the owned-scope guard, unless a `flush()` of the program drains a rerun under an owner (ADR 0613, `flush_drains_under_owner`), yet the write walk left it `function-run-unplaced`. `execution_role::returned_cleanup_write_role` gives such a write `UntrackedCallback` when every one of these holds: the role is unplaced; the site is written directly in a non-async, non-generator function returned by the inline apply literal at an exact `createEffect` or `createRenderEffect` apply slot (`returned_cleanup_reruns_in_read_window` and `returned_cleanup_runs_outside_disposal`); the guard stands down; and no flush drains under an owner. It is asked only where a `ReactiveWrite` row is built (the setter in `local_access`, `refresh` in `static_api`), never in the shared write role, and each such write ends with a named silence (`local_access.push_setter_write.returned-cleanup`, `static_api.refresh.returned-cleanup`) on the new premise `ReturnedCleanupWriteGuard`, whose span is the effect call. The role arm `write_roles.returned-cleanup-write` has a stated boundary gap: the generator's cleanup cells are never clean, because the effect's creation keeps its own rows. An action call and `onFlush` share that role, and both throw under a `For` row's disposal (no disposal exemption), so they keep their rows. So do owner operations (silent under a row's disposal, `NO_OWNER_*` elsewhere: no violation either way), a strict read (warns on a rerun, silent on dispose), a named apply (it may be called elsewhere, `apply()()`) and code in a function written inside the cleanup.
*Measured* (main 1b03e7db9 against this build, release, 2,000 `effect-cleanup-*` programs, 1,034 of them legal): 27 legal programs U→clean, all REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE (`-for` 10, `-dispose` 8, `-rerun` 5, `-show` 4); nothing else moved, no violation moved, no misuse program moved. Fixtures `effect-cleanup-write-role` (the setter, `refresh` and a `For` row's write silent; the action, the named apply and the nested closure kept) and `effect-cleanup-write-role-flush` (a root-body `flush()`: every row kept). Chrome rc.21, oracle case `effect-cleanup-write-role`: 0 typing errors, no REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE anywhere (the reruns and the row removal run), the strict read covered by its row. `flush-veto-kept`'s `WritesInReturnedCleanup` is silent again, as its README says.
<a id="adr-1044"></a>
## ADR 1044 — A function held in a `const` copy or a closed literal's property runs where the holder's use runs
A stored throw in a function that is only referenced (ADR 0893) reports only where `reference()` finds its run, so two held shapes stayed `computation-error-unobserved` while Chrome reports at the site (R2's brief L3: 500 misuse rows of the mx-recall grid). The first is a `const` copy: `alias_end` knew only "called" or "argument of a primitive", so `const a = f; setTimeout(a, 0)`, `[1].forEach(a)`, a further copy and `a.call()` fell to `reference()` or were skipped. The second is a closed literal's property (`const b = { cb: () => … }; createMemo(b.cb)`, `setTimeout(b.cb)`, `const o = { m: hf }; o.m()`): a property value is no binding reference, so it fell to `reference()`. One dispatch now ends a reference by its hand-off class (`hand_off_end`, the arm `function_entries` had): a direct call, a carrier that runs it inline, a fresh-stack scheduler, a primitive's argument, a further `const` copy, a member read of a closed literal, or else `reference()`. `alias_end` asks each use of the copy its class (`hand_off_at`) and dispatches a call, an inline carrier, a scheduler, an argument or a further copy through it; any other use runs nothing, as before (`void a`). `closed_member_end` finds the member reads whose ADR 0351 value (`closed_member_value`) is the held function or the name holding it, and ends each like a reference; a read that is called (`o.m()`) runs it on the call's stack. Premises: ADR 0351's closure conditions and the reviewed hand-off table; nothing new. Each refusal stays an obligation: `use(b)`, `b.cb = g`, `let b`, `b[k]`, a spread copy, `let a`, `const a = c ? f : g`, `p.then(a).catch(h)`, an unread memo, and a run under `try`. A literal written in a component body also keeps the owner net's own row, because a function held in an object slot may run anywhere for that net (`function-run-unplaced`).
*Measured* (main 1b03e7db9 against this build, release, checker alone): the 500 misuse ids (cb-bundle 340, cb-alias 90, handoff-member 70; CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT, DYNAMIC_STATIC_PROMISE, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK) and their 827 legal twins: misuse U→V 500, legal unchanged (819 U, 8 clean, no violation), nothing else moved. Fixtures `stored-throw-held-callbacks` (six SC4001 violations; `MemberCall` and `AliasOfMember` keep the owner net's row in this program) and `stored-throw-held-callbacks-open` (the refusals, a separate program: a write of the key `cb` anywhere hands every function stored under it, ADR 0967). Chrome rc.21, oracle cases of the same names: NO_OWNER_CONTEXT at every placed site covered by a violation (`MemberCall`'s too, in the case's real-package program), the rest covered by uncertifiable rows, no violation claimed in the open case, 0 typing errors. `rediscovery.json` lists the 500 ids. Open: callback props (150), returned parameters (120), the updater (30), generators (105), assigned members (195), kept collections (120), and the generator's legal twins `bundle-escapes`, `alias-let` and `then-alias-caught`, which are fixtures here and not yet grid cells.

## ADR 1049 — A plain throw in an identity wrapper's literal or a stepped generator's first step ends where it runs
**The gap.** A plain throw (ADR 0893: `resolve`, `until`, a static `dynamic` promise, `useContext` with no provider, `flush` in a tracked effect, an owner-less context) in a function literal handed to an identity wrapper (`const run = same(() => …); run()`, `same(() => …)()` with `function same(cb) { return cb }`), or in a generator stepped once where it is made (`(function* () { …; yield 1 })().next()`), was `function-run-unplaced`: the walk saw a literal handed to a call and a generator body, and placed neither. Chrome reports the code in the body that runs them. R2's L3 scan: the `fire-return` group (60 misuse rows) and the `generator` group (105).
**The decision.** Two holders say where the function runs. (1) A literal at the parameter an exact identity wrapper returns (ADR 0346's `identity_wrapped_literal_span`: every completion returns that parameter, nothing else reads it): the call's value is the literal, so its end is a direct call of that value, or else the value's `const` alias and its uses, as for the literal itself (`returned_parameter_end`). (2) A site the first step of a generator stepped in place reaches (ADR 0521's `stepped_generator_in_place`, `StepReach::Reaches`): it runs on the stack of that non-computed `.next()` call (`stepped_generator_step`). Not read so (uncertifiable as before): a wrapper that also stores or reads its parameter, a conditional return, a site after a `yield`, an async generator, a held iterator (`const it = gen(); it.next()`), and a helper that returns the parameter in an object literal (`return { cb }`, then `box.cb()`: the `fire-store` group, 60 misuse rows, open in docs/open-work.md). A caught call keeps its reading (`try { run() } catch {}`).
**Evidence.** Fixture `stored-throw-returned-param`: uncertifiable to violation at `ReturnedCalled`, `ReturnedCalledDirectly` (SC2007) and `GeneratorStepped` (SC4002); `WrapperAlsoStores`, `ConditionalReturn`, `ReturnedCaught`, `GeneratorAfterYield`, `GeneratorStored`, `ReturnedInLiteral` stay uncertifiable. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/stored-throw-returned-param`): DYNAMIC_STATIC_PROMISE and CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND at the three (`covered-violation`), the stores, the held iterator and the boxed literal `covered-uncertifiable`, nothing at the caught call or after the `yield`. Probe (`--recall-full`, the six stored-throw codes, main 2e2b60bb6 against this build, the ids of the L3 rows): 1,479 programs; misuse 165 recall-gap to agree (generator 105 of 105, fire-return 60 of 60: CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND 35, DYNAMIC_STATIC_PROMISE 80, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT 30, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK 10, RESOLVE 5, UNTIL 5), nothing else; 719 legal programs, no move and no violation; oracle samples 0 behaviour differences.
<a id="adr-1036"></a>
## ADR 1036 — A definer on an object the program made, and a key that is a number by its syntax, reach no standard root (SC9012 `standard-member-impostor`)
After ADR 1024 two kinds of site hold the handed-root veto in projects with no other open write: `Object.defineProperties({}, d)` (`ReflectiveDefinition(*)`: solid-query's `createInfiniteQuery`, probus-hk's getters), and a write under a computed key that is an index (`out[i] = v`, `out[length++]`, `out[items.length - 1]`: most of app-game's `OpenMemberWrite(*)` sites).

*Decision.* (1) `root_definitions` (`base/contributions.rs`) keys the definer hazards as ADR 0951's `definers` does, except a call of `Object.defineProperty`, `Object.defineProperties` or `Reflect.defineProperty` on the global (no declaration of the file shadows `Object`/`Reflect`), with no spread target, whose first argument ADR 1024's `fresh_written_object` proves made: it defines keys of that object only, so it adds no hazard; through a factory it adds `FreshFactoryDefinitionAny`/`Sole(key)`, which `open_member_write_through_factory` reads as `ReflectiveDefinitionAny`/`Sole` while a factory may not be standard (ADR 1024's first-patch induction). A held, destructured or bare definer, `__defineGetter__`, and any other receiver stay as before. (2) `fresh_written::index_key`: a computed write key that is a number, a bigint or a boolean by its syntax names no member (an index or `true`/`false`; no standard call is named so) and is censused as `@@index`, which no formula reads: a numeric literal; an operator `numeric_operator` reads between two operands (arithmetic but `+`, shift, bitwise, relational) or a prefix `- ~ !` or `++`/`--` with no two operands; a `const` bound to such a key; a `let` (no direct `eval` in the file) whose initial value and every write is one, each assuming the previous value one. A parameter typed `number` proves nothing (a cast may lie); `+`, `typeof`, equality, `in`, logicals and conditionals are not read.

*Evidence.* Unit tests `a_definer_on_a_made_object_defines_on_no_root` and `an_index_key_names_no_member` (each form beside the shape that keeps it open: a parameter target, a held or destructured definer, a local `Object`, a spread target; `+`, `typeof`, a `let` seeded or rebound with a parameter, a `for … of` head, a direct `eval`, a `number` parameter, a logical or conditional that starts with `!` or `-`). Fixtures `fresh-target-definer` (`Number.isFinite` certified, was `standard-member-impostor` with `ReflectiveDefinition(*)`, `OpenMemberWrite(*)`), `-open` (a parameter target), `-shadowed` (a local `Object`), `index-key-open` (a `+` key beside the numeric ones): each negative keeps the row. Fuzz: five seam forms (`seam-shapes.mjs`: `indexlet`, `indexlogical`, `indexternary`, `definerebound`, `definepath`) in the `bseam-isfinite`/`then`/`settimeout` pairs; boundary scan of every `bseam` form (576 programs): no misuse cell silent, no legal cell reported.
**Coverage.** `uncertifiable-repro/sc9012`: 9 rows close, 7 `standard-member-impostor` (the veto's index writes are gone) and, at `fetchCurrentUser().then(...)` in `leaf-project-function.tsx`, `handed-member-read` and SC2001 `function-run-unplaced` (the `then` is now the standard one; SC1002 and `leaf-callback-opaque` stay there). New fixtures' rows in `scripts/guard/counts.json`.

*Measured* (development build; ADR 1024's commit f4aba794c against this change on it, before the rebase onto #272; rc.21 frozen corpus, all 34 projects): 212 violations and 257,233 uncertifiable in both, nothing moved: no project's last open site was one of these. The open sites shrink (`OpenMemberWrite(*)` old to new): app-game 637 to 456, compass-ui 24 to 21, error-menu-web 16 to 14, probus-hk 13 to 12, inferay 11 to 10, ai-memory-ui 3 to 1; `ReflectiveDefinition(*)` no longer fires in ai-memory-ui and inferay. ai-memory-ui's 858 `standard-member-impostor` rows now stand on one site: `Object.assign(draft, …)` in a `createProjection` callback in `@tanstack/solid-query`'s `build/dev.js` (the draft is a store over the seed; next lever, open work). Not run: Chrome on the new forms (their misuse is JavaScript's own: each writes the root).

## ADR 1045 — A standard definer on a made object, and a never-written `Symbol()` `var`, write no standard member (ADR 0939 `handed_root_patch`)
ADR 0939's "written" condition holds through `ReflectiveDefinition(*)` and `OpenMemberWrite(*)`. With both assumed away (what-if, ADR 0950) viviana-ui-web goes from V 2 to V 12 and U drops by 1,577 (`tuple-iteration-written` 726 to 0); ai-memory-ui stays blocked by solid-query's `Object.assign(draft, …)` in `createProjection`.

*Decision.* (a) A call whose callee is the spelled global `Object.defineProperty`, `Object.defineProperties` or `Reflect.defineProperty` (no declaration of the file shadows `Object`/`Reflect`), not a construct, with a first argument that is not a spread and that ADR 1024's `fresh_written_object` proves **Made** adds no key to `definers` in the handed-root census: it defines on that object, not on a standard root. The file records `ReflectiveDefinitionMade` instead, which counts as `ReflectiveDefinition(*)` again wherever a patch may reach one of those definers (`reflective_definition_through_made`, ADR 1024's first-patch induction). A definer held as a value or destructured, a Factory-form target, a parameter target, a local `Object` and `__defineGetter__` keep the row. Sites: `@tanstack/solid-router` `link.jsx:317/320/328` (`const linkProps = {}`), solid-query `dev.js:565` (`Object.defineProperties({}, …)`). (c) ADR 0877's symbol key also accepts a `let` or `var` of a module (a file with an import or export) bound to `Symbol()`, never the target of a write or delete (a computed key of a written member reads it), the only binding of its name in the file, with no direct `eval`. A read before the declarator gives `undefined`, and the key `"undefined"` names no writable standard member. A classic script's top-level `var` is a global property anyone may write, so it stays open. Site: `@tanstack/solid-start-server` `StartServer.js:12` (`this[_m$] = _p`).

*Evidence.* Unit tests `a_definer_on_a_made_target_defines_no_standard_member` and `a_never_written_symbol_binding_is_a_symbol_key`. Fixtures `handed-root-patch-definer-made` (`Number.isFinite` certified) with `-param`, `-shadowed`, `-patched`, `-held` (each keeps SC1001 on `Number.isFinite`), and `handed-root-patch-symbol-var` (certified) with `-symbol-var-written` (kept). `make coverage`: no existing snapshot moved.

*Not built.* (b), a `reduce` over an exported `const` array literal (viviana `themeGen.ts:70`): it needs program-wide proof that no importer writes, pushes to or hands on the array, which the per-file binding form cannot give. Deferred with its required twin (an importer's `push`, kept U).

<a id="adr-1051"></a>
## ADR 1051 — An action call whose first step stops at a plain `yield` flushes inside an effect's apply (SC2008)
Found by ADR 1047's oracle case: Chrome rc.21 warned FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at every call of an action like `const a = action(function* () { yield 1; … })` made in a `createEffect` apply, and no build of the checker reported anything there. The function `action` returns runs the first step on the caller's stack; `run` hands a result that is no thenable straight to `inTransaction(t, q, () => step(r.value))` (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.21` `dist/dev.js:2365`), and `inTransaction` calls `flush()` once its step returns when no action step is on the stack (`:2198-2208`). On an apply's stack the global queue is running and `inEffectCallback` is up (the step restores it), so that `flush()` drains nothing and the dev build warns, as for a `flush()` written there (`dist/dev-shared.js:3032-3077`).

*Decision.* `static_api.rs` `check_action_resume_flush` reports SC2008 at a call when: the callee is a `const` holding `action(function* …)` that no alias or write reaches (`named_action_generator`, `stepped_action_generator`); the generator's first statement is a `yield` that ADR 1047's `action_resuming_yields` names (a plain operand, a non-async generator, the dialect's synchronous resumption, on rc.21 only), with nothing but whitespace before it (no code that may throw or return first); and `effect_phase::ownerless_effect_phase_origin_through` proves every run of the call on a `createEffect` apply's stack with no owner (not mixed, not undecided), the `solid-js` instance read from the `action` call's own import. With an owner the call would throw ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE before any step; from `onSettled` or a tracked effect the flush throws another error; a `createRenderEffect` or `createReaction` apply is not read. The claim is the rule's universal no-op claim: whenever the call runs, its resumed step's flush runs inside the flush draining effects.

*Evidence.* Fixture `action-resume-flush`: `YieldNumber`, `BareYield`, `YieldString` (an argument) proved; no row for `YieldPromise`, `YieldBinding`, `FromSettled`, `AsyncGenerator`, `CodeBeforeYield` (a known miss). Chrome rc.21, oracle case `action-resume-flush`: FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at the three calls is `unproven-clean` on main 5780918b8 and `covered-violation` on this build; `CodeBeforeYield`'s stays `unproven-clean`; the others are quiet.

## ADR 1052 — A check Solid makes earlier at the same call throws first: the later rule is uncertifiable
**The gap.** A census of the stacked claims (the judge's `stacked-claim`, ledgered R-stacked) on main a3ba1dd92: 153 mx-census programs (149 still stacked) where our violation's line ran, Solid threw another code there first, and our code never fired. 165 (rule, first code) pairs: SC7002 behind PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE 51 and PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK 42; missing-owner behind PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK 47, PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE 6, CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE 1; leaf-owner-forbidden-call behind MISSING_EFFECT_FN 8; missing-context-provider behind NO_OWNER_CONTEXT 6. Under the 2026-11-17 ruling (ADR 1018: a check no run reaches gives no violation) the tolerance of `stacked-pairs.json` ("wrong if it runs") no longer holds them.
**The decision.** One fact over the final rows (`competing_checks.rs`, run before the typed blockers): a row that would be a violation becomes uncertifiable when an earlier check is *proven* to throw at its call (path and first byte). Earlier, by the pinned rc.21 source: the effect-callback guard (an SC6002 violation) before `createEffect`'s `NO_OWNER_EFFECT`, which it reports after creating, so for an effect only (a boundary reports `NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY` before it creates anything; the smoke's 14 boundary rows in an apply, Chrome-reported, stay violations); the leaf owner's refusal (an SC3001 violation at the operation's call, `sites` of ADR 0942) throws on the leaf caller's run and halts the system, so an unowned caller of the same call that runs later never reports (a component's tracked effect at mount, its handler after: the generated shapes and `leaf-owner`'s `DynamicExtent`); which run comes first is not proven in general (a timer or module code may run the unowned caller first), so the row is an obligation either way, every operation; `MISSING_EFFECT_FN` (an SC7001 violation) before SC3001's refusal; and a context read proven unowned (a missing-owner violation of the read) before SC4002's provider lookup. Blockers `creation-throws-first` (W4's, ADR 1020's constant) and `owner-check-throws-first`. An obligation of the earlier check proves nothing: the first build that also took SC6002 and SC3001 obligations, and missing-owner obligations of a read, moved 478 smoke programs Chrome reports from agree to recall-gap.
**Evidence.** Fixture `competing-check-first`: SC4001 uncertifiable at `EffectInApply`, `NamespaceEffectInApply`, `TrackedAndHandler`, `TrackedAndHandlerCleanup`, SC3001 at `MissingEffectFunctionInTracked`; `HandlerOnly` (SC4001), `EffectFunctionPresentInTracked` (SC3001) and every earlier check stay violations. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/competing-check-*`, one case a family, generated programs): only the earlier code is reported (PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, MISSING_EFFECT_FN); the boundary negative reports NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY then PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, the handler negative NO_OWNER_EFFECT. Existing fixtures: SC4001 violation to `creation-throws-first` at an effect created on an apply's stack (`deferred-effect-apply-callees` 2, `flush-veto-kept`, `primitive-in-effect-callback-tag`) and at `leaf-owner`'s `registerTeardown` `onCleanup` (a tracked effect and a handler call it). Smoke mx-census, main against this build (39,650 programs): 44 stacked-claim leave (36 not-fired, 8 agree), nothing else moves. The 153 ledger ids: 105 stacked remain (93 SC7002, the second part on W4's branch; 13 others open in docs/open-work.md), 4 were already not-fired on main. `stacked-pairs.json` retires CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE|missing-owner, PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE|missing-owner and MISSING_EFFECT_FN|leaf-owner-forbidden-call, so main's build fails `fuzz-focus` on those ids (15 false positives) and this one passes.
