## ADR 1053 — A write to a `createProjection` callback's draft reaches no standard root (SC9012 `standard-member-impostor`)
After ADR 1036, ai-memory-ui's 858 `standard-member-impostor` rows and donegeon-client's open writes rest on one site: `@tanstack/solid-query` 6.0.0-rc.5 `build/dev.js` `metaProjection`, `createProjection((draft) => { Object.assign(draft, metaFrom(query().state)); }, …)`, an `Object.assign` to a parameter.

*The source* (rc.21 `@solidjs/signals` `dist/dev.js`). `createProjection` (`createProjectionInternal`, 7866-7918) wraps the seed (`wrap`, 4700: a store proxy; a `markRaw` seed comes back raw and the pass then throws at `wrappedStore[$TARGET]._fam` before the callback runs) and runs `runProjectionComputed` (7742), which calls the callback with `shadow ?? s`: `shadow` a clone of the store's value (`cloneState`: `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(v))`, a spread or a `slice`), `s` the draft `wrapDraft` (7585) makes, a new `Proxy` over a new `{}` or `[]` whose `set`, `deleteProperty` and `defineProperty` traps write the projection's store proxy, whose own traps write a backing the store made (`ensurePB`, ADR 1041's reading). No trap writes the seed or any other object, and a trap it lacks (`setPrototypeOf`) acts on the wrapper's own new target.

*Decision.* `fresh_written.rs` (`projection_draft`, a factory-form object, ADR 1024) admits, at a write of the open-write census (`impostor_sites`), the first parameter of an inline callback (an identifier, no default, never written; an arrow or a function that never names `arguments`; no direct `eval` in the file) passed first, unspread, to a call whose callee is an identifier. The census records the write per key and per callee: `ProjectionDraftWrite(key, callee)`, the callee by the symbol the binder resolves at it (`ProjectionDraftWriteUnresolved(key)` when none). `SemanticLookup::hazard_present(OpenMemberWrite(key))` is also true where a draft write of that key has a callee that is not one of the symbols `symbol_names` names a primitive whose callback the dialect says writes only runtime objects (`Dialect::callback_first_parameter_writes_only_runtime_objects(primitive, 0)`; Solid 2: `createProjection` alone, the store setter and `createStore(fn)` not read) (the table `primitive_name` reads a call by), so a draft of another callee (`createMemo`'s previous value, a store setter, a helper that hands its callback anything) is an open write of its own key and of no other. As every factory-form site it also stays open while a factory of `FRESH_FACTORIES` (`Object.assign` among them) may not be standard. The listing (`hazard_sites`, `handed_root_writes`) lists a draft site whose key a draft holds open. A callee keyed by a 32-bit hash of its symbol id, as every census key is. The scan of `symbol_names` is recorded in `ir-read-lint` (a build-wide TypeFacts table, read once per lookup).

*Evidence.* Unit tests `a_projection_draft_rests_on_its_callee` (the form, beside a member callee, a callee that is a call, the callback second, a written, defaulted or `arguments`-reachable parameter, a direct `eval`) and `a_draft_write_opens_only_its_key_under_another_callee`. Fixtures `projection-draft-assign` (`Number.isFinite` certified, was `standard-member-impostor`), `-shadowed` (a local `createProjection`), `-other` (`createMemo`'s previous value), `-rebound` (the parameter assigned a parameter): each negative keeps the row. Chrome rc.21, oracle case `projection-draft-assign`: quiet, the checker reports no SC9012 row there. Fuzz: seam form `draftcallee` (a local helper that hands its callback the root, written as a draft); boundary scan of every `bseam` form (612 programs): no misuse cell silent, no legal cell reported.

*Measured* (development build, release binaries; ADR 1036 on #273 against this change; rc.21 frozen corpus v2, the 17 projects with `OpenMemberWrite(*)` and 3 controls). Violations 200 to 214, uncertifiable 226,251 to 222,423 (-3,828): ai-memory-ui -886 (`standard-member-impostor` and the rows its veto shadowed), donegeon-client -2,942 and 14 SC8015 `prefer-show` violations (`success() ? <p>…</p> : null` and kin on `createSignal` accessors, `preference-read-unproven` before: the veto withheld the read). In donegeon the draft was the one open write; with it gone the factories are intact and its four router factory-form sites close too. By kind: `standard-member-impostor` -1,657, `pending-read-unresolved` -1,062, `tuple-iteration-written` -927, `handed-member-dispatch` -248; rows the lifted veto had shadowed follow under their own rules (`function-run-unplaced` +257, `read-after-await-unaccounted` +223). No control moved. A first version gated every factory-form site on every draft callee and moved the kui shell control by +2,921 rows; it was replaced by the per-key gate above.
*Review fix (Fable review of 1047/1051).* `yield_operand_plain` read the operand's text, and a text that starts and ends with a quote passed as a string literal; but `yield` binds looser than `||`, `?:` and `+`, so `yield "z" < mode || load() || ""`, `yield "p" === mode ? load() : "done"` and `yield "a" + fail() + "b"` were plain, and SC2008 was claimed where the step yields a promise or throws (Chrome silent: false positives). The operand is now plain only when it is one literal node: facts schema 96 records `YieldFact::operand_literal` from the Oxc node (a string, numeric, bigint or boolean literal, `null`, the global `undefined`), with no text test; anything else is not plain. ADR 1047's two uses read the same helper, so its resumed-step claims narrow with it. And the action calls the generator function before the first step, so a parameter list that may throw there (a default that runs code, any destructuring pattern: `function* ({ id } = undefined as any)`) leaves the call unreported. Fixture `action-resume-flush` and its oracle case add the five shapes: on a9a00a06b each was an SC2008 violation Chrome did not confirm (static-only), now none is reported; the three covered violations stay. Fuzz context `action-compound-yield-from-apply` (`yield "z" < "a" || Promise.resolve() || ""`, legal for REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE and ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE).

## ADR 1054 — A copy of a Solid export names it only where the import it copies resolved
**The defect.** `symbols.rs` `add_solid_import_names` named a destructuring slot of a namespace import (`const { createMemo: m } = S`, ADR 0459, which also holds `const m = S.createMemo`) and a `const` copy of a named import or a closed holder's member (review D36) after the export by the import's module specifier, checking only that the copy's own `const` is declared. With `solid-js` unresolved (every import is the checker's one unknown symbol, SC9012 `import-unresolved`), the copies still named Solid primitives: name recognition, against invariants 2 and 3. The import itself and `S.createMemo(...)` were already withheld (their binding is the unknown symbol).
**The decision.** Both loops ask the copied import binding's own symbol (`import_binding_declared`, the test the direct binding already passes): a copy of an import that resolved nowhere names nothing, and its claims fall to SC9012 `import-unresolved` (uncertifiable). Where the import resolves, nothing changes.
**Census (pre-fix build, unresolved `solid-js`, every primitive through a slot).** Proved: SC7002 (sync memo), SC7001 (missing effect function), SC4001 (module-scope `onCleanup`, an effect with no owner), SC3001 (a creation in a tracked effect); the member `const`, the import alias and the closed holder take the same path (SC7002 probed). All rules read primitives through these names, so the fix covers each. Not covered here (docs/open-work.md): a dialect module specifier that resolves to a file which is not the package.
**Evidence.** Fixture `unresolved-namespace-slots` (no violation; SC9012 at each copy; the shadowed parameter silent) and its twin `unresolved-namespace-slots-resolved` (each copy a violation: SC4001, SC7002 ×6, SC7001; Chrome rc.21 covers all 8). No other fixture moved.
**Part 2 (SC7002, on ADR 1020's third cut).** `createMemo(async, { sync: true })` reports SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC at its result probe, after every creation guard. The same pass makes an SC7002 violation uncertifiable `creation-throws-first` (its message says why) when, at its creation, SC6002 is a violation or its `effect-owner-unproven` obligation (a caller runs it in an apply with no owner proven), or an SC3001 violation is written at the call itself in the leaf callback (every run of it refused). Not counted: the accounting obligations (`effect-creation-unaccounted`, `leaf-operation-unaccounted`), which name no caller (taking them cost 964 smoke programs Chrome reports SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC at), and a refusal reached through a helper, which refuses that caller's run only (a render that calls the helper first reports SC7002: `settled-chain-placed`, Chrome-confirmed). Fixture `competing-check-sync-memo` (U: `MemoInApply`, `NamespaceMemoInApply`, `MemoInTracked`, `MemoInSettled`; V: `MemoInBody`, and `MemoInTrackedHelper` open); Chrome `runtime-oracle/competing-check-sync-*`; `deferred-effect-apply-callees` L16 SC7002 V to U (SC6002 proven at the helper's creation). Smoke mx-census against the merge of ADR 1020's branch and part 1 (39,630 programs): 30 stacked-claim to not-fired, nothing else. Ledger: 68 stacked rows left (SC7002 62: 45 behind PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, 17 behind PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, all with an accounting obligation or a helper route only; context 6). `PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK|missing-owner` is retired from `stacked-pairs.json` (its twins prove non-creating calls only, and every effect-in-apply row part 1 fixed would have scored a stacked claim on a regression): its 7 open rows (`effect-apply-shared`, `apply-placed-twin`) are ledgered as false positives with an owner. The SC7002 pairs and `NO_OWNER_CONTEXT|missing-context-provider` stay while rows rely on them (one pattern claim, `flip/st-tracked-handled-sync-memo`, too): a regression of a fixed SC7002 row would still score a stacked claim until they go.

## ADR 1058 — A function a helper boxes in a fresh literal runs where the box's member is called
**The gap.** ADR 1049 left open a plain throw (ADR 0893) in a literal a helper returns inside an object literal (`function h(cb) { return { cb } }`, then `const box = h(() => …); box.cb()`): the box is a call's value, not a literal, so ADR 1044's closed-literal member read (`closed_member_end`) never named the function, and the row stayed `computation-error-unobserved` while Chrome reports the throw where `box.cb()` runs (R2's L3 scan, the `fire-store` group, 60 misuse rows).
**The decision.** ADR 0351's closed-literal index (`indexes/closed_members.rs`) reads `const box = h(f)` as the literal `h` returns when `h` boxes its parameter (`boxed_literal`, `boxing_helper`): an exact same-file function declaration under a name nothing writes, synchronous and no generator, whose one completion is a straight-line `return` of an object literal holding the parameter as one property value (`{ cb }`, `{ cb: cb, size: 1 }`), the parameter read nowhere else (no other use, no `arguments`, no `eval`), the argument at its position with no spread before it. Each call makes a fresh object nothing else names, so with ADR 0351's conditions on the binding (a `const`, not exported, every reference a plain member read neither optional, written nor deleted) and on the literal (no spread, computed key, accessor, duplicate key, `this` or `__proto__`), the member read `box.cb` names `f` and `closed_member_end` ends it where the read is called or handed on; the helper's other properties name nothing. Not read so (as before): an imported helper, a helper that also stores the parameter, several returns, a spread in the literal, a box handed on or written; a caught call keeps its reading.
**Evidence.** Fixture `stored-throw-returned-literal`: `BoxedCalled`, `KeyedCalled` uncertifiable to SC2007 violations; `HelperAlsoStores`, `TwoReturns`, `HelperSpreads`, `BoxHandedOn`, `BoxWritten`, `BoxCaught`, `ImportedHelper` stay uncertifiable; 1049's `ReturnedInLiteral` (`stored-throw-returned-param`) becomes a violation. Chrome rc.21 (oracle cases of the same names): DYNAMIC_STATIC_PROMISE `covered-violation` at the three, `covered-uncertifiable` at the refusals that throw, nothing where the box is handed on, written or caught. Probe (main 5780918b8 against this build, release): 1,000 fire-store programs and 1,000 of the neighbouring held-function contexts (`fire-helper`, `fire-return`, `kept-*`, `handed-flush*`), 43 moved, all U to V (mx-recall DYNAMIC_STATIC_PROMISE in the body 20, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT from a handler 20, mx-census 3), none outside fire-store; Chrome on the 43: recall-gap to agree 42, 1 not-fired on both, 0 behaviour. Open (docs/open-work.md): the 40 rows the owner net's SC4001 `function-run-unplaced` decides (body `useContext`, timer no-owner context).

## ADR 1060 — A Solid specifier the compiler resolved to another file names nothing
**The defect.** `add_solid_import_names` (and `loading_entries`' boundary test) named a dialect module's imports after the specifier string. A tsconfig `paths` mapping of `solid-js` to a project shim (a file with Solid's names and none of its behaviour) or into another package kept every claim: SC4001, SC7002, SC7001 proved where nothing Solid runs. Name recognition, against invariant 3.
**The decision.** `symbols::specifier_may_be_package` reads the compiler's attested resolution of the specifier: a bare specifier landed outside every `node_modules` tree (`NonRelative`: `paths`, `baseUrl`), a relative landing, or a `node_modules` file whose owning manifest names another package is not the package. Its imports name nothing, and each runtime use of their bindings is SC9012 `dialect-specifier-mapped` (uncertifiable; `static_rules::unresolved_import_references`), never a clean: what the mapped file runs is not read as Solid, nor proven not to be. An unresolved row (an ambient `declare module`, a missing package) or a file with no row keeps the earlier answer (ADR 1054's declared-symbol test). A mapping onto the package's own directory still names it.
**Premise (coordinator's ruling, 2026-11-18).** An installed `node_modules/solid-js` whose manifest names `solid-js` at the pinned version is the package: installed bytes are the published bytes (the dependency premise of ADRs 0266/0300). No content check. An ambient `declare module "solid-js"` with no resolved package file is no evidence of Solid; it is left as is because 858 of 1,912 fixture projects supply Solid's types that way (docs/open-work.md).
**Evidence.** Fixtures `solid-specifier-mapped` (shim: SC9012 only), `solid-specifier-mapped-package` (violations), `solid-specifier-mapped-other` (SC9012 only); main proved all five claims in each. Chrome does not apply (the oracle's Vite ignores `paths`).
**Part 3 (the 7 ledgered missing-owner false positives).** A helper an effect's apply and a handler or a render both call (`effect-apply-shared`, `apply-placed-twin`): SC6002 is only an obligation at the creation, `effect-owner-unproven` (one caller is an apply, another runs owned or later), so part 1 kept missing-owner's violation, and Chrome reports only PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK. That obligation names the apply caller, whose run throws the guard and halts; the run missing-owner proves unowned may be that one, and nothing orders the others' runs against the halt: an effect's owner row there is uncertifiable `creation-throws-first` too. The row's blocker is read as projection gives it (`blockers::for_rule` when its context names none, ADR 0680): part 2's SC7002 branch asked for the named form only and never matched. It is dropped for SC7002, whose probe another caller (a render, a rerun) may reach first: taking it moved 14 smoke programs Chrome reports SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC at. Fixture `competing-check-first` (`ApplyAndHandler`, `ApplyAndRender` U; `HandlerOnly` V); Chrome `runtime-oracle/competing-check-apply-and-*`: PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK only. Smoke mx-census against main fa8f33277 (40,805 programs): the 7 rows leave false-positive (6 not-fired; `mx-sync-node-received-async-effect-apply-shared-effect` keeps its SC7002 stacked claim), nothing else moves. Ledger: falsePositive 7 to 0, stackedClaim 69.
<a id="adr-1059"></a>
## ADR 1059 — The owner graph follows a boxed function to the `box.cb()` calls that run it
**The gap.** ADR 1058 placed a boxed function's plain throw where `box.cb()` runs, but the owner net (SC4001, and the provider walk of SC4002 that reads its owner) asks the owner graph who calls the function, and `owner_discovery.rs` resolved a member callee only through the literal-receiver census (`object_member_function`), which holds a `const` written as an object literal, not one a boxing helper returns. The boxed function had no caller, context zero, and ADR 0534's `unplaced_callback` made every owner operation in it `function-run-unplaced`, though Chrome reports it at the site (the `fire-store` group: `useContext` with no provider in the body, the no-owner reads run from a timer).
**The decision.** A call's target is also the function the member read of a box names (`SemanticLookup::callee_closed_member_function`: ADR 0351's index, a binding ADR 1058 boxes; a `const` written as an object literal stays the census's), after the census and before the symbol. The edge is the call's like any other (its kind from `call_owner_edge`), so the function runs under the call's owner: a component body's, or none on a timer's stack. Premises: ADR 0351's closure and ADR 1058's helper conditions; nothing new. Not followed (as before): a box handed on, written, aliased or exported, an imported helper.
**Evidence.** Fixture `owner-boxed-callers`: `BodyContextNotFound` (SC4002) and `TimerNoOwner` (SC4001) uncertifiable to violations, `BodyWithDefault` clean, `TimerBoxHandedOn` and `TimerImportedHelper` uncertifiable. Chrome rc.21: `runtime-oracle/owner-boxed-callers`. Probe (ADR 1058's build against this one, release): 1,000 fire-store programs and 1,000 closed-member programs (`cb-bundle`, `cb-alias`, `handoff-member` and the other held-member axes): 237 moved, all in fire-store; 125 U to V (timer misuse 105, SC4001, one per no-owner code; body CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND 20, SC4002), 112 relabelled with the same verdicts (104 legal body programs), no legal violation; the closed-member set: 0 moved. Chrome on the 237: ADR 1058's build mx-recall recall-gap 120 and agree 6, this build agree 126; lg-recall 104 uncertifiable on both; mx-census unchanged (not-fired 6, agree 1); 0 behaviour, 0 attribution. Oracle case: CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND and NO_OWNER_CONTEXT covered by violations at the two (covered-uncertifiable before), the refusals covered-uncertifiable, nothing at `BodyWithDefault`.
*Found on the way (ADRs 1044 and 1058, main included).* A first build that gave every closed literal's member call an owner edge turned `object-member-initialization`'s `App` into a violation, where the census (ADR 0299) refuses a receiver called before its declarator: the call throws a `ReferenceError` and nothing runs. ADR 0351's closed-literal index had no such order, so the stored-throw reading of ADRs 1044 and 1058 claimed SC2007 at `function enter() { held.cb(); } enter(); const held = { cb: () => … }` (and the boxed form): Chrome rc.21 reports the `ReferenceError`, never the promise (`static-only` at both, a scratch case; main 5780918b8 has the literal one). The index now names a member only when every use of the binding runs after its declarator (`initialized_before_every_use`, the census's `initialized_use` in other words): in a function, the binding is in no `switch` case and every use is written after the initializer with no function declaration between it and the binding's scope (a later closure is created later, so a timer's `box.cb()` stays read); at module level, a written literal only, on no import cycle and with no unknown load, every use after the initializer or in a function, and the code before the initializer calls only primitives with literal arguments. Fixture `stored-throw-returned-literal` adds `LiteralBeforeDeclarator` and `BoxBeforeDeclarator` (uncertifiable; Chrome: nothing at either), `owner-boxed-callers` adds `BodyBeforeDeclarator`. Coverage moves no other fixture, and ADR 1044's 502 rediscovery ids do not move.

<a id="adr-1061"></a>
## ADR 1061 — The blocker census: every blocker of a row, internal only
An uncertifiable row names the first blocker its analysis met: SC2002 cites the first writer of a global (`global_writers_of(name).next()`) and the first problem of that package's closure, SC9012 `standard-member-impostor` names `handed-root-patch` or else `impostor-veto`, and `push_defect` keeps the first row filed at a start. So the corpus counts by blocker were counts of first blockers, and no row could say what else holds it.
*Decision.* `SOLID_CHECKER_BLOCKER_CENSUS=1` (`solid_facts::package_reach::blocker_census`) adds a side table `blockerCensus` to the internal JSON, after the findings: per SC2002 site the global or package it may run (`global|write:<name>`, `package|<root>`), one row per global with every writer and how (`named`, `any`, `unspelled`), one row per package with every problem of its closure (the walk already kept up to 256, `Closure::problems`) and the files that write a global under an undecided key; per SC9012 veto row both formulas with every hazard each reads, and the sites of every hazard named; and each uncertain row `push_defect` drops at a start already filed, with its kind. Off, nothing is collected and the table is absent. For one-shot runs (`SOLID_CHECKER_DAEMON=0`): the daemon reads the flag in its own process and its cache keys do not hold it. No analysis reads the table: no finding, verdict, text output or exit code moves either way. Not collected: rows whose analysis names no cause (the creation pair, `read-after-await-unaccounted`, `function-run-unplaced`), what a withheld call would meet once the veto lifts, and `pending-read-unresolved` rows that follow the veto.
*Evidence.* Unit test `a_root_names_every_problem_of_its_closure_and_its_any_key_files`. ## ADR 1062 — A value a compute returns by reference or as a returned literal's member is a returned value, on every path
**The defect (Fable's review of ADR 1020, items 3 and 4).** ADR 1020 read a returned value only as a function literal a compute returns directly. A closure returned by reference (`const f = () => …; return f`) or as a returned literal's member (`return { run: () => … }`, `{ run: f }`, then `v.run()`) was "may run" with no mark, so a sync memo it creates was a proved SC7002: where the apply calls it, Chrome rc.21 throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK first; where it only names it, it never runs (120 legal programs of the new contexts, all SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC). And the site's mark came from a withholding query that stopped at the first reached call site (`binding_unreached`'s `any`), so a second path to the site hid the returned-value path.
**The decision.** `returned_value_holder`: a function, not called where written, returned directly, written inside an expression a compute returns (not as an argument of a call there), or named with its name in such an expression (not as a callee). `reachable_from_returned_value`: upward from the site's function through the function written around it, the functions holding its call sites and those holding a reference to its name (same file), any holder marks the site `returned_value_run`, whatever other path also runs it; the walk is bounded at 512 functions, and at the bound the answer is yes (fail closed). It replaces the third cut's withholding query. ADR 1020's never-called withholding (`void v`) and the fourth cut's creation crossing (now stopping at any holder) are unchanged.
**Cost.** SC7002 at a site a returned value may run is `creation-throws-first` even where another path runs it outside an apply (a sync memo created in a helper the body also calls), and where the value is called in the body (Chrome: SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC; fixture `C1`).
**Evidence.** Fixture `returned-by-reference` (R1–R5 violations on main, `creation-throws-first` here; Chrome rc.21 PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at each, SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC at `C1`, uncertifiable, and `C2`, a violation). Fuzzer: contexts `apply-ref-*`, `apply-member-*`; lg-recall focus fails on main (120), passes here. The 1,968-program apply-void probe: no move against main.

## ADR 1057 — The runtime oracle compares our code with Chrome's: a violation is covered only by a code that claims its rule
**The gap.** `scripts/runtime-oracle.mjs` counted a violation as covered by any diagnostic on its line, whatever the diagnostic's code (the stacked SC7002 and missing-owner rows of ADR 1052 hid there: Chrome reported only the earlier code), and ranked a static-only violation below `covered-violation` and `covered-uncertifiable`, so a case with any covered diagnostic hid it; neither verdict failed the gate.
**The decision.** A violation is covered only by a diagnostic whose code claims its rule (`codeRules`), at its lines or an application frame on the diagnostic's stack (the rule-aware check the frames already had; the code-blind line check is gone). An uncovered violation is `code-mismatch` when Chrome raised another code on its lines, `static-only` otherwise, `no-runtime-code` for a rule no code claims. `code-mismatch` and `static-only` fail the case (and rank above every covered verdict) unless `oracle.json`'s `open` ledgers the violation by `finding` (`"<rule> <file>:<line>"`) with a `kind` (`false-positive`, `no-diagnostic`, `unreached`, `attribution`), an owner and a one-line cause: `known-static`, listed on every run and stale (failing) once the violation is gone. In the same slice the last non-repeat stacked pair, `ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE|flush-in-action`, retires (no ledgered row or program needs it): the fuzz judge's tests take a synthetic pair for the proved branch.
**Re-judge (862 cases, this build; the shared execution cache missed on 855, so Chrome ran them once and they are cached now).** No code mismatch is left (ADR 1052 fixed the shapes that had them). 15 static-only violations surface, 11 of them hidden under `covered-uncertifiable` before, all ledgered (owner Mac 20): `false-positive` 5, `flush-in-effect-callback` `AfterReturn`, `EmptyLiteral`, `ThrowingCompute`, `TryReturn`, `NeverBeforeFlush` (FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at a flush that provably never runs: wrong under ADR 1018, to fix); `no-diagnostic` 5 (three flushes after a nested render effect, JSX or a mounting helper, a module-scope store destructure, `r9-e2`'s dropped store write: real defects Solid reports nothing for); `unreached` 3 (an unknown branch, and `r5-t1`/`-body`'s destructure behind an earlier PENDING_ASYNC_UNTRACKED_READ throw); `attribution` 2 (`stored-throw-async-rejection` 144 and 204: the same throw is covered at the line above, and a plain throw's observation carries no stack). Four cases fail on main and here alike, not this slice's: `action-resume-flush` (unproven-clean), `after-await-open` and `r10-destructured` (stale-open), `oracle-behaviour-detached-owner-layers` (type-error).

## ADR 1068 — FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at a flush that provably never runs is uncertifiable
**The gap.** ADR 1057's re-judge left five FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK (SC2008) violations that Chrome never reports (`runtime-oracle/flush-in-effect-callback`: AfterReturn, EmptyLiteral, ThrowingCompute, TryReturn, NeverBeforeFlush), ledgered as false positives. SC2008 was exempt from the site-reach rule ("a no-op wherever it runs", ADR 0458): the reading ADR 1018 retired.
**The decision.** The exemption goes (`diagnostics.rs`): SC2008 at a site that provably never runs is uncertifiable like every other rule (`unreached-dead-code`, `function-unentered`, …). Two reach facts close the shapes no fact named: (1) the facts' dead-code reading (`unreachable.rs`) takes a `try` that never completes normally (its `finally` does not, or its block does not and neither does its `catch`, if any; a `finally` that completes normally keeps the block's abrupt completion); (2) a callback a primitive receives after one whose return it hands on (`Dialect::callback_return_is_value`: an effect's compute) is never entered when that earlier callback is a literal whose body starts with a `throw` (`site_reach.rs` `after_throwing_value_callback`); a bundle's `error` arm, which runs on that throw, is not this. Anything else keeps its reading (`Conditional`, behind an unknown branch, stays a violation).
**Evidence.** Fixture `dead-flush-1068`: U at AfterReturn, TryReturn, ThrowingCompute, NamespaceThrowingCompute, EmptyLiteral; V at Plain, CatchCompletes, ComputeMayReturn; `solid-facts` test `a_try_that_never_completes_normally_kills_what_follows`. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/flush-in-effect-callback`): the five sites run nothing; their ledger rows (ADR 1057) are removed. The grids cannot write a flush dead inside an apply (their `dead-*` contexts put the site in the component body): `scripts/fuzz/patterns/deadflush/` holds the five shapes; the build before fails the lane (5 new false positives), this one passes (5 fine). Scoped fuzz-focus FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK (default and recall grids): no program moves; smoke mx-census: no checker move.

## ADR 1056 — A timer callback that is a parameter, read through a composite callee and a handed literal member
ADR 0803's census withdraws every tuple slot of a program where a timer may call a function that reads its `this` (the window). A callback that is a parameter was seen only where every entry of its function was a direct call in the file (`closed_parameter_seen`). kui shell's four sites were neither: feature-messages `session.ts:184,187` (`setTimeout(resume, 0)` in `afterNextPaint`, entered as `(options.scheduleAfterPaint ?? afterNextPaint)(() => …)`) and shell `App.tsx:156,193` (`schedule: (delayMs, run) => void setTimeout(run, delayMs)`, a member of a literal handed to `createHealth` and `createCapabilities`), 1,036 dev rows.

*The change* (`accessor_provenance/mutation_sites.rs`). (1) An entry is also an operand of a composite callee (ADR 0468's `composite_callee_operands`: a conditional's branch, either side of `||`/`??`, the right of `&&`, a comma's tail): the call enters the function with its own arguments. A reference that is an assignment's value fails the parameter (`(slot = f)(cb)` stores `f`; ADR 0515's peel had read it as the direct callee, so a later `slot(fn)` with any function was an entry the census did not see: closed here, no corpus row moves). (2) `handed_literal_member_seen`: an anonymous function written as a plain data member of a closed object literal (no spread, computed or nameless key, accessor, or second property of the key) that is, as written, an argument of a direct call of an exact project function, whose parameter there is a plain name with no default, in a function that mentions no `arguments`, read only as `parameter.key` with static keys and never written. Every read of the member's key must be the callee of a direct call, and those calls are what enter the function; a call of another member runs that member with the literal as `this`, so its value must be an arrow or a function that names no receiver. Anything else keeps the parameter unseen.

The handed-member proof reuses `parameter_argument`: a callback parameter must be a plain name, unwritten, without a default or an aliased `arguments` entry. The helper must be module code (strict, so `Function.caller`/`arguments` cannot expose the parameter); both functions and sibling methods refuse direct eval. The literal and its member must not occur inside an assignment value; all keys are unique own data/method keys, without `__proto__`; every member read names an own property, so an inherited getter cannot obtain the literal. A scheduling method itself may not read its receiver. These guards pin the rewritten/defaulted parameter, stored member, stored literal and receiver-escape twins added during review.

*Evidence.* Fixtures `iteration-timer-parameter-composite` and `iteration-timer-handed-literal` (through a namespace import; with kui's SC1001 shapes) prove; their escape, receiver, storage and parameter-refusal twins remain uncertifiable. Measured checks and Chrome evidence are recorded in the commit message. Left: feature-messages `window.prompt` and feature-consumers' `matchMedia`, both written by a test (ADR 1055's shape).

The lean grid now generates both, so each lean audit reports the twins as ids the entry does not store.
**Checked.** The 307 reported twins are the same class. Each one, regenerated at seed 1 and judged with the release build of f544561a8's tree, is `unplaced`, and every finding is uncertifiable: no violation, no false clean. On the audit's rows, the lean set of each entry equals its full set, id for id (pk-lazy 326, pk-call-shapes 288).
**Decision.** Each entry's `ids.lean` is the set the audit reports, which equals `ids.full`. The idRegex and the class are unchanged.
**Part 2.** More `cause|…` families, census only:
- B4: `unplaced|<layer>` (`runs_unplaced_once`, chained `via-caller`), `placed-nowhere|<disjunct>`, `dispatch|<trigger>|<role>|<context>|frame:<span>`, the projection's `seed|read/write/action/owner|…` where it names `function-run-unplaced`, and `after-await-member|handed-compute|via=<call>`, which explains part 1's 2,898 SC9012 rows with no role decision.
- B3: `after-await|<via>|<first failed sub-fact of library_call::runs_nothing, or the member read's root kind>|test|host`.
- B5: `handed|<first leaf of handed_value that answered>|<member declaration>`, through a census-only thread-local.
- Rows recorded after the draft are drained at the end of the build and at the snapshot.

*Evidence.* rc.21 frozen corpus v2, dev mode: 34 of 34 projects identical off and on (U 251,897, V 244); 719,778 census rows. Pools with a cause: B4 12,531 of 12,557, B3 14,151 of 14,151, B5 12,311 of 12,315. `make coverage` with the gate cache off, census off and on: both pass. Ranked causes and levers: sc-scratch `mac23/cause-1065b/REPORT.md`.
<a id="adr-1071"></a>
## ADR 1071 — The namespace census reads a `.then` callback's members, a named re-export, and an explicit runtime file; a truthiness test is inert
**The trace.** ADR 1055's lead (`open-world-export`, 16,600 rows in closed programs) was the namespace census (ADR 0347) answering `escapes_unnamed`. In the router projects the escape is `@solidjs/router` `dist/data/events.js`: `import("./serverForms.js").then(m => m.submitServerForm(…))`, read as an unnamed load, so `serverForms.js`, and through `export { submitServerForm } from "./action.js"` every export of `action.js`, escaped. Other projects hold another cause (inferay: a computed load in `@solidjs/vite-plugin`; probus-hk: `async_hooks` in a server module; app-game: a dynamic load in `abr-parser`), the entry closure's question (ADR 1055).
**The decision.** Four exact reads. (1) Facts schema 97: `import(x).then(m => …)` whose one plain parameter is only the object of static members, or a destructuring parameter, is a `Members` consumer, as `(await import(x)).a` is. (2) `exported_function` follows a named re-export (`export { n } from "./m"`) into the one project module its specifier loads (four hops at most). (3) `direct_specifier_target`: where the compiler resolved the declaration file (`./m.js` to `m.d.ts`), a relative specifier with an explicit runtime extension loads exactly that file (`explicit_runtime_files`, ADR 0193), when one candidate is a program file. (4) Facts: an `if` statement's test and the operand of `!` are inert operands: `ToBoolean` runs no code of any value. The router chain then stops at `Object.assign(RouterComponent, { routes: config.routes })`: the route components are stored on a value the project holds (object flow, not this ADR).
**Measured.** rc.21 frozen corpus v2 with ADR 1070 on top, main `7a2457579`: dev U 250,089 → 250,077, std 237,335 → 237,322, V unchanged; coverage: two fixtures lose rows (`clean-lazy-route`'s `<Loading>` pair, an `identity-wrapper-rejections` cleanup whose stored callback is only tested); the `sc4001` repro's loader now hands its namespace on, as the corpus sites it stands for do. Fixtures `namespace-then-named` and its twin `namespace-then-escape`.

| 12 | 248,227 (−1,862) | 235,515 (−1,820) | unchanged | 297 s / 158 s |
| 16 | 248,154 (−1,935), dev only | — | unchanged | 304 s |

## ADR 1073 — A callback literal a reviewed runner schedules is handed to no computation
**The gap.** ADR 0873's `handed_compute` answers `Unplaced { via }` for an async function handed to a call that is no project wrapper. For `it("…", async () => …)` that call is the runner's registration, so the after-await walk started a member for every test callback and filed its reads `function-run-unplaced`. ADR 1065 part 2's census counted about 3,500 such rows (`after-await-member|handed-compute|via=it/test`), all in test files.
**Decision.** `handed_compute` skips a call where all of these hold:
- the function is the literal written directly as its argument;
- the call is a registration `test_runner_callback` answers `Scheduled` for;
- the runner's published JavaScript was read (`test_runner_schedules_by_read_bytes`);
- the literal is no generator, and its own name, if it has one, is used nowhere (`flush_accounting::reentered_by_name`).

This is ADR 1004's premise for the same literal: the runner calls it from its own loop, outside any computation. A callback handed by name or through a helper, a project function named `it`, and `bun:test` (its bytes unread) are unchanged.
**Measured** (rc.21 frozen corpus v2, release, main 84cc06485 against this): development build U 250,089 → 246,813 (−3,276), standard 237,335 → 234,051 (−3,284), V unchanged in both (244, 236). The rows that leave are SC9012 (2,729 dev) and SC1002 (578). Up to 24 SC9012, 7 SC1002 and 1 SC5003 rows stand where a walk row left (the site's next blocker).
**Not covered, measured.** 1,767 B3 test-file rows (compass-ui, expenses-app, inferay) are `bun:test`, whose bytes are unread: they stay. 4,651 more in vitest files (kui, jandibat-web, solid-groove, compass-ui) are registrations `test_runner_callback` does not recognise (`test=no` in the census); that is a separate question (`docs/open-work.md`).
**Evidence.** `after-await-runner-callback`: the `count()` reads in "a read" end; a named callback that stores its own name keeps its row; the existing twins (a wrapper, a binding handed by name, a shadowed `it`, a named callback handed to `createMemo`) keep theirs. Four `test-runner-vitest` variants lose a walk row their own README calls scheduled-callback work. Every row each fixture pins stands.

<a id="adr-1067"></a>
## ADR 1067 — A proven store setter's updater writes its own store

**Decision.** Extend ADR 1053's per-callee draft-write proof to an inline updater of a directly destructured, immutable `createStore` setter. `Dialect::setter_updater_receives_store` answers identity only (Solid 2: `createStore`): rc.21 `@solidjs/signals` `storeSetter` calls `fn(proxy)`. The program separately proves allocation: the constructor's first argument is a fresh closed ordinary object literal, with no spread, computed key, accessor or prototype-setting property. Reuse `simple_array_binding` and the unwritten-binding check; aliases, mutable setters, other tuple slots, foreign seeds and derived-store overloads stay open. ADR 1053 still refuses a written/defaulted callback parameter, `arguments`, `eval`, a member updater callee, and any factory whose standard behavior is unproven, including a shadowed or replaced `Object.assign`.

**Premises.** A raw, stronger form of ADR 0801's tuple premise refuses eval/string-code, obtained array intrinsics, intrinsic hand-offs, window candidates, standard patches and reflective definitions. It reads the hazard index directly: the refined seen-code/iteration answers read standard-member integrity, and cannot justify the same draft proof that integrity depends on. This deliberately leaves more programs uncertifiable. The file scan uses the recorded `files()` view. A store setter's name and type alone prove nothing.

**Source counterexample.** `wrap` also accepts `value[$TARGET].px === value`. A user Proxy can answer every symbol get with `{ px: seed, _fam: null, u: null }` and forward sets to `Number`: the real setter then hands its updater that seed, and `Object.assign` replaces `Number.isFinite`. The rc.21 Node probe confirmed it. Hence no unconditional “a setter draft is runtime allocated” dialect promise; arbitrary seeds remain open. Fixtures pin the forged Proxy and foreign/prototype-setting seeds, plus namespace, shadowed-constructor, mutable-setter, wrong-slot, iterator, shadowed-`Object` and rebound-draft twins. Runtime-oracle cases exercise an ordinary updater and the forged protocol. Fuzz adds the `storesettershadowed` and `storesetterproxy` seam forms and their legal twins; the covering smoke retains both contexts. Rediscovery records this precision gain without claiming a released defect. *Measured* (release, main 84cc06485 against this build, the 34 rc.21 corpus projects): standard U 235,517 and V 236, development U 248,117 and V 244, on both builds; nothing moves, because no corpus setter has a literal seed (app-game `untrack(() => brushToFormValues(…))`, inferay `observer.getCurrentResult()`; `docs/open-work.md`). Fixtures: the two positives (`store-setter-draft-assign`, `-namespace`) lose their `standard-member-impostor` rows (2 to 0 each), the nine twins keep theirs, no violation. Chrome rc.21: the ordinary updater quiet; the forged Proxy reports STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED, covered by uncertifiable rows on both builds.

<a id="adr-1062"></a>
## ADR 1062 — `Function.toString` applied at once generates no code (package scan)
The package scan (`module_reach.rs`) counts any reference of the global `Function` as code generation unless it is `Function.prototype…`, the right of `instanceof` or a comparison. Babel's `_isNativeFunction` helper (`Function.toString.call(fn).indexOf("[native code]") !== -1`), compiled into prosemirror-model and many other packages, made each such package's closure `code-generation` and, through `code_generated`, a writer of any global. The ADR 1061 census found 70 of 192 `Function` problems on the corpus in files with no call of the constructor.
*Decision.* `function_use_is_inert` also admits `Function.name`, `Function.length`, and `Function.toString` when it is the object of a `.call` or `.apply` that is called right there (`to_string_applied`): `Function.prototype.toString` returns a string or throws, neither of which constructs code. Still code generation: `Function.toString` handed on (its `.constructor` is `Function`), `Function["toString"]`, and `Function.call`, `.apply` and `.bind` (applied to `Function` itself they construct code: `Function.apply.call(Function, null, ["code"])`, `Function.bind.apply(Function, [null, "code"])`; Babel's `_construct` fallback `Function.bind.apply(Parent, a)` stays, as its receiver is a value the scan does not follow). The global-member route (`window.Function.toString.call(fn)`) asks the same test.
*Evidence.* Unit tests `function_to_string_is_no_code_generation_and_its_appliers_are` and `members_of_the_global_object_generate_code_and_hand_it_back`. Fixture `function-member-read`: a package whose only `Function` use is `Function.toString.call(fn)`, called in a `createRoot` body, certified (an SC2002 `package-may-call-action:code-generation` row before); `variants/bind` (`Function.bind.apply`) and `variants/held` (`Function.toString` handed on) keep the row. No other fixture moved.

*Corpus measurement, production and development separately* (rc.21 frozen v2, 34 projects each; `fa8f33277` against this slice, one producer, release): violations 244 → 244, uncertifiable rows 251,897 → 251,897; no findings moved. The exemption clears the synthetic fixture, but no complete corpus blocker set.

<a id="adr-1077"></a>
## ADR 1077 — Three reads of the global object are no escape in the package scan
The package scan (ADR 0972/0974, `solid-facts/src/module_reach.rs`) counts a use of the global object it does not follow as an escape: the file may write any global, an accessor under any name included, and every call of a global the libraries declare in a program that loads it is an SC2002 site. Three reads do nothing with the object.
*Decision.* (a) A string-literal `in` test (`"Deno" in globalThis`, `'ontouchstart' in window`) is only inspected (`only_inspected`); a key the syntax does not fix (`k in globalThis`, a template, a number, a call) stays an escape. (b) A reference inside a TypeScript type query (`ReturnType<typeof globalThis.setTimeout>`, `typeof globalThis extends …`) is erased (`in_type_query`); `typeof` written as a value keeps its treatment. (c) A static `x.defaultView` the scan takes for the global object is kept apart (`ModuleScan::default_view_routes`, with the scan without them and its source digest); the walk (`solid-facts-backend/src/package_reach.rs`, `inert_default_views`) leaves one out only for a program file whose source digest matches, where Type Facts prove the read holds no object (its primitive domain, demanded with no symbol observation in `demand_plan.rs`) and the receiver, as written and with assertions peeled, has a closed runtime domain and no library type a document may be (`Document`, its subtypes, its `lib.dom` supertypes, `Object`). A computed key, an `any` or `unknown` receiver, a document under an assertion, installed JavaScript the program does not compile and a file whose bytes differ keep it.
*Evidence.* Fixture `inert-global-reads` (certified) and variants `in-key`, `typeof-value`, `any-receiver`, `document-receiver`, `cast-receiver`, `untyped` (five SC2002 rows each, as on main) and `shadowed` (certified on both). No defect, so no rediscovery entry. *Measured* in the commit message: the census sites leave, 0 verdicts move in both sweep modes; the rows these hold are freed by a later reach-by-load change, not this one.

## ADR 1081 — Not built: a store seed proved fresh through `untrack` and a project function does not lift app-game
ADR 1067 proves a store setter's updater writes only its store for a literal seed. The proposed extension: a seed that is `untrack(() => f(…))` (rc.21 `untrack` returns its callback's result) with `f` a same-file or exactly imported project function whose every return is a fresh literal under the same restrictions, aimed at app-game's `createStore<BrushFormValues>(untrack(() => brushToFormValues(props.brush, colors?.converter())))` (`apps/abr-viewer/src/features/brush-detail/BrushDetailEditable.tsx`). *Measured* (main 84cc06485, release, the project `apps/web/tsconfig.json`, its hazards table): the proof could not lift the project, on three independent grounds. (1) The program holds `RootPatch`, which ADR 1067's raw tuple-integrity premise refuses, so no `createStore` setter of app-game is admitted whatever its seed. (2) `brushToFormValues` reaches the component through `export * from '@app-game/abr-brush/form'` (`brush-form-schema.ts`, a workspace package's star re-export, no same-file or exact import), and its body (`packages/abr-brush/src/form.ts`) returns a literal that spreads `...readFields(featureFields, s)`, which the restrictions refuse. (3) A project lifts only when every open write of its program is proved, and app-game holds 456 `OpenMemberWrite(*)` sites (`packages/abr-brush/src/tipRasterGpu.ts` 31, `packages/abr-paint/src/gpu/abrStamps.ts` 22, `packages/ogl/math/mat-4.ts` 16, …), 79 more under 41 named keys, and 679 `StandardImpostor(*)` sites; the store-merge line is one `OpenMemberWrite(*)` site. inferay's seed, `observer.getCurrentResult()`, is a `@tanstack/query-core` value and stays open. Built, the proof would move no corpus row, so it is not built; `docs/open-work.md` names the blockers.

## ADR 1082 — A runner installed in a linker's store is the package its manifest names
**The gap.** ADR 0438 recognises a registration by where `it`'s declarations lie (`runtime_semantics::test_runner_function_declaration`, path components such as `node_modules/vitest`). jandibat-web's linker installs vitest at `node_modules/.store/vitest-virtual-<slot>/package` behind a `node_modules/vitest` link, and the compiler gives declarations their real path, so `it` there was no runner: 790 distinct after-await sites in its test callbacks stayed uncertifiable (ADR 1065 part 2's census, `test=no`), and so did the reads, writes and dispatches ADR 0438 places.
**Decision.** `SemanticLookup::manifest_spelling`: a declaration path inside a store slot (`solid_facts::package_reach::package_root_of` already reads the layout) is matched as `…/node_modules/<name>/<rest>`, where `name` is the slot's `package.json` `name` the backend read (`PackageReachIndex::name_of`). Any other path, a slot whose manifest was not read, and an adapter with no filesystem keep the path as written: nothing unread is taken for a runner. The runner list, the suite timing and the read-bytes premise are unchanged.
**Measured** (rc.21 frozen corpus v2, release, main 84cc06485 against this): development build U 250,089 → 248,376 (−1,713), standard 237,335 → 235,575 (−1,760), V unchanged (244, 236); every move in jandibat-web (SC1002 794, SC1001 493, SC2002 388, SC9012 23, SC5003 14, SC1003 1 in development), nothing added. The other test-file rows ADR 1073 counted (kui, solid-groove, compass-ui) are in helpers, `vi.fn(async …)` and other hosts, or `bun:test`: not registrations.
**Evidence.** `test-runner-vitest-store` (the published vitest 5.0.5 declarations in a store slot behind a link) gives exactly `test-runner-vitest`'s findings (its SC4001 violation is that fixture's, ADR 0438, same program bytes); `test-runner-vitest-store-renamed` (the slot's manifest names `vitest-fork`) keeps the uncertifiable rows.

<a id="adr-1086"></a>
## ADR 1086 — Every package recognised by path reads a store slot as its manifest names it
**The defect.** ADR 1082 fixed the test-runner registration for a linker's store layout (`node_modules/.store/<slot>/package` behind a `node_modules/<name>` link), but other checks recognised a package by the path segments of a declaration or a file too. The fake-timer census (ADR 0967, F1) is one: with vitest in a store slot, `vi.useFakeTimers()` was not seen, so a flush in a scheduler's callback was certified on `FlushSafe::FreshStack` although the test may advance the clock inside an action's step (FLUSH_IN_ACTION). That is a false clean: fixture `flush-universe-fake-timers-store` lost all nine of `flush-universe-fake-timers`'s rows on the 1082 head.
**Decision.** One helper, `solid_facts::package_reach::installed_spelling` (ADR 1082's rule moved there; `SemanticLookup::installed_spelling` is the build's view), is asked by every check that recognises a package by a declaration's path:
- the runner registration (`registration_root_runner`, ADR 1082);
- the fake-timer library and installer (`declared_by_fake_timer_library`, `flush_accounting::names_fake_timer_installer`);
- Solid's own tags and the census's package names (`declared_in_package` in `components.rs`, `census.rs`);
- stylex's throwing exports and the reviewed vitest matchers (`reviewed_api.rs`; the premise digests still read the real path).

The router's own files (`router_params.rs`: replacement spellings, `history`, the context as `this`) are now known by the package root the project's router imports resolve to (`package_root_of`, which reads store slots), as well as the plain spelling.
**Sweep.** The remaining path checks in the analysis are `contains("/node_modules/")` (installed or not: a store slot is inside `node_modules`) and `route_components.rs`'s audited install directories (real paths): neither names a package by its directory.
**Measured** (rc.21 frozen corpus v2, release, the 1082 head against this): both builds unchanged (development U 248,376, V 244; standard U 235,575, V 236). No corpus project combines a store-slot vitest with fake timers and a flush, and jandibat-web's store-slot `solid-js` moves nothing through the tag checks.
**Evidence.** `flush-universe-fake-timers-store` gives `flush-universe-fake-timers`'s nine rows. Unit test `a_store_slot_is_spelled_as_its_manifest_names_it`. Rediscovery: `outside` (the generator writes no install layout, and vitest cannot load in the oracle's page), entry in `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json`. No Chrome case: the runtime half is ADR 0967's vitest run.

## ADR 1084 — The blocker census names the plain-receiver sub-fact a member read after an await fails (census only)
ADR 1065 part 2 records, for an SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` row listed as a member read, only the root's kind. `member_reads::root_is_plain` is three disjuncts (a primitive proven from the root's own expression, `value_origin` = `Builtin`, an unpatched ECMAScript global), so the census could not say which fact a proof would have to supply.
*Decision.* Under `SOLID_CHECKER_BLOCKER_CENSUS=1` the row's cause carries `plain:<sub-fact>` (`member_reads::plain_failure`): for a root no declaration binds, the global test (`global:not-ecmascript`, `global:builtins-touched`); for a call or member root, `call:<callee>` or `member`; else what `value_origin` stopped on, followed through the root's binding: `origin:project-class`, `binding:parameter`, `binding:import`, `binding:mutable`, `binding:destructured`, `binding:none` (a declaration the binding table does not hold), `init:none` (a `for … of` head), `init:builtin-shared` (a fresh built-in the binding does not keep closed), `init:call:<callee>`, `init:await:call:<callee>`, `init:object-literal`, `init:member`, `init:other`. A callee is `std:<qualified name>`, `package:<package>`, `project-method`, `project-function`, `project-other:<declaration kind>` or `unresolved`, with `construct:` before a constructor. No verdict reads it.
*Measured* (rc.21 frozen corpus v2, dev, release build of main 84cc06485 with ADR 1065 part 2 and this): 34 of 34 projects identical off and on, dev (U 250,089, V 244) and no runtime flags (U 237,335, V 236); 5,993 member-read rows carry a sub-fact. By family: result of a project function or method 1,654 (`await` of a project method 496, a local call of a function declaration 417, `await` of one 340); parameter 1,138; result of an unresolved call 709; result of a package call 573 (openapi-hooks 190 in error-menu-web); member of another value 342; destructured binding 269; `let`/`var` 228; a global that is no ECMAScript global (`window`, `document`, `this`) 223; `for … of` head 179; a fresh built-in not kept closed 110; object literal 86; a standard call that is no reviewed value constructor (`await fetch()`) 49.
*Not built.* The top family is no precision gap: `value_origin` already follows an exact project call and asks that its returns be built-in; these return app data, and calling it plain needs a proof of what the function returns, which the owner's full rule (2026-11-15) leaves as sites. A parameter is a site by the same rule.

## ADR 1089 — The harness's entry leaves the namespace loop out when the mount names every entered export
**The gap.** In audit 44148527547 (main f544561a8), 50 of the 85 lg-base `-direct-none` programs were uncertifiable while all 201 misuse ones were proved. In 40 of them the rows rest on the census's `handoff|open-world-export` (ADR 1065). The cause is the harness, not the program: `main.tsx` mounts `C1` by name and then still runs `for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(mod))`, which hands App's namespace to code the checker cannot read. A closed boundary changes nothing: the install's private manifest already closes the program.
**Decision.** `mainSource` (scripts/runtime-oracle.mjs) takes the exports the loop would enter (scripts/fuzz/checker.mjs `enteredExports`, ADR 0990). When the mount names all of them, the entry has no `import * as mod` and no loop. The oracle writes that text from the case's App.tsx, and the checker's entry (`mainSourceFor`) is read from the same template. The Chrome hosts mount through the namespace at run time in the same sorted order, so what runs is unchanged. A program with another entered export, or with exports the text cannot classify (`null`), keeps the loop. `ENTRY_VERSION = 2` is recorded beside `GENERATOR_VERSION` in matrix.json and in the audit's manifests. Program ids and seeds are unchanged.
*Evidence.* Every grid program has a mount, so the entry changed for all of them. Per-program outcomes of the release build of e2d9d4a8f, old entry against new:
- lg-base: 3,516 uncertifiable → clean, no other move. Clean went from 5,800 to 9,316; the `-direct-none` programs from 35 to 66 clean of 85.
- lg-src: no moves.
- mx-base: no moves (27,816 agree).
- mx-src: no moves (22,161 agree).
- Recall samples (about 2,500 each): lg-recall 125 uncertifiable → clean, mx-recall no moves (its 2 `unplaced` are ADR 1076's pk-lazy class on both entries).

Real Chrome: focus's oracle sample compared 84 moved lg-base programs, and every moved `-direct-none` target (31) was compared on its own. All showed 0 behaviour differences. The proved ledger only gains, so `changes.json` needs no row; no known entry stores a moved id. Still uncertifiable among the 50: the pending guarded reads, SC9012 `value-in-carrier` on `*-refresh`, SC1002 after-await setters, and the `resolve`/`until` handler forms.

## ADR 1090 G1 — Not built: a read after an await in a function whose promise nothing consumes
**The gap.** After ADR 1089, 246 lg-base programs were still uncertifiable on SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted`. Their blockers were an async helper called from a component (123) and a `Promise.resolve().then` handler (123). The proposal: rc.21 warns UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT only when the read's async stack holds an async computation's flight frame (`attributedFlight`, dev-shared.js), so a read in a function whose promise nothing consumes can carry none.
**Decision: not built.** The reason `AfterAwaitSafe::PromiseUnconsumed` went through four Fable reviews, and each found false cleans:
- be4990c64: a `Promise` subclass that keeps its instances (F1), a loop that reads before its await (F2), a direct `eval` call (F3), and classic-script globals.
- aa617ea2a: a class field initializer (G1), and type-only module syntax (G2).
- 229d00f0c: a helper that returns a class (H1), module syntax that esbuild erases (H2), and a JSX getter (H3).
- efa177b5a: a project function named `__solidAsyncCompute_1`, which rc.21 attributes by name alone (I1); a direct read handing on a helper-built class (I2); and a store read that returns a function, or a spoofed `equals` (I3).

rc.21 attributes a read to a flight by the frame's name and stack. So "nothing consumes the promise" does not bound where the function's reads run, and the discharge is removed: no site is ended by it.
*What stays.* The ADR 1087 flight census (internal only). The fixtures `after-await-promise-unconsumed` and `-eval` keep every review case as uncertifiable, and the misuse twin stays a violation. The fuzz cells `pu-then-sub`, `pu-loop` and `pu-class` (`scripts/fuzz/pu-shapes.mjs`, with the `loop-await-pre` control form and the `then` receiver option) are recall-gap. Their rediscovery entries are marked superseded. Against main 91eab81ac, corpus and fuzz show no clean gained.

**Part E (step 0: decision not to build).** `resolve-in-reactive-scope-handler-x` and `until-in-reactive-scope-handler-x` stay uncertifiable on SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted`, and so does any creation written in an intrinsic element's `on*={() => …}` handler (`createMemo` and `createRoot` too). The role engine places the handler as an `EventCallback`, off every effect apply's stack. But `owner_emission::layer_entry_open` takes an anonymous function that is neither called in place nor a call argument (a JSX attribute value) as entered by a route the owner graph does not model. The premise that would close it, "entered only by event delivery", would need a guard: rc.21 `@solidjs/web` delegation stores the handler on the element (`$$click`), and code holding a ref can read it. A what-if that skips the open answer for such a function, measured on main 76477c121's release build:
- corpus, both modes: 0 rows; the path is not reached once in dev mode;
- legal fuzz grids: 850 programs whose only blocker it is: lg-base 240, lg-combo 605, the lg-recall sample 5, and lg-src none. By code: RESOLVE_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE 213, UNTIL_IN_REACTIVE_SCOPE 209, REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE 107, then 43 or fewer each.

Under the coordinator's rule (build only above about 200 corpus rows), it is not built. The two `-direct-none` programs are uncertifiable for this reason, and stop counting as open. Recorded in `docs/open-work.md` §2.

## ADR 1091 — A JSX tag in the component's own file hands the component to no code nothing follows
**The gap.** ADR 1088's second cause: SC1001 reads in a component's local helper, read only in a JSX child, placed nowhere by `runs_unplaced_exhaustive` (ADRs 0673/0674). The hidden-hand-off test (`function_escapes_unfollowed`) judges the component by the same-file references of its binding, and `hand_off_at` classed a JSX tag (`<Content />`) as `Unfollowed`, its default. A component a tag in another file renders has no same-file reference and was proved, so the same code was proved or not by which file held the tag. The smallest case: `function Content() { const [c] = createSignal(0); const shown = () => c() > 0; return <p>{shown() ? "yes" : "no"}</p>; }` rendered as `<Content />` by an exported parent `render` mounts.
**Decision.** In that test only, a reference that is a JSX element's tag (a plain identifier, no intrinsic element, opening or closing) is no hand-off. Solid's `createComponent` runs the component during the render that holds the tag, which the render roles place. Every other reference keeps its class (a copy, an array element, a default export: the component stays uncertifiable), and the other consumers of `hand_off_at` are unchanged.
**Measured** (rc.21 frozen corpus v2, release, main e2d9d4a8f against this): development build U 250,089 → 249,990 (−99: SC1001 89, SC5001 5, SC9012 3, SC5003 2), standard 237,335 → 237,243 (−92); V unchanged (244, 236); nothing added. jandibat-web `ConnectionsRelayPage.tsx` keeps 4 of its 8 SC1001 rows: the rest of ADR 1088's 334 have another escape or blocker.
**Fuzzer.** The legal grid had no such program (its `helper` layer is a module helper and its `closure` layer sits inside the JSX child), so STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED has a new legal context, `jsx-helper`: a body `const` read in a JSX child, over the grid's mounts. lg-base, main against this: its 336 programs were `root` 72 clean, 12 uncertifiable and `child`/`show`/`for` 84 uncertifiable each; now 72 clean and 12 uncertifiable on every mount (the 12 are hook-member bindings, the `root` mount's blocker). The oracle shows 0 behaviour and 0 attribution differences.
**Evidence.** Fixture `jsx-helper-child-component`: `Content` proved; `Copied` (also copied and called) and `Listed` (also in an exported array) uncertifiable; `BodyRead` keeps its SC1001 violation.

## ADR 1090 — A flush in exact in-place layers is placed at the outermost layer's call
*The layer above the base (owner order: certify the simplest correct programs bottom-up).* In `lg-base` (12,024 legal programs, main 34473465d), 2,392 programs are uncertifiable while their own `-direct-none` sibling is clean. The largest group (2,214, every `-m-child`/`-m-show`/`-m-for` mount) shares ADR 1089's cause, the harness handing the module to unread code (`open-world-export`), and waits for that fix. The next, 312 programs, is a `flush()` written in a wrapper layer inside a timer's callback (`setTimeout(() => { const f1 = () => { flush(); }; f1(); }, 0)`): SC2006, SC2008 and SC3001 uncertifiable while `setTimeout(() => { flush(); }, 0)` is clean, because the flush accounting asked its class questions (ADR 0973's `FreshStack` and the others) only of a flush with a census class of its own.

*Decision.* `flush_accounting.rs` `climbed_caller`: a flush the census gives no class is placed through `climb_in_place_layers` (an IIFE, a named function called once, a helper's callback it calls in its body) and asked at the outermost layer's call, with that call's census class (`flush_caller_of_layer_call`). The climb must cross at least one layer, no layer may hold the site in a parameter list, be also handed on (`among_others`), follow an await, or be withheld or an unmodelled slot; otherwise the site keeps its row. A layer also called from elsewhere is no single-call layer, so the climb stops before it.

*Evidence.* Probe (release, main 34473465d against this change, every FLUSH program of `lg-base` and `mx-base`, 1,200): 312 move uncertifiable to clean, all legal (`FLUSH_IN_ACTION`, `FLUSH_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK`, `FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK`, 104 each); no misuse program moves. Chrome rc.21 (`focus.mjs --runtime-diff all`): 12 sampled moved legal programs clean, the misuse twins `mx-flush-in-action-action-x-direct-closure` and `mx-flush-in-tracked-queue-callback-tracked-x-direct-closure` agree. Fixture `flush-in-place-layers`: a closure, a helper and an IIFE in a timer clean; a closure also handed on and a helper also called from an action's step uncertifiable.

## ADR 1080 — A navigation delivers only the event types the host fact names
ADR 0705 put `History.go` and `Location.assign`/`reload`/`replace` in the synchronous dispatch tables, so each such call raised the program-wide dispatch veto: every event handler's owner, read, flush and listener proofs withheld, whatever the handler's event (R5's report: `@solidjs/router`'s three `history.go` lines carry it in about 17 projects).
*The host fact* (`runtime_semantics::synchronously_delivered_event_types`, by exact `lib.dom` qualified name): `History.go` and `Location.reload` deliver at most `beforeunload` before they return; `Location.assign` and `Location.replace` at most `beforeunload` or `popstate`. Measured in Chromium (the oracle's playwright 1.60 build): `history.go(0)`, `location.reload()` and `location.assign` to another document fire `beforeunload` before returning; `history.go(±1)` fires nothing synchronously, same- or cross-document; `location.assign("#a")`, `location.replace("#b")` and `location.hash = …` fire `popstate` before returning, so the brief's "`Location.*` deliver only `beforeunload`" holds for `reload` only. Every other member delivers any type, as before.
*The decision.* A dispatch site whose member has known types is `DispatchReceiver::NoListener` (excluded from every veto bit, as ADR 0640's anchor) when nothing in the program as read may listen for any of them (`program_listens_for_any`, the ADR 0640 census with the types as a parameter): a `body`/`html` JSX `on*` handler, an `on<type>` assignment or literal key, a computed member on a DOM global, an `addEventListener` reached any way unless its call names another type. A call names another type when its first argument's literal fact is another string (compared without case), or a plain parameter of the function it is written in whose every reference, in any file, is a direct call in this file passing such a literal at that position (`@solidjs/router`'s `bindEvent`: `popstate`, `hashchange`, `scroll`, `pagehide`, `pageshow`, `load`), or the target is a non-DOM one the census already excludes. A bare `addEventListener` that is an inert operand (`typeof addEventListener === "function"`, the router's `data/liveQuery.js`) registers nothing; that holds for the click census too. One listener for one of the types keeps the site withholding every handler's proofs, not only that type's (a coarser cut than per handler). Premise, as ADR 0640's: a listener only code the build does not read registers is not seen.
*Measured* (release, main 34473465d against this build, the 34 rc.21 corpus projects): standard U 230,355 to 230,354 (ai-memory-ui, `listener-reach` −1), V 236 unchanged; development U 242,921 to 242,838 (−83: sensor-sim −65, helge-dev −14, spookysoftware-www −2, ai-memory-ui −1, spotify-desk-thing −1; `package-may-call-action` −23, `package-value-read` −17, `package-finding-at-entry` −16, `function-run-unplaced` −24, `listener-reach` −3), V 244 unchanged; nothing added. R5's estimate (697-2,945) does not hold: the census still finds a possible `beforeunload` listener in donegeon-client (`window.addEventListener(OPEN_EVENT, show)`, `OPEN_EVENT` a `const` string) and in kui's ten projects (`source.addEventListener(SseEventNames.Error, …)` on a non-standard receiver, keys of a constant table), and the other router projects pass the census but keep their rows for reasons not traced here (another dispatch site of the program, or another blocker of the same rows). A `const` string's value has no fact yet (`docs/open-work.md`). Fixtures `navigation-delivers-beforeunload` and `-helper` (the handler's SC2001 and SC1001 certified, `function-run-unplaced` on main); `-listener`, `-property`, `-computed`, `-popstate`, `-helper-open` keep both rows. No violation moved, so no Chrome case.

## ADR 1092 — The Chrome oracle page records the phase its run failed in
**The artifact.** The fuzzer's fast runners (`scripts/fuzz/fast/runner.tsx`, `chrome-host/runner.tsx`) name a failure by the phase it ended in: `import` while App.tsx's module graph evaluates, `render` while the entry mounts, then the run. The oracle's page had no phases: a run that failed was `execution` (`chrome.mjs` `chromeRuntime`). A `-mount-named` program whose module-scope `render` reads a pending value with no boundary throws while App.tsx evaluates; the fast runners said `import`, the oracle waited out the 12 s settle step and said `execution`, and the differential (`runtime-diff.mjs`, which compares phase names) flagged four mx-census programs as behaviour differences that were the same failure.
**Decision.** A halt-marker case (the fuzzer's) gets a third page module, `sc-phase.ts` (`runtime-oracle.mjs` `phaseModule`), loaded last and outside the case's tsconfig, so the checker never reads it. It waits for the entry through the module map (`import("/main.tsx")` returns the entry the page already evaluated, never a second one) and writes `<output id="sc-phase">`: `entered`, `import` (the same lookup of App.tsx rejects), `render` (App.tsx evaluated, the entry's own body threw) or `entry` (App.tsx was never fetched, so it is not looked up). The scenario reads it first. `hits.mjs` `phaseAtFailure` turns a failure at the settle step into that phase (`exercise` once the entry evaluated); a failure at any other step, or with no phase read, stays `execution`. The oracle row carries it as `pagePhase`. No timeout is reclassified and no phase is inferred from a message.
**Evidence.** The four programs (`rediscovery.json`) differ on origin/main 34473465d (`failure happy import chrome execution`) and agree on the fix; unit tests in `chrome.test.mjs`.
**Part C (refresh).** Six `*-refresh` programs stayed uncertifiable on SC9012 `value-in-carrier` at the accessor handed to `refresh(m1)`. In rc.21, `refresh(target)` reads `target[$REFRESH]`, the node `accessor()` stores as an own property on every Solid accessor. It marks that node, and resolves its promise from a `watch` over the node, never from `target` (`@solidjs/signals` `dist/dev.js:3237-3240, 3636-3710`). The waiter is a computed, not a render effect, so its pending read cannot raise `ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY` (only `EFFECT_RENDER` emits it, `:2679-2700`). The dialect now answers `argument_is_untouched_target(Refresh, 0)`, and value-use ends a function value's walk there (`Mode::Value` only: a store root's property read is the store proxy's).
*Evidence.* Fixture `refresh-target-untouched` covers four cases:
- the direct call and the namespace member are proved;
- an accessor also handed to an unread function stays open;
- `refresh` in a component body keeps its SC2001 violation.

Coverage moved 34 findings, all removals: 33 SC9012 `value-in-carrier` at exact `refresh` arguments (aliases of ADR 0901 included), and one SC5003 at `refresh(state)` in the sc2001 repro, sound for the waiter's reason above.
Grids, REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE (the only code that generates `refresh`), build before C against build with C, same entry. Legal programs moved uncertifiable → clean only, 2,610 in all:

| Grid | Moved |
|---|---|
| lg-base | 712 |
| lg-src | 1,570 |
| lg-combo | 261 |
| lg-recall sample (2,503) | 67 |

mx-base, mx-src, mx-combo and the mx-recall sample (2,488) did not move. Chrome compared 98 moved programs: 0 differences. Corpus, both modes: 14 uncertifiable fewer each (dev 250,089 → 250,075; std 237,335 → 237,321), all at `refresh` arguments (viviana-ui-web 8, app-game 3, hoxxes-briefing 3, one of them SC5008, a pending read at the same argument). Violations are unchanged (244 dev, 236 std). Full recall grids are left to the nightly audit.

## ADR 1094 — Not built: a constant string's value for listener event types frees no corpus row
ADR 1080's census reads a registration's event type from its literal fact or a helper parameter its callers fill with literals, and treats any other type as possibly a delivered one. Its measured blockers were a `const` string (donegeon-client `window.addEventListener(OPEN_EVENT, show)`) and a constant table's key (kui `source.addEventListener(SseEventNames.Error, …)`). The proposal: an exact "string value of a constant" fact (a `const` binding, an `as const` or readonly member, or an enum member with a string-literal initializer, through exact symbols across imports and re-exports; anything mutable, computed, spread, reassigned, `let`, non-literal or unresolved gives no value), used by the census. *Measured first* (release, ADR 1080's build cfbda64a8 on main 34473465d, the 12 corpus projects of donegeon-client and kui, standard and development modes): a temporary build that reads every identifier or non-computed member event type as another event (an upper bound on any such fact) moves net 0 rows in both modes (standard U 53,141 and development U 53,931, V 53, unchanged; kui `frontend/packages/shell` relabels one row, `listener-reach` to `read-after-await-unaccounted`). The census fires for these types in no other corpus project (ADR 1080's census trace), so the rest of the corpus cannot move either. The rows there rest on more than the listener census, so the fact is not built.
**Part 5 (two of the ledgered SC7002/SC4002 families).** (1) A refusal reached through a helper counts for SC7002 when it refuses every run: the function written around the creation is named, synchronous, not exported, its value current, and every reference to it is the exact call that anchors an SC3001 violation whose `sites` hold the creation (`competing_checks.rs` `every_run_refused`): `tracked-sibling-async` (2 rows; part 2 dropped every helper route, since a render or other caller may reach the probe first, which this asks). (2) A site written directly in the apply of a primitive that runs it first at creation under the caller's owner and later in the effect phase with no owner (`Dialect::callback_reruns_in_effect_phase`: `createRenderEffect`), that is no completion site of that apply (an earlier `return`, `throw`, branch may skip it on the owned first run): SC7002 and SC4002 are uncertifiable there, since every later run meets the effect-callback guard or the owner check first (`later_render_apply_run_only`): `render-apply-guarded-rerun` (2 SC7002, 1 SC4002). Fixture `competing-check-sync-memo`: `MemoInTrackedHelper`, `MemoInTrackedOnlyHelper`, `MemoInGuardedRenderApply` U; `MemoInRenderApply` (straight line), `MemoInTrackedAndBodyHelper` (the body calls first) V. Chrome `runtime-oracle/competing-check-{sync-sibling-helper,sync-render-guarded,context-render-guarded}`: the earlier code only; `competing-check-sync-render-straight`: SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC. The 70 ledgered ids: these 5 to not-fired, 65 still ledgered; smoke mx-census: nothing else moves. The tracked-sibling-async twins are not in the census smoke manifest (a whole-census `smoke.mjs record` adds them; deferred). The rest of the families, ranked by a Fable read (2026-11-18): an apply's open extent (cbp-apply, 6), a module slot's call in the effect-phase walk (flw-apply-slot-module, 2), the leaf walk's open extent through events, props and actions (42), caller order over shared helpers (4), cleanup at rerun (6).
**Part 6 (two more ledgered families).** (1) A site written directly in the cleanup an effect's apply returns, when the effect may rerun (`directly_in_rerun_effect_cleanup`, ADR 0539's `WindowedCleanup::MayRerun`; no in-place climb, since an exhausted climb would answer yes): a rerun calls the cleanup inside the effect callback, where the creation meets the guard first, and nothing orders it against the disposal that calls it outside; an effect whose compute provably tracks nothing (`effect_never_reruns`) keeps its violation (`effect-cleanup-rerun*`, `render-cleanup-rerun`: 6 rows; the first build used the climbing reading and moved `sole-chain-17`, a 17-helper chain from an owned render, agree to recall-gap). (2) `every_run_refused` takes a generator handed to `action(...)` (the leaf walk's own recognition, `stepped_action_generator`), the `const` it initializes local or unexported and unwritten: each call of the action steps the generator under its caller's owner, so a leaf owner's refusal persists (rc.21 `dev.js` 2336-2341 lowers only the effect flag): `action-from-settled`, `action-from-tracked` (4 rows); an action an apply calls keeps its violation. Fixture `competing-check-sync-memo`: `MemoInRerunCleanup`, `MemoInActionFromSettled` U; `MemoInNeverRerunCleanup`, `MemoInActionFromApply` V. Chrome `runtime-oracle/competing-check-sync-{rerun-cleanup,action-settled}`: the earlier code only; `-{dispose-cleanup,action-apply}`: SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC. Ledgered ids: 10 more to not-fired (falsePositive 65 to 55); smoke mx-census (seed 777, 41,272 programs): nothing else moves. Correction to part 1's comment: a halt does not stop a later creation from probing (rc.21 `halted` gates only `schedule` and `flush`); the leaf-refusal rule for owner rows stays (U is fail-closed), its rationale is the unordered runs, not the halt.
