**The gap.** ADR 0297's default (`defaults_to_dependency_sources`, `main.rs`): an ordinary run with a declared target and build reads every Solid package from source; a run with `--feedback-facts` (the fuzz judge's `CHECKER_ARGS`, the development feedback) did not. So the two analyzed different programs. Mac 23's `q-anyat` showed it as "no standard-library declaration resolves in the user's run": its package names `solid-js` and writes `Array.prototype[key]` under a run-time key; read as source (the user's run), that write is a patch of any member, and `resolved_callee_call` withholds every standard call (`patch_vetoed`, `impostor_veto`), which is the fail-closed answer; unread (the judge's run), it is not in the program and the calls resolve. A control package that names Solid and patches nothing resolves every standard call in both modes (measured with a probe build: `Array.at`, `ArrayConstructor.construct`, `PromiseConstructor.resolve`, `StringConstructor.call`). On the rc.21 frozen corpus v2 (dev, main dba9d3cee) 31 of 34 projects had different findings in the two modes.
**Step 0 (no verdict change): the feedback facts under a selection.** `development_feedback::models` emits per file its path and hash, its functions (span, body, parent, `async`, generator), its calls, the result and allocation relevance (returns, bindings and references of the file: syntax), and `derivedOrigin` (a callback handed to an exactly resolved tracked primitive: `primitive_at_call`, the one semantic fact). Each holds under a selection for the project's own files: the syntax does not depend on it, and `derivedOrigin` was compared on the corpus with `--feedback-facts` against `--feedback-facts --dependency-source '*'`: project-file models identical in 34 of 34 projects. Withheld: models of the selected packages' files (1,194 on the corpus), which a run without the selection never had and the host does not instrument.
**Decision.** `defaults_to_dependency_sources` no longer excludes `--feedback-facts`, and `models` skips files in dependency source. The default's refusal fallback is the one an ordinary run takes.
**Gate.** Fixture `fact-mode-parity` (a package that names `solid-js` and writes `Array.prototype[key]`; a declared host and the Solid Vite plugin) and process test `fact_mode_parity_process.rs`: the runs with and without `--feedback-facts` give equal status, findings and hazards (SC9012 `standard-member-impostor` at the `at` call in both), and the feedback models are the project's files only. On main the feedback run reported SC9005 `package-source-unavailable` and no SC9012 there.
**Measured.** Smoke (`focus --smoke`, seed 1135, every grid, mx-recall and lg-recall included, Chrome off), main against this build: 116,355 programs in both, no outcome and no (site, code) moved (the harness already checks a case that ships a package as a user's run, `ORDINARY_ARGS`; the other programs import only Solid's own runtime, which the default does not select); the same 10 pre-existing rows need a look on both. Corpus (rc.21 frozen v2, release, main dba9d3cee against this build): `make corpus-delta --all`, dev, a user's run: V 244 and U 396,007 to 396,004, nothing needs a look; the 3 are app-game's `pending-read-unresolved`, which varies run to run on main itself (open work). std (no host): byte-equal in 33 of 34, app-game again only by that variance, totals equal (U 382,930, V 236). The judge's run (this build with `--feedback-facts`) against a user's run of main: byte-equal in 33 of 34 projects, totals equal (U 396,007, V 244); before, 31 of 34 differed.

## ADR 1141 — A delegated handler a spread reaches on a control disabled from mount is not proven to run (SC4001)
**The defect** (live on main a64fc92ad). ADR 1134 refused every control with a spread, so `createEffect` in the `onClick` of `<button disabled {...rest}>` (its own fixture's `StillRuns` case, `rest = { title: "t" }`) or in an `onClick` a spread literal holds (`<button disabled {...{ onClick: () => … }}>`) stayed an SC4001 `missing-owner` violation. With a spread the compiler hands every attribute and spread to rc.21's `spread` as one array of sources (`spread(el, [{ disabled: true }, rest, { onClick: f }])`); `assignProp` (`web.dev.js` 1919) stores a key `on` + upper-case letter whose lower-cased event is in `DelegatedEvents` (36) for the dispatcher, which skips a disabled node (1975): Chrome is quiet.
**Decision.** A Dialect question, `spread_event_delegated` (Solid 2's audited spread keys: that list), and in `disabled_handlers.rs` a control with spreads counts when it is one of ADR 1134's elements with one bare or `{true}` `disabled` and no `ref`, and every spread's own keys are proven (`spread_own_keys`: a closed object literal in place, or an unwritten `const` initialized by one that ADR 0358's spread resolution accepts) with no `disabled`, `ref` or namespaced key; the row moves when its operation is in the control's own `on…` attribute whose key is delegated, or in one of ADR 0358's exact targets of an in-place literal spread every listener key of which (the facts' cooked keys) is delegated. ADR 1134's program-wide enable scan still applies. Only V to U (`handler-on-disabled-control`); anything else keeps its row.
**Evidence.** Fixture `disabled-spread-handler-owner`: `SpreadDisabled` (the `{...rest}` case, a spread literal's `onClick`, an `input`'s `onKeyDown` beside `{...{ title: "t" }}`) violations on main, uncertifiable here; `SpreadStillRuns` keeps 4 violations (a spread holding `disabled: false`, unproven keys, a spread's `onWheel`, the driven twin). Chrome rc.21 (runtime-oracle case of the same name): NO_OWNER_EFFECT at the 4 `SpreadStillRuns` handlers only, no TypeScript error. `disabled-handler-owner` drops its spread case to this fixture. Fuzz: new legal context `dny-legal-mount-disabled-spread`; lg-recall focus, main 4 `unexecuted-violation` rows (exit 1), here none (exit 0); `rediscovery.json` lists the ids.
**Not covered** (keep a violation): a spread of a value whose keys are not a literal (props, a call, `Object.freeze`), a literal in another file's `const` holding the handler, a handler named by reference, and ADR 1134's list.

## ADR 1140 — A handler a later source of its element overrides is not proven attached (SC4001)
**The defect.** `<button {...{ onClick: () => { createRenderEffect(…) } }} onClick={…}>`: a literal-spread handler that a later source of the same element supplies under its key (a later attribute, a later spread, `onClick={undefined}`) was an SC4001 `missing-owner` violation. ADR 0358 places the literal's `on…` functions as attached handlers with a proven-unowned run, and nothing asked whether the key survives. The handler is never attached and never runs: a false positive on main a64fc92ad.
**The source.** rc.21 `@solidjs/web` `dist/web.dev.js` (integrity `sha512-1E9dvR3…GUA==`): an element with a spread compiles to `spread(el, [source, …], true)` with its spreads and attributes as sources in source order, and `collectProps` (980) skips a key that `sourceHas` finds in any later source (986), whatever its value. An attribute written before a literal spread holding its key is overridden the same way, and is TS2783 when the spread's key is not optional.
**Decision.** Dialect question `spread_skips_key_a_later_source_has` (Solid 2: true; default true, so an unaudited runtime proves no attachment). `overridden_handlers.rs` asks whether a later source of an intrinsic element may supply a key: a later attribute of that name does; a later spread does unless it is a closed object literal written in the spread without the key or its declared key set is complete without it (ADR 0436's premise); anything else may. An overridden spread-literal handler (`owner_discovery`) and an overridden attribute handler (its edge there and its seed in `owner_graph`) take `MayBeUnowned`, the bare unowned bit, so a helper it calls is no proven-unowned run either; a pass over the final owner rows, beside ADR 1134's, names every row written inside such a handler `handler-key-overridden`. A row only moves from a violation to an obligation, never to a clean. W6's ADR 1129 changes the spread proof itself (`SpreadTargetsAt`); this change stays in the placement.
**Evidence.** Fixture `overridden-spread-handler`: `Overridden` (later attribute, later spread, later `undefined`), `AttributeOverridden` and the overridden `Helpers` move V to U; `StillAttached` (a later `title`, a later literal without the key, a later `onDblClick`, the key only in an earlier spread) and the attached helper keep their violations. Chrome (runtime-oracle `overridden-spread-handler`): nothing at any overridden handler, NO_OWNER_EFFECT at every attached one, each covered. Generator contexts `dny-legal-spread-overridden-{attr,spread,undefined}` (lg-recall, 207 programs): main has 12 unexecuted-violation rows, this build none (rediscovery.json).
**Not covered.** A row in a spread-literal handler whose literal is declared in another file than the element keeps the U from its edge but not the blocker's name. A later spread the checker cannot read (an unresolved value, an open declared type) demotes the earlier handler's violation even where the value never holds the key (recall only).

## ADR 1128 — A start's verdict does not depend on the worker or the order that walked it
**The defect.** app-game's SC5003 `pending-read-unresolved` at `strokeDrawing.ts:8365` (`samples.push(…)`) flipped in about one run in eighteen of a corpus run, and the project's counts moved by tens of rows between identical runs on the default worker count: five runs gave five reports (141,149 findings in four), the row always there and its message naming another accessor each time (`additions()`, `msaa()`, `mode()`, `this value`, `root()`). A run on one worker answered alike twice, and another order of the same starts answered otherwise.
**The cause.** ADR 0909's contract is that a start's answer is a function of the build and the start alone, so the value-use census carries one `Census` per analysis worker from start to start. It broke at `run_past_withheld` (ADR 0876): the walks past a call a reached patch withholds queue late walks and rows (ADR 1104: a `for…of` binding's name, a position, a computed call) as the earlier walks do, and `run_escapes` ran the queue only for the earlier ones. `begin_start` asserted the other queues empty and not `late` and `late_rows`, so the start the worker took next ran the leftover under its own source, `carried`, `async_walk` and memo, which start that was followed the atomic claim counter of `parallel_balanced_with_state_from`, its rows were named for that start's reach (`pending_accounting` names the first reach in start order), and the last start of each worker dropped its queue, so the worker count moved rows too. On app-game one worker had 70 of 9,999 starts begin with leftover work (235 items, mostly ADR 1104's `for…of` names and ADR 1106's pattern parameters, in many files) and no other per-start field leaked.
**The reproduction, without a scheduler.** `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_CLAIM_ORDER=forward|reverse|rotate:<n>|shuffle:<seed>` names the order the claims are taken in (`pipeline::claim_permutation`, serial and threaded path; the results come back in input order; a misspelled order panics, so a check never compares a run with itself). On one worker the unfixed build gave 141,172 findings forward and 141,168, 141,166 and 141,171 under reverse and two shuffles, the row at 8365 naming `root()`, `running()`, `b()` and `position()`.
**The decision.** The late walks and rows a start's walks past a withheld call queue are that start's, and run before it ends: `run_past_withheld` runs them twice, once on those walks' memo (ADR 0876's "memo and budget of its own", as `run_escapes` runs the earlier ones on theirs) and once on the start's own memo, and keeps the rows of both. One memo is not enough: a late walk on the withheld walks' memo stops at every position those walks already answered, and a start that ran past the step budget answered some without having explored what lies past them, so it reaches fewer open uses there than a walk that explores them again under a budget of its own. The review of the first cut found them (app-game, one start, `virtual-tree.ts` 1588-3216, `cut`: the late name at `createDnd.ts` 4739 walks 26 steps and places no row on the withheld walks' memo and 194 steps and 33 rows on the start's own): 13 uses reached only by the second, none only by the first, so the union is the fail-closed choice and a row is only ever added. `begin_start` destructures the census without `..`, so a new field has to be classed: the build, a cache that answers from the build alone, or the start's own state (empty here), and drops a queue it finds rather than run it as this start's; `end_start` fails closed where one is left (the start is cut, so its caller files the budget row, the rows placed stay its own) with a debug assertion. A census per start (the walks' leftover dropped) is deterministic as well and loses rows silently, the false-clean direction (app-game: 41 rows fewer than the fix on main 5c1435e8c, and at the first measure the SC5003 at 8365 gone), and was not taken.
**The gate.** `rust/crates/solid-facts-backend/tests/verdict_determinism_process.rs` repeats the unit of `fixtures/reactive-ir/census-claim-order` (two copies of a start whose walks past a withheld call leave a `for…of` name queued, reduced by delta debugging from a corpus tree mapper; reverse and a shuffle give another report on the unfixed build) 48 times, past the 64-start threshold at which the starts run on several workers, and holds workers 1, 3 and the default × five claim orders and three repeats to the first report, byte for byte; the unfixed code fails it with the rows that moved, and an unknown order is refused. `scripts/determinism-check.mjs` is the same on any project or on the corpus (`--corpus`): every `(workers, order)` and repeat against the first run, with the findings that moved. `scripts/fuzz/rediscovery.json` says why no generated program can express it (`outside`).
**Evidence.** app-game, release build of the fix on main 5c1435e8c: 8 runs (workers 1 and default × forward, reverse and two shuffles) and 18 default-worker runs give one report (hash ab78db7086, 26 runs); the unfixed build at the same tree gave 8 distinct reports in the same 8 runs and 18 distinct reports in 18 default-worker runs. Corpus delta on one worker (the unfixed build is not deterministic on many), unfixed against fixed, 34 projects: violations 244 -> 244, uncertifiable 482,280 -> 482,257, every move in app-game (25 rows): 24 (rule, site) uncertifiable rows gone (SC9012 `value-forwarded` 13, `value-to-unresolved-callee` 6, `value-use-unclassified` 2; SC5003 `pending-read-unresolved` 3) and one added (31 and 8 by rule, blocker and site). The rows gone are in none of the runs that keep each start's own context: not on the withheld walks' memo alone, not on the start's own memo alone, not in the census per start (0 of 24); all 8 rows added are in the census per start (the unfixed last start of a worker had dropped them); the fix holds every row of the three runs (0 lost, 11 violations in all). They exist only where one start's leftover ran under another start's source, `carried`, `async_walk` or memo (geometry.ts, a file with no async source, with an SC5003 "async accessor"). The other 33 corpus projects, `scripts/determinism-check.mjs --corpus` (workers 1 and default × forward and reverse claims, 4 runs each): 132 runs, every project one report. `make coverage`: 1,581 projects, no existing snapshot moved, one new; `counts.json` takes the new fixture's rows. `make ir-edit-fuzz`: 0 mismatches in 76 steps; textbook 21 programs, 0 problems; `make verify` (by verify-delta's escalation) passed.
**Not covered.** The other per-worker states of the Reactive IR (`after_await`'s reach walks, `site_reach`) answer from the build alone by their own contracts, and the gate holds them end to end (a whole report under every claim order), not one by one. A start that ran past `MAX_STEPS` keeps its own budget row; nothing queued is dropped but by `end_start`'s refusal. No fixture holds the rows of the second memo: they need a start whose walks past a withheld call ran past the step budget (app-game's `virtual-tree.ts` start), so the same-start runs of the Evidence are what shows them kept.

## ADR 1144 — Vite's reviewed dev client: the unloaded `vite` root is the page's host, not a prototype writer (M7v)
**The gap.** The reach index walks every installed root from its runtime entries. No program file loads `vite`, so its walk reads `dist/node`, where generated code and the packages it loads (rollup, jiti, postcss, esbuild) make it a writer of any prototype member, and every family-3 SC2002 site meets it (M0 writer census, main 51d3655f7: helge-dev 114 rows, donegeon-client/web/apps/client 6,651, each with the one writer `vite`, counted, not loaded, no importer). That code runs in the dev server's process. What Vite puts in a development page is `dist/client/client.mjs` and `env.mjs`.
**Decision.** `product_realm::reviewed_host`, read in `check::package_inputs` after the realm and whatever it decided, sets `PackageReachIndex.reviewed_hosts` (root → premise id; in the boundary fingerprint, not folded) for each root named `vite` that writes a prototype, where all of these hold, else none (the realm census names the first refusal, `reviewedHost`):
- a development build in a browser (a production page's polyfill and preload helper are not read);
- no program load reaches the package named `vite`, decided by the attested resolution (review F1: a specifier `"v"` that tsconfig `paths` sends there counts, whatever its spelling; `import type` loads nothing); a project file's load that no row answers or that resolves nowhere, a load with a specifier the file does not spell, a hidden load (`import.meta.glob`, a worker, `new URL(…, import.meta.url)`: review F2) and a Vite alias whose target is `vite`, `vite/*` or a path into it end the premise;
- no other installed root of the index depends on `vite` by manifest (`vitest` loads Vite into the test process);
- every Vite config of the chain parses in the closed grammar (`parse_realm`: no `define`, no `server.forwardConsole`) in the page's mode, with no plugin but Solid's, whose package's own content is a row of `SOLID_PLUGIN_READS` (the package row of ADR 0270's audit: the SHA-256 of its sorted `(path, sha256)` list outside `node_modules`; nothing about the closure, and nothing for host inference). `@solidjs/vite-plugin` 3.0.0-next.51 (`8f09539a…`, every rc.21 corpus install of it) defines `__SOLID_SERVER_COMPONENTS__`; `vite-plugin-solid` 3.0.0-next.27 (`70dc711e…`) re-exports the `@solidjs/vite-plugin` it resolves, which must have a row; the fixture stand-in `0.0.0-fixture` defines nothing. Each key must pass `define_key_admitted` (ruling (a), stricter: one segment `__UPPER__`; a prototype path, `Promise.x`, `window.x` or any other shape refuses);
- the root is the `vite` the configs' directories resolve, and the whole package is a row of `VITE_CLIENTS` by its content digest (review F3: the page's text comes from the dev server's Node code too, `__DEFINES__`'s substitution and the HTML hook, so the reading is of the release, not of its client files alone): 8.3.0 (`75537a8e…`, helge-dev's install) and 7.3.1 (`93e25dfe…`, donegeon's), each equal to the extracted published tarball (integrity recorded, equal to the corpus lockfiles'), and two fixture stand-ins; the client files each row's reading rests on are recorded beside it;
- every global the client writes is one the root's closure already writes in the index, by name or under any name, so every site that reads it still meets the writer: the row's `global_writes` (`console` for 8.3.0, whose `error` and `warn` its console forwarding replaces, `member_writes`) and each define key.
*Consumed* (`package_action_calls.rs`): `full_scope` and `product_scope` leave the reviewed hosts out (`WriterScope` `hosts_out`). `realm_sites` finds each file's sites again with them kept, and a site only they make (`host_clear`) ends in the typed silence `package_action_calls.package_action_calls.reviewed-host` (premise `ReviewedHostClient`, proof log; boundary premise `reviewed-host-client`). Dropping it (`SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE`) keeps the hosts in every scope, which gives the base's rows. A site the scope makes and the wider writers do not is kept, never dropped. Every other consumer of the writer sets (ADR 1145's list) still holds the host, and its global writes are untouched.
**The plugin reading** (`@solidjs/vite-plugin` 3.0.0-next.51, `dist/esm/index.mjs`, the `import` condition; the row pins `dist/cjs` too). Under the options the grammar admits (no `start`, `ssr` and `serverFunctions` false, `extensions`, `diagnostics`), `solidPlugin` (:4789) returns `boundaryModules()` (:619, only `resolveId` and `load`), `mainPlugin` (:6139; `serverFunctions` plugins only with the option, :6126; start plugins only with `start`, :6144; the `ssr` pair only with `ssr`, :6232), `solidDiagnostics` unless `diagnostics: false` (:6177) and `solidPerformanceTracks` (:6185). Their config hooks:
- `mainPlugin.config` (:5069) returns, at :5285, `define: { [SERVER_COMPONENTS_DEFINE]: serverComponentsDefine }` (:5294). The key is the constant `'__SOLID_SERVER_COMPONENTS__'` (:4788); the value is `JSON.stringify(serverComponents)` of a boolean (:4798, :4801), or a user `define` of that key (:5283, which the grammar admits none of). The dependency calls reached from it are vitefu's `crawlFrameworkPkgs` (:5090, :5148), whose result flows only into `optimizeDeps.include` as array elements (:5347) and as the value of `optimizeDeps.exclude` (:5348). Vite merges a plugin's returned config by path, so a value under `optimizeDeps` cannot reach `define`. The others are `searchForWorkspaceRoot` (Vite's, a path), and the plugin's own `findPackageDir` (:4311) and `getJestDomExport` (:4333, test mode), which return a path or a specifier into `resolve.dedupe` and `test.setupFiles`. No dependency's object is spread into the returned config.
- `mainPlugin.configEnvironment` (:5364) writes `optimizeDeps.rolldownOptions.transform.define[SERVER_COMPONENTS_DEFINE]` (:5373): the optimizer's transform, not the environment's `define`, which Vite's client injection reads. It also writes `resolve.conditions`, `externalConditions`, `noExternal` and `external`, where vitefu's `ssr` lists flow (:5486, :5510). `mainPlugin.configResolved` (:5514) only reads.
- `solidDiagnostics.config` (:763) returns `optimizeDeps.include` of two literals (:766); its `configResolved` (:772) and `solidPerformanceTracks.configResolved` (:1032) assign locals.
- `merge-anything`'s `mergeAndConcat` is called only in transforms (babel options, :5036-:6104), and `loadEnv` and `runnerImport` only from start mode (:3399, :3557, :3709).
A release whose content differs has no row. Any other hook that returns a config, or a dependency result that flows into the returned config's keys, would be a new reading, so it ends the premise (fail closed).
**Premises.** (1) The dev server of a pinned release serves its client files and no other Vite code into the page (the whole package is pinned; no integrity premise is relied on for its Node code). (2) The client writes no built-in's prototype and only the globals the row names. It was read in both releases and run in Chrome (`scripts/probes/vite-dev-client`: a blank page served by each release's JS API, with prototype descriptors, globals and console compared by `Object.is`). 7.3.1 changes nothing; 8.3.0 replaces `console.error` and `console.warn`; a define `__SOLID_SERVER_COMPONENTS__` adds that global; a define `Array.prototype.__w7` adds a prototype member (why ruling (a) refuses a path). (3) Vite adds no client define of its own (`configDefaults.define` is `{}`; `__DEFINES__` is `config.define` minus `import.meta.env.*`, `clientInjectionsPlugin`).
**Not scoped.** The plugin's own page modules (the diagnostics bridge, performance tracks) and the dev client's other loads are Solid's or Vite's and were never writers in the index; this premise neither adds nor drops them. Other Solid plugin releases, a production build, and the other plugins (`@wyw-in-js/vite`, `vite-plugin-pwa`) are owed (`docs/open-work.md`).
*Evidence.* Fixture `vite-dev-client` (published 8.3.0 manifest and client bytes, a stand-in Node entry; program names `vite` by its client types only). Cleared: three sites, and the variants `-type-import`, `-solid-plugin` and `-vite-7`. Kept: `-runtime-import`, `-alias-paths` and `-alias` (review F1), `-glob` and `-url` (F2), `-depends-on-vite` (F4), `-plugin`, `-define`, `-production`, `-mismatch` (a client file differs), `-solid-plugin-patched` (the plugin package differs); cleared `-diagnostics-on` (F4) too; and in every project the reads of a global the package writes (`console`; `Float32Array`, where the walk reads `dist/client`). `product_realm_process.rs` checks every cleared site against the proof log and the ablation. Unit tests: the rows are the bytes the fixtures copy, the corpus installs (`SOLID_CHECKER_VITE_CORPUS`, run on W), ruling (a) and the plugin content rows.
*Cost* (`corpus-delta --all --proof`, W v1 rebuild of the rc.21 corpus, release main 408fc4645 against this): violations unchanged (243); uncertifiable 470,865 to 470,749, **-116 SC2002 rows, all in helge-dev** (265 to 149: 114 sites gone, 2 rows merged into one), 114 (site, code) up and none down, nothing needs a look. donegeon-client keeps its 13,634: `@wyw-in-js/vite` ends the premise.
<a id="adr-1145"></a>
## ADR 1145 — A site is judged against the prototype writers the page loads (the product realm)
**The gap.** ADR 1108 and 1114 family 3 judge every site that may run a member a package writes on a built-in's prototype against every installed package any file of the program imports and whose closure writes one. A project's tests import a runner, jsdom, an assertion library and a mock, whose closures write prototypes (kui's packages: 3-16 any-name and 2-17 named writers), and under a writer that may reach Solid every member call, constructor, template, conversion, iteration and JSX value of the product is an uncertifiable site (SC2002 `package-may-call-action:*:prototype-*`: 117,829 of the 204,389 uncertifiable rows of the corpus's second half). The page loads none of those packages. A file-name split measured 22,941 such rows in 13 projects (M0, `mac20b/M0-results.md`); ADR 1120's realm scoping (every realm loads a module the build does not read) moved one row. The owner's ruling (M2b): product code is not judged against writers only a test or a config loads, provided the split is a checked build-configuration fact, never a file name.
**Decision.** *The realm* (`solid-facts-backend/src/product_realm.rs`, read in `check::package_inputs`, which one-shot and daemon share; the result rides in `PackageReachIndex.product` and in the boundary fingerprint). Every stage is read, and any doubt ends it (`Realm::Unknown`: every site keeps every writer, as before):
- *runtime*: a declared browser target and a declared build;
- *entries*: the module scripts of the `index.html` beside the project (host discovery's HTML grammar: no classic script, inline module, entity, handler, `<noscript>` or external URL) and the runtime targets of its `package.json` (`exports` outside `types`, `main`, `module`, `browser`; a `*` pattern or a target outside the program ends it; a style sheet or JSON loads nothing); a project with neither is unknown;
- *pages*: any other HTML file of the project (outside `node_modules` and `.git`, as host discovery's inventory) that can run code (a script element, `import(`, `javascript:`, an inline handler) may share a module with the page, so it ends the read; a built output that holds one does too;
- *bundler*: some `vite.config.*` from the project up to its workspace root names the build, every one there parses in host discovery's closed grammar (`host_config::parse_realm`: the same grammar plus the bundler's `output` naming options, whose callbacks run in Node) with **no plugin but Solid's**, and where the realm would narrow a site that plugin's installed closure must be one of ADR 0270's pins (a missing or unpinned install ends the read: a name is no proof); a Vite alias, a deduplicated package, the Solid plugin's `start` mode, another bundler's config file (`rsbuild`, `webpack`, `rollup`, `app.config`, `astro`, ...), another Vite config file (`vite.config.prod.ts`: `vite --config` may select it) and two Vite configs of one directory end it; so does a `package.json` script of the chain that runs `vite` other than plainly in the project directory (`script_run_differs`: a `--config`, a launcher option such as `pnpm --dir`, a `cd`, a project-root argument, shell quoting or grouping, and arguments another script forwards to a script that runs `vite`, `npm run build -- --config x`). A `--mode` does not: it picks env files and the branches of a function-form config, the grammar takes both branches of a data conditional (and refuses where they differ in aliases or entries), a tsconfig `paths` counts as applied only on every branch, and the realm holds Vite's development and production page code in either mode;
- *closure*: the entries' closure over every `import`, `export from`, literal `import()`/`require` and `import x = require()` by the producer's attested resolution of each specifier (an installed package is named by its root and not entered: the reach index already holds the writes of each root's closure). A computed load, `import.meta.glob`, a `Worker`/`SharedWorker` identifier, `serviceWorker`, `importScripts`, `new URL(…, import.meta.url)`, a specifier no row attests or that resolves nowhere, and a resolved file the program does not analyze (an asset and JSON excepted) end it;
- *resolution* (the premise **the closure equals Vite's resolution**): the closure follows TypeScript's attested resolution and Vite builds the page with its own, so the read ends wherever they can differ. A relative specifier is probed as Vite does (`resolve.extensions` order `.mjs .js .mts .ts .jsx .tsx .json`, the `.js` to `.ts` swap, `index.*`) and must pick the file the attestation names (`-js-sibling`: `./util.ts` beside `./util.js`); a `#` specifier (package `imports`, read under each tool's own conditions: `-subpath-imports`) and a root-absolute one end it; so do a tsconfig `customConditions`, `rootDirs` or `moduleSuffixes` (no Vite counterpart: `-custom-conditions`) and `paths` or `baseUrl` where no config has `resolve.tsconfigPaths` literally `true` on every branch (`-tsconfig-paths`; `-tsconfig-paths-applied` clears, and only for the `tsconfig.json` Vite finds); a query on a script module or a package (`?url`, `?raw`, `?inline`, `?worker`: the page may load or run what the string or the URL holds) ends it, and a data file's query loads nothing (`-url-script` against `-asset-query`).
- *manifests* (what the loaded packages load that no entry names): the reach index does not walk Solid's own packages (`@solidjs/*`, the dialect's: `package_reach` returns before the walk), so a writer only such a package's dependencies load is no writer of its root, and the realm would drop it where the base keeps it (round 2, `-solid-scope-dependency`: the entries import `@solidjs/router`, whose manifest depends on a writer a test imports; base 7 rows, realm 0). The realm holds every package the manifests of the loaded packages depend on (`dependencies`, `optionalDependencies` and `peerDependencies`, transitively, each found as Node finds it from the package that names it: `manifest_closure`, ended above 20,000 packages), those of the Solid runtime the plugin's compile output imports (`solid-js`, `@solidjs/web`, `@solidjs/signals`), and, where the plugin's dev-serve diagnostics bridge may be on, those of the app's own `@solidjs/diagnostics`: the bridge (`solidDiagnostics`, serve only) injects `<script type="module" src="/@id/virtual:solid-diagnostics/client">` into `index.html` when `diagnostics` is `true` or, with the option absent, the nearest `package.json` declares the package, and that module imports the app's copy. The bridge is off only for the literal `diagnostics: false` with no `package.json` of the chain declaring the package (`host_config::SolidDiagnostics`: the maximum over the branches of a conditional config, an absent or non-boolean option is the plugin's own detection, which the realm does not read as off: another pinned release may detect it another way).
*Listings.* The read lists only the project's own directories: the project directory (the page search walks its tree) and the directories up to a workspace root (`listable`: a `.git`, a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or a `package.json` with `workspaces`; a chain that finds none is the project directory alone). A directory above that is asked about by name (`exists`, `is_file`) and never listed, because the owned (WASM) host's input store faults on a directory that lists a FIFO, a socket or a device and the fault poisons the checker (CI's `/tmp` held a FIFO: the ancestors' `other_vite_config` scan listed it). A listing that cannot be read, or holds an entry that is no regular file, directory or link, ends the read (`listing`), as a read of one (a FIFO named `page.html`, a link to one) would block.
*Applied*: of `prototype_writers` and `prototype_writers_any` the realm keeps the roots the closure's files load (symlink and real spelling compared by canonical path) and, in either build, the roots named `vite` and the packages the Vite configs import (Vite puts code in the page: the dev client in a development build, the `modulepreload` polyfill in a production one; a name kept is a writer kept, the direction that only narrows the change).
*Consumed* (`package_action_calls.rs` `realm_sites`): in a file the entries load, under a realm that holds fewer writers than the program, the sites are those of the realm's writers; each site only the program's writers make is kept (`product_clear`) and ends in the typed silence `package_action_calls.package_action_calls.product-realm` (premise `ProductRealmWriters`, named in the proof log, registered as the boundary premise `product-realm-writers`). Dropping the silence (`SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE=<id>` or `all`) judges every site against every writer and files the base's rows byte for byte (monotone M1). `SOLID_CHECKER_PRODUCT_REALM_CENSUS=<file|dir>` writes one line per check naming the realm's status, every blocker, and the writers kept (a measurement; it moves no verdict).
*Plugins.* The first build recognised Tailwind, tsconfig-paths and Uno by name beside the Solid plugin. A name is no proof (invariant 3): fixture `product-realm-plugin-name` is a package called `vite-tsconfig-paths` whose `transform` adds an import of a writer to every module, which that allowlist cleared wrongly. The review of that build found the Solid plugin trusted by name too: any installed package called `vite-plugin-solid` or `@solidjs/vite-plugin` would have passed. The Solid plugin is the dialect's compile step (its output loads Solid's own packages); it counts only as an installed closure ADR 0270 pins (`host_plugins::audit`: every package's file digests and dependency edges, runtime peers included), asked where the realm changes a site (`-plugin-unpinned`, `-plugin-missing`). Any other plugin ends the read, and no reading of an installed plugin's source (no `resolveId`, `load`, `transform` or `transformIndexHtml` that adds an import, no `config` hook that adds an entry) is built to prove one inert. The rc.21 corpus's installs were not pinned (the nine measured: kui, `compass-ui`, `spotify-desk-thing`, `helge-dev`, `jar-hell-web`, `every-deck-of-cards`, `error-menu-web`, `app-game`, `ai-memory-ui`: every digest is a closure of its own, peers included), so the realm narrowed nothing there until kui's install (`vite-plugin-solid` next.27 over `@solidjs/vite-plugin` next.38 and compiler rc.6, shared by the 11 packages) was pinned in the commit after this one. The process fixtures that need a pinned plugin use the inert stand-in `@solidjs/vite-plugin` 0.0.0-fixture of `fixtures/reactive-ir/node_modules` (not published bytes), whose closure is pinned for them. Round 2 (review): the pinned bytes add one load from outside Solid's closure, the dev-serve diagnostics bridge (*manifests* above), and the reach index's blind spot for Solid's own packages is the realm's too; both are held by manifest.
**Premises.** (1) The Solid plugin, an installed closure ADR 0270 pins, adds only Solid's own loads and its diagnostics bridge's (held by manifest, or off). (2) `defineConfig` (from `vite` or `vitest/config`) returns its argument, as Vite documents it; its installed bytes are not read. (3) The page is built by the Vite build the config describes, run plainly in the project directory (the scripts are read: a `--config`, a launcher option, a `cd`, a project-root argument or forwarded arguments end the read), and the closure equals Vite's resolution wherever the read has not ended (the refusals under *resolution* are where it can differ); a script that runs another bundler over the same page is not seen. (4) The entries are complete for the page's realm: another realm that shares a module (a worker, a service worker, a second page) ends the read. (5) Tests, stories and configs are not the product (the owner's ruling): a product file's site is judged against what the page loads, though a test loads the same file with more writers, and a test's own sites keep every writer. (6) Code outside the program shares the page with it as ADR 0300 assumes (a consumer app's own writers are as invisible as before).
**Not scoped** (`docs/open-work.md`): the other consumers of the writer sets still judge against every writer: the standard-call patch veto (`indexes/callees.rs`, the SC9012 `standard-member-impostor` row that stays at a freed `reverse` call), the after-await library-call accounting (`after_await_accounting/library_call.rs`), ADR 1129's standard-member premise (`accessor_provenance/mutation_sites.rs` `standard_member_replaced`, `PackageReachIndex::prototype_member_writers`), and the global writers (`global_writers`, the SC2002 `written` sites). Readers not built: rsbuild, webpack and rollup configurations, `build.rollupOptions.input` (a configured second page), framework entries (SolidStart's `app.config`), a plugin's installed source, the HTML grammar's refusals (entities, `<noscript>`, inline stylesheets, boolean attributes).
*Evidence.* Twenty-six fixtures, each its own project (`product-realm-*`): cleared `-test-writer` (an HTML page, vitest's `setupFiles` and a test that imports the app: the product's seven sites end in the silence, the test's own sites keep their rows), `-package-exports` (a package's `exports`, kui's shape and kui's scripts, `vite build --watch --mode development` among them), `-tsconfig-paths-applied`, `-asset-query`, `-diagnostics-off` (a pinned Solid plugin with `diagnostics: false`: the page never loads the package) and `-solid-scope-inert` (the entries import `@solidjs/router`, whose manifest depends on nothing that writes); kept `-product-writer` (the page loads the named writer), `-dev-client` and `-dev-client-production` (the package named `vite` is a writer, and Vite puts code in the page in either build), `-second-page`, `-plugin-name`, `-plugin-unpinned` and `-plugin-missing` (a Solid plugin that is no pinned closure), `-config-writer` (a config that imports a writer), `-computed-load`, and one for each place the closure can differ from Vite's resolution: `-js-sibling`, `-subpath-imports`, `-custom-conditions`, `-tsconfig-paths`, `-url-script`, `-other-vite-config`, `-vite-script-config`, `-solid-scope-dependency` (that package's manifest depends on a writer a test imports: base 7 rows, cc1795538 0, now 7) and `-diagnostics-on`, `-diagnostics-auto` and `-diagnostics-declared` (the bridge may be on, so the diagnostics package's dependency, a writer, stays; they were not run on cc1795538, which needs the pinned stand-in). `product_realm_process.rs`: each cleared fixture's rows come back with the silence dropped and nothing else moves, each cleared site has a `silent` proof-log line on an overlapping span, and the kept fixtures name no silence. Unit tests: entries, page search, bundler rules, script runs (`script_run_differs`: refused and plain shapes), Vite's probe order, tsconfig options, the every-branch `tsconfigPaths` flag and the `diagnostics` option of the grammar, the manifest closure, the diagnostics package's keep, assets and hidden loads, the realm grammar, the writer scopes. The Chrome oracle runs single-file cases and the generator programs of one file: neither can hold a page and its build configuration, so no pair is registered (`scripts/fuzz/boundary.mjs`). On real output (kui's `kernel`, `shell` and `feature-messages`) every row the base filed and the head did not carries a `product-realm` proof line: 0 unnamed.
*Cost* (`corpus-delta --all --proof`, 34 projects, release main a7e9e7113 against this, one IR worker): violations unchanged (244); uncertifiable 482,280 to 471,134, **-11,146 SC2002 rows, all in the 11 kui packages** (`kernel` 3,296, `shell` 2,089, `feature-messages` 1,938, `feature-topics` 965, `feature-clusters` 847, `feature-consumers` 649, `feature-schemas` 510, `feature-ksql` 319, `feature-connect` 223, `feature-alerts` 185, `api` 125): 11,058 rows gone and 88 sites where one of two rows at a span cleared; every move uncertifiable to gone, 10,713 (site, code) moved up and none down or sideways. The realm is Known for 12 of 34 projects (the 11 packages and `compass-ui`, whose page loads writers itself and frees nothing); the other 22 are unknown: no `index.html` and no package entries (12), a plugin or import outside the grammar, an HTML grammar refusal, a second page, a generated `routeTree.gen` that is missing, a service worker. 49% of M0's file-name estimate: files no entry reaches (stories, helpers) keep every writer, and the page of `jar-hell-web` loads two any-name writers itself. *Round 1* (the six refusals, the pin check; kui's install pinned): the same rows move, project for project (violations unchanged, uncertifiable 482,280 to 471,134, 10,713 (site, code) up and none down, the realm Known for the same 12 projects); unpinned, no corpus row moves. Gates: monotone (1,970 programs: textbook, fixtures, 400 lg-base grid programs): M1 0 not identical, M2 0 down or sideways and 28 (site, code) up (the four cleared fixtures), M2b 0 unexplained; coverage (1,549 projects: only the eleven new snapshots differ; no existing snapshot moved); textbook check unchanged (21 programs, 14 certified); ownership gate (96 cases); `guard/count` (the new fixtures' rows, a rise). *Round 2* (the manifest closure; kui and the stand-in pinned): the same rows move, project for project (-11,146 SC2002 rows, all kui, 10,713 (site, code) up and none down, the realm Known for the same 12 projects, nothing needs a look). Gates: monotone (1,976 programs): M1 0 not identical, M2 0 down or sideways and 42 (site, code) up (the six cleared fixtures), M2b 0 unexplained; coverage (1,555 projects: only the six new snapshots differ); textbook check unchanged (21 programs, 14 certified); ownership gate (96 cases); `guard/count` a rise.

## ADR 1139 — Shadow delivery leaves the owner bit; the guard covers every creation a handler may reach (SC4001)
**The debt (ADR 1125, owed).** ADR 1125 put "an apply may deliver into a shadow tree" into the dispatch veto's owner bit, because rc.21 reports PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, not NO_OWNER_EFFECT, at a creation in a handler delivered there. That withheld every owner proof of such a handler: 5 smoke-census rows (NO_OWNER_CLEANUP, NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY loading/errored, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT, SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED in `evt-apply-dispatch-shadow`) went recall-gap, where Chrome reports NO_OWNER_*. Separately (Fable round 2, N3), a call past an `await` in an async JSX handler took `MayResumeUnowned`, not `ResumesUnowned`: `continuation_function` bounds its JSX test by the whole file, so a site under the handler's own element had no continuation. The proof rested on the handler's proven-unowned seed, which the veto withholds (`object-member-import`'s `onCleanup` in `timer.useTicker`).
**Decision.** (1) `dispatch_veto`'s owner bit (and its report) no longer takes `shadow_roots_answer()`: a shadow delivery runs the handler with no owner too. (2) `competing_checks`: where `apply_delivery_in_shadow_possible`, an Effect owner row and an SC7002 row are `creation-throws-first` when the creation is in the code a JSX handler may run (`ShadowReach`). The reach covers the `on*` attribute values; then the functions their calls and arguments name, transitively; and the callbacks handed to the primitive call that bound a called accessor or setter (a memo's compute runs where its accessor is read). A call or argument that names no function makes the reach unbounded (every creation). The check was lexical in the handler before (ADR 1115 part 2). (3) `call_owner_edge`: `follows_dominating_await_in_own_body`, the dominating-await test bounded by the async function itself, so only JSX and tracked regions inside the function keep a site off its continuation.
**Evidence.** mx-census, contexts `evt-apply-dispatch-shadow`, `evt-apply-shadow-concat` (32 programs, release): main 16 recall-gap, here the 10 NO_OWNER_* and SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED rows agree (the 5 owed ids and their shadow-concat twins); the 6 PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK rows stay recall-gap with SC4001 `creation-throws-first`. mx-recall over the same contexts: with the lexical check only, 72 false positives (helpers, closures, IIFEs and module helpers a handler runs, 1125's 12 shadow-concat `store-(render-)effect-carried` among them); with the reach, see the commit. Fixtures: `object-member-import`, `dependency-source-object-member` (2) and `dependency-source-owner` (`InTryBlock`) return to the violations ADR 1125 withheld (regress rows); `event-dispatch-shadow/variants/shadow-creation` names `creation-throws-first`.
**Cost (recall).** Where the delivery premise is broken anywhere (ADR 1125's program realm) and some handler makes a call the reach cannot name, every Effect creation is an obligation: `uncertifiable-repro/sc4001`'s ref-callback `createEffect` moves V to U.
**Round 1 (Opus review, FIX-FIRST).** F1: `ShadowReach` started from the calls written inside a handler attribute's value, so a handler named by its value (`onScroll={handle}`, `obj.m`) was outside it, and a creation in its body was a violation on the 1139 build where Chrome throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK. F2 (pre-existing on main): `may_hold_handler`, the "this program may hold a handler" half of the delivery and shadow answers, read only `on*` attributes, so a handler a JSX spread hands the element (`{...{ onScroll: () => … }}`) kept every event proof. Fix: the reach adds the function a handler value names (one nothing resolves makes it unbounded) and an intrinsic spread's exact handlers (ADR 0358; an unresolved spread makes it unbounded); `may_hold_handler` counts any JSX spread. *Evidence.* Fixture variants `shadow-creation-{named,member,spread}` (U `creation-throws-first`) and the light twin `light-creation-named` (V); Chrome `runtime-oracle/shadow-handler-forms`: PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at the named, member and spread handlers, NO_OWNER_EFFECT at the light twin, all covered. Generator contexts `evt-apply-dispatch-shadow-{named,spread}` (mx-census + mx-recall): main 8 census and 108 recall false positives and 972 false cleans; the 1139 build the F1 false positives; here none, the two cast prop reads of ADR 1146 (pre-existing, its own fix) aside. Cost: `jsx-creation-sites` (an unresolved `{...rest}`) loses 4 render-effect violations to `creation-throws-first`; `route-mount-throw`'s 10 SC2008 rows name `handler-dispatch-unproven`.
**Bundle j smoke-census (#305).** Six proved SC7002 violations went V to U (`lst-handler-object`, `export-namespace-call-handler`, `flw-owned-eval`, each an effect and a memo twin; Chrome reports SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC). None of those programs has a shadow root or an apply dispatch: the dispatch veto's broken-delivery early return answers "an apply may deliver" for every program whose delivery premise is broken, and the reach (unbounded at their `window.dispatchEvent`, `self[…]()` or `eval`) then took every creation. Narrowed: the widened reach is asked only where `apply_dispatch_into_shadow_possible` holds, a shadow root possible (the shadow scan: an `attachShadow` spelling, a decoded key, an unproven computed key, a code sink, an unread module, `eval`) and an apply dispatch possible, failing closed (a dispatch site an apply runs, `eval` or a code-evaluating call, an unread module anywhere, or a call in an apply that names no project function, primitive or standard call); elsewhere the check is the lexical in-handler test of ADR 1115 part 2, as on main. Fixtures `shadow-creation-eval` (the root attached by an eval string) and `shadow-creation-package` (by a stand-in package the build does not read) stay U. Four of the six return to violations; the two `flw-owned-eval` twins stay U (their `eval` may attach a root and dispatch: named trade, `proved/changes.json`, owed in `owed.json`).

## ADR 1154 — The page grammar tokenizes HTML as HTML does: a solidus separates attributes, names are lower case, what it cannot tokenize is refused
**The gap (a false clean on main 5e9f20381, found by the round-2 review of ADR 1151).** `inferred_host/html.rs` is the one reader of a page's HTML: host discovery admits a passive page by it, and ADR 1145's product realm reads the entries and the pages by it (`html_module_entries`, `may_run_code`). It ended a tag name at white space or `/` and an attribute name only at white space or `=`, so a handler after a solidus (`<body/onload=…>`, `<div id="root"/onclick=…>`) was read as an attribute named `/onload`, which passed the refusal of a key that starts with `on`. The scan of other pages (`product_realm::may_run_code`, a `public/` page) took `on` for the start of a name after white space only. HTML's tokenizer starts an attribute name after white space, after a `/` that is not followed by `>`, and directly after a quoted value, and compares event attributes in lower case. Chrome 148 (headless shell 1223, `fixtures/reactive-ir/product-realm-page-handler-solidus/html-tokenizer-probe.mjs`) runs the handler in every one of those spellings, the same as with a space before it: `<body/onload>`, `<BODY/ONLOAD>`, `<body / onload>`, `<div id="root"/onclick>`, `<div id="root"onclick>` (adjacent), `<body/onfocusin>`, and the `<body onload>` after a comment HTML ends at `--!>`.
**What it did on main.** `product-realm-diagnostics-off` clears the seven SC2002 sites of `App.tsx` because the realm holds no writer (the page loads only the entry; ADR 1145). With `<body onload="import('/node_modules/fz-prealm-any/index.js')">` the page loads the writer through its handler, the grammar refuses it ("executable inline event attribute"), the realm is unknown and the seven rows stay. The same page with `<body/onload=…>` (or `<BODY/ONLOAD=…>`, or `<div id="root"/onclick=…>`) left the realm known and narrowed and the seven sites cleared: a false clean (main 5e9f20381: 0 rows; this change: 7). A `public/frame.html` of `<body/onfocus="parent.hook()">` is a second page that can run code and was not read as one (0 rows; 7). The same read admitted such a page as a passive host (host discovery), and the focus proof of ADR 1151 reads the page by it.
**Decision.** The attribute loop of the reader follows the tokenizer: the tag name ends at white space or `/`; before each attribute name, white space and `/` are skipped; the name ends at white space, `/` or `=` and is compared in lower case; the value follows the existing grammar (quoted, no character reference, no duplicate), and the next name may follow it directly (`id="root"onclick=…`). A name that is empty or holds a quote or `<`, a boolean attribute and an unquoted value are refused, as they were: the tokenizer reads such a name some other way than written. A comment HTML ends at `--!>` is refused (the reader ends one at `-->`, so markup after it would read as comment text); everything else it refused it still refuses. `may_run_code` takes `on…=` after any byte that is no part of a longer name (white space, `/`, a quote, `<`), in lower case, for the start of a handler: a text that only looks like one ends the premise too, the fail-closed direction. A script's body is not tokenized (a classic script is refused unless independent, a module script with a body is refused), so `</script>` spelled another way is a refusal, not a hidden handler.
**Evidence.** Unit tests: `a_solidus_separates_attributes_as_html_tokenizes_and_a_handler_after_one_is_refused` (host discovery's reader: 18 spellings refused, 5 forms the tokenizer reads without a handler still read, a `<script/type=…/src=…>` entry read, 7 names or values refused), `a_comment_html_ends_at_bang_is_refused_and_an_ordinary_comment_is_skipped`, `a_page_scan_reads_an_inline_handler_after_a_solidus_a_quote_or_in_upper_case`, `a_handler_after_a_solidus_is_read_in_the_entry_page_and_in_a_public_page`. Six twins of `product-realm-diagnostics-off`, only the page changed: `product-realm-page-handler` (a space: the control, 7 rows on main and here), `-solidus`, `-upper`, `-attribute` and `product-realm-public-handler` (0 rows on main, 7 here), and `product-realm-public-static` (a second page of markup alone: cleared on both). The probe's Chrome run is the measurement above.
**Not covered.** The reader stays a grammar of the pages Solid projects have: an element it does not name, an entity in an attribute value, a `>` in a quoted value and a script body it cannot prove independent are refusals, never a page without code. A page a dev server transforms (a plugin that injects markup) is the realm's premise (ADR 1145: the Solid plugin's bridge), not this reader's.

## ADR 1149 — A producer that parks at startup fails the spawn: the wait after the kill is bounded
**The defect.** W7's stall capture: the checker hung for good when the Type Facts producer parked at startup. `ProcessConnection::spawn` bounds the wait for the startup frame (60 s), then called `terminate_child`: `Child::kill` and an unbounded `Child::wait` (`wait4`). The producer was parked in `dispatch_semaphore_wait`, and macOS delivers no `SIGKILL` to a process its exec check still holds, so `wait4` never returned: the 60 s bound only moved the hang. The same unbounded wait stood under `ProcessConnection::terminate` (so `Drop`, `Session::close` and `restart_and_replay`), which then joined the reader thread of the child's pipe, a wait of its own while a child the kernel holds keeps the pipe open.
**Decision.** `rust/crates/typefacts/src/session.rs`. `terminate_child` kills the child and polls `Child::try_wait`, which never blocks (first ask at once, the pause doubling from 100 µs to 10 ms, so a child that dies in a millisecond costs about that), for at most 5 s (`REAP_BOUND`). A child still not reaped is handed to a detached `typefacts-reaper` thread that waits for it however long the kernel takes, so no zombie outlives it, and its pid is logged to standard error. The failed spawn is the named error it always was, `SessionError::Handshake` ("producer did not report compatibility within 60 seconds", the bound and the text unchanged), with the pid and "left to a background reaper" appended where the child could not be reaped; the backend maps it to exit 3 and prints it ("wrong build", never a verdict: no finding, clean or certified, is made of a run that has no producer). The startup reader is no longer joined on a failed spawn (it ends with the child's pipe); `terminate` joins the connection's reader once the child is reaped and detaches it otherwise. A startup frame that is unreadable, or whose reader panicked, now kills the child as the other refusals do (it was dropped running). `unsafe_code` stays denied: `try_wait` is safe std, and no FFI is added.
**Not changed.** The 60 s handshake bound and its text, `Session::close`'s acknowledgement bound, and a producer that is slow rather than parked. A child that never dies stays a process of the machine: its pid is in the log, and the reaper thread holds nothing else.
**Tests.** `Terms { handshake, reap, kill }` (production: `Terms::PRODUCTION`) is the seam. `SIGKILL` cannot be blocked from a test and a stopped process still dies of it, so the child the kernel will not let die is a kill that does nothing beside a fake producer (`/bin/sh -c "trap '' TERM; exec sleep 1149"`: it never reports and ignores `SIGTERM`). `session::tests::bounded_termination` (each case runs in a thread with a timeout, so a regression is a failure, not a hang): a child that dies of the kill is reaped (no zombie); an unkillable one is given up after the bound, still alive, and the reaper reaps it once it dies; a spawn whose producer never reports fails with the 0.3 s bound's text, and with an unkillable producer fails naming the pid and the reaper; closing a connection (`terminate`, then `Drop`) to an unkillable producer that passed the handshake returns; the production bound's text is the old one. Each clause fails without it (mutation checked: the unbounded wait, the reader joined after an abandoned child).

## ADR 1148 — A `change` handler of a literal checkbox or radio keeps the host-delivery proof
**The gap.** ADR 0642 keeps `change` out of the events whose handler only the host delivers: a text control delivers it by a state change with no call to name (whatever makes the focused element leave: `blur()`, `focus()` elsewhere, `remove()`, `replaceWith()`, `disabled = true`, Solid's own unmount), on the stack of whatever made it, so the handler may run inside an owned scope. Every `change` handler was `execution_role.denied-event`, its body unplaced: SC2001 `function-run-unplaced` at a setter, SC1001 at a read. The textbook programs `cs-form-input` (a checkbox's `onChange` setter) and `id-todo-for` (a row checkbox's store update reading `index()`) were uncertifiable for it, though the same handlers on `onInput` and `onClick` certify.
**Measured** (`scripts/fuzz/change-delivery-probe.mjs`: Chrome 148.0.7778.96, the runtime oracle's headless shell 1223, Playwright 1.60; each scenario in a fresh page, with whether each event ran inside the scenario's own script call):
- *Checkbox.* A user's click, the Space key and a click on its `<label>` deliver `click`, `input` and `change`, trusted, on the host's stack. `el.click()`, `label.click()` and `dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent("click"))` deliver the same three inside the call; `dispatchEvent(new Event("change"))` delivers that one (a disabled control too, while `el.click()` on a disabled one delivers nothing). A write of `checked` delivers nothing, and `form.reset()`, `blur()`, `focus()` elsewhere, `remove()` and `disabled = true`, after a click, deliver no `change` beyond the click's own.
- *Radio.* A click on the unchecked radio and an arrow key deliver `change` to it alone (the radio that was checked gets none); `r2.click()` and `dispatchEvent(click)` deliver inside the call; `click()` on the checked one delivers `click` only; a write of `checked` delivers nothing, and `form.reset()` after a click no `change` beyond the click's own.
- *Text control (the denied delivery).* `change` at a user's Tab or Enter, and inside the call of `blur()`, `focus()` elsewhere, `remove()`, `disabled = true`, `replaceWith()` and a removed parent; none after a write of `value` then `blur()`, nor after `form.reset()`.
- *Retyped.* A checkbox given `setAttribute("type", "text")` delivers `change` inside the `remove()` call, one given `removeAttribute("type")` (the default type is text) inside a `focus()` elsewhere, and one given `type = "text"` at the user's Tab: it behaves as a text control from then on.
**Decision.** `solid-reactive-ir/src/change_delivery.rs`. The permit sits in `handler_event_denied` (every consumer of a handler's event reads it; `handler_event_denied_by_name` is the old, name-only test), and the invocation-flow worlds ask it (`FlowWorld::handler_event_denied`: the lookup asks directly; the memo world records one whole-program read, only for these handlers). A handler keeps the proof when its attribute is `onChange` (`onchange`) of: (1) an intrinsic `<input>` with one plain `type` attribute that is the string `checkbox` or `radio` (ASCII case-insensitive), no spread, no `ref`, no `is`, and no `use:`, `prop:`, `attr:` or `bool:` attribute; (2) in a program whose delivery is intact (ADR 1125: no Proxy, `Reflect`, `with`, `Object.assign` onto a value not made in place, definer, code built from a string, key reader or unread module); (3) where no file the program runs may write an element's `type` (`RetypeVeto`, project memo 51, over every file of the program, a dependency's source as the project's, since a dependency needs no element handed to it: `document.querySelectorAll("input").forEach((i) => { i.type = "text"; })`, or a library setter, which is a computed write in the library's own source): a write target (assignment, update, `delete`, destructuring or iteration leaf) whose key is `type` or a computed one no proof narrows away from it; a spelling anywhere of the DOM's attribute API (`setAttribute`, `removeAttribute`, `attributes`, `getAttributeNode`, …), of an accessor lookup (`__lookupSetter__`, which hands out the `type` setter itself, and its three kin) or of any route to the control's `Attr` node, whose `value`, `nodeValue` or `textContent` is the attribute (`document.evaluate("//input/@type", …).singleNodeValue.value = "text"` writes no key `type` and spells none of the names before it, and Chrome retypes the control: the XPath family `evaluate`, `createExpression`, `XPathEvaluator`, `singleNodeValue`, `snapshotItem`, `iterateNext`, `createAttribute(NS)`, with the named-item and node methods), and a name is read as the engine reads it, not as the source writes it (round 2): the match runs over the source text and over the decoded words of every identifier, string literal and template piece written with an escape (`AstFacts::escaped_words`, facts schema 107; the key `type` counts as one of the names there: `el.t\u0079pe = "text"`); a computed key that folds to one of those names (`el["set" + "Attribute"]`, the key's proof naming what no spelling does); or a module of the dialect's own runtime taken into the file that may write an element. The dialect answers per module specifier, the root and every subpath (`Dialect::runtime_module_element_writes`, `Option<ElementWrites>`): rc.21 `@solidjs/web` (and `jsx-runtime`, `jsx-dev-runtime`, which resolve to the same file) exports six writers that take the name from the caller, `assign`, `spread`, `setAttribute`, `setAttributeNS`, `setProperty` and `setStatefulProperty` (`ElementWrites::Exports`, each a row of the audited export table); the frames tier (`@solidjs/web/frames` and its `client`, `server`, `trace`, `regions`, `assets`, `wire` subpaths) morphs the children it finds with the server's markup, `type` included (`frames/dist/wire.js` `morphAttributes`: `oldEl.setAttribute(name, attr.value)`), so any import of it may retype (`Any`); the reactive core, the serialization, server-function, storage and performance-track tiers and the type declarations write no element (`None`); and a specifier no release was audited for is `None` of the option, unknown, and taken as writing. A test holds every exported subpath of the pinned packages (`exports/solid_v2_runtime_subpaths.txt`, itself held against the installed packages by `scripts/fuzz/runtime-exports.test.mjs`) against the audit, so a release that adds a subpath fails closed until it is audited. The proof asks of every file whether it takes such a module in: a named import (the alias is the program's; the export is what the import names, and only the listed exports of an `Exports` module count), a default or namespace import of the module, a side-effect import of an `Any` or unaudited one (it runs its own load-time code), `export … from` or `export *` of it, an `import()` or a `require()` that names one or escapes unnamed. A specifier that is no runtime package's by name but resolves into a file of one (a relative path into `node_modules`, a `paths` alias) reaches that file by a name no audit lists, so it is unknown too (the build's attested resolution says where it lands; `change-retyped-frames-alias`). A function the program declares under the same name is no import: the proof is not refused by a name (`change-local-setproperty`). The DOM's own names stay a spelling: a veto by spelling can only withdraw the proof, and the platform's methods are reached through values the types may not name. The files of the dialect's own runtime packages (`Dialect::primitive_defining_packages`: `solid-js`, `@solidjs/signals`, `@solidjs/web`) are not read for a retype (ADR 0027: the dialect states what its runtime does, and it does so at the import, per specifier, as above), and its ecosystem packages (`@solidjs/router`, …) are read like any other; a dependency whose source the program does not hold is the delivery premise's unread module, which withholds the proof beside this answer. The dispatch veto applies as for `click`: it does not look at the event's name, and `click()` on a checkbox delivers `change` in the call. Ablation: the arm `change_delivery.checkable-input-activation` (`SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_ARM`, or the same id as a silence) denies `change` again, and each decision that relies on it names the arm in the proof log. `SOLID_CHECKER_CHANGE_CENSUS=<file|dir>` (a measurement, no verdict) writes per project the handler count, the delivery premise's first hazard and the first place that may retype (its file and whether a write, a spelling or a folded key).
**Premises.** (1) The measurements hold for rc.21's host: `onChange` runs when the browser dispatches `change` at the control (the handler is the element's own listener: `@solidjs/web` 2.0.0-rc.21 `dist/web.js` `DelegatedEvents` lists 22 names, none `change`, and `assignProp` binds the handler with `addEvent(node, "change", handler, false)`), and a checkbox or radio is delivered `change` by its click activation alone in the engines the app runs in (measured in Chrome 148 only; the HTML standard's activation behavior is the same claim, not re-read here). (2) The dialect's own runtime, but for the frames tier (which the audit names), writes a `type` only on an element whose `type` is dynamic or spread: the compiler writes a literal one into the template, and rc.21's `assignProp`, `setProperty` and `setStatefulProperty` run on what compiled output hands them, which is no checkable input here (an element with a literal `type`, no spread, no `ref`: the element rule withdraws the proof for a non-constant `type`, a spread that carries one and `prop:type`, one element and one row each in `change-element-denied`, and Solid 2 refuses `attr:` at compile time, `change-attr-namespace`); its exports that write by a name, and the frames tier, are the dialect's answer per specifier, asked of every other file. Each subpath of the pinned packages was read for element writes (`dist/web.js`, `frames/dist/*.js`, `storage`, `serialization`, `server-functions`, `performance-tracks`, `solid-js`, `@solidjs/signals`): outside the root's writers and the frames tier none writes an element it was not handed. Code outside the analyzed program (a browser extension, a page script the program does not import) is not read: the kind of premise ADR 0300 states. (3) ADR 1125's delivery premise and the dispatch veto, as for every event proof.
**Evidence.** Fixtures `change-checkbox-handler` (no row; the base held 8 uncertifiable) and `change-checkbox-misuse` (SC4001 violations at a checkbox's and a radio's `createEffect`; Chrome warns NO_OWNER_EFFECT at both: runtime-oracle `change-checkbox-misuse`, and `change-checkbox-legal` is quiet) prove; `change-dependency-plain` (the same beside a loaded dependency that writes nothing of the kind) and `change-local-setproperty` (the same beside a project function named `setProperty`, which is no import: the proof is not refused by a name) prove too; `change-element-denied` (15 handlers, each failing one element rule), `change-attr-namespace` (Solid 2 removed `attr:`: the compiler refuses the file, SC9015, and nothing in it is proven), `change-retyped-assignment`, `-attribute-api`, `-computed-key`, `-lookup-setter`, `-folded-name`, `-dependency` (a package whose analysed source queries every input and writes its `type`: a proven violation on the head before the dependency scan), `-runtime-writer` (`setProperty(el, "type", …)` from `@solidjs/web`: likewise), `-runtime-writer-alias` (`import { setProperty as sp }`), `-attr-node` (probe p34 of the Opus review of a537da96b: an `Attr` node reached by XPath, written, the control removed while focused and dirty; a false clean on the reviewed head) `-frames` (p43: `createFrame` from `@solidjs/web/frames/client`, a stand-in module the program loads; a false clean on the reviewed head) and `-frames-alias` (the same module through a `paths` alias, which the specifier audit alone did not see: found while fixing p43, and a false clean on the head of the first round-1 draft), `change-dispatch-veto` and `change-delivery-hazard` keep every row the base had; `change-attr-node-control` (p36: `-attr-node` without the two lines that reach the node) stays certified. Chrome (runtime oracle, pinned rc.21): `change-attr-node-retype` raises STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED and REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at the handler's read and setter (the retyped control delivers `change` inside `Grab`'s owned body), `change-attr-node-control` is quiet, and the three `createEffect` variants of the Attr write (`value`, `nodeValue`, `textContent`; p03-p05) warn NO_OWNER_EFFECT at the checkbox's `createEffect`, so the violation the reviewed head proved there was true and is now withheld with the rest. The probe (`scripts/fuzz/change-delivery-probe.mjs`, group `replace`) shows that replacing an ancestor of the control (`innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `replaceWith` and `after` of a clone, `replaceChildren`) delivers `change` to the document for a new text control and nothing to the original node's listener, which is where Solid attached the handler: no retype of the handler's control, so no veto. The dependency packages are stand-ins written for the fixtures (`0.0.0-fixture`), not published ones. Textbook `cs-form-input` and `id-todo-for` certify: 16 of 21 programs, 4 keys newly proved. Unit tests: the element rule, the retype veto by every spelling of a write, of the attribute API and the accessor lookups, and by a folded key, and the runtime writers as exact symbols (an alias, a namespace or default import, a re-export, `export *`, a dynamic import that names one or escapes, a `require`, an import-equals; not a type import, a side-effect import, an ordinary export of the module, another module's `setProperty`, a function of the same name; each case fails without its clause), the dialect's list held against its export table, the whole-word match, and the dependency scan (a dependency that queries and retypes, one that spells the API, a library setter's computed write, a class's `this.type`, an ecosystem package; not the dialect's runtime packages at any depth of a store layout; a benign dependency leaves the project's answer). Fourteen further twin programs were run (before the review): eleven retype spellings, of which an accessor lookup and a folded name were not vetoed and are now (fixtures `-lookup-setter`, `-folded-name`) and nine already were (`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `Reflect.set`, `Proxy`, `defineProperty`, a destructuring write, a loop write, an update write, a template key, a prototype write: the delivery premise or the write scan); and three that retype nothing (`innerHTML`, another element's dynamic `type`, a write of `value`), which leave the proof standing. In the oracle's own harness (`Object.entries` in its entry) delivery is not intact, so its cases show the claims' Chrome side (a quiet legal case, a diagnostic at each flagged site), not the proof.
**Cost.** `corpus-delta --all --proof` (34 projects, release): no row moves. The census: 17 checks hold 75 literal checkbox or radio `change` handlers, and in all 17 the delivery premise is not intact (a code sink 14: a navigation URL not proven free of `javascript:` 12, 11 of them `@solidjs/router`'s `dist/claims.js` and one an app's own file, and `eval` 2; an unproven computed key 2; a key reader 1, `assign` in `@tanstack/solid-query`'s dev build) and a retype is possible (measured on project files alone, before the dependency scan; the scan can only make it true more often), so none takes the proof: the premise ADR 1125 states keeps these programs out as it does for `click`. Monotone (2,009 programs: textbook, fixtures, 400 lg-base grid programs): M1 0 not identical (the ablated head equals the base), M2 0 down or sideways and 14 (site, code) up (the four textbook keys, `change-checkbox-handler`'s eight, `change-checkbox-misuse`'s two), M2b 0 unexplained. The dependency scan and the runtime writers as exact symbols were added after these runs and only add vetoes: the textbook, rechecked on the final build, still certifies 16 of 21 (its programs import `solid-js` and `@solidjs/web` only, whose source is analysed under the declared target and build and is not read for a retype), and nothing can move down or sideways. Coverage (1,588 projects, before them): only the eight new snapshots differ.
**Round 2 (N1: a name written with an escape).** The Opus re-check of d0c1d494e (`coord-land/review-1148-r2.md`; F1-F3 closed, the ancestor-replacement claim held) found one false clean, Chrome-verified in three forms: the spelling veto matched the 28 names in the source text, and the parser decodes a name written with an escape to the name the veto looks for, so `document.ev\u0061luate(…).singleNodeV\u0061lue` (n1: identifiers), `(document as any)["ev\u0061luate"](…)` with `["singleNodeV\u0061lue"]` (n2: string keys; the handler's rows were gone and only the computed call's SC9012 remained) and `(box as any)["\u0061ttributes"].type.value = "text"` (n3) were certified while Chrome retypes the control and warns REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE and STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at the handler's setter and read. The same hole was open for a template-literal key (`` [`ev\u0061luate`] ``) and for the key `type` written as an identifier with an escape (`box.t\u0079pe = "text"`: the write-target check compared the property's source text, which no key `type` equals). **Fix, by family:** the facts list the words a file spells with an escape (`solid-facts/src/ast/escaped_words.rs`, `AstFacts::escaped_words`, schema 107): for each identifier name, identifier reference, binding, label, string literal and template piece whose source text holds a backslash, the words (runs of identifier characters) of its decoded text, so `\u`, `\x`, `\u{}`, an escape of a character that needs none (`"\evaluate"`) and a line continuation all decode to the name; a word written without an escape is the source text's own and is not listed, so a file with no escape lists nothing. `change_delivery.rs` `spells_by_escape` matches them against the 28 names and the key `type` beside the unchanged source-text scan (which still sees a name in a comment or a type): the veto reads the name the engine reads. Escapes alone withdraw nothing (`change-escaped-benign`: a string with a tab and an accented letter, an accented identifier, a template with an escaped letter). **Evidence.** Fixtures `change-escaped-identifier`, `-string-key`, `-collection`, `-template`, `-type-member` (the reviewed head certified each, or printed only the computed call's row; uncertifiable now, on the base's rows: SC1001 `callee-callback-timing` and SC2001 `function-run-unplaced` at the handler), `-type-string` (vetoed before and now: the facts decode a literal computed key; the route's guard) and `-benign` (certified), each with a runtime-oracle case of the same name: Chrome (pinned rc.21) warns at every flagged case and is quiet at `-benign`, `change-attr-node-control` and `change-checkbox-legal`. The reviewer's n1-n3 and the fixtures' programs in the real rc.21 install: the reviewed head certified n1, n3, `-collection` and `-type-member` and printed only SC9012 for n2 and `-template`; the fixed build is uncertifiable on all, equal to the ablated arm, and the control p36 stays certified. Fuzz: the eight `dny-change-checkbox-*` contexts (`misuse.mjs` `CHECKBOX_RETYPES`: a literal checkbox whose `type` the program rewrites before a focus and typed text that a later root's body disables, so `change` runs owned; one plain spelling and seven with an escape or a method) in the mx-recall grids of REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE and STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED, 552 programs against the fast host with Chrome confirming: the reviewed head 234 false cleans (18 and 216, the six escaped spellings; the plain cell and the string key were vetoed already), the fixed build 0 (every program a recall gap); `rediscovery.json` lists them (two rows). Monotone (2,055 programs: textbook, fixtures, 400 lg-base grid programs; release builds): against main M1 0 not identical (the ablated head equals main on every program), M2 0 down or sideways and 20 (site, code) up (round 1's 18 and the control's 2), M2b 0 unexplained; against the round-1b head only the five escaped fixtures move, certified to uncertifiable, and nothing moves up. Textbook: 16 of 21, 0 newly proved, 0 problems. The change only adds vetoes to a proof that moved no corpus row. **Not changed.** Other raw-text name reads outside this veto (`listener_reach.rs` `registers` reads `addEventListener` from the source text, so an escaped spelling drops the two SC9012 `listener-reach` rows of a window-listener cell and leaves its write site SC2001 uncertifiable; the `eval` call test of the completion index, whose facts-level hazard compares the decoded name): `docs/open-work.md`.
**Not scoped.** A retype by code outside the analyzed program (premise 2). `change` of any other control (a text control, a select, a retyped or handed-out checkbox) and of a `<form>` or other ancestor (the event bubbles from every control); a handler passed through a component prop to a control the file does not show (the element is read where the attribute is written).
