## ADR 1152 — A program that writes a name with an escape is not proven
**The defect.** A name is its decoded value: `ev\u0061l` is `eval`, `"c\u006cick"` is the event `click` (an identifier's StringValue, a string's or a template piece's cooked text). About 145 of the 889 `source_text` reads in 132 files compare a name with a literal, and others take its first letter (is this a component?) or look it up in a list, reading the source text of the span, which for an escaped name is its spelling. The `escape` rewrite (`scripts/fuzz/rewrite.mjs`, `escape.mjs`: every identifier, string and template piece of a program written with an escape, the file parsing to the same tree, `sameProgram`) and its sweep (`escape-sweep.mjs`: each site classed as the fuzz harness reads a verdict) found it on the build before this ADR (50e7fc48a, release): with every name escaped, the fixtures (1,641 programs, the checker's own projects) lose 116 violations with no finding left at the site (52 programs) and gain 188 violations the plain program lacks (147 programs: 180 over an obligation, 8 over nothing), and lose 1,239 obligations; the keywords pass (the identifiers a TypeScript keyword is spelled like) loses 1 more; the fuzz grids lose violations silently too (mx-base 500 programs: 54, mx-src 300: 4) and, on the legal grids, only obligations (lg-base 1, lg-src 23); the textbook (21 programs, no violation in it) gains obligations only. Roots: the first-letter component premise (`census.rs`), raw compares of option keys and of globals (`Promise`, `Math`, `defineProperty`, `eval`, `arguments`, `Reflect`, `Proxy`) and of the listener registration (`listener_reach.rs` `registers`): the escaped spelling gained a violation at code that is not one, lost one, or left the site with no finding at all.

**Decision (the veto; the decode of the name is not built).** When any analyzed file writes an identifier with an escape (facts `escaped_names`: an identifier, a private name, a member chain that holds one), or a string or a template with an escape whose whole value is one word (`escaped_strings`: ASCII letters and digits with `_ $ - : .` among them: a key, an event name, an option's name; a plain string such as `"\n"` is none, nor a template with a substitution or a tag, nor a JSX attribute's string), nothing in the program is proven. Every violation of an execution rule becomes uncertifiable with the blocker `escaped-name-unresolved` (the context it had stays as the detail after the colon), and every project file gets one SC9012 that spans it (`subjectKind: file`: internal like every uncertifiable result, ADR 0328), so a site a misread name hid altogether does not read clean. It is the program's, not the file's, because a file's names reach the others through the summaries, the call graph and the component test. Style rules (SC80xx) and a proven compiler refusal (SC9015) stand. One pass in `diagnostics.rs` after the compiler-refusal pass, under `DropPass::EscapedName` and the typed premise `EscapedNameWritten`. The harness reads a finding by its start line (the report names no end line), so a file-wide obligation holds every line of its file in the judges (`scripts/fuzz/finding-lines.mjs`, used by `checker.mjs` `siteVerdicts` and `runtime-oracle.mjs`). Owners: `solid-facts/src/ast/escaped_names.rs`, `escaped_strings.rs` (facts schema 108), `solid-facts-backend/src/escaped_names.rs` (`veto`), `diagnostics.rs`.

**Scope (the census).** `scripts/fuzz/escape-census.mjs` parses every source file of the rc.21 corpus (and rc.17) that holds `\u` or `\x`: an identifier written with an escape in **0** of 459,755 files (project 11,098, build output 3,007, dependency 445,650; rc.17 the same); a string or template in a key, import or export position with an escape: 1 project file and 935 dependency files, every one an escape-character map or an accent table (`"\n"`, `"\\"`, `"\u00e9"`), no word; a string whose whole value is a word (`"cl\u0069ck"`): 17 dependency files (entity tables, minified lighthouse and pdf.worker), none in a project; plain string escapes in 63 project files and 10,616 dependency files. So the veto reads the word-valued strings and not the 935 key maps (a key that is no word is no name any check compares).

**Measured.** the same programs with every name escaped, the build of this ADR (release; the sites read as the harness reads a verdict, a file-wide obligation holding every line of its file): fixtures `V->V 15` (style rules that stand), `V->U 2,704`, `V->clean 0`, `U->clean 0`, gained violations 0, in the names pass, the keywords pass and with the dependencies' sources escaped too; the textbook (names, keywords, dependencies, specifiers passes) 0 and 0; lg-base 500, mx-base 500 (`V->U` 538), lg-src 300 and mx-src 300 (`V->U` 137) 0 and 0, and the build before them exits 1 on the sweep of the fixtures, the keywords pass, mx-base and mx-src (`--expect-veto`). The control (the program copied, nothing escaped) moves nothing (1,523 same, 114 context-only: the temporary path in a context, 4 projects the checker cannot read from a copy). Corpus (the rc.21 frozen v2 corpus, 34 projects, release builds, `make corpus-delta DELTA_ARGS=--all`, the build before this ADR against this head): violations 244 to 244, uncertifiable rows 471,111 to 471,111, **0 rows moved** in any project, nothing to look at: no file the analysis reads in any of the 34 writes an identifier with an escape or a word-valued string with an escape (the 17 dependency files that do are not analyzed as source by any project).

**Evidence.** Fixtures `escaped-name-identifier`, `-other-file`, `-key`, `-event` (the violation is uncertifiable, one notice per file), `-component` (the escaped component name: the existing `component-identity-unproven` row and the notice) and the negative `escaped-name-plain-string` (strings with escapes that are no word: the SC2001 stands, no notice); `change-escaped-benign-strings` keeps ADR 1148's certified control, since `change-escaped-benign` (an accented identifier, a template with an escaped letter) is now uncertifiable as a whole. Moved snapshots (14, all read): 11 gain only the notice, and 22 violations turn uncertifiable in place (`async-call-prefix` 15, `prop-head-get` 4, `value-use-census` 3); no violation is added and none leaves. Unit tests: `escaped_names.rs`, `escaped_strings.rs` (facts), `escaped_names/tests.rs` (backend). Rediscovery: the escape sweep on the build before and after (`rediscovery.json`).

**Trades.** (1) Names the facts already decode correctly (a global spelled `\u0062toa`, a key `"th\u0065n"`, a destructured key `escap\u0065dRead`) lose their proofs with the rest: the 14 moved fixtures above write them on purpose and keep their uncertifiable rows (owner ruling, 2026-11-21: the decode is recall for a construct no real file writes, so it is a named trade in `docs/open-work.md`). (2) A key written with an escape whose value is no word (`{ "\n": f, "\u000a": g }`) is a plain value: two spellings of one non-word key read as two members to the repeated-key check, a known miss with no corpus site. (3) Not names: a string that is no word wherever it stands, a tagged template's pieces, a JSX attribute's string, a module specifier that is no word (`"./\u0068elpers"`, resolved by its value). (4) A user's project with one escaped identifier loses every reported violation (they are internal uncertifiable results now), the price of a program the checker cannot read name by name. Not built: the central decode (`escaped_names` read by `source_text`, then the veto narrowed to what it does not read); reopen if a census finds an identifier written with an escape in a project's own source.

## ADR 1150 — `affects(accessor)` is an untouched target, once the prototype it reads through is proven plain
**The gap.** The textbook case `cs-api-2-0-1` (`affects(rows)` beside `refresh(rows)`, `rows = createDeferred(…)`; cheatsheet 2.0.1) was uncertifiable on SC9012 `value-in-carrier` at the accessor handed to `affects`: the value-use census had no model of the API (ADR 1089 part C ended a function value's walk at `refresh`'s argument only).
**The source.** rc.21 `@solidjs/signals` `dist/dev.js:10018-10050` (`dist/prod/affects.js:56-69`): `affects(target, key)` reads `target?.[$TARGET]` (the store half), then `target?.[$REFRESH]` (the node `accessor()` sets as an own property, `:3237-3240`), `register(node)` (a count on the node, listed with the flush's transaction or the ambient list; `repoll` queues the readers of its verdict to re-derive) and `schedule()`. It never calls the target and never hands it on; the dev build's `invalid(…)` throws before any of that for a target with no node. No accessor owns `$TARGET` (`Symbol(0)`, `dist/prod/store/types.js:2`, exported by `@solidjs/signals` only), so on a function the first read walks `Function.prototype`, then `Object.prototype`: a hook there, or a prototype swapped for the accessor's own, runs project code with the accessor as its receiver, in the scope the call is written in. `refresh` reads `$REFRESH` only.

## ADR 1151 — An element's `focus()` in a leaf callback is no obligation where nothing in the program can run on its stack
**The gap.** The textbook case `cs-ref-directive` (`onSettled(() => input?.focus())`, the cheatsheet's ref idiom) was uncertifiable on SC9012 `leaf-callback-opaque` at the call: ADR 0329 refuses every `lib.dom` member that dispatches an event synchronously, since a listener it reaches runs on the stack of the leaf callback under the leaf owner, where `onCleanup`, `flush()` and a creation are refused.
**`onSettled` (rc.21 `@solidjs/signals` `dist/prod/signals.js:649`, `dist/dev.js`).** With an owner that does not forbid children it is `trackedEffect(() => untrack(callback))`: a leaf owner, run in the settle flush after the render, whose reads are untracked, whose `onCleanup` throws `CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE` and whose creation throws `PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE` (a returned cleanup is honored from an owned scope only); unowned (an event handler, another `onSettled`) it is `globalQueue.enqueue(EFFECT_USER, fire)`, a plain queued function with no owner. Chrome rc.21 confirms both textbook programs quiet.
**What `focus()` delivers.** Measured in Chrome 148 (the pinned headless shell 1223; `fixtures/reactive-ir/leaf-focus-no-listener/focus-events-probe.mjs`): with every `on*` event type of `window` and the legacy and composition names listened for in the capture phase on `window`, `document` and a child frame, over 18 moves (from nothing, from an edited input, into a textarea, a button, a contenteditable, a shadow tree, a dialog, a frame and back, a closed `<details>`, a select, a popover, with `preventScroll`, from a removed element), the types delivered before `focus()` returns are `focus`, `focusin`, `DOMFocusIn` (the receiver's), `blur`, `focusout`, `DOMFocusOut`, `change` (an input the user edited, when focus leaves it) and, across a frame boundary, `focus` and `blur` at the window. `scripts/fuzz/surface-dom.json` (`HTMLOrSVGElement.focus`: `focus`, `focusin`) agrees on the receiver's half. A composition active in the element losing focus is committed by the move: the composition and input events of a commit are named after ADR 0642, never measured (a headless page has none).
**Decision.** An element's `focus()` is no obligation of the leaf walk (`cleanup.rs`, `member_call_operations`) when (`focus_delivery.rs`): the call is `x.focus(…)` or `x?.focus(…)` with the exact `lib.dom` declaration, valid, not withheld (`standard_call_withheld`) and its member not replaced (`standard_member_replaced`); every argument is a primitive or an object literal of data (`kernel::inert_evaluation`: the host reads an option bag's members while it converts it, so an operand or a literal with an accessor runs code on the call's stack); and no analysed file may run code on the stack of a focus move. Every name below is compared by its **cooked value** (a decoded identifier, a string's or a template's cooked text: `el.\u0061ddEventListener`, `"\u0066ocus"`, `el.\u006fnfocus`), never by its source text. The files read are the project's and every loaded package's, a dependency's source as the project's, except the dialect's own runtime packages (below). In each file:
- no listener for an event of the list: a JSX attribute naming one (`onFocus`, `onBlur`, `onFocusIn`, `onFocusOut`, `onChange`, `onInput`, …, namespaced or not), any JSX spread (on an intrinsic element, a component or `Dynamic`: no fact names its keys), no `on<event>` property written or keyed (`el.onfocus = f`, and on the global object `onfocus = f`, `onchange ??= h`), no `addEventListener` that is not a direct call with a literal type outside the list (a value, an alias, `.call`, a destructured method, a variable type, the bare global), no computed member the program may read as a registering name: a key nothing proves is another name, or one proven to be `addEventListener`, `focus`, `innerHTML`, a handler property or a private delegated key (`$$focusin`), wherever the member's value is called, written or kept (`el[add]("focus", h)` with `const add = "addEventListener"`; a read whose value is provably neither called nor kept, `arr[i] + 1`, runs no method), no code built from a string (`eval`, `Function`, a string timer, a `<script>` made at run time, markup or an event attribute written as text, a computed or glob load, wasm), no JSX `innerHTML`, `outerHTML` or `srcdoc` attribute unless its value is a constant string the markup judgment (K5, `solid_facts::kernel::markup_is_inert`) reads as free of event attributes, scripts and `javascript:` URLs (a character reference in a JSX string is decoded by the transform before the parser reads it, so it fails), no private delegated key, and, in every file, the reflective routes (`Proxy`, `Reflect`, `Object.assign` onto a value with keys no fact fixes, a prototype route, `with`) and a write to a global under a registering name;
- nothing standing in for `focus`: no class member, object literal member or assignment named `focus`, nor a write the standard-member premise (ADR 1129) withholds (a prototype route, a Proxy, `Reflect`, code built from a string, a key no fact decides, an unread module);
- no registrar of the dialect's own runtime. `Dialect::runtime_module_listener_registrations(specifier)` (sibling of ADR 1148's `runtime_module_element_writes`; the same frozen subpath list `exports/solid_v2_runtime_subpaths.txt` and its audit, the same attested-resolution rule) answers, per module as a program writes it, root and subpath alike: `None` (the reactive core, the server and transport tiers register nothing a focus move delivers to), `Exports` (the root and the two JSX runtimes: `addEvent`, `delegateEvents`, `registerDelegatedContainer`/`Root`, `setProperty`, `setStatefulProperty`, `setAttribute`, `setAttributeNS`, `spread`, `assign`, `template`, `Dynamic`/`dynamic`, and the hydration, asset and head helpers, each by a `RuntimeListenerRole`) or `Any` (the frames tier fills the page from the server's markup and wires listeners as it loads); a specifier no release was audited for is unknown. Read from rc.21 `dist/web.js` (`addEvent`: `node.addEventListener(name, handler)` or the delegated slot `node.$$<name> = handler`; `template`: `t.innerHTML = html`; `setProperty`: `node[name] = value`; the asset elements' `load`/`error` listeners; `DOMContentLoaded`; `writeSelectValue`'s capture `change` listener on a `<select>`, which runs the runtime's own `selectChange` and no project code) and `frames/dist/client.js` (`template.innerHTML = html`, `DEFER_EVENTS` listeners). A named import takes a registrar only where the dialect lists that export; a default or namespace import, `export … from` and `export *` take every export; an `import()` or `require()` takes the exports its consumer names, all when it escapes; an import that erases takes nothing. A registrar that reads the event type or the property name (`addEvent(el, "click", h, false)`, `setAttribute(el, "class", v)`, `template("<div></div>")`) is exempt when every call passes a constant outside the focus list (the cooked constant, through `const` bindings), and `Dynamic` is judged where it is a JSX tag (its attributes and spreads are the scans' above) and is a registration anywhere else. An export the dialect lists nowhere under a runtime module is a registration only where it is no value export of the audited surface (`tsc` rejects such an import). A specifier that is no runtime package's by name but resolves into a file of one (a relative path into `node_modules`, a `paths` alias) reaches it by a name no audit lists, and counts (ADR 1148 round 1b);
- no code the build does not read: a module outside the program's files, an asset, a computed or glob load, and an installed package whose analysed files are declarations alone (TypeScript resolved the load to its `.d.ts`; the runtime source was never scanned);
- the page: where the project has an `index.html` (or another HTML file that can run code) host discovery's own grammar must read it (`product_realm::page_may_run_code`, reusing `inferred_host::html_module_entries`, no second parser: an inline `on*` handler, an element it does not name or a classic script ends it), it must hold no `<script>` but the module entries that grammar names (an inline or a second script is another script), and every entry must be a file of the program; a page that cannot be read ends it too. With no project HTML the program is closed, the premise of ADR 0640 and ADR 1080's listener census (a page's code that no analysed file holds is outside the program, as every proof already assumes). The verdict is a field of the package-reach index (`PackageReachIndex::page_may_run_code`, in the boundary's digest only where true).

The files of the dialect's runtime packages (`primitive_defining_packages`, by the package a path names, a store layout's real path included) are not read for these scans: what they register is what their exports register, which the answers above hold (the delegated listeners `addEvent` and `delegateEvents` attach deliver only handlers one of them stored; the runtime's own `change` listener on a `<select>` runs no project code). `indexes::tests::the_focus_proof_reads_every_file_but_the_dialects_runtime` pins the skip over a program whose files include `@solidjs/web`'s `dist/web.js` (the same code in any other package, `@solidjs/router` included, ends the proof). **Under `--runtime-resolution required` the proof does not fire**, and the cause is unexplained. The review saw it: `f-control` keeps its SC9012 there, built and ablated alike, and so do F1 and F7. The proof log shows only `main.tsx` and `App.tsx` analysed, so the runtime's source is not what ends it, and the skip above is not claimed to be the cause or the fix. A hand run here (a `vite.config`, the resolver, `dependencySources: ["@solidjs/web"]`) certifies the control under the reviewed build and under this one, so it did not reproduce it either. It is safe: a withheld proof is the fail-closed direction and no false clean follows. The review's inferred reading, not verified: under runtime resolution `plain_premise::loads_skipping` takes the resolver's outcome, and a load whose resolved path is no program path string (`./App`) becomes `Unread`. A proof that fires in that mode reads the pages by the grammar of ADR 1154. `blur()`, `click()`, `dispatchEvent`, the dialog and popover members and the bare global `focus()` keep ADR 0329's refusal. Proof id `leaf_walk.focus_delivers_nothing` (ablation and `silent` lines as above, at the call and at every call or callback the walk entered from the leaf callback's own text: the row it removes stands at the outermost).
**Round 1 (the Opus review of 35704e13e, FIX-FIRST).** The v1 census read the syntax of a few spellings and did not follow the runtime's registration helpers. Chrome rc.21 confirmed four false cleans, from one cause: `addEvent(el, "focus", h, false)` and `addEvent(el, "focusin", h, true)` with `delegateEvents(["focusin"])` (`@solidjs/web`'s own registrar), `el[add]("focus", h)` with `const add = "addEventListener"`, and a spread onto `Dynamic` that `Object.fromEntries` fills with `onFocus`. Three more are inferred (an inline handler's frame has no source URL, so the oracle cannot attribute it): a JSX `innerHTML` attribute, `template('<input onfocus=…>')` and `setAttribute(el, "onfocus", …)` from `@solidjs/web`. Found beside them: the bare global `onfocus = f` and `onchange ??= h`, an installed package's computed registration (a package whose analysed files are declarations was not scanned), the page's own HTML, and (the coordinator's item from ADR 1148's round 2) a spelling veto read from source text, which a unicode escape bypasses: the bare global `\u0061ddEventListener("focus", h)` was one (every member, key and string name was already cooked). All are in the decision above. Each Chrome-verified case is a negative fixture (`leaf-focus-no-listener/variants/oracle-*`: the reviewer's four, the handler in a package so that only the finding at the `focus()` line covers Chrome's diagnostic) and a fuzz shape with a rediscovery row.

## ADR 1146 — A helper handed to a handler slot is no silent use under the read veto (SC1001), and the judge never only prints a certified false clean
**The defect (pre-existing on main 5c1435e8c, found by ADR 1139 r1's `evt-apply-dispatch-shadow-named`).** A prop read in a handler named by its value (`const f = () => { (props as typeof props).r; }; <div onScroll={f} />`) was certified clean in a program where an effect's apply dispatches into a shadow tree, where Chrome warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED; the same read in an inline handler was uncertifiable. The TypeScript wrapper was not the cause: `props.r`, `props!.r`, `(props satisfies P).r` and `(props).r` were certified alike. `local_access`'s helper pass asked `helper_value_execution` for the slot `f` is handed to: an event-handler slot answered `EventCallback` without the dispatch veto that `named_callbacks` (ADR 0934) and `body_roles` apply, so the slot was "silent" and the definition site ended `HelperCallsAccounted`. A slot whose role is unplaced was neither silent nor an unproven use, so it also ended there. The judge then missed it: the rows match the open-defects family entry `R-near` (`mx-strict-read-untracked-`, `signal…`), and in a run whose selection is not the ledger's (another sample seed) a failing row of a listed family is only printed ("not judged"), so `focus` said "nothing needs a look".
**Decision.** (a) `helper_value_execution`: an event-handler slot is `Unknown` while `synchronous_event_read_dispatch_present` holds; a slot whose role is unplaced makes the use unproven (the read is unplaced at its definition, never ended by the other calls). (b) `open-defects.gridStanding`: a certified false clean or a false positive is never `unlisted`; off the ledger it fails the run whatever the sample, until it is listed by id or fixed.
**Evidence.** Fixture `named-handler-prop-read`: the cast, non-null, `satisfies`, parenthesised and plain reads are certified on main and U `function-run-unplaced` here; `variants/quiet` (no dispatch) is clean on both. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/named-handler-prop-read`): STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at the cast and plain reads, unproven-clean on main, covered-uncertifiable here. `uncertifiable-repro/sc9012`: two prop reads in a `toggle` handed to `onClick`, in a program whose delivery premise is broken, go from silent to U. Rediscovery: see the commit.

## ADR 1153 — `Errored`'s `fallback`, written in place, runs in a computation of its own
*The gap.* The textbook program `id-async-memo-loading` (`<Errored fallback={(error) => <p>{String(error())}</p>}>`) kept one uncertifiable row, SC4001 `function-run-unplaced` at the render effect of its dynamic child. The dialect already said `Errored` calls its `fallback` function (ADR 0971, B2: `control_flow_prop_function_run`), and the in-place rule dropped the function's JSX creation sites for SC3001 and SC6002, but the entry walk (`owner_emission::layer_entry_open`) closed only the function child of `For`, `Repeat`, `Show` and `Match`, and ADR 0971 B1 kept `Errored`'s `fallback` as a named cost: the owner graph had no edge for the function, so a creation site written directly in it had no known owner. 25 sites in 8 fixtures, 188 grid programs and 6 corpus rows were that one row.

*What rc.21 does.* `solid-js` `dist/solid.dev.js` `Errored` calls `f(err, reset)` (`err` is an accessor, not the error). `@solidjs/signals` `dist/dev.js` `createBoundary`, `fallback(b)`: `b._fb = runWithOwner(out._parent, () => computed(() => b._show(b), { id: out.id, lazy: 1 }))`, read in the output's pass. The function runs synchronously in a lazy computed of its own, created under the owner that encloses the tag, once per show and again when a signal its body reads changes; its errors and runs are the enclosing boundary's (the source's words: "built in its own scope, like `Show`'s function child"). That is ADR 0883's class, an owner of its own whoever owns the tag, which `For`'s row function and `Show`'s memo already have.

*Decision.* The function gets an `Owned` owner edge (`owner_discovery`) and the entry walk stops at it (`layer_entry_open`), under one silence id, `owners.control_flow_prop_function` (`SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE` drops both). Three kinds of `silent` proof-log line of SC4001 name it: one at each function; one at the site a walk began from when it ended at the stop; and one at the callee of an edge that leaves the function (`setTimeout(release, 0)` names `release`). A callee lies outside the function's span, and ADR 1118's M2b asks the proof log which arm moved a row. The edge, the stop and the predicate are W7's WIP (7b853a25945); this change adds what it did not ask. A function qualifies when: the tag is the dialect primitive exactly (`element_primitive`: a local component of the same name, a user component's `fallback` prop and a namespace or alias resolve as their declaration does); the prop is a plain attribute (no namespace) whose whole value is the function literal, through parentheses and type assertions only (a name, a call or a conditional is a value handed on); **the element has no spread** (`props.fallback` would be a merge: the WIP's doc said so, its code never asked); the dialect says the tag calls it and it is no generator (`runs_as_child`); **it is no `async` function** (the code after its first `await` runs with no owner, Chrome rc.21 NO_OWNER_CLEANUP; the existing after-await rows keep it, but the edge does not lean on them); and it cannot hand itself on (`can_hand_itself_on`: a named function expression that uses its own name, or reads `arguments`, keeps its row, ADR 0971 B1). The edge moves the owner contexts of the sites in the function and of the callees only it reaches, so the rows that read them (SC4001, and SC3001 and SC6002 where the program holds a leaf opener or an effect's apply) end in the same silences they do for a `For` row. One more thing moves, upward and true (the review of this ADR): a callback the function defers (`setTimeout(release, 0)`, `Promise.resolve().then(run)`) runs later with no owner, which was unknown while the function's own owner was, so its `onCleanup` is now an SC4001 violation where main had an uncertifiable row. Chrome rc.21 reports NO_OWNER_CLEANUP at both: `covered-violation` against main's `covered-uncertifiable` (oracle case `errored-fallback-deferred`; fixture `Deferred` and `DeferredThen`); the ablated build keeps main's row. Nothing else moves: a layer written inside the function (an effect's apply, a tracked effect's callback, a handler) is its own and its violations stay (fixture `Nested`: the SC6002 at a `createMemo` in an apply and the SC3001 at an `onCleanup` in a tracked callback stay violations, as on main), a write or a read in the body keeps its SC2001 and SC1001 rows, and the SC5003 row of a read of an accessor the program does not prove stays.

*Evidence.* Chrome rc.21, the oracle's cases `errored-fallback-*`: in `-owned` the function runs twice (its body reads `tick`, so it is tracked), finds the provider's value, and `onCleanup`, `createMemo`, `createEffect`, `useContext` and JSX written in it raise nothing (`assert-text` `provided:2:2:4:function`; the oracle records the step in the case's `report.json` and does not turn a failed one into a verdict, so it is read there, and a deliberately wrong text is recorded `passed: false`); `-write`: a write in the body raises REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE (an owned computed), `covered-uncertifiable` before and after; `-control`: the same `onCleanup` in a handler raises NO_OWNER_CLEANUP; `-handler` and `-sync-helper` are quiet; the negatives `-async`, `-async-helper`, `-named`, `-userprop`, `-shadow` raise NO_OWNER_CLEANUP at their sites with the same rows on main and on this change; `-nested-apply` and `-nested-tracked` raise PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK and CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, `covered-violation` before and after (one case each: the apply's throw halts the reactive system before the tracked callback runs); `-deferred` raises NO_OWNER_CLEANUP at a helper handed to `setTimeout` and at an arrow handed to `.then`: `covered-uncertifiable` on main, `covered-violation` with the edge (the one case whose verdict changes, and in the true direction). No case is `unproven-clean`. ADR 0971's `owner-call-inplace-function`, `-ops` and `-escapes` show the legal forms, the write and the hand-on on the same position. The textbook program itself: with `steps: []` the oracle's two passes stop at page 3 and its fallback never ran; with one more click (page 4 throws "no more pages") the fallback runs, Chrome is quiet, and `String(error())` shows `Error: no more pages`. Fixture `errored-fallback-owner`: nine functions get the edge (`Message`, `Parenthesized`, `Creates`, `ViaHelper`, `ViaNamespace`, `NamedQuiet`, `Nested`'s own, `Deferred`, `DeferredThen`), 21 rows go (SC4001 11, SC3001 7, SC6002 3; the SC5003 row of `Creates` stays) and the two deferred callbacks' SC4001 rows become violations; a spread, an `async` function, a name, a conditional, a function that stores itself, a user component and a shadowing local component keep every row, and the ablated build equals main on it. `an_errored_fallback_written_in_place_is_an_owned_run` (proof_log_process.rs) pins the nine names, the two callees' (`release`, `releaseLater`), the six functions that get none and the ablation (the only rows the edge adds are the two deferred violations); removing the spread check, the async exclusion or the hand-on test each fails it at its negative.

*Cost and gates.* 25 existing sites in 8 fixtures (`route-mount-throw` 2, `stored-throw-dynamic-mount` 1, `-nested-component` 2, `-observation` 4, `-portal` 1, `-render-run` 3, `-value-mount` 2, `-wrapper-boundary` 10), all `SC4001` `function-run-unplaced` at a `String(e())` JSX effect, uncertifiable to gone; no project certifies. Monotone (M1 with `--ablate-silence owners.control_flow_prop_function`, M2, M2b; 3,029 programs: textbook, fixtures, 400 lg-base and 1,000 mx-census grid programs): M1 0 not identical, M2 0 down or sideways, 50 (site, code) up (the 25, the 21 of the new fixture and its two deferred violations, the textbook program and one in the mx-census sample), M2b 0 unnamed; M2b first flagged the helper only a fallback calls (and, once the deferred cases were added, the helper handed to `setTimeout`), neither inside the function's span, which is why the proof log names the arm at the site a walk began from and at the callee of an edge that leaves the function. The grid programs with an `<Errored fallback={function}>` (every grid searched: lg-recall 50, mx-census 132, mx-recall 14, 6 of which move; none in lg-base, lg-combo, lg-src, lg-pairs, mx-base, mx-combo, mx-src, mx-pairs): 188 programs move one SC4001 each, `String(e())`, with 0 down or sideways, M1 0, M2b 0, none certifies (they carry their defect rows). `monotone.mjs` could not take a whole grid (a `push(...programs)` of lg-recall's 744,797 rows overflowed the stack; fixed in its own commit), so these ran by id list. Corpus (`corpus-delta --all --proof`, the 11 apps that use `<Errored`, 12 projects, rc21-frozen-v2): 6 of 320,550 uncertifiable rows go (5 `function-run-unplaced`, 1 `owner-callers-unenumerated`: ai-memory-ui 1, hoxxes-briefing 2, jar-hell-web 1, sensor-sim 1, skyjtx-website 1), violations unchanged (181), 0 down or sideways, nothing to look at. Textbook: `id-async-memo-loading` certified (the ledger records it), and its bytes changed with it: `String(error())` for `String(error)` (rc.21 passes an accessor; the cheatsheet's form) and a click step so the oracle runs the fallback (admitted with `record --admit` after tsc and Chrome).

*Fuzz.* `er-shapes.mjs` gets two routes and their never-run twins: `namedfb` (the site directly in a named fallback that stores itself, called by the host's apply) and `fbnest` (an arrow stored from inside the fallback, called the same way): `er-namedfb-apply`, `er-fbnest-apply` and `-never`, 16 misuse programs (`recall-gap`) and 16 legal twins (uncertifiable) on main and on this change, no false clean and no false positive. They are regression cells, not a rediscovery: nothing found a defect here. Each guard was removed in turn (release builds, the fixture): removing the spread check clears the `Spread` row (SC4001 at its `String(error())`), which is no false clean either (a literal a spread overrides never runs, and one it does not override runs in the owned computation); removing the async exclusion or the hand-on test changes no row (the after-await rows keep an async function; `referenced_only_by_entry` closes a function that references itself, so both guards would have to go). So no mutation produces a false clean to rediscover, and the process test pins each guard at its silence line.

*Not covered, named.* A fallback handed by name or call result, an `async` or generator function, an element with a spread, `Loading`'s `fallback` (a value the boundary shows), the server build (`dist/server.js` calls the fallback under `runWithOwner(outputOwner)` with a render context and directly without one: an owner exists in the first, not shown in the second; the oracle is CSR, as for ADR 0883's `For` and `Show`), hydration, and `reset`'s semantics.

## ADR 1147 — Context flow: a provider's children are owned by its memo, and a context's `[store, { actions }]` literal reaches its readers
**The gap.** Textbook `cs-context-provider` and `id-context` (Chrome rc.21 quiet) were uncertifiable on main 5c1435e8c: `theme()` (SC3001, SC6002) and `id-context`'s eleven keys. Every SC3001/SC6002 decline was `unread-package-may-run`: the hand-off walk took the dialect's provider element for an unread package's component, so its children were handed (ADR 1123 withdrew the arm that read them in place). `id-context`'s other five (SC9012 at the provided `cart`, the readers' pattern and read, Count's `cart`; SC2001 at `setCart`) were the value-use census and the write-role walk stopping at the context.
**Decision.** Two arms, each switched off by `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE=<id>` and named in the proof log (`decision` lines) where it decides.
- **Arm 1, `context-provider-children-owned`** (the owner codes). rc.21's provider is `createRoot(() => { setContext(provider, props.value); return children(() => props.children); })`: a child runs inside the `children()` memo's computation, whose owner is that memo wherever and whenever the memo is read. So the owner codes (SC3001's PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE and CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, SC6002's PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, whose guard is `inEffectCallback && context === null`) do not depend on where the provider's value goes (the review of 1123's F3: true of the owner questions, not of the stack). `UnreadPackageHandOff::for_owner_questions` (the leaf universe only) places a child of an exact provider (`callback_return::exact_context_provider`: the tag is the tuple arm's `sole_reference_binding`, an unwritten, unexported `const` of one name, initialized by the dialect's `createContext` resolved exactly, the review's F2; no spread, no `children` attribute, no direct `eval`) in `element_hands` and `evaluated_by_element`. The flush accounting and the after-await accounting keep `UnreadPackageHandOff::new`: a flush (SC3001's FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK, SC2006, SC2008) and SC1002's reads in a provider's child are stack questions and keep their rows (the review's k11 and k9: fixture `context-provider-children-owned`'s `FlushStoredApp`, `FlushInnerApp`). The rest of the leaf universe still asks (a leaf bit, an unowned entry on an apply: `LeafApp`, `ApplyApp` keep their rows).
- **Arm 3, `context-provided-store-tuple`** (`callback_return::provided_store_tuples`, per file: the context is unexported, so every reader is in its file). ADR 1123's context premises (one provider, every reference its tag or an exact `useContext` a `const` array pattern takes apart at once), with the value an array literal (or a `const` it initializes whose one reference is the value; `as const` is read by its syntax) of a store root (slot 0 of an exact `createStore` `const` pattern) and, optionally, a closed object literal of data properties each a `const` bound to a function it holds now. Each reader's pattern (`pattern_elements`, facts schema 62, which tells a hole from a nested pattern) names slot 0 by one identifier and slot 1 by an object pattern of the object's keys, each local only called, and each call written where the dialect or the DOM runs it (every function between the reader and the call the whole argument of a dialect primitive's call or the whole expression of an intrinsic element's attribute: the Opus review's F1, `hand(() => add("x"))` with `hand` a package read as source calling it in `createTrackedEffect`, gave SC2001 a violation Chrome never reports; the arm now refuses, and the write keeps its uncertifiable row); ADR 1137's veto (`SemanticLookup::program_builds_code`, now shared with `string_code_patch_withheld`) and `array_slots_withdrawn` refuse. Then a reader's slot-0 name is a store source of its own (as a hook's returned store, ADR 0628, with the creation's facts), the census's `bound()` gives a reader only the names of the slot it walks, and the write-role caller fold walks an action's readers' calls beside the call graph's sites, the literal's reference counted as the entry they account for. Refused (SC9012, SC2001 as before): a tuple held whole, an action local aliased or handed on (`const f = add; queueMicrotask(…)`), slot 1 bound whole, the value's `const` handed on, a second provider, a signal in slot 0, an `eval` program. A setter also handed elsewhere (`keep(setCart)`) keeps that hand-off's row; the reader is the same store, so the root's census of it covers the reader.
- **Arm 2 (the stack codes through a transitive placement) is not built** (`docs/open-work.md`); nor a generator source for arm 3 (the grids' `context` source hands an object): the arm-shape contexts `barm-ctxstore-memo`, `-handler` and `-alias` (REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, recall grids) place a site in an action a local reader calls.

*Evidence* (release builds, main 5c1435e8c against 9c0bd8ce6; the code is unchanged to the merged head). *Textbook:* 16 of 21 certified (main 14): `cs-context-provider` and `id-context` certified, 0 problems; Chrome rc.21 quiet on both. *Monotone* (`monotone.mjs`, textbook, fixtures and six grid samples, 3,604 programs): both arms ablated M1 0, M2 0, M2b 0; 302 (site, code) up, none down or sideways. Arm 1 moves 92 programs (M1 with arm 3 alone ablated: textbook 2, fixtures 16, lg-src 30, mx-src 44), every move SC3001/SC6002 uncertifiable to clean at a child under a provider; arm 3 moves 2 (`id-context` and its fixture: SC9012 and SC2001). *Fuzz:* focus on PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK and FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK over mx/lg base, src, combo and recall (92,000+ programs): no false clean, false positive or wrong rule, every Chrome comparison 0 behaviour and 0 attribution differences; the 74 grid programs arm 1 moved, rerun by id with Chrome: lg 12 clean and 18 uncertifiable, mx 17 agree and 27 recall-gap, all 74 runtime records the same. *Chrome cases:* `context-provider-children-owned` (new) quiet; `context-provider-children-handed`, `-package`, `-placed` and `context-signal-tuple-forms`, `-twins` covered-uncertifiable; `context-signal-tuple` covered-violation. *Fixtures:* 14 snapshots move, exactly arm 1's programs, every move an SC3001/SC6002 row removed; 3 new projects. *Corpus* (`corpus-delta --all --proof`, one IR worker, 34 projects; a measured scope note, the coordinator's ruling): violations 244 -> 244, uncertifiable -250 (SC3001 -128, SC6002 -122, every move uncertifiable to gone, none down) in four projects: app-game 138 (svg-editor's `layers-view`, ui-components-examples' `cloud-storage-tree`, gpu-text-rendering's viewer), skyjtx-website 88, expenses-app 20, hoxxes-briefing 4. Rerun per site with the proof log, all 250 are owner-call rows arm 1's decision names, nothing added; spot-checked: skyjtx's `<Router>` created inside `<ClientSettingsProvider>` (a project component returning `<Ctx value>{props.children}</Ctx>`) and the memo and effect of a hook its components call, hoxxes' children of `<I18nProvider>`; the elements in the router's own children stay uncertifiable (the package hands them on). The withdrawn arm moved 68 rows there: it needed the provider element placed, arm 1 holds wherever the value goes, so an app whose root is wrapped in a provider moves its whole tree's owner rows.

## ADR 1155 — A write forwarded to a leaf owner's callback is the leaf's, and a context provider's children are owned by its memo
**The gap** (the Opus review of ADR 1147, verified on main 408fc4645 against Chrome rc.21; patterns `ctxmemo/*`). Two violation families Chrome never reports, both on main before ADR 1147.
- (a) F1's root, `ctxmemo/s11-hand-direct`: `hand(() => setN(1))`, `hand` a package read as source that calls its parameter in `createTrackedEffect`'s compute, was SC2001 a violation. ADR 0200's forwarding (`callee_roles::forwarded_tracked_compute_role`) gave the literal the tracked role (`TrackedJsx`) and the write guard's leaf exemption (`write_roles::write_region_adjustment`, `CallbackOwner::Leaf`) read only the leaf's own literal; rc.21 exempts every write that runs in the leaf callback.
- (b) N1: a creation or a cleanup written in a context provider's child was a violation of the code around the provider element: SC4001 in a timer (`p14b-timeout-control`, Chrome NO_OWNER_CLEANUP only at the control outside) or an effect's apply (`p9-apply-project`, Chrome PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK at the tag), SC3001 in a tracked effect (`p8-tracked-project`, Chrome at the tag), SC6002 on a package's apply (`p2-render-apply`, Chrome at the tag). rc.21 evaluates a provider's children only inside its `children()` memo, whose owner is that memo.
**Decision.** Two arms, each switched off by `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE=<id>` and named in the proof log where it decides.
- (a) `write_roles.forwarded-leaf-scope` (`write_roles::forwarded_leaf_scope`): ADR 0200's proof is now one helper (`callee_roles::forwarded_compute_slot`: the literal is the whole argument of a call of a project or read-package function, synchronous, whose parameter at that slot is one identifier, never reassigned, only ever called directly in one literal, in a wrapper that is an arrow or reads no `arguments` (review r1 F1: `arguments[0]()` in the memo that calls `hand` is a second run, Chrome REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE; r2, below), written as the whole argument of a primitive call directly in its body, the primitive's callback slot executing). Where that slot's owner is `CallbackOwner::Leaf` (and not `onSettled`'s drained run, ADR 0613), a write in the literal takes `WriteRegionAdjustment::LeafScope`, as the leaf's own literal does. Reads keep the tracked role. A memo's compute (`handMemo(fn) { createMemo(() => fn()) }`) keeps its violation; any other forwarding (the parameter also handed to a timer, an unread callee) keeps the row it had.
- (b) `context-provider-children-memo-owner` (`callback_return::in_exact_provider_children`, `exact_provider_child_spans`), for ADR 1147's exact provider only: the children the compiler evaluates in the `children` getter (`callback_return::provider_getter_regions`: an expression child traced as a caller-context `ComponentChild`, or an element child; review r1 N2: a lone child with no call, `{(new Make(), 1)}`, is traced `EagerOnce`, evaluated at the tag, and keeps its rows) are owner-providing regions of the owner analysis (`OwnerFileIndex::providing_regions`: the owner requirements, SC4001's), the leaf walk files no creation or cleanup written directly in a child (the leaf's own text and a helper's body; a flush, an observer-guarded call and a helper's call are walked as before: the stack's questions), and the effect-phase walk (SC6002's origin) stops there (an owner is set). The tag's own creation is not in its children and keeps its row (`p8`'s SC3001 at the tag, `p9`'s SC6002 uncertifiable at the tag). One stack row moves down, and stays so (review r1 N1): SC2008, a flush in a provider child created in an effect's apply, goes from violation to uncertifiable, because main's violation was never proven: the children memo is lazy, so the flush runs wherever the children are first read, not on the apply's stack.
*Evidence* (release builds, main 408fc4645 against 1fb197f70, which carries ADR 1147 r1). *Patterns* (`ctxmemo`, Chrome rc.21): main four new false positives (s11, p14b, p8, p2; p9 judged fine by the lane's rule family though its violation was at the child), here 5 of 5 fine; the known-open rows moved to `rediscovery.json`. *Generator:* new arm-shape contexts `barm-fwdleaf-tracked` (legal) and `-memo` (misuse) with a shipped package read as source: main 3 false positives on the legal cells, here 3 clean; the misuse twin agrees with Chrome on both. *Monotone* (`--base-ablated` on this build, the two arms ablated: 3,645 programs, textbook, fixtures, six grid samples): M1 0, M2b 0; the only non-up moves are the fixtures' named false-positive sites (`forwarded-leaf-write` HandApp's SC2001 V to clean; `provider-children-memo-owner` TimeoutApp's SC4001 V to clean, TrackedApp's child SC3001 V to uncertifiable), one up; no grid program moves. *Fixtures:* `forwarded-leaf-write` (forwarding through project functions: a stub `solid-js` cannot back a package read as source; the patterns and the generator hold the package path) and `provider-children-memo-owner` (the four review shapes and three stack or exactness negatives); `context-provided-store-tuple` relabels one SC9012 row (main 408fc4645's own reading). *Corpus* (`corpus-delta --all --proof`, one IR worker, 34 projects, against main): violations 243 to 243; this ADR's own rows, per site against this build with both arms ablated: skyjtx-website `components/Tabs/Tabs.tsx:102` (two SC4001 uncertifiable rows go: the `<div class>` and the `{props.children}` insert in `<TabsContext value>`, an exact provider: owned by the memo) and app-game `pixijs-examples/pages/RenderLayers/CharacterUI.tsx:14` (an SC2002 `package-may-call-action` row goes: `() => props.layer` forwarded by `useAttachToRenderLayer` to `createTrackedEffect`'s compute; rc.21's `action()` applies the write guard's scope test, so a leaf callback may call an action); the other 250 rows are ADR 1147's. *Textbook* 16 of 21, 0 problems. *Round 1* (release build of the r1 head): `ArgsApp` and `SwapApp` uncertifiable (`ArgsApp` main V, 1155's head clean: the false clean); `barm-fwdleaf-args` 3 cells: 1155's head 3 false cleans, here 3 uncertifiable, main 3 violations; `NewApp` uncertifiable on every build (N2 latent: a call-free child reaches a creation only through code no build places); patterns 5 of 5, textbook 16 of 21, monotone M1 0, M2b 0, the same three named downs.

*Round 2 (Mac 27, taking over F1).* Refusing every wrapper that reads `arguments` lost a true violation: `loading-member-callee` `ViaArgumentsId` (SC5003, Chrome warns), whose tracked role on main is ADR 0200's forwarding (ADR 1011's proof rides on it), and gave `ArgLenNs` and `ArgLenId` new SC1001 rows. The move showed on main plus 1155 (bundle m), not on 1155's own tree. Now `forwarded_compute_slot` accepts a non-arrow wrapper whose every `arguments` use is written directly in its body as `arguments.length` or a direct call `arguments[k]()` (`arguments_runs_in_place`). A nested function, a hand-off, a write or anything else refuses as before. A call means the literal may also run on the stack of the wrapper's call (`ForwardedCompute::also_at_call`):
- a read keeps the forwarded tracked role only where that call's own role is the same (`forwarded-tracked-compute-arguments-differ`, Unknown, otherwise);
- a write whose forwarded slot is a leaf is unplaced (`forwarded_tracked_compute_role.leaf-arguments-run`), and `forwarded_leaf_scope` refuses: the leaf exempts the slot's write, so a verdict would rest on the `arguments[k]()` run alone, which may be conditional.

`arguments.length` alone runs nothing. *Evidence* (debug build): `ViaArgumentsId` SC5003 a violation again; `ArgLenNs`/`ArgLenId` no SC1001 row (SC5003 uncertifiable, as main); `ArgsApp` SC2001 uncertifiable (`function-run-unplaced`); new `LengthApp` (`arguments.length` only) clean. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/forwarded-leaf-write`): quiet at `HandApp` and `LengthApp`, REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at `MemoApp` (violation) and `ArgsApp` (uncertifiable).

*Round 3 (Mac 27; bundle o's census smoke, mac24/o-census-fp.md).* 1155's census contexts `barm-fwdleaf-{memo,tracked}` showed ten false positives that main b06a4e71a has too. A pending read in a literal ADR 0200 forwards (`hand(() => { a1(); })`) took the forwarded `TrackedJsx` role, and `async_read_clause` read that as a render read: SC5003. Chrome is quiet in the memo compute and reports PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE in createTrackedEffect's. A `sync: true` creation forwarded into the leaf was SC7002, where Chrome reports PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE first.
- `local_access::push_async_read` now places such a read at the wrapper's call of its parameter in the slot's callback (`callee_roles::forwarded_async_site`): the role (`async_read_role`), the computation (`computation_read_suspends`) and the leaf owner (`containing_leaf_owner`) of a read written there. A memo's compute is no render read (uncertifiable here); createTrackedEffect's gives SC5001, as its direct twin.
- A leaf that needs an owned call site (`onSettled`) is unplaced.
- Two forms are left as before: a wrapper that also runs the literal through `arguments`, and an async boundary's held slot (the dialect's `async_boundary_shape`). This keeps `loading-member-callee` exactly as r2.
- `competing_checks`: SC7002 at a creation forwarded only into a leaf (`forwarded_only_into_leaf`) is `creation-throws-first`.

*Evidence.* Census focus on the three contexts (126 programs, release, the census run's Chrome cache): main 12 false positives, r3 0. The 11 go to not-fired, `pending-async-forbidden-scope-…-tracked` to agree, and the two `args` twins agree to recall-gap (r1's, accepted). The ten are in rediscovery.json and the census smoke manifest. Fixture `forwarded-async-read`, Chrome `runtime-oracle/forwarded-async-read`: TrackedApp's PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE is covered by SC5001; SyncApp's PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE is covered; MemoApp is silent. *Found, not fixed:* ADR 0200's callee resolution is not exact for a reassigned `let` (`loading-member-callee` `WrapLet`) or a factory's result (`ViaWrap`, `ignore(fn)` returns another function). Their V stands by coincidence, since the real run is bare in the render; a write through such a callee could take the wrong scope (docs/open-work.md).

*Round 4 (Mac 27; bundle p's follow-up).* SyncApp's creation was SC7002 uncertifiable (`creation-throws-first`) and, under SC3001, `leaf-operation-unaccounted`: the leaf walk stops at the wrapper's `fn()` (SC9012 `leaf-callback-opaque`), so no row named the operation the leaf refuses. Now the leaf walk also reports, where it is written, a call the leaf refuses that sits directly in the body of a literal `forwarded_only_into_leaf` proves (`callee_roles::forwarded_leaf_call`), when neither the literal nor the leaf callback is `async` or a generator and the wrapper's call of its parameter is in the callback's body. SC7002 stays uncertifiable there; SC3001 is a violation. Fixture `forwarded-leaf-operation` (Chrome `runtime-oracle/forwarded-leaf-operation`: the six violations covered; `BothApp`, `SettledApp` and `RelayApp` throw and stay uncertifiable; the rest silent). *Evidence* (release, Chrome cache): census contexts `barm-fwdleaf-{tracked,memo,args}` (126 programs) against 1155 r3: recall-gap 31 to 24, agree 20 to 27 (the seven `tracked` cells of PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE (memo, root, effect), CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE, FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK, `resolve` and `until`); the forbidden-scope codes on every grid (7,444 programs, legal grids included): no other move but two `lg-combo` uncertifiable-to-clean programs, clean with this pass switched off too (main's own move since 1155 r3). Coverage: `forwarded-async-read` SyncApp SC3001 uncertifiable to violation, nothing else.

## ADR 1167 — A never-rerunning effect's returned cleanup runs only at disposal: its reads are placed as an `onCleanup` callback's
**The gap.** R3's catalog group G3, legal half (L5, 651 programs): `createEffect(() => 1, () => () => { read })` inside a `Show` branch or a `For` row left the read uncertifiable (`function-run-unplaced`, arm `allowed-unplaced-nested`) though ADR 0539 proved the effect never reruns (`effect_never_reruns`, `WindowedCleanup::NeverReruns`) and the rule page already called that cleanup silent; Chrome is quiet there.
**Decision.** `write_roles::returned_cleanup_disposal_only`, read only (`read_execution_role`, when the read's role is unplaced): the read is in the body of the cleanup (no nested function, instance field or parameter default; the cleanup neither `async` nor a generator), the cleanup is the literal an apply returns at an effect's or render effect's own apply slot whose compute provably tracks nothing (so no rerun calls it, and no other code names it), and no project code can dispose an owner on a stack of its own (`project_may_dispose`, ADR 0695). The read is `DeferredCallback`, as an `onCleanup` callback's (`allowed-nested-disposal`). Only reads take it: a `For` row's disposal runs the cleanup owned, which owner codes (and actions, `onFlush`) read differently, so every other site keeps the unplaced role.
**Evidence.** Fixtures `effect-cleanup-disposal-only` (clean: `ShowRemoved`, `ForRowRemoved`, `RenderEffectCleanup`; uncertifiable: a tracking compute, a named apply, a nested read, an async cleanup) and `effect-cleanup-disposal-reachable` (a `createRoot` dispose: uncertifiable). Chrome rc.21 (`runtime-oracle/effect-cleanup-disposal-only`, `-reachable`): quiet at the clean three and at the `createRoot` case, STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at the tracking compute after its rerun. Probe, release builds, main b06a4e71a against the branch, 1,551 recall programs in the `effect-cleanup-*`/`render-cleanup-*` contexts (SRU, PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK, STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER, NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY, REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE; layer none, direct and alias): lg-recall 100 uncertifiable to clean (`effect-cleanup-show`, `-for`), mx-recall nothing moved, no owner or write code moved.

## ADR 1166 — A read a named callback's open entries leave unplaced is a violation where a run of the callback provably executes it
**The gap.** R3's catalog group G5 (M3 666 misuse, L9 477 legal, simple slice of the recall grids): a function a primitive names by its binding and also runs another way (`createMemo(f); [f].forEach((g) => g())`, `onSettled(f); f()`, `createEffect(f, …); [f].map(…)`) left its read uncertifiable (`function-run-unplaced`, the ADR 0517/1111/1119 arms) though Chrome reports STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at it.
**Decision.** A read rule asks whether some run of the read is untracked. `named_callbacks::reporting_run_role` answers, for reads only (`read_execution_role`, the member read path of `local_access`, and the timing check `callee_callback_timing`), when every premise holds: the read is in the body of its function (no nested function, instance field or parameter default), which is neither `async` nor a generator nor a method and is the whole initializer of a `const` binding; a run is a direct call of that binding or a carried `forEach`/`map` (ADR 1124's `foreach_carried_call`, `map` added: it runs each element on the same stack the same way) whose arrow calls its parameter on every completion; the run is written in the function that declares the binding, after the declarator, and is in `synchronously_unconditional_calls` of that function (no condition, loop or early exit; a dead `if (false) f()` is not); a read written at the run reports and passes the timing check; and outside the body's rendering no call stands between the declarator and the run (a creation in an effect's apply throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK first, rc.21; Chrome showed it on the fixture). The run's role is the read's. Anything else keeps the unplaced role, and every other site (writes, owner codes) keeps it too. `map` also completes the entry census (ADR 1119), so a `map` run where no read rule reports certifies the read clean.
**Evidence.** Fixture `named-callback-reporting-run` (7 violations, a clean handler `map`, 7 uncertifiable twins: dead, conditional carrier, loop, `filter`, `let`, nested read, creation before the run in an apply); Chrome rc.21 (`runtime-oracle/named-callback-reporting-run`): covered-violation at the 7, quiet at the clean and the apply twin. Coverage: 8 projects, every move U to V where Chrome warns (`named-callback-escaped-entry`, `named-fn-expr-calls`, `effect-compute-also-called`, `destructure-store-slots` SC1003, `accessor-provenance` `Eager`) or a U blocker renamed. Probe, release builds, main b600297eb against the branch, 1,497 SRU recall programs (store variants `byname*`, `settled*`, `effect*`, `render-effect*`, layer none, direct): mx-recall 59 recall-gap to agree, lg-recall 9 uncertifiable to clean (`byname-mapped` under a memo, compute, JSX or `untrack`), nothing else moved.
**Not covered, named.** A run in another function than the declaring one (the body's `f` carried in an apply), a non-literal or aliased carrier, `filter`/`some`/other methods, a `let` or function-declaration binding, a nested read, a signal read the program-wide SC9012 tuple withdrawal holds (`foreach-carrier`).
**Round 2 (census false cleans).** Bundle q's census smoke found two false cleans from round 1, `mx-{resolve,until}-in-reactive-scope-barm-carried-body-x-direct-none` (`const f1 = () => { resolve(() => 1); }; createEffect(f1, () => {}); [f1].forEach((g) => g());`: Chrome throws in the compute run). The reporting run sat in shared code: the generic `callee_callback_timing` (which SC2004/SC2005's `resolve_scope` and every other rule read) declared the timing proven from the untracked carried run, and `read_execution_role` gave every caller the reporting role. One untracked run is a witness only for a claim each untracked run raises on its own (SC1001's warning); a throwing rule or one that fires on a tracked run needs every run, and an earlier run (an effect's compute runs at creation) may throw first. So the reporting run now places strict reads only: `strict_read_role` and `strict_read_callee_timing`, applied where `local_access` builds a `ReactiveRead` (five row sites and `member_read`); `read_execution_role` and `callee_callback_timing` are main's again; the member path hands its async row the unplaced role. Fixture twins `TwinResolveComputeCarried`, `TwinUntilComputeCarried` (SC2004/SC2005 `function-run-unplaced` kept; the r1 build: silent), Chrome case `named-callback-reporting-run-tracked` (both throws in the page's console). Round 1's fixture findings are unchanged. Boundary gap for `execution_role.read_execution_role.reporting-run`, and the named rise of `foreach-carrier` (from the integrator's join). Smoke (release, this branch, `--cover all --cover-seed 1 --sample 0`, the smoke's judge on code-level rows): census leg 44,471 programs, nothing needs a look (0 false-clean; the 3 known-open false positives and 8 R-unplaced of open-defects); rest leg (mx-recall 34,294, lg-recall 6,537 and the base, src, combo and pairs grids), nothing needs a look. Of the 3,943 mx-recall programs round 1 moved to agree (the integrator's judge), 3,567 stay agree; 376 return to recall-gap (`flush-read-body` and `-iife` 360, `pos-class-ctor`/`-method` 16), where the carried run sits in a callback of a helper the body calls and round 1 placed that helper's body through the shared arm: the named cost of keeping the reporting run to strict reads. **Corpus (bundle s).** The joint run's corpus delta found 2 new SC1001 violations (4 rows, both builds) at kui `GroupRoute.tsx:80` (`feature-consumers`, `shell`): a `const refresh` declared in an effect's apply reads `props.clusterId`, the apply calls it once after the declarator and a timer re-runs it. ADR 1132's ruling makes that handler reachable; while the element is mounted the component owns the effect, so the write reruns it with its owner alive, and the rerun calls the cleanup in the apply's window. ## ADR 1156 — The smoke's `rest` leg runs as two jobs of one cover, split by program id (`smoke` and `smoke-2`)
**The problem.** ADR 1001 split the pull request's smoke into the legs `rest` and `census` when the cover held 67,086 programs. It holds 90,071 now (`--cover all`, seed 1: `rest` 45,600, census 44,471), and the one `rest` job outgrew the pull request's 60 minutes: #307's `smoke` was cancelled at the limit (no failure; the job had taken 24, then 51 minutes on earlier pull requests). The cover cannot be cut (ADR 1001), and the ruling of 2026-11-21 is to shard the leg, not to raise the limit.
**Decision.** `focus.mjs --smoke-shard i/N` (with `--smoke`, `--sample 0`, on grids the cover samples: beside a per-code cover the census runs whole, so there it is refused) draws the whole cover as ADR 1001 does, then keeps of each grid the programs whose `shardOf(id, N)` is `i` (`shard.mjs`: `fnv("shard:<id>") mod N`, the pick `--grid-shard` makes of a grid, which the cover's seed and tie-breaks do not touch). It judges the proved-verdict ledger within that part only (`ledgerPart`): a ledger program of another part has no row in this job and is judged where its row is, so none is lost twice or in none. Every job prints the whole cover's hash (a shard adds `cover shard i/N: K of P programs`). `fuzz-pr.yml`'s matrix is `smoke` (`rest`, 0/2), `smoke-2` (`rest`, 1/2) and `smoke-census`. Each job has its own installs, cache restore, build, artifacts and runtime cache (`fuzz-pr-runtime-rest-0-`, `rest-1-` and `census-<sha>`, restoring its own, then its leg's, then any: records are keyed by program bytes); the cache trim of a push to main divides its 20,000-entry floor by N for a shard; the textbook tier stays in the census job. `smoke` keeps its name and is now the first part, `smoke-2` is new, and neither is a required check. `shard.test.mjs` reads the matrix and fails when a leg's parts are not every index of one N once each, or two jobs share a name or a cache. Owners: `scripts/fuzz/shard.mjs` (`smokeShardOf`, `inShard`, `ledgerPart`), `cover.mjs` (`writeCover`, `writeSample`), `focus.mjs`, `.github/workflows/fuzz-pr.yml`; the fuzz README's Merge gate.
**Evidence.** The real cover at the pull request's parameters, written whole and as shards through `writeCover`: `rest` 45,600 = 22,832 + 22,768 programs (50.1% and 49.9%; mx-recall 17,174 + 17,120), each grid's parts a partition of its cover in its order; the 12,671 programs of the eleven grids' ledgers divide 6,379 and 6,292, each in one part and in that shard's manifest. `focus.mjs` end to end (release checker, Chrome oracle on) on the six base grids, 1,085 programs: the whole run and the two shards together judge the same programs with the same outcome each (agree 468, clean 106, recall-gap 314, uncertifiable 197), none in both; the ledger's 215 programs are 109 + 106, none lost; all three print the same cover hash. Six corruptions of the workflow (a part dropped, renumbered, a cache shared, the shard not passed, a leg renamed, the census sharded alone) each fail the matrix test.
**Not changed, named.** The cover, its seed, required ids, families and the census job. The split is by program count, not by cost. Measured on the CI of the pull request that landed it (#309, job totals with setup): `smoke` 31m38s, `smoke-2` 28m11s, `smoke-census` 29m56s, against the one `rest` job that the 60-minute limit cancelled on #307. The oracle's sample (a program per stratum, at most 25 per grid process) is drawn inside each job from its own programs, so two jobs compare more programs than one did (266 against 150 on the six base grids). A failing job reruns alone: `focus.mjs --smoke --smoke-leg rest --smoke-shard i/2 --cover all --cover-seed 1 --sample 0` with the checker and producer paths.

## ADR 1162 — A store destructure hands over every property whose key is exact: quoted, renamed, defaulted, empty nested
**The gap** (R3 catalog G7; main b600297eb). ADR 1107 handed a store destructure that setup does not provably run to SC1001's placement only when every property was a shorthand name. A quoted key (`{ "v": x }`), a renamed slot, a default and an empty nested pattern (`{ a: {} }`, `{ items: [] }`, `{ v, a: {} }`) were left to SC1003's own role. That role is uncertifiable in an effect's apply or a ref, where Chrome reports STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED. A `then`-only pattern (`{ then: w }`, `{ "then": w }`, `{ then = 1 }`, `{ then: {} }`) was `store-key-undecided`, even where Chrome is silent.
**Decision.** `static_rules::destructure_slot_keys` reads each property as the one Get it makes, by the parser's key (facts schema 100). It also finds the span whose source text is that key: the key as written, or inside its quotes when it has no escape. It refuses the whole pattern for a computed key, a rest element, an escaped key, or a nested pattern that is not empty: such a pattern reads past its key. A default is evaluated after the Get, as code of its own. `delegated_destructure_slots` builds a synthetic member at the whole property, with the key's span as its property. That is where the read universe has the site (`proof_universe.rs`). `store_head_get` and `exempt_store_get_runs_nothing` read a slot's key from it, so a `then` slot over a literal `then` that nothing writes is exempt, as `store.then` is. A form ADR 1107 did not hand over keeps SC1003's role silence where that role proves one (`destructure_role_does_not_report`). Without it, three lg-recall programs went clean to uncertifiable: a helper reached through a `let` copy in a handler, whose member twin is unplaced.
**Measured** (release, b600297eb against this; 999 mx-recall and 999 lg-recall `store-dstr-{empty-*,quoted,then-*,object,empty-comment}` programs, Chrome results cached). mx-recall: recall-gap to agree 120, recall-gap stays 740, agree 139 unchanged. lg-recall: uncertifiable to clean 240, uncertifiable stays 422, clean 332 unchanged, 0 false positives, no other move. The 5 `unexecuted` violations (`arm-tag`) are main's, unchanged (R3 section 2). Coverage: the new fixture, and two moves in `destructure-store-slots`. `SiblingEmptyInHelper` is uncertifiable both ways (`props-callers-unenumerated` to `summary-read-unplaced`, as its `{ v }` twin). `ThenFirstInApply`'s `then` slot loses its SC9012 `store-key-undecided` row: the literal's `then` is data and there is no setter, so it is exempt as `store.then` is. The SC1003 violation (from `v`) stays, and Chrome covers it. Ownership gate 96 passed. Fixture `destructure-store-slot-patterns`. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/destructure-store-slot-patterns`) covers the six violations, is silent at the four `then` cases, and reports at `{ then: { b } }`, which stays uncertifiable.
**Not covered.** An escaped key: an escape anywhere makes the file uncertifiable (ADR 1152). A non-empty nested pattern, a computed key, a rest element and a written backing stay uncertifiable. A destructure written in setup keeps SC1003's own verdict.

## ADR 1161 — `flush(fn)` in a closure that only in-place layers run takes the role of that run's call
**The gap** (R3 catalog G11; main b600297eb). `const f1 = () => { flush(() => { r1(); }); return 1; }; f1();` was SC1001 uncertifiable `function-run-unplaced`. Chrome reports STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED. The `flush` callback takes the role of its call (`inline_callback_execution_role`). That role is the lexical `UntrackedRendering` of the closure's body, and `nested_literal_runs_during_body` does not prove that `f1` runs in the body, so the role was Unknown.
**Decision.** `callback_standing::in_place_call_role`: before falling back to Unknown, climb from the `flush` call through the in-place layers (`climb_in_place_layers`: a closure whose only reference is one direct call, `sole_call_of_named_function`; an IIFE; an inline standard-library callback). The climb must cross at least one layer, with no bound, no parameter list, no await, no other run and no withheld call. The callback then takes the role of the call it reaches. As for the call itself, `UntrackedRendering` stands only where that call runs during the body. `flush(fn)` runs `fn` on its caller's stack and keeps the caller's window (rule page; ADR 0859).
**Measured** (release, d917ff74f + this against b600297eb's runs, Chrome cached; 999 mx-recall and 999 lg-recall programs from every context named `*flush*`). mx-recall: recall-gap to agree 112, 447 stay recall-gap, agree 423 unchanged, not-fired 17. lg-recall: no move (766 U, 233 clean). Coverage: the new fixture, and `read-flush-layer-placed` `HelperInBody` (uncertifiable to violation; Chrome warns). Fixture `flush-closure-called-once`. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/flush-closure-called-once`) covers the four violations and is silent at the two clean cases.
**Not covered.** A closure also handed on (a timer, `forEach`), called twice, or stored stays uncertifiable. So do the legal `flush-read-each` and `handed-flush` rows, a closure handed to `forEach` in tracked JSX: no climb crosses a handed reference.

## ADR 1163 — A read written in an effect bundle's `error` member reads in no window while no drain of the program has one
**The gap** (R3 catalog G8; main b600297eb). `createEffect(c, { effect, error: () => { r1(); } })` was SC1001 uncertifiable `function-run-unplaced`, in 510 legal lg-recall programs where Chrome is silent. ADR 0548 placed the member's owner (none), but the read role fell through `nested_unplaced_role` to `allowed-unplaced-nested`.
**What rc.21 does** (`@solidjs/signals@2.0.0-rc.21`):
- `notifyEffectStatus` queues a user effect whose compute errored (`dist/dev.js:2660-2668`).
- `runEffect` runs its `_errorFn` before `setStrictRead("an effect callback")`, `setEffectCallback` and `enterCallback` (`:2737-2758`, `:2767`).
- `createEffect` passes `effectFn.error` (`:3349`); `createReaction` hands it to its effect (`:3495`).
- The queue drains on the stack of whoever drains it, and `flush` leaves `strictRead` as it found it (`dist/dev-shared.js:3032-3110`). So the arm reads in the drainer's window.

Chrome confirms it: the arm drained by a `flush()` in a component body reports STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED (`runtime-oracle/effect-error-arm-read-flush-in-body`).
**Decision.** In `callee_roles::nested_unplaced_role`, a read written directly in an exact bundle's `error` member (`bundle_error_member`: a literal, no spread) is `DeferredCallback`, as a disposal's cleanup is. That holds only when `error_arm_drains_unwindowed`:
- ADR 0613's census proves every drain the program makes ownerless or empty. Of those callers only `runWithOwner(null, …)` keeps a window, so a program naming `runWithOwner` is refused.
- No action steps: `inTransaction` drains on its caller's stack (`dist/dev.js:2196-2206`).
- No synchronous event dispatch could carry a read (`synchronous_event_read_dispatch_present`).

Otherwise the read is Unknown. Each premise reads a section its reader already binds (FlushVeto, ProjectPrimitives, DispatchVeto). Writes and owner rules are unchanged. `bundle_error_member_runs_unowned` now cites rc.21.
**Measured** (release, d917ff74f + this against b600297eb's runs, Chrome cached; every `*error-arm*` program of the simple slices: 472 mx-recall, 827 lg-recall). lg-recall: uncertifiable to clean 116, 623 stay uncertifiable, 88 clean unchanged. mx-recall: no move (408 agree, 64 recall-gap). Coverage: only the new fixture's three projects. Fixture `effect-error-arm-read`: four reads clean; a named bundle, a spread bundle, and a `flush` in a root or the body stay uncertifiable. Chrome: quiet at the clean reads and in the root variant, reports in the body variant.
**Not covered.** A read in a closure nested in the arm, a named or spread bundle, and any program the premise refuses stay uncertifiable. A drain a dependency makes is ADR 0613's documented premise: hydration, a delegated event's own stack, an async landing on its continuation. Writes and primitives in the arm (SC2001, SC6002, SC2008 legal rows) are not placed here.

## ADR 1159 — SC6002: a creation in an inline event handler, or after an unconditional `await`, runs off every apply
**The problem.** A creation (`resolve`, `until`, `createMemo`) written in an element's inline `onClick={() => …}`, or after an `await` in an async function, kept `effect-creation-unaccounted` where Chrome is quiet (G10 of the r3 catalog: 458 legal programs, 240 of lg-base). The role silence (ADR 0969) asks that no layer around the site is entered by a reference that is no direct call, and the entry walk reads an inline handler as a function value no binding names that is no whole argument of a call: open. A site after an `await` was declined as not plain (`after-suspension`).
**Decision.** (1) `owner_emission::runs_in_delivered_handler` answers SC6002's `effect-creation-runs-off-apply` beside the entry walk: the layers around the site, out to an element's inline event handler literal (the compiler's `EventHandler` callback, no generator, an event no fact denies, a compiler result not withheld), are each an unnamed function called where it is written; the literal has no binding, so its delivery is its one entry. It holds only where no effect's apply may dispatch an event (`apply_dispatch_possible`, failing closed on `eval`, unread modules and calls in an apply no fact names): ADR 1139's shadow delivery runs a handler inside the apply's effect-callback window. A named layer (a local helper, an exported one an unseen importer may call) keeps the walk's answer. (2) `effect-creation-after-await` (premise `AfterAwait`, the `await`): a creation written directly in an async function, after an `await` of that function every run reaches first (`unconditional_await_before`), not in JSX or a field initializer, runs from the await's continuation, a microtask on an empty stack, never inside an apply's synchronous run. An `await` some run may skip (a branch, a loop, `finally`) proves nothing.
**Evidence.** Fixture `owner-call-effect-creation`: `ApplyAfterAwait` moves `effect-creation-unaccounted` to silent; `ApplyBeforeAwait` and `PropHandler` (a component's prop its apply calls) are violations, `ApplyBranchAwait` uncertifiable; `Handler` keeps its row there (`Kid`'s apply calls a prop, which may dispatch); `variants/inline-handler`: `Handler`, `HandlerResolve`, `HandlerIife` silent, `HandlerNamed` and `HandlerExported` keep their rows; `variants/sync-dispatch` unchanged. Coverage: 35 SC6002 `effect-creation-unaccounted` rows leave 22 other fixtures (inline handlers in programs with no apply dispatch, and test callbacks past an unconditional `await`), nothing else; a first cut that let the entry walk pass a handler silenced `exported-helper-in-apply`'s exported helper and `sync-dispatch`'s handler, which the conditions above keep. Chrome: `runtime-oracle/handler-creation` quiet on both builds (the checker silent here, uncertifiable on main); `runtime-oracle/apply-await-creation` `covered-uncertifiable` on both (PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK before the `await`, at the skipped branch and at `PropHandler`; quiet after the `await`). Fuzz, release against main (b600297eb build; branch on d917ff74f): mx-base and lg-base × RESOLVE, UNTIL, PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK (2,040 programs): lg-base 64 of the 240 uncertifiable to clean (the direct and IIFE layers; the named closure and helper layers keep their rows), mx-base 840 agree on both; mx-recall and lg-recall over the 115 handler, async and event contexts of the three codes (18,930 programs): lg-recall 552 uncertifiable to clean (`handler` 144, `memo-async` 126, `async`, `effect-async`, `async-entry-late` 94 each), mx-recall identical findings, nothing needs a look. The loop and `finally` forms keep their rows.

## ADR 1160 — `ref={name}` is the named function's entry at that reference
**The problem.** A named function used only as an intrinsic element's `ref={rf1}` kept `function-run-unplaced` (SC2001 on a setter call, SC1001's read role undecided) where Chrome is quiet (G14 of the r3 catalog: 84 legal programs, `ref-named`). **Decision.** `NamedCallbackRoles`: where a `ref` expression the compiler names as the element's `DirectiveApply` is exactly the function's own binding (an identifier whose declaration is that binding), the position is that reference; any other expression (a factory call, a conditional, an array) keeps the element as before. A second reference (a call, an export, a hand-off, a component's `ref` prop) is still an entry the census refuses.
**Evidence.** Fixture `named-ref-entry`: `RefWrite` moves SC2001 `function-run-unplaced` to silent; `AlsoCalled` and `ComponentRef` stay SC2001 violations, `Exported` uncertifiable, `RefRead` an SC1001 violation. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/named-ref-entry`): quiet at `RefWrite` and `Exported`, REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE and STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at the three reported sites, covered on both builds. **Not built.** A function a factory returns (`ref={dir1()}`, `ref-factory`) has no binding, so the census has no name to count: it keeps `function-run-unplaced`.
