## ADR 1170 — A store literal proves when `sort`, `reverse`, `fill` and `copyWithin` write
**The gap** (R3 catalog G13; main b600297eb). ADR 0718 left these four methods on a store path uncertifiable `store-operation-may-not-write`: they read the length and write nothing on a short array or an empty range. In `createStore({ items: [1, 2] })` with `store.items.reverse()` they do write, and Chrome reports STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER.
**Upstream.** eslint-plugin-solid at `6d3bc311` has no mutator list and no store-write rule. This logic is product-owned (ADRs 0425, 0491, 0718), although it lives under `upstream_compat/`, so there is no upstream heuristic to keep. The module-scope ownership case `no-store-mutation-outside-setter/array-mutator/001` stays uncertifiable: ADR 0491's proof takes a function-local store only.
**Decision.** `literal_mutator_writes` (`shared_reactivity.rs`) reads the array literal ADR 0491's proof resolves (`LiteralValue::Array` now carries its span). Every element must be a value: no spread, no hole.
- `reverse()` writes on two or more elements.
- `sort()` writes on two or more number literals, with no comparator or `(a, b) => b - a` / `a - b` of its own two parameters. V8 returns a shorter array as is, else writes every element back, and nothing throws first.
- `fill(v, s?, e?)` and `copyWithin(t, s?, e?)` write on a non-empty range whose bounds are non-negative integer literals clamped to the length.

Each write meets the proxy's `set` trap, which warns whatever the value (rc.21 `dist/dev.js:6663-6668`). `contained_store_use` accepts such a call as a use that leaks no proxy: number elements reach the comparator. `links_proven_wrappable` reports it. `no_store_mutator_call` lifts the blocker through `literal_mutator_proven`, which a store that is itself an array never meets.
**Measured** (release, d917ff74f + this against b600297eb's runs, Chrome cached; 1,278 mx-recall STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER programs, every `items-*` and `noop-*` variant, and all 396 legal ones). mx-recall: recall-gap to agree 566, 2 stay recall-gap, agree 710 unchanged. lg-recall: no move (the `noop-*` rows on a root array stay uncertifiable). Fixture `store-array-mutators-literal`: seven violations and seven uncertifiable. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/store-array-mutators-literal`) reports at the seven and at the three uncertifiable that write, and is silent at the four no-ops.
**Not covered.** A store that is itself an array, string or other elements under `sort`, any other comparator, a negative or computed bound, a module-scope store, and anything ADR 0491's proof refuses stay uncertifiable.

The reactive direction stays `resolve_forwarded_props`' (ADR 0919): a first cut that also carried a forwarder's reactive witness here skipped its getter checks and made 7 of `spread-prop-backing`'s kept-uncertifiable reads violations. Depth 4.

Chrome (`runtime-oracle/prop-spread-forward-sources`): REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at `Body` (main covered-uncertifiable, here covered-violation), the rest quiet. ## ADR 1171 — A component prop's function literal is entered by the child's calls of it
**The problem.** A function literal written as a component prop (`<Kid run={() => …} />`) had no owner edge (ADR 0971's accepted trade) and no entry the walk could follow, so what it creates or registers kept SC4001 `owner-callers-unenumerated` or `function-run-unplaced` whether the child calls it in its body (owned: Chrome quiet), in an effect's apply or a handler (no owner: Chrome NO_OWNER_*), or never (G2 of the r3 catalog).
**Decision.** `execution_role::prop_literal_call_sites`: the literal is the whole value of the element's one attribute of that name, the element has no spread, its tag renders a project component written in the same file that nothing else names (every reference of its binding is this tag, no export), and in the component `props` is kept (`props_kept`, factored out of ADR 0204's body-call test: a plain parameter only read through static members, never written) and every `props.<prop>` is a call's callee, none in a class written in the component. Those calls are then all the literal's runs. The owner graph takes an edge from each, as a direct call's (`MayRun` where the call may not run), and the entry walk (`layer_entry_open`) reads them as the literal's entries. A literal the child never calls keeps its row (no run to place it by; the 2026-11-17 dead-site ruling gives U).
**Evidence.** Fixture `component-prop-call-owner` (closed): `Body` (called in the child's body) loses SC4001; `Apply` (called in an effect's apply) is an SC4001 violation, NO_OWNER_CLEANUP; `Never`, `Twice`, `Held` and `Spread` keep their rows. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/component-prop-call-owner`): NO_OWNER_CLEANUP at `Apply` (main uncertifiable, here `covered-violation`) and at `Held`'s timer (covered-uncertifiable on both), `Body` quiet. Coverage: `errored-fallback-owner` `UserComponent` and `Shadowed` (a component calls its `fallback` prop from a handler) become SC4001 violations, Chrome NO_OWNER_CLEANUP on `errored-fallback-userprop` and `-shadow`; SC4001 rows leave `fp-owner-component-ref` (2, a `ref` prop the child calls in its body), `owner-callback-prop` (one; one becomes SC4002 `computation-error-unobserved`), `prop-body-call-guard` (one) and `stored-throw-observation` (one); a first cut silenced `prop-body-call-guard`'s class-field call, now refused. Fuzz, release against main (b600297eb build; branch on d917ff74f), every `cbp-*` context × its 19 codes: lg-recall 19,554 programs, 204 uncertifiable to clean (`cbp-body`, `cbp-jsx`: NO_OWNER_EFFECT, NO_OWNER_CONTEXT, SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED), 480 more lose their SC4001 row (SC3001/SC6002 stay, B3: the exported `C1` may be rendered by an unseen importer); mx-recall 14,076 programs, 150 recall-gap to agree (`cbp-apply`, `cbp-settled`: NO_OWNER_CLEANUP, NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY, SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED), 90 change only an uncertifiable row; nothing needs a look. The never-called cells keep every row.
**Not built.** The read and write roles (SC1001's `callee-callback-timing`, SC2001's `function-run-unplaced` for a prop called in an apply) still take the literal's lexical role; the destructured, forwarded, spread and named (`run={f}`) forms; a child in another file or rendered twice.

## ADR 1172 — Part 1: a write's row answers its own Set, not a Get of a link on its chain
**The defect** (on main b06a4e71a; found building this ADR's fixture). A store a component received by prop and held in a `const` alias (`const held = props.s1; held.a.v = 9`) had no row of any rule at the Get `held.a`. Chrome warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED there (`runtime-oracle/prop-alias-link-get`: unproven-clean on main). The value-use census (ADR 1114) took a decided SC2003 write that starts at a member reached through an alias (`write_decided`) as the answer for that member, though in a deeper write the member is a Get of its own. The same Get alone (`void held.a`) kept SC9012 `value-held-in-binding`.
**Decision.** `value_use::Census::member` counts a decided write only where it is the member's own Set (`write_decided_target`). A deeper write leaves the Get open, with SC9012 `value-held-in-binding` (fail closed; a violation needs the alias proven to be the store, ADR 1169).
**Evidence.** Fixture `prop-alias-link-get`: WriteChild gets the row; RootWriteChild (`held.items = [1]`, a Set with no Get of a link) is unchanged. Chrome covers it (covered-uncertifiable). Coverage: SC9012 rises only, at the same shape in `local-alias-member-reads` (`holder.state.nested.v = 1`, whose direct twin is an SC1001 violation) and `store-write-literal-links` (`thing.useIt.a.v = 1`); named in rises.json. Probe (release, 1,837 programs: R4's N1 rows and 396 legal STORE_WRITE programs): no outcome moves. Rediscovery: an `outside` row. The read grids do not cross a store variant with a prop or context source, and mx-src judges the generated program `…-nested-assign-alias-none-s-prop` for STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER only.

**Part 2 — a store written through a prop** (R4 group N1: 764 misuse rows, blocker `store-write-unproven`). `props.s1.a.v = 7`, with `<C1 s1={s1} setS1={setS1} />` and `s1` a local `createStore`, was uncertifiable: ADR 0919's handed route proves `props.s1` is the store, but the link past it needs ADR 0491's literal proof, which refused a store or setter used as a JSX attribute value. ADR 0491 now accepts a hand-off to an exact local component (a JSX tag that resolves to a function of the file; `handed_component_prop`):
- the store handed as an attribute whose every read in the component (`props.s1`, a destructured `s1`, or an exact `const` alias of either, four levels; `component_prop_reads`, `const_alias_reads`) is a contained use;
- the setter handed as an attribute the component never reads.

The component must read its props only through static members, or a pattern of static keys with no rest, default or nested value. `handed_container_write` then proves the links from the store's own binding (`handed_links_wrappable`, same strictNullChecks and optional-link conditions as ADR 0491).
*Measured* (release, against main b06a4e71a; Chrome cached). R4's 1,441 N1 programs plus the 396 legal STORE_WRITE programs of lg-recall: U to V 428 (mx-src 208, mx-pairs 208, mx-combo 12); no legal row moved; no V lost. Fixture `store-write-through-prop`: 4 violations, 4 uncertifiable (a setter read and called, the prop handed on, props used whole, the store also leaving the parent). Chrome covers all eight. Coverage: `store-handed-root` `Nested` goes from uncertifiable to violation (Chrome-confirmed on a scratch case of it).
*Not covered.* A context, `merge`/`omit` view or spread hand-off; a component in another file; a write in the setter's callback reached through a prop (R4 N1's legal `in-setter` rows stay uncertifiable); an SC1001 violation at an alias's Get (part 1's SC9012 row stands).

## ADR 1169 — Part 1: a Get through a held store link has a row
**The defect** (main 14469fac2 and ADR 1172's tip; found starting this ADR). `const held = s1.a; void held.v` had no row of any rule at the Get `held.v`. Chrome warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED there (`runtime-oracle/store-link-alias-get`, unproven-clean on both). The value-use census answered a store root's own member chain (`Mode::Root`, the root's own reference) where the chain ended, and never walked a binding that holds the chain's link.
**Decision.** `value_use::Census::member`: the root's own static chain, held whole in an identifier binding, is walked on as the root. Its uses are then an alias's: a Get with no read row stands open as SC9012 `value-held-in-binding` (fail closed). Part 2 proves the exact alias as the store's link.

## ADR 1164 — A read in a `for await` body that runs, and a `finally` after `await Promise.resolve()`, are past the await
G1 of the R3 catalog (S half). ADR 1038 already reads a `for await` body as past the loop's suspension, so what stayed uncertifiable was two things. The SC1002 walk marked every read after an implicit suspension as an obligation (`after_implicit_suspension`, `SuspensionUnplaced`). The try-head proof (`follows_try_head_await`, ADR 0612) took only a call of an async function declaration, not the `await Promise.resolve()` every generated `finally` uses.

**Decision.**
- *`for await`* (`after_await.rs` `for_await_bodies_that_run`): a read written directly in the body of a `for await`, in the walked async non-generator function, is not marked when the iterable is an array literal whose first element is a decimal integer, boolean or `null` literal and no visible write reaches the array iterator. The first `next()` then fulfills and the body runs, every run past the loop's await, in the computation's flight. Its row is a violation unless an obligation of its own (an earlier tracked read, ADR 0195) stands.
- *`finally`* (`body_roles.rs` `operand_cannot_throw`): a `try` head may also await the global `Promise.resolve(…)` with literal arguments only. That means no shadowing declaration and no computed member, the call resolving to `PromiseConstructor.resolve`, and the Promise intrinsics intact. Such a call returns a native promise and runs no project code. A `new` operand is refused for both forms (`new` of an async function throws).
- The read roles that answer `Unreported` past an await keep the declaration-only proof (`follows_declared_try_head_await`, and a climb whose suspension rests on such a head: `window_after_awaits`, `layered_window_after_awaits`, `unwindowed_role_at_call`, `inherits_callback_role`). As ADR 1112 says of a `for await` body, `Unreported` silences SC1002 too, and a compute the tracked-computation walk does not find is asked by nothing else. The write, owner, hand-off and reach proofs take the wider one.

**Not changed.**
- A stream, a named or spread iterable, a promise element, a read in a closure or helper the body runs, and code after the loop keep their obligations.
- So does a `try` head with a name argument, `globalThis.Promise`, or code before its await.
- A read past an await in an async function that only a handler or the component body calls stays SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted`: no "no flight" reason exists (owner ruling 5 of ADR 0973). The legal half of G1 is not built.

**Evidence.**
- Fixture `after-await-for-await-finally`:
  - `ForAwaitRead` and `ForAwaitReadGuarded` move from SC1002 U to V;
  - `FinallyWrite` and `FinallyWriteLiteral` move from SC2001 U to clean;
  - the eight counterexamples stay U.
- `write-past-layered-await` `Named`'s write in the `finally`: U to clean.
- Chrome (`runtime-oracle/after-await-for-await-finally`): UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT at the three violations (`covered-violation`) and at every uncertifiable read that runs (`covered-uncertifiable`); nothing at the clean writes.
- Probe, release, VM, main b600297eb against this branch: 2,160 programs of mx-recall and lg-recall in the `*-for-await` and `*-finally` contexts, every code, layers none, closure, iife and helper, stratified by code, context, variant and binding. Results:

## ADR 1165 — An owner call in a `for await` body that runs is past the await
G4 of the R3 catalog (S half), on ADR 1164. The owner pass places an operation past an await from the producer's `calls_after_await` (statement awaits only), climbed layers (ADR 0493) and ADR 1164's try head. It never read ADR 1038's `for await` body: `createMemo(async () => { for await (const _x of [1]) { createEffect(…); } })` kept both an owned and an unowned context (`owner-varies-by-caller`) where Chrome reports NO_OWNER_EFFECT.

**Decision.** `owner_emission.rs` also counts as after-await an operation (effect, cleanup, context read, boundary call) or an `onSettled` call that `body_roles::in_for_await_body_that_runs` places. That predicate is the ADR 1164 condition: written in the body of a `for await` in its own async non-generator function, the iterable an array literal led by a number, boolean or `null` literal, and the array iterator intact. The function must not probe `getOwner()`, as `call_owner_edge` requires.

**Not changed.**
- An empty literal (a dead site, ADR 1018), a named iterable, a `finally` around the loop, and a `getOwner()` guard (`flw-guard-for-await`) stay uncertifiable.
- The counted loop with an `i > 0` guard (G4's M half) is not built.
- SC6002's `effect-creation-unaccounted` row at a creation stays beside the new SC4001 violation.

**Evidence.**
- Fixture `store-link-alias-get`: two alias Gets go from no row to uncertifiable; the member twin stays an SC1001 violation. Chrome covers them.
- Coverage: SC9012 rises only, in 11 existing fixtures (named in rises.json; no finding removed).
- Probe (release, 1,998 programs: mx-recall `nested-held`/`sw-let`/`nested-assign`/`nested-push`, lg-recall `store-*`): no outcome worse. The U to clean rows are ADR 1162's, counted against R3's older base.
- Rediscovery: an `outside` row (no read variant holds a link; generator work deferred).

**Part 2 — the exact alias is the store's link** (R3 G15: `(() => { const held = s1.a; held.v = 7; })()`, SC2003 `unproven-container-root`).
An exact alias is an immutable identifier binding of one name whose whole initializer is a static, non-optional chain from the store's own binding, or from another such alias (`link_alias_literal`). Where ADR 0491's proof holds for the store and its literal holds an object literal at those keys, the alias holds that link's proxy, and:
- ADR 0491's use check accepts the alias's initializer when every use of the alias is itself a contained use of that object (`link_alias_contained`);
- `container_root::handed_root` resolves a write through the alias to the store, its root `below` the store's (`HandedRoot::Store { below }`), so the write counts as past the root until `handed_links_wrappable` proves it from the alias's object;
- `local_access` places a Get through the alias (`held.v`) as the store's Get `s1.a.v`, a synthetic member read at the alias's member (`exact_link_alias_chain`; the literal proof moved to `store_literal_proof`, which `local_access` can ask).

A prop's alias (`const held = props.s1; held.a`) stays SC9012: its direct twin `props.s1.a` is itself SC1001 uncertifiable (`read-backing-unproven`).
*Measured* (release, against part 1; Chrome cached; 999 mx-recall `nested-held`/`sw-let`/`nested-assign`/`nested-push`, 999 lg-recall `store-*`): mx-recall U to V 51; lg-recall unchanged; nothing needs a look. Fixture `store-link-alias-write`: 4 violations (an IIFE, a timer, a deeper link and its Get, a read), 4 uncertifiable (a referenced setter, the alias handed on, a `let` alias, an array link). Chrome covers every site. Coverage: `store-link-alias-get`'s two alias Gets go from uncertifiable to violation; `flush-write-path` `Alias` (`const q = s.a; q.v = 7` in `flush`) goes from SC2003 uncertifiable to violation (Chrome-confirmed on a scratch copy); `after-await-read-first-writes` and `store-sub-value-flow` relabel `unproven-container-root` to `store-write-unproven` / `store-operation-may-not-write`, U to U (`scripts/guard/count.mjs` now takes a list for `relabeledTo`, as ADR 1133's `movedToFixture`).
- Fixture `owner-after-await-for-await`:
  - `EffectInBody`, `CleanupInBody` and `SettledInBody` move from SC4001 U to V;
  - `HelperInBody` and `CleanupInFinally` (ADR 1164) stay V;
  - the four counterexamples stay U.
- Chrome: `runtime-oracle/owner-after-await-for-await`.
- `for-await-body` `CleanupInBody` moves from U to V. It was uncertifiable only because an exported component's callers are not enumerated; past the suspension, no caller gives an owner.
- Chrome (`runtime-oracle/owner-after-await-for-await`): NO_OWNER_EFFECT and NO_OWNER_CLEANUP at the violations (`covered-violation`), and NO_OWNER_CLEANUP at the uncertifiable sites that run. SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED is raised unattributed (no application frame), so `SettledInBody` reads static-only there; the one-site fuzz programs judge it agree.
- Probe, release, VM, ADR 1164's build against this branch, the same 2,160 programs: 22 misuse recall-gap to agree (NO_OWNER_EFFECT 9, NO_OWNER_CLEANUP 9, NO_OWNER_BOUNDARY 2, SETTLED_CLEANUP_UNOWNED 2, all in `memo-`/`effect-async-for-await`). Nothing else moved, and nothing needs a look. Against main b600297eb: 210 moves, ADR 1164's 188 and these 22.

## ADR 1178 — A store handed whole to a reviewed reader is followed through what it answers
**The gap** (R3 catalog G6, research R5; main b06a4e71a). The per-callee read rows of a whole store exist (ADRs 0620, 0621, 0635: `Object.values(s)` in a body is a proven SC1001), but the value-use census cleared only `Object.keys`/`getOwnPropertyNames` (ADR 0810): every other store argument, spread, iteration and template substitution stood as SC9012 `value-in-carrier`, so a legal program with such a read was uncertifiable. rc.21 warns only from the store's `get` trap with a string key; `has`, `ownKeys` and `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` never do, and `snapshot` reads `$TARGET` and walks the raw backing.
**Decision** (`value_use.rs` `whole_store_argument`, `whole_store_form`; proof id `value_use.whole_store_argument`, ablated by `SOLID_CHECKER_IR_ABLATE_SILENCE`). A store root (not props, not a root a helper received) ends its walk at the reader with no row, and the walk goes on through what the reader answers:
- step 1: `Object.values(s)`, `Object.entries(s)`, one-argument `Array.from(s)` where ADR 0621's row stands exactly at the call; `deep(s)` (`Dialect::whole_store_argument` `ReadsEveryKey`) where ADR 0620's row stands; `Object.hasOwn(s, k)` on a store settled from its creation (`Dialect::creates_settled_store_from_value`: an exact `createStore` of an array or closed object literal held by a `const` tuple's first slot, a proxy by ADR 0634, not pending) or where ADR 0635's key-probe row stands; `snapshot(s)` (`ReadsRawBacking`) on a settled store only (and ADR 1150's `$TARGET` premise).
- step 2: `[...s]`, `{ ...s }` (no `this` in the literal), `for (const x of s)` with identifier bindings (no pattern, no `for await`), and a template substitution, each where ADR 0621's row stands at the spread or operand.
- The results: an array (`values`, `entries`, `from`, `[...s]`) or object (`{ ...s }`) holds the store's values as `[s]` holds a root (`RootHolder`), so an element Get (`Object.values(s)[0].v`) keeps a row; a `for…of` binding is walked as a root; `deep`'s and `snapshot`'s copies are walked as the root itself; `hasOwn` and a template answer a primitive.
- Premises: a standard callee is the exact default-library declaration, not withheld (ADRs 0840, 0876, 1137) and not replaced (ADR 1129's `standard_member_replaced`); an iteration also asks it of `Array.@@symbol`, `Object.@@symbol`, `ArrayIterator.next`/`return`, a template of `toString`, `valueOf`, `join` and `@@symbol`. `deep` and `snapshot` rest on the dialect's reviewed runtime code (rc.21 `dist/dev.js:6983-7068`), as every primitive does.
**Not built.** Step 3, a callback on the result (`[s].map((x) => x.v)`, ADR 1109's row): the callback's parameter read has no SC1001 row, so clearing it would make false cleans (R5: 216). A result read further, returned from a primitive's callback (`createMemo(() => deep(s))`) or handed on keeps its row (now at the use); so do a props root, a helper's parameter, a call spread, a derive, an optimistic store or projection under `snapshot`/`hasOwn`, and a store whose value is not a literal.
**Measured** (release, b06a4e71a against this, in the sc VM; Chrome cached). A pool of 3,996 `store-*` whole-store programs (mx-recall and lg-recall, 220 per grid and variant by a stable hash); the base's blocker scan put `value-in-carrier` in 2,884; a hash sample of 2,000 of those (888 mx-recall, 1,112 lg-recall) ran through `focus.mjs`. lg-recall: 613 uncertifiable to clean (has-own 101, snapshot 96, deep 58, template 53, array-from 50, array-spread 50, empty-spread 48, for-of 44, entries 43, empty-values 37, values 33), 479 stay uncertifiable (351 by SC1001's own role alone; SC9012 still in 105), 20 typed away, 0 violations. mx-recall: no move (139 agree, 749 recall-gap). R5's estimate was about 668 + 348 rows grid-wide; this is the measured sample only. Coverage: two new fixtures, and three moved: `store-standard-library-writes` (`({ ...store }).v = 7`, a write to a copy, loses its row: clean, as its README says), `store-element-flow` (three rows relabelled to `value-held-in-binding`/`value-root-in-helper` or moved to `.forEach`, all still U), `rc21-whole-store-reads` (rows moved from references to the uses of what the readers answer; `createMemo(() => deep(row))` is `value-from-primitive-callback`). Ownership gate 96 passed. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/store-whole-standard-census`, release build): STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at the three `BodyForms` reads, each a proven SC1001; silent at `TrackedForms` (clean) and every case that stays uncertifiable.
**Boundary.** No new role arm or named end: the silence is a census walk's `Followed`, logged as `silent` with the proof id. The two Dialect questions classify as `dialect-primitive-tables`. Its pair is the fixture (`TrackedForms` clean against `ResultUsed`, `NotTheForms`, `Unsettled` and the impostor twin) and the ablation, which puts all eleven `TrackedForms` rows back.

## ADR 1177 — A context read in a JSX handler with no run proven first makes no provider claim
**The problem.** Census false positive (`mx-context-not-found-dny-flush-{load,popover,unmount}`, open-defects, Mac 23): a `useContext` of a default-less context in an `onLoad`, `onBeforeToggle` or `onBlur` handler reached by a later flush got SC4002 (ContextNotFoundError) while Chrome throws NO_OWNER_CONTEXT: `useContext` checks the owner first. SC4001 was uncertifiable (`owner-varies-by-caller`), and ADR 0577 reported SC4002 because an owned run "throws first", which holds for a body call beside a handler (the body runs before the handler exists), not for a handler literal whose every run is a delivery that is owned on one stack and unowned on another.
**Decision.** `competing_checks`: a reported context-read requirement whose owner varies by caller or may be null, at a read written in a JSX handler (`in_jsx_handler`), makes the provider claim at the same call uncertifiable, `owner-check-throws-first`. A read in a function the body calls keeps ADR 0577's violation.
**Evidence.** Fixture `context-read-owner-varies`: `Varies` (an `onLoad` under a `Show` a timer opens) SC4002 violation to uncertifiable; `Body` and `BodyAndHandler` (ADR 0577) stay violations. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/context-read-owner-varies`): NO_OWNER_CONTEXT at `Varies` (covered by SC4001's row), CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND at the other two (covered violations). Fuzz, release builds of 14469fac2 and this branch, CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND and NO_OWNER_CONTEXT over mx-base, mx-combo, lg-base, lg-combo and mx-census (6,440 programs): the three false positives become not-fired (open-defects emptied of them, ratchet `falsePositive` 3 to 0); 34 census programs move agree to recall-gap (open-work: the order proof); nothing else, findings identical elsewhere. A first cut without the handler test also took 8 body-call and flow programs ADR 0577 proves. Coverage: only the new fixture.

## ADR 1179 — ADR 0200's forwarding takes only a wrapper the call runs exactly
**The defect** (found in ADR 1155 r3; on main a63e1302e). `callee_roles::forwarded_compute_slot` named its wrapper through `function_for_symbol` / `function_called_at`, which answer the first function a name was bound to: the initializer of a `let` written later, or the literal handed to a factory whose result the name holds. A literal handed to such a name took the role of the slot the first function forwards to, whatever the function the call runs does with it. Where that function never calls the literal, the claim is a false positive: fixture `forwarded-wrapper-exact` `DropApp`, `FactoryDropApp`, `MemberDropApp` (SC5001 on main, Chrome silent); generator contexts `barm-fwdwrap-let` and `barm-fwdwrap-factory` (SC2001 at a write that never runs, 6 legal cells).
**Decision.** The wrapper is resolved as ADR 0278 resolves a call (`project_callee_at_parameter`) and must be exact: a function declaration, a `const` (or a `let` nothing writes, ADR 0516) bound to the function itself, or a member the census resolves (ADR 0279/0299), with no spread before the literal. Anything else forwards nothing. The member census (`object_members::memo::literal_function`) now also follows a data slot whose value is an identifier naming a function declaration nothing writes (`{ hand: handDecl }`), as it follows the shorthand (`{ hand }`).
**Fail-closed losses (V to uncertifiable, each Chrome-reported; accepted: a violation right by coincidence is no proof).** `loading-member-callee` `WrapLet` and `ViaWrap` (SC5003, ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY); `forwarded-wrapper-exact` `SwapApp`, `FactoryApp`, `MemberSwapApp` (SC5001, PENDING_ASYNC_UNTRACKED_READ) and `PassApp` (SC5001, PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE). Follow-up (docs/open-work.md): a proof that every value the binding can hold is an exact function that calls the literal.
*Evidence* (release, Chrome cache). The forwarding contexts (`barm-fwdleaf-{tracked,memo,args}`, `barm-fwdwrap-{let,factory}`; lg-recall 9, mx-recall 6, mx-census 210): main a63e1302e 6 unexecuted violations, this build 6 uncertifiable, every other program the same. All of lg-recall (97,176 programs, legal): those 6 move and nothing else. Fixtures: `forwarded-wrapper-exact` (Chrome `runtime-oracle/forwarded-wrapper-exact`), `loading-member-callee` (`WrapLet`, `ViaWrap`); no other fixture moves, the data-slot route included. Not covered: a data slot naming a `const` arrow (`DataArrowApp`, uncertifiable, Chrome reports).

## ADR 1180 — A call that omits an argument runs that parameter's default in the leaf walk
**The problem.** A creation, `onCleanup` or `flush` written as a parameter default stayed possible-only. ADR 0454 demotes an operation in a parameter list, and ADR 0961 adds the `parameter-initializer-unplaced` net. So `const h = (p = flush()) => p` called as `h()` in a tracked effect's callback kept SC3001 uncertifiable, though every such call throws (G9 of the r4 catalog, 650 rows).
**Decision.** When the leaf walk enters a helper by a direct call with no spread argument (`helper_forbidden_operations_walk`), it hands `function_forbidden_operations` the argument count. A call in the parameter list is walked as a call in the body when it is exactly the (peeled) default of a parameter at that index or past it, in a non-generator function. It is guaranteed with the entry unless an earlier parameter's default holds a call, since a throw there stops the list. A primitive is recorded as a body call's would be, and a helper is walked. The default's span is then exempt from ADR 0454's final demotion (`proven_defaults`). A passed argument proves nothing, since it may be `undefined` at run time. A spread, a default nested in a destructuring pattern, one under a condition and a method's default all keep their rows.
**Evidence.** Fixture `param-default-leaf`: SC3001 violations at the calls for the value, helper and namespace flush, the creation and the cleanup (main: uncertifiable). Passed, spread, `undefined`, earlier-calling and method cases stay uncertifiable, and the shadowed flush is clean. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/param-default-leaf`): the creation and the cleanup are covered-violation, with stacks running from the default to the call. Each flush throws at its default, and a thrown error reaches the feedback report with no frames, so the oracle ledgers the three flush calls as `attribution`. The earlier-calling default fires as well (`first()` returned); it is uncertifiable here. Fuzz, release against main a63e1302e, the 7 leaf and PD codes over every PD context: mx-recall 7,872 programs, 450 recall-gap to agree (CLEANUP/PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE and FLUSH_IN_TRACKED_QUEUE_CALLBACK × the value, IIFE and helper forms × 3 layers), with 0 V to U and 0 clean to U. The 45 flush programs whose site row left now agree through the call's violation (`remote`). lg-recall 924 programs: unchanged, and no legal row gains a V. Coverage: only the new fixture moves.
**Not built.** A definedness proof for a passed argument (the legal `pd-passed-*` twins stay uncertifiable); the closure, destructured and constructor forms; an object literal's method; SC2006/SC2008/SC6002's `parameter-initializer-unplaced` net (ADR 0961), which still reads no call.

## ADR 1175 — An optimistic setter in an effect apply's first run, before the first answer, is a violation
**The gap** (R4 group N4, blocker `optimistic-reach-unresolved`; main a63e1302e). ADR 0636 proves SC2009 only on the creating stack, so `const [, setO] = createOptimistic(async () => 1); createEffect(() => 1, () => { setO(2); })` stayed uncertifiable while rc.21 throws OPTIMISTIC_WRITE_BEFORE_LOAD there: the apply's first run comes in `render`'s synchronous tail flush (`@solidjs/web` `dist/web.dev.js:540-551`), and the async compute answers a microtask later at the earliest. The setters guard first (`devGuardOptimisticBeforeLoad`, `dist/dev.js:3257`, `:8695-8699`).
**Decision** (`local_access.rs` `written_in_pending_apply`, proof id `local_access.optimistic_pending_apply`; `execution_role/write_roles.rs` `pending_apply_first_write`). ADR 0504's apply proof is split into its apply half (`pending_apply_first_run`, unchanged for reads) and its source half. The setter call is proven when:
- the apply half holds: the call on every completion of the first run of a `createEffect`/`createRenderEffect` apply, after no other call of it, the effect with no options and a compute that is one primitive literal, created on every completion of a component a module-scope `render` mounts (`first_run_proven_at_call`). For the setter only, a function literal handed to it (an updater) is not code run before it, since the guard throws first;
- the source is ADR 0505's own-body arm with the optimistic creation in place of the memo: a `const` array pattern of the same body naming the setter, whose whole initializer is the dialect's optimistic creation (`Dialect::optimistic_unanswered_arguments`: `createOptimistic` with one argument, `createOptimisticStore` with at most two; no `loadingValue`) of an async function literal, on every completion before the effect with nothing run between;
- a `createEffect` also needs ADR 0505's mount flush (a static intrinsic tree, a body that runs nothing else, the source's own tuple admitted under ADR 0510's plain-pattern premise, `plain_tuple_pattern`, and `render_runs_first`). The compute may be one primitive literal or, new here, a closed object literal of primitive literals (`compute_is_primitive_object`: a store's `async () => ({ v: 1 })`), which runs no code either. A `createRenderEffect` runs its apply at creation.
**Measured** (release, VM, Chrome cached; main a63e1302e against this). The blocker scan of the SC2009 code (mx-recall, lg-recall, mx-census; 6,934 programs) put `optimistic-reach-unresolved` in 5,645; 74 have the setter written in an effect apply (all mx-census). Probe: those 74 plus a hash sample of the rest, 2,000 programs (843 mx-census, 825 mx-recall, 332 lg-recall). mx-census: recall-gap to agree 6 (`effect-apply`, `render-apply`, `rnd-shadow`, signal and store each), recall-gap stays 336, agree 55, not-fired 437, typed away 9 unchanged; mx-recall (408 agree, 409 recall-gap) and lg-recall (17 clean, 312 uncertifiable) do not move: 0 legal violations, 0 V to U, 0 clean to U. Of the 74, Chrome throws in 32 and is silent in 40 (guarded, deferred, cleanup, timer and microtask hand-offs, an error arm). The coordinator's R4 count (152 misuse, 16 legal) is from its catalog; this measures only the sample above. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/optimistic-apply-before-load`) throws in `Apply`, `RenderStore`, `Namespace` and `StoreEffect` and is silent in `Guarded`, `Declared` and `Reads`; the case renders each export as its own root, so the checker stays uncertifiable there and the fixtures hold the proofs.
**Not covered.** The other 26 throwing apply programs fail one of ADR 0505's premises: a `flush()` or a nested `render()` in the body, a compute that reads a signal, a tree with a handler or component, an effect created in a loop or a handler. So do a namespace import of the primitives (the body premise reads no member: `optimistic-apply-before-load-namespace`), a source from a hook, a prop or another module, and a setter a `let` holds. Fixtures `optimistic-apply-before-load` (+ `-render`, `-store`, `-namespace`, `-guarded`, `-declared`, `-reads`). Boundary: the change adds violations only, no silent-capable arm. Proof gate: the render-effect fixture's setter call is a C2 candidate (`candidates.json`, the write table's `first-run-reporting` decision with no write row), the masked-site shape `optimistic-write-site-code` already lists: SC2001 `write-unaccounted` stands beside the violation.

## ADR 1184 — A prop read in an IIFE inside a named local function is unplaced, not placed elsewhere
**The defect (pre-existing on main a63e1302e and 01d5fdc5f, found by ADR 1180's `make fuzz-smoke`).** In `const dir1 = () => { (() => { (props as typeof props).r1; })(); return () => {}; }` with `<p ref={dir1()} />`, the prop read runs untracked in the render, and Chrome warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED. The program was certified clean (census `mx-strict-read-untracked-ref-factory-body-signal-direct-iife-s-prop-value-cast`). `discover_member` gave the read the right role (UntrackedRendering) but ended it `placed-elsewhere` (premise `CallEdgePlaces` at `dir1()`), trusting ADR 0936's fallback to the named function's call edges. No summary carries a prop read in an IIFE to those calls, so no row stood anywhere. The same holds for a body call `go()`, a function-expression IIFE and a plain attribute call. ADR 1103 had closed the sibling where the literal is handed to a project helper.
**Decision.** `handed_anonymous_literal` also answers for an anonymous, unbound literal that is the callee of a non-`new` call where it is written (`calls_with_peeled_callee`). As with ADR 1103, this applies to a component prop's read only, since an accessor's or a store's read of such a literal is carried to the call (a violation there). The read is now SC1001 uncertifiable. Proving the violation at the named function's calls would need the summaries to carry a prop read of the IIFE; that is not built.
**Evidence.** Fixture `iife-prop-read`: `Arrow`, `RefFactory` and `Expression` go from no row to SC1001 uncertifiable at the read. `Direct` and `BodyIife` stay violations at the read or the call, `AccessorIife` stays a violation at `go()`, and `Untracked` and `PlainObject` stay clean. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/iife-prop-read`): STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at each read; the IIFE reads are covered-uncertifiable (main: unproven-clean), the controls covered-violation, and the clean controls quiet. Rediscovery: `matrix.mjs --recall --ids` gives false-clean on main 01d5fdc5f and recall-gap here. Fuzz, release against main 01d5fdc5f, every STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED program with an IIFE in its id on six grids (94,055 programs): mx-recall's 2 false cleans of this shape become recall-gap; 0 V lost, 0 legal V gained; 24 legal programs go from clean to uncertifiable (lg-recall 22, lg-src 2: `jsx-helper`, `async`/`handler-async`, `proto-*`, all `-iife-s-prop-value`). Their cleans rested on the same `CallEdgePlaces` premise, which is false for an IIFE's prop read. The call happened to be tracked or past an `await`, so the clean held by luck, not by proof (invariant 2).
**Not built.** Summaries that carry a component prop's read in an IIFE to the named function's calls, as ADR 0522 carries an accessor's or a store's (`in_place_layer_owners`). That would win back the 24 cleans and prove the census shape a violation at `dir1()`.

## ADR 1186 — A call that runs what a carrier held keeps a row of its own
**The defect (pre-existing on main a63e1302e and 01d5fdc5f, found by ADR 1180's `make fuzz-smoke`).** In `const fns = [setW1]; const loop = (...xs) => { for (const f of fns) return (f as any)(...xs); }`, the SC9012 `value-in-carrier` row stood only at the carrier `fns`. Chrome's frame for the write (REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE, ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE) is at the call through `f`. The escaped walk reached that call, but the call's role (EventCallback, from a handler that also calls the function) cleared it: a handler may write, and the role ignores a `runWithOwner` around the call or a memo's compute that also runs it. The program stayed uncertifiable, but the fuzz judge saw a false clean: no row at the frame. This affected 3 census programs (`memo-shared-signal-loop-callee-module-helper`, `pos-handler-owner-signal-loop-callee-closure`, `pos-handler-owner-x-loop-callee-none`).
**Decision.** `escaped_through`'s callee arm: a call reached past a `value-in-carrier` escape, whose role cleared it, keeps a row at the call (`call_use_span`, the frame's position). The row goes into `late_rows`, apart from the uses, so the carrier's own row still stands. This only adds rows, and only in a program the carrier's row already makes uncertifiable. A violation is never moved and no silence is new.
**Evidence.** Fixture `carrier-call-row` (the census text): a new row at the call, the carrier's row kept, the control clean. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/carrier-call-row`): covered-uncertifiable. The 23 programs of the smoke's list, against main 01d5fdc5f: the 3 loop programs go from false-clean to recall-gap, nothing else changes. Every recall program whose callee runs through a carrier (`-loop-callee`, `-values-callee`, `-entries-callee`; 18,492 programs): mx-recall 78 false-clean to recall-gap, lg-recall unchanged, 0 V lost, 0 legal V gained, 0 clean to uncertifiable. Rediscovery entries name the 3 smoke programs. Coverage: `value-use-calls-carriers` gains a row at a call; `context-provided-store-tuple` relabels one row (`value-to-unresolved-callee` to `value-in-carrier`, same span); `loading-entries` has SC9012 rows at 6 calls, 5 of them where SC3001/SC6002's unaccounted rows stood (the leaf census reads a withholding row at the call as accounting for the site, which stays uncertifiable).
**Not built.** Two of the five programs stay false cleans by the judge, each still uncertifiable as a program. `mx-reactive-write-in-owned-scope-untrack-store-values-callee-none` (`Object.values(box)[0](…)`): the escaped walk from `box` does not reach the keyed call through the standard enumeration's result. `mx-caught-reactive-read-handed-flush-each-async-loop-callee-closure-helper`: Chrome records no app frame (the diagnostic is at the JSX child), so the judge looks at the site's line, the `loop()` call, which no row reaches. A fix there is a row at the call of the function that holds the dispatch.

## ADR 1182 — The one function a wrapper's name holds at a call, where it is not the one first written
**The gap** (ADR 1179's fail-closed losses). ADR 1179 took only a wrapper the call runs exactly, so a written `let`, a factory's result and a replaced member forwarded nothing: `loading-member-callee` `WrapLet`, `ViaWrap` (SC5003) and `forwarded-wrapper-exact` `SwapApp`, `FactoryApp`, `MemberSwapApp`, `PassApp`, `SwapInApp` (SC5001) were uncertifiable where Chrome reports them; `DataArrowApp` (a slot naming a `const` arrow) too.
**Decision.** `callback_standing::declared_in` (ADR 0278's resolution, so every exact consumer) first asks `settled_callee`: the one function the callee names at the call.
- A written `let`: every write a module-level straight-line plain `name = <function literal>` (new fact `straight_line_assignments`, AST schema 109), and the mention runs after the last write: the temporal-dead-zone proof (`initialization::initialized_before`) with a declarator standing at that write (`Scratch::stand_in`; the initializer's own function is no exception there). The rows ride on `UninitializedReferences` (`settled_let_function`, also a `CalleeWorld` question for the flow memos).
- A replaced member: a module-level `const` bound to a closed literal, every reference in its file a member call or a module-level straight-line `receiver.name = <function literal>`, no function of it reading `this`, `arguments` or `super`, not exported; the call follows the name's last write (the same proof). `callee_in` asks it before the census withholds the call.
- A `const` bound to `f(…)`: `f` exact, synchronous, running no call, member read or `throw` of its own before one straight-line `return` of a function literal written in it (`factory_result`) or of its own unwritten parameter whose argument is a function literal; chains of four at most.
- The member census (`object_members::memo::literal_function`) follows a data slot naming a module-level `const` (or unwritten `let`) arrow declared before the literal, both at module level.
- `forwarded_compute_slot` refuses a callee mention that may precede its binding's initialization.
*Evidence.* Fixtures: `forwarded-wrapper-exact` (Chrome: every target a violation it reports, PENDING_ASYNC_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE or PENDING_ASYNC_UNTRACKED_READ; `DropApp`, `FactoryDropApp`, `MemberDropApp`, `DataSwapApp`, `DataReplacedApp` uncertifiable, Chrome silent), `forwarded-wrapper-values` (the refused shapes uncertifiable; `LateApp`, whose call follows the last write, a violation Chrome reports), `loading-member-callee` (`WrapLet`, `ViaWrap` SC5003 violations again, ASYNC_OUTSIDE_LOADING_BOUNDARY), `effect-phase-windows` (`ShadowedReaction`: `createReactionLike`'s sole return calls its argument at once, an SC1001 violation, Chrome STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED at the read); no other fixture moves. Probe (release; main 0751069bf against this): the forwarding contexts (`barm-fwdleaf-*`, `barm-fwdwrap-*`; 225 programs) the same on both; lg-recall, a 0.004 stratified sample (97,176 legal programs, concurrency 2), the same outcome on every program. Both builds show 26 SC1001 false positives on `lg-strict-read-untracked-handed-flush-store-*` cells there (main's, not this change's). Not covered: a write of a name (`w = bare`), a function-local `let` or receiver, a factory that runs code first.

## ADR 1188 — The global `undefined` as an argument runs that parameter's default in the leaf walk
**The problem.** ADR 1180 runs a parameter's default only for a call that omits the argument. `h(undefined)` for `const h = (p = flush()) => p` runs the default too (a default runs for an argument that is `undefined`), yet it stayed uncertifiable.
**Decision** (`cleanup.rs`, `passed_arguments`). The direct call the walk enters a helper by hands over, per argument, whether it is the unshadowed global `undefined` (`ArgumentValueKind::Undefined`, set by the facts only for the global binding). Such an index counts as omitted for ADR 1180's rule; every other premise is unchanged. A variable holding `undefined`, a shadowed `undefined`, `void 0` and any other value keep the row: a value's definedness is not proven.
**Evidence.** Fixture `param-default-leaf`: `UndefinedArgument` (`valued(undefined)`) moves from uncertifiable to an SC3001 violation; the twin `UndefinedThroughVariable` (`const none = undefined; valued(none)`) stays uncertifiable. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/param-default-leaf`): the flush throws at its default with no frames, ledgered as `attribution`. Fuzz, release, main ff7f6cf0c against this, every PD program: mx-recall 890 and lg-recall 770, 0 programs change at code level. No grid row passes a literal `undefined`: the `pd-*-undef` and `-cond` variants pass `Math.random() > 2 ? 1 : undefined`, which no syntax proves undefined (about 700 of the remaining rows). Coverage: only this fixture moves. Boundary: violations only, no silent-capable arm.
**Not built.** A value proof for a non-literal argument (the grid's undef and cond rows); `void 0`; ADR 1180's closure, destructured and constructor forms.

## ADR 1187 — A prop read in an IIFE is the named helper's read at the IIFE's call
**The problem.** ADR 1184 made a component prop read in an IIFE inside a named local helper uncertifiable. Nothing charged such a read to the helper's calls: the helper pass (ADR 0933, `project_helper_prop_read`) took the read's innermost function, the anonymous IIFE, as its helper and found no name. Legal programs whose helper call is tracked (`<p>{rh1()}</p>`) or past an `await` lost their cleans, and `const go = () => { (() => props.v)(); }; go();` in a body was uncertifiable where Chrome warns at `go()`.
**Decision.** `component_prop_helper` climbs from the read through each IIFE around it to the named helper. A layer is an anonymous, unbound literal, neither async nor a generator, called where it is written (not `new`), with that call written directly in the enclosing function's body. The helper pass then answers as for a read written at the outermost IIFE call: `body_site_runs_during_call` is asked of that call, and each of the helper's calls carries the read with its own role. The read's site and ends stay its own.
**Evidence.** Fixture `iife-prop-read`: `Arrow` and `Expression` are SC1001 violations at `go()`; `RefFactory` stays uncertifiable, as main leaves the same read written without the IIFE (`ref={dir()}` is no call the helper pass places); the controls are unchanged. Fuzz, release, every STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED `-iife-s-prop-value` cell (960 programs on four grids; mx-pairs and lg-pairs hold none), against main 01d5fdc5f and against ADR 1184: 8 of 1184's 24 legal programs are clean again (`jsx-helper`, `async`, `handler-async`). The other 16 (`proto-*`, `async-loop`, `async-finally`, `handler-async-loop`, `handler-async-finally`) stay uncertifiable: each one's twin with the read written in the helper itself (`-direct-none-s-prop-value-cast`, 20 programs run) is uncertifiable too, so their cleans came only from the false premise. The census ref-factory programs stay recall-gap. 0 V lost, 0 legal V gained.
**Not built.** A violation for the ref factory: `ref={dir()}`'s call is not placed by the helper pass, with or without an IIFE.

## ADR 1189 — A reporting run counts only where the declaring function's role is its own
**The defect** (bundle t, main 0751069bf and ff7f6cf0c; found by the ADR 1182 probe). 26 legal `lg-strict-read-untracked-handed-flush-store-*` cells were SC1001 violations where Chrome is silent: `Row` runs `flush(() => wrapUse())` and is called by `[1].map(Row)` inside a JSX expression (tracked); `wrapUse` declares `const f = () => { void s1.v; }` and runs it (`[f].forEach((g) => g())`). Bisect: 960bfa1f9 and 01d5fdc5f uncertifiable, 0751069bf violation; inside bundle t, the merge of ADR 1166 (`ddc55b05e`; 742ca3d75, with 1181, uncertifiable); 1166's own tip alone reproduces it. ADR 1166's reporting run gave the read the role `read_execution_role` gives code at the run (`UntrackedRendering`, which `wrapUse` takes from its call in `Row`). A read written at the run is reported at that call, inside `Row`, which the backend downgrades (`component-identity-unproven`: `Row` is handed to code that may call it as a plain function); the reporting run reports at the read itself, where no downgrade reaches.
**Decision.** `named_callbacks::reporting_run_role` requires `declarer_role_is_its_own`: the declaring function is an unbound literal that is the whole argument of a dialect primitive's call, or every reference of its name is the name, an export statement of it, or a direct call written outside every undecided component region (`site_in_undecided_component`) in a function that qualifies in turn (an immediately invoked literal: its call); four functions deep at most. Anything else keeps the read unplaced.
**Evidence.** The whole family (`focus.mjs --codes STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED --grids lg-recall -- --contexts handed-flush`, 2,824 legal programs, Chrome judge, release): main ff7f6cf0c 102 false positives (the 26 among them), this build 0; the 102 move to uncertifiable and nothing else moves (rediscovery.json). Fixture `reporting-run-called-helper` (Chrome `runtime-oracle/reporting-run-called-helper`): `MappedRow` (the reduced census program) and `RowDeclared` uncertifiable, Chrome silent; `BodyCalledHelper`, `DeclaredHelper`, `InvokedHelper`, `BodyDeclared` violations, Chrome STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED. A first cut that refused every called helper lost those three and two Chrome-confirmed violations in `construct-only-class` (`ClosureInMethod`, a method entered by `new K().m()`) and `destructure-store-slots` (`HandedAndCalled`, rendered by a JSX tag); the predicate follows calls, member calls and JSX tags, and coverage moves nothing. `named-callback-reporting-run` keeps its 8 violations.

## ADR 1185 — An owner call in a counted loop's later pass is past the await
G4 of the R3 catalog (M half), on ADR 1165. `createMemo(async () => { for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { if (i > 0) { createEffect(…); } await Promise.resolve(); } })` kept SC4001 `owner-varies-by-caller`: the owner pass saw the loop's owned first pass and its later ones. Chrome reports NO_OWNER_EFFECT on the second pass.
**Decision** (`body_roles.rs` `in_counted_loop_later_pass`, asked where `owner_emission.rs` asks ADR 1165's `for await` body).
- The site is in the consequent of `if (i > 0)` in the body of a `for` whose head reads token by token as `for (let i = 0; i < N; i += 1)`. `<=` and `i++` or `++i` are accepted, and `N` is a decimal literal that lets a second pass run.
- The test's `i` resolves to the head's `let` binding, and the update's reference is its only write; there is no direct `eval` in the function.
- The body is a block with an `await` at its own statement level (`dominating_awaits`, its region ending with the loop) and no `break` or `continue` (`jump_statements`).
- So `i > 0` holds only on passes after one whose body completed past that await (a throw or `return` leaves the loop). Every run of the site is a continuation of its own async non-generator function, with no owner.
- The operation may be written directly or at the outermost call of in-place layers (ADR 0493's climb premises), and the function must not probe `getOwner()`.

**Evidence.**
- Fixture `owner-after-await-counted-loop`: violations at `EffectLaterPass`, `CleanupLaterPass` (`<=`, `i++`), `HelperLaterPass` (an async helper the component calls, `++i`) and `IifeLaterPass`. Uncertifiable as before: no guard, a `continue`, a conditional await, a counter the body writes, a guard on a shadowing binding, a single pass (dead site) and a `getOwner()` probe.
- Chrome (`runtime-oracle/owner-after-await-counted-loop`): covered, nothing static-only.
- Probe (release, VM, Chrome judge), main 176445e77 against this, on every `*-async-loop` program of the five owner codes (the whole family): mx-recall 12,636 programs, 5,727 recall-gap to agree, 4,811 still recall-gap, 2,098 agree unchanged, nothing needs a look. At code level, 5,793 programs change: +5,727 SC4001 violations, all at the site, and no violation lost. 66 programs relabel U to U (`component-identity-unproven` for the dynamic mounts, `owner-allocation-unproven` for `onSettled` forms). lg-recall: 30 programs, unchanged (no legal violation).
- Boundary: no role arm and no silent-capable path; it adds violations only.

**Not built.** In-place layers in an async function the component body or a handler calls (most of the 4,811), another counter or guard shape, a `while` loop, and SC6002's `effect-creation-unaccounted` row at the creation, which stays beside the violation.
<a id="adr-1191"></a>
## ADR 1191 — A read in a counted loop's later pass, or in layers run in place in a placed body, is past the await
G1 of the R3 catalog (misuse half), on ADRs 1164 and 1185. In an async memo's or effect's compute, `for (let i = 0; i < 2; i += 1) { if (i > 0) { r1(); } await p; }` and `for await (const _ of [1]) { (() => r1())(); }` kept SC1002 uncertifiable. Chrome warns UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT at both reads.
**Decision.**
- *Placement* (`after_await.rs` `after_implicit_suspension`): beside ADR 1164's `for await` bodies that run, a row stays unmarked when its site is placed:
  - written directly in a counted loop's later pass (`body_roles::in_counted_loop_later_pass`, ADR 1185's predicate), or
  - in function layers run in place (`climb_in_place_layers`) whose outermost call is placed so.
  - The climb premises are those of ADR 1185's owner climb: no bound, no parameter-list layer, no layer that also runs its callback elsewhere, nothing withheld or unmodelled, and no library or package callback crossed (`climb_crosses_library_callback`), so no primitive's slot (`untrack`) and no `forEach` either.
- *No dependency* (`pre_await.rs`): the window before the first suspension skips what is written inside a later pass's consequent (`in_counted_loop_later_pass_region`). The first pass skips it, every later pass follows the first pass's await, and a function written there does not exist earlier. A counter reference is a primitive (`counted_loop_counter`: a `let` set to `0` whose only write adds `1`), so `i < 2` and `i > 0` coerce nothing. Before this, both made the read `MayBeTracked`.
- The 1185 predicate is split (`counted_loop`, `later_pass_consequents`) and is unchanged for owners.

**Evidence.**
- Fixture `after-await-read-later-pass`: violations at `LaterPassRead`, `LaterPassIife`, `ForAwaitClosure` (a closure called once) and `ForAwaitHelper` (a project helper's callback, an effect compute). Uncertifiable as before: no guard (the first pass reads before any await), a `continue`, a shadowing guard binding, `forEach`, a stored closure. `untrack`'s callback has no SC1002 row, on main too. ADR 0973's accounting rows at the layer calls stand beside the violations.
- `after-await-for-await-finally` `ForAwaitClosure` (an IIFE in the body): uncertifiable to violation.
- Chrome (`runtime-oracle/after-await-read-later-pass`, `after-await-for-await-finally`): covered, nothing static-only.
- Probe (release, VM, Chrome judge), main 176445e77 against this, every UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT program of both recall grids:
  - mx-recall, 36,503 programs: 2,196 recall-gap to agree (memo and effect × the counted loop, about 1,240, every layer and source, and `for await`'s layers, about 950); nothing needs a look; not-fired (1,370) and typed-away unchanged.
  - At code level, exactly 2,196 programs change, each one SC1002 row from uncertifiable to violation.
  - lg-recall, 12,974 programs: none changes.
- Boundary: no role arm; it adds violations only.

**Not built.**
- The legal half of G1: a read after an await in an async function only a handler, a `ref` or the component body calls. This is ADR 0973 ruling 5: there is no "no flight" reason. The ruling question was sent with the step-0 report.
- A `finally`'s layered reads.
- Member reads in a later pass.
- Other loop shapes.
<a id="adr-1195"></a>
## ADR 1195 — A read or a write in layers run in place inside a returned effect cleanup is placed where the cleanup runs
G3 leftovers (R3 catalog; research R6), on ADRs 1037 and 1183. Scan of main 60a7cf1db: every cleanup context of both recall grids, 85,440 programs. The dominant blocker was `function-run-unplaced` in the `*-cleanup-rerun*` contexts:
- STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED (misuse): 2,956 programs plus 1,551 named;
- REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE (legal): 2,632 programs plus 1,556 named.

Both answers looked only at a site written in the cleanup's own body. A closure, an IIFE or a helper's callback inside the cleanup left the site unplaced.

**Decision** (`write_roles.rs` `returned_cleanup_placed_site`).
- The site placed is either the site itself or the outermost call of the function layers run in place around it, on ADR 0493's climb premises: no bound, no parameter-list layer, no layer that also runs its callback elsewhere, nothing withheld or unmodelled, no library or package callback crossed (`forEach`, a primitive's slot), and no await on the way.
- `returned_cleanup_write_role` (ADR 1037: a setter or `refresh` in the cleanup is legal on its every run) and `returned_cleanup_rerun_reached` (ADR 1183: a reached click reruns the effect with its owner alive, so the read runs in the apply's window) take their cleanup from that call.
- The read itself must still be a primitive accessor's call, so no helper call at the site is placed (1183 r2).

**Evidence.**
- Fixture `effect-cleanup-rerun-layers`:
  - SC1001 violations: `ReadInClosure`, `ReadInIife`, `ReadInHelperCallback`.
  - SC2001 clean: `WriteInClosure`, `WriteInIife`, `WriteInHelperCallback`.
  - Uncertifiable as before: a `forEach` callback, a stored closure, a read past an await in an async IIFE.
  - `WriteInSharedHelper` keeps main's rows: a helper the body also calls is no in-place layer.
- Chrome (`runtime-oracle/effect-cleanup-rerun-layers`): covered, nothing static-only.
- Probe (release, VM, Chrome judge), main 60a7cf1db against this, every cleanup-context program of every code:
  - mx-recall, 45,675 programs: 592 recall-gap to agree. At code level, 1,166 programs gain violations, every one replacing an uncertifiable row at the same site: 1,046 SC1001 and 120 with two SC1003 rows. No violation is lost.
  - lg-recall, 39,765 programs: 4,935 uncertifiable to clean (Chrome silent). At code level, 5,090 SC2001 rows go and no violation is added; 50 programs relabel an SC9012 row (U to U).
  - Nothing needs a look on either build but one mx false clean that main has too (`mx-action-called-in-owned-scope-effect-cleanup-for-x-values-callee-none`). That is pre-existing, unchanged, and not this change's.
- Boundary: the write arm `write_roles.returned-cleanup-write` keeps its stated gap. Legal cells now run clean through it, but no misuse cell writes in a rerun cleanup. The premise `kind-returned-cleanup-write-guard` names the new fixture.

**Not built.**
- A named apply (`effect-cleanup-rerun-named`).
- The disposal-only contexts (`effect-cleanup-dispose`, `-show`, `-for`, `wh-root-cleanup`, about 6.5k lg rows), which need an "only disposal reruns it" proof.
- The owner codes' `effect-owner-unproven` and `owner-callers-unenumerated`.
- A loop or a handed function inside the cleanup.
<a id="adr-1190"></a>
## ADR 1190 — A callback prop's literal is walked at the child's calls: the leaf walk and the unread-package question
**The problem.** ADR 1171 proved where a component prop's function literal runs (the child's calls of `props.<prop>`), but only the owner graph read that proof. The leaf walk did not resolve `props.run()` to the literal: an SC9012 `leaf-callback-opaque` or `closed-parameter-member-dispatch` row, and the literal's creations kept SC3001 `leaf-operation-unaccounted`. The unread-package question (B3, `package_hand_off`) read the literal's position, a JSX attribute value, as handed to the web runtime: `unread-package-may-run` declined every census row in it (SC3001/SC6002). R6 counted 2,757 simple G2 (`cbp-*`) rows still uncertifiable: 85% in forms 1171 does not recognize (named, forwarded, destructured, spread), the plain rest mostly the creation and leaf censuses.
**Decision (slice 1, the plain form).** `package_hand_off::function_value_in`: a literal whose `prop_literal_call_sites` list is not empty is run only at those calls, so a package may run it only where it may run one of them (`runs_where_written` of each call). An empty list (never called) keeps the old answer: the dead-site ruling. `cleanup.rs`: a call that is one of a literal's proven call sites (`prop_literal_called_at`) walks the literal as its callee (`Entry::Called`), as a named helper's call is.
**Evidence.** Fixture `callback-prop-leaf`: `Body` is clean (main: SC3001/SC6002 uncertifiable), `Settled` and `Tracked` are SC3001 violations at the child's call (main: uncertifiable), and `Never` and `Spread` keep their rows. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/callback-prop-leaf`): Settled is covered-violation, Spread covered-uncertifiable, and Body quiet. Tracked's flush throws without frames, so its violation is ledgered as `attribution` (ADR 1180's case). Fuzz, release against main 176445e77, the whole `cbp-*` family on mx-recall, lg-recall and mx-census (34,491 programs): mx-recall 75 `cbp-settled` recall-gap to agree (60 of them now agree through the call's violation, the literal's own row gone); lg-recall 900 uncertifiable to clean (`cbp-body` 420, `cbp-jsx` 420, `cbp-handler` 60). 0 legal V, 0 V to U, 0 clean to U; mx-census unchanged. Predicted (R6's simple slice, plain form, census class): up to 212 rows. The measure covers the whole family, not the simple slice. Coverage: 20 uncertifiable rows leave 8 fixtures of ADR 1171's shapes (`component-prop-call-owner`, `fp-owner-component-ref`, `owner-callback-prop`, `owner-call-jsx-prop-arrow`, `provider-children-memo-owner`, `stored-throw-wrapper-boundary`, `competing-check-sync-memo`, and `flush-universe-package-hand-off-flip`'s `ComponentPropsCalled`, which its README already names a silent twin); one SC9012 `leaf-callback-opaque` becomes SC3001 `leaf-owner-unproven`; no violation moves.
**Fix (before merge; Mac 24c's bundle y scan).** The first cut certified two programs Chrome throws in (`mx-primitive-in-effect-callback-er-prop-apply-jsx-fragment` and `-jsx-component`): a literal whose JSX creation runs in the child's effect apply. Once the B3 gate stopped declining, SC6002's role silence (`effect-creation-runs-off-apply`) answered from the literal's lexical role, and 1171's entry walk called the layer closed. `leaf_universe::prop_literal_calls_off_apply`: a component prop literal around the site whose proven calls are not each placed off every apply by the role engine (out through nested literals, depth 4) keeps the row. Fixture twins `ApplyFragment` and `ApplyComponent` (uncertifiable; Chrome PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK covered-uncertifiable) and rediscovery entries. Re-probe on `cbp-*` and `er-prop-*` (34,507 programs) against main: no false clean.
**Slice 3: the named and destructured forms.** `prop_literal_call_sites` takes, beside the literal written at the attribute, a function bound to a name whose one reference is the attribute's whole value (`run={run1}`: not exported, not written, not a named function expression), and, beside a kept `props`, a first parameter that destructures the prop (`({ run }) => …`: one plain slot of that static key, no default, no nested pattern, the name never written, every reference of it the callee of a call). The leaf walk's lookup (`prop_literal_called_at`) takes any such function. `layer_entry_open` asks 1171's call sites before a named function's reference hand-offs. A named function handed as a component's `ref` is not taken (the compiler wraps a `ref` value). ADR 0509's passed value (`props_reactivity`) is a function, not an unknown value, for such a name (`named_prop_function`), as the literal is, so the call's `closed-parameter-member-dispatch` row goes. Fixture `callback-prop-forms`: `NamedSettled` and `DestructuredSettled` are SC3001 violations at the call, and `NamedBody` and `DestructuredBody` are clean (main: uncertifiable). `NamedTwice` (the name also called elsewhere) and `DestructuredDefault` (a defaulted slot) keep their rows. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/callback-prop-forms`): covered-violation at each settled call and at NamedTwice's, covered-uncertifiable at the defaulted slot, nothing static-only. Fuzz, against slice 1 on the same family: mx-recall 720 recall-gap to agree, lg-recall 2,004 uncertifiable to clean; 0 legal V, 0 V to U, 0 clean to U; mx-census unchanged. Slices 1 and 3 against main: 795 agree and 2,904 clean. Predicted for slice 3: up to about 850 rows (R6's simple slice); the measure covers the whole family. Left in these forms: the read and write roles (`strict-read-untracked`, `no-write-in-pure-computation`, the async reads; slice 2) and some owner rows (`missing-owner` in `attached`/`view`).
**Slice 2: the read and write roles.** A site written in a callback prop's literal (inline, named or destructured; directly, or through layers that run in place, on a clean climb) runs where the child's calls run (`execution_role::prop_literal_run_calls`), when each call is placed by the role engine alone (`call_plainly_placed`: directly in the child component's body, or directly in an anonymous literal that is a primitive's callback or an intrinsic element's attribute value written directly there; a call in a named local function is placed by that function's own entries and hand-offs, which the role at the call does not check). The read role is the calls' one role (`execution_role.prop-literal-calls`; Unknown where they differ). The write role folds them: a call that rejects the write proves it rejected; otherwise their one role (`write_roles.prop-literal-calls`). `write_roles::caller_loop` walks the calls' callees as entries beside the graph's sites, with the named form's reference held. `handed_role` reads the calls as carrier positions. `callee_callback_timing` and `unplaced_run_but` ask each call. Fixture `callback-prop-roles`: `ApplyRead` and `NamedBodyRead` are SC1001 violations, `DestructuredBodyWrite` is an SC2001 violation, and `DestructuredHandlerWrite` and `JsxIifeRead` are clean (main: all uncertifiable). Chrome (`runtime-oracle/callback-prop-roles`): covered-violation at each, quiet at the two clean ones, nothing static-only. A first cut asked the climb in the timing check but not in the role, so a read in an IIFE the child runs in tracked JSX kept its lexical rendering role and became a false positive (96 mx-recall, 112 lg-recall programs in the probe). The climb in `prop_literal_run_calls` makes every hook ask the same site; `JsxIifeRead` pins it. Fuzz against slices 1 and 3 on the whole `cbp-*` and `er-prop-*` family (34,507 programs): mx-recall 792 recall-gap to agree, lg-recall 726 uncertifiable to clean, 0 false results, 0 legal V, 0 V to U, 0 clean to U; mx-census unchanged. Repro case `prop-in-effect-apply-read` (sc1001) keeps its row under a more exact cause: the literal's read now has the apply's role, and what leaves it uncertifiable is the exported, unrendered component's props (`direct-read-callers-unenumerable`), no longer the callback's consumer. Coverage: see the commit; `forwarded-event-prop`'s named-handler cases keep their rows (a first cut without `call_plainly_placed` moved them both ways: an aliased handler's read became clean, and three clean sites got rows).
**Slice 4: forwarded and spread props.** `element_prop_calls` follows the value an element passes on: in a component that receives it, `props.<prop>` used whole as a component element's attribute (`<Kid run={props.run} />`, not a `ref`) or `props` spread alone onto one component element with no attribute of that name (`<Kid {...props} />`, `props` used nowhere else) recurses into that element's component (depth 4), with the same proofs at each step (one element renders it, not exported, the prop called or forwarded on). `props_reactivity`'s passed value is a function for a forwarded `props.<prop>` a proven literal reaches (`named_prop_function`). Fixture `callback-prop-forwarded`: `ForwardedSettled` and `SpreadSettled` are SC3001 violations at the last child's call, and `ForwardedBody` and `SpreadedBody` are clean (main: uncertifiable). `SpreadOverridden` (a later attribute replaces the spread's prop) and `ForwardedToButton` (an intrinsic handler) keep their rows. Chrome (`runtime-oracle/callback-prop-forwarded`): covered-violation at both settled calls, quiet elsewhere, nothing static-only. Fuzz against slice 2 on the whole family (34,507 programs): mx-recall 1,218 recall-gap to agree (120 now agree through the call's violation, the literal's own row gone), lg-recall 2,580 uncertifiable to clean, 0 false results, 0 legal V, 0 V to U, 0 clean to U; mx-census unchanged. Predicted (R6's simple slice): up to about 690 rows; the measure covers the whole family. Coverage: `owner-callback-prop`'s `Forwarded` (a default-less context read in a literal forwarded once and called in the child's body) becomes an SC4002 violation; Chrome raises CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND there (`callback-prop-forwarded`'s `ForwardedContext`, covered-violation). Its SC9012 dispatch row leaves.
**Not built (this slice).** The flush census (SC2008 `flush-in-effect-unaccounted`, `flush_accounting.rs`) has no class that reads a function's entries, so a flush in such a literal keeps its row. The named, destructured, forwarded and spread forms are slices 3 and 4. `function-run-unplaced` (slice 2) has no plain-form row.

## ADR 1194 — A declaring function's role is its own through an importer's tag or call and through a helper's callback
**The cost** (bundle x): of the 3,943 mx-recall programs ADR 1166 moved to agree, ADR 1189 sent 3,208 back to recall-gap. Its `declarer_role_is_its_own` refused every reference in another file (the harness renders `C1` by its tag from an entry module, so even a read in the component body was refused) and every literal handed to a call that is no dialect primitive (`h1(() => { const f = …; [f].forEach((g) => g()); })`).
**Decision.** `named_callbacks::declarer_role_within` judges each reference in its own file: an import or export statement, a JSX tag, or a call (`f()`, `o.m()`) whose `caller_qualifies` there (outside every undecided component region, in a function that qualifies in turn; module code qualifies). An unbound literal handed to any call qualifies when that call does; `read_execution_role` still decides the role (a helper that does not run its argument in place gives none). A function handed on as a value (`[1].map(Row)`) still refuses, and a call inside an undecided component region still refuses: the 1189 false positives stay out.
**Evidence** (release, Chrome judging every program). The 3,943 programs (bundle q's list): agree 2,440, recall-gap 1,503 (ADR 1189: 735 / 3,208), so 1,705 come back; no false positive, no false clean. The 2,824 `handed-flush` legal programs: uncertifiable 2,552, clean 272, no false positive (ADR 1189's 102 stay out). Fixture `reporting-run-called-helper` gains `HelperCallback` (a violation, Chrome STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED), `MappedRowHelperCallback` (uncertifiable, Chrome silent) and `Entry.tsx` (an importer's tag of `BodyDeclared`, whose violation stands); coverage moves nothing else.
**Not built.** The 1,503 still recall-gap: a declarer reached through a function handed on as a value, a reference the reference list does not have, or a chain past four functions.

## ADR 1196 — ADR 1167's disposal-only answer is the strict read's alone (a false clean of ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE)
**The defect** (fuzz, found in ADR 1195's probe on main 60a7cf1db and 25f525504; not in `open-defects.json`): `mx-action-called-in-owned-scope-effect-cleanup-for-x-values-callee-none` judged false-clean.
- A `For` row's effect returns a cleanup that calls an action through `Object.values(box)[0]()`.
- A click empties the list, the row's disposal runs the cleanup under the row's owner, and rc.21 throws ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE at the call.
- The checker kept only the SC9012 row at `box` (the carrier), not the dispatch's withholding row at the call, where Chrome's frame is.
- Cause: ADR 1167 answered `returned-cleanup-disposal` (DeferredCallback, silent) in `read_execution_role` for a site in such a cleanup. Its doc said "reads only", but the read role is also what the dispatch of an unselectable callee asks, and that silence dropped the call's row. The same leak family as ADR 1166 r2 and ADR 1183 r2.

**Fix (fail closed).** The arm moves to `strict_read_role`, which only SC1001's strict read asks. A `For` row's disposal runs the cleanup owned, which the strict read does not care about and the action rule does.

**Evidence.**
- Fixture `effect-cleanup-for-action-dispatch`: `ValuesCallee` gains the SC9012 row at the call. `MemberCallee` (already a row at the call), `DirectCall` (SC2002) and `ReadAtDisposal` (silent, ADR 1167's strict read) are unchanged. `effect-cleanup-disposal-only` is unchanged.
- Chrome (`runtime-oracle/effect-cleanup-for-action-dispatch`, `effect-cleanup-disposal-only`): covered, nothing static-only.
- Probe (release, VM, Chrome judge), main 25f525504 against this, ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE in every cleanup context: mx-recall 1,436 programs, the false clean becomes a recall gap and nothing else moves. lg-recall 3,380 programs: none moves.
- Code level, every cleanup-context program of both grids (85,440), checker only:
  - mx-recall: 82 programs gain uncertifiable rows (80 SC1001 `function-run-unplaced`, at reads ADR 1167's read-role answer had silenced for consumers other than the strict read; 2 SC9012).
  - lg-recall: 300 programs gain rows; 8 relabel U to U at the same site.
  - Nothing goes clean and no violation is added or lost: the fail-closed cost of the move.
- Rediscovery: the id, its build fails focus on main and passes here.

## ADR 1197 — Closed callers: a read after an await in an async function no computation runs (the owner's addendum to ADR 0973's ruling 5)
**The ruling** (owner, 2026-11-23, an addendum to ADR 0973's ruling 5, asked in ADR 1191's step-0 report). A read past an await in an async function counts as "no async computation runs it" when every call is enumerated and none escapes. The conditions:
- the function is in the same file and not exported;
- every reference is a direct call, never stored, returned, passed as an argument, spread or put in an object;
- each caller resolves exactly to a handler or the component body, and a helper caller qualifies only if the same holds for it (bounded depth);
- no memo or effect compute or tracked async callback is anywhere in the chain;
- anything unresolved (a dynamic call, `eval`, `arguments`, an unknown callee) keeps the row.

**Decision** (`after_await_accounting/closed_callers.rs`, the typed ending `closed-callers`, after the six of ADRs 0973, 0976, 1004 and 1097). A site ADR 0973's accounting lists ends when the async non-generator function it is written in satisfies `closed`:
- The function is named (a declaration or a `const`'s literal), same-file, unexported (`binding_exported`) and never rebound (`function_value_is_current`). No unseen code enters it, it is no method and no component, and there is no `eval` in the file.
- ADR 0565's census of its references (`function_reference_hand_offs`) holds only `HandOff::Call`, with no foreign reference or call. It also lists every reference the binder resolved to the name, type positions aside.
- Each call is no `new` and not in a parameter list, and is the own code of its function (`runs_with_its_function`: no JSX expression, tracked region or field between). That function is an intrinsic element's `on…` handler literal (a lowercase tag with no spread), a proven component's body (`ComponentStatus::Proven`), or a helper for which the same holds (four links).
- It asks no index of computations, so it is not the census reason ADR 0973 refused.

**Evidence.**
- Fixture `after-await-closed-callers`:
  - Clean (uncertifiable on main, `read-after-await-unaccounted`): `BodyCall`, `HandlerCall`, `HelperChain`.
  - Uncertifiable, the ruling's twins: `ExportedCall` (exported), `PassedAsCallback` (`queueMicrotask(later)`), `CalledFromMemo`, `HelperFromMemo`.
- The component body's SC1001 `summary-read-unplaced` row at the call stays: another claim.
- Chrome (`runtime-oracle/after-await-closed-callers`): quiet, every clean silent at run time.
- Probe (release, VM, Chrome judge), main 25f525504 against this, every UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT program of both recall grids:
  - mx-recall, 36,503 (misuse): no outcome changes and no program changes at code level. No misuse program becomes clean, and no violation is lost.
  - lg-recall, 12,974 (legal): 513 move from uncertifiable to clean, Chrome silent, nothing needs a look. At code level, 3,927 programs lose 4,007 SC1002 `read-after-await-unaccounted` rows and nothing is added (the rest keep other rows: an SC1001 summary read at the call, a handed member, an unplaced function run).
- Boundary: the accounting's endings are no `SiteSilence` (ADR 0973) and the boundary inventory lists none of them, so there is no pair or gap to add; the separation is the probe's (no misuse move against 513 legal cleans) and the fixture's twins.

**Accepted as ruled.** The component body is a terminal as the ruling names it: a proven component that unseen code also ran as a computation's compute would break the premise. Not observed, and recorded in `docs/open-work.md`.
